the rapporteur. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, this is the first time that we have spoken in this chamber about the initiative which was unanimously adopted by the juri committee, following the work carried out by a working group which i chaired from 2010 onwards, with a view to the proposal for a regulation laying down rules of administrative procedure in the administration of the union, which is legitimated by article 298 of the treaty and article 41 of the charter of fundamental rights, which refers to the right to good administration. we've prepared a lot of material, heard a lot of opinions, studied the situation; the commission has already taken a number of initiatives in this area, and it has been possible to draw up a legislative own-initiative report, which we are submitting to parliament today, in which the commission and the council are asked to draw up a regulation on this subject. the importance of this fact lies in the fact that there are legislative disciplines of administrative procedures, but that this matter, having grown in a stratified and historical way, has led to the existence of a multifaceted reality governed by different sets of regulations, in which, however, the administration has achieved an "exorbitant power", which creates conditions of disadvantage for citizens, institutions and businesses in their relationship with the administration. that 's the real point: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. what procedure will be followed? what are my rights during the procedure? do i have the right to access my file or to be heard? what are the deadlines and times? i am giving examples to show that the european union needs to be given greater legitimacy in relation to its citizens than in the past, with clarity as regards the relationship between citizens and administration, business and administration. we therefore call for a lex generalis, a kind of de minimis rule in the absence of lex specialis, with a core of general principles providing for a regulation and therefore protection no less than that provided for in the member states, general principles of good administration. we are convinced that the aim is to strike the right balance between an efficient administration, capable of producing qualified activity, but also transparent and open, and protecting the rights of citizens. it is an essential balance which i believe is possible today, but not without such a standard. the principles thus developed will then enrich the whole, because they will stimulate the production of case law by the european court of justice and the national courts. finally, i thank commissioner šefčovič for his attention to this subject and i hope that at least in this legislature the first concrete steps will be taken in this direction.
vice-president of the commission. − mr president, the commission welcomes the own-initiative report prepared by mr berlinguer, as this report clearly identifies and elaborates a core set of fundamental administrative principles and rules stemming from different sources. in addition, a wide range of valuable background material was collected during its preparation, and i would really like to express my appreciation of the impressive work carried out by mr berlinguer and his team. the end result puts our administrative practices into perspective and raises pertinent questions in terms of how to further improve the administration of the union institutions, bodies and agencies. the right to good administration is one of the fundamental rights to be enjoyed by everyone in the european union – be it a multinational company facing a decision, an ngo applying for a grant, or a citizen seeking information – and it is enshrined in article 41 of the eu charter of fundamental rights. moreover, all eu institutions are bound by it. in the areas where the eu is involved in administrative procedures, a substantive framework of principles and rules has developed and currently applies. it consists of treaty provisions, including the eu charter of fundamental rights; general principles established by case law; cross-cutting legislation, such as staff regulations; access to documents; and legislation that is specific to sectors such as competition or procurement. in addition to these legal obligations, staff are bound by codes of good administrative behaviour in almost all eu institutions, bodies and agencies. against this backdrop, the development of a generally applicable, and thus comprehensive, regulation on eu administrative procedures – i.e. a codification exercise – has to be considered with great care. the codification of administrative law is a delicate instrument that should be used with precaution and a sense of proportion. to involve the commission and the legislator in such an exercise may have some undeniable benefits in terms of legal security and legibility, as stated clearly in the report. but it is a complicated exercise that bears some possible costs as well. it can often have unintended consequences and entail certain risks in terms of lack of flexibility or adaptability over time, oversimplification, which limits its added value, or, on the contrary, over-complexity resulting from an overlap with existing rules. the bottom line, therefore, is that it is incumbent upon us, when analysing whether or not to propose a codified instrument for the whole eu administration and all institutions, to weigh the possible advantages against the costs. and it is this very analysis that the commission is currently conducting, based on the very valuable guidelines and material provided by your report, mr berlinguer. for example, our services are currently looking into the cases of maladministration identified by the added-value report, and these cases are very useful in addressing the issue of how to improve our administrative practices. therefore, taking your substance-based report as a starting point, the commission is examining whether there are examples of maladministration that result from weaknesses in the current framework, and how such instances can be most effectively avoided in the future. to sum up, the commission welcomes the own-initiative report and the impressive background material that comes with it. we are studying it carefully, and i can assure you that in doing so we are guided by the same interests as yours in an open, efficient and independent eu administration. we, of course, will inform parliament of the anticipated follow-up within the three-month period provided for by the framework agreement.

the rapporteur. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to thank commissioner šefčovič and i do not want to interpret his caution as a coldness towards this subject. there are two ways to make an administrative procedure law: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to the full. we wouldn 't want that . we would like to see a law on administrative procedure that streamlines, makes the process more fluid, gives greater certainty and reduces the resulting conflicts of jurisdiction. there are two ways of doing this. so we do not think that making a law on the administrative procedure of the european administration alone will make the relationship between citizens and the administration more burdensome: it's the exact opposite. we want an administration that is efficient but also democratic, open and accountable. we must therefore overcome the impression, which may be unfounded, that some in the commission are concerned about being overly observed and evaluated from the outside through the administrative procedure. i believe that it is in the interests of the commission and the administration to be clear on this matter. i would like to ask the commissioner to give us a clear indication of the extent to which the commission is prepared to take action in this area. european citizenship, the credibility of the institutions and the love of the citizen for europe are not only based on the great strategies or the great measures of economic growth, but also on the everyday relationship between the citizen and the administration. it would increase the legitimacy of europe, its credibility, europe itself. we expect a lot: if there is a large majority tomorrow approving this measure, it will be a solemn invitation from parliament to make a concrete proposal.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the six months of the cypriot presidency have in fact ended in failure, because it has not succeeded in liberating the part of europe that is militarily occupied by a third country. in 1974 turkey invaded the northern part of cyprus, driving out the local population and replacing them with anatolian turks, who occupied villages and towns, taking away the property, the houses, the work of the rightful owners. the christian religion is effectively banned and masses can be celebrated only in a few authorized churches. as you are well aware, over 500 religious buildings, including cemeteries, have been destroyed and their property stolen. the european union, perhaps out of pure economic interest, has never had the courage to take a firm stand on the situation, going so far as to finance the construction of public works in turkey itself. i thought that your presidency would make the liberation of occupied northern cyprus and the return of property to its rightful owners the first condition for any further relations with turkey. but that is not the case.

vice-president of the commission. − i could not agree more with what ms geoghegan-quinn mentioned in talking about cyber security. it calls for another mindset, so to speak; it is no longer the old-fashioned definition of military activities, rather it is talking about all those actions and activities that are connected with services that are made for our society. i am talking about water services, energy, etc. i would also take this opportunity, to say that this is connected to what we are discussing this morning. it started with creating jobs and talking about a future economy. the future economy of europe is connected with research and innovation; otherwise we cannot beat our competitors outside europe. i can assure you they are alert. i am talking about south korea, taiwan, the people’s republic of china, and what they are spending on research and innovation is nearly double what we are. having said that, there is also a connection with the issue of jobs and the younger generation in particular. if we are talking about new areas – for example ict – where research is being focused, it is new industrial areas where we can play a major role as europe. i am talking about photonics, nano-electronics, micro-electronics. all of this relates to research and innovation, otherwise we are losing, and we are losing opportunities for the younger generation too. so, please be aware that a different mindset is needed when talking about all those phases we are faced with.
member of the commission. − first of all let me say that it is exactly for this reason that the eit was created. for many years europe has been investing quite rightly in research – and we should continue doing that – but in comparison with our competitors from around the world we are lagging behind in innovation. we have excellent research centres, excellent universities and very dynamic businesses, but we do not innovate, we do not produce products and services directly to the market. this is exactly the purpose of the eit. i know that you are a great supporter of the eit, but coming from a less developed part of europe i fully share your concern that, for the time being, the eit and its kics are concentrated more in the core countries of the european union. believe me, our purpose – and that is why we have made it one of our three priorities for the future of the eit – is to extend the knowledge and the benefits that are being acquired from the kics to the less developed areas of europe. i know that one of the amendments put forward by parliament is the creation of the regional innovation schemes. i support that, but let me be frank: we should try to do this, but not to the detriment of excellence, because eit is based on excellence and the kics, in the way they are created, are bottom-up partnerships and unless we have excellence in certain areas we cannot have a full-fledged kic in that area. however, at the same time we want to give the chance to experts, in the various regions of europe, to work together with existing kics and the eit in order to transfer this knowledge to the less developed areas and gradually help in building these regional innovation schemes which you are proposing. so i am in favour and we have to discuss the details of these schemes.
member of the commission. − let me say that we have already started awareness-raising activities in the various member states, because you are absolutely right: there is ignorance about this. when i speak about the eit, people do not know what it is all about. that is the only way that we can mobilise the expertise that there is in the various regions, and that is why i am vigorously promoting awareness-raising activities in the various countries.

member of the commission. − yes, i think sharing of information is crucially important, and showing them the elements of simplification that are particularly directed at smes. this is something we can help you with. anytime you simplify, an sme is truly delighted that this has happened. we also will have in place an instrument like the small business innovation research (sbir) programme they have in the united states, which again is crucially important for smes. we will have the financial instrument that i talked about earlier, the risk-sharing instrument, which is targeted at smes, and we will also have the national contact points which are there already for smes, but they obviously will be reinforced. i think there are a lot of elements there that are particularly directed at smes. we had a target in the last framework programme of 15% of the funding going to smes. as you know last year we passed that target and we were very pleased with it. we have proposed a target in horizon 2020. i am sure that will be one of the elements of the discussions in the trialogue, but we are very conscious of bringing more and more smes to the table and into the framework programme.

member of the commission. − you can be assured that we are very conscious of the fact that we need to communicate what our policies are. in this area i think the ‘science: it’s a girl thing!’ policy is particularly important. as i said, it got a lot of publicity at the beginning, when it was launched. it is now being rolled out over a number of member states – last autumn, for example – very successfully. we are using social media because we think that social media is a really important aspect, and an area in which young women, as well as all young people, get a lot of their information. it is also important to say that the web is available in all of the languages, so there is no excuse at the moment for people to say they could not understand what was on the webpage. it is available in all of the languages and we are, you can be assured, very conscious of the fact that we need to communicate what we are doing because it is, we believe, a very positive policy area.

mr president, more than two thirds of the european population live in urban areas and it is in cities that problems such as unemployment, poverty and discrimination are concentrated. promoting urban redevelopment and regeneration is therefore one of the main challenges facing the european union. only through careful spatial planning and a revival of the urban sector will it be possible to strengthen the link between the centre and the periphery, create new development opportunities and make european cities safer, more modern and more tolerant.
mr president, i too voted in favour of this dossier, which concretely develops initiatives aimed at economic cohesion and sustainable and intelligent growth. 80% of the population live in urban areas, so the resources used for this purpose should promote well-being and quality of life. in particular, a series of initiatives aimed at the redevelopment of urban centres, the introduction of new activities to ensure quality standards in line with the expectations of the population. the structural funds must be used correctly in this respect, with measurable and defined objectives which best meet the needs of the population: the commission has also proposed measures to protect natural resources, promote energy efficiency and, finally, initiatives such as the covenant of mayors, which best meet the needs of the local community.
mr president, i voted in favour of this important resolution. i have always been convinced that the urban context is the most important place in which to make europe's presence felt, to improve the social and economic growth of our societies and, above all, to regain the trust of our citizens. democracy is built from the bottom up and it is at the level closest to the citizens that appropriate policies and services must be ensured, which directly improve our daily lives. this is the purpose of european cohesion policy, which must always keep pace with economic and social change. the local development model today must be innovative and adapted to meet new challenges, including the economic crisis, climate change and ageing populations. urban redevelopment should also include experimental actions, abandoning traditional approaches and rethinking spatial planning methodologies. in this respect, i strongly support the choice to provide in the cohesion policy that at least 5% of the european development fund be devoted to this.
mr president, the allocation of 5% of the fund managed directly by the cities to integrated urban development measures is a good starting point for the european institutions to think about the cities of the future. urban redevelopment is an essential tool for economic and social growth at local level. in this respect, the new eu cohesion policy will have to ensure the social sustainability of urban transformation in order to contain the risk of displacement of the weaker sections of the population from areas affected by redevelopment processes. mr president, cohesion policies are an instrument which aims to eliminate social imbalances between citizens and the territory of the union, and in this sense, in this context, urban redevelopment can be an instrument for improving the quality of life, provided, however, that the identity and memory of cultural and territorial subjectivities embedded in urban contexts are enhanced.
mr president, i would like to express my appreciation for this report, because it finally puts the urban dimension at the heart of cohesion policy. 2013 will be a decisive year, as all the actors in the economic and social development of the european region will be engaged in preparing their operational programmes, in the hope that they will give due attention to the redevelopment of the urban suburbs and degraded areas of our cities, planning real programmes of social urban regeneration. urban areas are certainly a growth engine, but they are also the places where the major social problems are located, which can only be tackled in a new logic of integration, which also takes into account those suburban and peripheral areas. the central role of the urban dimension will mean making a wise use of the new resources of cohesion policy and the structural funds.
mr president, the economic recovery of cities is a source of job creation and improvement in the quality of life. but above all it means social and territorial integration. i think it is very important that 5% of the european regional development fund should be allocated to integrated actions for sustainable urban development. this will mean finally activating new policies for urban redevelopment, reviving the popular housing sector - which has been dead for too long - and having additional and valuable resources to build better public services, more equipped green spaces and leisure, cultural and sport facilities. i would therefore like to thank mr cozzolino for his excellent work.
mr president, i voted in favour of this report, not only because of the work done in committee but also because of the positive outcome of yesterday's debate, which saw parliament and the commission converge positively on the main points of the regi committee's own-initiative report. i was a shadow rapporteur on the cozzolino report and i am firmly convinced that the territorial dimension and, for it, urban space is an instrument for promoting social and economic cohesion in europe through a transparent and intelligent use of structural resources. cities need to be given a new face to enable them to absorb the economic crisis, by breaking down cultural and social barriers and promoting integration among urban citizens. to achieve these objectives, we are asking in the cozzolino report - and yesterday commissioner hahn seems to have agreed with our request - that the urban agenda should focus on the objectives of sustainability, innovation and inclusiveness, that multi-fund actions should be promoted so that the 5% erdf is only the starting point, that the local development model should be of the participatory type and that local administrators should therefore participate not only in the management phase but also in the decision-making phase.
mr president, with the vote just taken by a large majority, parliament intends to give a more concrete dimension to the european union's cohesion policy by putting the context in which more than two thirds of the european population live, namely urban centres, at the centre of the action. cities are historically places where the difficulties of daily life are most felt: i am not referring only to economic terms, but also to social and interpersonal terms. the european cohesion policy, which in the period 2007-2013 represented a significant share of the european budget with eur 347 billion (corresponding to 35.7% of the total budget), aims with this resolution to highlight the dimension closer to the citizens. obviously, a new approach to problems such as efficient energy management, waste management, immigration, the ageing of the population, to name just a few, cannot ignore the need for the european institutions to attach greater importance to local elected representatives, namely mayors.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the contribution of urban redevelopment to economic growth in eu cohesion policy as i believe that it can have a positive impact on regional imbalances within the community, thus avoiding the segregation of the most deprived social classes, which are often concentrated and polarized in peripheral areas. moreover, in a time of crisis such as the present, redeveloping the city to attract an increasing number of tourists could be beneficial to the economic recovery which is closely linked to urban redevelopment; it is therefore essential to give back symbolic spaces to the community and thus promote cultural heritage.
in writing. - the importance of the urban dimension in the european union today is undeniable, considering that as many as 80% of community citizens live in this context. this is the area most affected by the current crisis, and in recent years many changes have taken place in our cities. the whole european strategy must therefore be revised in order to be able to cope with the new challenges facing cities, starting with a phenomenon which has become increasingly evident, with the rush to move from central areas to peripheral areas, where housing costs are often more affordable. we must avoid the risk of depopulation of the city centres, which are historical and cultural assets of absolute value, and which can lead in the worst case to degradation and abandonment. the urban area is often also the driving force behind the surrounding rural area, and the two dimensions must be seen as a unit, as is rightly emphasized in this report. the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of the environment in the event of a natural disaster is a good one.
in writing. − 2013 opens with a key objective for the european union: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. all sectors are involved and are obliged to commit themselves to an organised and effective programme. within the eu's cohesion policy, one of the contributions to economic growth is the so-called urban redevelopment which, based on the analysis of migration flows from peripheral areas, will have to set an agenda capable of ensuring sustainability and development in situations of constant population growth.
in writing. - i vote in favour of the report on the contribution of urban regeneration to economic growth in eu cohesion policy. urban redevelopment and regeneration is one of the main challenges facing the european union, and it is necessary to strengthen the link between cities and development and between urban centres and the surrounding area. the report proposes methods for revitalising town planning and spatial planning, and opens a debate on planning practices and instruments of intervention which can enrich environmental, territorial, commercial and road policies. i am convinced that the proposal, in addition to providing the means to improve the quality of life of european citizens, will make a significant contribution to the development of cohesion policies.
in writing. - i welcome the motion for a resolution tabled by parliament. europe is no longer in a phase of constant economic growth, and many cities are facing serious threats of economic stagnation or decline. demographic change is creating a number of challenges: the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council should be consulted on the proposal. today, 80% of europe's citizens live in urban areas, a proportion that is growing further as migration from rural to urban areas accelerates. problems such as unemployment, discrimination and poverty are crucial to understanding that the european model of sustainable urban development is in danger. it is in cities that the effects of the economic crisis are most concentrated and that the challenges of job creation, well-being and quality of life are most acute. the local development model is a strength of cohesion policy because it mobilises decisive factors, encourages the selection of the best choices that are closest to the citizens, more coherent, effective and efficient joint actions, and gives greater visibility to community action even in areas of the eu facing the most difficult challenges.
mr president, it is clear that cohesion policy funding is becoming increasingly important for the regions of the union. in particular, in view of the economic crisis that has affected europe since 2008, it is necessary to ensure that the available resources are spent efficiently in order for citizens to benefit fully from union funding. the involvement of local and regional authorities at every stage of the design, development and implementation of funding programmes is therefore essential to ensure that local needs are met and that the territorial potential is used to the best possible effect in achieving the objectives of cohesion policy.
mr president, i think this resolution deserves our full support. the european union's funding programmes, which form part of the commission's common strategic framework and are designed to implement cohesion policies, must be coordinated as much as possible in order to be most effective. territorial cohesion is one of the objectives recognised by the treaty of lisbon and is a cross-cutting aspect of the various programmes: that is why we must get the best out of all the programmes and coordinate them. european funding is now more than ever an important resource for the territories, given the shortage of regional and local budgets, which has been exacerbated by the economic crisis. therefore, funds must increasingly be spent in a smart and effective way, involving local and regional authorities through partnership agreements, to achieve participatory local development through integrated territorial investments.
mr president, just as i voted in favour of mr cozzolino's report, which i welcome, i voted in favour of the vaughan report on optimising the role of the territorial dimension in cohesion policy. the commission has already taken a number of initiatives to improve the quality of the information provided by the member states. only a comprehensive view of the problems and an integrated policy approach with integrated implementation of funding programmes will determine the effectiveness of union funds at local and regional level. to understand and to give an example, just think of the structural funds and the horizon 2020 funds, both of which should be able to apply to projects which aim to strengthen one of the main elements on which we are concentrating, namely research, technological development, innovation, one of the priorities which, as i said before, we have set ourselves among the 11 main thematic objectives. the instruments suggested by the commission to encourage greater synergies between the funds should therefore be supported by concrete implementation mechanisms at regional and local level.
mr president, cohesion policy is a fundamental instrument for social and economic growth and for ensuring, with the funds available, integration between urban and rural areas. this requires promoting multi-level governance by creating partnerships, networks and projects with the common provisions regulation funds. these integrated territorial investments can bring great benefits to young people, smes, social policies, the fight against poverty and social exclusion and much more. it is therefore a good package of proposals and i hope that a portal will also be set up as soon as possible to enable citizens, businesses and local and regional authorities to have easy access to all the information on european funds.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the vaughan report, which analyses the role of territorial development in cohesion policies. the text strongly emphasises the importance of multi-level governance as a tool to ensure that decisions are ever closer to and in line with the needs of citizens and our territories. i hope that the revision of cohesion policy for the future 2014-2020 programming period will converge towards a massive simplification of the administrative burden associated with the use of the funds, in order to ensure optimal access to resources and greater coordination between them and individual programmes.
in writing. − the importance of creating multi-level governance, with a particular focus on the creation of macro-regions that take decisions at a level closer to the citizens, is a positive development at european level. the simplification of the procedure for obtaining european funds and the development of links between rural and urban areas are also fully acceptable objectives. for all these reasons, my vote was in favour.
in writing. − optimising the role of the territorial dimension in cohesion policy involves choices concerning more effective communication between the different political and institutional levels, joint collaboration between them and a community of interest in meeting and achieving the needs and objectives of the territories. with the new multiannual financial framework (mff) coming into force, which will set the spending ceilings for the community budget over the next seven years (2014-2020), the role of territorial realities will be questioned again and put at the centre of the debate. it is clear that the optimisation of the territorial dimension is important for the effective and efficient spending of european funds. the commission has therefore decided to continue along the path traced so far, keeping in mind the difficulties encountered so far, in order to analyse the causes and find the appropriate solutions for a sustainable growth, both from an economic and social point of view, of local realities.
in writing. − territorial cohesion is now recognised by the lisbon treaty as a key objective of the eu; cohesion policy aims instead to reduce disparities between eu regions by strengthening economic, social and territorial cohesion. the territorial dimension is a cross-cutting aspect of cohesion policy and offers the union's regions the opportunity to exploit their territorial potential in order to achieve cohesion policy objectives. in the current economic climate, it is clear that cohesion policy funding is becoming increasingly important for the eu's regions. in addition, it is becoming increasingly necessary to ensure that resources are spent efficiently so that citizens can fully benefit from eu funding. the involvement of local and regional authorities at every stage of the design, development and implementation of eu funding programmes becomes crucial to ensure that local needs are met. moreover, the territorial dimension, as a cross-cutting aspect of cohesion policy, gives eu regions the opportunity to exploit their territorial potential in pursuing cohesion policy objectives. in short, we need a real contribution and an efficient and effective cohesion policy in this respect.
mr president, in 2002, after the devastating floods in central europe, the european union launched the solidarity fund to help the people affected and the member states affected by the disaster. over the past 10 years, the fund has provided valuable financial support but has also revealed some shortcomings: the commission has already taken steps to ensure that the rules on the free movement of goods are applied in the member states. given the need to adapt the solidarity fund to the present situation, i welcome changes which, without entailing additional costs, can simplify procedures by defining more clearly the concept of catastrophe and by outlining more precisely when you are entitled to benefit from this instrument.
mr president, let me express my surprise at hearing from the british nationalists' benches statements about the public spending of the european union, when in order to stay in europe they are calling for a discount, a rebate, and vice versa, they are calling for the application of full rights. turning to the european union solidarity fund, we have unfortunately seen in this house on several occasions statements of solidarity and witness to the serious damage that weather events and unforeseeable situations have caused to our people. i believe that the solidarity fund has proved to be one of the most effective instruments for european integration policies, being one of the few instruments that the european union has at its disposal to bear witness, to demonstrate directly solidarity and closeness to the european citizens. the current wording of the regulation, however, required some changes, both to shorten the time for granting aid and to clarify the definition of disaster itself, which was currently ambiguous and therefore raised - as my colleague mrs zanicchi said - undue expectations. as a member of parliament, i would like to see and welcome the acceptance of the requests for agreement on at least these two points - i am addressing myself to the council and the commission - which would dissolve several procedural knots in the implementation of the solidarity fund.
mr president, as my predecessor mr tannock rightly pointed out, italy recently benefited from this european union solidarity fund following the terrible earthquake which struck three regions, especially emilia romagna but also lombardy and my region of veneto. we are certainly talking about one of the most effective and practical instruments for bringing about the spirit of solidarity and closeness to citizens affected by disasters, whether natural or man-made. we need these changes. we need more streamlined and transparent procedures. we need above all to make the citizens feel that europe is close to them, but unfortunately it is too often perceived as an entity incapable of meeting the concrete needs and requirements of the citizens. i voted with conviction with my political family in favour of this document and i hope that we will be able to welcome it in the same way and continue to work on this principle when my report 'strengthening european disaster response: the role of civil protection and humanitarian assistance' arrives in the house shortly.
in writing. - i share the recommendations of my colleague estaràs ferragut on the need to amend the current regulation on the european union solidarity fund, improving the efficiency and speed of the administrative procedures for its mobilisation, introducing the possibility of making advance payments to speed up the disbursement of aid, especially in the event of so-called 'slow-moving' disasters. italy has suffered two "extraordinary regional disasters" this year: the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the draft budget for the financial year. in this connection, i believe, as the rapporteur has also requested, that the fund should also cover the 'collateral damage' caused by these events to the socioeconomic fabric, such as smes. i hope very much that the criteria for access to aid will be clarified soon.
in writing. i voted in favour of mr ferragut's report. two years after the terrible floods in veneto, parliament is finally heeding my calls and the battles fought to bring to the commission's attention the urgency of changing the way the european union solidarity fund (eusf) operates. help that comes late is help that can lose its usefulness. the veneto region has waited a year to receive the funds allocated by brussels, while those for the earthquake-stricken areas of emilia have even been threatened with being blocked. the rules of solidarity in europe and its financial instrument need to be rewritten: the commission's proposal for a regulation on the financing of the european social fund is a good one, but it is not enough to make it a priority.
in writing. − the eusf is one of the main instruments for implementing the principle of european solidarity; the commission's proposal is based on the principle of subsidiarity, which is the basis of the treaty of rome. even with limited ambition, a review of the discipline could be useful to ensure a prompt response by the institutions, to shield governments from unfounded and recurrent initiatives dictated by political opportunism, and to strengthen the concept of european citizenship through a prompt provision, including the use of conditional advance, which translates into concrete actions for the benefit of the affected populations. we must start with the two facts that two thirds of the applications for special regional disasters have been rejected and that the ceiling of 1.5% of regional gdp is not adequate to filter or set priorities. in voting in favour of the report, i support the request that the implementation include legally binding declaratory aspects which, while taking into account the relative unpredictability of disasters, can nevertheless be triggered by a wide cascade of events, duly analysed over ten years of activity.
in writing. - i think that this report is fully acceptable and does not present any problems, and it will also facilitate the rapid allocation of funds in the event of natural disasters, thus avoiding the recurrence of the problems of disbursement of funds as in the case of the earthquake in emilia. for these reasons, i voted in favour.
in writing. − the european union solidarity fund is an instrument that has shown its european added value and has proven its effectiveness since it was first introduced. in this connection, i would like to highlight one of the last cases, in chronological order, in which this fund has played a decisive role for a territory suffering from the disastrous consequences of a natural disaster. i am referring to the earthquake which struck the areas of emilia-romagna and for which we were able, with considerable difficulty, to secure the funds needed for the reconstruction of those areas. in view of the improvement of the criteria for access to this fund, especially in relation to regional disasters, i believe that the proposals in the report are going in the right direction. we must think of weighting criteria which take more and more account of the scale of disasters and their frequency in the most affected regions of europe.
in writing. − over the past 20 years, natural disasters have killed around 90,000 people and caused more than €200 billion in damage. the solidarity fund is the union's main solidarity instrument. the time needed to mobilise the fund is unfortunately too long and the criteria for intervention are not very transparent. advance payments are therefore necessary to accelerate the response rate and the visibility of union support. finally, i think it is essential to amend the regulation by redefining the criteria for regional disasters in a simple, objective and transparent way.
in writing. - i have spoken on several occasions to point out some criticisms concerning the methods of access to this fund: the biggest problem is to define what are 'minor' disasters on a regional basis. often the damage caused is not "minor" at all and therefore objective criteria should be established on a regional basis to assess whether they are eligible for european support. in the past there have been instances of mismanagement by the authorities, such as the snow emergency last february, in which many southern regions wanted to be included without entitlement, thus compromising the entire application. i think that we should therefore move towards a more direct link between the regional authorities and brussels, in order to define real emergency situations, bypassing the national dimension in which they often try to sneak in without the necessary qualifications, thus penalising those who have really been affected by natural disasters. in tuscany, money for the 2011 floods in lunigiana has arrived, albeit with considerable delay: however, we are still awaiting a decision on the damage caused to the gross tonnage by the heavy rains last november.
in writing. - i welcome parliament's motion for a resolution because the european union solidarity fund (eusf) is the main instrument for demonstrating the union's solidarity action, providing important financial support to member states or regions affected by major disasters, facing a difficult situation. however, the time currently required to mobilise the fund appears to be too long and prolonged in its implementation, which is why the efficiency and speed of the administrative procedures provided for should be improved. the need is therefore to simplify the bureaucratic processes necessary to mobilise the eu instrument, in order to shorten the time - sometimes extended to over a year - between the time when the disaster occurs and the time when the member state or region in question receives aid. the administrative procedures are slow, complicated and cumbersome.
mr president, i voted in favour of this resolution because i am in favour of a commission legislative initiative which sets out appropriate rules to ensure administrative legality and the protection of citizens' rights vis-à-vis the european institutions. the growth of the union administration in recent decades, both in size and in importance, requires adequate legislation on procedural rights in the context of the union's administrative procedures. these rights can no longer be guaranteed only in the interpretative case-law of the court of justice, although the latter has played an essential role in this context. it is true that europe must be divided up into states with different legal traditions: but it is true that the solution of the encryption is undoubtedly fundamental. and we must try to achieve this and strengthen it through the treaties, namely the treaty of lisbon but also the european charter of human rights. i believe that this is a fundamental step towards a greater europe.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the berlinguer report on european union law on administrative procedures. the text calls on the commission to submit a proposal for a regulation defining the construction of a community case-law on administrative procedures to be applied for the management of relations between the eu institutions and bodies and citizens. i believe that this choice would help to ensure greater certainty and transparency in relations between citizens and europe.
in writing. − the report aims to provide clearer and more certain rights for citizens and businesses in their dealings with the european union administration. as the greater participation of citizens in the work of the union is one of the main objectives we are aiming to achieve, i voted in favour.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the recommendations to the commission on administrative law because i believe that the process of european union integration must also include a single administrative law, limited to the direct administration of the eu and binding on the european institutions. this would enable clear rules to be established for citizens and legal persons, thus improving the relationship between the latter and the union administration. for these reasons, i believe that a legislative initiative by the commission is necessary to identify a core of general de minimis principles, which serve as guidelines for good administrative behaviour in the european context. such procedural rules would ensure increased levels of transparency and accountability of the european institutions, and at the same time, confidence by citizens.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report in question, fully agreeing with its scope. the aim of the regulation is to guarantee the right to good administration through an open, efficient and independent administration based on european union law on administrative procedures. the rapporteur believes that administrative procedural law is an opportunity to strengthen the legitimacy of the european union, while providing citizens and legal persons with clearer rights and greater legal certainty in their relations with the union's administration. the aim is to ensure fair and impartial administrative procedures, based on the constitutional traditions of the different member states and linked to the principles of legality, proportionality, fairness and transparency.
in writing. − the european union's administration has grown considerably in recent decades. despite this growth, the union currently does not have comprehensive legislation on the procedural rights of citizens in administrative proceedings. administrative procedural law thus provides an opportunity to strengthen the legitimacy of the european union by providing citizens and legal persons with clearer rights and greater legal certainty in their dealings with the union administration. i therefore welcomed mr berlinguer's proposal to invite the commission to submit a proposal for a regulation on european law on administrative procedures.
mr president, in the third quarter of 2011, job losses were almost twice as high as the jobs created, and unfortunately we know that this trend is set to increase, especially if we take into account the news about major restructuring in strategic sectors. between 2008 and 2011, more than 6 million jobs were lost in construction and manufacturing alone. the situation today requires companies and their employees to make the necessary changes to safeguard competitiveness and jobs: this becomes a problem for the parties concerned, especially in the late stage, when layoffs are most often expected. the positive export performance of some member states shows that success on world markets depends not only on price competitiveness but also on broader factors such as sectoral specialisation, innovation and skill levels, which enhance real competitiveness. this is precisely what the european union should be doing more of. the new cycle of economic planning is approaching and i think we should take account of the data that emerge from this report and review the investment strategy and focus on innovation and the real economy.
mr president, as many colleagues have already mentioned, unfortunately the economic and financial crisis has led to an increase in the number of firms being forced to close down or to restructure their businesses at european level. in many cases, it was the latter that led management to opt for intra-european relocation. it is clear that these cases have affected employment levels in europe and in particular in italy we have had, in the last year, many striking cases, which have put many workers on the streets. the fundamental point raised in the cercas report, which deals with these hypotheses, is the call for common european regulations, which avoid competitive imbalances between countries. it is absurd to think that by differentiating legislation and, above all, by making taxation systems different, our countries, the member states, would be engaging in unfair competition, reducing employment levels considerably and thus going against the general european policies. i voted in favour of the report for these reasons.
in writing. the aim of the cercas report is to improve the protection of workers who are at risk of redundancy because of the likely failure or transfer of an undertaking. the scope of the measures proposed in the text is similar to that of the european globalisation adjustment fund, but the initiatives described by mr cercas are aimed at the launching of programmes for the preventive retraining of workers, well before the bankruptcy or transfer of the company. although i think the idea of anticipating the negative effects of company restructuring is a positive one, i think there is a real risk that some companies may feel justified in using the redundancy tool more readily than they do now, on the strength of the fact that a re-skilled worker has, on paper, less trouble relocating. for these reasons i voted to abstain.
in writing. i voted in favour of mr cercas' report on the information and consultation of workers and the management of company restructuring because, in the light of the latest developments in the italian steel industry, i find the situation of many workers in italy and in europe extremely worrying. we must work towards careful regulation of business management which protects workers and is able to keep companies competitive. the european union must be able to make its assessments by adapting them to specific cases, taking into account the human side as much as the economic balance and not relying solely on the interpretation of the law.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report calling on the commission to put forward a legislative proposal to create minimum european levels of protection for workers who undergo company restructuring, because national governments do not seem to be able to deal adequately with major restructuring of international companies, which requires a european approach. european legislation is needed to take account of such restructuring and to provide for fair and balanced management of it when it occurs. today more than ever, the situation of many firms affected by the crisis calls for timely action so that the continuing and profound changes in the global landscape, which greatly increase the risk of the firm, can be addressed by limiting the risks, so that even a possible company restructuring does not necessarily have to become a cause of job loss for workers, but can be transformed into an opportunity. the commission is expected to adopt measures to protect workers and involve all the parties concerned, including the social partners.
in writing. - in mr cercas' report, parliament asks the commission to draw up a proposal for a 'legal act' on the information and consultation of workers in the event of restructuring, in order to anticipate and better manage such processes. given that change is a constant phenomenon in the lives of businesses and workers and that the ability to adapt to change is an essential element in preserving competitiveness, supporting growth and creating jobs, i believe that the institutions, by taking an integrated approach to the problem, should focus their efforts on those measures which can stimulate economic growth.
in writing. - unfortunately, the horn of africa has been subject to a series of conflicts for decades, due to its natural resources, fossil fuels and water, and the overwhelming demand of some oil and gas producing states to gain infrastructure access to other states or to the sea. in addition, a severe famine crisis due to drought has worsened the situation in recent years, causing a terrible humanitarian crisis affecting over 12 million people, including many children. i am in favour of the eu strategy for the horn of africa, which aims to restore the socio-political situation in the region and to make these peoples aware of the great economic potential they possess. it is necessary, however, to explain to future political bodies that european financial assistance is conditional on the achievement of specific objectives, such as programmes to avert future humanitarian crises and to restore the development of many strategic sectors.
in writing. - the horn of africa is today one of the most food insecure regions in the world. millions of people living in the region are undernourished and at risk of famine, as well as living in health standards considered to be among the lowest in the world. governance is almost entirely absent, and human insecurity and food insecurity in particular are causing serious humanitarian crises in the region. we must acknowledge that the international community has not yet been able to take preventive measures to deal with the issues of human security, drought and famine in this area. that is why i think that the path of aid and peacekeeping is a two-track road that must be pursued more intensively. i therefore welcome some of the measures contained in mr tannock's report, such as my call on the commission to consider providing aid and support to all african countries which have made military commitments to maintain peace in the horn of africa. in particular, i very much welcome the eu's decision to provide additional support to amisom so that it can fulfil its mandate and reach a total military force of 17 731 units, as authorised by the united nations.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because it makes a clear assessment of the eu’s engagement in the horn of africa, which is one of the world’s poorest regions and one of those most lacking in governance. particular attention should be given to the fact that the international community has failed to take any preventive steps to address the issues of human security, drought and famine in the region. the horn of africa has a long history of conflicts and it is important to bear in mind that sustainable development cannot be achieved in an environment characterised by armed conflicts and unstable government institutions. at the same time, any credible strategy must acknowledge that poverty and underdevelopment operate as conflict-generating factors. for all these reasons, the vicious circle of insecurity, poverty and bad governance can only be successfully addressed through a comprehensive approach.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the tannock report on the european strategy for the horn of africa. the horn of africa is notoriously one of the most politically unstable regions on the planet: the text outlines possible community measures which would help to improve the socioeconomic dynamics of a geopolitically extremely complex situation. the report stresses three actions which it considers to be priorities over the others: the european union is also committed to combating terrorism, supporting the united nations in humanitarian operations and securing international trade routes affected by piracy.
in writing. - i believe that this proposal deserves support from a number of angles. first of all, the objective of pacifying one of the most unstable areas on the planet cannot but be shared. the following proposals should therefore be implemented: building strong and accountable political structures in the region; aim at the resolution of armed conflicts; to intervene to promote economic growth and reduce poverty and foster political and economic cooperation between the countries of the horn of africa. for all these reasons, my vote was in favour.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the european union's action in the horn of africa because this situation of instability, which has been going on for some time now, has consequences for all the countries in the region and for the whole continent. a comprehensive approach to achieving sustainable development in the region is essential, as the horn of africa is a region where criminal activity, including terrorism and piracy, is very intense due to extreme poverty and bad governance. moreover, the continuation of this critical situation could have repercussions on relations between the countries of the region and the rest of the continent, in the first place, and consequently also with other actors, including the european union itself. it would be better to put an end to the continuing violations of human rights, such as in eritrea, rather than to the restrictions on freedom of opinion and expression which are an obstacle to the process of democratization in the horn of africa. it is therefore important to implement a programme of democratic development accompanied by political dialogue, so that a cycle of lasting peace and stability can be achieved.
in writing. - coup d'états, civil wars and, in recent years, piracy have drawn the eu's attention to the horn of africa. the search for peace, stability and the will to create the basis for the development of these countries is the driving force behind the solidarity of the european union, which must look beyond its strategic interests and help this region. i support the eu's initiatives to ensure the rule of law, to deal with security and stability issues, humanitarian aid and the development of a democratic system. respect for human rights and the end of conflict are the main objectives of the entire horn of africa, which needs help and not western intervention.
in writing. - i have expressed a favourable opinion on the report in question as it welcomes the eu strategy for the horn of africa and in particular its comprehensive approach based on addressing issues of security, stability, respect for the rule of law and the guarantee of a process to ensure the application of the law, as well as an independent judicial system. the region has a long history of conflict, poverty and underdevelopment; sustainable development cannot be achieved in a climate of tension, poverty, armed conflict, and unstable government institutions. this prolonged instability in the horn of africa also affects the security of neighbouring countries and the whole continent. the eu strategic framework for the horn of africa supports some of the key points on which to build democratic, robust and accountable political structures; these include cooperation with countries in the region, interaction between regional and international actors and organisations, and support for interventions to promote economic growth and reduce poverty by addressing the basic needs of the population.
in writing. - the long history of conflict in the horn of africa has made it one of the poorest regions in the world, with very poor health standards, severe food insecurity and a very high mortality rate. the prolonged instability in this region has also had an impact on the security of neighbouring countries, which are also affected by conflict, poverty and underdevelopment. i am therefore in favour of measures to combat internal conflicts, terrorism and piracy which, by strengthening security in the horn of africa, can promote better development cooperation and the consequent gradual elimination of poverty and famine.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the preservation of the planet's genetic diversity, a crucial element of sustainable agriculture and food security, is one of the millennium development goals that has been mentioned many times. a phenomenon to be fought in this field unfortunately growing exponentially is certainly the so-called biopiracy, a really odious practice because it occurs when biological resources are taken in a way that is sometimes illegal or at least irregular but not only from local or indigenous communities and then patented but the revenues generated from this withdrawal do not benefit the countries to which these resources belong. so fighting bio-piracy is a major challenge that we have to face, because these practices are totally contrary to the commitments we have made to eradicate poverty and to protect biodiversity. i think it is important to stress, with our vote, that the fight against poverty in the developing countries also involves, in a very concrete way, issues which are only apparently technical and legal.
in writing. - i support the report by mrs grèze on 'aspects relating to the development of intellectual property rights in genetic resources'. the text urges the european union to take action to combat the phenomena of 'biopiracy', an increasingly widespread practice in which industrialised countries appropriate, by patenting them, biological resources belonging to local communities in developing countries, without any economic return for them. the resolution also calls on the commission to take the necessary steps to ensure that the eu is able to meet the challenges of the global financial crisis.
in writing. - the report by mrs grèze has the merit of bringing to the attention of the european institutions the problem of 'biopiracy', which is difficult to identify legally. genetic diversity is a heritage to be preserved and is a good that is now increasingly enjoyed by so-called emerging countries. however, precisely because of the phenomenon of 'biopiracy', the beneficiaries of biodiversity are the already industrialised countries. in this sense, the proposal to endorse the nagoya protocol should be welcomed. the protocol on the right of access to genetic resources and traditional knowledge concerns the obligation to provide benefits in return for access to genetic resources and traditional knowledge and also provides for the obligation to obtain prior informed consent before access.
in writing. - i believe that the european union must take action to counter the bio-piracy activities carried out by multinational companies to the detriment of developing countries. very often, these companies exploit plants with medicinal properties and traditional remedies originating in these countries, without sharing in any way the profits. patenting their medicinal traditions means blocking their economic development, which is clearly contrary to the objectives of the european union itself.
in writing. − the protection and conservation of genetic diversity is a key element in achieving the millennium development goals. genetic resources are essential, above all, for the sustainability of agriculture and food security. moreover, genetic diversity is one of the main components for the survival of species and the preservation of the ecosystem. it should also be stressed that the genetic resources of countries rich in biodiversity make a significant contribution to pharmaceutical research and development. unfortunately, it has been shown that intellectual property rights (ipr) significantly hinder access to medicines in poor countries. i am also in favour of fighting against bio-piracy, which is a major challenge facing the eu, as these practices are contrary to the commitments made to eradicate poverty and protect biodiversity, as well as to the principle of policy coherence for development enshrined in article 208 of the lisbon treaty.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, mr chancellor, to discuss the future of europe means to answer two questions: is the european social model a burden or a resource in dealing with globalisation? and can its defence and revival be left to the individual states or does it require the construction of a genuine democratic government of the euro? our group gives a positive answer to both questions and we are glad that your words go in the same direction: the european union is not only a europe of stability, but also of growth, solidarity and democracy. overcoming blind austerity does not mean returning to fiscal irresponsibility but working alongside budgetary discipline to define european policies in co-decision for growth and social inclusion. this is why we need a european budget worthy of the name, based on own resources. i very much appreciated your comments on this and growth-friendly fiscal consolidation, which allows for countercyclical policies and does not penalise public investment. this requires a strong social pillar, starting with the implementation and adequate financing of the european youth guarantee which works so well in austria. mr chancellor, thank you for coming and for your words: we are confident that in the coming months the battle for the definition of a european social pact and for a genuine and democratic economic and monetary union will be able to count on its support.

madam president, ladies and gentlemen, france's military intervention in mali marked the beginning of an operation which had been in the making for some time. president hollande has, in this respect, broken all delays, putting into practice what is now inevitably the only way to restore balance. but now we need stronger action from the european union: the problem of the sahel and the presence of islamic fundamentalism and terrorism cannot be tackled by fragmented action on the initiative of individual countries. the stakes are high and the outcome of this operation must also prefigure the future scenarios in which we will have to work, to bring greater democracy and stability to geopolitical realities that for centuries have been a land of conquest and that today have become the scene of human rights violations and cultural barbarism. for these reasons, it is necessary to coordinate and agree on an action plan, which brings together present and future and involves all the actors concerned as quickly as possible.
vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy. − madam president, we have heard a complete spectrum of views, for which i am extremely grateful, but i want people first of all just to rewind the clock a little and to look back on what was happening a year and two years ago, because it would be completely wrong to suggest that somehow this has come upon us and that no thought and strategy has gone into it. we have in fact been looking for a long time at how to support this part of the world. you might not like the word ‘strategy’ but actually you need one. if you talk to any military commander on the ground – and i have spoken to many – and if you talk to any military planning team – and i have spoken to many – the first thing that they will say to you is that it is not enough to think of military action, important though that may be. what you always need is a political, developmental, strategic approach to what you can do. with the support of all member states, which we have built, with the support of the african union and with the support of the united nations, we have pulled together the creation of a strategy which looks at the different elements of what you need to do. you need to find ways to actually put in place a development plan. this part of the world has got many challenges. there are people who are hungry, there are children who are not educated, and there are communities that do not see any representative of anything that we would vaguely call a government. you have the development necessity of needing to build from every aspect of life something that people can actually have, in order to create the circumstances where you can get some kind of security for that dimension. the second thing you have to do is to build the political structure that is going to bring together the countries of that region to tackle some of the security challenges that they face. we have had meetings with the foreign ministers and with many officials from all of the countries of the sahel to get them to work together to develop that strategy too. you need to be able to be sure that you are working with them. this is not about turning up in a country and doing things to people. we do not do that. we work on a strategy that has at its heart the desire to see that it is owned by the people and the governments of the region and is supported in this context, with african ownership for the security strategy that needs to be set in place. no one has ever suggested that we should do anything other than that. if they did suggest it, they would be wrong, because that is what we have done and that is what we have built and pulled together. now what we face is a sudden offensive, an offensive that actually did take people by surprise. i am afraid the world is full of surprises. we can think about the last two or three years and reflect on areas that, yes, we might have thought could be volatile, but we did not know when and how and in which way. this is no exception to that. at that point, a member state was asked to give support. we have been in constant touch with france throughout that whole process, as they took their decision on what they should do. we do not have a european defence force. what we have are the groupings of defence ministers, foreign ministers and the intergovernmental work that they do. that is the structure that we work with. that is the structure that we use to try to support these situations and support member states. it is why i have convened the foreign affairs council as quickly as i can to bring together 27 foreign ministers, as well as the malian foreign minister and the military representatives of the eu, so that we can talk about how best to show solidarity with what france is doing, but also how best to begin to push further forward on this strategy. one of the key elements of this was to support the malian army, which needed training help. the structures may take too long – i am not disputing that – but they are the structures that i have been given, that we have been given in the service, that either have been determined through regulations or determined through the intergovernmental methods and, yes, i would like to see some of them speeded up. we have managed to speed this one up rather dramatically, because a lot of the planning was done. but if you are going to send a training mission to another country, you also have to have it ready on the ground, and that means working with the military forces and the government on the ground. so it is not always that we are delayed, it is that actually the recipients need to be ready to receive us. that mission is specifically designed to help the malian army be able to cope with the situation it finds itself in. there are elements of that training which we can start even now, even though they are engaged directly in trying to secure part of the country. it is a really important mission and it is never to be underestimated how important it is. but it is part of a much bigger programme of how you bring political security to that part of the world. but please, honourable members, do not underestimate the challenges of what is happening in that part of the world and do not underestimate the amount of work that is going on to try and secure a political future for the people of that part of the world. this is the european union in operation. it may not be what all of you or some of you would want. you may want to have in reserve a force that can go in. what you saw was a member state responding very quickly, very effectively, and which is now being supported by other member states, and we will see that solidarity coming into action. it was responding to a situation that people did not predict, and did not know about, so it has actually been a very, very rapid deployment. all of that has been in conjunction with us in brussels, in trying to pull together and make sure we are supporting it: additional humanitarian aid going in, additional development support being prepared, support for the government to be able to cope, training for their army, support for the other countries at risk in the region – remember we already have a programme in niger – and all of that sahel strategy coming into action. i hope that what you will see is a much better response from the european union than you would have seen five years ago, but a building of that response, so we can get better and better at how we do it. i end by expressing my solidarity with france and of course we think about the soldiers fighting tonight, the malian army soldiers, our french forces and we of course remember those who have lost their lives in that conflict.

excellent work he has done in this area. we have come to this debate and the vote in the house on the third regulation on credit rating agencies and the related directive after a long, complicated and some of the proposed reform measures, particularly because of the conservative will expressed by the council. i am referring in particular to important and innovative proposals put forward by the commission, such as the civil liability of credit rating agencies and the obligation to rotate, i.e. to change credit rating agencies by the customer every three years, proposals which, thanks to the commitment of the european parliament, have been avoided and the principle of the regulation has been maintained, although it has to accept a reduction in their scope and the change of some significant aspects. this is a paradoxical situation, in my view. we would very likely not have had this new rating agency regulation, the third in just over three years, if it hadn't been for the sovereign debt rating controversy. but when it came to getting down to the nitty-gritty, proposing new measures and taking concrete action, many governments pulled the handbrake and even backed off. yet it was the same governments, the same national and european politicians who attacked the rating agencies with force, holding them explicitly responsible for encouraging sovereign debt speculation by their choices, their statements and their behaviour which they considered to be very irresponsible. why this contradiction? unless our governments and the council are suffering from some kind of stockholm syndrome, i believe there are two main reasons: the first is that the rating agencies are very effective lobbyists. the second is that, all in all, sometimes it's helpful to have someone to criticize and attack when things are going wrong and there are problems. but the game is risky and the tendency to leave things as they are can lead to the consolidation of the dependence of the public institutions themselves on the judgments of the rating agencies. however, with this new regulation we are also making progress - and not just progress - on the question of sovereign debts, thanks in particular to the contribution of the european parliament. the establishment of a provisional timetable for unsolicited ratings on sovereign debt; the prohibition of statements intended to influence the policies to be implemented and pursued by governments; greater transparency and accountability in the rating methodologies used and, above all, the launching of a process to achieve an internal assessment by the european union of the creditworthiness of the member states and, in the future, the possibility of establishing a european public agency for the rating of sovereign debt, are all important new features of the new regulation, which are fully consistent with the underlying inspiration of this measure, which is to promote internal ratings, to have a plurality of reliable and comparable voices at the service of investors and thus to challenge the oligopolistic condition that has characterised the rating offer to date. to all this must be added measures to overcome all the rules in european legislation which require reference to external ratings, and even more precise rules on conflict of interest and the quality of the rating produced, in addition to the rotations and civil liability already mentioned. the measure we are discussing today is therefore going in the right direction but will still require a lot of work in the implementation phase. we need to check for any unintended consequences and achieve the objectives which we have set out in the regulation which are aimed, along with many other measures which have been discussed and will be discussed in this parliament, at reforming the markets and having a more transparent, more accountable and more democratic financial system.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, in recent years the three great american sisters have been able to do as they wished, without anyone holding them accountable for any mistakes they might have made. mistakes that were many: according to some estimates, since 2008, half of the assessments have been wrong. the point is that their decisions can have a profound impact not only on markets but on the entire political and economic stability of a country. there is also a prosecutor in italy who is investigating any wrongdoing by these gentlemen. i would like to stress, however, a point which is of great concern not only to me but also to our intelligence services: china is gaining more and more ground with its rating agency, dagong, whose reference figure, i'm not in italy, is a person we all know well, the former president of the european commission romano prodi; commissioner barnier will also know him. i would not like us to jump from the frying pan to the fire, because the chinese worry me much more than the americans, because they have specific interests and great financial availability. perhaps it is time for europe to wake up and not be late in such a sensitive and strategic area.

debate stems from a real need in the real economy. while growth is still sluggish and unemployment high, we have seen a certain calming of the markets recently. this has helped to restore confidence it is indispensable that the risks of moral hazard are addressed first. therefore, a further reinforced economic governance is necessary. this should involve enhanced budgetary surveillance and
