in writing. - i support the proposal for a european parliament and council directive on the transparency of measures regulating the pricing of medicinal products for human use and their inclusion in public insurance schemes. i am of the opinion that the general objective of this proposal should be to update the existing legislative framework in order to clarify the procedural obligations of the member states, to ensure the proper functioning of the single market and the effectiveness of internal market legislation, to avoid delays in decisions on pricing and reimbursement and to prevent the emergence of barriers to trade in medicinal products. instead, minimum procedural requirements should ensure legal certainty and transparency for the competent national authorities, promote the production of medicinal products, the entry of generic medicinal products onto the market, and encourage research and development of new medicinal products, with the ultimate aim of facilitating access to affordable care for all patients in europe.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, today's vote on the reform of the common fisheries policy is a historic vote. the failed policy of overfishing over the last 40 years has threatened the biodiversity of our seas and made our fishermen unemployed or dependent on subsidies, and with the decline of fish stocks europe is now forced to import 66% of the fish it consumes. if we really want to give our seas a future, allow fish stocks to recover and guarantee a concrete future for european fishermen, we must reverse course. by 2015, overfishing must be converted to ecologically sustainable fishing. european subsidies will have to be conditional on compliance with the new rules and coastal and selective fishing will receive special support. the multiannual management plans and the possibility of establishing a network of reserves where all fishing activities are prohibited are therefore welcome in order to repopulate our seas. the ban on discarding dead fish, which results in the waste of 1.7 million tonnes of dead fish in europe every year, must be strengthened by the obligation to land all catches, without exception. the only future for european fisheries is to achieve ecologically sustainable fisheries.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to explain my vote, almost unanimously, against this measure. i fully agree with the stated objective of this regulatory initiative to review the common fisheries policy and thus to ensure the sustainability of fisheries, to review the quota system and to rebuild fish stocks. i believe, however, that this objective is being undermined or at least undermined by the european union's attitude of being a mere soulless regulator of the processes it implements. the european union cannot ignore the economic and social implications of such radical reform. i would add that the european legislator must also realistically situate his interventions in the context to which they relate. it is impossible to imagine that the required transformations will take place overnight. for these reasons i voted in favour of mrs fraga's amendment and for these reasons i did not vote in favour of this proposal for a regulation.
in writing. − the fisheries reform aims to ensure that fisheries and aquaculture activities create sustainable environmental conditions in the long term and contribute to food security. although this is an important reform, and one that is all the more necessary given that the current legislation dates back to 2002, it should be stressed that the text voted today severely penalises operators in the sector. i voted against because i thought it was important to provide for a timetable and gradual percentages for the implementation of the landing obligation, including a study of the actual situation of discards and the impact of the landing obligation on the various fisheries. today's vote does not help to reverse the decline of the sector, which has led to a reduction in the profitability of the sector and of the fishing fleets, causing the loss of thousands of jobs.
in writing. - the common fisheries policy in europe has, over the years, failed to achieve much of its objectives. the over-exploitation of our fish stocks, the dramatic weakening of existing stocks and the importation of more than 60% of the fish products consumed on european markets give the impression of a wrong policy. the adoption of this report and the amendments which parliament has made to the commission's proposal are laying the foundations for a reversal of the trend. the introduction of maximum sustainable yield, recovery of fish stocks, marine protected areas, prohibition of discards, regionalisation of responsibilities: the commission has already proposed a number of measures to help the fishermen in the mediterranean, such as the introduction of a new system of fishing quotas for the mediterranean, the establishment of a sustainable fisheries and aquaculture policy, the protection of the great environmental resource of our seas and the guarantee of the availability of good quality food. this will be coupled with benefits for income and employment levels in the sector. this confirms the fundamental role of parliament as a co-legislator. it is hoped that this largely positive attitude will be confirmed in the discussions with the commission and the council in the coming weeks.
in writing. - the current common fisheries policy has proved to be a failure. the long-standing problems of overfishing, overcapacity, the precarious economic situation of many fisheries undertakings and the social problems associated with the decline of fisheries in coastal regions have not been solved. the new regulation has the ambitious aim of reversing the negative trend and ensuring sustainable and effective fisheries in europe. in particular, overcapacity is a problem in many european fisheries that needs to be addressed urgently. the situation also remains unsatisfactory with regard to the application of regulation (ec) no 1967/2006 to bottom trawling which, despite some commendable initiatives implemented at national level, continues to create serious problems for operators in the market segment concerned. i agree with the rapporteur that the adjustment of fishing capacity to the available fishing opportunities should be coordinated between member states and that multiannual plans should be used in order to avoid a patchwork of different national measures. finally, in order to ensure that the objectives of the common fisheries policy are achieved, i would stress the need for the commission to carry out a periodic evaluation of the measures taken at national level in this field.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the rodust report analysing the proposal for a parliament and council regulation on the common fisheries policy. the rules and operating mechanisms established for this sector in the previous programming period are outdated and far from the needs of the market and the environment. the fundamental problems of overfishing, the failure of european centralism and the crisis situation of many fisheries companies must be tackled with a new approach. to this end, i certainly welcomed the content of the regulation proposed by the european commission which aims to 'ensure that fishing and aquaculture activities create sustainable environmental conditions in the long term and contribute to the availability of food supplies', mainly affecting maximum sustainable catch, the modification of the functioning of fisheries waste and aquaculture.
in writing. - today's debate saw the adoption by a large majority of the basic regulation for the new common fisheries policy, which, if ratified by the member states, will ensure the sustainability of the sector and put an end to the discharge of fisheries products at sea. i fully agree with the need to ensure the sustainability of the fisheries themselves, to review the quota system and to restore fish stocks. i think that the objective is to be shared, but i do not think that the adoption of this regulation takes account of the economic and social consequences of this reform. the european union today has shown an attitude that is out of touch with reality, because it is impossible to think that the changes required will take place overnight. for these reasons i have accepted the almost isolated position of opposition and have not voted in favour of the regulation.
in writing. - a substantial reform of the common fisheries policy is becoming increasingly necessary and urgent. the long-standing problems (overfishing, overcapacity, the precarious economic situation of many fisheries undertakings, social problems linked to the decline of fisheries in many coastal regions) have not been solved. the new basic regulation must therefore constitute an ambitious pillar to reverse the ongoing negative trend and ensure sustainable and effective fisheries in europe. in order to further increase consistency and ensure that the objectives set are achieved, we believe it is necessary for the commission to periodically assess the measures taken at national level. the advisory bodies should also be consulted on the introduction of the landing obligation and, before its entry into force, should make proposals for the development of a fully documented fishery. they should also make proposals for derogations for fish with a high survival probability. these proposals must of course be subject to subsequent scientific verification.
in writing. - it is undeniable that the common fisheries policy pursued by the european union has so far proved to be a failure. reform was therefore necessary and the report adopted today is going in that direction. european seas have seen fish stocks decline dramatically in recent years, with the risk that imports from outside the eu will have to be relied on more and more. in addition, fishing has shown a declining profitability, with the risk that fewer and fewer people will be engaged in this type of activity which has its great economic and commercial importance, which unfortunately is often not valued. i am pleased that the reform of the cfp has given due weight to small-scale fishing, which is a valuable source of livelihood for many families and which has been too often neglected in recent years in favour of large fleets of fishing vessels. i hope that fishing will gain a new impetus, because for many sea-faring communities it is an essential activity with significant, and we hope increasing, economic and employment implications.
in writing. − the reform of the common fisheries policy is a priority for the european union as a whole. from 2014 it will be easier to plan for a sustainable development of the sector that will end the dumping of so-called 'waste' at sea. intensive fishing practices will now be countered by new rules which will take into account the reproduction rates of the different species, bringing fishing back to a more qualitative and sustainable dimension.
in writing. − the process of reforming the common fisheries policy (cfp) is a priority for italy and it is hoped that it will be adopted by the end of 2013. i voted in favour because the commission's proposal is in the interests of our country. we are particularly committed to protecting small-scale fisheries, a concept which has been defined in a uniform way at european level and which aims to enhance the specific character of the mediterranean basin. the united kingdom, for example, also recognized at the fisheries council on 28 january the need to deal with these particular situations using different methods. this reform is aimed primarily at fishermen, the main actors who have to bear the social and economic costs of implementing the new european fisheries policy. this reform must aim to exploit the potential of the sector as much as possible.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of the report and i think it is an important achievement for our parliament. the fight against noise pollution is a goal that cannot be left unfulfilled, and yet this goal can only be fully achieved if we make it compatible with the duty to make our society and our world more equal for all, less unequal. i have taken up with the majority of my colleagues in this parliament the question of the protection of the rights and the free movement of blind and partially sighted persons, which we have undertaken to guarantee by signing, among other things, the relevant un convention. fortunately, an amendment was adopted and a neglect on the part of parliament and the european institutions to guarantee fundamental rights was avoided. i believe that we have made a step forward with this measure, but i agree with the objections made by mrs le brun that in future, in relation to these policies, we will have to pay more attention to protecting the interests of small businesses as well and regulate economic sectors in such a way as not to create imbalances and to always give the big companies an advantage.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the proposal provides for the introduction of a new test method for measuring the noise level of motor vehicles and new noise limit values for several categories. at such a bad time for the car market in europe, there was absolutely no need to produce a further regulation which would impose further burdens on motor vehicle manufacturers. the measure, already bad in its origins for an economy in crisis, was further aggravated by an amendment proposed by the left and approved by a narrow margin in the envi committee. the text that came out of the committee was so negative that the rapporteur, mr ouzký, had voted against it. the house then tabled amendments to bring the regulation back into line. this morning those amendments were voted in favour and so, consequently, our vote was in favour too.
in writing. the commission's proposal for a regulation on the noise level of motor vehicles has the main objective of protecting public health and the environment by means of measures to reduce the noise level of motor vehicles. it provides for the introduction of a new test method for measuring the sound level of motor vehicles and new noise limit values for different categories of light, medium and heavy vehicles. while i welcome the general thrust of the proposal as an important step in countering the effects on public health and the environment of noise emissions from motor vehicles, i do not think it pays sufficient attention to consumer information on the noise level of motor vehicles. i therefore agree with the rapporteur on the introduction of a vehicle noise labelling system which promotes low-noise vehicles and allows consumers to make an informed choice before buying a vehicle. i would draw the commission's attention to the need to update the technical requirements governing methods of measuring the sound levels of motor vehicles in order to adapt the proposal to technical developments in test procedures and to improve the general applicability of the requirements.
in writing. - we pay attention to technical additions and adjustments to encourage the manufacture of vehicles with lower noise levels. this can make the industry more competitive and high-level but could mean additional burdens and costs for the automotive industries especially who are experiencing a time of crisis. noise is the consequence of many factors, machines cannot be the only ones to blame. there is no doubt that the health of the citizens comes first and it is our duty to improve their quality of life, but we must be careful about technical aspects, as they could have consequences in terms of employment in europe.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mrs liotard's report because i believe that it sets out some important initiatives to combat the effects of noise emissions from motor vehicles on public health and the environment. in detail, the problems related to the noise level of motor vehicles are brought under the magnifying glass, making consumers aware and informed as regards the possibility of purchasing motor vehicles with a low noise emission level. i also find the proposal to introduce a system of labelling of vehicle noise emissions, aimed at promoting low-noise vehicle types, interesting.
in writing. - in our cities, noise pollution caused by normal daily traffic has reached levels that are now very difficult to sustain and it is therefore right that proposals are put forward to reduce this type of pollution as well. the text voted on today can be considered a good compromise, since it has succeeded in eliminating some ultra-environmental excesses which could have caused considerable damage to motor vehicle manufacturers, who are already not operating in optimum conditions at this time. the right balance must always be struck between respect for the environment and health and the protection of industries and workers. the case of the taranto ilva that has emerged in recent months is perhaps the most striking example, but there are often similar situations and this, with the appropriate comparisons, could be one of them. as vice-president of the disability intergroup in this parliament i am also particularly pleased that an amendment supported by the italian blind and visually impaired union has been included in the report. protecting the autonomy and safety of travel for visually impaired people is undoubtedly of paramount importance.
in writing. - we voted today in strasbourg on the dossier by mr ouzký. the draft law proposes to introduce new noise limits gradually within six (for the type approval of new vehicle types) and eight years (for the registration, sale and entry into service of new vehicles) from the entry into force of the legislation. the limit for standard cars will be reduced from 74 db to 68 db. the most powerful vehicles will have a margin of up to 2 to 6 decibels more. the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to carcinogens at work. the fact remains, however, that vehicle noise is also caused by asphalt, tyres and aerodynamics. it also proposes to introduce a system of labelling for new cars to inform consumers about noise levels. similar labels are already used for fuel consumption, tyre noise and co2 emissions.
in writing. - i believe that limits on car noise should be lowered to protect public health. today, in fact, numerous scientific studies show that prolonged exposure to high levels of noise pollution can limit the functioning of internal organs, facilitating the onset of diseases such as cardiovascular diseases. similarly, there is a need to inform consumers about the noise levels of cars, for example by making hybrid and electric vehicles more audible for better protection of pedestrians.
in writing. - i supported the proposal for a regulation on the noise level of motor vehicles because i believe that it has focused on the objective of finding the right balance between respect for the environment and the health of european citizens on the one hand and the protection of the internal market in motor vehicles and the interests of european industry on the other, particularly at this time of crisis for the whole sector. as regards the noise level of motor vehicles, we have been engaged in a tough negotiation on the limits, checks and timetables of the original european commission proposal. these were too costly for the undertakings and did not take due account of the resources and time available to them. italy has the support of other member states, including germany, in its willingness to favour businesses in a gradual and reasonable transition to the new legislation.
in writing. − traffic noise affects the health and wellbeing of european citizens and the european commission has therefore put forward a proposal for a regulation aimed at reducing noise emissions from motor vehicles by around 25%. this proposal provides for a very ambitious and gradual reduction in noise emissions, which in some cases would create problems for the companies in the sector concerned to implement within the time limits. i would therefore have suggested a slight reduction in the proposed limit values, even if i voted in favour, since the health of european citizens must be protected at all times and in all circumstances. i also support an integrated approach which can provide a combination of vehicle noise limits, effective traffic management, speed limits, better road surfaces, more efficient tyres and proper driving behaviour.
in writing. − the global financial crisis provoked a marked deterioration in economic and social conditions in several member states. nevertheless it is essential that member states with significant economic challenges retain the capacity to handle the tasks related to management of migration flows. therefore it is in the interest of all member states that the commitments made with regards to migration are not compromised as a result of economic difficulties. thus, we support the commission proposal to increase the co-financing rate of the european refugee fund, the european return fund and the european fund for the integration of third-country nationals for member states experiencing serious financial stability difficulties. the proposal is also an expression of solidarity between member states when it comes to the management of migration flows.
in writing. − in view of the current economic and financial crisis, a rapid response is increasingly needed to counter the effects of the crisis on the economy as a whole, both at european and national level. the commission is therefore proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the following areas: for some member states, the public debt deficit threatens economic growth and a desirable recovery as soon as possible. in order to facilitate the management of union funding in the areas covered by the european refugee fund, the european return fund and the european fund for the integration of third-country nationals, it is appropriate to allow for an increase of 20% in the eu co-financing rate, as provided for in the text which i voted in favour of.
in writing. - the phenomenon of migration flows in europe is not evenly distributed. effective management of migration flows is very important for the whole of the european union. the failure of a member state to ensure efficient management of migration flows not only affects the country concerned, but also the rest of the member states. it is in the interest of all member states to ensure that the commitments they have made in the field of migration are not affected by the economic difficulties of some of them. efficient systems for monitoring and evaluating the use of resources, with efficient and continuous monitoring, are therefore necessary. since the cofinancing conditions have already been amended to a similar extent and approved for several other funds (e.g. cohesion fund, fisheries fund, agriculture fund, etc.), i think it is reasonable that the migration funds should also be subject to similar amendments.
in writing. − in many member states, the consequences of the economic and financial crisis have had a negative impact on public finances and have resulted in difficulties in meeting the co-financing requirements linked to eu funds. the commission has therefore proposed to increase the co-financing rates for member states benefiting from a financial support mechanism. i believe that effective management of migration flows is in the interest of the whole union. the failure of a country to ensure an efficient management of migration flows not only affects that country but also the other member states. it is therefore essential that member states in serious economic difficulties are still able to carry out the activities related to the management of migration flows. given that the increase in cofinancing rates is a temporary measure, i welcome the proposal to increase the cofinancing rate for member states receiving financial support, thereby creating a solidarity mechanism between member states in the management of migration flows. efficient systems for monitoring the use of resources are essential to avoid, as has already happened, that the misuse of funds in the member states causes difficulties in absorbing european funds.
in writing. − the aim of this report is to approve a proposal from the european commission to increase the possibility of eu co-financing for the external borders fund for member states in financial difficulty. i think this is a good measure, because the european union should be doing more to protect our external borders. we cannot leave a few member states alone to deal with and receive large numbers of migrants. we often talk about european solidarity, sometimes inadequately. this seems to me to be a real area where this principle should really apply. the arab spring uprisings of 2011, the consequences of which are still far from being fully understood, for example, led thousands of north africans to seek refuge in italy. there has been no concrete support from europe, but rather only ingenuous criticism of the way the situation has been handled. the european union must therefore take responsibility for better management of the external borders, not just in words but in concrete actions and initiatives.
in writing. - i gave a favourable opinion on the proposal for a european parliament and council decision amending decision no 574/2007/ec in order to increase the co-financing rate of the external borders fund for certain member states experiencing or threatened with serious difficulties in financial stability. today, due to the serious economic situation, some member states have encountered difficulties in meeting the co-financing requirements linked to eu funds, which has also been evident with regard to the funds related to the general programme 'solidarity and management of migration flows'. the aim of the proposal is to increase the union co-financing rate by 20 percentage points, thereby reducing the co-financing needs of the member state concerned. this would bring the co-financing rate to 70%, which could be increased to 95% for projects concerning specific priorities and member states benefiting from the cohesion fund. effective management of migration flows is very important for the whole of the european union. the failure of a member state to ensure efficient management of migration flows not only affects the country concerned, but also many other member states
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, overcapacity is not only destroying the biodiversity of our seas, it is also severely reducing any future prospects for the fishermen of the union. the regulation on the protection of juveniles is certainly an effective instrument if we really want to allow fish stocks to recover. by adopting specific measures to determine the type of gear used, the mesh size of the nets, the respect of the quotas allowed and the times during which fishing is allowed, we can and must prevent the continued fishing of the young fish that must be allowed to grow to repopulate our seas. without these measures and without strict controls, our sea has no future. unfortunately, in many member states, and particularly in italy, not a day goes by without the coast guard registering serious breaches of the regulation on the protection of juveniles. the european fisheries sector can only survive if it becomes truly sustainable.
in writing. − the adoption of these measures in conjunction with the vote on the new regulation on the common fisheries policy represents an integrated approach, widely shared in parliament, to a subject which is fundamental to the future sustainability of the union's fisheries resources. pending the adoption of a regionalised framework of technical measures in accordance with the common fisheries policy, this regulation will certainly be able to contribute to the satisfactory achievement of the objectives of the cfp.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the gallagher report on the amendment of council regulation (ec) no 850/98 for the conservation of fishery resources through technical measures for the protection of juveniles of marine organisms and repealing council regulation (ec) no 1288/2009. the technical measures shall lay down rules on fishing zones, the gear used in respect of the permitted quantities, the minimum mesh size of nets, the zones and the periods of prohibition. the text proposes a transitional extension of the rules on these measures, which will remain valid until a framework of technical measures in line with the new common fisheries policy is adopted, and an update of them following the opinion of the scientific, technical and economic committee for fisheries.
in writing. − i am in favour of the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending council regulation (ec) no 850/98 for the conservation of fishery resources through technical measures for the protection of juveniles and repealing council regulation (ec) no 1288/2009, as technical conservation measures are standards that fishermen throughout the european union are required to comply with on a daily basis in their fishing trips to ensure that fishing is always sustainable, regardless of how and where it is carried out. these measures concern, inter alia, minimum landing sizes, minimum mesh size of nets, no-take zones and periods, limitation of by-catches, criteria for the use of more selective fishing gear and measures to protect the marine environment, thus having a significant impact on the achievement of the objectives of the common fisheries policy (cfp). i therefore fully recognize the need for technical measures to ensure the sustainable exploitation of fish stocks and the conservation of ecosystems. i believe that european fishermen need more legal clarity.
in writing. the commissioner also stressed that the eu's policy on fisheries was not a one-size-fits-all approach, but rather a policy of cooperation between the member states and the commission. while i strongly recognise the need to respect the marine environment, i believe it would be more appropriate to bring the rate of discard from the 3% proposed in the report to the 10% proposed by the ppe group, to protect operators in the sector who, in some cases, risk not seeing their interests safeguarded.
in writing. − i voted for this resolution because violence against women remains one of the most serious human rights violations present in every country of the world. many societies where women and men are not ensured equal rights perpetuate a structural form of violence against women. we need to bear in mind that all forms of gender-based violence, physical, sexual or psychological, need to be tackled. to put an end to the violence against women requires international cooperation and action, firm commitment from political leaders at all levels, as well as more substantial levels of financing. for these reasons, with this resolution we urge the commission to propose an eu strategy against violence against women, including a directive laying down minimum standards of protection. in addition we ask the eu external action service to ensure that the human rights of women and girls are protected and advanced in all actions and dialogues in which the service is involved.
in writing. - violence against women remains one of the most serious scourges in european societies and in the world. it affects girls and women in a dramatic way and across cultures, religions, social classes, economic situations and nationalities. the political responsibilities arising from this phenomenon, which shows no sign of abating, are heavy and call into question all institutional levels. the responses and initiatives so far have proved to be wholly inadequate. the union and the member states must make every effort to change their political behaviour as soon as possible, both within the union and in their relations with third countries. we need more support for local and international ngos and all those working for women at risk of or victims of violence. the union and the member states are also responsible for defining stringent policies and allocating more resources to programmes, projects and initiatives to support any useful action in this area. the ratification of the council of europe convention on preventing and combating violence against women can no longer be postponed. it is the task of the union to urge the member states to do so.
in writing. - i wanted to support this resolution so that the european union too could send a strong signal to try to prevent and eliminate all forms of violence against women, also in view of the 57th session of the united nations commission on the status of women which is to be held at the beginning of march. in fact, millions of women and girls are still victims of violence every day and in every part of the world. we are talking about the mutilation of the genitals in africa, the rape in india, and all the other things that are happening in italy and europe. i am pleased that the text refers to the need for the status of women to be considered as one of the essential values in the eu's external action, to which the european external action service must pay the utmost attention. of course, action must also be taken within the union, and quickly, and the member states must make efforts to prevent any possible manifestation of violence against women. it is certainly not easy, considering also the fact that a great deal of violence takes place within the walls of the home, but action must be continuous and unceasing, to put an end to these heinous crimes.
in writing. - it is not easy to reach agreement on the conjugacy of violence against women. there is physical violence that must be condemned at all times and in all circumstances. there is social violence: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to finance the necessary measures to combat poverty. and there is violence that comes from certain tribal cultures that force girls to undergo horrendous genital mutilation. i believe we cannot discriminate and select the form of violence that is most convenient for us. all forms of violence must be condemned without appeal, without discount, without justification or false remorse. rape is unprecedented violence, prostitution is an unforgivable crime, mutilation is barbaric brutality, a lower wage is an unacceptable abuse, covering up against one's will is a coercion that does not respect the dignity of women, preventing education is criminal tyranny. and to stop the birth of daughters against the will of the mother, what form of violence is that? is it permissible to speak of violence, of extreme violence, in these cases? i support the resolution in the hope that the un committee will take account of all the violence against "half of the sky".
in writing. - i give my vote in favour of the european parliament resolution on the 57th session of the united nations commission on the status of women (csw): prevention and elimination of all forms of violence against women and girls. violence against women and girls is one of the most serious and widespread structural human rights violations worldwide. it is a phenomenon that involves victims and perpetrators of all ages, educational levels, incomes and social positions and is both a consequence and a cause of inequality between women and men. to eradicate this scourge, more international cooperation and action, a strong commitment from policy makers at all levels, and more appropriate funding are needed. for these reasons, i hope that this proposal will urge the eu and its member states to review the policies, programmes and resources available to tackle the problem of violence inside and outside the eu and to strengthen their strategy with updated tools and ambitious targets.
in writing. - the proposal to prevent and eliminate all forms of violence against women and girls is one with which i fully agree. violence against women persists in all countries of the world as the most widespread violation of human rights worldwide. it is a phenomenon that involves victims and perpetrators of all ages, educational levels, income and social status, and is both a consequence and a cause of inequality between women and men with significant economic and social costs, limiting and undermining the economic growth and development of the countries concerned. the eu and its member states are therefore required to increase the allocation of funds to eradicate violence against women and girls globally. the eu must therefore continue to pursue and support a global awareness-raising campaign to prevent violence against women and girls in order to take further steps to make our communities and countries safe, ensuring full respect for the human rights of women and girls worldwide.

president-in-office of the council. − mr president, i would like to thank the honourable members for their contribution to this very important debate. i agree with the many contributions which said that this is an urgent matter and that we have to address it as such, and in a coherent and effective manner. that is one of the biggest global challenges that we face, but it is one that the eu and our member states can take the lead on in shaping a new legally binding agreement for all. that is our clear objective. that is the objective of the irish presidency and it is the objective of all of the european institutions. listening to the comments here, all our institutions share that ambition to take real action which can embrace, and indeed champion, the move to a low-carbon and more sustainable economy. that is what we have to work towards. each of us has opportunities to actively engage and to promote more concerted and ambitious action by other countries besides the european union. i would encourage all of you to continue to speak to your counterparts and to try to build momentum towards 2015, which is what we will be doing. i will address a number of points that were specifically made and the questions asked. mr eickhout asked what the irish presidency is doing about leading on the development of a 2030 target. as i said in my introduction, as the presidency we are working closely with the commission. we are facilitating a debate at ministerial level at the forthcoming informal council meeting in april, which will involve both energy and environment ministers. this will make an important contribution to driving the debate forward. on the issue of climate finance, which was raised by a number of contributors, the irish presidency intends to move forward the analysis, and indeed the debate, on climate finance, especially in relation to future finance flows. the eu has fully met its fast-start finance contribution of over eur 7 billion, and in doha countries have made pledges over eur 5 billion for 2013 and beyond. we want to make further progress and to ensure that we deliver effective financial assistance to the least-developed countries. that work is ongoing and we will continue it. the irish presidency is working collaboratively with all member states, including poland, and with our other partners through the unfccc groupings, in order to further clarify and to better understand our respective positions and to find ways to move closer to an agreed solution. that is the process. it is a process of achieving consensus and of moving together and finding ways in which we can move forward. that is precisely the role of us as presidency and it is precisely what we are trying to do in the council. in response to mr gerbrandy’s question, the irish presidency will do its utmost to engage with parliament. we will also ensure that the key messages which have been sent here this evening will be communicated back to council and to member states. there are a just a few other points which were raised and which i would like to address. ms anderson suggested that the irish presidency should work to identify clear milestones and targets. we will do that, but it is not just the irish presidency. it is important that we do this in a coherent fashion. it is the reason why we have trio presidencies now. we are working very closely with the lithuanian and the greek presidencies – the future presidencies – in order to identify those milestones. we are doing that with the very important assistance of, and stimulation from, the european commission. it is our common objective to get an agreement by 2015. i agree with mr arsenis that we need to accelerate our work and develop clear targets and milestones, not just for the eu and its member states but in partnership with our allies. it is very important that we build alliances and that we reach out to other groupings, regions and countries to build partnerships and to ensure that our position is most effective. the irish presidency, and the entire council, recognises that we cannot simply wait for a 2020 climate-effective world. under the adp we are prioritising actions to improve emissions mitigation now. a number of those steps have already been highlighted by the commissioner, and i do not propose to go over them again. i would simply say in conclusion member of the commission. − mr president, the european legal culture is made up of a diversity of legal systems that are progressively brought closer to each other. europe’s legal diversity is a source of strength. article 67 of the treaty makes it clear that respect for the different legal systems and traditions of the member states underpins the union’s area of justice. through more cooperation between legal practitioners in the different member states, exchanges of experience and judicial training, we can promote the rule of law and strengthen the mutual trust between these different legal systems. we can indeed bring these different legal cultures together without eliminating the differences. european judicial training is a crucial tool to achieve that goal. legal practitioners must have a good knowledge of eu law. they must have trust in the different national judicial systems in order to apply european law correctly all over the european union. as the eu’s legal order interacts with diverse national legal traditions and systems often built upon continual layers of history, this requires first of all well-informed and well-trained legal practitioners. in september 2011, the commission set out its objective to enable half of the legal practitioners in the european union to participate in european judicial training activities by 2020. this involves the use of all available resources at local, national and european level. since 2011 the commission has been taking action with national authorities and with the support of the european networks such as the european judicial training network, the european law academy and the european law institute. the commission values the fact that parliament shares the commission’s vision and ambition on this subject. as regards the specific questions i would like to highlight the following. first, regarding the length of time taken to award contracts. there have not been any unusual delays in the implementation of the pilot project. the pilot project was published on time, applicants were given the usual deadlines and three out of the four contracts are in the process of being signed this month. as regards the second question on how account is taken of the conference of coordinators of european law, representatives of the commission were present at the conference in the hague last september. we welcomed the debate on having eu law court coordinators within the national court structure. however, we need to keep in mind that organisation of the judiciaries is a matter for member states alone. we should also avoid duplication of tasks with the established european judicial networks in civil and commercial as well as in criminal matters. regarding the third question about investment in modern tools, the commission continues to develop the european e-justice portal to give citizens and legal practitioners access to information. the judicial training section of the portal is being developed. it will serve as a single entry point for trainers and legal practitioners looking for training content. the first training content will be available online in a matter of weeks. the commission is also willing to support financially the development of high quality e-learning. the development of two training models on eu cross-border family law including e-learning courses has been tendered as part of a pilot project in 2012. e-learning courses may be helpful in certain areas but they cannot replace personal contacts between legal practitioners from different jurisdictions. personal contact is necessary to build mutual trust and to exchange ideas. furthermore, e-learning tools are only one possible way of addressing the time restrictions preventing legal professionals from participating more often in exchanges and specific training. however, time restrictions would have less impact if continuous training were to be duly taken into account by the member states when calculating the workload of judges and prosecutors. regarding the fourth question on broadening the scope, the commission communication of september 2011 makes it clear that it intends to target training activities at all legal practitioners. this includes judges, prosecutors, court staff, lawyers and other legal professions. the commission also supports future knowledge partnerships between universities, judicial schools and bar associations to develop innovative training solutions. however, the eu has no competence to regulate the curriculum and teaching of law at european universities.

the rapporteur. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, in thanking my shadow colleagues who have helped me to prepare this report, let me briefly outline the main points of the report. firstly, and this is the reason for the only amendment in the report, when the report was first drafted we wanted the european investment bank to be able to count on a capital increase. the decision of the 27 member states a few weeks ago to approve this eur 10 billion increase in the capital of the eib was therefore welcomed. this capital increase is essential for the maintenance of the triple a, given that the majority of investors in eib securities require it. the eib is expected to make available up to eur 60 billion more for eib lending in the period 2013-2015, for a total of eur 180 billion of investment, thanks to leverage. to ensure the best possible functioning of the eib's leverage, new financial instruments based on the effective combination of the resources of the eu budget and the eib's high lending capacity must also be designed and implemented rapidly. the pilot phase of project bonds, which has just started, will be followed up with interest and will give us the opportunity to see the first results at the end of 2013. to enable the development of new joint eu-eib financial instruments, a new framework must be established which clearly allocates tasks between the institutions involved, ensures transparency and flexibility and draws resources from the public and private sectors. in addition, it is essential to avoid excessive bureaucratic constraints for the institutions managing the funds, the intermediaries and the final beneficiaries. in short, the eib must be able, also by clearly defining its objectives and control criteria, to preserve its independence in the selection of projects in order to ensure a sustainable use of its resources. the eib must also ensure greater transparency by providing more data on the loans granted and on controls, in particular on beneficiaries and intermediaries in third countries. the eib's consultancy activities were also highlighted. sometimes the problem is not access to finance but the lack of real managerial and administrative capacity of the project beneficiaries, which slows down development. the eib should continue to focus on smes within the european union, but should further develop microfinance instruments and expand the range of credit institutions involved in sme financing, such as non-conventional financial intermediaries. at a time of welfare cuts, the report encourages the eib to support the social economy, which is already contributing to welfare and job creation through tailor-made loans and guarantee schemes that are as flexible as possible in terms of size and rules, also taking into account possible synergies with the social business initiative. in addition, new instruments should be developed for the cultural, creative and training sectors, which have been hit hard by the financial crisis. the eib is in the difficult position of having to make do in those areas where the cuts imposed on the national governments by tightened budgetary discipline, but also by the european union itself, have been felt the most, if we consider the tough debate on the multiannual financial framework in these days. the report also mentions the european investment bank's investments in research and innovation, agricultural policy, energy efficiency and resources, as well as synergies with the european union for programmes such as the cap, horizon 2020 and the structural funds. outside the european union, the report focuses on investments in the mediterranean and the candidate countries. the eib is called upon to play its part by financing investment in infrastructure and small and medium-sized enterprises and by combating climate change, mainly to support the progress of political and economic reforms. the important thing is that it should also maintain its role as the union's bank in its external activities, in close coordination with the other institutions and the european external action service, and that it should focus on the areas and areas with the greatest impact, such as the enlargement and neighbourhood countries. the report also proposes that the eib should play a special role as the european bank and as a natural partner of the european community and the external action service in supporting the european union's external policy objectives.

president of the european investment bank. - the mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the european parliament has been a great help to us. i am grateful for this meeting in the european parliament, and questions. this was one of the main issues i took on my shoulders when i came to this bank, because we are under particular scrutiny from the public and the european institutions, including the european parliament. in this context the question of supervision is very relevant. of course it is necessary to be supervised and to be under strict control. now there's a history to it, because there's no textbook on the supervision of international financial institutions. we are an international financial institution, a bank and a political institution at the same time. this is why the bank, years ago - years before i started there - mr audy - put forward the proposal for the eib to be under the supervision of the european central bank, long before anyone would think of giving the banking supervision to the european central bank. at that time the idea was rejected. this is why we voluntarily went under the umbrella of the central bank of luxembourg. this is why we are ready to think about all kinds of new developments in this field, and we are going to see the new regulation very soon and we will be ready to be part of that european system. of course an international financial institution like ours has specifics which have to be addressed, but we are ready to be a transparent, accountable, responsible bank of the european union vis-à-vis you, vis-à-vis the european court of auditors and of course the european court of justice and of course vis-à-vis the banking supervision. in this context, the question of the bank's capital has been raised. let us understand the role of the bank correctly. since the treaty of rome, the bank's role has been to provide, in particular, long-term financing for projects in the interests of the citizens of the european union which would not otherwise be able to be financed, in compliance with the targets and objectives set by the treaty and by the decisions of the european council. that is what our job is, and for that purpose the role of the bank is to mobilize money on the international capital markets. what we lend to our clients is not these ten billion additional euros which we have just got from the member states; it is the money that we raise on the international capital markets. last year it was eur 70 billion, this year much more. that means we need the trust and confidence of the participants in the international capital markets. triple-a is not a fetish, it is not an objective in itself but it is one of the keys for gaining and retaining the confidence of the participants in the international capital markets. this is why we consider triple-a very important, and this is why we consider the quality of our projects decisive. if we stint on the quality of a project then the business model of this bank is at risk, and this is what we're not going to do. credit bonds are currently a very important initiative. we are addressing them with enthusiasm and resolve. but let us be clear: they are one more instrument in the toolbox which we, you, the commission and the council have. this new instrument must stand the test of the market, because it is private investors at the other kinds of instruments that we use. we are doing the very best at the bank in order to make this new instrument a success. on smes: at the outset, smes were not the bank's core idea. but we have separate talk about this. over the course of the bank's history it has not been part of our core business, but for a public bank which serves the objectives of the european union, it is important to in writing. − demographic change is posing a number of challenges to the european union, including the gradual increase in the population over 65: more than 87 million people. it is important to encourage synergy between public institutions at european, national and territorial level to promote measures that enable healthy ageing for all. prevention and information, along with access to quality healthcare, are essential elements in enabling older people to remain as independent and healthy as possible. active ageing must be a priority for all member states and it is necessary to ensure that older people can play an active role in society, for example by staying longer in the labour market and avoiding social exclusion.
in writing. - i supported the report by mrs liotard on the european innovation partnership in the field of active and healthy ageing. the demographic transition will lead to 35% of the european population being over 60 by 2050, with 80% of the population concentrated in urban areas. the aim is to create living environments that ensure good ageing and good health, not only in terms of disease-free living but also in terms of physical, mental and social well-being. i believe that the involvement of regional and local policy-makers in decision-making processes is essential to the achievement of these objectives.
in writing. − the ageing of the eu population is proceeding rapidly and is an issue to which particular attention should be paid. by 2060, the population aged over 65 will have risen from 85 million in 2008 to 151 million, with a birth rate that is increasing but decreasing. these figures provide the tools and the keys to legislative measures and choices to innovate best practices aimed at innovation in active and healthy ageing. moreover, this report places a strong emphasis on the close relationship between active ageing and the environment and the social and urban context in which it matures, an essential condition to be taken into account when adopting such measures.
in writing. - i welcome the report in question because better ageing brings benefits to citizens and less cost to the public health system. in particular, all early diagnosis and prevention activities from birth are essential to reduce the negative impacts of diseases and pathologies. proper and non-invasive information campaigns, anti-smoking, anti-obesity, promotion of physical activity and better eating habits can lead to an extension of healthy life. the elderly population, which often lives in isolated settings, such as mountain areas or small towns, must have the same opportunities as those living in large urban centres. distance from hospitals or social care centres must be compensated by better home care and e-health services. the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of the health of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos at work is a very good one. i am sorry that the rapporteur, who is completely unaware of the measure in question, is giving immigration a beneficial and indispensable role.
in writing. - i agree with the motion for a resolution by parliament on innovation in active ageing and good health. the elderly are the fastest growing age group in europe and infrastructure, services and tools to respond to this social transition need to be developed as quickly as possible. the european union is undergoing an unprecedented demographic transition. its population is aging rapidly, with the number of people over 65 years old rising from 85 million in 2008 to 151 million by 2060. moreover, while in 2010 the population aged over 60 was 20%, by 2050 it will reach at least 35%. i am convinced that a clear and unambiguous strategy - with social objectives that allow the role of older people and the value of their experience and contribution to society and the economy to be formally promoted and recognised, eliminating any stigmatisation and discrimination - is a necessary and indispensable prerequisite for the eu.
in writing. the report by mrs hohlmeier analyses parliament's resolution on the general guidelines for the 2014 budgetary procedure. the text provides guidelines indicating areas where the quality of spending could still be improved and where substantial budgetary savings could be achieved. the committee also calls for the commission to take the necessary steps to ensure that the budgetary authority is able to meet its obligations under the treaty. i therefore voted in favour of the report.
in writing. the guidelines just voted provide for a commitment by the european parliament and the other institutions to freeze administrative and operating expenditure, showing awareness of the difficult economic and budgetary situation of the member states, without, however, compromising the quality of the institutions' activities, compliance with legal obligations and the imperative to invest in development. as the european parliament, we intend to continue in the direction already taken with the last budgets, also foreseeing for 2014 a reduction in real terms of the budget of the european parliament, through a series of measures aimed at achieving greater efficiency, without compromising legislative excellence and the quality of working conditions. in particular, some cuts were made in budget lines for members' travel, a reduction in the duration and number of missions, increased use of videoconferencing and optimisation of translation and interpretation services. as for the other institutions, we are aware of the limited room for manoeuvre they enjoy in this year's budget, but we believe that the resources allocated are in most cases sufficient to allow the proper and effective execution of their activities.
in writing. the eu budget represents only 2% of total european public expenditure. however, the european institutions must demonstrate that this budget is able to add value to national public spending by initiating, supporting and complementing investment in those policies which are the basis of the recipe for restarting growth. austerity is necessary for the administrative expenditure of the european institutions. the structural and organisational reforms aimed at achieving greater efficiency must be pursued. the increased cooperation between the institutions to optimise costs, the freezing of all members' allowances at 2011 levels and the suspension of the indexation of staff mission allowances are concrete examples of the efforts made. i think that continuing along this rigorous line is a test of credibility.
in writing. - i am in full agreement with the freezing of the european institutions' expenditure, although i would have preferred a reduction. however, care must also be taken in this area not to make indiscriminate cuts, otherwise the work of important bodies, with the european parliament at the forefront, may be affected. in recent years we have always followed this trend, namely no increase in administrative expenditure, with reductions where possible. but it is useless to continue to refuse to take seriously what is the real waste of the european parliament, namely this strasbourg seat. the french president, françois hollande, also said yesterday in this house that strasbourg is untouchable, making it a supreme symbol of european history. it is an attitude which is perhaps understandable for the french, but it is far from the european spirit which he himself has evoked. if we really want to improve this european union and give it a future, we must start with the obvious critical points, and the question of the double, or even triple, seat of parliament is one of them, and must therefore be tackled as soon as possible. i hope therefore that the next italian president-in-office will bring the matter to the european table to try to resolve this intolerable situation.
in writing. − to date, no agreement has been reached on the new multiannual financial framework for the period 2014-2020. the european parliament and all the institutions of the european union should, however, continue to exercise the highest degree of responsibility, control and rigor in budgetary matters. the vote therefore states that the institutions should continue to limit or freeze administrative expenditure, showing solidarity with the difficult economic and budgetary situation of the member states, without compromising the quality of the institutions' essential activities, compliance with legal obligations and the imperative to invest in development. in addition, the institutions are urged to strengthen cooperation with each other in order to share best practice where possible and where justified, and to identify possible savings through the mutualisation and sharing of human and technical resources, for example in the areas of information technology, translation, interpretation and transport services and possibly also in other areas.
in writing. the text voted today supports the limitation or freezing of the administrative budgets of the institutions, which are called upon to cooperate more closely with each other. while stressing the need for reforms, it is worth recalling that legislative excellence must be safeguarded and the institutions' room for manoeuvre guaranteed, which excessive cuts would jeopardise.
in writing. the european commission proposes a new definition of 'corporate social responsibility' recognised as the 'responsibility of enterprises for their impact on society'. this new definition means that companies must have a process in place in their core and commercial strategy which takes into account social, environmental and ethical issues, human rights and consumer demands. this report recognises the primary role of enterprises in defining and implementing actions in support of csr. in my view, businesses can contribute to the development of a social market economy and to the achievement of the europe 2020 strategy by ensuring job creation and facilitating economic recovery. i welcome the effort to strike a balance between the positions expressed by the commission in its strategy in support of corporate social responsibility and a more favourable approach towards european enterprises. in this respect, i share the rapporteur's firm opposition to the adoption of specific performance indicators which would risk leading to additional bureaucratic burdens and costs for european companies, thus penalising them in the arena of international competition.
in writing. − the report by mr baldassarre develops parliament's position on the renewed eu strategy for 2011-2014 on corporate social responsibility (csr), defined as 'the responsibility of companies for their impact on society'. the aim of the text is to ensure that companies incorporate into their core business strategy a process which integrates social, environmental and ethical issues, human rights and the demands of end consumers. the report also calls for the introduction of a european social security system for all citizens of the union. i believe that in this time of crisis european companies need short-term incentives to competitiveness and not measures which create additional costs, even if they are moderate. that is why i voted to abstain.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the positions taken by mr baldassarre in the report on corporate social responsibility, agreeing with the new definition of csr proposed by the commission, according to which companies must have a process that manages to integrate social, environmental and ethical issues, human rights and consumer concerns into their core business strategy. this requires the development of innovative solutions such as intelligent transport and eco-efficient products. concerns remain about the actual effectiveness of specific performance indicators, such as key performance indicators (kpis), which could lead to additional bureaucratic burdens and costs for firms. in line with this position, i am turning my attention to the specific needs of smes by aiming at their greater involvement in csr, stressing the need to exclude them from any measures that may entail new costs or burdens. the overall objective is to improve transparency, self-regulation processes and the market premium for csr, while taking into account its multidimensional nature. in this respect, i am opposed to 'universalist' solutions which do not take account of the specificities of the markets and the various sectors in which firms operate.
in writing. - until now, the definition of csr has been based on a voluntary approach by individual companies. being an entrepreneur meant voluntarily going beyond simple economic logic and taking into account how one's business behaviour affects the environment and in relationships with staff, the local community, business partners, customers and institutions. the revolutionary definition of csr that we are adopting today attests to its added value as a steering wheel for competitiveness, transparency and efficiency. however, this should not entail any additional costs for the companies. we are therefore paying attention to the needs of small and mediumsized enterprises, the backbone of the european and italian economic fabric. they should not be excluded from doing business but rather encouraged by tax and legal incentives as they have the ambition to set social and environmental standards. we help these companies communicate better with investors and consumers.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mr baldassarre's report because i believe that csr can find new life and new fields of application as a result of the proposals made. the belief that csr practices create added value for businesses and therefore also competitive value must be increasingly disseminated and supported by adequate information and communication investments. it is desirable to involve smes in this process, which aims to make the process of communicating the commercial behaviour of enterprises more transparent. practices in the field of social responsibility should be adequately supported and their added value should be communicated to those who implement them in a virtuous manner.
in writing. - the process of globalisation has created an increasingly attentive, informed and aware society in which companies are expected to behave responsibly. i voted in favour of this because i believe that the complementarity between business and civil society is essential. the competitiveness factor is very important. in this respect, i believe it is essential to strengthen the relationship between csr and citizens by implementing strategies that are in line with the social context in which civil society lives and that enable businesses to address social and environmental challenges. another important element is transparency. progress is needed to increase the level of trust that citizens place in business by attempting to close the gap between citizens' expectations and the actual behaviour of business. smes provide the framework for these two elements. they represent 90% of the european business community. with csr embedded in smes, it would be much easier to achieve results, as they actually operate much closer to civil society. it is therefore necessary for parliament to make this process one of its future political priorities, since the results of this process are not tangible in the short term.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the baldassarre report on corporate social responsibility because i share the new approach expressed in it, which aims to consider csr as the responsibility of companies for the impact of their actions on the society in which they operate. companies will therefore have to integrate social, environmental, ethical, respect for fundamental rights and consumer protection into their business activities. if this is achieved, it will result in a sustainable economic recovery. i also support the rapporteur's approach to allowing companies to calibrate the implementation of sustainable actions on the basis of their specific capabilities and needs. giving a range of flexibility to enterprises, especially smes, is essential so that csr does not result in increased administrative or financial burdens. finally, i share the view that excessive bonuses, liquidations and remuneration for managers, particularly where the company is in difficulty, are not compatible with socially responsible behaviour.
in writing. the concept of a 'social market economy' is a key point in guiding the political action of the european union. i supported the baldassarre report because it proposes a new definition of corporate social responsibility, one that is more sensitive to the impact of economic activity on individuals and society. it also wishes to underline the active role of enterprises in defining and implementing actions in this area. the report places particular emphasis on the role of small and medium-sized enterprises and suggests ways of involving them more in the csr framework; the specific situation of italy, which sees the contribution of smes as the main engine of its industrial development, can only benefit from these new provisions.
in writing. - i abstained on the baldassarre report because, while i agree in principle with the establishment of rules for corporate social responsibility, i do not agree with the inclusion of small and micro-enterprises among the target groups of possible future measures. i believe that in order to survive the economic and financial crisis we are experiencing, small and micro enterprises now need only genuine incentives to competitiveness, growth and development, and not other financial or management burdens.
in writing. − the report voted today supports the commission's commitment to international approaches and calls for eu-wide solutions to close existing governance gaps and improve transparency, while suggesting new ideas to promote corporate social responsibility. the european commission is proposing a new definition of csr, defined as the responsibility of enterprises for their impact on society, and in line with the new definition, enterprises must have a process that integrates social, environmental and ethical issues, human rights and consumer concerns in order to secure new jobs and facilitate the exit from the crisis.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this report because it clearly states that corporate social responsibility (csr) is indispensable to the restoration of trust in business and a sustainable economic recovery. indeed, an active awareness of social responsibility brings businesses greater social acceptance. i believe that csr policies must be respected not only by the main company but also by any subcontractors or supply chains which it may use, whether in the supply of goods, workers or services, in the eu or in a third country. we must promote a level playing field based on fair pay and decent working conditions, and guarantee trade union rights and freedoms. in particular, i support the call for csr policies to include specific measures to tackle the unlawful practice of blacklisting workers and denying them access to employment, often due to their trade union membership and activities or to their role as health and safety representatives. any enterprise that is found to be blacklisting workers or breaching human rights and labour standards should be excluded from consideration for eu grants and funding and from taking part in calls for other public procurement contracts at the eu or national level.
in writing. - i voted against mr howitt's report on corporate social responsibility (csr). although this subject has interesting implications for both workers and consumers, i do not share the approach taken by the text. the report does not provide a clear definition of csr and presents measures which, in fact, put all types of enterprises on the same level, forgetting that they constitute a heterogeneous universe. the new burdens resulting from the proposals contained in the report would inevitably fall on the shoulders of the smaller firms or those which are experiencing particularly difficult times. for all these reasons, i decided not to support the report when i voted.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the argument put forward by mr howitt in the committee on employment and social affairs on the subject of corporate social responsibility, which is the voluntary integration of environmental and social considerations into business operations, the latter therefore playing a primary role in the definition and implementation of csr support actions. he is calling for a regulation with certain minimum principles and also for the need to respect international standards. while this report supports the commission's proposal to propose a new definition of csr, which is now recognised as 'corporate responsibility for their impact on society', there are some points on which i do not agree. first of all, i do not agree with the call for more widespread use of regulatory intervention on csr issues, nor do i agree with the call for a greater legislative role for public authorities. i also do not support the call on the commission to submit a legislative proposal on the disclosure of non-financial information by companies. in conclusion, i am not even a supporter of the hope that integrated forms of reporting, which therefore include both financial and non-financial information, will become the norm in the next decade.
in writing. - i have supported mr david's report. it gives a member state the means to apply to the commission for an accelerated authorization procedure to combat vat fraud where it is sudden and causes serious damage to a particular sector.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the commission's proposal for a rapid reaction mechanism against vat fraud. the commission is proposing to introduce into its national legislation a reverse charge system, i.e. the reverse accounting mechanism, which eliminates the deduction of vat on purchases in sectors where fraud of particular gravity and size is detected. i believe that the ordinary procedures of the vat directive can be changed to allow this, but with procedural time which i consider too long in relation to the need to combat fraud quickly. it must be borne in mind that this proposal unfortunately risks introducing accounting reversal mechanisms in a sudden manner in the individual member states. this could complicate the management of vat compliance by leading to considerable costs of changing management systems, to the detriment of companies that act in a transparent and compliant manner, without harming those that set up fraudulent mechanisms. finally, i think it is appropriate to envisage more efficient mechanisms for tax cooperation between member states.
in writing. - i am in favour of the report as a whole, although there are some points which merit further consideration. i am referring in particular to the regulatory and organisational uncertainty which the reversal of burden mechanism can generate, especially for smes which are operating properly. on the other hand, we can only welcome a proposal to combat tax evasion, which must be condemned because it penalizes all others, with very high social costs. i believe that the best way to eliminate vat fraud is through greater tax cooperation between member states, possibly leading to total harmonization of rates. it is not entirely meaningful to talk about the internal market if, for example, an e-commerce company is penalized by living in a country where the rates are higher because customers are not willing to pay the vat increased by their own country. i hope that the next step in this matter will be in that direction.
in writing. - every year there is a great deal of vat fraud within the european union, and this amounts to several billion dollars in damage to both the community budget and the member states' budgets. one of the major problems in combating this phenomenon is precisely to overcome the current procedural slowdown. the instruments proposed in this report are moving in the right direction, namely by providing for a rapid action mechanism based on the reverse charge system for vat. it is also a measure which is applied at the discretion of the member states and which therefore also fully respects the principle of subsidiarity. of course this is only part of a larger programme which should redraw the way vat is collected and applied at european union level, because the current system is very complicated and has left too much room for fraud, with billions of dollars of damage being inflicted on all european citizens.
in writing. - vat fraud costs the union and member states' budgets several billion euros each year and also harms compliant companies that operate legally. in times of budgetary constraints and austerity, a rapid reaction mechanism can therefore be a valuable and effective tool for member states to combat tax fraud. however, as the rapporteur has pointed out, anti-fraud measures should not create additional burdens for serious and law-abiding companies, but should instead target those who have been guilty of serious fraud.
