in writing. − the annual growth survey is the first meeting of the european semester, which sets out the priority areas in which member states are called upon to act in the months ahead. i voted against the report because it would have been desirable to adopt a document more geared to action for growth and employment rather than to policies of austerity. the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos at work is a welcome one. it is time for eu countries to make a real commitment to cutting waste and rationalising spending and, above all, to focus available resources and policies on real and concrete measures to boost the economy.
in writing. - i did not support the ferreira report on the european semester for the coordination of economic policies: the commission shall submit to the european parliament and to the council a report on the implementation of this decision. the text is full of criticism of member states failing to adapt to the policies agreed at european level to deal with the crisis, but it has amended all the passages that were critical of the effectiveness and the way the eu's austerity measures are being implemented.
in writing. - i have decided to abstain on mrs ferreira's report on the prospects for the european semester because the final result we reached after the vote on the amendments was unfortunately not up to the expectations and pressing needs. the calls for the member states to adopt a more moderate and prudent spending policy, seeking to limit current expenditure, are certainly to be welcomed. however, alongside these austerity and austerity measures, there should also be strong and clear support for policies aimed at fostering and stimulating growth, for example by providing for greater flexibility over the constraints of the stability pact, and also by excluding from these all investments that provide for a financial return in the medium and long-term economic cycle. it would have been equally appropriate to have taken a clear and firm stand in favour of the creation of a redemption fund to relieve at least part of the crushing burden of public debt on the economies of the member states. i feel that the text presented is not sufficiently ambitious and therefore i cannot give my support.
in writing. − the debt situation of several eu member states and the continuing economic crisis require serious reflection on the types of intervention that the european institutions can and must put in place to promote growth and development. improving national budgets, with a view to promoting effective and sustainable budgetary policies, is one of the virtuous paths to follow. however, fiscal austerity and balance of payments accuracy, if not accompanied by adequate growth policies, risk sliding several member states into recession and delaying the moment of recovery. the negotiations for the 2014-2020 multiannual financial framework have just begun and, despite the cuts requested by some national governments, there is a need to increase expenditure for a financial year in which some 96% of the money is returned to the member states in the form of investments.
in writing. - i did not support the fontagné report on the european semester for the coordination of economic policies: the commission has published a report on the employment and social aspects of the annual growth analysis for 2013. i consider this text to be incomplete and weak. on the one hand, it fully shares the principle underlying the european semester, namely the increase in fiscal surveillance of the member states, and on the other hand it makes proposals for a solution to the crisis which are not very credible, without supporting them with any impact assessment, based on certain data, showing how such a package of measures can lead to an exit from the economic and employment stagnation. the report also fails to analyse, or even to assess, the responsibility of phenomena such as relocation and the excessive international opening up of the single market for the continuation of the crisis we are experiencing.
in writing. - statistical figures and reports are alarming. in italy, the unemployment rate in december reached 11.2% while the inactive persons accounted for 36.4% of the total. i would like to draw your attention to this last fact. the economic loss due to the posting of the workforce creates an annual loss of eur 153 million, which corresponds to 1.2% of european gdp. five years after the start of the crisis, we have reached the point where it is preferable to live with inactivity rather than with precarious, low-paid and uninsured work. it is our responsibility to address this situation of extreme vulnerability, to combat public (and market) mistrust, and to work towards a new balance. we must not stop at a debate which is limited to the contention between those who want more state and those who want less. economic policies must put citizens back at the centre of the choices. we don't have a magic wand, and there are no "miracle" solutions. a structural plan with targeted interventions for job creation, tax reforms and employment incentives is needed. the possibility of facilitating access to finance for small and medium-sized enterprises should be provided. finally, the employment potential of growth sectors such as the green economy must be exploited.
in writing. - unfortunately, the employment situation in europe has worsened and the forecasts for this year are negative. i voted in favour of this because i believe it is essential for the council to include the issue of youth employment among the priorities of the 2013 programme. strategies must be developed to provide employment opportunities for young people who decide not to continue their studies. this requires close cooperation between the member states and the social partners to create employment or training solutions after a maximum of four months of unemployment or the end of the study cycle. in addition, recent years have seen a diversification of the labour market, which is increasingly oriented towards new sectors such as the green economy and healthcare. synergy between the education and vocational training sectors is needed to create young professionals with the skills to cope with changes in the labour market. finally, we must encourage greater participation in the world of work, especially for the vulnerable and disadvantaged, including the young and the elderly, who unfortunately have serious difficulties in entering the labour market.
in writing. − i support this text because i believe that an effective single market is needed more than ever to boost growth, create jobs and revitalise the european economy. the single market should be completed as quickly as possible, while maintaining a careful balance between its economic and social dimensions. most of all, it is important to stress the interdependence between the single market and other horizontal policy areas, including consumer and worker protection, social rights, the environment and sustainable development. concrete actions, both at member state and union level, are still needed to implement fully freedom of movement for goods, persons, services and capital in the european union. for all these reason, as was proposed by this report, i believe it is critical to strengthen the role of the single market within the european semester.

the rapporteur. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, i think it is very important that on this world women's day we have devoted a report to the countries of tunisia, egypt, libya and morocco, in which we women and men members of the european parliament wish to express our strong solidarity and political support for the women of north africa who fought and are fighting for democracy and freedom in their countries, which were hit by the impetuous wind of the arab spring two years ago, which saw them play a leading role in the streets, in the media, in associations and now, in a different and also controversial but tenacious way, in the places where new constitutions, laws and the future are decided. nor can we remain silent in the face of the crimes perpetrated by the syrian regime. we've met them, we've heard them: women of different backgrounds and generations. they explained that fighting for democracy and for their rights in the new constitutions is the same for them, that by freeing women they want to free their countries from the previous dictatorships, but also from those fundamentalist currents, which would like to return them to a cultural and psychological subordination. we have been denounced the improper use of sexual violence and torture against protesters, or genital mutilation, or the repression of religious and political minorities, including copts, as in egypt, human trafficking as in libya, the lack of recognition of human and political rights, as for the saharawi by morocco, the temptation in egypt to put the sharia in the constitution as the basis of state laws. but they also told us about the successful struggle of women in tunisia for the new draft constitution, which incorporates equal rights, and the growing presence of women among university students, journalists, ngos, trade unions and parties in different countries. the debate on the principle of the autonomy of the state from religious power, not only between women and secular and religious parties, but also within the latter, is also interesting in this respect. women in these four countries are concerned about the economic and social crisis which is exacerbating political tensions, but they consider the process started by women to be irreversible. they know that the transition will be long and marked by conflict and risks, primarily those of political polarization and fundamentalism. today we know that in egypt the challenge is on the constitution after the referendum imposed by morsi and the postponement of the elections; in tunisia, president marzouki is trying to install a new technocratic government after the attacks of the last few months and has asked a woman to take over the role of minister of human rights; no agreement on the constitution is reached in libya and it is proposed to hold a consultation; in morocco, a strong concentration of power by the king continues alongside constitutional reform. but we know that without the active participation of women and their involvement in the building of institutions from below and their rights as an integral and inalienable part of human rights, there will be neither democracy nor effective and sustainable development. for this reason, the women of these countries have been and are currently engaged in rewriting the constitution and new laws, starting with the electoral one. thanks to quotas in electoral laws, in tunisia 27% of women are parliamentarians and in libya 17% - this is the first time since the country held free elections that women are elected to the libyan congress - in morocco they are 16%, in egypt just 2%, because they are at the bottom of the lists. the women's awakening is strong everywhere, and it calls for the european union's support and continued attention. i ask that the european union place respect for women's human rights, the principle of 'more for more', gender equality and the active participation of women at the negotiating table and in regional bilateral processes at the heart of its new euro-mediterranean partnership strategy and bilateral agreements with these countries. we call on the commission and the high representative to ensure that programmes and actions for women are based on the institutional, social and regional and local community levels, starting in particular with rural areas and the urban peripheries, including through microfinance, supporting the great energies of women in business, university networks and even the media. the report sets out very clearly the demands made on the european union: finally, i would also ask the union for the mediterranean to dedicate an annual session to the situation of women in the region in its parliamentary assembly. i thank the shadow rapporteurs and the chairman of the femm committee and the colleagues on the deve committee.

in writing. gender equality is a fundamental human right. in accordance with article 8 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union: 'in all its activities, the union shall aim to eliminate inequalities and to promote equality between men and women.' in 1995, the fourth world conference on women was held in beijing, aimed at "removing all obstacles to the active participation of women in all areas of public and private life through equal participation in economic, social, cultural and political decision-making". since then, parliament has adopted three resolutions on women's rights. however, more than 15 years after the conference, gender stereotypes and inequalities are still common problems in the union today. the prevalence of negative gender stereotypes based on social prejudices and attitudes harms women and limits their opportunities in the social, economic and political spheres. the seriousness of the problem is confirmed by the high gender pay gap, which stood at 16.4% in 2010. in my view, the decisive approach to the problem requires new union policies and ad hoc legislation to combat gender stereotypes in education, the labour market and economic and political decision-making.

vice-president of the commission. − madam president, the importance of this moment and of this vote for europe’s economic future can hardly be overstated. together with the six-pack, these two regulations bring us several steps towards a genuine economic and monetary union (emu). i want to take this opportunity to thank all the rapporteurs, shadow rapporteurs, other meps, friends and colleagues who have tirelessly worked with the commission and with the council presidencies to make this possible, to make this happen. i would also like to thank you all for the many amendments that you have introduced, often through very resolute insistence – sometimes, i have to say, bordering on stubbornness – that have improved and strengthened in the end the proposals in the course of the legislative process. i dare to state that if the six-pack and the two-pack had been there at the introduction of the euro, we would never have suffered from a crisis of such magnitude. in any event, we would have got over the crisis much more quickly and with less social and financial costs. with the vote today, i trust we will demonstrate the benefits and the functioning of the community method. when looking in retrospect at the eu’s crisis response, and thinking of today’s vote and of the commission’s declaration on a redemption fund and eurobills, i can only wish that the council had already been persuaded and supportive of the community method in spring 2010, three years ago. i am referring to the critical ecofin meeting on 9-10 may 2010, when the commission – on europe day, in one of our crisis meetings – made a proposal to create a single european financial stability mechanism, based first on guarantees by the eu budget up to eur 60 billion, and then on joint and several guarantees beyond that. that would have presented the kind of big bazooka that has helped to tame the systemic crisis only since last year, with the ecb’s ltro interventions and omt decisions. instead, we got the far clumsier efsf, which was only last year turned into a permanent and well capitalised institution, the esm. i dare to claim that our response to the crisis would have delivered better and faster results for our citizens, if the commission’s original proposals had in spring 2010 found acceptance among the member states. but the time was not yet ripe then for decisions of such magnitude. (heckling) to make clear the commission’s intentions as regards future steps, i would like to declare the following on behalf of the commission. i ask for your patience and you will have to forgive me if i am exceptionally long, by my standards, but this is all a rather comprehensive and fragile solution. once the legislation proposed by the commission on the two-pack is adopted, the commission intends to take steps in the short-term towards a deep and genuine emu, as outlined in the blueprint. short-term steps, from 6 to 12 months, will include: in its blueprint for a deep and genuine emu, the commission considered that, in the medium-term, a redemption fund and eurobills could be possible elements of a deep and genuine emu under certain rigorous conditions. the guiding principle would be that any steps to further mutualisation of risk must go hand in hand with greater fiscal discipline and integration. the required deeper integration of financial regulation, fiscal and economic policy and corresponding instruments must be accompanied by commensurate political integration, ensuring democratic legitimacy and accountability, the commission will establish an expert group to deepen the analysis of the possible merits, risks, requirements and obstacles of partial substitution of national issuance of debt through joint issuance in the form of a redemption fund and eurobills. the group will be tasked with thoroughly assessing the possible features in terms of legal provisions, financial architecture and the necessary complementary economic and budgetary framework. democratic accountability will be a central issue to be considered,(heckling) the group will take into account the ongoing reform of the european economic and budgetary governance and assess the added value for such instruments in this context. the group will pay particular attention to recent and on-going reforms, such as the implementation of the two-pack, the esm and other relevant instruments, in its analysis the group will pay particular attention to the sustainability of public finances, to the avoidance of moral hazard, as well as to other central issues, such as financial stability, financial integration and monetary policy transmission, the members of the group will be experts in law and economics, public finances, financial markets and sovereign debt management. the group will be invited to present its final report to the commission no later than march 2014. the commission will assess the report and, if appropriate, make proposals before the end of its mandate. an exploration of further ways, within the preventive arm of the stability and growth pact, to accommodate under certain conditions, non-recurrent, public investment programmes with a proven impact on the sustainability of public finances made by the member states in the assessment of their stability and convergence programmes will be done in spring-summer 2013, in the context of the publication of the communication on the calendar of convergence towards the medium-term objective; after the decision on the next multiannual financial framework for the eu and before the end of 2013, the commission will put forward the following proposals to complement the existing framework for economic governance: measures to ensure greater ex-ante coordination of major economic reforms and the creation of a ‘convergence and competitiveness instrument’ to provide financial support for the timely implementation of structural reforms that enhance sustainable growth. vice-president of the commission. − madam president, the new system, fully in line with the community method, will build on existing eu surveillance procedures. it would combine deeper integration of economic policy with financial support, thereby observing the principle that steps towards greater responsibility and economic discipline should be combined with greater solidarity. it would, in particular, aim at enhancing the capacity of a member state to absorb asymmetric shocks. this instrument would serve as the initial phase in moves towards the establishment of stronger fiscal capacity. furthermore, the commission commits to following up, in a speedy and comprehensive manner, on its action plan to strengthen the fight against tax fraud and tax evasion, in particular with a view to the revision of the directives identified in the action plan and the measures and proposals announced by the commission in its 2012 package in the field of employment and social policy. this is the commission’s overall commitment. i trust that this declaration has provided sufficient clarity about the intentions of the commission, and i hope that you can vote in favour of the ‘two-pack’ just in time before this week’s european council – which will be very important for rebuilding economic confidence in europe. this would be a significant step forward in terms of our shared ambition to create a genuine european monetary union for the benefit of all our citizens. thank you for your kind attention, your support and your confidence. mr president, i voted in favour of the report on transeuropean energy infrastructure because i believe that this regulation has the advantage of promoting certain fundamental aspects of european energy policy. first, it gives a strong impetus to the completion of the internal energy market and its full integration, thus contributing to the objectives of energy security and, at the same time, to those of diversification of sources of supply. we will also be able to modernise our energy networks to ensure that environmental sustainability is achieved by 2020. we naturally also want to see more development and employment for local communities, including through renewable sources and energy innovation. we also welcome the simplification of the authorization procedures. less bureaucracy very often equals higher investment productivity.
mr president, sustainable, safe and affordable energy is one of the main challenges facing the european citizens. despite the good intentions and ambitious targets set by the commission, european energy policy is making slow progress. the resources allocated at union level are scarce and only recently, with the adoption of the treaty, has the issue gained greater prominence. i therefore voted in favour of the text by mr correia de campos, which aims to speed up the completion of the internal energy market, thus achieving the objectives of the european union's energy and environmental policy.
in writing. - i supported the correia de campos report on the proposal for a european parliament and council regulation on guidelines for transeuropean energy infrastructures (ten-t). the creation of a crossborder market and the development of its infrastructure impose onerous costs and investments which are a real barrier to entry. this requires a new regulation to overcome these obstacles and to achieve the modernisation and interconnection of energy networks, minimising waste and maximising the effectiveness of interventions.
in writing. - i congratulate mr correia de campos on his work on this report. i believe that the procedural complexities caused by the wide scope of the regulation and reflected in the opinions of five committees have added to an already thorny and demanding problem. just think about the implications of these guidelines: the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of the environment and the environment from the adverse effects of pollution of the atmosphere by nitrates and their salts is a very good one. i particularly welcome the overall vision and the efficiency approach that is being taken to reduce the need for infrastructure as the european economy decarbonises. in this field, whose strategic importance is crucial to ensuring well-being and prosperity in the decades to come, a mistake can be very costly both in economic terms and in terms of the impact on the real economy. i therefore welcome the work done and invite my colleagues and the public to monitor the long-term prospects of this measure.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mr correia de campos' report because i believe that it is a step in the right direction towards renewing europe's energy policy, with particular reference to transeuropean energy infrastructures. in order to achieve the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy, the new regulation is an important initiative, as it aims to make a decisive move towards the completion of the internal energy market. it is clear that such action must be pursued through adequate modernisation and interconnection of energy networks. but not only: a trans-european energy market should ensure greater competitiveness, counter decentralised production, attract new producers and act as a driver for the economy of the future.
in writing. − energy that is at the same time sustainable, safe, guaranteed and naturally accessible in cost is one of the main challenges of the european single market. unfortunately, the resources allocated have proved insufficient to achieve this ambitious initial objective. the internal energy market remains insufficiently integrated: some geographical areas remain energy-isolated. access to diversified energy sources that can enhance energy security is not sufficient and there are no tangible benefits for consumers and businesses in terms of prices and sustainability. a new approach at european level is therefore needed: we call on europe to play a more active role in coordinating and integrating national efforts, to accelerate the completion of the internal energy market, achieving the objectives of energy and environmental policy by mobilising very significant investments, boosting economic growth and creating jobs in the european union.
in writing. − one of the most important challenges to be overcome is the ability to generate sustainable energy that is safe and affordable. unfortunately, europe has so far grown slowly in this respect, allocating insufficient resources to achieve this ambitious goal. a new approach at european level must be defined as soon as possible, one which can support the energy interdependence between the various countries, with brussels increasingly at the centre of a strong coordination of national efforts.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the correia de campos report because i believe that the implementation of the regulation contained in it can help to achieve a secure, sustainable, guaranteed and economic energy system. the coordination of european energy networks is a priority to be achieved as soon as possible and energy policy is central to the european agenda. the interconnection of european energy sources is proceeding too slowly and there are still obstacles, bottlenecks and bottlenecks, as well as wide gaps between the various countries. the completion of appropriate infrastructure, such as so-called 'smart grids', is necessary to achieve a competitive cross-border energy market. this regulation should be able to speed up the completion of these infrastructures by stimulating new investments, especially private ones. projects of common interest (pcis) have been selected for implementation and the authorisation procedure has been simplified. the adoption of this report will lead to more secure and reliable energy supplies and will bring significant benefits to consumers.
in writing. − within the europe 2020 programming framework, clear targets have been set for reducing ghg emissions, increasing the consumption of renewable energy sources and improving energy efficiency. this includes the prospect of a more integrated european energy system, enabling efficient trans-european energy exchange, by modernising and interconnecting energy and gas networks and by providing infrastructure for the transport of oil and carbon dioxide. a plan for securing the main energy networks and developing some of the most important ones will also be provided. the implementation of this project will be carried out through the icps (projects of common interest), which will be selected in detail according to established criteria, paying attention to the predominance of the european interest over the national or regional one. it is important that the funds allocated are distributed in a virtuous way to ensure that the projects chosen are indeed worthy of european aid. it is an ambitious project but i believe it is valuable for achieving the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy. i therefore welcome the commission's proposal.
in writing. - i supported the auken report: the document we have voted on clearly shows what i have repeatedly said in the chambers of this parliament, namely that the european institutions are not immune to instances of maladministration, lack of transparency or outright corruption. the text denounces, for example, the involvement of the european commission in a clear case of conflict of interest. i believe that it is our duty as representatives of democracy in europe to be vigilant and to exercise in every possible way the control of transparency at any institutional level.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because i believe it is extremely important to give a voice to the citizens who turn to the european ombudsman, who, together with the committee on petitions and solvit, is one of the european union's bodies that ensure that citizens are heard, and who often and willingly prove to be the best observers of the correct implementation of european legislation. furthermore, i believe that the case of vienna airport is an important starting point for reflection in order to highlight the shortcomings of the current environmental impact assessment directive and to recognise the need to ensure less discretionary assessment parameters, ensuring the objectivity and impartiality of the competent authorities, avoiding conflicts of interest.
in writing. − the role of the european ombudsman is essential in resolving disputes between the european institutions and citizens. the ombudsman can help to resolve complaints more quickly. the case of the special report in question, for which i voted in favour, concerns a situation which has been going on for years at vienna airport. citizens have reported infrastructure deficiencies which are among the infringements for which the commission should intervene by sanctioning the austrian state if it does not resolve the problem in due time. the ombudsman examined the situation and identified the existing shortcomings which will be examined by the commission.
in writing. - vienna airport has been undergoing renovation and expansion since 1999. such works should generally be preceded by an environmental impact assessment (eia), which is not the procedure used in this case. this, following a complaint received by the commission, provided the possibility of an ex post eia which would be similar to an ex ante eia. the complainants, considering the procedure not to be fully legitimate, requested the intervention of the european ombudsman who, after a careful inquiry, concluded that, although the commission had not acted in a correct manner, it should nevertheless be given the confidence to continue with the environmental impact assessment, and closed the inquiry in 2009. in november 2010, the complainants again contacted the ombudsman, who launched a second inquiry, which concluded with a finding that the complaint was well founded and resulted in a draft recommendation to the commission, urging it to correct its approach to the eia and to conclude the evaluation as soon as possible. i am in favour of this.
mr president, i am speaking on both the arsenis and eickhout reports because i am in fact strongly opposed to these very similar reports, since both require greater efforts on the part of individual european states at a time of crisis such as the one we are living through. i think that's really over the top. the european union cannot continue to be the leader in environmental and climate policy: the commitments must be global and binding on all. it must be borne in mind that the european union is not self-sufficient in agricultural products: we import cereals from several non-community countries, even though we know that substances prohibited in europe are often used in their production. the commission has already made a number of proposals. i think that policies aimed at better management of unused land and uncultivated forests are needed. an example of poor management of italian forestry is the apennine ridge across liguria, which is completely abandoned and which, with no vegetation, is the cause of continuous fires and in which no replanting has ever taken place. i think it would be better to clear the abandoned land first than to abandon other land instead of cultivated.

in writing. − we believe that accounting for land use, land use change and forestry is a key element in climate policy and can contribute to mitigation, adaptation and conservation of biodiversity, as well as to the sustainable use of natural resources. first, effective rules for accounting for greenhouse gas emissions and removals resulting from land-use activities should be established. it will be necessary to provide for the obligation to establish accounting for emissions and the resulting removals and to propose, accordingly, that drainage and re-wetting of wetlands be considered as a category of activity for which accounting should be established. in order to ensure harmonisation with a view to further integration into the union's emission reduction commitments and with current eu legislation, all member states should be required to account for carbon stocks using the same carbon and greenhouse gas sinks. the commission will have the task of providing guidance and technical assistance to member states, where appropriate, and the power to make recommendations for further action, ensuring public participation and transparency as required by union legislative acts.
in writing. - i believe that we are all in favour of respecting and protecting the environment and the climate at the highest level in this house. it is good that europe is setting an example, but without this being a case of imposing excessive and difficult obligations. the climate and environmental issue is very complex and by its very nature global: the rules and principles must be set in the broadest possible context, whereas europe too often finds itself acting in isolation, as other large countries put their economic and commercial interests ahead of the protection of the planet. i am not saying that we should accept the downturn, but we must be very careful not to risk imposing rules which are too restrictive and whose effectiveness is not always demonstrable, and which can have a depressing effect on the whole european economy.
in writing. − this vote aims to re-emphasise the importance of climate policies, making a concrete contribution to mitigation, adaptation and conservation of biodiversity and the sustainable use of natural resources. the final objective should be to facilitate compliance with international obligations under the united nations framework convention on climate change and the kyoto protocol, ensuring full integration of these rules into the common agricultural policy and the renewable energy directive.
in writing. − the proposal provides for the establishment of effective standards for accounting for emissions and removals resulting from land use, land use change and forestry (lulucf). it provides for compliance with international and eu obligations in this field, including the kyoto protocol, ensures consistency with future and current policies on environmental issues and with the principles of transparency, consistency, comparability, completeness and accuracy. if these criteria are met and the corrections made to the draft, which include the possibility of making accounting compulsory for all carbon and greenhouse gas reservoirs related to the various categories of activities, of accounting for emissions from harvested wood products (hwp) extracted outside the union and used for energy purposes in the territory for indicative purposes, of applying the instantaneous oxidation method and at the same time providing information on the country of collection of hwp and the sustainability criteria adopted, the proposal can be an effective step forward for environmental monitoring policies and therefore meets my favourable opinion.
mr president, we have today approved the draft report on the mechanism for monitoring and reporting greenhouse gas emissions and other information on climate change at national and european union level. the objective of this proposal is to review the monitoring mechanism and to strengthen the existing system in order to ensure that the european union and its member states respect and comply with their commitments under existing international climate change agreements and implement the related requirements of the climate and energy package at european level. the agreement reached with the council after a long and complex negotiating process must, in my view, be regarded positively. by reducing the rigidities that had been created between the various positions, this agreement avoided an unjustified widening of the scope of the proposal and thus an overlap with other regulatory instruments that would have led to the creation of additional burdens, and it was possible to ensure a good level of flexibility in the perspective of future international agreements in the climate field.
accounting for land use and land use change and forestry must focus on three general objectives. first, it must promote the fulfilment of the international obligations of the member states and the european union under the united nations framework convention on climate change and the kyoto protocol; ensure policy coherence with union legislation on coordination and integration, including inter alia the common agricultural policy and the renewable energy directive; finally, it must ensure that accounting practices and methods comply with the principles of transparency, consistency, comparability, completeness and accuracy, not only within the member states but also between them, as members of the european union. the report by mr arsenis succeeded in meeting these principles, and i therefore voted in favour of it.

in writing. − the commission has proposed some improvements to the provisions contained in decision no 280/2004/ec on the mechanism for monitoring and reporting greenhouse gas emissions and overall energy use, leading to the possible adoption of a regulation. the report also requires the union and the member states to comply with their reporting obligations and to ensure transparency, timeliness and comparability of the data collected and reported. they will also have to include information on the amount of energy from renewable sources and total final energy consumption in their reports. it is desirable that member states develop projects, which are well defined in terms of costs, timing and objectives to be achieved, and which fit well within the framework of the europe 2020 programming. in addition, with the aim of reducing and monitoring the emission of greenhouse gases into the atmosphere, the regulation encourages the european union to involve both industrialised and developing countries in the project in order to achieve a common and winning strategy. i therefore express my favourable opinion.

in writing. − to promote access to quick, inexpensive and effective dispute resolution between consumers and traders, the commission has presented this package of legislative proposals to ensure that all consumers in the union can resolve their problems out of court, i.e. without having to go to court, regardless of the type of product, the way it was purchased and the eu country in which the transaction took place. the two proposed legislative instruments, the adr directive and the odr regulation, are designed to build trust in the single market and make life easier for consumers. the proposals on adr and odr aim to enhance the functioning of the digital single market, in particular by improving consumer access to compensation in the form of alternative dispute resolution and thereby strengthening consumer confidence, which is currently insufficient with regard to web-based transactions. i voted in favour of this proposal because the platform is a necessary tool to ensure consumer protection in the single market and will be free of charge and available in all the official languages of the european union.

in writing. the consultation report by the french member of parliament for guadeloupe should be seen in the light of the new recasting of the principles guiding the european union's cooperation with the overseas countries and territories (octs). the current overseas association decision (oda) of 2001 expires on 31 december 2013 and the renewal of that scope of association is essential for the octs. this new approach must promote their sustainable development, taking account of their specificities. i shall vote in favour of the report.
in writing. − the regional and international context in which the overseas countries and territories (octs) operate has changed considerably since the adoption of the current association decision in 2001. today, in an increasingly globalised and rapidly changing environment, the main challenge for the octs is to steer their economies towards growth that can be reconciled with the major economic challenges facing the rest of the world. the key is to work with neighbouring countries, establishing specific and profitable trade partnerships and opening up to integration into the regional or world economy. in this sense, the european union can certainly play an important role in contributing to the growth and development of the octs.
in writing. − the overseas countries and territories (octs) are key outposts for europe, often called upon to play a part in the eu's aspirational global role in the globalisation of trade, new environmental challenges and climate change. all collaborative projects must therefore be improved and their participation in the european integration process stimulated, since, with their natural advantages and the opportunities for action they offer, they can become essential pawns in the strategies of the european union and innovative contributors in the framework of international negotiations. in order to take full advantage of the trade preferences granted to the octs, measures should be developed to overcome certain specific competitive disadvantages; the european union should support the development of niche markets and value-added products and services and enhance the brand value of their specific products by supporting their promotion and labelling. on the other hand, the areas of cooperation for sustainable development could include competitiveness and refer to community programmes relating to innovation, research and enterprise. finally, we reiterate our wish for a simplified and more flexible financial instrument, particularly in view of the limited administrative and budgetary capacity of some octs.
in writing. − the overseas countries and territories (octs) are outposts and assets for europe as they are called upon to participate in the role it aspires to play on the world stage, and the eu should further help the octs to improve their supervisory and engineering capacity to enable them to respond to calls for proposals from the commission. although i do not agree with all the points, i voted in favour of the proposal because i believe that support from the representatives of the union or the commission in the geographical areas of the oct would help to improve oct access to horizontal programmes.
in writing. − the overseas countries and territories are an important resource for europe in international strategies and negotiations. the octs are therefore linked to the european union by the 2001 overseas association decision (oda), which expires on 31 december 2013. the review of the same was initiated as early as 2008 and resulted in a new decision approved on 16 july 2012 by the college of commissioners. the objectives of the new octs, as already set out in the common position of february 2011, aim at improving the octs' competitiveness, reducing their weaknesses and promoting cooperation with other partners, and are intended to drive the sustainable development of the octs, with particular attention to the expansion of the market for their products. the proposal also makes reference to regional cooperation, in particular with the countries neighbouring the octs, and provides for better coordination between cooperation programmes supported by the various eu financial instruments. in view of the strategic importance of the oct, i shall vote in favour of the new proposal for a decision on overseas association.
in writing. - the rivasi report aims to fill the gaps in the implementation of directive 98/83/ec on the quality of water intended for human consumption by incorporating the requirements for monitoring radioactive substances in drinking water into special legislation adopted under the euratom treaty. i believe that the protection of public health must always be the first priority, and that is why i voted in favour of this text.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mrs rivasi's report because the proposal for a directive lays down requirements for the protection of public health in relation to radioactive substances in water intended for human consumption. in particular, the inclusion of natural and man-made sources of radioactivity, and the different exposure groups, taking into account age, represent significant steps forward in protecting citizens and all consumers of a public and indispensable good. greater attention and stricter controls are also essential requirements for continuing the work of prevention and mitigation of the phenomenon until its disappearance.
in writing. − water is one of the main and essential sources of life and it is therefore a duty and a necessity that water intended for human consumption be as safe as possible and present the least risk to health. the report we have voted on today fills in some of the gaps in european legislation, particularly with regard to certain chemical and radioactive substances. more stringent and effective controls must be in place to ensure that the water we drink every day is pure, uncontaminated and therefore free from any risk to our health. italian households often use bottled water or new purification systems: but it must be said that the water that flows from our taps is subject to a significant number of controls and must meet very strict parameters, which make it certainly comparable or even better than commercial alternatives. in conclusion, we in europe should be assured of whatever water we choose to consume, and this is essential, because in other parts of the world water is not only scarce, but often polluted and causes enormous damage to human health.
in writing. - mr president, i voted in favour of the resolution. we all know that water contains radioactive substances. the european states are not very transparent and admit the presence of tritium, radon and other carcinogens which, even in small quantities, could have health effects. that is why we are today calling for stricter measures and stricter controls, and for the data collected by the member states to be made public in order to make all available information available to consumers. it is also necessary to impose penalties on those who pollute, by ordering those responsible to bear the costs of the clean-up.
in writing. − ensuring that all european citizens have access to safe drinking water is a priority for policies concerning human health and environmental protection. european legislation must now be updated, introducing legal certainty and consistency in the quality of drinking water, putting so-called radionuclides on the same level as all carcinogenic pollutants. after this step, the need for systematic and periodic review of radioactive substances control techniques and sampling and analysis methods in the light of scientific progress will be equally important.
in writing. the proposal for a directive on radioactive substances intended for human consumption aims to regulate health protection at european level. several member states have not yet applied the requirements for the control of tritium and the total indicative dose, although these were to be transposed by 2003. i believe that the council and the commission should also regulate the presence of other substances which are dangerous to health, since in some member states there are no adequate risk prevention policies in place. i would like to take the example of italy, where there is a law that allows the use of water containing up to 50 μg/l of total chromium as drinking water. this means that in italy it is possible to administer water containing up to 50 μg/l of hexavalent chromium, a known and potent carcinogen and mutagen. it is enough to remember that the who provides for a maximum limit of 5 μg/l of hexavalent chromium for groundwater and non-potable waters.
in writing. − water purity is one of the priorities of eu policies in the field of environmental protection and human health protection. however, there are still many regions in europe where pollution levels are high. i support mr rivasi's report, because it seeks to increase control in this area. the only european legal basis in this field is the euratom treaty, whose main control measure is the consultation procedure of the european parliament. the report calls for greater powers for the european parliament under the lisbon treaty (article 149 tfeu) to be able to draw up genuine legislative provisions in this area. they also agree to increase transparency and to inform the public about the quality and treatment of water intended for human consumption.
in writing. - the directive in question focuses on a major issue, namely exposure to certain radioactive substances through drinking water. that directive, adopted under the treaty on the functioning of the european union, updates the parametric indicators set out in part c of annex i to directive 98/83/ec and lays down rules on the monitoring of the presence of radioactive substances in drinking water. this will allow any abnormal value to be examined and its origin and possible effect on the consumer to be clarified. the latter must be kept informed at all times of what it is taking, of the areas at risk of potential radioactive contamination and of the quality of the water in the region. while natural mineral waters and medicinal waters, which are subject to specific rules laid down in directive 2009/54/ec of the european parliament and of the council of 18 june 2009 on the use and marketing of mineral waters, are excluded from the scope of this directive, it remains an important element for the protection of human health, a priceless asset that is constantly defended by the european union. for that reason, i am in favour of it.
in writing. - i did not support the report by mr gauzès on the economic and budgetary surveillance of member states which are experiencing or are threatened with serious difficulties with regard to their financial stability in the euro area. i do not think that the surveillance measures which europe wants to impose on the economic policies of member states in difficulty are acceptable. the possibility for the european institutions to intervene in the budgets presented by the member states is yet another excessive interference which is the prelude to the erosion of another important national sovereign prerogative: the power of balance.
in writing. - this is a timely and necessary measure to continue to stem the crisis which continues to plague the public finances of the member states and which prevents resources, so precious at the moment, from being allocated to development. if we look at the measure from a systemic point of view, we can see how important it is to maintain the monetary system that the european union has established. unfortunately, the disconnect between the level of monetary sovereignty and the level of decision-making in fiscal policy becomes a factor of risk and stagnation: on the one hand, there is the unquestionable need for the member states to use the various levers at their disposal in a democratic system to deal with the crisis; on the other hand, there is a set of mechanisms and structures built to defend the purchasing power of money and to join efforts to better defend against financial speculation. this is where the need to balance these two powers comes in to ensure that short-term political goals and small realities do not overshadow economic policies geared to the long-term well-being of a large economy like the euro area. it is a good sign that lithuania, a recent recipient of technical assistance for its monetary system, is keen to join the euro.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mr gauzès' report because i think it is a good thing that a tool for economic and budgetary surveillance has been adopted for member states which are experiencing or are likely to experience serious difficulties with regard to their financial stability in the euro area. the economic and financial crisis has for years now been seriously jeopardizing the solvency of the member states, and in a unitary economic environment - such as that of europe - the failure of a national economy would mean the failure of a project which, in addition to being economic, is also political and social. with the adoption of the six-pack and two-pack, the eu has given itself new rules of economic governance to meet the challenges ahead. however, the case of the bailout of cyprus through forced withdrawals from current accounts risks representing a mistake that was already said not to be repeated after the management of the greek economic crisis.
in writing. − the package providing for the economic and budgetary surveillance of member states in or threatened with serious difficulties and the monitoring and evaluation of budgetary programming documents for the correction of excessive deficits in the euro area (two pack) contains provisions aimed at enhancing control of the economic and budgetary policies of the member states. the aim of the text is to complement the six pack by giving the eu's control bodies the possibility to intervene with preventive instruments where states need them. in addition, member states will be required to submit annually to the council and the commission the draft budgets for the following year with the introduction of strict monitoring measures for states subject to an excessive deficit procedure. the amendments to the texts have given the commission greater powers to control national budgets, to correct excessive deficits and to monitor the national budgets of euro-area countries with serious problems of financial instability.
in writing. − the draft regulation on the strengthening of the economic and budgetary surveillance of member states experiencing or threatened with serious difficulties with respect to their financial stability in the euro area is part of the context of the financial and sovereign debt crisis currently facing the european union. i agree that the decision-making procedure needs to be adapted to allow for a rapid reaction and that it is for the commission to take the necessary decisions, including that of subjecting a member state to the enhanced surveillance procedure; i therefore voted in favour of the proposal.
in writing. − the proposal for a regulation on strengthening economic surveillance of those states experiencing or potentially affected by economic difficulties is added to the package on european economic governance, approved by parliament and the council in 2011 and in the context of the financial crisis which has been affecting the countries of the european union for several years now. the question of the excessive indebtedness of some european states does not describe a problem which concerns and affects only those particular countries, but which threatens the whole eurozone, through a dangerous chain effect. that is why, if there is any indication that one of them is entering a phase of financial instability, it will be appropriate to take targeted action, based on a strong and urgent monitoring which will be arranged from time to time by the commission after consulting the council, and which may also be accompanied by a legal protection system, which would involve in particular a suspension of contractual clauses relating to expiry of the term or credit events. i am in favour of this.
mr president, with this vote we have dealt a further, strong and final blow to the european economy and to the autonomy of our states. since the 1999 stability and growth pact, europe has been in a constant race to over-strictness, removing all room for manoeuvre and freedom of action. the european treaties from maastricht to lisbon, on the other hand, provide that a state retains certain growth prerogatives, for example by setting the threshold between the deficit and gdp at 3% per annum. with the agreements that have been added since then, in clear violation of the treaties, this possibility has been lost and we are therefore forced to suffer the restrictive impositions that have been dropped from above. these are measures which in a time of crisis only make the situation worse. the commission now wants to redraw the member states' approaches, perhaps following the example of the splendid intervention in greece. brussels must admit its failure to bring an already troubled country to a desperate and perhaps hopeless situation, with the risk that other states will follow suit.
in writing. - i do not support the ferreira report on the monitoring and evaluation of budgetary programming documents and the correction of excessive deficits in the euro area member states. i think that the text is pushing too far towards surveillance measures which involve excessive interference by the commission in the economic policies of the member states.
in writing. − the monitoring and evaluation of the budgetary programming documents of excessive deficits in the euro area member states are actions to be adopted and used with due caution. a policy focused on controlling national budgets is certainly necessary in a context of high deficits and rising public debt, especially for some eurozone countries. however, this monitoring and evaluation activity must not turn into a further austerity coup or an aid-oriented practice that merely temporarily postpones an insolvency problem. finally, i think it is also appropriate here to consider a virtuous economic circle which can help public finances by starting from the recovery of consumption.
in writing. − the package providing for the economic and budgetary surveillance of member states in or threatened with serious difficulties and the monitoring and evaluation of budgetary programming documents for the correction of excessive deficits in the euro area (two pack) contains provisions aimed at enhancing control of the economic and budgetary policies of the member states. the aim of the text is to complement the six pack by giving the eu's control bodies the possibility to intervene with preventive instruments where states need them. in addition, member states will be required to submit annually to the council and the commission the draft budgets for the following year with the introduction of strict monitoring measures for states subject to an excessive deficit procedure. the amendments to the texts have given the commission greater powers to control national budgets, to correct excessive deficits and to monitor the national budgets of euro-area countries with serious problems of financial instability.
in writing. − having regard to the formal approval by the european parliament and the council of the legislative package to strengthen economic governance in the eu and the euro area and agreeing that eu budgetary policy must be fully aligned with the new strategy for growth and jobs, the europe 2020 strategy, which is also intended to help overcome the eu crisis, i voted in favour of the proposal in order to move the eu economy towards smart, sustainable and inclusive growth accompanied by high levels of employment, productivity and social cohesion.
in writing. − in the context of the pressing financial crisis affecting the european union, many initiatives are being taken to halt the serious consequences that are and will be caused by it and to stem the effects that can still be avoided. these include the set of measures provided for in the economic governance legislative package approved in 2011, which provides for a detailed budgetary control procedure for all countries that are in financial conditions considered potentially dangerous for the entire european union. in addition to these preventive and control measures, the proposal for a regulation introduces a synchronised monitoring initiative of budgetary policies and a strengthened surveillance procedure for those countries subject to an excessive deficit procedure. all these provisions must at the same time respect the community's objectives of the europe 2020 strategy, linked to responsible and sustainable economic growth. i therefore express a favourable opinion.
in writing. the report analyses the proposal for a regulation on european venture capital funds, i.e. financing for activities that are about to be launched on the market. at present, firms rely mainly on the banking system for financing, and its limitations are becoming increasingly apparent, especially during the crisis. i therefore believe that venture capital would offer a viable alternative source of capital for smes and could help them to grow and become more competitive. for all these reasons i voted in favour of the text proposed by mr lamberts.
in writing. − i am voting in favour of the report, in the belief that the establishment of european venture capital funds, subject to specific regulation in relation to directive 2011/61/eu, can be an important tool for recovery and growth of competitiveness and innovation, particularly in countries where the credit crunch is significantly affecting the production system, or where, for a complex of reasons, the venture capital culture is weaker. even more significant benefits will be seen in countries whose production structure is dominated by smes in high value-added sectors, especially technological ones, with positive effects on employment and consumers. the forecasts, set out in point 2 of the preamble, seem to me to set a correct overall regulatory framework, which emphasises the values of accessibility and competitiveness. the declaration is stringent and promises to provide significant incentives for investment in the young, innovative and competitive enterprise. the combined provisions of articles 1a and 13 provide a medium-term perspective which ensures the sustainability and strategic value of the initiative in the medium to long term, significantly reducing the risk of fraud or a disastrous interventionist change in the market.
in writing. - i congratulate mr lamberts on this report, which is a step forward in the regulation of european venture capital funds. i welcome this for two basic reasons: the first is that we need to stimulate the use of these particular financial instruments in europe because they are functional to the kind of industrial policy the eu is trying to pursue. although the public perception is unfortunately a little different, it must be remembered that these funds, with private resources, act in the same direction as many public policies are directed with money from the citizens; furthermore, their presence is a sign of a thriving market for highly innovative and research-based products, and so attracting them must go hand in hand with fostering a research environment that orients innovations towards the market. at the same time, we've seen in the last few years what it means to leave finance with a free hand: the commission's proposal for a directive on the harmonization of the laws of the member states relating to turnover taxes is a good one. that is why i voted in favour of this measure.
in writing. - in the context of the severe economic and financial crisis we are currently experiencing, the introduction of measures to guarantee small and medium-sized enterprises and the adoption of measures to boost growth and development can only be welcomed by this house. in particular, the proposal for a regulation establishes the legal and regulatory framework within which several investment funds may obtain the status of 'european venture capital fund' and the associated passport. the aim is to create a venture capital investment sector for smes. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's industrial policy is not disrupted by the economic and productive forces which dominate the whole of european industry.
in writing. - whereas the proposal for a regulation establishes the legal framework within which different types of investment funds may obtain the status of 'european venture capital fund' and the corresponding passport, and whereas the objective of this proposal is to create a european venture capital investment sector for small and medium-sized enterprises (smes); i also agree that the proposal for a regulation lays down the criteria, in terms of available assets, which a fund must meet in order to obtain the status and passport mentioned above and that it also lays down the requirements for managers of venture capital funds and the restrictions on the investments which can be made with the assets of a fund, i therefore voted in favour of the proposal.
in writing. - we voted today to give the go-ahead to the agreement with the council on the new rules relating to the european social entrepreneurship fund. these measures will also make it easier for investors to find funds specialised in financing european social enterprises, and the funds will be obliged to inform investors about the monitoring and publication of information on the impact of investments made. social investment is a key element in the investment landscape for growth, particularly for those who have been most affected by the economic crisis or are chronically under-resourced. for this reason, i believe that the new regulation will finally overcome the difficulty, which many people have experienced, of identifying funds investing in social enterprises and allowing the companies themselves to monitor the visibility of their investment and the transparency of it.
in writing. - with regard to the proposal to adopt a regulation on european venture capital funds, i would like to stress the importance of these funds for the creation and development of smes, often by increasing the number of employees and the productivity of these enterprises. for these reasons too, the need for detailed and stringent rules in this area is becoming increasingly felt. a regulation would clarify the requirements for different types of investment funds to qualify as a european venture capital fund, thus creating a uniform european scenario, and would also make binding the criteria for selecting the investments that can be made with a given fund. in addition, there are control measures by a competent authority to ensure that the criteria imposed by the regulation are strictly and continuously respected. for these reasons, i am in favour of the proposal.
in writing. - i believe that social enterprises bring benefits not only in economic and social terms but also in terms of employment, especially at this historic moment when youth unemployment in europe stands at 23.6%, i.e. some 6 million young people without a job. today, social enterprises represent 10% of european enterprises and employ some 11 million people. they need to be supported by appropriate forms of financing, by improving the legal and fiscal environment and by adopting a european social etiquette. these measures can help to achieve financial independence and should be publicised through appropriate communication campaigns. for many young europeans, the proposal to create a legislative framework adapted to the needs of social enterprises and investors is an important starting point.
in writing. - i abstained in the vote on the report by mrs auconie on the european social entrepreneurship funds, because i think the analysis contained in the text is not sufficiently detailed and some passages are unclear.
in writing. - i shall vote in favour of the report. our social model, from welfare to the labour market, is now under question, and must be thoroughly revised, if we are to guarantee - even to the next generation - the maintenance of the present quality of life. the answers to this challenge are to be found in the application of the principle of subsidiarity, and in this context, social entrepreneurship plays a prominent role. the vision behind the report is to promote balanced development and encourage practical solidarity and social responsibility in a realistic market environment; the commission's proposal for a regulation on the establishment of a european agency for the evaluation of medicinal products for human use (emah) is a very good one. the proposal for a regulation has the effect of aligning and systematizing national legislation (some of which is very advanced), but which is lagging behind (i am thinking of italy) in relation to the social changes of the last thirty years. it is therefore appropriate to take action by establishing a common framework with benchmarks for qualitative requirements on portfolio composition, investor profile and investment eligibility.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i am pleased with the direction that this proposal is taking in the funds which are concerned in particular with social projects. there is a well-established economic literature on the so-called 'third sector' (which is in addition to the public and private sectors), and even the best practices that can be observed at the empirical level deserve to be framed and supported by appropriate regulatory forecasts. the fact that the european union brings together countries with well-functioning market economies (as required by the copenhagen criteria) does not mean that we should put aside those who, for reasons unrelated to goodwill, are unable to keep up with the competitive pace of our economies. this is not only one of the principles of my group, but it is now widely accepted as an exit clause for all those who, despite the opportunities, are left behind. mrs auconie has found the right balance between the regulatory requirements necessary to limit the scope of these funds and the flexibility of the instruments to allow eligible investments to produce significant positive effects on the european economy.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mrs auconie's report because i believe that, in the same way as european venture capital funds, the establishment of the european social entrepreneurship fund can meet the investment needs of legal persons carrying out non-profit-making activities. it is of the utmost importance that we, as the european parliament and the european union in general, also pay attention to the social entrepreneurship sector, especially in a context of such a severe crisis as the present one. on several occasions, especially during the debate on the european budget for 2014-2020, we have stressed the need to respond to the crisis with measures that focus on growth and development. the establishment of these funds is precisely in this direction.
in writing. − considering that helping to combat the social consequences of the financial crisis and making a valuable contribution to the achievement of the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy is of fundamental importance in order to allow the formation within the eu of a social investment market represented by investment funds for social enterprises and agreeing that investors also pursue social objectives and not just a financial return, i voted in favour of the proposal.
in writing. − the european union must immediately boost social entrepreneurship: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial interests are protected. the need for a genuine social investment market, including investment funds for social enterprises, is emerging day by day throughout europe. these resources already provide funding for positive social change, innovative solutions to problems and the fight against the consequences of the financial crisis, all in the context of achieving the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy.

in writing. - i voted in favour of mrs auconie's report because i fully share its objectives, first and foremost the objective of giving greater importance to social enterprises in the eu, which account for 10% of european enterprises and employ 11 million people. this report, on the one hand, increases the attractiveness of the label 'european social entrepreneurship fund' and, on the other hand, ensures a high level of protection for investments. companies that are not profit-oriented but aim to provide goods and social services to citizens are finding it difficult to finance their activities in this period of economic crisis. as a result of our negotiations, we have managed to achieve a regulatory framework that facilitates access to funds and their management for both beneficiaries and investors, thanks to a traceability system.
in writing. - the proposal for a regulation on the european social entrepreneurship funds (esif) is to my liking, as it aims, among other things, to protect investors who will be informed about these funds and thus be able to compare investment proposals from different esifs. the above-mentioned regulation will impose selective criteria for acquiring the designation of 'european social entrepreneurship fund' and will thus ensure uniformity within the countries of the european union, thus also increasing the confidence of investors who wish to invest in funds for social enterprises. attention will also be paid to the type of investment made with these funds and to the social enterprises considered as eligible portfolio enterprises. the regulation stipulates that an eligible portfolio undertaking must have as its primary objective the achievement of a measurable and positive social impact, use profits to achieve its primary objective and be managed in a responsible and transparent manner. in order to prevent the use of the efsi for purposes other than those for which it was created, there is a need for supervisory action by the competent authorities to eliminate any risk of abuse.
mr president, it is quite clear that the austerity policies imposed throughout europe and the dramatic cuts in social welfare spending, which in some cases have been implemented blindly and indiscriminately by national governments, are primarily affecting women and mothers. it is the task of the european parliament to denounce this situation in the interests of the european union, of our fellow citizens, so that the necessary budgetary discipline does not affect european women and families, their projects and programmes, because hitting women feeds the vicious economic circle in which we find ourselves. the balance of the budget cannot mean indiscriminate cuts in the welfare state, education, the rights of children and young people. last month, a written declaration was adopted calling for 2014 to be the european year of work-life balance: it is now up to the commission to give concrete answers to this question and it is very urgent that these answers should be received. we celebrated international women's day on monday, but this celebration may be over if we do not get immediate and positive responses, and that is our hope.
mr president, i have given a favourable opinion on the report on the impact of the economic crisis on gender equality and women's rights. in the economic crisis which has hit europe in recent years, women have suffered from a precariousness of work, which has resulted in the predominant growth of atypical forms of work. women are often forced to leave work to care for children or older relatives; this has had a profound impact on their careers. the situation is even more critical in the peripheral areas of the european union, where member states should exploit the enormous amounts of alternative forms of energy to create jobs, such as in the green sector, and reduce female unemployment. in order to try to stem the effects of the crisis, it is also necessary that the european institute for gender equality in vilnius monitor the consequences of the crisis and its effects on the female labour market, in order to eliminate any form of discrimination in the recruitment process, in order to ensure equal rights in the labour market.
in writing. − i voted for this report because gender equality must be a key consideration when defining the response to the current economic and financial crisis. as we all know, the effects of this crisis are more serious for vulnerable people, and in particular for women, who are affected directly through loss of their jobs or pay cuts, or indirectly through budget cuts in public services and welfare. for this reason, with this text we deplore the fact that policy responses to the crisis have failed to rectify the gender impact of the crisis and we call on the member states to ensure that the measures taken are long term in scope, and do not undermine welfare policies and public sector structures, such as social services and care facilities, healthcare, education and workers’ rights, that are a precondition for greater gender equality.
in writing. − the world economy has experienced a series of successive crises since 2008: the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat fraud. the latter factor, in my view, has been underestimated by european governments, which immediately adopted fiscal stimulus measures and only subsequently defined budgetary savings plans to stop the spiral of public deficits. the consolidation of the budgets of the member states has largely obscured the social crisis which has hit europe, particularly women. in 2011, 31.6% of women worked part-time; the phenomenon is so widespread that the european commission does not express itself in terms of 'part-time work' but of 'part-time unemployment'. in my view, one of the first levers of action to tackle the problem is through education and training, both initial and continuing, to enable women to adapt to the evolution of the labour market. in this context, the european social fund should also be mobilised, along with all other european programmes, to promote greater social inclusion. the commission should also use the economic recovery plans to strengthen women's rights and include the gender equality dimension in all aspects of the multiannual financial framework 2014-2020.
