in writing. − the proposal for a decision on the overseas association was approved by the commission on 16 july 2012 and is currently being negotiated in the council. this includes the design of the multiannual financial framework for the financing of eu cooperation with african, caribbean and pacific states and overseas countries and territories. the objectives of this planning are, inter alia, the progressive reduction and consequent elimination of poverty in these territories and the economic and social development of the octs. the commission has proposed full budgetisation of the edf from 2021 onwards and a maximum total amount to be allocated to the 11th edf, which will also include an allocation for each acp country, irrespective of its level of development. i therefore express a favourable opinion.
in writing. - i voted in favour of parliament's resolution on the european council conclusions on the multiannual financial framework because i believe it is essential that this house express its own position on a subject so crucial for the future of the union, although unfortunately it is unsatisfactory in several respects. parliament rightly rejects the council's position, calling for greater involvement in the decision-making process to ensure genuine democratic representation. in particular, it is desirable to increase the flexibility of the financial framework itself, so as to allow for adjustments and corrections 'in progress' should urgent difficulties arise, such as those we have seen in previous years. we must learn from past mistakes to be more courageous and more timely. i particularly appreciate the strong call for an increase in the own resources available to the eu, although it would have been appropriate to specify better how these resources can be recovered, by outlining a strategy that would give a sign of discontinuity with the strict austerity policies implemented so far. it is now up to the european council to take parliament's views and suggestions into account, showing a willingness to cooperate and a genuine community spirit.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution in response to the conclusions of the european council last february on the multiannual financial framework. the council had requested a reduction in the commitments of the european budget for the next seven years (2014-2020) of 8% - compared to the european commission's 2012 proposal. considering the current financial programming period (2007 - 2013), we are faced with a decrease of about 5%. the council did not consider that, in the current economic crisis, it was necessary to increase the overall budget of the union in order to finance important multiannual programmes in the fields of competitiveness, growth and education. the european budget must not be based on a short-term vision but on the long-term economic recovery, avoiding a further increase in the european deficit. in doing so, the european council is deliberately violating the treaty of lisbon by not respecting the european parliament's co-decision role in the community budget-making process. the resolution which i supported with my vote gives parliament a stronger bargaining power vis-à-vis the council.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the resolution tabled by the european parliament following the european council conclusions of 7 and 8 february 2013 on the multiannual financial framework as they do not reflect the priorities set for the seven-year period 2014-2020. i support the idea of finding a fair compromise with the council to ensure that the community budget is able to ensure the best possible implementation of the europe 2020 strategy by increasing investment in innovation, research and development. we strongly urge that we be equal players in the final decision on the european budget. it is not possible to adopt a budget with a view to restricting resources in an economic context in which the revival of growth and development is becoming a priority objective. i hope that a balance can be found between parliament and the council which sees as its final result the full satisfaction of an economic recovery which europe needs now more than ever.
in writing. - with this vote we wanted to send a strong signal of commitment and hope. on the one hand it is true that in a period of general austerity we cannot expect more, but on the other hand we must not allow resignation to prevail. parliament had set out clear priorities, which were to promote greater growth and development. the council decided instead to "snap out of it", with no prospects for the future: i am aware that europe too must adapt to the crisis situation, but i do not think it can give up the necessary impetus. infrastructure, energy, research, employment, immigration and agriculture are areas where the european union has great responsibilities and must therefore have the appropriate instruments to do so. we cannot accept that austerity rules should prevail in europe, after we have seen the damage it has done in the countries where it has been applied, starting with italy. what we are asking for is european financial planning that is not utopian, but not insufficient, and above all that parliament's voice be heard, which carries the voice and the alarm cries of the european citizens who elected it.
in writing. the rejection of the european budget is a strong signal to all governments: the way out of the crisis is through more modern economic planning. it is not possible at a time like this to sign an agreement which does not invest in growth and jobs. we are too far from expectations and cannot afford to take a step back that would make no sense. this proposal cuts all investment in research and innovation, youth employment, education and mobility.
in writing. - as regards the negotiations on the planning and approval of the mff, parliament expressed its full willingness to open full-scale negotiations with the council on matters of particular relevance, with a view to achieving a budget that meets the current needs of the member states and stimulates the growth of an economy in crisis, while ensuring compliance with the europe 2020 strategy. first of all, transparency on the political agreement on the mff is required in terms of both expenditure and revenue, as well as more information on the size of the national appropriations established under the cohesion and agricultural policies. in this resolution, parliament also expressed its negative opinion on the accumulation and deferral of unpaid payment claims for 2013, calling for these to be paid by the end of the current financial year. finally, i would like to stress the real desire to reach agreement on a reform of the system of own resources, pointing out that the financing of the union budget should be based on actual own resources, as provided for in the treaty. i therefore express a favourable opinion of this resolution.
in writing. - i supported the bowles report on the 'proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the european system of national and regional accounts in the european union'. this regulation lays down the rules to be used for compiling and publishing the reporting data which will then be compared with those of all member states in order to assess and monitor the real economic situation in the eu. i believe that it is essential to have reliable, reliable and comparable data on the economic structure and development of the economies of the member states.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mrs bowles' report because i think it best addresses and expresses the need to provide ever clearer and more consistent data on the national and regional accounts of the member states. in particular, the regulation lays down rules for the compilation and publication of key macroeconomic data in the eu. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos at work. producing timely macroeconomic data based on reliable criteria is essential to be able to conduct accurate analyses and avoid inappropriate readings.
in writing. − whereas much of european legislation takes the form of directives setting general standards and objectives, leaving the choice of how to achieve these objectives to the member states and local and regional authorities, and whereas the lack of accurate information and knowledge on the state of implementation and quantitative data concerning various environmental sectors hinders the proper implementation of the environmental acquis; i believe that regional and local authorities can strengthen the sense of cooperation and ensure better implementation of legislation in the formulation of eu environmental policies, and i voted in favour of the proposal, although i do not fully agree with all the points.
in writing. - i have decided to vote in favour of the report by mr bowles, as it seeks to identify rules for the compilation and publication of reporting data which will then be compared between the various member states in order to assess and monitor the economic reality of the union. these rules will ensure and increase the transparency of public accounts and improve the accessibility of information. in addition, member states will have to provide eurostat with information on their budgets and on the debt of public enterprises, the level of guarantees provided to public entities and pension obligations.
in writing. the proposed regulation provides for a more detailed european system of regional and national accounts for the european union and sets out uniform rules for the compilation of key macroeconomic data. this makes the data easier and more uniquely interpretable in comparisons between member states' economies. the problem of the cost of adopting the new procedure was raised, but parliament thought that the problem could be solved by means of automated systems that collect data in real time. the proposed amendments also aim to ensure that the information is more complete and more accurate, so that data can be obtained that are truly comparable, with reduced discretion, particularly for the public sector, so that the user can easily make use of the data. it also provides that the commission (eurostat) is to report regularly to parliament on the quality of data relating to national and regional accounts. on these grounds, i am in favour.
in writing. − this regulation lays down the rules to be followed for the compilation and publication of key macroeconomic data in the european union. the information provided must be as complete as possible and ensure maximum transparency, in particular as regards the public sector, in order to inform european citizens in the best possible way. i consider the concerns of the member states about possible administrative burdens to be well founded and therefore welcome the idea of opting, where possible, for the use of automated methods which allow real-time data collection.
in writing. - i did not vote in favour of mrs berès' report on flag state responsibility. although i believe it is important to improve the working conditions of seafarers on european ships, i consider that the nature of the measures proposed by parliament are disproportionate. on the one hand, they seem to be a way of forcing all member countries to ratify the maritime labour convention of 2006, and on the other, they impose surveillance measures that could lead to a paralysis of maritime trade.
in writing. − the maritime labour convention (mlc) signed in 2008 is about to be implemented into european law, providing for national enforcement. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. in addition, a maritime labour certification and a maritime labour declaration of conformity for each ship and close monitoring by flag states are provided for. the convention also ensures safe and uniform working conditions in all member states, marking a major step forward in this field. that is why i am in favour of it.
in writing. − the jensen report sets out the guidelines for the 2014 budget with the european parliament's priorities. i particularly agree with the text in that it analyses the importance of the eu budget for the implementation of the europe 2020 strategy, identifying the key areas on which it should focus: education, research and innovation, support for smes, entrepreneurship and employment, with particular attention to young people. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on the general guidelines for the preparation of the 2014 budget, section iii, as a proper definition of the 2014 budget will be crucial to lay the foundations for future economic growth that can lead to greater competitiveness, youth employment and development. the commission has also been asked to present a report on the implementation of the new multiannual financial framework for the period 2014-2020. the eu budget is an indispensable lever for economic growth, and inadequate funds could jeopardise the development of the eu's entire economy and the achievement of the europe 2020 objectives. the financing system for the eu budget is closely linked to national treasuries, and this represents a limitation, especially in times of crisis and budgetary constraints at national level. a reform of the union's revenue system is therefore essential to ensure that the european budget is more autonomous and, through enhanced synergy with national budgets, to promote the effective implementation of political commitments and priorities, as well as sustainable growth that supports education, innovation, infrastructure, smes and sustainable development as a whole.
in writing. - the economic situation in the european union is worrying. our economies have not yet recovered from the crisis and the downward spiral has not yet stopped. the european union has a duty to implement measures for growth and the role of the eu budget is crucial. parliament could not help but reject a draft budget which provided for cuts in expenditure in crucial areas such as research and development and education rather than fostering a genuine process of growth on a european scale. no more downside tradeoffs. we must now boost growth in europe and reduce unemployment. we have waited a long time for the european parliament to have a role in the process of adopting the eu budget. today parliament has sent an unmistakable signal in support of european citizens and businesses.
in writing. - the aim of today's vote is to break the vicious circle of the payment deficit: the unpaid invoices for 2012 and 2013 should not be carried over to the budget for the following year because 2014 - the first year of the new multiannual framework - must be able to start without a deficit contrary to european law. the accumulated year-on-year debt reached an unprecedented level of over eur 217 billion at the end of 2012: the commission must now commit itself to presenting a draft amending budget for last year's invoices by the end of this month at the latest, to ensure that the budget negotiations for next year are not compromised.
in writing. − as regards the regulation on the next multiannual financial framework, an opinion is being prepared on the budgetary forecasts and general guidelines for 2014, taking due account of the inherent needs arising from the financial crisis, which should spur and support member states towards a new economic growth that involves a reduction in youth unemployment and the revival of employment. in order to avoid the inconveniences already experienced in the past due to incorrect expenditure forecasts, it is desirable to make more careful planning and to adopt realistic and adequate estimates, which are as transparent as possible as to the use of the funds available. 2014 will also be a year of transition between two multiannual financial programming periods and for this very reason it will be helpful and essential to look at what was previously achieved with the last multiannual plan in order to obtain a more comprehensive overview of the projects to be implemented under the new mff. the latter will have to be based on the europe 2020 strategy, focusing on the so-called knowledge triangle (education, research, innovation) but giving particular attention to the development of small businesses, the use of renewable energy and sustainable development. i am in favour of these general guidelines.
in writing. − the 2014 budget, with the financial crisis still ongoing and the difficulties in finding a satisfactory agreement for all, will be drawn up in a context of great uncertainty. it is for these reasons that we must avoid the mistakes of the past and provide for an adequate and realistic level of payment appropriations. moreover, it is essential to base the union budget for 2014 on what has not been done so far, namely measures to support competitiveness and economic growth while boosting employment and combating youth unemployment.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on the composition of the european parliament for the 2014 elections because the solution proposed by the rapporteurs for the allocation of seats reflects proportionally the size of the populations of the member states. since the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, the european parliament has played a central role as co-legislator with the council, particularly in defining the multiannual financial framework, which is essential for implementing the european union's policies of economic growth and development. the european parliament is the european institution representing 500 million citizens. the elected parliamentarians must be able to exercise their mandate in defence of the rights of their fellow citizens and to express their needs in accordance with balanced criteria of representation which promote the economic and social cohesion of the territories.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution, rejoicing at the new colleagues from 12 observer countries who will soon be welcomed to the chamber, at croatia becoming an effective member on 1 july 2013 and, last but not least, at the unchanging number of meps who will represent italy in 2014: it wasn't a foregone conclusion. some states will have to give up some of their members: the biggest loser will be germany, which will go from its current 99 to 96. i also welcome the adoption by the european commission of a recommendation which gives the political parties in our parliament the opportunity to nominate a candidate for the presidency of the european commission, because this is the path of electoral democracy that the european citizens are asking for.
in writing. - with this document we have managed to reach a compromise to respect the limit of 751 members set by the lisbon treaty and at the same time allow the arrival of members from croatia. in this way no country will lose more than one member and no country will gain more.
in writing. − the next term of the european parliament will begin in 2014, and the composition of the european parliament will need to be redrawn in view of the accession of croatia, which currently has only 12 observers. these observers will be replaced by the same number of meps in 2014. moreover, with the current derogation from article 14 (2) of the treaty on european union (teu), the european parliament will, as of 2014, be composed of 751 members - compared to the current 754 - with the consequence that it is essential to think about a reorganisation and a redistribution of seats between member states, the total number of seats having to be reduced with the simultaneous introduction of 12 new seats. parliament will then have to submit a draft to the european council on the way in which seats will be redistributed. there have been many speculations in this respect, whether the criterion of degressive proportionality should be respected, or alternatively, the introduction of the 'fixed + support' method which would allocate six seats to each state, with the addition of a proportional criterion. i am in favour of the proposal to minimise the loss to the member states, while respecting the principle of proportionality as much as possible, by first redistributing seats between countries and then politically reallocating them.
in writing. − spirit drinks are classified into categories on the basis of the definitions set out in annex ii to regulation (ec) no 110/2008. in this way, the traditional nature of their composition and their particular recipes is ensured, while respecting regional characteristics based on the availability of ingredients. however, in the case of absinthe spirit, strict classification and definition of ingredients would not specifically respect the specificity of the production and therefore i am opposed to a regulation imposing restrictions in this respect. it would also be more appropriate to have a regulation which regulates regional specificities instead. i therefore oppose the adoption of the draft commission regulation amending annexes ii and iii to regulation (ec) no 110/2008 of the european parliament and of the council on the definition, description, presentation, labelling and the protection of geographical indications of spirit drinks.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the mandate for negotiations on the resolution by mr capoulas santos because i believe that it is necessary to give a strong signal of parliament's unity, to enable this institution to negotiate with greater strength and credibility with the council. in view of the many controversial points in this report, i believe that the long work carried out in the commission has led to a satisfactory result overall. the forecasts for crop diversification take due account of the size of the area under cultivation itself, reducing the burden on farmers, as well as the obligation to implement the new greening measures applicable only to large plots. i agree with the choice to leave it to the discretion of the member states to implement the small farmers scheme and all the rules relating to it, especially as regards payments, with the possibility therefore of taking due account of local peculiarities. the proposal to revise the lists of beneficiaries, so that the funds are allocated to those who actually carry out agricultural activities, and excluding those, in particular bodies and legal persons, who continue to benefit from aid because of a situation that is no longer current, is also very positive.

in writing. - i welcome today's vote on the reform of the common agricultural policy; the approach adopted and approved by the european parliament's agriculture committee last january has been confirmed. this is the end of a long and difficult process that started in october 2011 when we received the legislative proposals from the european commission. in view of the initial proposal and the criticisms that have emerged, i would say that the result achieved is positive and shows our commitment to modifying the commission proposal taking into account the italian context, specificities and interests, making the cap more flexible and less bureaucratic, protecting businesses and farmers' incomes on the one hand and food quality and safety on the other. the vote also has a symbolic value: for the first time thanks to the changes introduced in 2009 by the lisbon treaty the european parliament, the only democratically elected institution, has had an active and decisive role. we are therefore entering the trilogue phase with the council and the commission with the aim and the hope of reaching an agreement leading to the final approval of the new common agricultural policy.
in writing. − the cap for the period 2014/2020 is a major challenge for european agriculture. much has changed for what has always been considered the quintessential european policy. the objectives and objectives have changed over time and an increasingly diverse global context has made the cap a policy that has adapted to the challenges of the moment, always ensuring that european farmers receive important support for their activities and for what their work represents in our civil society. my support for this report is a further indication of my unwavering commitment to farmers and their families, whose work must always be recognized and rewarded.
mr president, i would like to emphasize that this is the first time that parliament has been called upon to decide on the reform of the cap with full legislative powers. there are many factors at play, and it is difficult to strike a balance, but i think that the starting point for negotiations with the member states and the commission at the end of march and the beginning of april is a good basis. i would like to stress the intention of parliament to de-bureaucratize as much as possible everything that concerns the cap: it is absurd, for example, that farmers have to go through paperwork every year! we think that only when there are changes should the farmer apply for aid. i also think that it is important and fundamental, not only for the agricultural sector, which also has very impressive figures - 12 million enterprises, 10 million employees - but for all citizens, especially in this context. in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the decision on the opening of interinstitutional negotiations on the reform of the common agricultural policy and, in particular, on the related mandate on the financing, management and monitoring of the cap because i believe that the new measures contained in it will be able to give a boost to a sector, the agricultural sector, which is now in deep crisis. certain guidelines are needed to ensure that european farmers have an adequate income, a precise definition of 'active farmer' which will make it possible to grant concrete aid to those who actually carry out this activity, greater transparency in the funding provided and increasing simplification of bureaucracy, especially for smes and young farmers. today, there is a greater need to protect european agricultural products and fruit and vegetables, particularly those from southern europe, which are subject to competition from agricultural products from the other side of the mediterranean. in order to ensure the competitiveness of european production, priority should be given to shorter agri-food chains and the negotiation of trade agreements with third countries which bring about conditions of balance and reciprocity. we must protect our producers from selling their products below cost and promote competitive and sustainable agriculture which is in favour of territorial development and respectful of the environment.
in writing. − the new common agricultural policy must be able to guarantee a stable and high-quality food supply for all european consumers. the new cap will have the tools to make 'green' measures mandatory, introducing the flexibility needed to enable farmers to meet the new challenges of the markets. finally, a balance has been struck between food security and improved environmental protection: now the eu's new agricultural policy will be able to provide even more public goods for european citizens.
in writing. − the reform of the common agricultural policy plays a key role in the european economic policy, and therefore it is necessary to take into account challenges such as climate change, water and energy conservation, soil erosion and biodiversity. the result of comagri's work on the cap is to strike the right balance between 'greening' measures (corrected to avoid impact on farm production costs and questionable environmental effects) and market measures, while also reducing the bureaucratic burden of cap measures and their management and control. i also believe that it is essential that the new agricultural policy should encourage farmers to take care of the environment, by stimulating the creation of new jobs, by supporting women in agriculture and the professional farmer. unfortunately for italy, this means that there will be less money available overall, also because compared to the previous cap, the european countries that will share it will be 27 instead of 15.
in writing. - yesterday we voted on the reform of the common agricultural policy. being a farmer is a difficult business challenge, often dependent on atmospheric and environmental variables and characterised by harsh and prolonged working conditions. it is an example of sacrifice to work, in the face of which the complaint of those colleagues who asked yesterday in this house to suspend the voting sessions, which began at 12 noon, to give way to lunch and a lighter course of parliamentary work, which lasted for well over two hours, is shouting and hurting with the force of an insult. some colleagues may have lost touch with the reality that those who are already fortunate enough to have a job will certainly not complain if they start at noon and work for a few hours. the honourable members could have had a snack before noon, since the number of votes to be taken had been known for some time, and they should have remembered that working in brussels and strasbourg is a privilege, representing millions of citizens who, if they are lucky, work and often do so in uncomfortable conditions with the problem of making ends meet with their salary.
mr president, the positive aspects have already been mentioned: i also agree that we need a long-term perspective that ensures predictability of investments in low-carbon technologies, etc., etc. there are, however, a number of points which concern me very much, which is why i finally abstained from voting. i would remind you that the european union accounts for only 11% of global greenhouse gas emissions and is still the only international economic community to have adopted binding legislation on greenhouse gas emissions. i would remind you that we urgently need to adopt measures which will really contribute to economic recovery and employment. i would like to remind you of the public resistance to major projects in the energy and infrastructure sectors. i would remind you that it is of paramount importance that energy consumers be protected from further increases in the cost of energy. all this has not been taken into account and i also regret very much that paragraph 91 has been adopted, which calls for permanent amendments to the current rules on emissions trading.
in writing. - i agree with the european union's objectives of reducing greenhouse gas emissions by 80-95% by 2050: the eu is still the only international economic community to have adopted binding legislation on greenhouse gas emissions. we must, however, take account of the fact that there are some critical issues to be resolved, including the need to provide for measures to compensate for the increase in energy prices, which is an inevitable consequence of the decarbonisation process. in this respect, consumer protection is needed, as energy prices in europe are higher than in most of our global partners. i voted against paragraph 91 which calls for permanent amendments to the current emissions trading regulations: the proposed measures penalise industrial sectors through increased production costs and would severely curb growth and employment opportunities.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on the energy roadmap 2050 because it recognises the need for member states to work together to transform the energy system. this text sets the basis for proposing legislative initiatives on energy policy, with a view to developing a policy framework for 2030, including milestones and targets on greenhouse gas emissions, renewable energy and energy efficiency. i believe that, as energy infrastructure and installations typically take many years to complete and have a very long lifetime, we need to take action immediately setting up the right targets for the short, middle and long-term. i also welcome the importance of a social dimension being included in the roadmap, which encourages member states to cooperate in a spirit of solidarity, paying special attention to energy poverty and low-income vulnerable households that are most affected by higher energy prices.
in writing. − while welcoming the commission's commitment to explore the possibilities of achieving the union's decarbonisation target while ensuring security of energy supply, i am concerned that it has based decarbonisation scenarios on the assumption of global climate action but has not carried out any analysis to determine a scenario based on achieving high levels of energy efficiency. taking into account the variations in the energy mix between member states, it is necessary to address urgently the lack of studies in the commission's impact assessment on the social and economic implications of further greenhouse gas emission reductions for individual member states. these studies, in my view, could form the basis for the formulation of equitable long-term solutions in the energy sector. i believe that post-2020 commitments to new greenhouse gas emission reduction targets should be conditional on the commission presenting progress made, firstly, in implementing the 2020 reduction targets. the commission should also present a supplementary assessment offering suggestions to avoid the risk of carbon leakage due to the relocation of production outside the union.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mrs tzavela's report on the energy roadmap 2050. i think this text is very balanced and acceptable, especially when it focuses on the lack of flexibility in the commission's roadmap and on the scenarios envisaged. i support the rapporteur's view that it is essential to change the current approach to climate policy, which does not take account of the specificities of the various geographical areas and the socioeconomic realities of the individual regions of europe.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mrs tzavela's report which sets out a roadmap to 2050 in the energy sector because a long-term strategy is indispensable if we are to guarantee the social welfare and competitiveness of our industries. in the light of the eu's commitment to reduce co2 emissions by 80% by 2050, the balance achieved between safeguarding the autonomy of member states to decide on the energy mix best suited to their national circumstances and the need for strong coordination at community level to maintain the consistency of action is commendable. i share the strong call for the development of ccs technologies, the ets market, new technologies and alternative fuels. in particular, investment in renewable energy research is needed: energy policies must be supported alongside innovation policies to make a significant contribution to the recovery of the european economy and growth in all productive sectors.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because the importance of an energy policy for the european union at a time of economic and financial crisis such as the present one cannot be underestimated. energy can and must also play a role as a stimulus for growth and the creation of new jobs. improving energy efficiency, a greater commitment to the use of renewable energy and new energy infrastructure that is modern, intelligent and capable of enabling more flexible energy storage and use capacity, will have to be the pillars of the future european energy policy. the industrial sector must be given the necessary incentives to promote investment that can foster development and reduce co2 emissions at the same time. in this context, it is essential to establish common intermediate objectives also for 2030 and 2040, which therefore go beyond the 20-20-20 agenda. the ambition must be to have a green economy that is competitive in the world and capable of producing growth, jobs and prosperity.
in writing. - i am voting in favour of the report on the energy roadmap 2050 - a future with energy. at a time of economic and financial crisis such as the present one, the european union's energy policy cannot be underestimated. energy can and must also play a role as a stimulus for growth and the creation of new jobs. improving energy efficiency, greater commitment to the use of renewable energy and new modern, intelligent energy infrastructure capable of enabling more flexible energy storage and use capacity will have to be the pillars of future european energy policy. the industry needs to be given the necessary incentives to promote investments that can foster development and reduce co2 emissions at the same time. in this context, it is essential to establish common intermediate objectives also for 2030 and 2040, thus going beyond the 20-20-20 agenda. for these reasons, i am convinced that the way forward is a green economy, which is competitive in the world and capable of generating growth, jobs and prosperity.
in writing. − the 85% to 90% reduction in emissions compared with 1990 identified in the roadmap sets the path towards a decarbonised economy by 2050, which will require major investment in all sectors of activity and particularly in research. we have a long way to go . the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. in this scenario of emission reductions, energy efficiency is a cost-effective way to achieve energy saving targets. i understand that at this stage all technologies which can contribute to the reduction of emissions must be considered. although i voted in favour of the report, i would urge caution on the geological storage of carbon dioxide (ccs). the effects on the environment and the ecosystem are not yet known.
in writing. - we voted on mr tzavela's report during the sitting. the report welcomes the commission's energy roadmap 2050 and its objective of ensuring fair and universal access to a sustainable energy supply for all european citizens. the report recalls the competence of the member states to draw up their own energy plans but also stresses the importance of a community approach. renewable energy, energy efficiency, flexible infrastructure and training on energy issues are key elements of a long-term strategy.
in writing. - i have decided to vote in favour of the report by mrs tzavela, as it highlights the shortcomings of the commission's energy roadmap 2050. it also criticises the effectiveness of the current eu climate policy approach of binding, top-down limits that are the same for everyone (one-size-fits-all), and strongly calls for this approach to be reversed, taking into account the specific geographical and socio-economic realities of the member states and regions. the long-term (2050) objectives should therefore be measured at union rather than national level and not be based on binding milestones to 2030 and 2040. finally, it rightly insists on the wider energy mix, without prejudicial exclusions on any energy source and supply channel
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the energy roadmap for 2050. this report deals with a central issue for the union: the european union's energy policy. i recognise the strategic importance of the priorities set out in this roadmap for a long-term strategy. improving energy policy also means thinking about the future of europe and its industry, stimulating its competitiveness and also providing a social response: an efficient energy policy allows consumers to keep costs down considerably. the report stresses first of all the need to improve energy efficiency and savings as soon as possible and also urges the member states to cooperate with each other in order to complete the internal energy market and the necessary infrastructure. other important objectives set out in the report to be achieved by 2050 are diversification of sources and suppliers, the organisation of the gas market and the switch to renewable energy.
in writing. − energy policies are a very topical issue and of great interest to the european union, especially in the light of the europe 2020 strategy. the union's objective is to have a broad-ranging and longer-term strategic planning which can identify the main objectives and promote and support them in the most appropriate way. the targets for the next programming period are to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 80% to 95% by 2050 compared to 1990 levels, while the forecasts are based on certain assumptions about technological and economic developments. in this climate, member states are urged to prepare a fertile ground for new policies and objectives, and the union is committed to promoting crossborder infrastructure affecting many member states. i therefore express a favourable opinion.
in writing. - on the nuclear issue, a position must be taken, not least because after the serious tragedy at the fukushima plant in japan and even before chernobyl, it is necessary to reassure european citizens, member states hosting nuclear power stations and neighbouring states, that health and safety are priority issues for the eu. it is the duty of the institutions to ensure maximum transparency by closing obsolete plants and taking more stringent measures to avoid the least risk and by requiring that stress tests be carried out on nuclear power stations on our territory as well as those built in countries bordering the eu. it is also essential to apply strict measures not only on the operation of the plants but also on the disposal of waste. last but not least, we must engage in dialogue with citizens and local authorities, respecting their views and wishes.
in writing. - exactly two years after the fukushima disaster, the european union is preparing to revise the nuclear safety directive. in today's resolution parliament calls for guarantees for the safety of the installations and the treatment of waste to protect european citizens. i believe that stress tests are useful in improving safety culture; we are aware that the implications of nuclear safety are transnational: we need to find a common line of action. i believe we must avoid that investment in security has a negative impact on the price of energy for businesses and citizens, who are already bearing the brunt of the crisis.
in writing. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' in the context of the directive. the european parliament expects the results of the stress test of 145 reactors in the union and 20 outside it to help promote a culture of nuclear safety in europe. as a result of the stress tests, some countries have started to implement measures to improve the safety of their power plants. however, the stress tests initiated by the commission and ensreg were limited in scope and were aimed at assessing the robustness and ability of nuclear power plants to cope with extreme external events. stress tests cannot therefore replace in-depth safety inspections of nuclear power plants which are the national responsibility of the member states. the house also called for the commission to be given the power to adopt a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to carcinogens and to the risk of carcinogens being released into the environment. the commission has also concluded that the measures in question are not imputable to the state and that the state aid is imputable to the state. parliament recommended that the union should support international efforts to develop safety standards as high as possible.
in writing. - on the safety of nuclear power stations, parliament adopted a motion for a resolution calling on all national authorities in the european union to carry out a comprehensive assessment of the risks and reliability of the safety of nuclear power stations in their territories. the responsibility for such controls lies primarily with the member states, as reaffirmed by council directive 2009/71/euratom of 25 june 2009. however, we all know about the very painful nuclear disaster that occurred in 2011 at the fukushima daiichi nuclear power plant in japan. the commission has also examined the impact of the measures on the environment and the environment protection. the purpose of these procedures is to monitor constantly the situation of nuclear power stations and their safety, in order to avoid the recurrence of disastrous events, the consequences of which, as is well known, also affect the populations of neighbouring countries. parliament therefore called on all member states to carry out regular monitoring of nuclear power stations and to report on the results obtained in a completely transparent and clear manner, so that citizens could also be freely informed about the data. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. − i strongly back this resolution because it points to the need for member states to transpose measures agreed at eu level on fighting extremism and racism into national law. i believe that europe must be at the forefront in promoting a culture of respect, acceptance and tolerance. for this reason, fighting racism and xenophobia, in both the private and public sphere must be an eu priority. the only way to start hindering this enormous problem is by ensuring that bias-motivated offences – such as these with racist, xenophobic and homophobic intent – are punishable within criminal law systems. in addition, these offences must be properly recorded and effectively investigated, and victims must be offered proper assistance, protection and compensation. one big problem to be faced is that many crimes still remain unreported because of a lack of trust in the reaction of institutions, particularly in the context of an economic crisis, where scapegoats are easily blamed.
in writing. the european parliament adopted a resolution on the situation in the democratic republic of congo. the resolution stressed that all forms of intolerance and discrimination must remain unacceptable in the european union. the commission, the council and the member states must step up the fight against hate crime and discriminatory attitudes and behaviour. parliament called for a comprehensive strategy to combat hate crime, prejudice-based violence and discrimination. member states are invited to take all appropriate measures to encourage the reporting of such offences and of any other form of crime based on racism and xenophobia, while ensuring adequate protection for reporting persons and victims of offences of a racist or xenophobic nature. parliament called on the eu to support training programmes for judicial and law enforcement authorities and relevant eu bodies in the fight against discriminatory practices and hate crime and called for a wider collection of reliable data on hate crime, as well as for the development of mechanisms to make hate crime visible in the eu.
in writing. − social issues are one of the pillars of eu policies, and in this context the eu has adopted a number of instruments to combat discrimination, such as council directive 2000/43/ec implementing the principle of equal treatment between persons irrespective of racial or ethnic origin and council directive 2000/78/ec establishing a general framework for equal treatment in employment and working conditions. in many eu countries, intolerance towards ethnic minorities is still common, as in austria, where the right-wing populist party allows and encourages a rising level of hate crime, or in hungary, where incitement to hatred is directed at the roma population, often branded as unfit for coexistence. it is intolerable that racism or intolerance still exists and the issue becomes even more odious when it is an integral part of the politics of a country. the resolution calls on the commission, the council and the member states to launch a strategy against these crimes and for the eu to sign the united nations convention on the elimination of all forms of racial discrimination (uncerd). the resolution meets with my favourable opinion.
in writing. − article 35 of the treaty underlines that the protection of human health is an important element of the european union's policy. the current research reports on endocrine disruptors and their effects on humans and animals reveal a worrying trend: in the last two decades, there has been a dramatic increase in hormone-related disorders worldwide. the main problem is that endocrine disruptors are everywhere in our daily lives: the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council should be given the opportunity to discuss the matter with the council and the european parliament. as one of the cornerstones of the european union's chemicals policy is the precautionary principle, i agree with the rapporteur in urging the commission to take all appropriate measures to strengthen the safety criteria for citizens first. it is particularly important, in my view, that endocrine disruptors be labelled in chemicals for those categories of products - such as textiles - with which children come in contact in particular.
in writing. - i did not support the westlund report on the protection of public health from endocrine disruptors. i think that this text is too alarmist and unbalanced, leading to the view that the reactions of the endocrine system to chemical substances (natural or synthetic) are dangerous a priori. we need to take a more balanced approach, and it is essential that the legislation in force provides for appropriate screening tests, based on criteria based on a full risk assessment.
in writing. − determined action is needed by introducing a screw-in for hormone-disrupting chemicals, reducing exposure to so-called 'endocrine disruptors'. in the last two decades, more and more people in europe have begun to suffer from hormonal disorders. we must act now, by addressing all potential endocrine disruptors such as steroid hormones, certain pesticides, dioxins and plastic additives.
in writing. - i am opposed to the text of the report which is part of the work on the definition of criteria for the identification of endocrine disrupting substances, as it takes an excessively alarmist tone: the danger-based approach and therefore the a priori application of the precautionary principle could lead to the indiscriminate prohibition of entire groups of chemicals which might otherwise prove to be safe. in short, the perspective is to regard the reactions of the endocrine system to chemicals (natural or synthetic) as dangerous a priori. a more sensible approach should instead be based on the who definitions of 'endocrine disruptor' and 'adverse effect', with a case-by-case assessment based on un-defined criteria. i think it is essential to set a threshold for each chemical substance, beyond which, according to scientific evidence, there may be risks to the health of citizens.
in writing. − health protection is an important element of eu policies as enshrined in article 35 of the treaty, and is closely linked to the precautionary principle (article 191). in recent years there has been an increase in diseases linked to hormonal dysfunctions which have caused more or less serious problems such as the impossibility of conception, or the increase in the incidence of breast cancer, which in the united states has doubled since 1980. this cannot be linked to genetic changes alone, but is undoubtedly influenced by external factors such as lifestyle habits, drug use, stress or poor diet or a combination of these. the presence of endocrine disruptors is therefore undeniable, but it is difficult to carry out a thorough investigation of these substances to establish a cause and effect relationship, but it is impossible for the consumer to protect himself, given their widespread use in many areas of our daily lives. i am in favour of this resolution which proposes to review and develop all the relevant legislation, providing for more targeted controls on particular types of products such as those intended for children, and perhaps providing for a classification of endocrine disruptors.
in writing. - i believe that the hirsch report's sole purpose is to ensure the entry of immigrants into the labour market and into the world of politics. the rapporteur is supporting her arguments by presenting partial, incomplete data, with a clear manipulative and biased intent, aimed at offering an unrealistic picture of the needs and priorities of our society. for these reasons i did not support this text.
in writing. i have already spoken in this chamber the other night about some of the puzzling aspects of this report, and i wonder how it is possible that anyone can even think about some of the things. i refer in particular to a point in the text which states that irregular migrants should be able to participate in the social, political and economic life of the country in which they are: someone should explain to me how this could be possible, since they are illegal immigrants, therefore illegal. fortunately, an amendment has been adopted which has removed this paragraph, but the problem remains: how can europe think of managing and solving the problems of immigration if it comes to propose such solutions? as i have said on other occasions, in my scale of assessment of employment and social policies, the tuscans should come first, then the italians, the europeans and then the regular immigrants. for those who are not regular, therefore who do not respect the law, there can and must be no preferential treatment: this is also to protect the immigrants themselves who are in compliance with all the rules. it is not by false optimism and such improvisations that europe can solve its problems.
in writing. - 2013 is the european year of citizens, so the issue of immigration is even more pressing. it is now seen as a resource which can act as a barrier to the gradual decline in the working age population and the shortage of skilled workers. in 2000, about a quarter of jobs were created by immigrants. it would be desirable, however, that the migrant population should have equal opportunities to access even highly qualified jobs, and for this to happen it is necessary to provide for a commitment on the part of both the host and the country of origin to guarantee equal levels of education and to eliminate all kinds of barriers to access to the labour market. the introduction and respect of the 'culture of integration' is therefore called for, which concerns not only the world of work but also participation in social and political life, and which distinguishes europe as a continent from the culture of welcome. a number of infrastructures will therefore have to be put in place to ensure adequate integration. i therefore express my favourable opinion.
in writing. − despite a communitywide ban, asbestos is still found in buildings, pipes, trains, ships and schools. according to the who, there are 20 to 30 thousand cases of asbestos-related diseases in the eu every year. and that number continues to grow. i would like to stress, however, that the european parliament legislates on policies relating to the registration of asbestos, the vocational training of construction workers and maintenance workers, the development of removal programmes and the recognition of asbestos-related diseases. yet just last week, asbestos was leaked from a factory in the course of work at the strasbourg site. needless to say, the question of the second location and its associated costs is coming back to the fore in good time, as all these incidents could have been avoided.
in writing. − according to the world health organisation, the number of asbestos-related illnesses reported each year in the european union alone is between 20 and 30 thousand, and it is estimated that more than 300 thousand european citizens could die of cancer by 2030. the lack of information from many member states prevents reliable mortality forecasting in europe. in this context, i believe that information and training of citizens and the exchange of best practice between member states are essential for the diagnosis of asbestos-related diseases. i agree with the rapporteur in urging the commission to draw up a study to record the problems caused by the use of asbestos in each member state and to identify, where necessary, targeted actions for its removal. i would also draw the commission's attention to the need to promote research and remediation activities aimed at preventing the production of single fibres and/or destroying the crystalline latticework similar to asbestos fibres. finally, i believe that controls should be strengthened to require all interested parties, in particular those involved in the treatment of asbestos waste in landfills, to classify any waste containing asbestos as hazardous waste to be disposed of only in specific landfills.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mr hughes' report because i strongly share the main objective of the text: to eliminate all residual asbestos deposits. i also find the other proposals put forward by the rapporteur extremely interesting: the eu must raise the issue of asbestos dumping in developing countries and apply diplomatic pressure to exporting countries to stop mining by preventing ships transiting eu routes from calling at or using port facilities and temporary storage facilities in the eu.
in writing. this report focuses on the health risks from the presence of asbestos in the workplace: i would say that we are almost at the grotesque point, considering that asbestos was found in this very european parliament in strasbourg, no later than two weeks ago. but the question is unfortunately very serious and dramatic: the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat asbestos in the community. the case of eternit is perhaps the best known, and just yesterday the turin prosecutor's office called for a severe punishment for the people responsible for the swiss multinational; in tuscany too, the number of workers affected by asbestos-related diseases is impressive, mainly linked to the shipyards where ships were built filled with this very dangerous substance. the negative effects of asbestos persist over time, and it is therefore necessary to achieve a complete removal of asbestos from many buildings, both public and private. the european union must also work with its trading partners to ensure that they too eliminate any possible danger linked to this substance, which has caused too many victims, often unaware of the risks they faced in their daily workplace.
in writing. - i am in favour of this report, as direct exposure to asbestos fibres continues to cause considerable biological, moral, social and environmental damage to the populations concerned. i believe it is important to protect the health of citizens, which is closely linked to the quality of the environment in which they live and work. a european plan for the census and remediation of all european asbestos sites should be activated in order to inform and protect future generations. it is of concern that the worldwide extraction, processing and use of asbestos fibres has only been transferred and concentrated in developing countries (china, india, russia). in fact, asbestos consumption has increased exponentially over the last decade. europe must commit itself to the drafting of an international convention that will ban extraction, trade and use in all those countries where there is no protection for workers and the community.
in writing. - i have decided to vote in favour of the report by mr hughes, which calls for action to be taken to identify asbestos deposits still existing within the union, with a view to their elimination. the rapporteur's calls for the eu to exert international pressure, particularly on developing third countries, are particularly welcome. the commission is also being asked to ensure that ships carrying asbestos cannot dock or use port infrastructure or temporary storage facilities when transiting through community waters.
in writing. − asbestos is a known source of serious disease and there is no maximum exposure threshold below which it mitigates its destructive effects on human health. however, there are still too many areas in europe where there are no measures to mitigate these effects and often, especially during renovation work on old buildings, workers come into contact with asbestos without protective measures. given that poland is the only member state to date to have implemented an action plan for an asbestos-free country, it seems urgent to plan for european union action to censor asbestos through public registers and plan for its final removal by 2028. a training plan is also provided for workers potentially exposed to asbestos. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the european parliament's right of initiative, the right to vote and the right to stand as a candidate in elections. i therefore vote in favour.
in writing. asbestos is the second most polluting substance in europe, after nuclear power stations. so any parliamentary initiative to eradicate this terrible scourge, which threatens everyone, no one excluded, can only be welcomed. but more needs to be done, much more. i am thinking, for example, of the introduction of the already tried and tested methods of disposing of asbestos, alternatives to landfilling, by productive recovery of the waste. but i am thinking above all of the ex-legislature's assertion that those responsible for this environmental disaster, who have become immensely rich at the expense of the citizens, are called upon to bear the very high costs of cleaning up and securing the contaminated sites. we cannot expect that the potential victims of asbestos should also pay the price necessary to free themselves from a threat on which the executioner has indecently speculated.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the berlinguer report analysing the proposal for a statute for the european mutual fund. the text is intended to facilitate the development of crossborder mutual societies by providing the member states with the appropriate legal instruments to enable them to do so. i consider it essential to emphasize that the statute is not intended to replace the laws of the various member states or to bring them into line, and that, bearing in mind the importance of protecting the specific features of the national legal systems, one of its essential objectives is to remove the obstacles which currently prevent crossborder cooperation between mutual societies.
in writing. - mutual funds are voluntary groups of natural or legal persons whose purpose is to meet the needs of the members rather than to obtain a return on investment; they shall operate in accordance with the principles of voluntary membership and solidarity between members and shall be managed in accordance with democratic principles, thereby contributing to responsible and sustainable management. they play an important role within the countries of the union by providing social and insurance services at lower costs and access to credit for members with low or near-zero interest rates. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the rules on the protection of employees are applied in the member states. such a statute would also make it possible to extend the widespread use of the model among the member states, some of which do not provide for regulation of this type of company, and would allow mutual societies to operate on a european scale but also across borders, by carrying out cross-border mergers or transformations and the creation of genuine european mutual societies. i therefore express a favourable opinion.
in writing. − i voted for this resolution because the alarming situation in egypt cannot be ignored. in particular i strongly support this text as it call on member states to made efforts aimed at facilitating the return of misappropriated assets stolen by the former regime to the people of egypt. i believe in the necessity to establish an eu team of investigators, lawyers and prosecutors to deliver legal support and assistance to egyptian authorities in this process. i would like to emphasise that, beyond its economic significance, assets recovery can contribute to bolstering justice and accountability in the egyptian institutional system and it is therefore an issue of great symbolic importance in relations between the eu and egypt.
in writing. - i believe that the european union should seriously consider withdrawing financial support to egypt until significant progress is made in the field of human rights and democracy. as a first step, the death sentences of the 21 football fans involved in the port said tragedy must be immediately commuted to prison sentences and a moratorium on all capital sentences in progress must be approved immediately. the aim is to break the spiral of violence that the country is sinking into, by bringing to justice anyone who commits crimes against women and women's rights activists in the country.
in writing. − i voted for this resolution because the humanitarian situation in the dprk is deeply alarming. the dprk government does not allow any political opposition or freedom of information. the justice system is subservient to the state and the death penalty is applied for a broad range of crimes against the state. moreover the dprk state authorities systematically carry out extrajudicial killings, arbitrary detentions and disappearances, interning more than 200 000 people in prison and ‘re-education’ camps. as for the nuclear threat, i strongly believe that until we accept that nuclear weapons are abhorrent and a grave danger no matters who possesses them, we are unlike to make meaningful progress in halting the spread of these devices. for this reason we need to intensify worldwide efforts for nuclear disarmament.
in writing. − north korea's recent history is marked by political, social and cultural regression. this is evident from recent developments concerning nuclear threats or the declaration of the nullity of the armistice with south korea and the united states, following a hard line by the un security council. this has obviously reignited tensions between the above countries, with frequent threats from the dprk. in terms of social conditions, the north korean people do not enjoy freedom of access to information or the right to free elections or freedom of expression. the european union has spoken out against the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction, with a strategy adopted by the european council in december 2003, and against the unjustified restriction of the freedoms of the population. the resolution underlines the condemnation of the dprk's nuclear threat attitude towards other states and calls for the restoration of its commitments to a moratorium on missile tests and the ratification of the treaty on the total nuclear test ban, and calls for the establishment of a special united nations commission of inquiry into the human rights situation in the dprk. i am in favour of this.
in writing. the report by mr belder analyses very precisely the many critical points which remain in relations between europe and china and is not afraid to denounce many uncomfortable situations, calling for a rapid reversal of course. i am referring, for example, to the call for greater attention to human rights, for a genuine process of democratization, for compliance with the rules of the international labour organisation. for all these reasons, which i share, i voted in favour of this text.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report on eu-china relations, as it is not afraid to denounce many problematic aspects, including: the concept of strategic partnership is called for. the member states are called upon to refrain from undertaking bilateral foreign policy initiatives which would jeopardise the efforts of the eeas. they would like to see substantial progress in democratization within the chinese communist party. china is invited to respect minimum social standards and the rules of the international labour organisation. we are concerned about the continued application of the death penalty in a country where trials are not considered to be fully transparent. they deplore the chinese authorities' control and censorship of the internet. this de facto rule removes any limitation on the possibility of censorship. the chinese government is invited to engage the tibetan and uighur peoples in a responsible and meaningful way in matters related to the governance of their territories, while respecting their religion. the chinese government is urged to grant official recognition to religions other than the officially recognized ones, eliminating the requirement of registration.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mr belder's report because i believe that at this time of change in china (we are in fact on the eve of the appointment of the new leader, xi jinping), it is important to underline our willingness to deepen and improve the strategic partnership between europe and the people's republic of china. we also appreciate the enormous progress that china has been able to make in a very short period of time. we would nevertheless like to call on the chinese authorities to make an effort to promote the democratic rights of their citizens and we support their activism. there are still some areas where we would like to see further progress made: think about censorship, poor food security, one-child policy, low religious tolerance. we believe that china's new hierarchy can lead the country into a new era, but only if it takes into account the dreams, and the rights, of its citizens.
in writing. - diplomatic relations between the european union and china have been in place since may 1975 and have been considerably intensified since the signing of the cooperation agreement in 1985. however, while economic relations between china and the european union are seen as growing, it is time to focus attention on the humanitarian conditions of the chinese people. for example, from the point of view of the certainty of law enforcement, in 2007, president hu jintao ruled that judges must submit to three authorities: the party, the people and the law, in the order indicated; lawyers must pledge allegiance to the chinese communist party to obtain a license to practice. abortion is also inflicted during the last months of pregnancy, respecting the one-child rule. freedom of association and expression is still far from being a guaranteed right, and only five religions are considered and tolerated. in view of this, and welcoming the economic progress made by china and its opening up to other markets, and hoping for their continued growth, this resolution, which i support, is intended to call on the chinese government to find a solution to the social ills plaguing the country.

in writing. − on monday 4 february 2013, europol announced that it had uncovered a large criminal network responsible for the manipulation of football matches across europe and 50 people have been arrested so far. the world of football and sport in general is afflicted by a serious pathology of sports betting. the huge sums of money that circulate in this area spoil the outcome and the genuineness of sports matches, compromising their validity. given the fundamental importance of sport also in the process of individual growth, it is important to keep sports out of the market logic that affects their results. the resolution therefore calls on the member states to ensure the implementation of the declaration on the specific characteristics of sport and its social function in europe to be taken into account in the implementation of common policies, adopted at the nice european council in december 2000, and to impose a maximum ceiling on the remuneration of sportsmen and sportswomen which does not detract from the predominantly recreational nature of sport. i am in favour of this.
