mr president, the european parliament has just decided to refer back to the relevant committees the directive on the timing of greenhouse gas auctioning arrangements, which i agree with because i am against the back-loading proposal. environmental protection - let me be clear - is our top priority, but in this time of crisis, back-loading would have led to a general increase in energy costs which, combined with a significant contraction in production, would have helped to slow down the recovery in the sectors most affected by the crisis, as well as creating further uncertainty for investors. it was not appropriate to ask more of european companies, especially energy-intensive companies. the european commission, before imposing new and more intransigent rules on european companies, must demand that reciprocity rules be respected with non-eu countries that do not agree to be part of a global climate agreement and therefore produce in the absence of adequate environmental protection rules.
in writing. - while expressing a positive view of the ets as a means of regulating and progressively reducing carbon dioxide emissions, i have decided to vote against the european commission's proposal to re-modulate the auction calendar and withdraw some 900 million greenhouse gas emission allowances from the market in order to increase their price. in a period of crisis, economic stagnation and difficulties for the competitiveness of european manufacturing industry, an artificial increase in prices could have meant a further aggravation of the crisis for many industries, especially for those "energy-intensive". in my region, sardinia, the cost of energy for industry is already unsustainable and is the main cause of the closure of many factories and the thousands of unemployed or in cash. a measure designed to artificially increase the price of the certificates would have put at risk the factories which still resist and frustrated the interest of some investors in taking over those which had already closed. if the european emissions trading system needs updating, then work should be done on structural reforms to ensure that companies can also plan for the medium to long term.
in writing. - i voted against the commission's proposal for a backloading mechanism for co2 emissions trading, because there are too many concerns about this initiative. i have always had doubts about this system, and in particular about its actual effectiveness in helping to reduce co2 emissions, a laudable objective which certainly deserves support. in the light of the poor results achieved by the ets, and even more so in the light of the inherent problems which have emerged in conjunction with the economic crisis and the contraction in industrial production, it may be worthwhile to consider alternative solutions. the commission's attempt to intervene in an existing system which was assured of being able to self-regulate, with the sole purpose of artificially increasing the price of emission allowances, is a reflection of these difficulties and would represent an undue distortion of a market on which many investors rely, as well as a further burden on already tried and tested undertakings.
in writing. - discussions on this subject cannot be left without a thorough reflection on the development model we want and how to achieve it. in the present economic climate we cannot afford to have two commissions working to conflicting conclusions and we must coordinate our efforts better. i believe that at the moment, in these circumstances, a mandate to negotiate cannot be given until parliament has been able to agree on how to achieve the environmental policy objectives and how to compensate for the losses that the industrial sector is expected to suffer, especially in terms of employment. in the absence of a serious and credible strategy, environmental issues will have to undermine the economic well-being of thousands of families who depend on the industrial sector for their livelihood.
in writing. - i voted against the proposal to amend the rules on co2 emissions trading which was intended to freeze temporarily 900 million tonnes of co2 allowances with the aim of raising the price (or at least containing the fall). without forgetting the fight against climate change, i believe that, at this time of crisis and economic difficulties, backloading would have led to the closure or relocation of our companies outside the eu, as the minimum price for co2 allowances would have been set by the european commission, not the market, as has been the case so far. it should be said that the emissions market has not always been an incentive for the use of clean technologies, so the whole system would probably have to be rethought, with the eventual overcoming of this mechanism.
in writing. - i voted in favour of rejecting the european commission's proposal to artificially change the price for ets emission allowances. the introduction of this mechanism, which is itself rather questionable, was intended to sell these shares on the free market, at prices determined by supply and demand. the european commission was surprised by a drastic reduction in the cost of these emissions, which should be welcomed, since the environmental objective would be achieved at a lower cost to producers and polluters. the word pollution should not be understood in the usual negative sense of the term, but as an obvious result of a production process, which cannot therefore be eliminated. the european union would do well to ask itself why the prices of this system have fallen, which is due to the lower productivity of european industry: if the back-loading measure had been passed, the situation would certainly have worsened dramatically, and in a time of crisis like this we cannot afford to have more companies close, with a consequent, predictable and unsustainable decline in employment.
in writing. − the european union emissions trading system (eu ets) is a key tool for cost-efficient reduction of eu industrial emissions and since the start of the second trading period in 2008, emissions have been reduced by more than 10%. although i do not fully agree with the rapporteur, i voted in favour of the proposal, believing that the commission should have the power to adjust the auction calendar adopted pursuant to article 10 (4) of directive 2003/87/ec.
in writing. − the current economic crisis has caused an oversupply of greenhouse gas emission certificates, causing their price to fall on the market. the european commission, which has the power to manage this system, has put forward a proposal for artificial intervention to correct the natural course of the market. as chairman of the itre commission i am opposed to the commission's back-loading proposal. back-loading is the temporary withdrawal of emission allowances from the market. firstly, i believe that you cannot intervene in a market which is designed to be free. in addition, the current european economic crisis, which has particularly affected the manufacturing and steel sectors, cannot support an additional energy cost. our priorities are growth and jobs: a new tax on the crisis is not the way to achieve our objectives.
in writing. − in view of a cost-efficient reduction of eu industrial emissions, the eu emissions trading scheme (eu ets) has proved useful, producing an emission reduction of 10%. in fact, this can be seen as partly a consequence of the economic and financial crisis which has drastically reduced commercial and productive activities. the system is therefore faced with serious imbalances, with a significant surplus of allowances on offer, with an upward trend. the price of carbon has therefore fallen significantly, and this has led to a decline in investment in low-carbon technologies. short-term and long-term measures are therefore necessary to remedy this imbalance by adjusting the auction calendar for allowances also for the third period. i therefore express a favourable opinion.
in writing. - mr president, i am voting in favour of the report as a political act with the value of facilitating and building consensus around the objectives of europe 2020 and the principles on which the eu ets is based. it is reasonable to support the work of icao and offer a conciliatory gesture on a matter which has been hotly debated in the institutions and in the courts. the temporary amendment to directive 2003/87/ec is therefore a good thing, but in a context of clarity that encourages concrete steps towards a global emissions governance policy: more explicitly, i agree with the net declaratory in the interest of legal certainty; i agree with the limitation to the year 2012 for reasons of fairness and market transparency. i agree with the statement, which must be made clear at the time of approval, that this derogation is linked to substantial results of the work of the icao assembly, with a roadmap that does not expose the assembly to the risk of seeing an established strategy enshrined in the fundamental documents and constituent international agreements being dismantled. in this sense, the investment constraint on the proceeds of the auctions for the purpose of implementing a global mbm should also be assessed positively.
in writing. - i am in favour of this measure. the contents of the report are not exactly what i wanted, but in times of crisis we must act quickly and get as close as possible to the intended results. the speed with which this measure has come to a vote before this house shows how efficient and conscientious our colleagues have been in following up this dossier in the envi and tran committees.
in writing. − protecting the european market, and not only the european market, from any distortions that could jeopardise its results is one of the main tasks of this institution. i voted in favour; i think it is right to include the aviation sector in the ets precisely to ensure equal treatment and avoid possible (and just) complaints. it is also important to remember that there are other issues at stake in the issue of greenhouse gas emission trading. the debate is much broader. we have expressed our deep concern with the epp about the proposal to withdraw from the market the quantity of allowances needed to bring the price up. this proposal calls into question the competitiveness of the whole european manufacturing sector. the crisis has brought the problem of the cost of energy to our companies into sharper focus. it is the main item of expenditure in the budgets. many companies, i am thinking for example of the manufacturing sector, faced with a further increase in the cost of energy (the first consequence if the measure were to pass) would be forced to close down. a thorough and rapid reflection on this subject is therefore necessary, followed (within a reasonable time) by the facts. i am thinking of concrete measures to bring growth back, not measures which would further stifle business, big and small.
in writing. − in 2008, after long and careful deliberation, the european parliament and the council reached agreement on the inclusion of aviation in the eu's greenhouse gas emissions trading system (ets). the rationale behind the inclusion of aviation was the need to address the rapid increase in greenhouse gas emissions from the sector. the commission proposal offers an opportunity to make it unequivocally clear that it is not the european union which is standing in the way of an international agreement. i voted in favour of the proposal, agreeing that reaching an agreement within icao is the preferred solution for all, including the european union.
in writing. - this vote avoids interference with the emissions trading system designed to cut greenhouse gas production, which needs a major overhaul.
in writing. - greenhouse gas emissions from air traffic are continuing to increase: since the 1990s, it's actually doubled. the decision to include aviation in the ets is an important choice to limit the negative environmental effects of climate change; however, this decision will only make sense if we can reach a global agreement. the european commission has put forward a proposal to grant third countries a temporary derogation from the ets for a period of one year. the aim is to reach a global agreement on the co2 emissions system. i am in favour of the commission's proposal: europe must send a strong signal of its commitment to climate change to the rest of the world and facilitate this process of accession by third countries.
in writing. − the aviation system is now producing significant amounts of greenhouse gas emissions, which are expected to increase in the coming years. for this reason, it is considered that aviation should be included in the european union emissions trading scheme (ets). the legislation received unanimous support from the council and a large majority in parliament. despite objections to this initiative by airlines, the committee on transport noted that 'the inclusion in the community scheme of trading in emission allowances of third country aircraft arriving or departing from community airports is legally admissible'. the court of justice confirmed this in 2011. the impact of such legislation on the cost of flights for passengers is very small and depends on the length of the journey. however, arrangements are needed to conclude an international agreement in a short time. i am in favour of this.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the package on strengthening the banking sector presented by mr karas because i believe it is a great step forward towards a safer and more solid financial system. i am convinced that we must continue on the road to a full and efficient banking union, because only then can we overcome the unfair differences which today characterize the markets of the euro area and which unfairly penalise industries and productive activities solely on the basis of their geographical distribution. a certain degree of flexibility to allow national states some room for manoeuvre must certainly be maintained, but only with a coherent regulatory framework will we be able to redress the distortions we see today, allowing all players to play on an equal footing. in setting up these rules we must be careful that excessive restrictions on the capital market do not end up making an already difficult situation worse, bringing the whole system to its knees. i particularly welcome the provisions specifically concerning smes, such as the 30% reduction in the risk-rate for loans, and the proposal to halve the risk-rate for loans to finance infrastructure projects in the fields of transport, energy and telecommunications.
in writing. − the economic and financial crisis that erupted in 2008 has shown us some difficulties and shortcomings in national banking systems, which have required the adoption, at european level, of extreme measures that are not always acceptable. the banking system has been subject to a series of attacks by the media, losing credibility and trust in the eyes of the public, and has become a negative icon of a crisis that shows no sign of abating. the implementation of a set of measures to coordinate and implement the role of the european banking authority (eba) and to review european legislation in the area of the regulation of the role of credit institutions is certainly a step in the right direction towards greater protection of citizens and a reduction of their exposure to the risks associated with and arising from the crisis.
in writing. − following numerous changes in the legislation on access to the business of credit institutions and the capital adequacy of investment firms and credit institutions, it was considered necessary to reorganise the subject by means of a single body of rules. the directive will be the essential instrument for the completion of the internal market, under the dual aspect of freedom of establishment and freedom to provide financial services in the field of credit institutions. in addition, a control system will ensure that auditors are required to inform the competent authorities promptly when, in the performance of their duties, they become aware of facts which could seriously affect the financial situation or the administrative and accounting organisation of the institution. in view of the need for these measures and the correct solutions to the problem of the organic nature of the legislation in this area, i am in favour of them.
in writing. - mr president, i voted in favour of the package on strengthening the banking sector presented by mr karas because i believe it is a great step forward towards a safer and more solid financial system. i am convinced that we must continue on the road to a full and efficient banking union, because only then can we overcome the unfair differences which today characterize the markets of the euro area and which unfairly penalise industries and productive activities solely on the basis of their geographical distribution. a certain degree of flexibility to allow national states some room for manoeuvre must certainly be maintained, but only with a coherent regulatory framework will we be able to redress the distortions we see today, allowing all players to play on an equal footing. in setting up these rules we must be careful that excessive restrictions on the capital market do not end up making an already difficult situation worse, bringing the whole system to its knees. i particularly welcome the provisions specifically concerning smes, such as the 30% reduction in the risk-rate for loans, and the proposal to halve the risk-rate for loans to finance infrastructure projects in the fields of transport, energy and telecommunications.
in writing. - the capital requirements directive was voted on today; it is a concrete measure to boost growth and employment by supporting entrepreneurship. the 'sme supporting factor' has been introduced, a rebate which reduces the amount of capital that banks must set aside for loans to smes with a turnover of less than eur 50 million and a financial exposure of less than eur 1,5 million. however, the data show that the economic crisis has made smes too vulnerable due to the lack of effective and practical support. there are too many difficulties facing small and mediumsized enterprises. this measure therefore represents a concrete action to support entrepreneurial activity. smes are the backbone of the european economy and of my country. we are exploiting the employment potential of smes, which represent 99% of employment in europe and provide 67% of jobs for the economic recovery.
in writing. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the provision of information on the use of the euro. this will be possible through a partial sterilisation of bank exposures to smes. this choice, in addition to giving fresh life to the main engine of the european real economy, will make it possible to have ever more solid and reliable banks without draining the credit that businesses so desperately need.
in writing. − the high level group on financial supervision in the eu called on the european union to develop more harmonised financial regulation. in the context of the future european supervisory architecture, the european council of 18 and 19 june 2009 stressed the need to establish a single set of european standards applicable to all credit institutions and investment firms in the single market. the adoption of such a regulation would subject all defined credit institutions and investment firms to the same rules across the union, which would also strengthen confidence in the stability of credit institutions and investment firms. in addition, the european banking authority (eba) was established by regulation (eu) no 1093/2010 of the european parliament and of the council of 24 november 2010 establishing a european supervisory authority. the aim of that regulation is to increase the quality and uniformity of national supervision by strengthening the supervision of cross-border groups. i therefore express a favourable opinion.
mr president, the approval of the ground handling dossier is a sign of the european parliament's desire to ensure greater efficiency and quality in ground handling services at european airports. i personally think that the debate on the dossier has been too much focused on whether or not to further liberalise the sector, increasing the number of service providers from two to three, without taking account of the many innovative elements that have been introduced compared to the 1996 framework. i refer in particular to the provisions to ensure that groundhandling services employees can benefit from protection and guarantees of re-employment, the mandatory introduction of minimum standards of quality of service, the provision of more detailed technical specifications in the selection procedures for tenders and the accounting separation imposed on airport operators in the event that they provide groundhandling services. it is a positive assessment, however, and it is also positive that the approval of this dossier opens the trilogue with regard to the whole aeroports package.
in writing. − in 2011, the commission published a proposal for a regulation on groundhandling services at eu airports. the ground handling sector has been waiting for this proposal for a long time, expecting to see the efficiency and quality of ground handling services enhanced through further market opening. although this proposal represents a significant improvement on the current legislative framework, i believe that some important issues still need to be addressed in order to ensure efficient market opening, based on consistency, transparency and a better service for airport users and therefore for passengers. first of all, the opening up of the groundhandling market must be balanced. over the last decade, this european sector has suffered a marginal contraction, despite the rapid growth in passenger numbers. a full opening of the market would risk increasing pressure on ground staff who would in turn be forced to reduce staff costs, leading to downward pressure on wages and less job stability. in order to ensure transparency and user planning at airports, i believe it is necessary to ensure a common and transparent charging system for centralised airport infrastructure and facilities.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mr zasada's report because i believe that the market for ground services should be liberalized wherever possible, with protection for workers and appropriate quality standards for companies. the text represents a step forward in terms of the quality of the services offered without penalising the social partners involved, and i hope that the council will share parliament's views and that the final text will be adopted.
in writing. the time at which this dossier is being discussed is emblematic of how much contact parliament must seek with everyday reality. in my own area, 2,500 workers in this sector are at risk of losing their jobs, and we cannot agree on some details which are too small to be compared with the tragedy of unemployment for 2,500 families. perhaps it is time to reduce the size of some of the national delegations. we can no longer afford to lose ourselves in procedures under the guise of democracy. the ping-pong effect of this measure is all the more scandalous the more national the majorities are. the commission and our colleagues who are dealing with this issue then reflect on the type of legal instrument and we remember that, especially in times of crisis, every minute we lose represents a huge cost to the community. i voted in favour of the proposed amendments because i think the new compromises reached in the commission are much more sensible than those of december, and i refer in particular to the criterion for the introduction of a second operator, changed from the number of passengers to the volume of goods transported, but i would ask my colleagues to be more efficient in the discussions in the commission.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mr artur zasada's proposal because, in a global context where air transport is constantly increasing, i believe that it was necessary to revise, after 15 years, the proposal governing airport ground handling services. i am convinced that by stimulating competition we can improve the quality of services and prevent social dumping. i particularly welcome the proposal to introduce minimum quality standards to ensure greater efficiency at all the major european airports and to increase staffing at all airports which have had at least 15 million passengers and/or 200,000 tonnes of cargo per year over the last three years. clauses have also been introduced to safeguard the rights of staff in the event of transfers, thus ensuring that collective agreements are respected.
in writing. − ground support services, which are essential for the smooth conduct of air operations, comprise the following categories: administrative ground handling and oversight, passenger handling, baggage handling, cargo and mail handling, runway operations, cleaning and landing services, fuel and oil handling, aircraft maintenance, air operations and crew management, ground transportation and catering. i agree that increasing the social pressure on workers in the sector and forcing them into a precarious situation is contrary to the interests of the safety of the population, and i therefore voted in favour of the proposal.
in writing. - this vote opens up the airport ground handling sector to greater competition, effectively increasing the minimum number of contractors. the aim is to ensure high efficiency in services and to prevent social dumping by introducing minimum quality standards and safeguard clauses for staff transfers. it is now necessary to start negotiations with the council immediately to reach a compromise agreement on the whole 'airports package' in order to revive the whole sector without delay.
in writing. − i am in favour of the proposal to improve the efficiency and quality of ground services at airports in the european union. after a first rejection of the original text, a satisfactory agreement has now finally been reached, which is agreed by the european parliament and the european commission. increasing the number of airport operators from 2 to 3 at the largest european airports will naturally lead to increased competition, which will result in a clear advantage for passengers: the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the proposal for a directive on the minimum standards of passenger service.
in writing. the draft legislative resolution of the european parliament on the proposal for a regulation on groundhandling services at union airports provides for the opening of the market for groundhandling services. in this way, member states may not prevent each airport user from freely choosing the service to be used and the provider of that service. the airport managing body will have to publish the list of centralised infrastructures present at the airport and, after consulting the interested parties, decide which of these to centralise. users will also be able to self-assist and have free access to the infrastructure. the italian airports concerned by this legislation are 96. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to carcinogens at work. i therefore express a favourable opinion.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report, which approves a regulation amending two previous ones governing fishing in the skagerrak, the name of the arm of the north sea between denmark and norway. i am in favour of the obligations laid down in the new rules, such as the landing obligation, and of the accompanying rules necessary to check and inspect that the obligation is being complied with. i am also in favour of evaluation to ensure that citizens respect the rules that are laid down and that they are considered fair and just. people want to obey the law, but they do so reluctantly if they feel that it is unjust. the legislator must therefore identify the most appropriate solutions and do everything possible to ensure that the rules adopted are respected to the fullest.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution: skagerrak waters are the only waters shared by member states and third countries and not governed by a fisheries agreement, in which quotas apply and in which third countries have established an obligation to land all catches; it is therefore reasonable to establish a specific set of rules on technical and control measures for the skagerrak which differs from the general regime in force in the union.
in writing. the main objective of the proposal is to establish a ban on discarding at sea in the skagerrak. the present situation, which in some cases involves the discarding of large percentages of total catches, is perhaps the most difficult for the general public to understand and to support in the context of the common fisheries policy. the fact that perfectly edible fish is thrown overboard at a time when the world is struggling to feed its population is considered incomprehensible and even immoral. i also agree that a voluntary system would allow the legislator to put an end to the issues of the size of ships and to fix a correct date for the entry into force of the ban on discarding. i therefore voted in favour of the proposal.
in writing. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. the vote was on a ban on discarding 35 species of fish caught accidentally in the skagerrak arm of the north sea between denmark and norway. this ban will take effect gradually between 2014 and 2016 and will be enforced by a system of remote electronic monitoring system. under this ban, fishing vessels will be obliged to bring all the fish they catch ashore. the new measures will apply to member states with fishing rights in the skagerrak (germany, belgium, the netherlands, denmark, sweden and norway). in addition, the commission should present, by the end of 2015, a legislative proposal for a coherent overall legislative framework to ensure the effective protection of cetaceans from all threats.
in writing. the common desire is to introduce a ban on discarding for fishermen operating in the skagerrak. the present situation means that in some cases they are obliged to discard a great many fish. this is increasingly difficult for european citizens to understand and support, even if it is provided for under the common fisheries policy. the fact that perfectly edible fish is thrown overboard at a time when the world is struggling to feed its population is no longer acceptable and this situation must end immediately.
in writing. - since 1986, fishing in the skagerrak has been governed by an international agreement, which norway has subsequently denounced, and a new agreement is therefore being negotiated. in this connection, it was considered to revise the legislation on fishing in skagerrak waters, making recommendations to harmonize the rules between the european union and norway. first, the obligation to land fish belonging to a total of 25 species listed in annex i to the regulation, followed by a prohibition on releasing them into the sea, except in the case of a high survival rate. it is also proposed that flag member states of vessels operating in the skagerrak install and operate an electronic remote control system and that all vessels of 12 metres or more overall length be required to install equipment for the collection of information and its transmission to the rem remote electronic control system. the legislation would also apply to european vessels transiting the norwegian coast when operating in the part of the skagerrak under norwegian jurisdiction. i therefore express a favourable opinion.
mr president, the judgment of the court of justice on the directive on equal treatment for men and women in the access to goods and services is likely to lead to the paradox that european citizens will pay higher insurance premiums and at the same time women will lose the recognition of that positive discrimination which in risk assessment and on the basis of actuarial and statistical data makes them, for a gender factor, less exposed to insurance risk and therefore beneficiaries of lower premiums. the commission must take corrective action by means of an instrument of equal legal value which also guarantees parliament's right to express its views. the guidelines published in december 2011 are not sufficient and a proposal should have been submitted before the court of justice judgment became effective. the publication of the report on the application of the directive, which is now three years late, could have helped in drawing up this corrective action. this is something we cannot afford, it is not acceptable, and it does not do justice to the efficiency of the commission. it would be right for it to scrupulously adhere to this request after today's largely positive vote.
in writing. − i support this report because the current eu legislation on gender equality must be properly implemented and transposed in all economic sectors and in all member states. the commission should take concrete measures to explain the directive on the ‘equal treatment between men and women in the access to and supply of goods and services’ and its impact. the potential for progress contained in this directive needs to be explained in detail in order to enable both women and men to make appropriate use of its features and possibilities.
in writing. − the entry into force of directive 2004/113/ec implementing the principle of equal treatment between men and women in the access to and supply of goods and services has marked an important milestone in the evolution of european gender equality laws. the directive addresses for the first time at union level the issues of gender equality and sex discrimination outside the labour market. the directive prohibits direct and indirect discrimination on grounds of sex in the access to and supply of goods and services which are available to the public. it also prohibits less favourable treatment of women on grounds of pregnancy and maternity, as well as sexual harassment. however, i am concerned about some member states where its transposition has been incomplete, mainly because of the lack of clarity of national laws or their vague and abstract nature. i therefore call on the commission to share best practice with the member states and to provide them with the necessary resources to support positive actions, thereby ensuring better implementation of the respective provisions at national level.
in writing. - i preferred to abstain on this report because, although i agree with its content in general, i considered it essential to reject certain specific points. i am referring in particular to discrimination on the grounds of gender identity and on grounds of maternity planning and access to reproductive health services and gender reassignment treatments provided for by law. in particular, maternity planning is not a european competence but a member state competence. the majority of the house has spoken in favour of these aspects and i therefore preferred to emphasize my position by a final abstention.
in writing. - mr president, i voted in favour of the application of directive 2004/113/ec prohibiting discrimination on grounds of sex in the access to and supply of goods and services in both the public and private sectors. i think this is a very important directive because it is intended to prohibit discrimination on grounds of sex in sectors outside the labour market, such as the services sector, where discrimination on grounds of sex often takes place. the directive applies to goods and services offered to the public and which are offered outside the private and family sphere; takes into account cases of discrimination on grounds of pregnancy, difficulties in obtaining loans or credit and calls for the european commission to monitor the different national systems with regard to discrimination linked to breastfeeding or access to public spaces and transport. the committee also welcomed the commission's proposal to extend the scope of the directive to cover the following categories of workers: workers who are selfemployed, selfemployed persons, selfemployed persons with disabilities, selfemployed persons with disabilities, persons with reduced mobility, persons with reduced mobility, persons with reduced mobility, persons with reduced mobility, persons with reduced mobility, persons with reduced mobility, persons with reduced mobility, persons with reduced mobility, persons with reduced mobility, persons with reduced mobility, persons with reduced mobility, persons with reduced mobility, persons with reduced mobility, persons with reduced mobility, persons with reduced mobility, persons with reduced mobility, persons with reduced mobility, persons with reduced mobility, persons with reduced mobility, persons with reduced mobility, persons with reduced mobility, persons with reduced mobility, persons with reduced mobility, persons with reduced mobility, persons with reduced mobility, persons with reduced mobility, persons with reduced mobility, persons with reduced mobility, persons with reduced mobility, persons with reduced mobility, persons with reduced mobility, persons with reduced mobility, persons with reduced mobility, persons with reduced mobility, persons with reduced mobility, persons with reduced mobility, persons with reduced mobility, persons with reduced mobility, persons with reduced mobility, persons with reduced mobility, persons with reduced mobility, etc.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution today because the european court of justice had already been clear in putting an end to the blatant discrimination perpetrated up to now by insurance companies and based on the gender of policyholders. in particular, for life insurance, we think it is unfair that the gender gap should affect the terms of insurance and the price. it is well known that policies differentiate between women (long-term residents) and men (high-risk, high-risk smokers). today, by voting this resolution, we have reaffirmed the supremacy of the rights enshrined in our constitutions and the european charter of rights over the statistics used by insurance companies.
in writing. − the entry into force of directive 2004/113/ec implementing the principle of equal treatment between men and women in the access to and supply of goods and services on 21 december 2004 marked an important milestone in the evolution of european gender equality laws. given that the member states had until 21 december 2007 to implement the directive, as provided for in article 17 of the text, although i did not fully agree with the rapporteur, i voted in favour of the proposal, believing that the european commission should have drawn up a summary report to assess this implementation by 21 december at the latest.
in writing. - mr president, today the plenary voted on the motion for a resolution on the transposition and application of council directive 2004/113/ec implementing the principle of equal treatment for men and women in the access to and supply of goods and services. the directive was supposed to have been implemented by december 2007, but the european commission informed the rapporteur that the report on the implementation of the directive would not be drawn up before 2014. parliament therefore calls on the commission to publish its report and all available data as soon as possible. calls on the commission and the member states to take concrete measures to explain the directive and its impact, by means of concrete examples; calls on the commission to take into account cases of discrimination on the grounds of pregnancy, birth planning and maternity; calls on the commission to monitor with particular attention any discrimination related to breastfeeding, in particular any discrimination in access to goods and services in public areas and spaces.
in writing. − the purpose of this report is to assess the impact and scope of the implementation of directive 2004/113/ec in the member states, which implements the principle of equal treatment between men and women in the access to and supply of goods and services, to identify existing gaps and to recommend possible solutions to fill them. after several delays, the european commission informed the rapporteur that the report on the implementation of the directive would not be completed before 2014. the directive has proved controversial in that it refers to the prohibition of differences in insurance policies on the basis of sex, but in the following paragraph, by way of derogation, gives insurance companies a choice where the factor is decisive in the assessment of risks. the directive provides for a shift in the burden of proof: the defendant must prove that there is no breach of the principle of equal treatment on the basis of the evidence adduced by the victim, and bodies to promote equal treatment will be set up. i am in favour of this.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the report on advancing development through trade, because i believe that the eu trade policy could have a substantial impact on development in poor countries. the formulation of trade agreements must drive developing countries to participate properly in the international economy and to benefit from the advantages of the globalisation. europe must be at the forefront of effort to reduce poverty.
in writing. − trade policy is one of the most important areas of action for the coherence of the european union's development policies. the current eu target is to bring the overall allocation for development aid to 0.7% of gdp by 2015. i believe that, in the light of the changing structure of international trade, the ownership of aid programmes by the beneficiary countries, together with transparency, accountability and sufficient resources, is one of the determining factors that can contribute to their effectiveness and success, with the aim of pursuing regional integration. i also believe that it is of fundamental importance that national, regional and local institutions and civil society are systematically involved in the planning and monitoring of these programmes. at the same time, i believe that careful and transparent monitoring of the economic and financial situation of countries receiving development aid should not be neglected. finally, i would draw the commission's attention to the need to take greater account of the new challenges of development aid through trade and to actively contribute to strengthening the capacity of governments to integrate sustainable economic development into their national trade strategies and programmes.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this measure because i was convinced by the approach taken in talking about the role of the private sector in stimulating growth in developing countries. international trade is a very important lever, but empirical experience teaches us that we cannot at all rely on sectors and companies that have come from above, and even more so from a foreign institution. we must encourage local entrepreneurship, create small businesses to support and encourage them, and rely on sectors that can develop skills and knowledge that can in turn stand on their own two feet. i therefore agree with the rapporteur that it is appropriate to conclude agreements with the private sector in order to trigger the virtuous circle which leads to self-sustaining employment, income, consumption and investment.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe it brings to our attention important aspects of trade and the related development issue. as the wto estimates, for every dollar invested in aid to increase the trading capacity of a developing country, there is an increase in its exports of about $42 on average. this is just one example of how trade agreements with developing countries contribute to an overall improvement in the social and economic conditions of developing countries. therefore, encouraging such agreements, identifying inefficiencies and removing them are key steps to continue progressing towards a europe of ever greater solidarity.
in writing. − the eu's trade policy towards developing countries aims to achieve better integration of the developing countries into the international trading system, but lacks clearly defined objectives, risking instead to destroy local production and increase dependence on exports of basic products. despite considerable efforts to liberalize, some developing countries have failed to diversify production and exports. this is where the eu must lend its support, because we must not forget that a large proportion of the population of developing countries still lives in extreme poverty, particularly in the least developed countries. in 1990, only 18% of the population living in extreme poverty lived in the least developed countries, but in 2007 this percentage doubled to 36%. numbers that speak for themselves and which the european union will soon come to the rescue
in writing. − trade policy is one of the most important areas of action for the coherence of the european union's development policies; if used properly, the instruments of trade policy can have a significant impact on the development of poor countries. agreeing that in order to achieve development objectives more effectively, eu trade policy must focus on positive impacts on both local, regional and national economies, and on promoting the diversification of the economies of developing countries, i voted in favour of the proposal.
in writing. - the motion for a resolution on improving development through trade was voted on today in plenary. parliament stressed that since trade liberalisation cannot be taken for granted to lead to growth and poverty reduction, trade and trade-aid policies must be developed on the basis of transparent, inclusive and participatory processes involving all stakeholders. parliament also called for the full implementation of policy coherence for development, including an end to all unfair production and marketing practices, excessive exploitation of fisheries resources and subsidies to agriculture which hamper development and threaten food security. it stressed that investment policy posed two major challenges for developing countries: at national level, this policy must be integrated into the development strategy, providing for sustainable development objectives, while at international level it is necessary to strengthen the development dimension in international investment agreements (iia) and to ensure a balance between the rights and obligations of states and investors.
in writing. - the european union has the power and the duty to implement trade policies that can promote the development of the poorest third countries. in this context there can be no room for protectionism either on the part of the eu or its member states in our trade relations with developing countries. the european union must also be prepared to make sacrifices, such as those it is prepared to make when concluding trade agreements with other partners. the union's intentions must of course be supported by internal changes in developing countries, consolidated by the targeted support of the european institutions. for example, multinational companies, if encouraged by these institutions, can do a lot for these countries, guaranteeing adequate wages and reasonable working conditions and thus leaving a positive imprint of change in these countries. i therefore express my favourable opinion.
in writing. - i fully agree with the report that mrs saifi, together with the inta committee, has submitted to us. i think the european commission has done a very good job in presenting this communication to us and has managed to focus on all the issues that should be given priority. in times of financial austerity, we must also plan development aid well, so that it is not a resource taken from our citizens but a successful investment on which to build the markets on which we ourselves must rely in the future.
in writing. - it is undeniable that trade and investment can be the driving force behind the growth and development of the least developed countries, and some of the points in this report are partially shared. i am referring, for example, to the fact that we must concentrate more on the countries which are paying in the most difficult conditions, with specific and targeted interventions. however, when we talk about international trade we must be extremely cautious and we must carefully evaluate the measures we take, lest they become a boomerang for our economy: the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos is a very good one. the clearest example, and perhaps the one that comes most naturally to me, as a prato resident, is that of the textile sector, which has suffered and continues to suffer unfair competition from various countries, especially asian ones. the question of relocation, a real economic and social scourge which the european union continues to pretend not to see, but which will have to deal with in earnest sooner or later, should also be examined more closely.
in writing. − south-south trade reached 23% of world trade in 2010; according to the 2011 world trade organisation world trade report, south-south preferential agreements account for two thirds of all such agreements, compared to only one quarter for north-south agreements. and yet, according to the world investment report 2012, emerging economies account for almost half of all global foreign direct investment (fdi). if we add that many countries are still not fully benefiting from trade, that the share of the least developed countries in world gdp is falling, and that, despite a high rate of economic growth, the 49 least developed countries still account for only 1.12% of world trade, exacerbating social disparities, it is clear that the situation is an emergency and an emergency in which the eu must act quickly.
in writing. - investment policy presents two main challenges for developing countries: at national level, this policy must be integrated into the development strategy, taking into account the sustainable development goals, while at international level, the development dimension in international investment agreements (iia) needs to be strengthened and a balance between the rights and obligations of states and investors ensured. agreeing with the eu's call on other aid donors, partner country authorities and local and international private actors in developing countries to assess possible areas of cooperation for sustainable development, i voted in favour of the proposal to maximise the contribution of trade to the achievement of development goals.
in writing. − trade policy is one of the most important areas of action for the coherence of the european union's development policies. we have therefore today emphasized that, if used properly, the instruments of trade policy can have a considerable impact on the development of the poorest and most deprived countries. promoting development worldwide, especially through means other than aid, means preserving the eu's core values and respecting its obligations under the treaties.
in writing. − the european union's trade and development policies must also act as a driver to support the growth of developing countries and contribute to free and fair trade. this is why measures should be taken to increase trade with these countries, and policies should be introduced to provide financial and infrastructure assistance and to create partnerships with the most disadvantaged regions. the european parliament therefore supports the commission's aim of improving synergies between trade and development policies and recommends that the needs and capacities of beneficiary countries be taken into account, by promoting instruments such as regional integration and encouraging developing countries to integrate the objective of economic development into their policies, covering industrial, agricultural and service sectors. i am in favour of this.
the agenda includes the report by marisa matias, on behalf of the committee on economic and monetary affairs, on the 2011 annual report of the european central bank (2012/2304(ini)) (a7-0031/2013). the house would of course warmly welcome the president of the european central bank, mario draghi.
madam president, mr draghi, between the end of 2011 and the beginning of 2012, the ecb granted over eur 1 trillion to banks in the form of loans at a 1% interest rate. the aim of this operation was certainly one which could be shared, namely to restart the european economy. the problem was that the banks used this money for their own personal interest, for example by investing in advantageous government bonds, as happened in italy. at the same time, there has been a reduction in lending to small and medium-sized enterprises, which are the most in need of such support. it was a shameful game and the ecb did nothing to prevent it. the european central bank seems to be more interested in the internal politics of countries than in the real economy. moreover, 2011 is the year of the famous "letter" to italy and the change of government, in which the ecb played a decisive role, as indeed also happened with the choice of the government friendly to athens. mr president, will you also tell us who will be the next italian prime minister and the next president of the republic?
in his speech in amsterdam, mr president draghi rightly stressed that monetary policy cannot take the place of economic policy and that the future of the eurozone depends on the ability of policy to make the right choices and to complete its institutional architecture. we share this position. on the monetary policy front, and in conditions which objectively make it difficult to replicate the anglo-saxon and japanese model of quantitative easing in europe, the ecb has been able to launch original unconventional measures which have been decisive in halting the spiral of the sovereign debt crisis, in particular with its famous whatever it takes and omt programme. the problem is not the ecb's monetary policy, but the eu's fiscal policy and the lack of determination to move towards economic and political union. and yet i would like to point out two critical points in the ecb's action over the last two years. the first concerns the role which the ecb has found itself playing in the field of the fiscal and economic policies of the member states - a role which appears objectively inappropriate, especially in the light of the methodological considerations which it has also made. this concerns the action of the troika in the countries under the programme, but not only. i think, for example, that in the light of the macroeconomic data, it is difficult today to deny that the letter that his predecessor sent in 2011 to the italian government suggesting to advance by one year, compared to the european obligations, the balanced budget was an error in method and substance. the second issue concerns the effects of the ltro on the real economy. i would like to ask a question on this, which is also a proposal: why not imagine, as suggested by bassanini and reviglio among others, a very long term refinancing operation to support long term investments? the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, mr draghi, at a time when europe is going through an unprecedented economic and social crisis, the economic weakness of the eurozone is in plain sight. the austerity measures imposed on european citizens have failed: the unemployment rate for the euro area rose from 7.6 percent in 2007 to 11.4 percent in 2012, while a large number of cash-strapped firms are closing their doors. the future of europe depends to a large extent on the redefinition of the role of the central bank: the united states and japan rely on strong central banks, which govern the currency to support exports; the european central bank must be able to intervene more effectively in real economic growth and support the flow of liquidity to firms that are dying of credit. italian banks, despite having received more than 250 billion euros from the ecb in 2012 alone, instead of investing in small and medium-sized enterprises, have turned off the credit taps, preferring to protect their treasury by buying government bonds. the ecb has to start over from here: the commission's proposal is to put businesses, citizens and productive investment at the centre of its action in order to try to create a climate of confidence before it is too late.
mr president, i recall that when i asked you why the ecb did not intervene in the case of credit institutions using the money they receive at the 0.75% rate to buy government bonds instead of lending to businesses or, even worse, lending to businesses at rates as high as 10%, you replied: 'the ecb cannot impose restrictions on financial institutions as it is the individual banks that decide on the conduct of their business.' on the contrary, a few days ago he said: "it is a serious problem that banks do not lend at reasonable rates. we cannot and will not subsidize insolvent institutions and governments". so i ask you: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the european union's financial system is not undermined by the failure of the european monetary system to provide a stable and stable monetary system. have you considered that perhaps, as all the other states in the world do, it is better to print money at the expense of the value of the euro? if you think that the ecb does not have the power to intervene directly in favour of households and businesses because of the treaty, have the courage to ask the institutions to change it!
mr president, commissioner, as you have seen, the approval of the discharge is not in question because, as you know, there is a widespread sensitivity among european citizens to the idea that they are responsible for the way their resources are used: the funds. in the light of the discussion which you have also attended, there are some aspects which should be focused on and on which i believe that a targeted and specific intervention by the commission is necessary. it has been stated, with incontrovertible data, that there is a too high error rate and this cannot remain a simple evocation of principle. the commission has also been asked to provide a report on the implementation of the new guidelines for the european year of the environment. a staffing problem is repeatedly raised: the commission has therefore decided to extend the period of validity of the new rules to the period from 1 january 1993 to 31 december 1993. finally, i think it is very important to have national rules to improve spending: it is not enough for parliament, the commission and the council to be virtuous, it is also necessary for the individual member states to behave in the same way!
on behalf of the efd group. mr president, it is clear that the european parliament should be the first to set an example of efficiency and cost reduction in this time of global crisis. however, the example we are giving again this week is the opposite: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. there is no logic in having more seats for this parliament and we must talk about this more and more because the citizens need to know how we are using their money, in this case wasting it. strasbourg is a beautiful city in the heart of europe, but there are many possible alternatives to the seat of the european parliament. since my amendment to emphasize the need for a single seat has already been rejected in the committee on budgets, i have tabled it again and i really want to see tomorrow whether my colleagues will have the courage to face up to this scandal. a compact european parliament would be a signal which governments could not ignore. this is an untenable situation: europe must listen to our voice, the voice of the millions of citizens we represent here.
mr president, i should like to begin by congratulating the rapporteur, mrs monika hohlmeier, on her excellent analysis of the areas and innovative ways of saving parliament's budget. i am referring in particular to the idea of merging the translation capacity of parliament with the committee of the regions and the economic and social committee. with any budget surpluses, parliament could therefore increase the resources to be devoted to research and assistance to parliamentarians, in order to ensure high-quality know-how for parliamentarians, also as a result of the increasing legislative powers that the european parliament is assuming. the increase of 3.2 percent actually represents a decrease in the budget, if we take into account that the extraordinary expenditure in 2014 and inflation will unfortunately, perhaps, increase. 2014 is going to be a special year: there are additional costs for the functioning of the parliament, because this is the year in which the elections for the new european parliament will take place, with its consequent installation, and additional costs for croatia's accession to the european union. we will therefore have costs for new interpreters, costs for recruiting croatian staff and costs for welcoming new members so that they can start their work here in the european parliament. it is with great regret, therefore, that i would like to point out that the european parliament's budget for 2014 will actually be reduced by 2.89% compared to 2013. it seems that there has been an increase, while in reality there will be a sharp decrease.
mr president, at the press conference on 4 april, president draghi was, inexpressibly, very annoyed by the question whether the seizure of accounts in cyprus could be a model for the whole eurozone in the future. in fact, the directive now before parliament prescribes, more or less, exactly what happened in cyprus and draghi, not by chance, urged parliament and the council to approve it in a hurry, that is, as early as 2014. in essence, this directive requires that, where the cancellation of financial debt may threaten the stability of the system, that debt must be paid, of course by the savers, as happened in cyprus. cyprus, if we are to be serious and sincere, is a test whether these expropriations can be carried out by the financial superbureaucracy that governs us without creating too many problems. the european union is preparing to place the european central bank under the supervision of its creditor, the ecb itself, in order to prevent its failure. no, not at all!

vice-president of the commission. − mr president, let me first of all thank you for a very substantive and serious debate and for your often very critical remarks. i have listened to you very carefully, and i can assure you that the commission will take this very important debate into account. i will now make some short comments, and my colleague mr barnier will, for his part, continue on some important issues. firstly, i would like to speak about the specific nature of the cyprus package, which has been referred to in many speeches during the discussion. the cypriot agreement consists of an economic stabilisation programme that is grounded on the financial sector, conditionality, strengthening banks’ capital buffers, improving liquidity conditions, enhancing prudential regulation, and supervision. these are elements that have been common to all programme countries. the bail-in of creditors is in fact less of a novelty than it might appear. after all, the irish programme also included very strong own contributions by bank creditors – over eur 5 billion of junior subordinated debt was bailed-in in ireland. at the same time, ireland’s pension reserve fund contributed close to eur 10 billion. given the heavy reliance of cypriot banks on deposits, a specific feature of the cypriot case is that standard creditor contributions could only deliver a part of the funds needed. the bailing-in of uninsured deposits was a consequence of this. given the unique nature of the cypriot case, the approach followed in cyprus should not be seen as a blueprint for any possible future activities. indeed, there are no templates as such. while each programme may have its similarities, each is tailored to the needs of the country in question. greece, ireland, portugal and spain have all had very clear specific conditions which have been taken into account in the programme design. mr lamberts referred to the programme’s cost, and i think that he has brought up a very important question. the confusion arises from the fact that two entirely different sets of figures are being compared – one net and the other gross. one is based on a set of assumptions from several months ago, while the other takes into account the most recent decisions and the most recent macro-economic projections. in other words, in public debate, in the media, people have, frankly, been comparing apples and pears and coming up with oranges. i shall refrain from remarking that this is what happens when stories are written based on leaked documents. if you look at these two figures of eur 17 billion and eur 23 billion to which mr lamberts referred, the difference is that the eur 17 billion is related to net financing needs, while the larger figure that has been voted on, eur 23 billion, relates to gross financing. moreover, the larger number also includes additional buffers in the second cypriot programme. the combined contribution to the programme from the esm and imf remains eur 10 billion. there is, therefore, no change in the financial envelope available for cyprus. i would like to conclude by saying that the commission urged cyprus to take swift action as early as november 2011 and worked tirelessly to reach quick agreement on a programme over the last year. unfortunately, this proved to be impossible. within the constraints handed to us, the room for manoeuvre was very limited, and not to reach an agreement at all would have been the worst outcome of all. in this regard, i think that what mr swoboda, mr verhofstadt and mr cohn-bendit said about the cumbersome and complex structure of decision-making within the eurozone is very important. indeed, we need to continue to intensify the reform of the eurozone together in order to rebuild our economic and monetary union so that it is up to its task. it is clear that the near future will be difficult. i will sum up. i am very much looking forward to continuing this discussion at the hearing of the committee on economic and monetary affairs on 25 april. i just want to say that the commission will do everything possible to alleviate the social consequences and mitigate the impact on the most vulnerable in society. we will stand by the cypriot people in these difficult times.
member of the commission. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, in all these crises, the one in cyprus which we have discussed this morning and all the others, there are always two times to act. the first stage is the emergency, the repair, i was going to say if i can use that word surgery. we in brussels know, you may be sure, what efforts are required of the peoples of europe at that time. then there is the time of prevention and the lessons to be learned. it is precisely in this time that not only my action or the proposals i am making are situated, but your action. cyprus is certainly not a model, but there are lessons to be learned in cyprus, as in other crises, and we have been learning them one by one, week by week, for the last three years together. it's bad supervision, you know? we have presented the creation of the european supervisory authorities and, in the spring of next year, we will finally have integrated supervision in the euro area with the european central bank. poor capital in the banks, unjustified and unreasonable bonuses, which encourage risk-taking. you answered on the basis of the report of your colleague, othmar karas. 608 of you voted yesterday on a text which is fundamental to the strength of banks. and then, finally, as many of you have said, clearly announced tools in advance for resolution, for bail-in, a complete toolbox. i presented to you more than a year ago the text which is now under discussion and in june i will present to you the creation of the european resolution authority within the framework of the present treaty. ladies and gentlemen, the commission will not allow it to be said that we are not reacting, that we are not learning the lessons. but it is true that we can and must go faster and we must complete this whole reform as quickly as possible. the commission and the commissioner speaking must continue to have your support.
