uachtarán na héireann. − a uachtaráin, a chomhaltaí de pharlaimint na heorpa, a choimisinéir máire geoghegan-quinn, tá athas orm agus is mian liom mo bhuíochas a ghabháil libh as ucht an deis a thabhairt dom labhairt leis an tionól seo ina dtugtar le chéile ionadaithe na saoránach, arna dtoghadh go díreach agus go daonlathach, ó na seacht mballstát fichead, ocht gcinn fichead go luath, den aontas eorpach. mr president, members of the european parliament, commissioner geoghegan quinn, may i thank you for giving me the opportunity of addressing this assembly which brings together the democratically elected representatives of the citizens of the 27 member states, soon to be 28, of the european union. i address you ‘mar uachtarán na héireann’, as president of ireland, an island that has always been connected to matters european; a country that has always looked outward; a people with a very strong connection with the cultures and learning of europe in all its diversity from ancient times; and a nation that has valued the european vocation through every century into the present when ireland holds, for the seventh time, the rotating presidency of the council of ministers in our 40th year of membership of the union. be it in our ancient celtic connections, in our continuous connection with european scholarship, or in our modern consistent support for european unity, we irish have been european in our consciousness and commitment. europe has always had an existence in the irish mind. in our own gaelic language the mythic stories of europe have always been present and some of our modern plays recall the use that was made of the classical sources of greek and roman myths in the gaelic hedge schools that preceded the widespread use of the english language in ireland. the irish language that preceded english had been deeply influenced by ancient european myths, particularly the great myths of sea and exile such as that of homer’s odyssey. in the areas of literature, of course the peoples of europe have had an old and enduring sense of respect for what is a cultural diversity frequently drawn from a shared sense of myth. it was, however, in the tasks of the mind and the spirit that the irish sought to make their greatest contribution. thus it was that in july 1950 the then irish prime minister, john a. costello, together with the irish foreign minister, and later, nobel peace laureate, and founding member of amnesty international, seán mcbride, travelled to luxeuil-les-bains to officially celebrate the 1400th anniversary of the birth of one of the greatest irish and european saints and scholars, columbanus. it was columbanus who with saint gall and others established centres of learning, manuscript illumination, monasteries and communities right across europe: stretching from the north of ireland to bobbio, where columbanus actually died. it is to the spirit of citizenship then, as it might be at a european level, as might motivate europeans who want to give to the two words – european and union – a sense of fulfilment, and of human flourishing that i wish to speak, in this year that has been dedicated as european year of citizens. but just one more word about that meeting in luxeuil-les-bains in july 1950. no more than some meetings of the contemporary period, of which i will not speak, its real agenda was not as publicly indicated. it was declared to be ecclesiastical in purpose; after all, the papal nuncio to france of the time, monsignor roncalli, later to be pope john xxiii, was present, as was the bishop of bobbio. but we know from the work of the distinguished scholar of the sorbonne, marguerite-marie dubois, modernist, linguist, philosopher and lexicographer, that the meeting was really organised so as to facilitate a meeting of robert schuman, foreign minister of france, with like-minded others from a number of european countries anxious to hear and test his great idea for the coming-together of the countries of europe. schuman, who was aware of ireland’s monastic efforts, reached back to recall the early monastic perigrinatio and offered the opinion that columbanus should be ‘the patron saint of all those who now seek to build a united europe’. that schuman meeting, and the others which followed it, assisted by such as jean monnet, was responding to near and terrible events. but we should never forget, and i emphasise it today, that in their response, at that meeting, they recognised the immense value of, and they drew on, the rich scholarship of philosophy, moral instincts and the general impulses of european thought as they sought, not just to replace war with peace, but more importantly, to construct a vision of europe’s people working together in an inclusive way. it was not just any abstract construction. it was a practical proposal drawn from the head and memory and experience, propelled by the heart, and it united economy and ethics in its aspiration for a common shared europe. yet the inspiration and the achievements of the founders of the european union we inherit as legacy cannot be taken for granted. today, citizens in europe are threatened with an unconscious drift to disharmony, a loss of social cohesion, a recurrence of racism and an increasing deficit of democratic accountability in some decision-making of an economic and fiscal kind. these threatening clouds hang over a europe that in more hopeful times had chosen to base its anthem, rather than on anything contemporary, on friedrich schiller’s poem ‘ode to joy’ and its musical setting by ludwig van beethoven in his ninth symphony. parliaments matter; parliaments must continue to matter. centuries of effort have been invested by european citizens in securing the vote, for example. in extending the vote, and it is to parliament that citizens look for accountability, for strategic alternatives. if national parliaments, if the european parliament, were to lose the capacity to deliver accountability where else might it be found? is there an alternative that can meet the requirements of a deliberative democracy? i believe not. but i believe that parliaments must draw on the resources of experience, of inherited intellectual capacity, in all its diversity and above all, from the best of contemporary intellectual work, and they must do so in a pluralist way. i am conscious, in this year of the european citizen, that as parliamentarians you are the elected component of the european union, elected by citizens from your diverse electorates within the same few days. i want to wish you well in all your deliberations together and with the other institutions of the union and particularly in your dialogue with your electorate – the citizens of europe. they, the citizens, place their trust in parliament when they vote and they rightly have expectations of parliaments responding to their needs. i very much welcome the increase in influence and decision-making powers that the european parliament has won in relation, for example, to the multi-annual budgeting process. it was a power that the parliament did not have when i visited here as minister – as president of the council of cultural ministers – in 1996. i wish you well in discharging that responsibility on behalf of the citizens of europe. how would the founders of the european union respond to our present circumstances one might ask? we know how hard the institutions, including this one, have worked to overcome the most serious economic crisis the union has faced since its foundation; how they have struggled to match the speed of their reaction to the ferocity of its onslaught and the onslaught that comes at times from sources that are not accountable at all. we cannot ignore the fact that european citizens are suffering the consequences of actions and opinions of bodies such as rating agencies, which, unlike parliaments, are simply unaccountable. many of our citizens in europe regard the response to the crisis in their lives as disparate, sometimes delayed, not equal to the urgency of the task of showing and often of not showing sufficient solidarity with them in their threatened or actual economic circumstances of today. they feel that in general terms the economic narrative of recent years has been driven by dry technical concerns; for example, by calculations that are abstract and not drawn from real problems, such an unemployment; geared primarily by a consideration of the impact of such measures on speculative markets, rather than driven by sufficient compassion and empathy with the predicament of european citizens who are, after all, together, members of a union, and for whom all of the resources of europe’s capacity – political, social, economic and intellectual – might have been drawn upon, if it had been driven by the binding moral spirit of a union. in facing up to the challenges europe currently faces, particularly in relation to unemployment, we cannot afford to place our singular sole trust in a single hegemonic model to the exclusion of other models that might engage best our problems such as unemployment by uncritically accepting solely and exclusively a version of a logistical, economic theory whose assumptions are narrow and intellectually questionable and largely indifferent to social consequences in terms of their outcomes. rather than any discourse that might define the european union as simply an economic space of contestation between the strong and the weak, our citizens yearn for the language of solidarity, a commitment to cohesion, for a generous inclusive rhetoric that is appropriate to an evolving political union, a union anxious to reach a future of peace, prosperity, inclusion and inter-generational justice, in a sustainable way. this is a serious challenge, not least because if we were to fail we run the risk of an economic crisis leading to a crisis of legitimacy for the union. a union that, after all, in its founding treaties is fundamentally founded on values; values such as respect for personal dignity, freedom, democracy, equality, the rule of law and respect for human rights. the union draws its legitimacy from the support of its citizens. that connection with the citizens – their belief that the european union is of them and for them – is fundamental. without it, we are adrift and citizens need an appeal to their heart thus, an appeal to their heart as well as their reason. they need reassurances now that this union will keep faith with its founding treaties. it is very many years since jacques delors declared ‘europe needs a soul’, but it remains just as true. we must not forget that that we are the inheritors of a profoundly important set of european values – greek democracy, roman law, the judeo-christian tradition, the reformation, the enlightenment, the great democratic revolution that began in france. europe is therefore more than an economic space of contestation in which our citizens are invited or required to deliver up their lives in the service of an abstract model of economy and society whose core assumptions they are assumed not to question or put to the democratic test in elections. as we face into the future, we need to draw strength from those founding values of the union, values that include cohesion and solidarity – among member states, among the citizens of our union, and between the european union and the rest of the world. we need to work together to apply ourselves to building a better future together – as jacques delors also said of this present crisis: europe does not just need fire-fighters, it needs architects too. a first and urgent task must be to get europe back to sustainable and fulfilling employment and a return to real growth. there is nothing more corrosive to society and more crushing to the person than endemic unemployment, particularly among the young. with 26 million people across the union without work, 5.7 million young people, and 115 million people in our union at risk of poverty and social exclusion; we simply cannot allow this to continue. irish presidencies have always drawn practically from the spirit of the founding treaties and the current irish presidency has, therefore, put job creation at the top of its agenda. the european council has agreed that addressing unemployment is the most important social challenge we face. at last month’s social summit, mr president, rightly you warned of the repercussions of the spread of unemployment and poverty across the union. therefore i commend the agreement reached in the european council in february on the youth employment initiative, and the subsequent proposals from the commission to make it operational by the start of next year. the matter is urgent and i also very much welcome the agreement reached in the council on the youth guarantee that will ensure all young people under the age of 25 a good quality offer of employment, education, apprenticeship or training within four months of being unemployed. but we need to do more. we need to ensure that women participate in the workplace as equals; that older workers are not left on the sidelines; and that the long-term unemployed are fully equipped to find their way back into today’s work place. we must, above all, ensure that, for all these european citizens that a loss of employment does not lead to exclusion from participation, particularly in the cultural space of one’s own community. we need also to consider how to encourage people to create jobs. we need to value and support our small and medium enterprises, the lifeblood of so many of our communities. we need to sustain those who want to create opportunity for themselves and for others. we need to encourage creativity, innovation, entrepreneurship. a generous vision then of europe is, of course, not one that looks solely inwards. the european model has inspired many others on their journey to peace and democratic institutions. while its light may not have dazzled so brightly in recent years, europe can yet be a beacon of hope and encouragement for many less fortunate people in the world. it can give a lead, for example, by speaking with a unified voice on climate change, recognising that those least contributing to our global problem are paying the highest price, even as i speak and we meet today. europe already is of course the largest donor in the fight against hunger and in the efforts at scaling up nutrition, and that is something europe can build on. how the european union engages with the rest of the world is a major test of its authority and its credibility. will the union allow its current economic difficulties to undermine its commitment on the great global challenges of our day – hunger, poverty, human rights, climate justice? i hope not. will we reaffirm rather the generous idealism at the heart of the european vision by rededicating ourselves to tackling these problems in solidarity with other partners? i hope we do. for indeed, measures that replace the millennium development goals – how they respect diversity, recognise different paths to development, have human rights at their centre – will be a major test, not only for europe, but for the global community. i believe that a european union that has the courage to face its past, including its darker periods of empire, with honesty, and its future with a commitment to values that are inclusive of all humanity, with a discourse that respects diversity, has a profound contribution to make – not only to its own citizens in europe but to the global community. it can give a lead in creating a form of ethical globalisation that recognises intergenerational responsibilities. such an integrated discourse as might allow for this to happen, i say frankly, is missing just now. (applause)the prevailing narrative seems to be trapped intellectually in a structure of thought which it appears unable to challenge, from which it seems unable, or at times even unwilling, to escape or exit. in the absence of considering, however, other possible models or approaches, we are in danger now of drifting into and sustaining a kind of moral and intellectual impotence. yet we have available to us, i repeat again, a rich legacy of intellectual, radical work upon which to draw from the past and in the contemporary world. there is, in our shared intellectual heritage, so much upon which we could draw. let us remember in the energetic pursuit of new thought that, for example, characterised the european enlightenment – itself formed from the thought of other ancient enlightenments – that there are some powerful examples of dissident and radical thought. let us never forget the singular example given by those dissident thinkers in their time, denis diderot, immanuel kant and herder. they in their times identified the flaw in the enlightenment thinking that supported empire, with its insatiable drive, and they courageously challenged it through their books, pamphlets and public expressions. the logistical strand of economics which today holds sway and stands as a single hegemonic model of economic theory, not only in europe, is the flaw of our times. this strand of neoclassical economics is of course useful for limited and defined tasks. it is insufficient however as an approach for our problems and our future. we need new substantive pluralist political economic models and an emancipatory discourse to deliver them, and i suggest that this is possible. because the dominating model and its method defines not only discourse, but policy options, there is an urgent need now for new models of connection between economy, society and policy. they are essential for genuine, pluralist choices in policy, not to speak of democratic accountability and relevance to our contemporary problems, if we are to address the current challenges. as european parliamentarians, i encourage you to let these new models into the european discourse, give them space in the committee structure of your parliament and the institutional structure of the union. but to achieve that discourse the role of public intellectuals is also an urgent one. they are called upon, i suggest, to state publicly and unequivocally that the problems of europe are not simply technical, and certainly not solely amenable to solution by technocratic measures at the expense of democratic accountability. (applause) the suggestion that citizens and their representatives are not fiscally or economically literate enough to carry the decision-making necessary for policies that impinge on their lives – be it unemployment, housing, health, education or the environment – has the most serious implications in legitimacy terms. it is an assumption that challenges democracy itself. a disembodied version of the economic space if used as a substitute for peoples, societies or states, loses its connection with history, contemporary challenges, and it lacks the moral connection with the ethics and solidarity we now need. it would evade rather than face our present challenges. a european union – if it is to be respected as the great project it is and can be – must draw on the intellectual heritage and the intellectual imaginings, and the existing talents and the capacity of the peoples of europe. it is a fully authentic union if it is characterised by solidarity. mar fhocal scoir, to conclude:if our european union and its prospects are not of this authentic character just now, it must be made so by changes in consciousness and commitment, and through reasserting the idealism, the intellectual strength and the moral courage too that drove the founding fathers of the union. european member states are after all peoples, with history, with current needs, with possibilities that are to be shared. if we were, as an alternative, simply to regard our people as dependent variables to the opinions of rating agencies, agencies unaccountable to any demos, and indeed found to be fallible on so many occasions, then instead of being citizens we would be reduced to the status of mere consumers; pawns in a speculative chess board of fiscal moves in a game derived from assumptions that are weak; assumptions that are weak in a scholarly sense, untestable in an empirical sense and very frequently undeclared. (applause)to ask that our decisions then be normative rather than being narrowly, fiscally technocratic is, i suggest, more than an integration of our intellectual capacities. it is to defend and deepen democracy. i readily acknowledge, i want to be very clear: i believe very much in the utility in so many areas of logistical economics. however, i believe that if its methods are elevated to being a substitute for the integrated multi-disciplinary scholarship that we now need to address the varying contexts and contingencies of current challenges, such a sole reliance on a technocratic approach would be markedly insufficient. if we are to deliver the european union of peace and prosperity that the founders envisaged, and that i believe the citizens of europe yearn for beyond the understandable fear of present circumstances, a strategy that draws on the research, scholarship and world views of all of the social sciences, and ethics and philosophy is required. president, members of parliament, commissioners, leaders of groups, from the flux of diverse histories, from our current problems, from our fears and our aspirations, i hope will emerge a response that constitutes a tapestry of many colours, of different strengths in its threads; and, in its design, evocative of what memory has made endure, and the human spirit has invested with hope. whether it is made out of wondrous reason or woven with a prayer will not matter in the end. what matters is that it be work of us all, working together, in cooperation, cosmopolitan and open to the world, caring for it, in an inter-generationally responsible way, and embracing all our people as equal citizens. so let us the citizens of the european union who want to make a real union together, move out of the dark into the light and achieve something indeed worthy of friedrich schiller’s poem originally called ‘ode to freedom’. go to it! go raibh míle maith agaibh go léir. (sheas a raibh sa teach agus thug bualadh bos don chainteoir)

mr president, in the face of the austerity measures adopted by many member states in response to the debt crisis, the european institutions have a moral duty to show a high degree of responsibility, on the one hand by seeking to strike a delicate balance between budgetary rigor and structural savings and, on the other, by making a joint effort to increase efficiency without compromising legislative excellence. for these reasons, and out of respect for the european citizens who are suffering the effects of the crisis, i believe that long-term investment should be assessed with caution and transparency and that the need for cost management, planning and monitoring of projects should be emphasized in an efficient and rigorous manner.

in writing. - i voted against the discharge for the committee of the regions: i have not acted in this way because of a matter of miscalculation or mismanagement, but simply because of the very fact of how this institution works. the idea of representing the voice of the regions in europe is certainly a good one, but the committee of the regions is only a structure for its own sake. its budget is purely administrative, with 72% of expenditure relating to the staff of the institution and 28% allocated to buildings, furniture, equipment and miscellaneous operating expenditure. i would therefore like to understand the usefulness of this body in the european decision-making process: i do not think that the issuing of non-binding opinions is enough to maintain a structure which costs us over 80 million euros a year. the same applies to the economic and social committee, which brings together representatives of the productive forces, workers and trade unions: these are good ideas, but they are not being implemented today in a meaningful way. i therefore believe that either the logic of these two institutions is radically changed or we can do without them.

in writing. − the revenue and expenditure forecast for the 2014 budget must take account of the particular moment of financial and economic crisis that the european union is experiencing, with greater attention to the countries that are most affected. this will require a breakdown of waste and unnecessary consumption, also in view of croatia's accession to the european union, which will involve an expenditure of some eur 13 million. in this connection, it is foreseen, for example, to reconsider the need and usefulness of the parliament's television channel (europarl tv), as well as to cut expenditure in the field of translation and interpretation and to review the policy for managing travel and the duration and number of missions. it is recommended that, in view of the very austerity climate that european citizens are experiencing, parliament's investment projects be managed with caution. i am in favour of this.
in writing. − the commission's proposal on balance of payments is an initiative to simplify financial assistance procedures between the euro area and the non-euro area. while i believe that financial assistance for balance of payments can play an important role in helping member states to improve their administrative capacity to absorb european union funds more effectively, i agree with the rapporteur that some amendments to the text should be made. in particular, i share the call for greater clarity on some of the key concepts in the proposal and the need to introduce procedures for financial assistance which are clear and fair, while not imposing the obligation of superfluous consultations where these are not justified. among the critical points in the commission's proposal i would point out the need to significantly increase the transparency and reliability of the procedure for requesting and granting financial assistance to member states in difficulty. finally, the role of the budget of the european union as the ultimate guarantor of financial assistance for member states whose currency is not the euro should be reflected in appropriate procedures to ensure accountability to the european parliament.
in writing. - with the economic and financial crisis hitting the european union, much has been done in the community's institutional bodies to shield the member states from speculative storms and to protect our single currency from repeated attempts to weaken it. the concept of solidarity which inspires our work in the european parliament must not, however, make us forget that the ten countries which have not yet joined the single currency also need adequate financial assistance mechanisms to cope with current and future emergencies. in this respect, i welcome the addition of a new financial assistance mechanism, in the form of a loan for indirect bank recapitalisation, alongside the three instruments already existing in the balance of payments framework.
in writing. the basic balance of payments proposal (bdp proposal) is a largely timely initiative to simplify financial assistance procedures between the euro area and the non-euro area. however, some amendments and additions are necessary, which are highlighted in this interim report. i agree that in order to create a real level playing field between the euro area member states and those outside the euro area, we must move in a direction which makes bank recapitalisation possible also for the member states outside the euro area.
in writing. - the intention clearly expressed today is to simplify procedures for financial assistance between the euro area and the non-euro area. in particular, the procedures for supporting these countries must always be guaranteed by absolute transparency and reliability, both in the requests for aid and in the allocation of the necessary funds.
in writing. - as regards the proposal on balance of payments, an initiative to simplify procedures for financial assistance between the euro area and the non-euro area, it was considered necessary to make some changes by means of an interlocutory report which would underline and explain them. the amendments will then be incorporated directly into the final text of the regulation, which will be approved by the council. this interim report calls for greater clarity on some of the central concepts of the proposed regulation and seeks to introduce clear and fair procedures for financial assistance. parliament and the commission have also just concluded negotiations on a single supervisory mechanism (ssm), one of the foundations of the next banking union, which is also open to non-euro area member states wishing to join the system. attention is drawn to the lack of a bank recapitalisation facility in the financial assistance toolkit offered to these states. in order to create a real level playing field between euro area and non-euro area member states, it is necessary to make bank recapitalisation possible also for non-euro area member states. i therefore express a favourable opinion.

in writing. - the differences in the tax treatment of vouchers between eu member states cause serious market inefficiencies. the commission has therefore proposed updating the relevant legislation to ensure uniform tax treatment of all types of vouchers. the commission proposes first of all that all vouchers be classified in the same way and that the taxable period be determined according to the nature of the voucher, thus eliminating the double taxation problem. the rules also lay down clear rules for the distribution of vouchers and technical measures concerning the right to deduct, redemption and refund procedures, the person liable for payment of the tax and other obligations of undertakings. i am in favour of this.

context, i would like to elaborate a little bit on the issue of drilling in the arctic. the arctic states and the european union have a shared interest in ensuring that the arctic’s natural resources, both on land, at sea and on or below the seabed, are utilised in a sustainable manner that does not compromise the arctic environment, and benefits local communities. the european union has no direct coastline with the arctic ocean. a majority of today’s known resources are within the boundaries of the 200-mile zone and/or continental shelves of the arctic coastal states. the debate has also member of the commission. − madam president, honourable members, it is unfortunate that vice-president rehn cannot be here today owing to his prior commitments in the context of the g20 and imf consult the european parliament on completion of the macroeconomic imbalance procedure scoreboard. that is not our intention, and is not our understanding of the process either. as a matter of fact, in choosing the eleventh indicator of the mip scoreboard, the commission acted in accordance with the relevant regulation and in pursuit of a political agreement with the council and parliament back in late 2011 for completion of a scoreboard with an eleventh indicator. it is useful to remember that according to that regulation – the mip regulation – it is the task of the commission to adjust technically the scoreboard definitions. i quote: ‘the commission shall assess on a regular basis the appropriateness of the scoreboard, including the composition of indicators, the thresholds set and the methodology used, and it shall adjust or modify them where necessary.’ the spirit of close cooperation with the council and parliament mentioned in recital 12, which was cited in your question, is a paramount principle for the commission. with that in mind, a political agreement with the two co-legislators regarding the financial sector was reached in 2011, through the parliament resolution of december 2011 and the ecofin council conclusions of november 2011. i would stress this aspect: the political choices were made in 2011 together with parliament. in 2012, there was a technical implementation of the political choice of adding a financial sector indicator to the scoreboard. responding specifically to the question: yes, the commission understands that a consultation took place in 2011 and that parliament’s resolution back then was the political response to the issues in question. i would also stress that the commission treated parliament and the council on the same footing and informed them at the same time. in carrying out this task, the commission benefited from the views provided by the economic policy committee. these latter should be regarded as being within the scope of the epc’s mandate to ‘provide advice to the commission’. in conclusion, on behalf of the commission, i would like to urge the honourable members to take a proportionate approach to this matter. while member states continue to experience macroeconomic imbalances to a different degree, a scoreboard that is efficiently designed and implemented is in the eu’s wider interests. as we all know, no choice is free from imperfections; no single indicator, taken in isolation, can fully measure the intricacies of the financial sector and its implications for the real economy. because of that, the current scoreboard is never interpreted mechanically or in isolation, it comprises a second layer of indicators and it does not exclude additional ones from consideration in in-depth reviews, which – as you may know – we published on 10 april. i hope that this clarifies the situation.

in writing. - mr president, today the motion for a resolution on the draft council decision on the conclusion of the agreement between the european union and ukraine amending the agreement between the european community and ukraine on the facilitation of the issuance of visas was voted during the plenary session. this agreement has been in force since 1 january 2008 and has proved to be extremely successful. however, an assessment of the functioning of the agreement has shown that some additional amendments would be necessary to correct any distortions or differences in the interpretation of the text. in particular, the provisions on the validity of the visa and the conditions for documents relating to the purpose of the journey have been summarised and clarified for a wider category of applicants. in addition, the system for introducing charges on grounds of urgency has been reviewed to improve the provisions. these charges are now abolished for users who submit an application at the last moment and live at a considerable distance from the consulate, and the provisions on outsourcing costs have been clarified. the amendments to this agreement facilitate the travel of representatives of civil society, ngos, journalists and young people.

the next item is the report by ivo belet, on behalf of the committee on industry, research and energy, on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on safety of offshore oil and gas prospection, exploration and production activities (com(2011)0688 – c7-0392/2011 – 2011/0309(cod)) (a7-0121/2013).
on behalf of the efd group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i am in favour of the text of the report, as i believe that it is appropriate to have european legislation on the safety of offshore activities, also in the wake of what we saw with the deepwater horizon disaster in the gulf of mexico in 2010. however, it was considered that a directive was the most appropriate legal instrument to avoid the risk of having to repeal and amend a large number of existing national provisions, a process which would have drained resources, already scarce, from the safety assessment and on-site inspections. pursuant to directive 2004/35/ec, authorisation holders are also the operators responsible for the security of operations and must, at all times, be competent to act in that regard. they must also reduce the risks of major accidents to a reasonable minimum, beyond which the cost of further risk reduction would be grossly disproportionate to the benefits gained. it is important that in the event of accidents with cross-border effects, emergency responses are more effective and that member states cooperate and coordinate with each other. the eu group of authorities for offshore oil activities can be used for this purpose.
in writing. in april 2010, an explosion on the deepwater horizon oil platform killed 11 men and leaked about 4.9 million barrels of crude oil. it took three months to seal the breach. the incident set in motion the review of the union's policies: the commission has launched an analysis of the safety of offshore oil and gas activities in european waters, which has revealed the need for further measures to ensure the spread across the union of best practices already covered by the legislation of some member states. i welcome the commission's proposal for a regulation because it contains concrete measures to overcome the disparities and fragmentation in the member states in the regulations in this specific area. it shall ensure that the sector uses best practices for controlling major risks and enhances its preparedness and response capacity to address major risks across the union. i believe that cooperation and the exchange of information between member states must also be strengthened. to this end, the recently established 'eu authorities group' should be more closely involved in the verification of the application and compliance with the existing legal framework on liability and compensation.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, there is no doubt that the eurema project, although it is, so to speak, a generous one, has not entirely achieved the results we all expected. it has been said: the fact that we have only 14 relocated persons and seven member states joining this project is a clear indication that we obviously expected much more. it is useful, however, to note what the commissioner has just said: the european union is a national forum which can be a tool for consultation and proposals and, above all, the shared need to make solidarity real, effective, authentic solidarity. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament on the subject of the future of the community. there is the instrument provided for in the financial perspective 2014-2020, there is the instrument provided for in the asylum and migration fund, which is however currently severely reduced. we must therefore work seriously and diligently to ensure that the resources are adequate, so that the european union can take up a matter which is certainly its own - above all the european union's - with positive, determined action, which makes this instrument a concrete instrument that can achieve the desired effects this time.

madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the issue of women's rights is always an important one, and it is even more so when it concerns countries which are moving towards the normalisation of democracy. it is very important, however, that this issue be taken into account both in the citizenship, as is normally done, and in the workplace. women are objectively a weak force in the labour market and are even more so when the crisis is raging and produces significant damage, such as the one that is right in front of everyone's eyes. for this reason, special attention must be paid to all aspects of the working methods and content of women, who often have difficulty finding employment - which is often poor employment because they lack sufficient knowledge - and are often penalized when carrying out their activities because they are discriminated against in relation to men in terms of pay or concrete rights. it is therefore desirable that citizenship and work should always be considered together.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the issue of freedom of the press is a very important one, a very delicate and complex one, not least because the restrictions on it are produced on different levels and are not always easily identifiable, especially by a superficial reading. there are freedoms that are denied through legislative acts this was the case in hungary there are other freedoms that are instead denied by concentration processes that exclude the smallest or the weakest and these are less visible, they are not immediately transposed, most of the time and then there are freedoms that are denied by virtue of the creation of a conflict of interest between those who manage a part of the communication system and at the same time manage or perform institutional or political functions of first importance; it's happened several times over the last few years in my country. i believe, however, that all these forms must be accompanied by an increased focus on the network. today, much of our communication is done through this channel, and this is where we must start if we want to have a process which guarantees full freedom for all, not just the traditional dimensions.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i certainly agree with the idea of fighting tax evasion and, above all, tax havens and perhaps also taxing the financial sector, which has unfortunately led to the current crisis. but i would also like to see it reflected in the lives of ordinary citizens, those who pay their taxes honestly and have done so up to now. i wonder if it is always a duty to pay taxes or if it comes to a point where paying taxes becomes expropriation by the state. let me give you some examples. in my country, you pay 45% in taxes for not having services; is it right to pay taxes if you don't have services? is it right to pay taxes and then see that your municipality doesn't have the money to pave the roads? is it right to pay them and then see them cut health care, to see that unfortunately schools don't work, to see that the whole state machine, to which you pay taxes, doesn't work? then there comes a point where you wonder what the right choice is. because you see, unfortunately in my country, businesses die because of taxes, they die because they want to pay taxes, and when the state has debts to these companies, these debts from the state are not paid. so let's also try to remember those honest citizens who pay their taxes and die for it.

answer to a blue-card question. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, there is no doubt that adjustments to fiscal policies are also needed within the european union. we cannot think of going outside the union to combat tax evasion if we do not take the necessary steps within the union to have a fair and balanced level of taxation. we cannot think that there are countries within the union where it is possible to pay a much lower level of taxation than in other countries. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, mr minister, commissioner, we are talking today about tax evasion and fraud, which have created a gap of a trillion in the annual budget of the european union. all this, which i personally consider a low estimate, is not damage caused by individual taxpayers, but by real criminal organizations: the biggest european banks are under investigation for tax evasion. we are striking at our citizens in the name of austerity and austerity, but austerity should serve above all to impose clear rules and transparency on the financial giants and the banking systems. italy, as mr rinaldi has already said, has in the past invented a criminal financial instrument called the tax shield, for the sole purpose of allowing the return of illicit capital resulting from criminal activities, arms trafficking, drugs, extortion and bribery. the european parliament has been silent about this, the european ministers have been silent about this. to be credible, we must immediately fill the regulatory gap. the crim committee, which i have the honour of chairing, has already identified several tax havens among the member states and we will be calling for exemplary sanctions. i ask the council to comment on the links between organised crime, money laundering and tax evasion; i would also ask the rapporteur to put her experience at the disposal of crim.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the council meeting tomorrow will have on its agenda energy policy, fiscal policy, the fight against fraud, economic and monetary union, practically the whole european question. i also heard in the debate this morning that this is a technical council because there will be a political council in june. i believe that the political council and therefore the political strategy and therefore, as a colleague has said, the european route are the prerequisites for solving these problems. i would like to draw your attention in particular to the letter which the president of the european council has written to the presidents of the various countries. it is a letter of urgency, if not of despair at what has not been done, a letter of demand to do more, to be able to harmonize, to be able to intervene for the individual states not in an intergovernmental situation but in a more strategic situation, in a federal situation. europe has been opening up to this discussion in recent times and we see that on the part of france and perhaps germany itself there is a willingness to understand that the culture of rigor has been overcome and that we have had consolidation of accounts in various countries, but there has been no growth; i would like to say that the commission has been very careful in its approach to the problem of the european parliament, and that it has been very careful in its approach to the problem of the european parliament. so, once again, parliament cannot give a specific indication of the real problems which the council must overcome, but a broad indication of a political path, as a prerequisite for solving all the problems of europe which are on the agenda for tomorrow.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, as we have understood, the european council of tomorrow is likely to be more of a sectoral council, a ministerial council, than a political institution that feels itself invested with major decisions in the face of enormous problems. but something is moving on the european horizon. the need for a credible political unity is being re-awakened, and on the other hand there is a call for concrete and urgent initiatives for young people and employment. but perhaps none of this will be echoed in the council tomorrow, and so we hope that this responsibility, we ask that this responsibility be assumed by the council in june, because the moment of the test has come. the united states and japan are invoking the cycle of recovery and europe is expected to make a breakthrough, including its political legitimacy. but we will not pass the test with words, as my colleagues used to say, and if we continue on a double track, with big proclamations, big programmes and few means, sometimes contradictory. energy is an example, and i would like to ask the commissioner, but above all the council: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. the council must say something, even if it does not say something, but it must say something! and then, as regards infrastructure, on the one hand the council is talking about large investment plans and on the other hand the council itself, madam minister, is reducing the budget for the cef from 9 to 5 billion. which is the real council, the first or the second? i shall ask you formally to put this contradiction on the table tomorrow, you must have an answer. you also know that parliament is asking for these funds to be given more for investment instruments than for aid, 5 billion for aid is ridiculous - with the need that we have in europe - and the council is asking for participation, not leaving it to the commission alone to decide on priorities. this is consistency: decisions, not words, and above all consistency.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i am against this report because it is weak and lacks substance. it is not possible to recommend to the member states that they should proceed with caution in introducing new taxes, but it is necessary to tell the member states that they must stop imposing new taxes at a time when the crisis is leading to the closure of businesses and unemployment. i would also like to remind you that the directive which was intended to give the commission the power to decide on the cost of co2 allowances was rejected at the last plenary session, thanks only to the house's vote against it. if this proposal were to pass, it would have distorted the market and pushed manufacturing firms and energy-intensive industries to third countries. we must have the courage to say that the european union too must stop imposing strict accounting rules, instead of considering the need to revise the rules governing the european central bank. it is essential to amend the treaties so that the ecb, instead of financing banks at a ridiculous rate of 0.50%, can finance companies and governments at the same rate.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, there is no doubt that tax evasion and fraud are now more than ever an essential part of money laundering. the money laundering activities which very often form an essential part of criminal systems are being discussed in detail in the crim committee which will be approved as a mid-term report in june this year. the commission and the council can and must do more, starting with the revision of the savings directive. harmonising tax rules is essential, as is the exchange of selected and up-to-date information, tax fairness and solidarity, but also a banking union and cooperation agreements with third countries - particularly those third countries where there are tax havens - linking trade with information exchanges, banking secrecy and effective sanctions against banks, including withdrawal of licences.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mr sarvamaa's text on the draft council decision on the conclusion of the agreement on certain aspects of air services between the eu and sri lanka. this text amends the agreements previously concluded in the parts which allow the government of sri lanka to unilaterally revoke, refuse or suspend the authorizations of a community air carrier, in the event that it is not owned or controlled by that member state or its nationals. i believe that this intervention is duly aimed at protecting european commercial interests.
in writing. the aim of the agreement is to put an end to discrimination against european carriers. in fact, as it stands, sri lanka can refuse, suspend and revoke the authorisations of an eu air carrier if the ownership or effective control of the aircraft is held by a national of another eu state. this is discrimination contrary to article 49 tfeu. i therefore vote in favour of this, in order to protect the interests of european airlines.
in writing. - pursuant to rule 81 of parliament's rules of procedure, we have been asked to give our opinion on an international agreement whose conclusion is subject to our approval. as relations between member states and third countries in the field of international air transport have always been governed by bilateral agreements, we consider it important to support the government of sri lanka, which has already signed 15 such agreements. when the commission negotiated the horizontal agreements with the third countries concerned in 2003, it allowed all european union carriers to enjoy the right of establishment and to have access without discrimination to routes between the eu and third countries. we therefore believe that it is essential that the provisions of the agreements signed by the sri lankan government be supplemented by the provisions of a single agreement concluded on behalf of the european union. in particular, we would like to stress the importance of article 2 of the agreement, which is aimed at regulating the designation of the authorization and the revocation of the authorization, but which explicitly provides that sri lanka may not discriminate against air carriers of member states of the european union on the basis of their nationality.
in writing. − in the field of international air transport, relations between member states and third countries are traditionally governed by bilateral air services agreements. these agreements contain a 'designation clause' which allows a third country to refuse, revoke or suspend the authorisations or licences of an air carrier designated by a member state but not substantially owned or effectively controlled by that member state or its nationals. i agree with the rapporteur, who recommends that the committee on transport and tourism give its approval to the conclusion of the agreement, and i have voted in favour of the proposal.
in writing. − the agreement between the member states of the european union and the government of the democratic socialist republic of sri lanka is necessary to unify, replace and supplement the provisions of the 15 bilateral agreements already signed governing relations between member states and third countries on air services. as stated by the court of justice of the european union in 2002, there cannot be provisions in air service agreements which limit the benefits to one state only, and it is essential to overcome the designation clause, through an eu designation clause, so as not to limit the content to air carriers belonging to one member state only but to extend it to all carriers of the countries of the european union. having regard to the council decision authorising the commission in 2003 to reach an agreement on the solution of the problem; having regard to the agreement itself between the union and sri lanka, which underlines the commitment of the asian country not to discriminate against air carriers of member states on the basis of their nationality, thus resolving potential conflicts of laws which make the new provisions fully compliant with european union law, i express a favourable opinion.
in writing. - i support the kohlicek report on the 'agreement establishing a general framework for enhanced cooperation between the european union and the european organisation for the safety of air navigation'. i believe that cooperation between the eu and the intergovernmental organisation eurocontrol will speed up the implementation of the single sky legislation, without which europe risks losing the challenge of maintaining high levels of competitiveness and efficiency in european industry.
in writing. - the european union has, since its foundation, been able to find what unites it and give it more importance than what divides it. again, i see this underlying philosophy confirmed: the european union has a role to play in this area, and the eu is not the only one to have a role to play. a partnership ensures their expertise with our legal cover. we all have something to gain. that is why i voted in favour of this proposal.
in writing. − since 2004, efforts have been made to bring the competences relating to the aviation sector, which until then had been the responsibility of the individual member states, under the community decision-making mechanism. this is to overcome the malfunctioning caused by the fact that airspace continues to be regulated according to national borders. the european industry must be made more competitive, and this would save 419 billion in the union's gdp and create up to 328 000 new jobs. i therefore vote in favour of the single sky project.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the agreement is a step towards strengthening relations between the european union and the european organisation for the safety of navigation, in particular by proposing particular synergies with the european aviation safety agency (easa). in particular, i welcome the confirmation of eurocontrol's role as the eu's technical and operational arm in the implementation of the single european sky (ses) programme. the programme aims to implement measures to make flights safer, greener and more cost-efficient, ultimately improving the service offered to citizens. it is hoped that the text of the agreement can be ratified and thus made operational as soon as possible.
in writing. − as expressly provided for in the single european sky legislation, the commission has designated eurocontrol as the single body for the assessment of performance, safety standards and air traffic management in europe since 2011. as eurocontrol is an intergovernmental organisation with 39 contracting parties from all over europe, we believe it is important to confirm it as the operational technical arm of the european union in the development and implementation of the single european sky programme. the agreement, which was signed provisionally in december last year, has been definitively approved by us today. we are convinced that the main objective of this agreement remains to improve cooperation between the european union and eurocontrol, with a view to strengthening its main role of assistance and coordination in the field of air safety. the establishment of a joint committee responsible for managing relations between the parties will, we are confident, ensure the proper application of the agreement.
in writing. − eurocontrol is an intergovernmental organisation with 39 contracting parties from all over europe, including all member states except estonia. in accordance with the single european sky (ses) legislation, the commission has designated eurocontrol as the performance evaluation body of the ses (in 2010) and as the network manager for atm network functions (in 2011). the objective of the agreement is to strengthen and consolidate cooperation between the european union and eurocontrol in order to enable eurocontrol to assist the eu in the implementation of the eusc and related european policies. i agree with the rapporteur that the agreement will make a further contribution to the achievement of the single european sky, and i voted in favour of the proposal.
in writing. - the report on the draft resolution on the conclusion of the agreement establishing cooperation between the european union and the european organisation for the safety of air navigation draws attention to the need to strengthen cooperation between the union and the intergovernmental organisation eurocontrol. i am in favour of the proposal because such cooperation would make an important contribution to the development and implementation of the cue (single european sky) programme which divides airspace into functional blocks in order to maximise the efficiency of its use and would enable eurocontrol to provide assistance to the eu by harmonising air traffic management and regulation, while keeping safety as a primary objective, without ignoring that european airspace is one of the most congested in the world. i also think it is useful that the agreement also provides for cooperation with the european aviation safety agency (aesa) on air traffic safety and environmental issues, as well as the establishment of a 'joint committee' responsible for the management and proper application of the agreement.
in writing. - i support the report by mr pack on the amendment of regulation (eec/euratom) no 354/83 on the storage of the historical archives of the institutions at the european university institute in florence. i believe that the amendments to this regulation will allow for the enhancement of the protection of personal data contained in the archive and, at the same time, for more effective consultation of the archive by making part of the archives available for electronic access where possible.
in writing. the regulation we have now adopted gives legal and financial stability to the preservation of the historical memory of all the european institutions. the archives in florence have been established on a contractual basis between the european institutions and the european university institute. it is now imperative to preserve and make available to the public and to scholars in an orderly manner all the documents which have built and are building europe. only the court of justice and the european central bank are exempt from this obligation, but may use the archives on a voluntary basis. the possible digitisation of the material stored will make it easier to consult and store it. in this way, knowledge of europe's roots will make its future path quicker and more confident. we must thank the italian government for providing a complex of buildings of extraordinary value, which are appropriate to the beauty of the european project. i should also like to thank the council and the commission for the speed with which the regulation was finalized and the parliament for the unanimous agreement it expressed. i am particularly grateful to the committee on culture and education and its chairman, mr pack. my committee, the afco, has been able to work together in complete harmony and with great determination.
in writing. the report concerns the amendment of the regulation on the deposit of eu archives at the university institute of florence. the changes concern the financing of these archives, their availability by electronic means and the protection of personal data contained therein. since the amendments do not affect the basis of the regulation, being marginal, i shall vote in favour of the proposal.
in writing. - the proposal for a council regulation which we have approved today finally provides a more solid legal and financial framework for cooperation between the european union and the european university institute in florence than the present one. the latter has always been responsible for managing the historical archives of the institutions of the union, having, thanks to a contract with the italian government, suitable premises at its disposal to house the archives on a permanent basis and free of charge. the amendments adopted today make it almost an explicit obligation for each institution of the european union to deposit its archives with the institute, and they set out in detail the system for financing archives and the possibility of using these archives electronically, where possible. the most interesting part is certainly the one concerning the obligation to finance the european university institute from the general budget of the union, i.e. through contributions from the depositing institutions, based on the criterion that the amount of the contributions is proportional to the size of the respective staffing tables of the depositing institutions. finally, in the light of these amendments, we consider it important that the text recognises the european data protection supervisor as the supervisory authority over the eu institutions, in accordance with regulation (ec) no 45/2001.
in writing. − the historical archives of the eu institutions are an important source of information on the history and heritage of the european union. it is therefore essential to allow access to archives for public consultation and preservation of information relating to the eu institutions and to support research on the history of european integration. agreeing that the proposal for a council regulation currently under consideration by the european parliament under the assent procedure (article 81 (1) of the regulation) provides a more solid legal and financial framework for cooperation between the eu and the ieu, i voted in favour of the proposal.
in writing. - i welcomed the proposal to amend commission regulation (eec/euratom) no 354/83 governing the keeping of the historical archives of the union by the florence eui. this proposal not only confirms the european university institute in florence as the manager of the historical archives of the institutions of the union but also lays the legal and financial foundations for interinstitutional cooperation. i consider it important that the institutions' files should be made available to the public by means of electronic documents thanks to optical archiving, that the institutions should be required to deposit all documents in their archives with the eui and that management costs should be financed by contributions from the eu budget. archives are part of europe's cultural and historical heritage and it is significant that the union, in addition to respecting the diversity of eu countries, is keen to protect and develop europe's cultural heritage as preserved in the records of our institutions.
in writing. − the historical archives of the european institutions are an important resource for the history of the union: the commission has also been asked to provide information on the european union's activities in the field of archives. i therefore voted in favour of the text presented by mrs on. pack, considering that this proposal for a regulation provides a more appropriate legal basis and a financial framework to improve cooperation between the eu and the european university institute in florence.
in writing. − the forthcoming european elections will be of particular importance as they could bring about a revival of european integration, despite the ongoing economic crisis and the growing distrust of the eu fuelled by populism. but the next vote may well be the turning point. it is a question of making the european citizens understand what is at stake and convincing them of the decisive effectiveness of their vote. the resolution we have just adopted is part of a set of instruments designed to achieve this objective. this means allowing the president of the commission and the commission as a whole to be appointed shortly after the vote, so that citizens can feel the effectiveness of their democratic participation. of course, this positive effect is added to another more substantial argument in favour of early voting: the commission is not prepared to accept the amendments tabled by the committee on budgets. the measure which is desired by the adoption of this resolution must of course be consistent with other more far-reaching rules, first of all the one which, by defining the statute of european political parties, allows a better spread of european consciousness which will guide citizens to make informed choices.

in writing. − in many of the member states the pentecost weekend will coincide with the previously chosen election period, i.e. 5-8 june 2014, so i voted in favour of moving this date forward to 22-25 may 2014. this will also give parliament more time to prepare for the election of the president of the european commission, since for the first time political parties will have to announce their candidate for this prestigious post. we are therefore awaiting the council's decision, which will have to be taken by june on the alternative electoral period.
in writing. − the request to consult the council on the draft amendment of the electoral period for the european elections is the result of a wish expressed several times in the past, in particular in the february 2012 report adopted by the committee on constitutional affairs. in order to enable the countries of the european union to organise and hold the elections in the most appropriate and correct way possible, and in view of the importance of this decision, we consider it essential to act swiftly and decisively in this matter, using the simplified procedure provided for in article 46 of our rules of procedure. we have therefore today voted in favour of moving the next european consultation period forward, which will take place in all 28 member states at the same time, from thursday 22 to sunday 25 may 2014, and not, therefore, from 9 to 12 june. in view of the fact that many member states celebrate pentecost in june, we thought it appropriate to approve the proposal for a council decision in its present form, in order to avoid overlapping the electoral period with the religious holiday. we also believe that this advance is essential to give the new parliament more time and to prepare it for the election of the new president of the european commission in july.
in writing. − the request echoes a wish already expressed several times in the past, in particular in the report adopted by the committee on constitutional affairs on 1 february 2012 on a proposal to amend the electoral act regarding the possibility of holding elections in the period from 15 to 18 may or from 22 to 25 may 2014. i agree with the rapporteur, who recommends that the committee on constitutional affairs adopt the proposal for a council decision in its present form and as soon as possible, and i therefore voted in favour of the proposal.
in writing. - having regard to the report by mr casini, i am in favour of the adoption of the proposal for a council decision by the committee on constitutional affairs as it stands at present and thus of bringing forward the election period for the eighth elections of the representatives of the european parliament, in order to avoid it coinciding with the long weekend of pentecost. also bearing in mind the resolution of 22 november 2012 in which parliament asked the council to be consulted on the possibility of assessing two periods in may and considering that the council has accordingly decided to set the new elections from thursday 22 to sunday 25 may 2014, i am confident that the decision on the new date will be adopted swiftly, so as to enable the governments of the member states to make the necessary arrangements for the organisation of the elections.
