in writing. - i agree with the report by mr lehne on the application of directive 2004/25/ec on public procurement. member states transposed this directive in 2006 to harmonise the rules on takeover bids. unfortunately, the adoption of the legislation coincided with the onset of the economic crisis and therefore, at present, it is not possible to assess its application correctly as there is no data to confirm any changes or harmonisation measures to be taken in the future.
in writing. − after a long procedural process, this important directive aimed at harmonising the rules on public procurement in the european union has been adopted. i agree with the european commission's assessment of the application of this instrument in the internal rules: additional harmonisation measures are necessary. it must be acknowledged, however, that the onset of the economic crisis has had a negative impact on the potential of these new rules. it is therefore worth waiting to consider the introduction of further amendments to the directive. i voted in favour because i agree with the points made.
in writing. − the market has suffered from a lack of funds to implement the may 2006 apa directive, which makes it difficult to assess its proper application. the report highlights some of the features of the directive: the level playing field between all member states, the competence of national authorities as regards supervision, concerted action to understand when the takeover obligation is triggered, national derogations for minority shareholders and the rules on informing employees of a company subject to takeover. i am voting in favour of the report as a whole.
in writing. the report adopted today concerns the definition of the rules governing public procurement, which have been the subject of harmonisation at european level for many years. there is no doubt that the economic crisis that erupted in 2008 severely affected the highly contracted public tender market, which was only partly offset by financial transactions. the revision of company law, which is not limited to the rules on takeover bids, must therefore be reversed by a revival of the sector. the report also calls for the commission to monitor the development of the market for corporate control and to prepare an analysis of the impact of the application of the directive when acquisition activity returns to pre-crisis levels.
in writing. - we have today welcomed mr lehne's request for a review of directive 2004/25/ec, adopted at the end of 2003, on public tenders, as we do not consider it to be exhaustive in its context of application. we believe that we should consider the possibility of introducing additional harmonisation measures at european union level, thanks to some data from external studies and on the basis of several reports from the commission itself, which suggest to us the need for a careful review of the directive. in the light of financial and economic developments in recent years, with particular reference to the financial crisis that has affected europe since 2007, we believe that there have been strong and dramatic repercussions on the financing of acquisitions. considering that support for m&a activity is essential for the proper functioning of the market and noting, furthermore, that market participants have suffered from credit shortages and that low equity prices due to the crisis have made equity acquisitions less attractive, we believe that further data collection is necessary not only to ascertain the need for changes to the directive but also to define the precise harmonisation measures to be taken in the near future.
in writing. - with regard to the motion for a resolution on the application of the directive on takeover bids, i expressed my favourable opinion because it seeks to safeguard the rights of shareholders, employees and other interested parties during the conduct of takeover bids. the economic and financial situation of recent years has limited the evaluation of the application of the directive because of the crisis which has had a worrying impact on the financing of acquisitions, but i consider the plan to protect workers' rights during acquisition processes and the provision to guarantee their representatives the rights of information and consultation, as well as the right to participate in the acquisition phases, to be able to negotiate on issues affecting their assistants, to be important. i also think it is important to adopt a system of controls and sanctions to combat violations of workers' rights and to make use of specific eu funds to help companies deal with the consequences of hostile takeovers.
in writing. the text presented by mr lehne, chairman of the committee on legal affairs, shares the approach of the european commission, which stresses the need to propose harmonised rules on public procurement within the union. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competition' in the context of the directive on the protection of consumers.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of this report because the european industrial sector, which has been in serious difficulty for several years, still remains a fixed point in gdp. the cause of the decline is in most cases linked to the backwardness of the industrial fabric and that is why europe, in order to emerge from the crisis, must provide concrete tools for those in difficulty, we must help them in an intelligent, creative way, following the most virtuous examples. there are several areas and infrastructures that could be reused, reinvented through the use of new technologies. such a change cannot be made immediately because it requires not only time but also considerable economic resources. in this sense, it is not possible to ask local authorities or local authorities, which are unable to provide basic services to their citizens, to pay for these measures. europe must help businesses to make the best use of the community's resources, the only resources that are certain and available for the coming years, resources needed for development, growth and jobs.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of this report because industry is certainly one of the main strengths of european competitiveness on the world stage. however, industrial policy still shows a certain lack and insufficiency of political initiative on the part of the union, despite the intention to increase the share of industrial production in eu gdp by 2020. the difficulties of old industrial regions, which have suffered a serious economic decline in recent years, are proof of this lack of policy and of the excessive tension which the community authorities have blindly wished to place solely on the need for financial discipline in public budgets. the report we have approved also stresses that industrial policy tends to focus on the specific day-to-day problems of industry and that further aid measures should be introduced to assist the old industrial regions. more importantly: it notes that more integrated and systematic approaches would be needed at the level of the european union. greater effort and efficiency are needed to help local authorities too.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to express my support for the report on regional strategies for industrial areas, because i have always considered and still consider it essential that this issue be dealt with in an appropriate manner in the current negotiations on the regulations concerning the structural funds for the period 2014-2020. in fact, in order to achieve the europe 2020 objectives, which are an integral part of the regulations, it is necessary to take into account the need to restructure or reconvert old industrial regions. at the same time, however, it seems appropriate and necessary to require, in view of the specific characteristics of each region, also in the industrial sector, that the regions adopt an integrated approach to a very complex issue such as industrial conversion, which must involve economic, environmental, labour and social policies in the broadest sense.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, as the shadow rapporteur for this report i can only support the work of the committee on regional development and, above all, stress the importance of the appeal we make to the commission in this report. the revival of industrial policy is of fundamental importance. if we look at the data of the last years, we see that from 2008 to 2011 there was a loss of 4 percentage points of gdp in industrial production with a decrease of 11% in employment. the relaunch of industrial action is essential, but it is equally important that the european union should begin to use its instruments in an integrated way, not just to relaunch sectors. it is important that this action announced and communicated by vice-president tajani finds its synergistic and productive dialogue with cohesion policy. only in this way will the relaunch of industrial policy and therefore the action announced by the commission be able to produce its effects.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, we welcome the rapporteur's proposal for the reindustrialisation of those areas which have been particularly exposed to radical decline and which now need specific support. the european industry accounts for 16% of the union's gdp, so a solution must be found to halt the decline. the commission must ensure and facilitate the use of the cohesion fund, which can help to revive european smes and, through regional plans, to reconvert industrial areas where europe has been at the forefront, thereby encouraging the development of specific infrastructures affecting transport, energy and telecommunications. the new programming period 2014-2020 could offer opportunities to overcome administrative boundaries and accompany the conversion process, devoting not only the cohesion fund but also a large part of those unused structural funds to modernisation, diversification and tax-free strategies, especially for smes and craft industries, with a particular focus on areas affected by natural disasters or otherwise disadvantaged.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the industrial sector can play a role in boosting the economy in europe, because according to the commission for every 100 jobs created in industry, 60 to 200 new jobs can be created in related sectors. unfortunately, with the crisis, there was a reduction in production of up to 20% and jobs were reduced by up to 11%. in view of the forthcoming programming, better formulation and implementation of the structural funds is needed, including policies aimed at the conversion of old industrial areas and especially the reindustrialisation of industrial areas in crisis, involving in particular young people. the aim is to safeguard employment levels by safeguarding the industrial heritage in terms of cultural, historical and architectural heritage and above all skills and know-how.
in writing. − the treaty on the functioning of the european union provides in article 173 that: 'the union and the member states shall ensure that the conditions necessary for the competitiveness of the union industry are met.' the industrial sector of the european union has always been a driving force for job creation, economic growth and the promotion of innovation in all regions of the union. european industry accounts for about 16% of the union's gdp. however, even as a result of the decline of many traditional industries, such as coal, steel or textiles, which had contributed to the prosperity of several regions for decades, some regions are experiencing economic difficulties. many of them are therefore dependent on european funding to support the conversion and restructuring of industrial areas. it is clear that, in the context of the economic and financial crisis, the high ambitions of the union's industrial policy and the europe 2020 strategy cannot be achieved by sectoral policies alone, but support from cohesion policy measures becomes strategic. in this context, the new instruments proposed in the draft regulation laying down provisions for the new programming period 2014-2020 could offer a concrete opportunity to overcome administrative boundaries and accompany the industrial restructuring process.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the geier report on regional strategies for industrial areas in the european union. a coordinated approach is needed at community, national, regional and interregional level in order to exploit the full potential of the european economy, in particular through the combined use of the cohesion fund and the structural funds.
in writing. - i strongly support the report, which reflects the values underlying our vision for the future of europe and our economies. in other cases, it was considered possible, partly due to the inadequate responsibilities of local governments, to deal with the manufacturing crisis that began in the 1990s with automatic and hasty strategies that favoured services and tertiary services, even where there were obviously neither resources nor relevant markets. i particularly agree with the points made in paragraph 10, noting that a more compelling scheme, for example the fas funds, would have resulted in conversion operations being more consistent with medium- and long-term objectives. the theme of reindustrialisation, based on high added value and technological advantage, is becoming central today as global governance bodies are confronting the problem of the hypertrophic growth of a purely financial economy that ends up damaging real economies and the quality of life in our communities. i believe it is a wise strategy, as well as a moral duty, to direct resources towards the recovery or return of productivity in our industrial districts.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because i appreciate the pragmatic approach of the rapporteur. increasing attention to and incentives for the development of renewable energy technologies has a twofold positive effect. firstly, to reduce the dependence on third countries, which is proving to be increasingly burdensome from an economic and political point of view, and secondly, to achieve the objectives we have set ourselves for the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions and the protection of the environment. in the light of the discussions currently under way to revise certain existing biofuel directives, i would like to remind you that in this specific sector, care must be taken to ensure that intensive cultivation of products intended to become alternative fuels does not undermine food security and is not counterproductive. this activity can only be of real benefit to our objectives if the total amount of energy used for cultivation does not exceed the amount saved. another key point is the need to complete and strengthen the transfrontier transmission networks. often sites suitable for renewable energy production are located in marginal locations. unless we ensure that there is a real european energy network, we will never be able to reap the benefits that renewable energy offers us.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this own-initiative report by parliament which deals with a subject of fundamental importance: the commission has already proposed a number of measures to improve the quality of the environment. it is undeniable that industry, with its 16% contribution to european gdp, is one of the union's strengths. the old industrial regions, which have produced a great deal of wealth, are now facing a period of serious decline, aggravated by the economic crisis, and therefore deserve a rapid and effective conversion strategy. it is therefore urgent to use all financial instruments to achieve the ambitious target of raising the level of contribution to gdp from 16% to 20% by 2020. in particular, the resources made available through cohesion policy and the structural funds, together with those provided by the european investment bank, must be managed in an integrated manner with national and regional resources, so as to optimise the result. at the same time, policies should include employment, training and education components to support young people and innovative smes.
in writing. the report focuses on those areas of europe which have seen intensive industrialisation followed by economic decline. it recognises the importance of industry in funding research, development and innovation but also stresses that the measures taken often do not address the specific problems of the various regions. new aid is needed in this regard. these include the redevelopment of housing, the renewal of infrastructure, the development of sustainable forms of transport and new skills. since the report also proposes the creation of high-technology parks based on cross-border cooperation, i am voting in favour.
in writing. − the industrial sector has always been a driving force for job creation, growth and the promotion of innovation in all regions of the european union. it is important to remember that although the importance of the industrial sector has declined over the last 50 years, european industry still accounts for around 16% of eu gdp. for all the areas that have suffered the most from the crisis, with a phenomenon of gradual, if not incessant, closure of industrial plants, it is necessary to think of a common strategy of redevelopment and conversion, in order to guarantee growth and prosperity and not fall into the abyss of recession. many regions in the european union are now dependent on finance to support the conversion and restructuring of their old industrial areas. the report stresses that sustainable regeneration in formerly industrialised regions is very expensive. i think that an effort to do so is necessary. europe, in the name of growth, can and must respond to the needs of the territories. european public funding should play an important role in the effort to reconvert abandoned industrial areas. of course, i am also convinced that resources cannot be wasted. there is a need for foresight and planning to highlight the risks and possible benefits of an operation such as this.
in writing. the historic period of crisis we are living through is seeing industrial production fall from 20% to 16%. although industrial jobs have fallen by 11%, industry remains one of the main strengths of the european economy and represents a real opportunity for economic recovery in the member states. i therefore support the decision to adopt targeted regional strategies for the structural transformation of the old industrialised regions in order to create new paths of development and growth. in detail, industrial districts, as exemplified by the italian case, have been excellent examples of social and economic development, through the development of highly professional and specialised local realities. with the economic crisis and the advent of globalisation, unfortunately, the industrial district system has also lost its competitiveness and taken a hit. the implementation and planning of policies for the development of regional industrial areas, through targeted investment strategies, is therefore a key starting point for the development of the european economy and of the individual member states.
in writing. − the proposal to provide support and guidance for decision-making in support of integrated territorial investment, which was adopted here today, focuses on the need to assist in the development of regional development strategies for old industrial areas. although each region has its own characteristics and there is currently no programme for a regional strategy for industrial areas, this own-initiative report aims to highlight the common features shared by all the old industrialised regions in order to identify opportunities and solutions. recently, due to the decline of many traditional industries, many regions of the european union have become dependent on european funding to support the conversion and restructuring of old industrial areas. given that, in the context of the economic crisis, the ambitions of the european union's industrial policy and the europe 2020 strategy cannot be achieved by sectoral policies alone, we believe that support from cohesion policy measures has become essential. as a result of the eu enlargement process, regional disparities have increased and as a result public awareness has moved away from the old industrialised areas. in the light of these considerations, we strongly believe that eu cohesion policy can play a leading role in such a context.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i am voting in favour of the european parliament's motion for a resolution on regional strategies for industrial areas in the european union. the european industrial sector has always been a driving force for job creation, growth, the promotion of innovation and european integration itself. the decline of many traditional industries, such as coal, steel and textiles, which had contributed to the prosperity of many regions, has made these regions particularly vulnerable to decline and in need of specific support. despite the economic and financial crisis, the european union must provide financial support for these regions, promoting the conversion and restructuring of their old industrial areas, with a view to a process of industrial redevelopment that will enable european industry to regain a central role in the continent's economy.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on regional strategies for industrial areas in the european union because i believe that the conversion and restructuring of industrial areas is necessary after the downsizing of european industry in recent decades. it is important to work on well-structured regional strategies to reconvert and develop old areas. strategies that will have to be environmentally sustainable, aiming at reducing carbon dioxide emissions and including measures to protect water, soil and air quality so that no harmful substances are released into the environment. given their high costs, these strategies will have to be implemented by relying on european but also national funding and the sale of abandoned industrial properties located in attractive locations. i believe it is essential that these processes also reduce health risks and the regions concerned will have to give greater importance to the participation of groups of citizens in the decision-making processes for planning the use of their territories.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the proposal for a regulation on the safety of offshore oil exploration, research and production aims to ensure, through a clear and updated framework, the dissemination in the european union of best practices already adopted by some member states. drilling is going deeper and deeper into dangerous waters where most of the oil fields are located, and only through reform involving both governments and industry will we be able to avoid environmental disasters such as those we often hear about in the newspapers or on television. one of the main issues to be stressed is the importance of ensuring that the authorities responsible for assessing the safety and environmental risks of drilling operations are independent of the authorities responsible for authorizing drilling.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, we welcome the adoption of this directive and the imposition of stricter limits on offshore oil exploration, as well as the provision of clear rules in terms of financial and economic liability for companies responsible for any damage to the environment. italy is second only to the united kingdom in the number of offshore installations, mainly located in the adriatic basin, a bassinethat is virtually closed and therefore all the more at serious risk if an accident should occur in its waters. the mediterranean is also one of the most biodiverse ecoregions in the world, with almost a quarter of the world's oil tankers passing through its waters. the italian installations are certainly less dangerous in terms of size, landform and technical characteristics than those in the north sea or the baltic sea, but this should not lead us to let down our guard with regard to safety and environmental protection. it is of paramount importance to avoid offshore drilling activities being carried out in the vicinity of tourist areas or where the effects on coastal communities and the marine environment would be devastating.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the proposal, as did my colleagues in the epp group, because i believe it is important, in the light of the 2010 deepwater horizon oil rig disaster, that companies based in the union operate worldwide in compliance with eu safety standards. not only should such high standards be promoted internationally in appropriate international and regional fora, but mechanisms to ensure that they are applied should also be further explored. the proposal for a regulation on the safety of offshore exploration activities is a very important piece of legislation in this respect. it is also a unique opportunity for the eu to address some serious shortcomings and to create a genuine security culture based on concrete measures and not, as is often the case, on mere bureaucracy. by ensuring a level playing field and reducing the margin for national, as well as regional, interpretation, the objective of the regulation can be effectively achieved, ultimately benefiting industry, national administrations and eu citizens.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by mr belet analysing the proposal for a european parliament and council regulation on the safety of offshore oil exploration, research and production. the need for european legislation to regulate the safety of this type of operation became clear following the deepwater horizon disaster in the gulf of mexico in 2010. i would like to reiterate my support for the principle: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's environmental policy is not disrupted by the introduction of new technologies.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this proposal for a directive because it was intolerable not to have a certain regulatory framework in the event of serious accidents in offshore activities linked to the extraction of hydrocarbons. we all remember the damage from the deepwater horizon tragedy in 2010, and none of us want anything like that to happen again. the first point concerns the prevention of accidents, and i think the rapporteur has done a very good job of finding the right text to deal with this. if something goes wrong, then there must be valid and effective emergency management protocols, and i think the text is appropriate on this second point too. finally, the allocation of responsibilities and competences must be clear, so as to avoid duplication which only harms the environment and workers. and here too the text proposed is very good. i congratulate the rapporteur.
in writing. − the need for european legislation in this area was already anticipated in april 2010, following the deepwater horizon accident in the gulf of mexico. the basic principles of this directive are as follows: who pollutes pays; the operator must have primary responsibility for the safety of operations and must have the competence to act, the public operator must be able to participate in the decision-making process and effective enforcement measures must also be taken. i am voting in favour of this.
in writing. - the news media have given us striking examples of the damage that offshore mining can cause. safety considerations are therefore needed to limit the possibility of accidents occurring off the european coast. a clear and defined regulatory framework is needed to achieve this. raising safety standards throughout the european union is the first step in this path of control and prevention. but as the report points out, the following are also essential: responsible licensing, the appointment of national safety authorities, the monitoring of drilling and clear environmental responsibility. the italian offshore activities, which have been operating since the 1960s, have never had a major accident or significant damage to the environment. in particular, italy has had no offshore accidents in the last 10 years, thanks to one of the most advanced regulations in the sector in europe. in other areas, where the weather conditions and operating procedures are different, however, the risk rises considerably. an accident, wherever it occurs in europe, has economic and environmental consequences affecting the whole community. it is therefore essential to start thinking about how to unify the rules in this area.
in writing. - having welcomed the european commission's proposal on the safety guarantees for offshore activities in the hydrocarbon sector, we have today approved a report suggesting some changes to strengthen it. recent major accidents have highlighted the limitations of offshore oil and gas installations, necessitating a safety response to ensure the protection of the eu marine environment in the event of major and potentially dangerous accidents. the proposal to require operators more clearly to implement the financial guarantees necessary to cover the costs of cleaning and compensation in the event of major accidents is unquestionably in line with the european union's environmental principle that 'the polluter pays'. we also believe that the provisions on public sector participation should be strengthened by introducing rules to ensure that the community is informed about major accidents and measures taken to limit environmental damage. finally, we hope that the work of the authorizing authorities will be in line with the relevant european directives, paying particular attention to ecologically sensitive marine environments and supporting employees with ever greater protection.
in writing. − we all remember the terrible disaster caused by the deepwater horizon oil spill in the gulf of mexico in april 2010, which killed 11 workers and spilled some 5 million barrels of crude oil into the sea: the environmental consequences have not yet been fully calculated, and we will probably be feeling them for a long time. it is therefore understandable that stricter rules and safer rules are needed in this sector, since the dangers and risks arising from this type of activity can be very serious. i regret, however, that this parliament has rejected an amendment to ensure greater protection for tourist areas and geologically unstable areas, where i believe offshore drilling should be banned: the environment must be respected as much as possible, especially where it requires special consideration. no one wants to stop research and development of new energy sources, but we must always act with the utmost care so that the damage caused by fate or imperfection does not prove to be unsustainable in the long run, both for nature and for man.
in writing. the commission has also adopted a proposal for a directive on the safety of gas and oil drilling operations. the new rules will oblige companies to prove their ability to cover potential damage arising from their activities, requiring them to submit a report on possible hazards and solutions before operations can begin. high standards are increasingly needed when it comes to risk management.
in writing. − the environmental accident of the deepwater horizon oil platform, which resulted in the spill of 780,000 m3 of crude oil in the gulf of mexico in 2010, has drawn the union's attention to the need to review eu policies to ensure greater safety in this area. i believe that best practice in the legislation of some member states needs to be disseminated throughout the eu and that it would be important to enhance cooperation between member states in order to exchange useful information on experience and expertise in accident prevention. i also welcome the need to involve the european maritime safety agency (emsa) in the preparation of contingency plans which promote regular exercises on possible risks. we expect union-based companies engaged in oil exploration and production worldwide to carry out their operations in accordance with the relevant eu safety rules everywhere and it will be important to promote these standards in international venues and thus to ensure their application. in addition, the licensing authorities should pay more attention to ecologically sensitive marine environments and also study any geological risks.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, it is absolutely imperative to promote the development of renewable energy sources. renewable energy, in addition to helping us fight climate change and strengthen europe's energy independence, offers clear environmental benefits, such as reducing air and waste pollution, increasing water protection and savings, and eliminating the risks associated with other forms of energy production. the european union has decided to phase out environmentally harmful subsidies by 2020 as indicated in the roadmap for a resource efficient europe. we call on the commission to propose an ambitious and binding union-wide target for 2030 to achieve a renewable economy by 2050. this commitment will ensure continuity and stability for companies wishing to invest in this sector. with the green technology market we are strengthening our industries for sustainable economic growth by creating, as the european commission has estimated, over three million jobs.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, as we know, the european union today is very much dependent on energy imports and therefore the time has come to start really promoting the development of our industries and new job opportunities by focusing on the new generation energy market. a secure, independent, diversified and low-emission energy supply throughout europe is certainly a goal and an opportunity to be realised; i am thinking in particular of small and medium-sized enterprises producing renewable energy on the energy market to promote the competitiveness of our industries and the creation of new green jobs. finally, the large-scale deployment of renewable energy sources also represents an opportunity for individual households and communities to become energy producers. experience has shown that to do this, binding long-term targets are needed, and it is therefore very important that, after this vote, the european commission sets a binding 2030 target for renewable energy in its new proposal.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the reference in the report we have adopted to the need for the european union to make a stronger and more binding commitment by 2030 to the share of renewable energy in the community's energy mix is undoubtedly making it stronger politically. the diversification of the european energy mix is based on a wide range of renewable energy technologies, which can ensure greater independence of the union from energy imports, which are still too high today, and greater autonomy from conventional energy sources, as well as concrete support for industrial recovery, in particular of energy-intensive industries in crisis, such as those in italy, for example, which concern the region from which i come, sardinia. secondly, greater diversification would ensure greater security of energy supply and greater environmental sustainability of energy production. finally, in implementing these policies, it should not be forgotten that the deployment of wind farms and solar panels can have an impact on the landscape and, consequently, on the tourism industry in small communities and islands. greater public consultation at local level should therefore be both necessary and mandatory.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, renewable energy policy is of the utmost importance for the future of the european union. it has already created 500 000 new jobs and will create more in the coming years. however, there are some important caveats to be aware of. first of all: the commission has already taken steps to ensure that the anti-dumping measures on chinese solar panels are not circumvented if certain countries acceding to the european union allow them to enter and that when these countries become an integral part of the union, they will have bypassed the anti-dumping measures. this is therefore a new fraud and a new danger. another aspect is the lack of constant and precise verification and control of the locations of some of these alternative energy instruments. we think about a lot of fields that should be agricultural and instead are used for solar panels, whereas instead all the roofs of buildings, factories, public facilities should have this system for creating energy. another warning is that too often foodstuffs that are supposed to be food or otherwise intended for livestock farming may be unfairly used for renewable energy. it's not renewable energy that destroys another heritage. i therefore welcome the report, which is very much in favour of further development, but i also support the call for effective controls and equal rules for all.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the binding targets set by the 2020 climate and energy package have given a strong impetus to the development of renewable energy and the green economy in europe, which holds the potential for growth and employment. continuing to invest in renewables is not only useful but necessary to move towards a european economy that is fossil-free, based on sustainability and energy independence. central to this design are the regional distribution networks needed to manage the integration of renewable energy production while maintaining security of supply. in order to provide certainty to investors and the market, it is essential that the european commission presents as soon as possible a legislative proposal on the new climate package, setting out the new targets to be achieved by 2030.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the renewable energies must be given maximum attention because the debate on energy is central and vital. the keywords must be: accessibility and sustainable prices. but i would like to make a few observations: gas in europe is four times more expensive than in the united states, and energy is twice as expensive. households spend between 7 and 17% on energy; the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the proposal for a directive on the protection of the environment in the event of a fire. so let us welcome the debate, but above all we need investment in infrastructure to rationalise supply and lower prices and also to make the technological leap for renewables. if we want to keep european industries in europe, if we want european companies to stay in europe, we must have competitive energy solutions.
in writing. − this report is part of the european debate on the promotion of renewable energy after 2020. in general, i share the need expressed in this report to carefully assess the costs and benefits associated with the introduction of a binding european target for 2030. in the light of national and european experience on the implementation of directive 2009/28/ec, i do not think it is cost-effective and effective to set a binding european target for 2030, while i believe that an indicative european target could be useful to set the path for future guidance on this matter. i believe that adequate support for research and development in this area is essential for the introduction of new renewable sources on the market, as is the strengthening of measures to facilitate the complicated process of building renewable energy production facilities. as the rapporteur has pointed out, the extreme disparity in the incentive schemes for renewable sources implemented by the member states has led to serious distortions of the internal market. i therefore share the request to the commission to harmonise incentive schemes at european level and to consider the advisability of entrusting a european superpartite authority with the responsibility of overseeing the harmonisation process.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution tabled by mr herbert reul, together with my colleagues from the ppe group, because i am convinced that action is needed to progressively increase the share of renewable energy sources in the energy supply of the countries of the european union, thus helping to reduce the dependence of our territories on fossil fuels. however, this will undoubtedly require the setting of sustainable targets and goals, including the redefinition of the eu roadmap to 2050. it should not be forgotten, among other things, that about half of europe's power stations will have to be replaced in the next decade and that the supply system will have to be made more modern and flexible in view of the increase in the share of renewable energy in the electricity, heating and transport sectors. it is a challenge the eu must take up if we are to make a decisive contribution to tackling climate change and to strengthening our energy independence. in addition, reducing the use of oil and its derivatives will undoubtedly bring benefits in terms of reducing air pollution, waste generation and water use for industrial purposes.
in writing. − recent independent studies identify res as a sector where europe retains a significant advantage: it is sufficient to consider that, as in 2012, individual member states are still among the top five investors in the five key sectors. germany and spain are immediately followed by the usa and china in terms of overall capacity excluding the hydro sector; in solar, four out of five of the top five global players are member states. across the union, the strong potential for cost reduction through new technologies is already altering the landscape, evolving towards mixed systems, based on widespread production and environmental awareness, to the point where the major fossil fuel energy players are at an advanced stage in their diversification and conversion processes, with greater emphasis on control of networks and services. this means that the rapporteur's recommendations, from targets above 30% of the mix, to the value of res for technological development, the growth of human capital, the diversification of energy sources, their potential for the single market, the importance of industrial and environmental policies, as well as the development of more environmentally sustainable lifestyles, are fully shared and justify my vote in favour.
in writing. − this proposal aims to highlight the benefits and advantages that member states and consumers can derive from renewable energy by implementing a series of changes that can ensure continued progress in the european internal energy market. i agree with the desire to facilitate the entry of new players into the market in order to increase competition and thus lower energy prices for consumers. the development of renewable energy is also important for the exploitation of biomass: waste represents a major opportunity for achieving the objectives of the european energy plan. i agree that europe must make further efforts in research, development and industry to make progress in renewable energy technologies. i agree with the call on the commission to help the member states to identify the most economically viable renewable energy sources in order to reduce costs and not hinder technological development. i have given a favourable opinion on this motion for a resolution and i fully agree with the views expressed.
in writing. − renewable energy sources will increasingly become the main source of energy supply for the eu in the future. the use of biomass, geothermal and biomethane is expected to increase and subsidies for harmful fossil fuels to decrease. the commission must assess whether the use of renewable sources in the eu can ensure sufficient energy production and whether there are additional supply possibilities. for example, in some member states the renewable energy generation network is not being fully exploited, consumers need to be empowered to save on their electricity bills, international cooperation needs to be increased and investment in innovation needs to be increased. the report does not take account of the fact that the european renewable energy policy has proved to be a failure, and i therefore vote against.
in writing. − i appreciate the realistic approach that emerges from the report and that seems to point towards a change of course on the european strategy for the promotion of renewable energies. there is a need to carefully assess the costs and benefits associated with introducing a binding european target for 2030. i think it would be more useful to give an indicative target to show the way forward. from a strictly economic point of view, it should not be forgotten that incentive schemes for renewable energy have been one of the main factors in the increase in energy prices in europe. i think it is therefore necessary to apply a criterion of economic and technical efficiency and to provide that the incentives for renewable sources for the period after 2020 are more market-oriented and limited in time. in other words, incentive schemes need to be harmonised at european level. finally, adequate support for research and development to enable 'technological leaps' is essential for the market uptake of new renewable sources, as is the harmonisation and strengthening of measures to facilitate the complex process of authorising and building renewable energy plants. the commission has also proposed that the community should develop cooperation with third countries with high solar, wind and water resources.
in writing. the market for renewable energy is a sector in strong growth with ample scope for development. this means that in real and market terms, the eu will have important opportunities for new investment and job creation, while safeguarding the environment and the territory. it is clear that in the context of the european single market, new methods of application must be considered in order to give greater impetus to this important economic sector. this is achieved by promoting renewable energy, investing more in research, making supply more competitive and providing the greatest possible protection for consumers. i believe that by working on these basic points, the renewable energy market can be one of the economic levers on which to restart the competitiveness of the european system.
in writing. - today we were asked to comment on the so-called 'no regrets' options for renewable energy sources identified by the european commission. together with energy efficiency measures and flexible and intelligent infrastructure, we are confident that these sources can represent an increasing share of europe's energy supply in the future. we believe that renewable energy will help tackle climate change and strengthen europe's energy independence, as well as having a positive impact on the environment in terms of reducing pollution and waste generation. we believe that it is essential to pursue this project and that it is necessary to emphasize the need for a cost-effective increase in the share of renewable energy sources, bearing in mind that they are an important growth engine for european competitiveness, as they offer enormous potential in terms of job creation and, moreover, make an important contribution to the development of new industries and export markets. we also believe that it is necessary to identify infrastructure solutions other than those which exist and which are developed exclusively on the basis of conventional energy sources. this is because we firmly believe that the greatest beneficiaries of the completion of the internal energy market will be consumers themselves.
in writing. - promoting the development of renewable energy sources must certainly be a primary objective for the european union, but this does not mean that heavy economic constraints should be imposed. renewable energy is attractive to the market today thanks to large public incentives and subsidies, i.e. thanks to a collective effort of taxpayers: i am not saying that this is wrong, especially if it can have positive repercussions in terms of energy saving and environmental protection. however, a careful analysis of the cost-benefit ratio should be carried out in order to find the right balance, which is above all sustainable in the long term. fortunately, an amendment to artificially and compulsorily increase the amount of renewables in the eu's energy mix by 2030 was rejected by this house today: i think that we cannot, in fact, place such a heavy bet on an area which has yet to be fully realised and in which continuous and thorough research is needed. i do not want europe to lose this important bet, but it must be managed realistically and pragmatically, without unnecessary leaps forward into the void.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i am voting in favour of the european parliament's motion for a resolution on the current challenges and opportunities for renewable energy in the european internal energy market. the share of renewable energy sources in the european energy mix is increasing. they make a significant contribution to a secure, independent, diversified and low-emission energy supply in europe, a priority of european energy policy. however, the potential of renewable energy sources in terms of energy supply is still not fully exploited and the eu still depends on energy imports for more than half of its final energy consumption. it is therefore necessary to set targets and targets for 2050 to ensure a credible and sustainable future for renewable energy in the eu.
in writing. - we need higher standards when it comes to risk management. i am convinced that the rules we are now adopting can become a model for the rest of the world. the rules laid down in the new directive on the safety of oil and gas drilling operations will oblige companies to prove their ability to cover potential damage arising from their activities and to report on possible hazards and solutions before operations can begin. i believe that all operators should ensure that they have access to sufficient physical, human and financial resources to prevent major accidents and to limit their consequences. i therefore call on the member states to prepare external contingency plans, which must include all offshore drilling installations under their jurisdiction. these plans should specify the role and financial obligations of the drilling companies and the role of the competent authorities and emergency teams.
in writing. - i gave a favourable opinion on the report which facilitates the promotion of renewable resources in europe for the production and use of clean energy. after this vote, it will be up to europe to do more to facilitate sustainable public and private investment in energy infrastructure and i hope for increased investment in renewable and clean energy, while avoiding incentives for the creation of large wind farms and huge expanses of solar panels that have already ruined our landscapes and taken acres from our crops. i hope that we can find a way of reconciling our agriculture with clean energy production facilities and at the same time encourage the energy self-sufficiency of small and mediumsized farms. we have a task to diversify the union's sources of supply by 2020 using clean energy sources. overall, these measures approved by the european parliament will boost the competitiveness of european businesses by ensuring lower energy tariffs for businesses and consumers.
in writing. - mr reul's report seems to be aiming at a change of course on the european strategy for the promotion of renewable energies. the latter not only help to tackle climate change and strengthen europe's energy independence, but also offer major additional environmental benefits in terms of reducing air pollution, waste generation and water use. this requires greater investment in research and development in this area and the provision of infrastructure to ensure the progressive integration of renewable energy sources into the european energy system.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted with conviction for the report, but there is still great concern that the transition from formal statements and legal provisions to a real change in attitude and the definition of mechanisms for the substantial application of the rules very often involves the risk of undermining the provisions on women's rights and gender equality. this is the case in several balkan countries in the process of accession, although gender equality is considered to be one of the fundamental rights of the european union, although, incidentally, much remains to be done in many member states as well. the commission, the council and parliament must therefore pay close attention to the real impact of the changes made by these states in their legislation and in their actual policies throughout the process leading to their accession. the number of women in political, public and business life in the balkan countries is still too low, and the knowledge and awareness of the public as a whole about the equality measures introduced or to be introduced in national legislation, the opportunities and rights that may flow from them, and the rights that must be guaranteed and exercised by women is poor. the balkan states must therefore make a greater effort, a tangible effort, in this important task.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of the report on women's rights in the balkan countries in the process of accession because in these countries, as regards gender equality, many of the laws required for access to europe have been adopted, but these laws have not always been effectively implemented within the political, civil and social fabric. promoting gender equality is a key part of the enlargement process of the european union and these governments are required to take concrete measures to provide accountability in both the private and political sectors and, above all, to strengthen the position of women in society. another worrying issue to be addressed in the balkan countries in the process of joining the european union is the question of stopping the trafficking of human beings within the union itself, which is fuelled by 30% of its citizens from the balkan countries and which often leads to prostitution offences in which women are victims. i therefore reaffirm my vote in favour of this report.
in writing. − i voted for this report which aims to stress the western balkans’ obligations, during the process of implementing the acquis communautaire, in the area of gender equality. it is fundamental that women in these countries increase their role in society through active participation and representation in political, economic and social life at all levels. the first step to making this possible is to increase public awareness of women’s rights and gender equality measures. for these reasons with this report we call on the commission and the governments of accession countries to foster awareness through the media, public campaigns and education programmes in order to eliminate gender stereotypes and promote female role models and women’s active participation in all paths of life.
in writing. - with regard to this proposal, i believe that women's rights are one of the cornerstones to be secured within our civil societies, especially with a view to the possible accession of new countries to the european union. in 2013, we can no longer afford to hear, speak and discuss cases of violence against women or discrimination in any field of social life. it is necessary to make the legal framework known so that every citizen knows his rights and can defend himself before a competent authority against any violations or discrimination. i believe that macedonia with the new draft law against sexual harassment and mobbing at work, the progress made in the fight against violence and the inclusion in the parliament of the "women's club" where mps from different parties cooperate in promoting women's rights, has done a good job, although there is still a need for greater functioning and coordination by the government in order to make the best progress. i voted in favour of this resolution because the points in this proposal are an excellent basis for working towards greater and more comprehensive protection for women in the western balkan countries.
in writing. − despite the great effort made by the balkan countries to align their legislation with the eu acquis in the field of women's rights and gender equality, to date these rights do not appear to us to be sufficiently protected. we therefore believe that it is necessary to provide for specific mechanisms for the application of provisions on women's rights. for these rights to have meaning and be effective, it is essential that there is a competent authority to receive complaints and to be prepared to defend the honour of women in the name of justice. promoting gender equality is an essential step for the accession countries, as it is a fundamental and founding value of the european union, enshrined in the treaties. we therefore call on the balkan countries in the process of accession to take specific measures to align their legislation on gender equality with that of the european union, to cooperate with civil society, and to organise initiatives in the field of police and the judiciary. the ultimate aim is to make clear to these countries what is expected of them, by giving them concrete incentives to bring their policies, budget and institutional framework into line with the fundamental principles of the european union.
in writing. - the report on women's rights in the balkan countries applying for eu membership, i give my favourable opinion. despite the significant efforts made by some countries to protect women's rights, unfortunately there are still some barriers to overcome. more efforts are needed to strengthen gender protection laws, to increase women's participation in the political system of their countries, to encourage authorities to increase support for internal debates and to strengthen the tools that allow women to denounce discrimination that still occurs in the labour market, in access to credit and, above all, in domestic abuse. in some countries, domestic violence has not yet been recognised as a criminal offence. women also play a very important role in stabilising and resolving conflicts. the protection of their rights must therefore be a priority to be placed at the centre of the negotiations with the candidate countries and with the potential candidate countries of the balkans.
in writing. − despite the great commitment of the balkan countries in their process of accession to the european union, much remains to be done in the field of women's rights and gender equality. the last report of the femm committee on this subject, dated 2008, highlighted gaps and very often unsatisfactory results. therefore, on the basis that promoting gender equality is a key part of the enlargement process, it is essential that these countries work to strengthen the concept of equal opportunities in society and pay greater attention to the protection of women, especially those exposed to discrimination.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, in the latest reporters without borders press freedom ranking, italy is in 57th place out of 179 countries, up only four places from the previous year. sixteen eu member states are among the top 30. this result is affected by italian defamation laws and the repeated so-called "babble" bills introduced in recent years by right-wing conservative forces. italy suffers from a very strong concentration in the television sector, where there is a substantial duopoly, but also in the wider publishing sector, which undermines pluralism and cultural diversity and leads to uniformity of content; i would like to ask the commissioner whether he is aware that the commission is not prepared to accept the amendments tabled by the committee on budgets. in this context, the role of the european institutions is crucial in ensuring that the european charter for freedom of the press and the charter of fundamental rights of the european union are not only respected but also implemented so that those countries which are lagging behind in terms of freedom of information and pluralism make substantial progress. the commission should present a legislative initiative in this area to set minimum requirements for member states.
in writing. − freedom of the media in europe is a cornerstone of the values enshrined in the treaties. an autonomous and strong public sphere, based on independent and plural media, constitutes the essential environment for the freedoms of civil society. for this reason this report reiterates that minimum essential standards should be defined in order to guarantee and promote freedom of information and a suitable level of media pluralism and independent media governance. member states and the eu must make sure that legally binding procedures are in place for the appointment of public media heads, management boards, media councils and regulatory bodies to ensure integrity, as well as maximum consensus in terms of representing the entire political and social spectrum. i also believe that it is important to stress the need for appropriate funding for public service media in order to guarantee their political and economic independence.
in writing. - i did not support mr weber's report on the 'eu charter: setting standards for media freedom throughout the eu' because i do not agree with the demand that the offence of defamation be decriminalised.
in writing. the report calls on eu member states to respect freedom of expression for both traditional and newer media - including social networks. the commission is also proposing to monitor legislation in this area, the independence of the editors, access to the media and the presentation of a commission study on the precarious working conditions of journalists. however, since the aim is to introduce decriminalisation of the crime of defamation in all member states, i am voting against it.
in writing. - today we have been asked to comment on the formulation of new standards for media freedom in europe. member states are invited to protect, promote and guarantee freedom of expression and information and pluralism in all media. we consider a pluralistic information landscape to be crucial for a functioning democratic system, and we hope that the working conditions of professionals in this sector, who are often working in precarious conditions today, will be improved. we believe that the scope of the audiovisual media services directive should be extended to establish minimum standards for the protection of the fundamental right to freedom of expression and information and media pluralism. we also call on the member states and the whole of the european union to support investigative journalism for its democratic function and its capacity to detect crime. finally, we are convinced that editorial statutes or "codes of conduct" for publishers and journalists are crucial to the independence of the industry, as they prevent owners, governments or others from interfering with the content of the information.
in writing. - i agree with the rapporteur on most of the points put forward and have therefore voted in favour of the proposal.
in writing. − media freedom and pluralism must be monitored in all member states and parliament must safeguard the independence of journalists from internal pressures from publishers or owners and from external pressures from political or economic lobbies. in this regard, member states are invited to guarantee, protect and promote the fundamental right to freedom of expression and information, as well as the freedom and pluralism of the media. it is also necessary that member states ensure the independence of journalists and publishers by means of appropriate legal and social safeguards, taking care to also provide for the interference of owners, shareholders and governments. finally, rules on media ownership transparency, concentration and conflicts of interest should be ensured.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by my colleague on the introduction of common eu-wide media freedom rules because i believe that guaranteeing the independence and pluralism of the media is a priority and is fundamental to the development of democracy. these elements have already proved their importance in the process of democratization in some countries and in the promotion of human rights. i believe that it is necessary for countries wishing to join the eu to comply with the union's acquis, recalling that media freedom and pluralism are one of the eligibility criteria. the member states will also have to set an example for countries outside the union. the european court of human rights, with reference to the convention for the protection of human rights, also recalled the obligation of the member states to guarantee freedom and pluralism of the media. these media must ensure free but objective information, and i believe it is necessary to preserve the provision of adequate funding to the media of the national public service, to ensure their educational, cultural and democratic role, as well as their independence from politics.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of the report on an agenda for adequate, secure and sustainable pensions because i believe that we need to close the gender gap and combat gender discrimination and thus promote a better work-life balance, especially for women. women often interrupt their careers to take on family tasks, and are more likely than men to take up part-time or even low-paid work, earning on average 16% less than men. women also receive a lower pension and are therefore more at risk of poverty and social exclusion than men. some pension systems also exacerbate gender imbalances, especially for women living alone, thus increasing their vulnerability.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, how can we think of adequate, secure and sustainable pensions for women when the pay gap between men and women is almost 17%? and then there are family responsibilities, the inadequacy of structures for reconciling work and family life, which forces women to continually interrupt their careers and often cannot work full time. at retirement, lower earnings add to the discontinuity of employment and career and of course there will be lower pensions. that is why in old age women are at a very high risk, much higher than men, of being in poverty. what about young people? in europe, one in four young people is unemployed, and in some member states this figure is over 50%.
in writing. − the objective of any pension system must be to ensure a sufficient standard of living for each pensioner. to achieve this, the single most important measure to work on is to significantly increase the number of taxpayers, i.e. the number of people in work, rather than discussing how to reshape pension systems in view of higher life expectancies or the different age structure of society. giving more jobs to young people is the first key to ensuring balanced pension systems and all the most important aspects of our society. particular attention should be paid to the position of women in the labour market and their retirement prospects. women suffer from greater discontinuity in employment and career, most often because of their role as mothers and wives within families. they often work part-time and are scandalously less paid than men, with a difference of almost 17%. this puts them at risk of poor pensions and thus of an old age of greater economic difficulties, if not even of poverty and social exclusion. a joint effort by the union to find broad and shared solutions would be desirable and positive.
in writing. − pension systems are under pressure in all eu countries: the euro area governments adopt austerity measures to comply with the stability and growth pact or are forced to take action to reduce high deficits. in europe, the working population is shrinking, birth rates are falling, young people are studying longer and entering the labour market later. by 2020, the proportion of the total population aged 65 and over will have risen from 16% in 2010 to 19.1%. the so-called 'intergenerational solidarity' by which young people in employment pay for pensions can no longer be guaranteed. in many member states, reforms aimed at pension sustainability have already been initiated, but more needs to be done to address the effects of population ageing. in particular, i believe that in the light of the high mobility of workers on the market, it is important to develop minimum rules on the acquisition and maintenance of the value of pension rights acquired when working experience is gained in different countries. in addition, member states should provide a clear pension framework to citizens so that they can have the information at their disposal on the basis of which to take the necessary action for the future.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution on adequate, sustainable and secure pensions, together with my colleagues from the ppe group, because i believe that it is precisely in this situation of stagnation of the euro area economies, such as italy's, that measures are necessary to ensure the efficiency of the pension system. it is obvious that systems are under severe pressure throughout europe, especially where, as in italy, economic contingency has forced governments to take drastic measures to reduce public deficits. at the same time, the average age of the population continues to rise, life expectancy and the number of pensioners are increasing, while the share of the working population is falling sharply. we are at a point where the solidarity between generations, on the basis of which young people in employment pay for pensions, is seriously threatened. this requires a european agenda on pensions, leading to a series of reforms: the responsibility and competence of individual member states must remain unchanged, but it is possible to agree on shared systems which are adequate and sustainable and which help to strengthen free movement in the labour market.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this important own-initiative report by parliament because the issue of pensions is as fundamental as that of better employment. the pension systems of all countries are under severe pressure, no doubt due to the austerity measures implemented at national level to comply with the stability pact. but not only that. society is changing and we have to deal with an ageing population and, at the same time, with increasing life expectancy. i agree with the need to introduce reforms through non-binding measures. we need to build systems that are adequate, safe and sustainable, but also help to strengthen mobility and free movement in the labour market, and provide solutions for the present and the future. whatever system is chosen, we must increase the number of people in work and have them set aside funds and save for old age. while respecting the division of competence between the union and the states, the union can do much in this field, including by using legislation if necessary.
in writing. the report follows closely the commission's white paper on pensions. the reforms of the pension system which we see in europe today - including italy - are the result of this approach. the first point to be discussed concerns the extension of the retirement age, which not only forces older people to work more, but also creates jobs for young people (150,000 fewer jobs for the young in our country). the second is the move from a public to a private pension system, which would entail an increase in administrative charges, a worsening of the protection of workers who have not served continuously, and this despite the ineffectiveness of these measures in reducing the public debt. for these reasons i am voting against the report.
in writing. - i thank the rapporteur for the excellent work she has done on this report. the statistics we have show that the european population is characterized by a high rate of over 55 (about 1/3 of the population). it follows, therefore, that without adequate coordination at european level, the sustainability of public pension schemes could be seriously called into question. as is well known, the provision of pensions is a matter for the member states, but in a time of crisis such as the present one, i believe that priority should be given to the long-term stability and sustainability of national pension systems. i believe that action is needed to ensure adequate support for europe's pensioners, while not forgetting that a major contribution can be made by the creation of new jobs. the current pension system must therefore be adapted to the expectations of a sustainable welfare system and a labour market that has seen its rules and dimensions change.
in writing. - we voted in favour of the report on a european agenda for adequate, secure and sustainable pensions for both young and old. we believe that it is an excellent instrument for initiating discussion and launching reforms by means of non-binding measures or even legislative instruments, where necessary. in practical terms, while recognising the absolute control of the member states and the social partners in this context, it is necessary to build adequate and sustainable systems that help to strengthen mobility and free movement in the labour market, with the ultimate aim of providing solutions for the future. furthermore, as the europe 2020 strategy explicitly refers to the need to ensure adequate pensions, we encourage all eu member states to define a clear pension framework, which can provide citizens with comprehensive information about the level of pension that each worker can expect. many member states have already implemented reforms aimed at pension sustainability, but new solutions are needed to address the problem of an ageing population. whatever system is chosen, we believe it is essential to increase the number of people in work and to educate them to save and save for their retirement.
in writing. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i am voting in favour of the european parliament's motion for a resolution on an agenda for adequate, sustainable and secure pensions. all member states are experiencing an ageing population, life expectancy is increasing across europe and the number of pensioners living longer and in better health is increasing. as a result of the severe crisis, pension systems are under severe pressure in all eu countries. in addition, young people are entering the labour market later and later, and the solidarity between generations, which is the basis for young people in work to pay for pensions, is being eroded. the european agenda on adequate, secure and sustainable pensions is a necessary tool to initiate a discussion and subsequently launch reforms aimed at the establishment of secure pension systems that also contribute to strengthening mobility and free movement in the labour market.

in writing. - i am strongly opposed to this agenda which identifies pensioners as the ones responsible for the economic crisis because they 'cost too much'. the eu has proved incapable of protecting its citizens from unemployment and economic decline by failing to promote a credible and concrete growth plan. the idea of shifting the costs of the crisis onto the shoulders of citizens and pensioners by attacking the rights they have acquired is unacceptable. in addition, amendments have been accepted, to which i have always voted against, which propose to cut pensions further by linking them to the ratio of unemployed to employed, thus impoverishing pensioners living in countries where unemployment is higher and attacking the right to live the last phase of life with serenity and dignity. the eu should have intervened on the ecb by changing its operating rules, which do not allow direct financing of states, companies and households, but only banks, at a ridiculous interest rate of 0.50%. i wonder why the banks should make exorbitant sums of money on the money the ecb lends them. why not favour businesses and households instead? why not, as the united states and japan have done, put new money into circulation?
in writing. − life expectancy is increasing in europe and the increase in life expectancy inevitably leads to an increase in the number of pensioners. the european states are having difficulty in guaranteeing pensions above the poverty line and more efforts are needed to find adequate solutions, given that solidarity between the generations, whereby young people in work pay for current pensions, is not being achieved today. i voted in favour of the report because europe, while recognising the responsibilities of the member states in this area, will have to try to build systems that provide guarantees, reinforcing the sustainability of pension costs through reforms that set common guidelines, favouring solutions for both the present and the future. in order to ensure pension fund cover, europe will need to increase its provisioning and can do so by committing to policies that facilitate the entry of young people into the world of work and by raising the retirement age so that in the future many pensioners, especially women, do not live below the poverty line. all member states will also have to make their pension systems clear, including in terms of information.
