mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i greet commissioner barnier and take this opportunity to inform him that an italian bathing-house owner has climbed up to the dome of st peter's in rome, where he has been since last night, to defend his job and his business, which is seriously threatened by the current bolkestein directive. the european banks have now reached a size that is difficult to control, and the crisis of one of them can bring the whole financial market and the economy of a country to the brink of collapse; the commission has already made a number of proposals in this area. i remain, however, sceptical of all the supervisory mechanisms which have failed in recent years, both at national and european level. in recent months in italy we have had the famous case of the monte dei paschi bank. i do not know whether a european supervisory mechanism would have been more effective, but it was certainly impossible to do worse. at that time, mario draghi was at the bank of italy and he did nothing, he was unable to do anything. i hope that this will not happen again with the new role of the ecb, because then the consequences will be felt throughout europe. i wonder what the usefulness and effectiveness of the new european banking authority will be, since it has so far been of little use. it was just another useless european agency, and perhaps it makes sense to bring it under the ecb. i believe that a large part of the banking problems stem from a mistake which i have already pointed out many times in this house, namely the unfortunate abolition of the banking segregation as provided for by the american glass-steagall act. just last week, a bill was introduced in the united states senate to reinstate glass-steagall, as has already happened in the house of representatives. europe should follow this path because today we are talking about banking unity and banking union, but perhaps a banking separation would bring much more benefits.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i have on several occasions argued that the eurozone should have a coherent and clear economic policy and should make progress in integrating spending and budgetary policies. the solution cannot be to build a kind of 'united states of the euro', but to create a mechanism to stop uncertainty and instability, a mechanism which will pool resources through the adoption of common bonds or through collective supervision measures which are much stricter than those currently in force on financial and budgetary policies. we must guarantee the spending commitments of individual states, protect european savers in particular from the failure of banks and create a system which enables consumers to take the necessary steps to protect themselves. we are in favour of the ecb being given responsibility for banking supervision in the euro area. it is intended to provide advice to national supervisory authorities and to those of those member states which, although not sharing the euro, are essential and important parts of the single market. we must encourage the integration of banks under single supervision without burdening the budgets of states in difficulty, and we must ensure that citizens, the savers who have supported the credit systems with their savings, have guarantees, and we must prevent excessive mergers of banking institutions and improve the definition between savings and investment banks.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, with great intellectual honesty i would like to thank mr thyssen and mr giegold for the excellent work they have done. they have done important work for the whole of europe. many colleagues spoke only of the critical points. there is no perfect law and i must say that this directive is a very important strategy for europe. the banking union - we have said this many times - is the single supervisory mechanism and is an important part of the construction of a genuine economic and monetary union, which will then have to be accompanied by a budgetary union and an economic union. for those who believe in europe, this is a very important road. the banking union with a single ecb supervisor will play a preventive role in preventing bank failures and preventing the instability of a single credit institution from spreading to the entire banking system, thus averting the damaging effects on the real economy that we have already had since 2008. the lack of transparency in the banking sector and especially the lack of supervision by some countries have made the banking sector easily vulnerable to contagion, which then spread even to the most stable countries. the crisis we are trying to get out of is a striking example of the fact that a failure in the banking sector has serious repercussions on the real economy of a country, which also have a negative effect on our internal market. the banking union is a cornerstone of the european union, there is no more time to delay some of the reforms needed to build a real economic and monetary union, now is the time to revive the european economy with new and better jobs, with an integrated internal market and greater competitiveness and the banking union is the right step in that direction. we must not forget that the european union is a major player in the world economy.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the establishment of a single supervisory mechanism is an important step towards building the banking union. the banking union is important because reducing the risk of the credit system is a fundamental condition for overcoming the private and sovereign debt imbalance which has made the current crisis so dramatic and has had such a heavy impact on citizens and businesses, who were first called upon to bear the cost of bank bailouts and still bear an unsustainable cost of money in many countries. however, for the banking union, single supervision is a necessary but not sufficient condition without a single resolution mechanism with adequate resources and without an effective deposit guarantee mechanism. in this respect, i think that the recent statements by minister scheuble on the need for a revision of the treaties in order to proceed with the single resolution mechanism are a pretext and recall similar objections to single supervision which have subsequently proved to be unfounded or at least surmountable. the agreement reached on single supervision is a good compromise, the differentiation introduced between credit institutions makes it possible to safeguard the specificity of banking systems and the principle of subsidiarity without affecting the exclusive competence and the role of the ecb and the ssm as the decision-maker of last resort. this differentiation can also provide the basis for the implementation of a separation of commercial and investment banking activities which we consider to be of great importance and which is another fundamental element of a true banking union and better regulation of financial markets. the role of the european parliament in appointing the monitoring committee of the ssm summit is also very positive, as well as being an important precedent. this role must now be consistently translated into an interinstitutional agreement between parliament and the ecb, which must ensure transparency and control commensurate with the importance of the new tasks assigned to the ecb and for which parliament will not make concessions.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, it is right that the harmonization of the various national deposit guarantee schemes and the preparation of a single set of rules on financial services will gradually reduce the unfair disparities which exist on the financial market today and which unfairly penalise the productive sectors of certain countries. i therefore share the call not only for a single corpus but also for its uniform application. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the banking sector is not left behind. the strong call for the safeguarding of these categories in article 8 must remain a constant in any reform we wish to implement. the citizens cannot be victims of the errors and frivolity of a system in which they are spectators, and this will have to be taken into account in every step we take. commissioner barnier, i have great confidence in you and great respect for you. when we talk about time, this is our weakness. does the realistic timetable that our excellent rapporteur has mentioned not seem to you to be full of obstacles and to be on a terrible slope? almost afraid to get there? and we've heard some colleagues express this fear. how long does the procedure required of that member state take? commissioner, what if they do not approve this procedure? what's going on? what's going on? this is the first of the three pillars that have been put in place in the banking union, the other two are missing, and this alone will perhaps create some problems. this banking union is one of the four pillars of the road map. let me end, mr president, with a quote from a great man of our land who was beatified a short time ago, who says that "in credit and finance we must have three fundamental aspects: morality, which is based on trust, distributive justice and general utility, because credit must be aimed at the public welfare, performing a social function".

president-in-office of the council. − mr president, my statement on this issue this evening will by necessity be brief. as you know, discussions within the world intellectual property organization (wipo) on how to provide better access to information, culture and communication for the visually impaired and persons with print disabilities have been underway since 2009. the focus of these discussions has been to expand the number of copyrighted works in accessible formats and improve access to them. in june last year the commission submitted to the council a recommendation requesting authorisation to open and conduct negotiations on behalf of the european union on an international agreement in the context of wipo. on 26 november 2012, the council issued negotiating directives to the commission and authorised it to participate in the negotiations on behalf of the union. the wipo general assembly decided on 18 december 2012 to convene a diplomatic conference in marrakesh on 17-28 june 2013. a draft text of an international instrument was recently circulated by the wipo secretariat as a basis for discussions at that conference. the commission will represent the eu at the marrakesh conference and will negotiate on its behalf in line with the negotiating directives which it has received from the council. it would clearly not be appropriate for me here to enter into a public discussion on the content of the mandate which has been given to the commission and which is internal to the eu. i am sure the commission, as negotiator, will keep parliament fully and immediately informed as the negotiations progress. i thank you for your attention, and i look forward to hearing the views of members this evening.
member of the commission. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, madam minister, dear lucinda, since i took up my duties as european commissioner three years ago, i have worked hard with you to draw up an international treaty to give visually impaired people the same opportunities as others to access books, wherever they live, in order to put an end once and for all to what is truly an unacceptable shortage, which hinders the access of a considerable number of citizens to knowledge and culture. in february 2012, right here, you will remember, when your resolution on this subject was voted by an extremely large majority, i personally committed myself to a binding treaty. since then i have had the opportunity to discuss this with mr lehne of the committee on legal affairs and with many of you, including mr berlinguer and mrs lichtenberger and others. today the commission is negotiating this treaty on behalf of the european union, as the presidency has just reminded us. our request for a council mandate in june 2012 resulted in an authorisation to negotiate in november 2012. we are keeping our promise and the commission is therefore, you can be sure, fully committed to this matter. i have repeatedly expressed my determination to see that we arrive at a strong and clear text which effectively guarantees strict equality of access to books, wherever people with a reading disability live, in particular. today, the european union, through the commission, is actively negotiating with its partners in the world intellectual property organization (wipo) to find the most effective solutions, which are of course mutually acceptable. the work has progressed rapidly; the extraordinary general assembly of december 2012 has called for a diplomatic conference in june, in a few weeks, to conclude these negotiations, we hope and we wish. a few weeks before the marrakesh conference opens, and despite a final negotiating session in april, there are still - i must say this in the clearest and most transparent way - a number of important questions that are still open. the commission's position is unambiguous. it is clear support for a targeted and effective treaty - and we are negotiating with this objective in mind in order to remove the barriers to access for the visually impaired to special and adapted book formats - a treaty that facilitates the cross-border distribution, export and import of these formats. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i think we are close to finding an answer to these questions which are still outstanding. for example, the question of verifying the unavailability of the formats in question in a country or, again, the distribution methods. all negotiators must be mobilized. we must overcome these various difficulties if the marrakesh conference is to be a success, and we will do everything, because that is our objective, to make it a success. but as i have stressed on several occasions, in these negotiations the commission represents the position of the european union and its member states on the basis of the mandate given to it. the solutions we have to find cannot ignore the scope of this mandate and must be acceptable, i repeat, to the member states. of course, the european union is negotiating with the other wipo member countries. it is not in a position to determine on its own what the outcome of these negotiations will be, although it is resolutely committed - i repeat - to seeking an agreement to fully meet the legitimate needs of the visually impaired. we want an effective treaty which takes account of all the legitimate concerns, including those which you have expressed very strongly here in the european parliament. there is no question of imposing some bureaucratic requirement. i have had the opportunity to say this, to give this assurance to the member associations of the ebu (european blind union), which i thank - i am speaking of the associations - for their support and, at the same time, for their very active vigilance on this matter. ladies and gentlemen, the effectiveness of this treaty, its ability to respond effectively to the needs of the visually impaired, will of course also depend, i repeat, on the possibility of its being signed and ratified in a short time. that is why i call on everyone to take responsibility and why i thank you for this new debate, which is a reminder of the determination that is very important for the member states of the union, as well as your support, your vigilance and your own determination, which is in line with that of the european commission.

member of the commission. − mr president, i should like to thank the honourable members who have participated in this debate. it was an interesting debate and, since for ten years i was minister of the interior, i felt at home and comfortable in the debate because i understood the concerns of the members. of course, governments have to govern. they have the responsibility to govern; they also reflect public opinion. but directives have to be scrutinised and the commission does scrutinise what the member states do: how they implement the acquis and how they implement the schengen acquis. so let me return to what i said in my introductory address: schengen is an achievement, but this does not mean there are no problems. i refer to mr guerrero salom, who said that there are difficulties in going from eastern europe to the uk. of course, the uk is not in schengen; it is entitled not to become part of schengen because it is within its rights under the treaties and its discretion not to do so, so therefore there are border controls at the border with the untied kingdom. but i have heard of some complaints by citizens of the country i know best, from people not being allowed in unless they produce a passport, which is against the acquis even for the non-schengen countries. one has to be very careful that the schengen acquis is not abused – in other words that, stealthily behind the scenes, we are not dismantling what we have achieved by raising borders and by carrying out systematic checks and not the random checks required by the schengen acquis. however, the commission monitors this situation regularly and also issues reports on the implementation of the schengen acquis. i note that several members referred to the european arrest warrant – in different ways, of course: some said that it is being applied unjustly against citizens, others that it is not being applied enough. of course the very idea of the european address warrant is based on the presumption – the premise – that our rules relating to freedom and the rule of law are so similar – not identical but so similar – that we should introduce a simplified express way of extradition. this is the value added of the european arrest warrant. we have already had the council of europe’s european convention on extradition. this is now an improvement within the european union, on the basis that, if we trust our each other and each other’s systems to this extent, then, on the mere issuing of a european arrest warrant, we should deliver a person to the other country within the european union. i remember that, on the very day when the united kingdom had a big controversy on this european arrest warrant, the british police succeeded in getting back to the united kingdom a school teacher who had eloped with one of his students to france and was extradited expressly by means of the european arrest warrant. so all countries apply the european arrest warrant. like so many other things it can be abused both ways: either someone who is a fugitive of justice is not sent back – because he is a national of the member state, which is not one of the reasons why you should refuse this simplified form of extradition, or on the basis of some other procedural rule – or someone uses the european arrest warrant in a flippant way. of course these are the two extremes, but in most cases it is applied justly – it has made a difference and helped in the creation of this common area of freedom and justice. i admire ms mazzoni from italy on her commitment to make the european union accountable to citizens by taking care of citizens’ needs, and as chair of the committee on petitions she is of course in an excellent position to know what the main concerns of the european citizen are. but i think we have to judge the stockholm programme and our achievements in the area of freedom, security and justice with the european union by looking not at what we should be in a utopian sense but at where we started from. only four years ago i was a member of the council of justice and home affairs ministers where practically everything had to pass by unanimous vote. so each member state, whether it was germany or malta, had a veto on justice and home affairs issues. today, after the lisbon treaty, not only has this changed but there are two co-legislators of equal rank. i emphasise this point – of equal rank – so i admire the balanced approach of mr moraes saying that the commission is on the energetic side of things in the introduction of legislation. it is natural. i spent 16 years as a government minister, and it is natural for governments to be slightly more conservative than parliamentarians because they have direct responsibility to govern, which is not an easy thing to do in the current times – nor is it an easy thing to be a parliamentarian, because there are responsibilities inherent in occupying the office of a parliamentarian. but we face this in most directives. this is the compromise which stems from having what president barroso likes to call ‘a federation but a federation of sovereign states’. it is a contradiction in terms up to a certain point – how can it be a federation and at the same time have sovereign states? – but this is the reality: that we have not become a federation but at the same time we are much more than just an organisation of sovereign states moving towards a more perfect union. so in answer to ms mazzoni – whose energy i admire for pushing the agenda and asking the question: ‘do we really have a common area?’ – i would say that perhaps we have not reached the level we would like to attain, but i think great strides forward have been made and in a very concrete way. not in an academic way, but in a very concrete way – which does not mean of course that every now and again there are not troubles which arise or obstacles of a nationalist nature which arise as well and which we as the commission should tackle and, where necessary, also take immediate action. i appreciated the comments of those who question how much solidarity there is on the immigration issue. of course the countries at the periphery, particularly in the south, complain that not enough is being done with regard to the intra-european transfer of protected persons who enter the periphery, and that these countries on the periphery have an excessive burden with regard to the refugee and the asylum problem. solidarity is not something which can be imposed. as soon as it is imposed, it is not really solidarity, merely the application of a legal obligation. even though some would prefer to have an imposed system of burden-sharing, it is perhaps a contradiction in terms up to a certain point. even if there is a forced way of burden-sharing, it has to be agreed to by the member states themselves. i appreciate my colleague commissioner malmström’s difficulty in pushing forward solidarity while at the same time i know very well that she does not have the full support of the member states in this regard, as they do not consider – not all of them, at least – that this is necessarily a pan-european problem. there are several other points i would like to reply to, but in particular i would refer to mr zwiefka’s comments. i agree entirely with him that judicial training is crucial in order to ensure that the law is known and that it is implemented. the commission will continue to support actions to strengthen judicial training because we feel that, through this method of training, one can ensure that the laws agreed to in brussels and strasbourg do not become a dead letter. i have already replied to the questions raised concerning schengen. regarding mr ehrenhauser’s question, i would like to tell him that the commission proposed a new legal basis for europol, basically with two objectives: firstly to improve the functioning of europol – notably by equipping it to be more efficient in exchanging information between police authorities – and secondly in increasing the parliamentary oversight, in line with the lisbon treaty, of the actions of europol. we all know that through the intervention of parliament in several pieces of legislation, including in the area of freedom and justice, the original bill – the draft proposal – has been changed and compromises have been reached. so parliament should not ignore the council, nor should the council ignore parliament. the idea of the lisbon treaty is that, through these two co-legislators, one would find through synthesis what the proper legislation should be within the european union.

member of the commission. − mr president, the commission is very satisfied that its succession regulation was adopted last year and is now part of the european union rule book. separate national rules on succession created a legal maze of red tape and costs through which citizens making use of the right to move had to navigate – and pay. having a framework for european cooperation on succession is a great achievement and a tangible concrete benefit to the life of citizens, as the regulation simplifies processes and brings legal security to citizens. this law is just one of the many examples of how the european union is working to resolve everyday legal problems and save money for europeans. obviously the regulation, like any new legislation that builds bridges between very different national legal systems, can raise questions of interpretation and implementation in the early days of its application. it is to minimise any such possible questions that the commission has for some years been sponsoring projects that would help citizens to find their way in this matter. this is the case with (and i shall give examples) the interconnection of registers of wills in the member states so as to facilitate the finding of wills across europe. one of the very first questions upon the death of a person is whether that person planned his or her succession or not. finding the will is a crucial element in the start of any succession proceeding. the organisation of a transparent exchange of information is another project on national succession laws which is easy to understand for citizens. such information is put online on a website called successions in europe. in addition, since the adoption of the regulation, the commission has put a lot of effort into ensuring the smooth application of the regulation. for instance, last year we awarded eur 1 million for an action grant to the council of the notariats of the european union, and thanks to this two-year project, 14 training courses are taking place to provide solid training to over 2 000 european notaries. we are also working on a standard form for the european certificate of succession, and the goal is to adopt the implementing regulation by the end of 2013. the european judicial network in civil and commercial matters, the so-called ejn, has started to prepare the publication of information on national legislations and procedures on the e-justice portal, and this will benefit citizens and their legal representatives. we are also launching a study to examine the need for a legal instrument on electronic registers of wills and of european certificates of succession at national level and ensuring the interoperability of such registers between member states. the succession regulation does not concern taxation. the way in which inheritance tax or its equivalent is assessed and calculated across the european union is very different. in certain situations the heirs only receive a very small part of their inheritance after it has been doubly or triply taxed by several member states. in extreme cases the total value of a cross-border inherited asset might even have to be paid in tax. this is because several member states may claim taxing rights on the same inheritance or tax foreign inheritance more heavily... (the president interrupted the speaker).
member of the commission. − mr president, in extreme cases the total value of a cross-border inherited asset might even have to be paid in tax. this is because several member states may claim taxing rights on the same inheritance or may tax foreign inheritances more heavily than local inheritances. as a result, citizens may be forced to sell inherited assets just to cover the taxes, and small businesses may face transfer difficulties on the death of their owners. inheritance tax can therefore give rise to obstacles that deter europeans from exercising their rights across borders within the european union. discriminatory taxation can also become an artificial disincentive to further investment across the single market in otherwise viable businesses. because of the fear of leaving huge inheritance tax and legal bills for their family members, business owners may consider investment-reducing alternatives such as liquidation, down-sizing or retirement from their cross-border investments. this is because they may not see the value in maintaining such highly taxable investments. it was to tackle these problems that, on 15 december 2011, the commission adopted a recommendation on how member states could eliminate double taxation of inheritances. on the same occasion the commission provided guidance to the member states on how to ensure that cross-border inheritance tax rules do not involve discrimination. the objective is very simple: to take action to tackle cross-border inheritance tax obstacles across the european union and resolve cases of double taxation. the aim is to ensure that the overall level of tax on a given inheritance is not higher than the level that would apply if only one member state had tax jurisdiction over the inheritance. the recommendation calls on member states to grant tax relief when applying inheritance taxes and to improve the cooperation of tax authorities to assist taxpayers subject to double taxation. the commission will report on the state of play of member states’ provisions for relief for double taxation of inheritances next year. if the report demonstrates that cross-border inheritance tax problems persist, the commission will consider all the different options, including the need to take appropriate legislative action to eliminate those obstacles. finally, in the meantime, the commission would like to use today’s debate to call on the member states to step up their cooperation and put the commission recommendation in place.
i think that the succession regulation is one of the most beautiful things this parliament has done. the subject may seem remote and hostile, but it is one which has touched the lives of citizens as european citizens. there are 450,000 cases a year where families are faced with an international succession and 120 billion euros that move. the numbers are important and the citizens who have relations with several member states are also an important issue. we've established the law applicable to this case. why is the discussion which we have called for and to which the commissioner has begun to respond important? because if you don't address the double taxation problem, the tax problem, that can seriously undermine the effectiveness of that law. we are therefore also moving in the direction of what we have just discussed in connection with stockholm, namely that the process of creating a european area must go step by step by checking what the bottlenecks and bottlenecks are and what the next action must be, because what is produced as a norm becomes everyday life. i would therefore like to recommend even more strongly that double taxation be overcome, that the 2011 recommendation be implemented effectively and substantially and that this law then become a reality, to affect the practical lives of citizens. let me make a final remark with tadeusz zwiefka, cecilia wikström, evelyn regner, who are my colleagues on the juri committee. as you can see, mr president, we do not like publicity and newspapers talking about our work, because the lawyer is a bit of a shadow and is a strange operative or european parliamentarian. yet we have put a great passion into this and today this passion has also been very rewarding.

in writing. - following the instructions of my group, i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation on the mutual recognition of protection measures in civil matters. the regulation is part of a legislative package to strengthen the rights of victims of crime in the eu. it is essential to ensure that a person who enjoys protection in one member state does not lose it when he travels to another member state. i therefore believe that it is essential to set up a mechanism to eliminate intermediate formalities through the use of a standardised, multilingual certificate. this would ensure not only quick and simple recognition but also the application of protection measures. the mechanism will also make the administrative procedure more linear for victims and ensure their protection when they travel or move to another member state. member states are also encouraged to ensure that the protected person does not bear the financial burden of the recognition of the protection measure in another member state.
in writing. − the latest available eurostat data gives the number of europeans who have moved to a country in the union other than their country of origin at 12 million, excluding the migration from the so-called 'a-8' countries, whose story will be defined as it is known in 2014. it is clear that an increase in the propensity to move requires adjustments to the system for the effective exercise of the rights of european citizenship. in the field under discussion today, new trends and new recurrent criminal cases are emerging: i am thinking of gender-based violence, sometimes originating from conflict with traditional cultures, or the situation of so-called whistleblowers in environments particularly affected by corruption and crime. in this context, the option of relocation, especially on the lines of friendship, family or professional solidarity, sometimes provides an opportunity to guarantee full rights to victims of crime and the opportunity for a new life protected from threats to personal integrity. the proposal for a regulation integrates in a single dimension a number of legal, procedural, documentary and practical aspects, in the overall interest of victims of crime and also of the right of defence. in particular, it provides for the convergence of civil and administrative aspects into a single instrument. i therefore vote in favour.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this regulation which implements the mutual recognition of protection measures in civil matters. it is essential to provide citizens who are victims of crime with a common european framework offering all possible guarantees to obtain redress for the damage suffered. this instrument is in fact in addition to the already provided for recognition of measures in criminal matters and undoubtedly strengthens the rights of europeans. it is right to ensure that a person who enjoys protection in one member state does not lose it when he travels to another member state. another important aspect which i agree with is the desire to deal further with the issue of victims of gender-based violence, who are too often women. in fact, it refers expressly to the rules laid down in the proposal for a directive which, together with this regulation, make up the legislative package for the protection of the rights of victims. i agree with encouraging the staff who deal with these cases, as well as with recognising and supporting the work of the many ngos, associations and voluntary organisations working in this sensitive and important area for our civil society.
in writing. - this proposal aims at creating an area of cooperation with regard to the civil sector only. the regulation is aimed at protecting against crossborder violence, without requiring member states to amend their national legislation. i think that the report as a whole deserves a favourable vote.
in writing. − the data from recent years on stalking and domestic violence, with one in four women admitting to having been the victim of such acts at least once in their lives, continue to leave a certain bitterness. however, there has also been a growing awareness among the european population of the fact that such acts are a common problem in europe, and today's vote is moving in that direction. mutual recognition of protection measures in civil matters allows for a higher level of protection for victims of these offences, providing a more coherent regulatory framework at european level. the simplification of intermediate formalities, through the use of a single model certificate and the right to assistance in an understandable language, must however be accompanied by adequate training of the personnel providing such assistance, who must have appropriate skills to deal with situations of violence. it is also desirable to organise adequate information campaigns throughout europe on the possibilities offered by the union for the free movement of protective measures.
in writing. - today we adopted the important report on the proposal for a regulation on the mutual recognition of protection measures in civil matters, aimed at strengthening the rights of victims within the european union. the regulation also includes a proposal for a directive on the rights, assistance and protection of victims of crime. there has long been a need for a general european policy framework to legitimize the position of victims of crime in terms of protection in all eu member states. the combined application of criminal and civil instruments will enable persons in a protected status to enjoy the same safety conditions and thus to move freely within all the member states of the union. we also believe that it is essential to establish a mechanism to eliminate intermediate formalities through the use of standardised and multilingual certificates. we are also convinced of the need to provide assistance in a comprehensible form and in an accessible language; in this connection, we invite the competent authorities to arrange for translations and interpretations of the regulations in the mother tongue of the person concerned. finally, we would point out that it is essential, for the purpose of comprehensive education, that each member state includes in its awareness campaigns the new directive on the mutual recognition of protection measures available within the european union.
in writing. - the measures we voted for today and which i supported should allow for full recognition and greater guarantee and protection for victims of crime, extending coverage beyond national borders, in all countries of the union. with the abolition of internal frontiers and the increasingly massive mobility of european citizens, it is essential to think of more extensive measures, which offer greater protection, without, of course, prejudicing the sovereignty of the member states in judicial and criminal matters. mutual recognition arrangements can be particularly useful, especially with regard to the status of women, which is still too often trampled on: the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the draft directive on the protection of the rights of victims of violence, harassment, intimidation and stalking. this is an important step forward, which makes us appreciate, for once, the fact that we are in a european union which is too often far removed from the needs of its citizens: i am not saying that we should not be concerned about the future of the community, but that we should not be concerned about the future of the community.
in writing. − victims of stalking, harassment or gender-based violence must be protected. that is why i support the legislation providing for guarantees and protection for victims in the community. i believe that victims of gender-based violence should be provided with support services throughout the community and that officials should be trained to provide such support. this would significantly strengthen the union's area of freedom, security and justice. i therefore share the outcome of the vote on the new civil law which complements the european protection order by ensuring that protection granted in one member state is maintained when the victim travels or moves to another member state.
in writing. the text adopted today is a key instrument for ensuring full legal protection for over 500 million european citizens. a package of legislation that finally gives every person full respect and recognition of his or her rights. this is a necessary means of establishing the principle of mutual recognition of judicial and extrajudicial decisions in civil matters in all the member states. in this area, stalking and violence against women are particularly relevant, since they require specific judicial safeguards. the tragedy of the now daily emergence of violence against women is unfortunately not exhausted by the outcry that is aroused by the media. it is a persistent and pervasive reality which even in advanced societies such as ours has the dimensions of a genuine social danger. only by providing victims with adequate protection and by fostering a cultural change in the hearts and minds of people will we be able to eradicate this evil.
in writing. the proposal for a regulation on the mutual recognition of protection measures in civil matters brings a clear improvement in legal terms and will, in fact, allow formal recognition for all victims of crime and greater protection within the european union. the numerous interinstitutional meetings and trilogues held in recent months have made it possible to reach agreements on such sensitive issues as simplification of procedures, the right to information and translation for the parties involved and the legal alignment of the text with the european protection order.
in writing. - following the instructions of my group, i voted in favour of the draft council decision on customs cooperation between the eu and canada on supply chain security. the previous agreement, dating back to 2011, needed to be extended and improved, reinforcing its customs aspects to make the logistics chain of international trade more secure, including container security, while facilitating legitimate trade. i think this is an important step towards paving the way for mutual recognition agreements on customs security.
in writing. − our trade relations with canada are healthy, flourishing and inspired by the creation of important synergies, even before the current agreements were drawn up in 1988. it is therefore worth taking a step forward, especially in the light of the security threats that are increasingly imposing costs on businesses worldwide. that is why, after two long years of negotiations, the commission has proposed this agreement to us, and i have not hesitated to promote it in view of a future, broad and comprehensive canada-eu trade agreement.
in writing. − the agreement covers customs relations between the eu and canada. negotiations for close cooperation have been ongoing since 2005. their purpose is to simplify procedures for legitimate trade and to increase the security of containers, so as to facilitate trade. the eu has already negotiated and concluded similar agreements with the usa and japan. now this project is also making it possible to reach an agreement with the north american country. i think it is valid, so i vote in favour.

in writing. − the eu-canada customs relations are based on the 1998 agreement on cooperation and mutual assistance in customs matters (cmaa). since 2005, canada has expressed its interest in closer cooperation with the eu on security along the supply chain and risk management. this paved the way for the mutual recognition of their trade partnership programmes with equivalent trade facilitation measures. for these reasons i am satisfied with the outcome of the vote on the extension of the scope of the existing legislation, in favour of an agreement providing for greater customs security, trade partnership programmes with equivalent trade facilitation measures and greater security of the supply chain. in this context, it is considered that a new agreement is needed, based on the customs cooperation developed between the two partners and capable of being supplemented by the comprehensive economic and trade agreement (ceta) currently under negotiation.
in writing. the cooperation agreement between the european union and canada, through certain partial mutual recognitions, will make it possible to streamline and simplify customs operations, with a consequent benefit for trade. for these reasons i voted in favour of mr šťastný's text.

in writing. − the ecb should cooperate with the eba in the eu system of financial supervision, and the commission has therefore presented a proposal for a regulation to align the current eba set-up with the new banking supervision. it is expected that eba will be able to request all necessary authorisations from financial institutions to carry out the various operations, and in the investigative field it may require the submission of various documents. the ecb will continue to exercise direct control over banks with assets of more than 30 billion, while the others will continue to be subject to the control of national authorities. the commission notes that the bank has not provided any information on the amount of the loan. i am voting in favour of this report.
in writing. - i am against this report because it does not have the courage to face reality. the banking system in many european countries is not working: in italy, for example, credit to businesses and households has collapsed, and money is being invested in government bonds instead of in the production system. in many cases the rates charged are over 8%, and many banks refuse to accept real estate as collateral. this means that a young couple who want to buy their house and need a loan from a bank cannot do so because they are refused as collateral for the property. the fact that i think is more serious is that the ecb not only does not intervene - for example by increasing the money in circulation by printing money as the usa and japan have done, which thanks to this choice are coming out of the crisis - but even lends money to banks at the rate of 0.50% without binding them. it is time to revise the rules governing the ecb and make it the bank of european businesses and households instead of being, in fact, a private institution that finances credit institutions.

in writing. − the current directive 2007/23/ec lays down the essential safety requirements to be met by pyrotechnic articles when they are made available on the union market. the inconsistent implementation of this legislation and its complexity have made it increasingly difficult for economic operators to implement its provisions correctly, leading to disparate market conditions and the marketing of non-compliant products. in order to close these gaps, a new regulatory framework has been adopted which, in my view, by introducing a simplified regulatory framework for products and allowing for a more consistent implementation of technical standards, will provide member states' authorities with more effective tools to carry out market surveillance checks, ensuring fair competition and a supply of safe products for citizens. i welcome the proposal to modernise the procedures to enable the eu declaration of conformity to be provided not only in paper format but also in electronic form in order to reduce red tape. in order to ensure a higher level of product market surveillance, i agree with the rapporteur in proposing to improve market surveillance in distance selling by ensuring that, also in electronic commerce, the relevant information requirements are displayed.
in writing. - i agree with the proposal for a european parliament directive to harmonise the laws of the individual member states on the marketing of pyrotechnic articles. i therefore voted in favour, as i had agreed with my colleagues in the epp. in a sensitive area such as fireworks, a common and shared regulatory framework is needed to close the gaps that have existed so far and thus ensure fair competition and the supply of safe products. it is true that the provisions of the new regulatory framework are not directly applicable: the commission will therefore be required to integrate the existing legislation so that all economic sectors to which the legislation applies benefit from the improvements introduced.

in writing. − the audiovisual media services directive 2010/13/eu is the basis for media regulation in the european union. according to the data published by the european audiovisual observatory, its application has a positive impact on the development of the market: at the end of 2012, there were more than 8000 television service providers and more than 2000 on-demand service providers registered in the union. with reference to this specific sector, i take this opportunity to stress the importance of the issue of the protection of minors, since they are the most exposed to the dangers arising from certain types of commercial communications. i therefore agree with the rapporteur that it is appropriate to promote the development of codes of conduct in the member states with the aim of tackling the problem of inappropriate audiovisual commercial communications in children's programmes. the audiovisual services market is subject to strong international competition. over 1500 suppliers are based outside the european union but target their offerings to european markets; these broadcasters are not always bound by the legal obligations of european broadcasters. i therefore call on the commission to continue to monitor compliance with the existing rules to protect european companies in the sector which could be harmed by unfair competition resulting from this disparity in legal obligations.

madam president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, may i say that there is a certain amount of political hypocrisy today in discussing the syrian refugees, in being rightly alarmed by the situation developing in neighbouring countries and in asking for more credible humanitarian intervention, when we continue to escape the fact that this situation is a direct consequence of the failure to resolve the syrian conflict and our inability to produce political initiative. eighteen months ago, on december 11, 2011, ehud barak predicted that bashar al-assad's days were numbered. since then the israeli defense minister has retired from politics while the syrian president is still in power. assad is strong with the political and military support of russia and iran, the entry of hezbollah is probably turning the battle around and we are watching. i do not know what the outcome of the geneva summit that is being prepared will be, but i do know that if nothing is done, not only will the death toll of 90,000 increase, but the refugee problem itself will continue to increase, creating a much more complicated and difficult picture for the whole region to manage. so, it would really help if we got here fast.
madam president, commissioner füle, the number of refugees from syria has passed the one million mark. throughout the conflict all sorts of abuses have been documented: war crimes, human rights and humanitarian abuses on a large scale have been perpetrated by both the assad regime and the various rebel groups. with no political solution in sight, militarisation of the conflict has escalated. russia and iran have continued to arm the assad side. syrian rebels have a supply of weapons from saudi arabia and qatar with the help of the usa, despite protestations that such transfers are illegal under international law. in spite of a desperate humanitarian crisis, the international community and even some eu member states appear more concerned with ‘who to harm’ than ‘how to aid’. if we want to be effective in reducing war crimes and abuses in syria we should enforce more strictly – and not lift – the arms embargo and advocate more, and not less, of a political and diplomatic solution.

about? i am talking about looking differently at humanitarian assistance. i am talking about looking differently at how our assistance is being provided. we have been used to addressing countries and groups within the countries. for the first time now, we are addressing the region. we should also be innovative inside syria, trying new ways to access those in pressing need. we intend to be creative, too, as far as outside assistance is concerned. for the first time we have included in our humanitarian assistance host-country support – funding not only those who are coming to countries like lebanon and jordan but also helping the communities which are accepting the refugees. we need to look too – as we have already started doing – not at how to keep syria outside the framework of our neighbourhood policy, but rather at everything we have learned, every experience we have gathered in the various instruments of neighbourhood policy, and at how we could use this and transform it in order to help the whole region. that is what i referred to when i said that we are working now on a comprehensive approach to this region. it is no longer just a matter of the high representative pursuing her political agenda, my colleague kristalina georgieva pursuing her humanitarian agenda, and me representing the neighbourhood policy – all trying to do a little here and there – along with jordan, lebanon and other countries. it is a matter of all of us working together. as far as the political dimension is concerned, it is absolutely clear that this has been our paramount objective, and the high representative has worked tirelessly, both openly and also discreetly, to that end. she participated last year in the geneva meeting and she has engaged consistently in that process with all the parties, including the un security council members, to work on, and build on, the geneva communiqué, seeking an agreement with the united states and russia in particular. i can confirm that she is using every possible opportunity to raise these issues with russian foreign minister lavrov and is pressing, in particular, for the success of the recent initiative for a conference and peace process based on the geneva communiqué to which i referred. i am not overly concerned with what some of you have called a lack of unity among the member states. we might have different approaches and we have had open and lengthy debates in the foreign affairs council, but at the end of those foreign affairs council meetings we have consistently come out with a united front. the concerns that we have are about a divided international community: that is what is preventing us from using the full potential of our organisation. with regard to the question of where the high representative is: this morning she was still trying to help the prime ministers of serbia and kosovo to put together the implementation plan for the very important deal that they achieved on 19 april, and later, in the afternoon, she participated in the european council. she is, of course, aware of the importance of the friends of syria meeting, but that meeting is taking place at core-group level – it is not a full plenary meeting – and the external action service is there representing her. i want to talk about the humanitarian and political dimensions. for various reasons i am not going to talk about the military dimension. for all of us dealing with these issues, what is happening is not just a distant tragedy. the people from the external action service are the ones who visit the region regularly. a couple of weeks ago i visited lebanon and tried, in particular, to address the plight of the palestinians – i will come back to them. i was there working out a programme for supporting host-country capacities. i was there together with the un agencies to work out programmes so that those arriving with small children could put them into school – ensuring capacity so that those children are not subjected to continuing tremendous psychological pressures throughout the day; so that there is an institution taking care of them for at least part of the day while their parents devote their energy and time to more pressing issues. i will be going to jordan very soon, and there too i will be visiting refugee camps. not least because of the many interventions on the subject in this house, i will make safety and security in those camps the priority of that visit. i will be exploring with the jordanian authorities how best to assist them to make sure, in particular, that the most vulnerable – the women you referred to, and the children – are protected. i agree with a number of the speakers who said that if we do not manage this crisis we will be the first to feel the consequences. that is clear to all of us, and it would be hard to find a foreign minister who would disagree. does this mean that we have more answers than questions? no, it does not. i wish i had all the answers to the many questions you have raised, and i wish i had smart reactions to all the serious – and less serious – proposals and initiatives. whether they are considered now to be more or less serious does not matter: we will scrutinise all of them because, in this unprecedented crisis, we cannot fail to give due consideration to all suggestions. regarding the resettlement of syrians from the middle east, which is a question a number of you referred to: so far, the office of the united nations high commissioner for refugees (unhcr) has not called for a large-scale resettlement of syrian nationals displaced by the conflict. it has called for the settlement of a small number of particularly vulnerable persons, and we are following that line. in the future we will be guided by the advice of the unhcr as regards the timing and scope of such an initiative at european level. i can also stress that the commission has urged the member states on many occasions to make use of their national quotas, pledged under the 2012-2013 eu joint resettlement programme, to allocate places to refugees originating from the middle east region, including syria. i should add that it is not possible to finance any extra resettlement places from the european refugee fund, but if the unhcr were to call for a wider resettlement effort the commission would be prepared to support such an initiative, for example by organising a pledging conference. i am well aware of, and very concerned about, the plight of palestinian refugees. i talked to many of them in lebanon – those refugees who find themselves as double refugees. the european union continues to be the biggest donor to the united nations relief and works agency for palestinian refugees (unrwa). i will continue to help this organisation, and we have specific ongoing projects for palestinian refugees. there was also an important question about the kidnapping of bishops boulos yazigi and youhanna ibrahim. i want to draw attention to the statement that the high representative made on 26 april 2013 condemning the kidnapping and calling for the bishops’ immediate release. we share that concern, and i thank you very much for the additional names. in conclusion – i am sorry to have spoken for so long – we have to be aware that ‘better’ must not become the enemy of ‘good’. we have to progressively enhance our efforts. an increasing volume of assistance, quick mobilisation of funds, effective access and coordination, coupled with an appropriate political response, are our signposts. we will continue for as long as necessary and work hand in hand with our partners in the international community to make good on our promise of assistance and try to bring a lasting political settlement to this terrible conflict. my concluding remark is that we need to be aware of the linkage between the political and humanitarian dimensions. we need to be aware that, the less committed we are to the political dimension, the more committed we will have to be to the humanitarian dimension. we need to reverse that thinking and address the political dimension, because that will make it manageable for us, and the international community, to deal with the humanitarian consequences.

on behalf of the efd group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, there are many reasons for giving back to the peoples of the arab spring what has been taken from them, first of all because it is a matter of vast and precious financial resources at a time of crisis and transition when they are building their future. the return of stolen goods must also serve as a warning to the dictators of today and tomorrow, showing the international community that no one can enjoy the wealth stolen from his people with impunity. i also agree with commissioner füle and my predecessors that there are moral and just reasons why these goods should go back to those who produced them, the people of the arab spring, and help to meet their needs and contribute to their economic and social development. finally, a non-secondary aspect concerns the return of assets which will remove any alibi from the present governments for their failings and make them de facto accountable to their peoples for the proper management of these resources. i would like to conclude with a question to commissioner füle: he spoke of bilateral return arrangements by member states to these maghreb countries. i would like to know what practical possibilities of coordination europe can put in place to make the return of these assets easier and faster.
madam president, commissioner füle, this resolution is the result of a strong political initiative led by the socialist group and shared by almost all the others. the return of a huge amount of assets stolen by former dictators to the arab-speaking countries is a moral and legal imperative. the repatriation of these assets is – beyond its economic significance – a strong step in combating the impunity surrounding corruption and money laundering that corrupt political leaders have so far enjoyed. egypt, libya and tunisia have already made considerable efforts aimed at ensuring that these assets are returned to the new legitimate governments, but poor results have been achieved in this respect. we do not yet have a satisfactory international legal framework governing these matters – and such a framework is essential, mr tannock. intergovernmental cooperation is not enough and, in itself, will not get us very far. there are only a couple of multilateral initiatives dedicated to this issue. the most relevant effort undertaken by the international community so far is the un convention against corruption, which devotes a full chapter to the issue of asset recovery. given the magnitude of the depredation of public resources suffered by a million people who have revolted against injustice and corruption in tunisia, egypt and libya, the time has come for strong, concrete measures. this resolution should kick-start the first large-scale attempt to identify, confiscate and repatriate assets that total more than the collective gdp of all the countries involved. we are calling for the establishment, without delay, of an eu mechanism comprising a team of first-class investigators, prosecutors and lawyers able to provide the arab league countries with all the technical assistance needed for a process of asset recovery. this mechanism should be funded through adequate eu resources and should be operational within a few months. i believe this effort will be one of the most significant contributions by the eu to the consolidation of the democratic transition in these crucial countries.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the question of the recovery of assets is of enormous importance in the relations between the european union and the north african countries which have embarked on the path of change. the new governments of egypt, tunisia and libya have repeatedly called on the european union to take the issue seriously and put it on the agenda. the economic and financial situation of these countries is objectively difficult, the unemployment rate is clearly worsening, tourist revenues have fallen vertically and the economic crisis affecting europe, the main trading partner, is not leaving these countries unscathed, with very negative repercussions. it should be clear to everyone that the possibility of consolidating democratic processes and strengthening institutions does not lie solely in the definition of new and more advanced constitutional frameworks for these countries, although this is important, but in the concrete possibility of responding positively to the many economic and social expectations of the citizens. for these reasons, the recovery of assets must also be a political priority for the european union. in addition to its important political significance, it also has a strong economic impact in these transition countries, which face enormous legal and practical difficulties. the tunisian authorities submitted 66 requests for letters rogatory, mainly to the european union and the arab states; it is difficult to estimate the amount of assets to be recovered, but the tunisian government estimates between 18 and 38 billion euros, almost 50 billion for egypt and almost 100 billion for libya, 40 of which in european countries. the european parliament has already expressed its full support for this process in its resolution on egypt and is preparing to vote on this resolution. it is important, however, that this resolution be accompanied by a spirit of cooperation on the part of all the european institutions and above all the governments of the various member states in order to overcome the limitations and delays which continue to exist. there is more to be done here, he wondered. we must define a new european legal framework which will allow us to intervene because bilateral relations are not enough. two second speakers, because i want to take advantage of the presence of the commissioner to ask him if he can and will give us more information, some more information on the situation in tunisia with the clashes between the security forces and the salafists.

madam president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, a comprehensive and balanced free trade agreement between the european union and the united states holds all the potential for the development of deeper economic cooperation between the world's largest economies, which account for 30% of world trade. it is a tremendous opportunity for all of us to foster sustainable economic growth and perhaps even employment in europe. it is therefore almost a duty for the european union to pursue the trade negotiations with the united states with seriousness and tenacity, even though it knows that they will be challenging. in fact, limited market access and the many non-tariff barriers that still exist today restrict the full development of trade between the two sides of the atlantic and are particularly harmful to our enterprises, especially small and mediumsized enterprises. the result will, however, have to be a balanced agreement in which the intensification of trade is accompanied by the safeguarding of the values of the european union and of important principles rooted in european consumers, such as the protection of health and food safety. in particular, we expect the european commission to work hard in the future negotiations to ensure that intellectual property rights are strongly protected, particularly - and this is essential - european geographical indications, in order to combat unfair competition and widespread misrepresentation, and thus safeguard quality european agri-food production. we believe it is essential that the commission negotiates this agreement with the united states, also in accordance with the principle of european cultural diversity, which must remain a key factor for our growth and competitiveness. only balanced and comprehensive trade agreements based on the principle of reciprocity can present a real opportunity for growth and development today and in the future.

the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect. europe has large regions which could reasonably solve their problems together, because the challenges are common and because common solutions work better than isolated ones. this is why strategies for such macro-regions certainly make sense. the alps are such a region par excellence. they cover at least five member states of the european union and two non-member countries, so a total of at least seven countries. the mountain - as has been said by several previous speakers - has common challenges in production, for example, especially in the production of agricultural products; the alps have always been, for thousands of years, an important route from the south to the north. but it is also a question of protecting the environment, of protecting people from natural disasters and the forces of nature, which are more pronounced in the mountains than in the plains. it also concerns the protection of resources, such as the protection and provision of clean drinking water, which will become an increasingly important issue, not only in the alps but in europe as a whole. the main concern is the preservation of the habitat, which is also becoming a recreational and tourist area. this also creates pressure to settle. it has also been said that we are not starting from scratch here. there is cooperation in the alps that has been developed over decades, be it in the arge alp, the alpine convention, but also within existing regional development programmes such as alpine space, which has developed very well in the past periods of european union funding. i am also convinced that a macro strategy for the alps must deal with the alps, i.e. the challenges of the mountains, and not with the challenges of the pedo-alpine areas. i'm not saying that they're not important, but they're two different things that you can't mix. we should find a strategy that is a strategy for the people who live in the alpine areas. this is why an alpine strategy cannot be played out between town and country. there are cities within the alps, of course. but a macro strategy for the alps cannot be a strategy for munich, milan or lyon. we'd miss the target with that.

answer to a blue-card question. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i believe that mountain communities are an extraordinary example of territorial organization and of how communities have, within themselves and also in their contiguous relations, between valley and valley, between village and village, a principle of subsidiarity which they respect and which they have self-codified for centuries. it is impossible to think of a strategy for the mountain that is brought down from above, it will never work, neither in italy nor in austria nor in france nor anywhere else, so of course we need the principle of subsidiarity, but be careful that the principle of subsidiarity does not become another scam and then do nothing. the challenge of the mountains must be that of a truly united strategy. it is an alpine arc, it must remain an alpine arc with its environmental, cultural and economic integrity, and i believe that we will have no problem in sharing our efforts in this respect.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the adoption of this regulation introduces provisions which will make it easier for owners to move their pets between member states and reduce animal health risks. the new rules will also put a stop to those who fraudulently trade in pets, particularly dogs and cats. among the main changes, the regulation provides that the microchip to ensure the protection of animals is to be applied only by a veterinarian or a qualified person and that blank documents are to be defined only by veterinarians, in order to avoid falsification of documents. but there are also provisions which, if not properly controlled, could create problems, such as the exemptions for those who want to move more than five animals and those on rabies vaccination and owners' self-certifications. more could certainly be done, but a uniform system of registration compatible and accessible in all member states is still lacking. it will be essential to keep an eye on member states by constantly monitoring the application of these new rules to prevent fraud and abuse.
in writing. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the regulation to include the use of the term 'customs' in the definition of the concept of 'commercial policy'. the text calls for the postponement of the date of application of the new customs code which was to enter into force on 24 june 2013. i felt i had to support this request because the code in question has been profoundly amended and the trilogues between the commission, the council and parliament are still in progress.
in writing. - i am very sorry that parliament has postponed the date of application of the new customs code, on which i am draftsman of the opinion of the inta committee. the commission has also proposed that the community should be able to provide the community with a financial contribution to the financing of the common agricultural policy. there can be no single market for consumers and businesses until the customs codes of the various european countries are uniform. it is also known from a report by the commission that some ports in northern europe have become a soft spot for the entry of goods which are not sufficiently controlled. harmonising customs legislation is essential to ensure consumer safety and fair and transparent trade in the member states. the code was due to enter into force on 24 june 2013, a date which is already far from expectations and the further delay will cause further inconvenience to the union, italian customs and operators in the sector, already penalised by the lack of harmonised rules.

in writing. − the eu is party to an agreement providing for the possibility of resolving investor-state disputes of a financial nature (see, for example, the energy charter treaty). the commission considers that, given the existence of any disputes, the responsibility lies with the controller and the eu only if the action of the member state is provided for by community law. it is a very controversial subject, which has problems with the transfer of such sensitive competence to the exclusive sphere of competence of the eu. we must wait for the council's opinion on this. however, i would like to vote in favour of the commission's report as an example of a balanced approach to the subject.
in writing. − since 2003, the movement of pet animals has been governed by regulation (ec) no 998/2003 and its subsequent amendments. the main objective of the commission proposal, which repeals and replaces this regulation, remains unchanged in relation to the changes which have taken place over the years: the protection of public and animal health. in general, while acknowledging the rapporteur's commitment to facilitating pet owners' movements with their animals within the european union or to third countries, it is important that, with reference to the specific requirement to present the animal's identification documents during transport, the report should have been enriched with the possibility of presenting a collective document rather than just an individual one. the latter is a particularly onerous animal identification document, especially in the case of the transport of large numbers of animals for sporting purposes or for exhibitions or competitions. in my view, in the case of the transport of thousands of animals - for which there are already regular health checks - individual identification documents are not only onerous but also worthless. this restriction contributes to creating real difficulties for citizens wishing to participate in certain events requiring travel between different member states.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation on the non-commercial transport of pet animals within the eu, because although it has been regulated since 2003, the situation has changed considerably. the commission and the member states have successfully conducted anti-rabies campaigns which have resulted in rabies being considered as extinct in principle in many parts of the union, although constant monitoring is still necessary. rabies, or the absence of rabies, has been the main, though not the only, reason for maintaining a special transitional regime for the movement of animals within the territory of certain member states. the expiry of another transitional regime under article 4 (1) (tattooing or transponder marking) is another good reason to revise the current regulation no 998/2003. the main objective of the regulation is to make it easier for pet owners to transport their pets across the eu, while taking all the necessary precautions and complying with safety rules.
in writing. - i have voted in favour of this regulation because i agree with the comments which have been considered. i think that some good arguments have been made. i fully agree with the need to ensure safety against health risks in order to protect both the health of citizens and the health of animals themselves. i think that, as regards the vaccination of pets, more clarity should be given to the rules to avoid confusion in the application by veterinarians and pet owners. i fully agree with the solutions suggested. however, as regards fraudulently disguised commercial movements of pet animals, such as movements of a non-commercial nature and the maximum number of animals that may be travelled for any competition or sporting event, clearer and more concrete rules should be identified in order to avoid fraudulent actions and at the same time protect those competitions or exhibitions or sporting events. i also agree to facilitate the identification of the animal concerned with a database to protect documents from possible falsification.
