mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner malmström, the mid-term report which we shall be voting on tomorrow in plenary is an important first step taken by the crim special committee after months of hard work and many hearings. i would like to stress that this is only a first step and that unfortunately we still have a long way to go to spread a culture of legality in europe and to assert the principle that the mafia is not a local phenomenon but a global phenomenon and must be treated as such. among the instruments and measures to be adopted at european level suggested by the report, i would like to mention once again, in particular, the common definition of organised crime and corruption, the harmonisation of criminal law, the abolition of banking secrecy, transparency in public procurement and in particular the creation of a blacklist of companies involved in corruption offences and the ban on participation in public tenders for five years for those economic operators who have committed offences related to corruption, organised crime and money laundering. then there is the establishment of a european public prosecutor, which has been mentioned on more than one occasion, the ineligibility in the european parliament of persons convicted of crimes relating to corruption, organised crime and money laundering, and also strict rules against environmental crimes, and the demand for specific legislation to protect witnesses and victims of trafficking. i thank the rapporteur for his work and hope that this report will be the basis for an even more ambitious final report, which will outline a clear european strategy to combat crime, corruption and money laundering.
member of the commission. − mr president, i would like to thank the honourable members for this very interesting debate. as every one of you has stated, organised crime groups have become ever more sophisticated and multi-tasked. they create huge harm to their victims and society as a whole. such corruption is also a very well-paid business. different figures have been circulating and it is very difficult to estimate the exact numbers here, but we have seen figures in the commission, and are working around them, saying that organised crime and its different assets amount to at least the collective gdp of several member states, and that corruption in the eu alone could be the equivalent of one eu annual budget – so if we could do away with that, we would not need to have the budget debates and struggles we have today! mr president, ladies and gentlemen, no one wants to question the aims of this programme - especially in a time of dramatic crisis with an increasing number of people who can no longer afford to buy food to feed themselves on a daily basis. so it's right to intervene, but the way it's done leaves me a little puzzled; there have been too many cases in the past of fraud and fraud with products intended for the poor and then resold by unscrupulous individuals without anyone properly checking. last year, i reported to the european commission several incidents in tuscany, in arezzo, of foodstuffs with eu labels still in good condition found in the garbage cans. the commission said that it was unaware of this and that the responsibility for the checks was solely and exclusively with the member states; i wonder, then, whether it would not be appropriate to renationalize these programmes, with a more easily controllable dimension, because it is unacceptable that there is an exculpatory of responsibility on such important matters.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution, the main purpose of which is to confirm a long-term plan for the conservation of cod stocks, ensuring their sustainable exploitation in the geographical areas of the kattegat, the north sea, the waters of western scotland and the irish sea, in accordance with the maximum sustainable yield. this is a subject which, of course, does not directly concern our italian seas, but as european parliamentarians elected without territorial limitations we must work in the interests of all european citizens and, as far as i am concerned, also for the protection of animals, no matter in which country, no matter in which sea they are. i hope that the honourable members from other countries will show solidarity and the same spirit of european solidarity towards my fellow citizens and the italian seas if the need arises.

madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of the report by mr garcés ramón on the new agenda for consumer policy. in fact, in a market which is increasingly complex and globalised and increasingly dominated by electronic commerce, it is even more essential to promote, by means of concrete legislative measures, correct and complete information for consumers, with particular reference to vulnerable categories of consumers such as children, the elderly and those who are not very familiar with electronic commerce, especially with regard to particular categories of products such as foodstuffs, and those who come into direct contact with the person providing financial and banking services. first of all, it is essential to strengthen the control of the safety of products placed on the market and to combat unfair commercial practices and the many forms of misleading advertising effectively, in order to protect the health of consumers and to combat counterfeiting on a european basis.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, ensuring respect for the rights of citizens in a social market economy is an objective pursued by the european union and it is achieved through action to protect consumers. over the years, the union has made great strides in protecting consumers from safety risks through legislation introducing mandatory labelling, control of gm crops, transparency in financial transactions and more. all this, while useful, no longer seems sufficient: the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the eu's new rules on the protection of personal data, in particular the provisions on the protection of personal data and the protection of personal data against unauthorised access to the internet. the adoption of a new agenda for european consumer policy, while also committing ourselves to combating conflicts of interest, which must be an essential part of this agenda, is now more necessary and indispensable than ever.
in writing. − the commission has published the draft european consumer agenda, as a follow-up to the eu's consumer policy strategy, which includes a series of consumer-oriented initiatives for the period 2014-2020. i welcome this project: the european consumer agenda gives concrete meaning to the principle of the treaty on european union that the interests of consumers must be taken into account in all relevant policies of the european union. at the global level, european consumers face new challenges such as globalisation of markets, financial deregulation, digitalisation of the economy and an ageing population. i therefore believe that food safety, health, financial and digital products must be the top priority on the european agenda. recent surveys show that the most important priorities for european consumers are better protection in the financial services and food sectors. it is clear that the issues of food safety and labelling, and the protection of consumers against the greed of financial systems, must be included in the consumer agenda without delay. the level of implementation of consumer protection needs to be the same throughout the european union and market surveillance activities need to be truly effective.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution, following the instructions of the epp group to which i belong, because i agree that ensuring food, health, energy, financial and digital products must be the top priority on the european consumer agenda. our citizens are facing new challenges such as the globalisation of markets, financial deregulation and the digitalisation of the economy, in a context of economic crisis that makes choices and decisions more complex. i therefore believe that consumers should have access to information on products that is as transparent, efficient, reliable and comparable as possible. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the future of the european union's external relations.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by mr gárces ramón, which seeks to establish a new agenda for european consumer policy. i believe that it is our duty to protect consumers in the best possible way and the proposals contained in this own-initiative report are acceptable. i think it is essential that the commission improves the means available to consumers to resolve any dispute, regardless of where or how it is purchased, and further increases food safety in europe, especially after the recent scandals affecting the sector.
in writing. − the new agenda for european consumer policy aims to create sustainable consumption and to increase growth and consumer confidence. an important first step is the commission's willingness to cooperate with economic operators: the quality, traceability, safety and authenticity of products must be guaranteed to increase consumer confidence. i agree with the rapporteur that a proposal should be made to improve the public's knowledge of the financial sector. i join in the call for rapid, accessible and effective redress mechanisms that are not hampered by the cross-border nature of the dispute or by the lack of information or resources to access legal aid. finally, i believe it is important to have cooperation between european, national and local authorities and consumer associations in order to establish consultation mechanisms to ensure the implementation of the measures set out in the agenda. i am voting in favour of this proposal, as i agree with many of the points listed.
in writing. − the adaptation of the european consumer policy agenda sets important targets, in line with the challenges posed by the evolution of the european and global market. in particular, the new perspectives designed for food safety, set themselves important operational objectives. in the light of recent cases of fraud in the agri-food sector, it is appropriate to work towards developing an agenda that takes account of the new needs of consumers and respect for their prerogatives. i think this report fully captures the necessary challenges to be undertaken to improve consumer protection.
in writing. − we have today adopted a new agenda covering all possible initiatives for european consumers for the period 2014-2020. we believe it is important to urge the european commission to prepare a green paper which will be useful to consumer rights organisations, citizens and national governments. we consider it a top priority to ensure food, health, energy, financial and digital product safety and to make information more transparent, efficient and reliable for consumers. it is therefore essential to give consumers greater decision-making power in their relationship with the markets, and to encourage them to take responsibility and to be aware of their rights. we are also convinced that the conditions of inequality within the european union must be addressed in the context of the solidarity inherent in the european social model. it is therefore necessary that elements such as social and environmental sustainability, food and product safety, with particular attention to the relationship between markets and minors, be taken into account in the construction of a new consumer agenda. in addition, the telecommunications market in the european union will have to be able to provide consumers with a secure digital environment while respecting the protection of all personal data.
in writing. consumption, which accounts for 56% of european gdp, is a very important economic factor. this is why consumers must be protected by making them aware of their rights and giving them the confidence they need to use sales networks, especially those on the internet. this report, by making proposals for consumer safety, good information, the guarantee of the existence of legal remedies and the alignment of rights with economic and social developments; meet my approval. that is why i voted without hesitation for this own-initiative report.
in writing. - i voted strongly in favour of this resolution and i ask the european commission to commit itself without delay to implementing as soon as possible all the measures necessary to ensure that the internal market is truly single, that protection against fraud is truly effective, that the resolution of disputes is rapid and proportionate to the value of the goods, that information for consumers is comprehensive and that electronic commerce is reliable. without these commitments, we will be back here in a few years' time debating and voting on the same demands, but then it will be too late.
in writing. as representatives of the european citizens, we have a great responsibility towards them, their quality of life, the freedom and ease with which they can develop their interests, and we must also look to the balances of the internal market of which the citizens are the main builders as consumers. i therefore believe that the european union needs to have a long-term political agenda, looking to 2020, in the interests of consumers. transparency of information, product safety and the protection of consumer rights require a long-term plan which, especially in this time of crisis, is able to guarantee greater freedom of choice and consequently a higher level of satisfaction.
in writing. - i am in favour of the text of the report as ensuring food safety, health, energy, financial and digital products must be the top priority on the european consumer agenda. this agenda also fits into the final phase of the digital single market, which requires online protection, legal certainty, consumer rights safeguards and efficient and reliable delivery services for the transport of goods and services. this agenda is necessary to reduce disparities between consumers in europe and contribute to a low-carbon economy. it is essential that food safety and labelling aspects are included in the food safety strategy, assessing the need to ensure safety in the food chain from production to consumption.
in writing. - 56% of the eu's gdp is accounted for by consumer spending, the real engine of the economy. in times of economic crisis like the one we are experiencing, it is more than ever necessary to incentivise consumer spending to get the economy moving again. however, the increasing globalisation and the rapid development of new information technologies are making consumers increasingly wary of the market: 60% of the population does not shop online and about 75% of small and medium-sized enterprises do not use the electronic channel to sell their products. the problem becomes more relevant for those groups of consumers who are less familiar with new technologies, such as the elderly. in order to help the economic recovery, i felt it necessary to support the proposal for a new consumer policy agenda, to encourage the spread of renewed consumer confidence in the market.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on a new agenda for european consumer policy because i believe it is important to adopt initiatives aimed at protecting consumers, who are constantly exposed to risks. consumers' associations, which play an important role in assisting citizens, should therefore be given more support. the draft european consumer agenda will have to contain measures to protect children from the advertising of food products that encourage bad habits and will have to step up controls on products of dubious origin containing dangerous chemicals. the commission will therefore have to step up its controls on labelling and invest in research to assess the health risks arising from the use of certain products. we will have to promote local food production by giving farmers aid to increase the production of agricultural products in view of the growing demand for food and by encouraging short circuits which would lead to a reduction in transport and therefore co2 emissions. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the proposal for a directive on the protection of consumers in the event of a dispute between the commission and the consumer. it is important to support the creation of tools that enable citizens to take collective action to protect their rights.
in writing. − the european consumer agenda gives concrete meaning to the treaty principle that the interests of consumers must be taken into account in all relevant union policies. european consumers are currently facing new challenges such as globalisation of markets, financial deregulation, digitalisation of the economy and an ageing population: this means that the tools for redress and support for consumer organisations will become more relevant. it is therefore essential to ensure that the european citizens are as attentive and effective as possible, and in this connection it is essential that there be efficient, transparent and reliable information.
in writing. − directive 2003/8/ec is an important tool for a european area of justice without administrative barriers, for the benefit of citizens. the aim of the directive is to improve access to justice in crossborder civil cases by laying down common minimum standards for legal aid and to ensure that people who cannot afford legal aid are provided with adequate legal aid. the greatest possible awareness and information is needed to strengthen the rights linked to european citizenship: only 12% of citizens are aware of the existence of such free legal aid at the expense of the state. i also agree that there is a need to provide for increased language skills and simplified procedures for the benefit of citizens and competent authorities, in order to maximise access to the possibilities provided for in the directive.
in writing. − directive 2003/8/ec is a piece of legislation of great importance to european citizens, as it ensures that the least well-off members of society have access to justice in other member states too. however, this directive has some problems: first of all, it's not very well known. the commission has established that only 12% of citizens are aware of the existence of legal aid in crossborder disputes, so it is unlikely that citizens would be able to exercise this right in a situation where it is provided for. in view of this, i would draw the commission's attention to the need to take measures to ensure that greater awareness is raised about legal aid, particularly among legal practitioners. another problem is that different member states have different thresholds for granting legal aid at the expense of the state. i agree with the rapporteur's proposal that applicants should be able to apply for legal aid in the member state of residence or in the member state where they are requested, in order to avoid a citizen who would have been entitled to legal aid in his country of residence being denied that right.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the zwiefka report on better access to justice: advocates at the public expense in cross-border civil and commercial disputes. although european citizens have had the right to request legal aid in crossborder disputes since 2004, only 12% of them are aware of it. i therefore share the text of the initiative proposal which seeks to promote information campaigns for the public and legal practitioners, introduce training programmes for the latter and above all would like to grant the possibility of requesting free legal aid for every citizen, thus overcoming the problem of access thresholds, which are different in each member state.
in writing. - only 12% of european citizens are aware of the existence of public procurement in crossborder disputes. this leads to a low level of use of this instrument, which is intended to ensure that the most disadvantaged members of society also have access to justice in other member states, for example when they exercise their right to free movement or benefit from the internal market. directive 2003/8/ec, which introduced this guarantee, has been positively transposed by the member states, although it is necessary to monitor those national realities where implementation is not yet complete. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial instruments are used effectively. in view of the existing legislation, i agree with the proposal to have the right of representation sought in the state of residence, which, if the requirements are met, will issue a certificate which can then be invoked in the country where the dispute is taking place. this would greatly simplify procedures and reduce the costs of language barriers.
in writing. - we welcomed the european commission's evaluation report on the application of council directive 2003/8/ec. we are satisfied with the way in which the countries of the european union are implementing it, which aims to improve access to justice in crossborder disputes, both civil and commercial, by defining common minimum standards for legal aid. as mr zwiefka has pointed out, there are still some difficulties and gaps in its application. we believe, first of all, that it is essential that the member states should make every effort to raise awareness among all european citizens of the subject, considering that the commission has established that only 12% of them are aware of the existence of legal aid even in crossborder disputes. in addition, in order to avoid problems of understanding between lawyers and clients, we consider it appropriate to take steps to ensure knowledge of the foreign language and legal system which is the subject of the disputes in question. we therefore call on all member states to promote its rapid and widespread application so that citizens can benefit from rapid and secure access to free legal aid throughout europe.
in writing. cross-border legal disputes are important issues, particularly in the context of the continuous strengthening of exchanges and interactions that are taking place within the european union. mr zwiefka, in pointing out the problems associated with these situations, has put forward proposals in his report, which i support. these include proposals to make the previous directive on the subject, which is little known to the general public, known. for many of our fellow europeans, justice in crossborder cases seems inaccessible. i support the idea of improving access to justice and that is why i am voting for this report.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution because the signal given is important: in a single internal market, consumer disputes must be resolved effectively and the logistics alone (let us imagine a problem between a swedish trader and a greek buyer) is in itself a barrier of distance, time and above all cost. the state should therefore take over this type of guarantee. i regret that the commission does not specifically address the issue of european procedures which also fall within the scope of the directive on legal aid, such as the european small claims procedure, despite the fact that the application of the directive in relation to the procedure in question could certainly have been studied during the period from 1 january 2009 to 31 december 2010. i am pleased to note, however, that all the member states have transposed the directive, although the interpretation of the scope of application varies on some points from one member state to another. i hope that in a future report information will be provided, broken down by country, on the number and substance of the cases, in order to obtain a more detailed and meaningful picture of the use of this instrument.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on legal aid in crossborder civil and commercial disputes because we must ensure that the most deprived citizens have better access to justice by defining common rules which enable them to benefit from legal aid, not only in their country of residence but also in other member states, and without difficulty. the commission's assessment of the directive is positive, but i believe that action must be taken to make it more widely known to the public, thus giving them access to it. it would be important to break down barriers to language skills between lawyers and citizens by creating databases of lawyers with relevant skills and no gaps in knowledge of the legal systems of other states. given that different countries have different thresholds for access to legal aid at the expense of the state, citizens may have a problem with the discrepancy between the procedures of the different countries, so i am in favour of a certificate that attributes the ownership of the benefit in the state of residence and that is recognized in any other state without having to resort to new expertise. these changes would make it possible to speed up procedures, simplifying procedures for citizens.
in writing. - i support the creutzmann report on the protection of intellectual property rights by customs authorities. i agree with the text where it calls for stricter rules on checks on goods in transit, but especially at the points where it calls for greater attention to small consignments, mainly from e-commerce purchases, and for the seizures of counterfeit goods to be reported to the companies concerned, giving them the opportunity to analyse the sample and investigate the origin of the counterfeit; i think that a standard of this kind would be extremely useful in supporting our companies.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this parliament's legislative resolution adopting the council's position with a view to the adoption of the regulation on the protection of intellectual property rights by customs authorities. the strengthening of the internal market and consumer protection depends to a large extent on better regulation of intellectual property. counterfeiting causes damage worth €250 billion a year, but its negative effects also affect the health and safety of citizens. this instrument introduced introduces new rules which will improve the whole and on which i have given my consent. in particular, the role and tasks of customs officers are strengthened: it is essential to strengthen controls when suspect goods arrive from third countries. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's internal market is not affected by the introduction of new technologies. this new regulation also has a positive impact on legal certainty, taking into account the legal, economic and commercial developments that have taken place in the meantime. finally, i am convinced that particular attention should be paid to medicines from non-eu countries, because of the significant implications for the health of citizens.
in writing. − the european union has taken an important step towards defending the rights of companies that work by the rules. the continuous violations of intellectual property rights by criminal organizations in recent years have caused considerable economic damage. the council of europe has recognised that large-scale infringements in trade in goods are a serious problem worldwide. the global legal framework on intellectual property rights must now be accompanied by more effective enforcement of the law. in this context i think it is precisely the customs authorities, with their valuable control work, who must play an increasingly important role in the application of this legislation.
in writing. intellectual property rights are a key element of the europe 2020 strategy to achieve smart, sustainable and inclusive growth. when we know the cost of piracy and counterfeiting in europe (€250 billion a year!) and the danger that copyright infringement can pose to consumers' health and safety, we must act. this is what the report proposes by increasing control measures but exempting goods in the luggage of final consumers, who are not always aware of the pirated or contraband nature of the goods they buy. that is why i am voting in favour of this report.
in writing. - we voted with satisfaction on the second reading of the report on the new rules for customs officers which will allow the control authorities to stop suspicious goods without interfering with the rules on intellectual property and goods carried by individual travellers. the phenomenon of counterfeiting, which amounts to 250 billion euros, is destroying european economic development through the loss of jobs and the closure of many smes, unable to face unfair competition from third countries, our economic partners and competitors, and also increases the risk to the health of european consumers who, relying on the internal market, buy without appropriate knowledge. we therefore support the text that has been voted, even if we do not hide the problem of medicines from non-eu countries and the increase in their online sale, where the possibility of confiscation of goods becomes ridiculous. unfortunately, without full harmonization of customs rules and control and sanctioning mechanisms, europe will still have a lot of work to do to defend its consumers and its manufacturing fabric if the single market is to regain the full confidence of european citizens, and that is why we underline our disappointment at the vote which allowed a further delay in the entry into force of the new customs code at the last part-session.
in writing. − in europe, on average, the ten most important brands in each member state produce 10% of european gdp. we need adequate measures to protect our products. the phenomenon of counterfeiting has serious consequences not only for manufacturing companies and consumers but also for the european economy as a whole. it is estimated that counterfeiting cost the creative industry €10 billion and over 185 000 jobs in 2008 alone. the amount of goods detained at customs suspected of infringing intellectual property rights has increased tenfold in the last decade: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to the full. i therefore support the proposal to revise the previous legislation on procedures for the confiscation and destruction of counterfeit goods by customs authorities. a simplified procedure for handling counterfeit goods, extended to all intellectual property rights, will relieve customs authorities of unnecessary red tape and stop shipments before they reach the market.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the council's position on the adoption of the regulation on the protection of intellectual property rights by customs authorities and i believe that stricter rules are necessary to protect our markets and the health of consumers. millions of counterfeit products are discovered each year, with significant economic repercussions for our companies and damaging their image, as well as often having harmful effects on the health of consumers. customs defenses should be strengthened by intensifying controls to prevent goods from entering the eu territory and by giving customs officers greater powers to stop suspicious goods, paying particular attention to products such as toys, cosmetics and pharmaceuticals, which, once they enter the european market, would have very serious effects on the health of citizens. in the meantime, it would be desirable for companies to facilitate traceability and provide customs with the information needed to identify genuine products and distinguish them from counterfeits.
in writing. − the turnover of counterfeit products in europe is worth €250 billion a year: it is therefore of paramount importance to prevent counterfeit goods from entering the union in order to protect european markets and citizens. as the rapporteur said, customs authorities are in a very good position to detect and eliminate counterfeit products before they are distributed throughout europe. the regulation will therefore enable customs officials to do their job more efficiently, stopping suspicious goods without altering the rules on intellectual property and goods carried by travellers.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, we voted and approved today the regulation on food for special medical purposes. this is the conclusion of an intensive and complex negotiation process, the main objectives of which were, on the one hand, to simplify the legislative framework and to bring it up to date with technical and scientific progress and, on the other, to guarantee high levels of health protection for those patients for whom a specific restriction is of vital importance. a legal framework has therefore been developed to fill in the legislative gaps and avoid unnecessary overlap, while maintaining the emphasis on the importance of innovation in this area and introducing safeguards to protect consumers from misleading information on food labelling. a framework setting maximum levels and prohibitions for the use of certain pesticides which reforms the list of substances that can be added to food. today's vote is therefore of the utmost importance and demonstrates the european union's concern to protect the health of its citizens.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the informal negotiations during the cypriot presidency were very quick and i am pleased that an agreement was reached in such a short time. the agreement on the dossier of 14 november 2012 fully meets all the demands of parliament and represents a significant step forward for food safety. however, some doubts arise in relation to the part of the agreement concerning food for people intolerant to gluten, which could have been already covered in the report. the additional information on the absence or reduced presence of gluten is a matter of great importance to the part of the consumers concerned by the subject and the fact that the agreement provides protection similar to that which already exists and does not seek improvements leaves me puzzled. i hope that this potential shortcoming will be taken seriously in the work that is planned and that parliament will be able to play its part here too.
in writing. − in a constantly changing market, where once niche products are now in increasing demand, there is a need for a comprehensive review of existing legislation on food intended for specific groups of the population, including the elderly, children, diabetics and celiacs. among the proposals put forward, i agree that the concept of dietetic food should be abolished and that a single legal act should be created to regulate the lists of foodstuffs, not only to ensure a harmonised treatment at european level but also to give greater attention to the specific needs of certain consumers. in this respect, i agree with the rapporteur on the importance of providing adequate legal cover for people who are intolerant to gluten or other forms of intolerance. it is not enough, as the commission believes, to say that a food is 'gluten-free' or 'lactose-free' when for many people these products are for everyday consumption, not occasional consumption, and are obtained by a particular manufacturing process. more attention should also be paid to children, especially those born underweight or premature, and to people with diabetes, a disease which we know is on the increase.
in writing. - i voted against all the amendments which have been tabled. to be honest, i can't and won't say that i don't share them: a year and a half ago, when the dossier was still in the hands of the committees (which had the power to give opinions on the matter), i, together with other italian colleagues from all the political groups, fought a fierce battle for greater and better consideration of celiac disease. it should be remembered that italy is particularly affected by celiac disease, probably because of the different consumption of gluten-rich foods (primarily bread and pasta). however, we are in the second reading and, in agreement with the associations of celiac patients, i felt that this battle should be fought in other places, in other dossiers, and that it was not worth throwing away more than 20 months of work. i am still bitter about the lack of attention paid to a problem which affects italy in particular, but i am confident in the solution found and in the commission's implementing acts.
in writing. - the resolution adopted today is the result of a compromise which does not take account of parliament's vote at first reading. in fact, although i protect infants and children, i find it scandalous that it excludes celiacs. by not including products with a nutritional profile similar to gluten in medical foods we are further penalising the many european citizens who suffer from celiac disease.
in writing. − the european council's position on foods for infants in early childhood covers a number of topics, including lactose, foods for infants, sports foods and pesticides. although i think that the agreement reached with the council is unsatisfactory as regards gluten - it does not seem appropriate to repeal the ad hoc regulation and rely on the commission - i am in favour of it.
in writing. - this parliament has been fighting for food safety and consumer protection on several occasions. in the present case, the guarantee of safety in products intended for infants, children and special medical purposes requires a very high degree of control and safety, both for the target group and for the risks involved. the measures to be taken, especially for food coming from the extra-eu border, must therefore take account of a high degree of caution and be very attentive to the specificities of the target audiences, considering that these are infants and children in the early stages of life.
in writing. - we adopted today in plenary a number of recommendations on the new rules on baby food, food for special diets and low-calorie food. the rapporteur, mr ries, wanted to emphasize that the rules on the labelling and content of infant milk and food for medical purposes need to be better defined. the aim is to improve consumer protection and to help consumers distinguish more clearly between food for everyday consumption and food for specific groups. we therefore consider the new legislation to be valid, which simplifies and clarifies the rules on the labelling and composition of infant formulae and follow-on formulae (between six and ten months of age). we also believe that it is essential and necessary to include a comprehensive list of substances such as vitamins and minerals to be added to the list of these foods. finally, we would like to stress the importance of the presentation and advertising of infant formulae, and ask that it not be misleading and therefore not attempt to induce people to abandon natural breastfeeding for these products unless it is really necessary.
in writing. - forgive me, but sometimes i have trouble understanding this parliament: i do not understand how i could have been in the minority in parliament, supporting an amendment which required the gluten content of a foodstuff intended for children to be clearly indicated. celiac disease, or gluten intolerance, develops at the very end of breastfeeding and i therefore think it is most appropriate to vote in favour of more information in this context. infants and children are vulnerable subjects who must be given more protection than adults, even when it is the adult who makes choices on their behalf and who, all the more so, has the right to be informed in greater detail as he is taking responsibility for the health of vulnerable subjects. i think we also missed an opportunity to send a message of solidarity to the 0.8% of the european population who suffer from celiac disease.
in writing. − health protection is a subject which includes such varied and specialised work plans that the european legislator has to deal with it in detail, as in the case of the newly adopted text on food for special medical purposes and food for infants and young children. the text is intended to provide guarantees on products intended for patients and children in order to guarantee their health and to certify the product purchased by parents. clear information on the substances contained in these foods facilitates their identification and ensures product safety, which can be easily detected from the labelling. the help of technology and science, together with the regulatory simplification that the text achieves, facilitates those patients and consumers who cannot do without the consumption of these foods.
in writing. − infants, children and seriously ill people are not like other consumers. i believe that it is our duty as legislators to establish stricter rules, particularly as regards the composition and labelling of the foodstuffs intended for them. i believe that the new legislation simplifies and clarifies the rules on the labelling and composition of infant and follow-on foods (for children aged between 6 and 10 months), cereal-based foods, foods for special medical purposes and dietetic foods. i believe that this new legislation can be a valuable tool to protect consumers and help them to distinguish more clearly between food for everyday consumption and food for specific groups.
in writing. − from now on, the labelling of products such as infant milk and food for medical purposes will be clearer and better defined, protecting consumers and helping them to choose the products best suited to their specific needs. the final text clearly showed the european parliament's desire to promote breast milk and breastfeeding by prohibiting advertising or illustrations which could induce consumers to prefer synthetic or powdered milk to it, except for medical reasons.
in writing. - today's vote marks the end of an intensive and difficult negotiation process which was intended both to simplify the legislative framework for certain particular foods and to ensure high levels of health protection for those patients who are bound to a specific diet. in order to make this document as complete as possible, safeguards have been introduced to protect consumers from all types of information which may appear misleading in the labelling, presentation or advertising of foodstuffs; the prohibition of the use of certain pesticides has been provided for; the list of substances that can be added to food has also been reformed.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the development of magnetic resonance imaging technology should have been excluded from the scope of the new directive, and i do not think there can be any doubt about that. the development of this important medical technique must continue and the strict measures initially proposed by the commission were in serious danger of jeopardising it. however, this derogation must be fully justified and the additional measures necessary to protect workers in the sector still need to be clarified and regulated. i realize that this is a very complicated matter and that is why i believe that the commission should continue with further studies and further research on this subject.
in writing. - i fully support the proposal by mrs morin-chartier to amend directive 2004/40/ec to define limit values for exposure to electromagnetic fields and to introduce new, more stringent protection measures. no worker may be exposed to electric, magnetic or electromagnetic fields with values above certain limits which may have biophysical effects dangerous to health. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to electromagnetic fields. in addition, the employer should be required to provide all necessary information on the risks of exposure to electromagnetic fields at the workplace and to train his employees in the use of protective measures, as is the case in the medical field in the use of magnetic resonance imaging.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this proposal for a directive, following the instructions given by my group, the ppe. i fully agree that the 2004 eu directive on the risks arising from continuous exposure to electromagnetic fields should be amended: the definition of very restrictive exposure limit values would have reduced the possibilities of using medical equipment for magnetic resonance imaging, which is absolutely essential for the diagnosis and treatment of many diseases. in addition, the medical sector has already put in place strict protective measures for staff, accompanied by strict checks and training on the short and long-term health risks of overexposure and non-compliance with safety measures. in view of these factors, it seems to me justified to introduce a derogation for magnetic resonance imaging and related activities, especially if this derogation is accompanied, as requested by the commission, by even more important safety measures.
in writing. - safety and health of workers are matters of considerable importance, the rate of accidents at work has increased dramatically both because of the lack of communication between the employer and the worker himself and because of the inadequacy of the means of protection. i believe that the social partners have a crucial role to play in the european decision-making process on safety and health at work, as their consultation is crucial and necessary. i agree with the strengthening of existing structures for the protection of workers in order to give them security and peace of mind. i would stress the importance of proper medical surveillance and appropriate protective measures taken by employers towards their workers in order to avoid accidents at work. i voted in favour of this proposal because i agree with everything that the rapporteur has said and discussed.
in writing. − directive 2004/40/ec sets exposure limits for electrical, electromagnetic and magnetic fields. parliament today approved new rules which aim to update the text, to balance the protection of workers' health and safety with the flexibility and proportionality required, safeguarding the health of all those who are exposed to electromagnetic fields at work. these new rules aim to establish international exposure limits, based on the recommendations of the international commission on non-ionizing radiation protection (icnirp). it will, however, be up to the employer to assess and set maximum exposure limits to electromagnetic fields.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by elisabeth morin-chartier on the protection of workers in the eu exposed to electromagnetic fields, as the directive provides greater protection for workers exposed to electromagnetic fields in the performance of their work commitments, while at the same time providing flexibility in taking account of the specific nature of certain risk activities. this new directive places a responsibility on employers to implement measures to reduce the exposure of their workers to electromagnetic fields, and examines the health risks to workers and the short and long-term harmful effects of occupational exposure to such electromagnetic fields. it applies to all sectors and is particularly relevant to workers exposed to high levels of risk, such as those in heavy industry, metal processing, or those working long hours in the vicinity of television, radio and radar installations.
in writing. i am proud to have voted today on my report on the health and safety of workers exposed to electromagnetic fields. i am proud of the work i have been able to lead with the european parliament's negotiating team for over two years. this proposal provides a common regulatory framework for protecting the health and safety of workers in the european union exposed to electromagnetic fields. the report also sets out all the conditions necessary for member states to finally transpose their safety rules within a reasonable period of time, including possible derogations in the medical field (mri) and in the field of military strategic surveillance (e.g. radar). i also fully agree with this proposal because it is a clear and simple text available to all workers and employers in the european union.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution because high frequency electromagnetic fields, which are what scare people, are becoming more and more an integral part of our lives: in 2012, italy overtook luxembourg to become the european country with the highest concentration of mobile phone users: 109.42 for every 100 people. the data comes from the itu, the united nations telecommunications agency. the world now beats us only by hong kong (114.53). my country also has the first place for the umts: with almost 4 million users, it is the first in europe and the 12th in the world (out of 70 countries using it). in absolute terms, with 62.75 million users, italy ranks second in europe after germany and seventh in the world after japan, the us, china, russia, germany and brazil. in view of a scenario which is therefore likely to get worse (or better, depending of course on the point of view) with the advent of the 4g network already present in some european cities, i can only welcome the fact that the european parliament has committed itself to setting health protection limits in the face of exposure to electromagnetic fields.
in writing. the text adopted today lays down new rules to protect workers exposed to electromagnetic fields more effectively. i think this text strikes a balance between the health and safety of workers and the possibility of using electromagnetic fields when necessary, for example for medical purposes. the legislation covers all sectors, but is mainly aimed at protecting workers exposed to a high level of risk, for example in the steel industry or people working for long hours near tv and radio transmitters and radar installations. finally, i think it is right to leave it to the employer to assess the risks of exposure to electromagnetic fields and to take the necessary measures to reduce the level of exposure, for example by choosing the equipment or by using blocking or shielding mechanisms.
in writing. the vote will strike a balance at european level between the need to protect the health of workers in environments exposed to magnetic fields and the possibility of using them when necessary, for example in the medical and diagnostic field. the new exposure limits will be decided on the basis of scientific findings which may be updated as technological research progresses.
in writing. − exposure to electromagnetic fields from telephone antennas, mobile phones, wlan, wifi, laptops and other sources typical of the era in which we live is a serious health hazard. patients with multiple sensitivities are vulnerable to environmental pollution and patients with electromagnetic hypersensitivity (ehs) to electromagnetic radiation. the european environment and health plan 2004-2010 (2007/2252 ((ini)) provided for greater protection of environments such as schools, nurseries, care homes and health institutions: the limit values for exposure to electromagnetic fields in italy today are 6 volts/metre for high frequencies and 10 and 3 microtesla for lower frequencies, and recent studies show that values of 0.4 for low and 0.2 for high are already very dangerous. given that health inequalities between the various member states should be eliminated and that in sweden electro-sensitivity is recognised as a disability and those affected are entitled to social security support, i think it is important that all member states include multiple chemical sensitivity and electro-sensitivity as recognised diseases in their national health systems, and i hope that minimum safety requirements can be achieved in order to protect the patient.
in writing. − the recent proposal for a european commission directive aims to recast directive 2004/40/ec on the minimum health and safety requirements regarding the exposure of workers to the risks arising from physical agents. the directive is of considerable importance in that it specifies the determination of risks, the protection of all workers exposed to such risks, the minimisation or elimination of identified risks, the training and consultation of workers involved, adequate medical surveillance and derogations for those medical devices which use magnetic resonance imaging.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the report establishing a long-term plan for cod stocks and the fisheries exploiting those stocks because it is necessary, through the adoption of a new plan, to fill in the gaps in the old stock recovery plan which did not meet expectations. it is desirable that the council should decide annually on the allowable catches for cod stocks in the areas concerned, ensuring maximum sustainable yield and the fishing mortality rate should be reduced over time to minimum levels. the new regulation will have to introduce a new fisheries management system by setting maximum levels to be managed by the member states, which will have to ensure that they are not exceeded and will have to allow landings of more than two tonnes of cod only in certain ports, establishing appropriate control procedures and recording the quantities landed. i believe it is essential that a plan which involves the stakeholders in the sector is more likely to succeed, but periodic evaluations will be appropriate to allow intervention to correct any shortcomings.

madam president, ladies and gentlemen, by voting this interim report on organised crime, the european parliament has taken a very important step: for the first time, it is recognised that the phenomenon of large-scale organised crime must be tackled with a coordinated strategy, at least at european level. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. the proposals in this report, starting with the establishment of a single european office to combat organised crime, are therefore moving in the right direction, which is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − i abstained in voting on this report because, although there are some good ideas like the one on the need to establish the figure of the european public prosecutor, which i very much endorse, it is too vague and predictable. in particular, this text seems to ignore the existence of the united nations convention against transnational organized crime, which was approved in palermo by 124 countries in december 2000 and has been fully operational since 2003. this was the first global treaty against organised crime and it has, as main points, the seizure of assets of illicit origin and the abolition of banking secrecy for criminal investigation. any serious text on organised crime approved by this parliament should take this convention as a basis and go beyond it, not just repeat its concepts in a different order.
