madam president, ladies and gentlemen, a growing number of people in europe are applying for social housing, including people with average incomes. the crisis has changed the socio-family profiles of applicants due to the increase in poverty in all member states. housing is a basic necessity and a right that cannot be denied: the continuing economic and social crisis has shown that the market alone is not able to meet the demand for affordable housing, particularly in urban areas with high housing density. the cuts in housing subsidies and the taxation of social housing companies have made the situation worse. it is urgent that the european commission should define a framework for action on social housing, giving member states the possibility of using the structural funds, both for new public housing and for protecting existing housing.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, social housing has always been - when used properly - an extraordinary and valuable tool for promoting access to housing for the weakest sections of society. in this period, one of the most difficult since the war, because of the economic and social crisis we all know, it has proved to be a valuable and indispensable instrument. indeed, it is only through a careful and determined use of public resources that it is possible to introduce housing policies for millions of people in families who otherwise could never have a decent home. that is why i voted in favour of this report with conviction, and it is crucial that the european union develops strong action, including the use of the structural funds, which can provide the impetus for a modern social housing policy that can provide a response to millions of people.
in writing. - i did not support the delli report on social housing in the european union, as i do not agree with many aspects of the text. it focuses heavily on green building but does not provide data to support the actual benefits that would result, nor does it mention the preservation of the historical value and cultural identity of historic centres that risk being completely distorted by the overuse of social housing as proposed. finally, there is a desire in several places to put immigrants at the centre of the member states' policies on social housing, which i cannot share, especially at this time of crisis which is affecting many citizens and families in venice, italy and europe in the first place.
in writing. - i have decided to abstain from voting on this own-initiative report. i agree with the importance of recognising the right to decent and affordable housing for the weakest sections of society, which are no longer just the marginalised or homeless communities but, as a result of the economic crisis and the increasing ageing of the population, also the elderly and the young. in fact, 25 million people in europe are in social housing and this figure is expected to increase. the commission has also proposed that the member states should be able to grant aid to the construction of new buildings in the event of a major accident or disaster. it would also help to mitigate the magnitude of housing cycles and housing bubbles that destabilise economies. although i agree with these points, i chose to abstain because i do not agree with some of the proposed measures which, in my view, would violate the principle of subsidiarity. this is particularly the case with the euro plus pact, which is intended to strengthen the economic and budgetary governance of the union and which also includes investment in social housing; the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a directive on the protection of the environment in the event of a fire.
in writing. - i thank the rapporteur, mrs delli, for addressing the shortcomings of the current european system. the issue of public housing is complex and involves many citizens. according to figures, 25 million european citizens live in public housing. recent studies also show that 17.86% of the european population lives in inadequate, overcrowded housing (with considerable differences between member states). due to the current economic crisis, demand for public housing is increasing. more and more middle-class families are having difficulty accessing the housing market. i believe that more decisive european action can bring a number of benefits, such as fighting property speculation and re-valuing buildings to meet higher energy efficiency requirements. in this respect, the banking system can play a key role in supporting the housing market. not only building owners but all european citizens could benefit from this.
in writing. - today, in plenary, we approved the report by mrs delli on the social housing sector in the european union. we believe it is our duty to find a practical solution to fill the gaps in the housing market. in fact, in order to meet the entire housing need and to ensure access to decent housing at affordable prices for all, we believe that it is necessary for the member states to ensure that a parallel supply of social housing is defined and organised to supplement what is already naturally available on the market. there are currently about 25 million european citizens living in social housing; more than 100 million are poor or at risk. on the economic side, investing in social housing also means helping the construction sector, which has been badly hit by the crisis, and the restructuring sector, particularly in the renewal of heating systems and renewable energy, which are high-yielding sectors and a breeding ground for jobs. we have therefore come to the conclusion that investment in social housing must, from now on, be given greater consideration in the macroeconomic and budgetary surveillance system of the european union.
in writing. - the delli report has the great merit of defining concretely the value of housing as a fundamental right, and of making this approach the basis for a european economic and social policy which supports its protection and ensures its realization. i voted in favour of the report because i consider that recognition necessary today to introduce the 'home' as one of the priorities of the 2020 strategy. however, i believe that it is necessary to respect the limits imposed by subsidiarity and not to invade a field which has historically been assigned to the powers of those who govern the territories and who therefore know the needs and difficulties of the citizens very well. it would be extremely difficult to impose a common european framework, which would be unfair and far removed from the real needs of those in difficulty.
in writing. when people know what the possibility of benefiting from social housing is, they understand its importance and perceive its necessity more easily. i voted for this resolution because for me social housing is not only an advance of the welfare state but also a necessity to achieve social inclusion. indeed, what better way to help the most vulnerable among us to stabilise their situation than with the social housing system. social housing is a valuable aid for citizens as it provides a solid basis for job search and provides a secure home for retired people. that is why i voted in favour of this text.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution because it recognizes the dramatic nature of the situation today: the problem of housing shortages, the difficulty of many households in paying their first mortgage, the difficulty for young people and all the other weaker groups, such as the elderly, the disabled, immigrants, separated parents, to have their right to housing recognised. promoting the social and economic role of social housing, moving forward with a european agenda for social housing, encouraging investment for local employment and the green economy, fighting poverty and promoting social inclusion and cohesion: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to the full.
in writing. − this own-initiative report calls for the community institutions and member state governments to step up their efforts to promote quality social housing that is easily accessible to the most disadvantaged social groups. in this sense, the document repeatedly points to roma and immigrants as a category to be given preference in the allocation of social housing. the rapporteur then includes in her strategy for social housing a series of objectives linked to energy efficiency. the traditional aims of the political group to which the rapporteur belongs, namely the greens, emerge here. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. the report is sufficiently critical to be rejected. it should be noted that it also makes no mention of the need to protect the historical value of urban centres, in particular by avoiding that the promotion of social housing deprives them of their cultural identity.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on low-cost housing in the eu because i believe that europe today must allocate more funds to prevent families below the poverty line and families close to it from being left homeless and in conditions of severe social hardship because of the severe crisis. today, there are many citizens of the union who live in social housing and the demands are unfortunately increasing. governments will have to commit themselves to not reducing the number of housing units and to making them affordable, especially for the most deprived, by combating discrimination and favouritism in allocations and by ensuring fair distribution systems at affordable prices. moreover, they will have to make the best use of resources so as to reduce the worrying and growing number of homeless people. europe, through the allocation of structural funds, should seek to stimulate investment in order to ensure greater accessibility to housing and to encourage the recovery of the construction and renovation sector, thus creating employment, avoiding dilapidated housing and aiming at the renewal of facilities in order to reduce energy waste, reducing consumption for households and environmental pollution.
in writing. − over a million job vacancies registered in the eu remain vacant because where they exist, there are no suitable candidates and too few people are travelling to work. it has been found that only 2% of eu citizens live in an eu country other than their own. this is of course worse for women alone and with the economic crisis the prospects are not much better. several factors contribute to these disparities: the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat the gender pay gap, gender segregation in the labour market, inadequate work-life balance measures, to name a few. yet the right to reside and work in another eu country is one of the fundamental freedoms of the union and a key instrument for creating a strong sense of european citizenship. it is therefore necessary to ensure that the role of girls and women is given special attention in the new programming for 2014-2020 and in the new programmes for mobility, both work and study.
in writing. − in the coming years, europe faces major challenges in making the labour market more open and accessible. one objective is that of occupational mobility, which highlights the need to adapt education/training systems better to the new requirements of the labour market. the still too low level of mobility of workers between member states shows that the benefits of the internal market are not yet fully exploited. there are still too many obstacles to mobility, including the lack of knowledge of foreign languages, the lack of favourable conditions for reconciling family and working life and the lack of updating of national social security legislation. it is therefore essential to ensure that the mix of learning opportunities responds to the need to ensure both employability and adaptability of workers throughout their working lives, thereby increasing their capacity for occupational mobility. in this context, it is essential that an increasing number of citizens achieve the highest possible level of education; this is particularly important for women who are temporarily out of the labour market - for maternity or family reasons - and for whom a good level of education is essential for their reintegration into the labour market.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i fully share the rapporteur's approach and her identification of the main problems. although the internal market commission, of which i am a member, has not been asked to give its opinion, i believe that the implications of the issues facing the eu as a whole are enormous. higher qualifications and greater mobility mean increased efficiency, increased adaptability, better ability to re-enter the labour market after temporary interruptions due to maternity or other family choices. europe, at this moment, needs to hit all the pockets of inefficiency and to extract its potential to resume growth and create jobs and wealth. i congratulate the rapporteur.
in writing. - the european parliament has once again shown itself to be at the forefront of defending the interests of citizens. it is clear that there are still too many obstacles in europe for women who want to move to another country for work. the promotion of flexible working hours, the mutual recognition of diplomas and professional qualifications, the improvement of childcare facilities and family services are very concrete actions that can help women workers in a difficult choice. europe must continue to work to promote the right of free movement of workers.
in writing. - today we have approved the report by mrs ronzulli on the objectives which the member states must set themselves in the coming years to make the labour market more open and accessible. we believe that first of all we must try to adapt education and training systems to the new requirements of the labour market, by strengthening lifelong learning and the acquisition of skills and by improving the systems for the recognition of professional qualifications. moreover, the level of mobility between member states is still too low, and the benefits of the internal market are not fully exploited. we also believe it is essential to address the linguistic gaps of citizens by providing learning opportunities and to ensure the employability and adaptability of workers throughout their working lives by promoting reconciliation with family life. it is clear that these objectives require a shared responsibility between governments, public authorities, employers, social partners and individual citizens; it is therefore essential that more and more people achieve the highest possible level of education, which is of crucial importance especially for women who, having temporarily left the labour force for maternity or family reasons, have greater difficulty in re-entering the world of work.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mrs ronzulli's report because the revival of women's employment requires the full realisation of the right of free movement and actions to promote professional mobility are vital to make the labour market more open and accessible and hopefully achieve the europe 2020 strategy target of integrating 75% of men and women (aged 20-64) into the world of work. the suggestions listed in the report propose awareness raising measures on the situation of women belonging to different age groups in education, integration, migration, employment, social protection and equal pay. the emphasis is also on ensuring safe working conditions and gender rights during mobility phases, and offering suitable services to women who often follow their husbands or partners to another member state, such as vocational courses, language courses and courses to facilitate integration into their new social and cultural environment, ensuring attention to the situation of women with disabilities and vulnerable groups, promoting entrepreneurship and offering clear rules to women to facilitate their access to company management.
in writing. − this own-initiative report serves to keep the focus on the situation of women in the world of work, with particular reference also to occupational mobility. the gender pay gap is still too wide and it is undeniable that women may face greater difficulties in their working careers, even if it is simply a 'biological' issue linked to the maternity period. but this cannot justify different treatment in the workplace and women should have the same opportunities as their male colleagues. women often give up on professional mobility or on any change of job because they are constrained by too many constraints, which should be eliminated or at least mitigated, as this report rightly suggests. finally, i find it positive that reference is made to the particular situation of many women who work in social services and professions, such as caring for the elderly or disabled: the commission has already proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos.
in writing. as vice-chair of the parliamentary committee on women's rights and gender equality, i am very pleased that a report from the european parliament once again explains how women's work can benefit the economy of the european union; as my report on the impact of the crisis on women's work demonstrated a few months ago. women, like men, have always been ready to be fully integrated economic agents, who must be able to benefit from equal opportunities, training and occupational mobility. this report highlights this and that is why i support it with the greatest gratitude.
in writing. − europe faces major challenges in the coming years to make the labour market increasingly open and accessible. the first is the objective of vocational mobility, which highlights the need to adapt education and training systems better to the new requirements of the labour market, to enhance lifelong learning and the acquisition of skills. secondly, the still too low level of labour mobility between member states shows that the benefits of the internal market are not being fully exploited. there are too many obstacles to mobility, including the lack of knowledge of foreign languages, the lack of conditions for reconciling family and working life and the lack of updating of national social security legislation. the first objective of the europe 2020 strategy is to raise the employment rate for people aged 20 to 64 to 75%. it is not a question of "pink quotas" in the companies: if we can implement a sound policy of gender equality, women will be able to enjoy their rights without any preferential or welfare channels. better education leads to higher employment rates and would contribute to more female employment. the broader positive effects on growth can only be achieved by stimulating investment in human capital and female productivity.
in writing. - the fight against unemployment starts with the creation of jobs and the long-term vision of the programmes that are defined. in this context, the concept of mobility must be included, which will be increasingly indispensable for the search for employment based on personal preparation and flexibility. the report on the educational and professional mobility of women in the european union, for which i have given my favourable opinion, shows that the importance of education is at the heart of the new concept of professional mobility. a higher level of education, particularly for women, but more generally for all of us and especially for young people, broadens the horizon which still too often limits the lives and therefore the professional activities of european citizens to their own territory, to their own family, without being able to seize those opportunities which improve the quality of life and which can create a more solid basis for the future.
in writing. - i supported this report because i support the need to implement measures to support women's educational and vocational mobility, with the ultimate aim of boosting women's employment. in view of the delicate situation at the moment and the fact that women are more exposed to social risks, i believe that action is urgently needed without further delay. the report provides concrete tools for greater dynamism in education and employment, which in turn allows for the promotion of gender equality. the family is the basis of society, but it often imposes obstacles to women's professional mobility: changing jobs, and countries, is a much more delicate and difficult choice for a woman than for a man. this is why the public social protection system must be made more efficient and the organization of working time must be changed if women so request, but also the contractual conditions must be made more appropriate. this report also pays particular attention to those who are disadvantaged. women represent an extraordinary human capital and the necessary investments must be made to improve their education and, consequently, the level and quality of employment: and only then can we make the most of their potential and their talents.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by my colleague on the educational and professional mobility of women in the eu because i consider it important to identify the necessary instruments that can help to open up the european labour market and make it more accessible to women in the eu countries. europe will have to ensure that the issue of work is placed at the centre of community strategies and will have to commit itself to strengthening the systems that can safeguard it, promoting the tools needed to overcome the difficulties encountered by those seeking employment in other countries of the union. action by the member states to ensure a higher level of education, promoting foreign languages and thus giving citizens greater opportunities for integration beyond national borders, would be crucial. i also think it is very important to give women guarantees at european level of job security when they are forced to leave the labour market for short periods because of maternity and to look after their families. it will therefore be important to promote female employment so that women do not feel excluded from the labour market for natural reasons which safeguard the important values of life and the family, and europe will therefore have to have among its objectives the raising of the female employment rate.
in writing. - i did not intend to vote in favour of the higgins report on the toll road and a stamp system for private light vehicles in europe. i believe that this system would only satisfy the interests and demands of large-scale industry, and that the entry of these 'suppliers' into the tolling industry would lead to additional costs that would be passed directly on to consumers.
in writing. − the electronic toll service facilitates the movement of vehicles for the transport of goods and people, reducing congestion on european roads and improving the impact on the environment. i believe that important steps still have to be taken before it can become a practical and, above all, positive reality. i agree that a study of the financial aspects of the set system is necessary, as is an improvement of the transport networks through project financing in order to speed up the implementation of the set system. the increased use of online payments is useful to provide greater price transparency and convenience for users not resident in the member state where the toll is charged. i am voting in favour of this proposal and hope that the commission will make a greater effort to make the sept a reality.
in writing. − mobility in europe goes hand in hand with the infrastructures made available to citizens. before a tether toll service and a tolling system for private light vehicles can be set up, a close comparison between the parties involved is necessary. it is important to understand how to create a platform for comparison between the two main stakeholders, which are the toll collectors and the suppliers of set, and the third stakeholder, which is the transport companies and the private motorists.
in writing. - today in the plenary we heard and welcomed mr higgings' ideas on a new toll service and a stamp system for private light vehicles in europe. we agree that the set (european tele-mail system) has not been a success so far; it is therefore necessary for the european commission to engage in dialogue with the member states in order to highlight the advantages of a single system at european level, identifying the aspects which are actually operational. we believe that the adoption of a regulation is the only way to achieve a concrete result in this ambitious project. we are convinced that the use of online payment systems is a priority to ensure price transparency and also a certain level of convenience, especially for users who do not reside in the eu country where the toll is charged. the use of tolls should also be encouraged as the tolling system or time-based charging systems do not reflect actual road use and therefore do not reflect the 'user pays' principle.
in writing. the idea of creating a european telepayment system, a kind of telepass for the whole continent, would have many advantages in itself, especially in terms of convenience for travellers who frequently move between countries in the union with their own vehicle. in italy the system works, and has low costs compared to traditional tolling: however, there are still many motorists who, for various reasons, prefer traditional payment systems, which often generate queues and long waiting periods, especially during periods of increased highway traffic congestion. there are, however, a few points which puzzle me about this proposal from the european commission: first, the possibility that tolls for motorists may increase due to higher operating costs is not excluded but mentioned. i would also not like to see behind this initiative, even if only very subtly, some big european giant ready to supply its technology and to get its hands on this sector, in such a way as to condition this market to its liking. the improvements should be made to make it easier for european citizens to save money, for example on the model of telephone roaming, which has fortunately been steadily declining for some years.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i must say that some doubts arise when reading this series of compromises that have been made on the right of asylum, because it is certainly true that we must protect people who are in difficulty and who come from wars and we must absolutely help them. it is also true that we must be careful, and eurodac is certainly going in the right direction in this respect, because we do not know who is behind it, whether it is human trafficking or terrorism. but there's something else i want you to think about. i've heard of rights, rights, it's certainly right, but we're sure we'll be able to meet these commitments that we make or make a series of nice words that then serve absolutely nothing. because to say that people have to work in europe when they come from other countries is certainly right if they can, but we don't have jobs for europeans right now! it is certainly right to say that the state must help them, but we are having a hard time helping the citizens of europe and above all i cannot understand why there will be this very strong pressure, especially on the countries of southern europe which are already experiencing a very serious economic crisis and therefore will have to shoulder the burden of refugees in addition to this economic crisis.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, like you, i am fighting every day for respect for the individual and for the protection of the most vulnerable, and this means, in the case of asylum seekers, protecting those who are unjustly persecuted by totalitarian regimes in their country of origin. but in the face of the economic crisis and terrorism, european citizens have also become vulnerable: their fundamental rights such as security or access to a decent job are no longer guaranteed. in italy we have three million unemployed; in veneto, my region, 170,000; in europe, 26 million people are unemployed. before making grand and demagogic declarations of intent, such as providing asylum seekers with a job in six months, and before considering the abolition of the crime of hiding as minister kyenge would like in italy, we have a duty to act to protect the interests of our people, who cannot be treated as citizens or b-list persons. we must think first of the millions of unemployed young europeans who are out of work, we must help the unemployed italians, not set up absurd principles that solve nothing.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, someone in this debate has said that the work is unfinished: it is true, but it is a very important symbolic work on the road to european integration. complete integration means no internal borders, only one external border. the problems are of course extremely complex, because it is a question of finding a balance between apparently contradictory values, safety on the one hand, and welcoming on the other. i therefore find it symbolically very important that in this extremely complex and long work we start to reflect on the kindergarten, that is, on the institution that speaks of reception, that speaks of human dignity. what we have done is of course imperfect, but it shows what the heart of europe is: the reception. in fact, in the measures we are about to discuss, we can see that a special attention is being paid to the most vulnerable people, even in the most difficult moments when we have to talk about detention, that is, the impeding of freedom, a special attention being paid to the establishment of minimum measures concerning minors. i think this is an aspect which points in the direction of a much more developed approach, but it is significant because at a time when codecision is being applied and in a field which was not previously linked to european integration, it is also based on the view of article 2 of the lisbon treaty, which states that human dignity is the foundation of europe.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to thank you for your report. there is no doubt that the package containing four dossiers on the common asylum system, with a series of measures to simplify the procedure, protecting the rights of those who have been punished in their territory of origin, as well as unaccompanied minors and vulnerable groups, should be welcomed. the same is true of the eurodac system, which is designed to combat organised crime with increasing severity, the rejection of the intergovernmental method and the approval of the community method, as well as the alert system. there is no doubt, however, mr president, that there are some questions which seem to be unresolved in this matter. the dublin mechanism in particular remains firm in its choice of being the first country of contact, which has to follow all the procedures and bear a great deal of responsibility. we are faced with a choice which again shows a very strong limitation of the european union in relation to that competition of solidarity and responsibility which we ask of the member states as we ask of the commission and the council. a concrete, authoritative and decisive european programme cannot fail to take account of the fact that in some areas the pressure of migration is formidable, and if we want to say no to a europe of the south as opposed to that of the north, we must take account of the fact that the system of burden sharing is not respected in the dublin programme, which is fully confirmed in this respect. that is why we are very concerned about a package which has many good things but some bad things, and particularly about the denial of burden sharing.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, just this sunday in switzerland a referendum was voted by a very large majority to maintain stricter rules on asylum applications and granting of asylum. swiss citizens have rights which unfortunately we europeans do not have. it would be interesting to have the decisions taken in brussels put to a referendum. we would probably realize how far europe is from its citizens. a europe that pretends to be a continent of unity and solidarity, but which, at the first sign of difficulties, leaves one country alone to deal with its emergencies: this is what happened with italy and the refugees fleeing the war in libya. a war that we didn't even want to start, but our french neighbours; the same neighbours who then closed the ventimiglia crossing, leaving italy to shoulder the entire responsibility for the reception. let us not even talk about germany, which is still criticizing us after two years and has done absolutely nothing. this europe is a petty one and if the citizens could speak out they would make that clear.
on behalf of the efd group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i must say that we are concerned about the schengen agreement, because we are facing a very difficult situation in our countries and i cannot understand why we cannot re-establish border controls when there are large migratory flows and this too seems to be an emergency. it is certainly a situation that has sometimes been realized. i read that in an emergency you can have border controls, the emergency can be quantified over a certain period of months, if it is two months, six months and maybe longer, what do you do? he's acting like nothing happened! unfortunately, we have to take into account that this directive must also be applied to those countries which have economic and social uniformity, because unfortunately there are not uncommon cases of people who perhaps go to other countries just to try to exploit the welfare state. unfortunately, europe is not only made up of good citizens, it is also made up of people who may not have good intentions and, as far as crime is concerned, it is much more difficult to combat crime if there are no adequate border controls. and just think that in my country, for example, in veneto, there have sometimes been attempts to repatriate people, members of the community, because they behaved badly, because they may have committed crimes, but after a while they returned safely. and we think that schengen, free movement is all right, but only if there is a counterbalance, if people can be returned and if border checks can actually be carried out.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, let me first of all thank our rapporteurs, mr coelho and mr weber, who have worked diligently to achieve the result we are discussing today. we welcome first of all the evaluation and monitoring mechanism in which the european commission, together with the member states and the agencies, plays a leading role, but also the ability to understand that something had to be changed: i am talking about the reintroduction of internal border controls in cases of exceptional circumstances. it is not a question of abandoning the principle of free movement of persons, which is one of the foundations of our union, but of adapting it to a series of needs which have emerged over time. we have also experienced moments of tension between some of our member states - difficult moments such as those following the so-called arab spring for example - and it was appropriate to intervene and regulate because there are still too many differences between our societies and where unilateral and sudden choices can really put the very reasons for our being together in crisis. but to see all our citizens now able to move freely between our countries, without police, without showing documents, is a source of pride and a proof that our union lives and grows with the passing of the years. because some of you, perhaps some of the visitors who are listening to this debate from the stands, are wondering whether we really want to inexplicably go back to a world that no longer exists, and we don't want that.
mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i would first of all like to express my sincere congratulations to mrs mccarthy and mr lehne on the work they have done and the high quality of the result. it is superfluous to stress the difficulties which have accompanied two dossiers of such importance and relevance to experts in the sector and to businesses in general. on the one hand, we are creating a single legislative act for european accounting legislation; on the other hand, we are creating a single legislative act for the european accounting legislation. the commission has already taken a number of initiatives to improve the transparency of information on regulated markets. the compromise reached in the accounting directive, in particular on the creation of a specific regime for small enterprises and on exemptions from certain obligations for micro entities, is acceptable. these are provisions which are a practical way of reducing the administrative burden on small and mediumsized enterprises and give tangible effect to the principle of 'thinking small first' in european legislation. as regards the so-called 'country-by-country' information, i support the compromise reached which limits the obligation to indicate payments to the various third countries to the extractive and deforestation sectors, which unfortunately are more prone to unfair or corrupt trading practices. i also welcome the agreement on the exemption and the important legal alignment of the two texts on this matter. the subject and the country-by-country information will certainly continue to be discussed in the coming months, especially in the light of the conclusions of the european council of 22 may. i believe, however, that the directives we are about to adopt have made a major step in the right direction.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i too believe that the outcome of this debate is very important, and the two rapporteurs must first of all acknowledge this. i would like to stress one specific point, which is that the extractive and forestry industries report all their payments to governments. this will enable communities where these activities are robust to be able to claim that these payments translate into actions for development and growth. i would like to say something specific to the commissioner about the hypothetical new transparency laws for businesses. i think it's a very important subject to develop, to finally make available, but i don't think that's the context in which to try to introduce the subject. as you said earlier, i think that in completing the discussion on corporate social responsibility, all non-direct economic information should also include this point. it would be a matter of strengthening measures already decided by parliament and, in any case, of making them consistent.
on behalf of the efd group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, competition is certainly necessary to develop the market's full potential: if agreements or cartels are created to distort this principle, the whole economy is affected, not just the final consumer. i would like to mention only two examples, which are particularly significant for italy: the first concerns an apparent agreement between oil producers and distributors to keep pump prices artificially high. there is also a judicial inquiry into this and i thank commissioner almunia for taking an interest in the matter. another striking example concerns the motor insurance sector: although the number of claims is steadily decreasing, the cost of policies continues to rise and has reached levels that are now unsustainable. we have reached the paradox that the insurance of a moped can cost even more than the moped itself and this is absurd! a scooter that has the same price for sale in italy or germany, but can have an annual insurance price from us that is up to 10 times higher than the german insurance market. the whole two-wheeler industry is suffering from this madness, with italy being the main european producer. historic companies such as piaggio di pontedera are in crisis for this reason too and europe cannot remain insensitive and immune to all this.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the excellent work of mr sanchez presedo allows us to emphasize once again - and this is never unnecessary - the value of competition in defining the social economy of the european market. it is also significant that we have managed to define as a guideline for future activity that the commission's action must not be aimed at strengthening the existing one, but at encouraging the increase of subjects, of actors, and at bringing out new ideas and techniques so that competition is real. but i wanted to draw the commissioner's attention to two specific issues, which he mentioned in his introduction: the first concerns the need, in my view, to draw up european legislation on collective redress. we cannot have a legislative structure like the present one which deprives consumers of the possibility of coming together to demand that their rights be respected, that they be compensated. because the issue of compensation and the other aspect has its own urgency: we are faced today with a contradiction that may seem absurd. if there is a breach, there is a fine for that breach which is paid by the member states, while there is no provision for consumers to be compensated either. these consumers are penalized twice: on the one hand, because they do not receive compensation and, on the other hand, because they pay through the state as taxpayers for the damage caused by others. i believe that for this reason, the two issues should ....... in writing. the competition policy instruments defined by the treaty of rome, antitrust, state aid and merger control, help to maintain fair conditions and an open and dynamic market. the european social market economy would be unthinkable without competition. it allows for proper pricing and efficient allocation and use of resources. during 2011, the intensification of tensions in sovereign debt markets, concerns in the banking sector, and severe economic uncertainty in a context of high oil prices and slowing global output growth contributed to a sharp loss of confidence and a consequent contraction in output. in my view, competition has proved to be a necessary tool in responding to the crisis: the commission has also taken steps to ensure that the financial sector is able to compete effectively in the global marketplace. for competition policy to be successful, i believe that parliament must be more involved in its formulation, that the commission must be adequately resourced and that the involvement of stakeholders and civil society must be increased.
i would like to say very clearly and emphatically that parliament cannot accept that the cut in direct payments is based on the conclusions of the european council of 7 and 8 february: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament. we find it unacceptable that the institution with the utmost democratic legitimacy should be circumvented in order to penalise european farmers in such an inconsistent way. pending an agreement, the cut in direct payments should be based on the ceiling for 2014 indicated by the commission in its proposal for the multiannual financial framework, which is consistent with the negotiating mandate approved by this plenary on the direct payments regulation. the commission's proposal is to be submitted to the council for approval, and the council will be consulted on it. we do not think that is fair and reasonable, and that is why we think that farmers who receive aid up to eur 5 000 should be exempted.
the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect. it is unfortunate that we are even talking about this issue, because it is unfortunate that during the last year of planning we have not been able to give the farmers, the farms, the assurance that what we have promised will be fulfilled. this means that legal certainty is guaranteed over the seven years of the planning period. but, commissioner, you have made a proposal on how to cut back, and you have reaffirmed that here today. i think this is a small sign of support and encouragement for small farms. we're not talking about big numbers here. the european union average is 10 to 15 euros per hectare. i think that makes sense. if small businesses are to survive, we too must give political signals. and i think that's a small, humble sign. but it's a sign in the right direction. of course, it raises the question of the distribution among the member states. i am in complete agreement with mr jahr on this point, but perhaps this could have been solved differently by first fixing the allocations to the member states and then applying this reduction in the member states. that's not what happened. but overall i think your proposal is right and that we should exclude these smaller farms and not confront them again. and that's why i'm going to support your proposal.

in writing. - illegal fishing may be economically attractive: in fact, fish caught in disregard of environmental, social and other standards can normally be sold by fishermen at a lower price. wholesale and retail traders buy the fish at a lower price, although they may not know that it was caught illegally. the european union's illegal fishing regulation is therefore only useful if it is fully applied: this is why action is needed to prevent the rules from being circumvented or cheated and to put an end to one of the most serious threats to marine biodiversity, which can cause food security problems in many coastal and developing countries.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, today's vote has adopted the structure of the common european asylum system, an important and innovative step in relation to the community structures of the individual member states. the scale of the asylum phenomenon makes it imperative to have a common management system for the handling of applications and applicants, which in 2012 amounted to over 330,000, to ensure equal treatment at all points of entry into the european union. if the sting of the return directive is removed, parliament could do better by standing up to be the cradle of human rights at the universal level. our colleague hidalgo is right when he says that we have taken a step towards peace and freedom.
in writing. − the amendments concern in particular the guarantees for asylum seekers in detention, the conditions of reception in detention centres, the time limits for access to the labour market, the level of health care provided to persons with special reception needs and the mechanisms for identifying those needs, access to material support and, finally, also information requirements to ensure better monitoring of the basic provisions of the directive. while access to employment could prevent asylum seekers from being excluded from the host society and promote self-sufficiency, it is clear that this provision has an impact on the extremely precarious socioeconomic situation in the countries of arrival of asylum seekers. do you want to ignore this harsh reality?
in writing. - all eu countries are bound by the dublin regulation. the application of this regulation has the consequence that some countries, including italy, have to deal with a number of asylum applications that exceeds their capacity. italy, malta and greece are the most popular 'first-arrival' countries for asylum seekers arriving by sea. i therefore think it is appropriate to introduce a safeguard clause in the regulation for the 'first arrival' countries which are most severely punished, in order to guarantee greater security to the host countries as well. in fact, in italy alone in 2012, 22,160 decisions were made, of which 8,260 people were granted some form of protection, while the remaining 13,900 asylum seekers were denied. what are the criteria for making such decisions? the inevitable bureaucratic red tape of country-to-country transfers creates even more confusion by keeping good people out of eu countries at the expense of dangerous people. the failure of eu countries to revise the solidarity clause of the regulation in a 'burden sharing' perspective demonstrates the lack, if not the absence, of solidarity between states which should be the precondition for the creation of a truly common european system.
in writing. the proposal aims to amend the safeguards for asylum seekers in reception centres. it also seeks to improve access to employment and the level of medical care. it is emphasized that facilitating the employment of foreigners has positive effects not only for the latter but also for the host state. the reasons for detaining a person are outlined and it is stated that no one can be detained for the sole reason of seeking international protection. furthermore, restrictions on movement may not be imposed. i therefore vote against the report.

" we are in the middle of a crisis, the worst the continent has ever been through, and the data is constantly being updated: the number of people in dire need is increasing day by day, and the figures are really impressive, because if in 2010 it was 8.7% of the percentage of people who were not able, in europe, gentlemen, to eat noble proteins at least once every two days, the latest figures tell us that these numbers are growing impressively; so the 4 million homeless are no longer 4 million, but many more! think of the tens of millions of children who are most at risk and who will have permanent scars for the rest of their lives. i voted for the obligation, i think we must be able to give this money in practice as soon as possible to be close to our citizens.
in writing. - i did not support the costello report on the european fund for the poor because i believe that its purpose, namely to support the poor, can be more effectively achieved by the member states. the report calls for the community institutions to decide on the programmes to be implemented, by centralising management and increasing bureaucracy. i believe that such a governance of the funds would not only violate the principle of subsidiarity but would in fact distance the citizens in need from real and effective aid.
in writing. − in europe, many people live below the poverty line and a small percentage benefited from the european food aid for the poor programme in 2011. the european union also exists for these people, because they receive food from the eu and so they understand that the european union thinks of them. i think that the proposed fund is a very good help for the poor, although it will certainly not help all the people in economic difficulties, but it must be seen as an instrument which complements the others already existing in the fight against the most serious forms of poverty. i agree with the rapporteur that the rules governing this fund should be as simple as possible and should contribute as much as possible to the reduction of poverty and social exclusion without the administrative burden being placed on the beneficiaries. i believe that this fund is proof that europe is taking its responsibilities in relation to poverty and social exclusion and therefore i am voting in favour of this report.
in writing. - the programme for aid to the poor has allowed member states since 1987 to release surplus food stocks to distribute them as aid to the poor. the project will cease at the end of this year, due to the decrease in available resources. the proposal therefore aims to reintroduce the instrument for at least eur 2,5 billion in the 2014-2020 programming period. the critical aspects are related to the fact that the distribution of aid can be better met by the member states and that the intervention of the commission only ends up producing more bureaucracy, jeopardizing the principle of subsidiarity and discouraging those who would need it from applying. for these reasons, and given the sensitivity of the matter, i am voting against.
in writing. − 40 million european citizens live in conditions of food deprivation and extreme poverty. in 2011, more than 25 million european children were at risk of poverty and social exclusion, and of these, almost 6 million cannot afford new clothes. important figures, which i can only be impressed with as a mother, especially when it comes to children. in the face of such figures, we cannot stand by and watch. the new fund is a practical expression of the european union's solidarity with its most vulnerable citizens. this will be practical help for the disadvantaged sections of the population, with particular attention to the homeless and children. the european fund for the poor is a key instrument available to europe to alleviate the effects of the economic and social crisis. however, the amount of €2.5 million foreseen by the commission for the period 2014-2020 seems to me to be wholly insufficient to achieve the objectives set out in europe 2020. i am referring in particular to the commitment to reduce by at least 20 million the number of people at risk or in situations of poverty and marginalisation.
in writing. - considering that the economic and financial crisis is nevertheless exacerbating poverty and social exclusion across the union and agreeing with the rapporteur that the fund has the potential in general to play an important role in improving the lives of people on the margins of society, i voted in favour of the proposal.
in writing. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. the european commission and the member states, during the negotiations on the eu's long-term budget, had proposed a sharp reduction in the amount of money available, from the 3.5 billion allocated so far to 2.5 billion. parliament, through its resolution on the maintenance of the european fund for the poor, wanted to offer a significant instrument against the global crisis and of solidarity with the most vulnerable europeans. i believe that all europeans should be supported by the institutions and that the maintenance of the above-mentioned fund is an important achievement, especially in view of the current economic situation and the fight against poverty in europe.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this text because i think that the cut of one billion euro proposed by the european commission and the member states in the allocation of the european fund for the poor is inappropriate. the eur 3.5 billion at its disposal is vital for the almost 120 million european citizens at risk of poverty or social exclusion, of whom more than 40 million suffer from severe material deprivation and more than four million are homeless.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a new european fund for aid to the most deprived and i welcome the fact that the eur 3.5 billion for the next seven years will continue to be used to finance the canteens of humanitarian organisations to provide meals for europe's citizens in need. europe, despite the overall crisis which has led to cuts in appropriations for several sectors, has not cut social spending and in italy this appropriation will be used to finance over 15,000 canteens and many other associations providing food aid to families. the serious crisis situation is exacerbating poverty in all the countries of the union and the allocation of funds represents a concrete and tangible effort by the european institutions which have decided to support the most needy by trying to combat the phenomenon of the "new poor" also with the european social fund. europe must also commit itself to providing the best possible support to those most in need, with ever-increasing interventions, and must have the fight against poverty as one of its objectives, by considering actions to reduce the number of citizens at risk within the next few years.
in writing. the report on the proposal for a european parliament and council regulation on the european fund for aid to the most deprived (fead) was voted on today. i think that this report is an acceptable compromise which integrates the different views expressed within the empl committee and also takes account of the views of the agri, budg, cont, femm and regi committees. in a time of worsening economic crisis and an increase in the number of people at risk of poverty and social exclusion, this report proposes concrete solutions to help the poor in the union and to meet their most urgent needs.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the infiltration of terrorists and other members of criminal organizations into europe through the exploitation of the asylum system is a current problem with unforeseeable consequences. the possibility for the authorities designated by the member states and the european police office to request the comparison of the data from the fingerprinting equipment with those recorded in the eurodac database, for the purpose of combating terrorist offences and other serious crimes, represents a significant step forward compared to the previous proposal. i am convinced that the measures contained in the report will make it possible to prevent these situations and at the same time to supplement european security. the work done by the rapporteur is going in the right direction and that is why i have given you my support.
in writing. - i supported the macovei report on the establishment of the eurodac system for comparing fingerprints. eurodac will offer member states' authorities and europol (european police office) the possibility to consult its central fingerprint database for the purposes of preventing, detecting and investigating terrorist offences and other serious criminal offences. this system will make law enforcement more effective and will certainly make it easier to combat crime.
in writing. − the aim is to give the member states' law enforcement authorities and europol the possibility of consulting the eurodac central database for the prevention, detection and investigation of terrorist offences and other serious criminal offences. in addition to fingerprints, data transmitted by eu countries include: the eu country of origin; the person's gender; the place and date and application for asylum or the person's arrest; the identification number; the date on which the fingerprints were taken; the date on which the data were transmitted to the central unit. the report is aimed at the activity of organised crime networks in third countries in seeking to exploit the asylum system in an illicit manner in order to bring their members into the eu. according to europol, human traffickers also try to abuse the asylum system by submitting applications with false information about the country of origin. in view of the above, the report welcomes the possibility for the designated authorities of the member states and europol to request the comparison of fingerprint data with those recorded in the eurodac database for the purpose of combating terrorist offences and other serious criminal offences.
in writing. - this proposal should be read in the context of the recent datagate scandal, my commitment to data protection and the framework of the debate on refugees within which this legislation is situated. i must congratulate the rapporteur on her work, because the text that has been adopted, including my vote in favour, contains answers for those who fear abuse of access to data, as well as for investigators who need adequate and up-to-date tools to deal with the challenges of illegal immigration and the security needs of citizens. fingerprints are, pending technological developments which make the cost of the latest innovations (biometric printing) affordable, the only tool at our disposal to react to false declarations of identity and to quickly trace a suspect's file. it is good to regulate its use and, above all, to make it available to all member states in a system where it can circulate freely.
in writing. − the proliferation of terrorists and criminal organisations in europe through the abuse of the asylum system is a problem that should not be underestimated and has serious and unforeseeable consequences. the possibility for the authorities designated by the member states and the european police office to request the comparison of the data from the fingerprinting equipment with those recorded in the eurodac database, for the purpose of combating terrorist offences and other serious crimes, represents a major improvement on the previous proposal. the measures provided for in the text will make it possible to prevent such situations and at the same time to protect the safety of citizens. that is why i supported the report.
in writing. − the eurodac system gives all eu member states access to a fingerprint database, which allows to find out whether the asylum seeker has already applied elsewhere or has already entered the eu illegally. this applies to those over 14 years of age. as organised crime seeks to exploit asylum seekers to bring their 'true allies' into the eu and expand into the common market, eurodac is an important development in combating this phenomenon. i therefore vote in favour.
in writing. the 'eurodac' system, which allows the comparison of asylum seekers' fingerprints, is certainly a step forward. the system will allow national authorities to compare the fingerprints of those who have applied for international protection, checking whether the application has already been lodged in another member state or whether the applicant has entered the eu illegally in the past. in europe, there was a need to simplify existing procedures and allow member states to determine quickly who is responsible for examining an asylum application. it is equally important that legislation allows the database to be consulted for the prevention and investigation of terrorist offences.
in writing. - we have approved the new rules on asylum which establish common procedures for all member states. we believe that it is necessary to manage the applications and basic rights of asylum seekers arriving in the european union with a single legal system at european level. therefore, in order to overcome the differences between the existing national procedures in this field, we consider it a good rule to apply common deadlines for handling applications and to train the staff dealing with applicants more rigorously; in addition, it is essential that new rules are drawn up for the special needs of unaccompanied minors and other more vulnerable persons and categories. asylum seekers will also not be transferred to eu countries where there is a risk of inhuman or degrading treatment; in addition, an early warning mechanism will be introduced to deal with problems in national systems before they develop into full-blown crises with domestic or international repercussions. finally, we consider it important to provide that the police forces of the member states and europol may have access to the fingerprints of those entering, in order to combat better the ever-increasing risk of crime and terrorism in europe.
in writing. - having regard to the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the protection of individuals with regard to the processing of personal data by the community institutions and bodies and on the free movement of such data,
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by my colleague on the establishment of the eurodac system for comparing fingerprints because today we need ever more effective measures for the prevention, investigation and detection of crime, including terrorism, and we need ever more careful and coordinated management of asylum applications, which are also used by organised crime in an illicit way to allow their affiliates access to eu countries with the aim of manipulating them within our territory. it is essential to strengthen our defenses through a coordinated system setting rules aimed at creating common procedures for the handling of asylum applications and it is important to ensure that member states' authorities and europol have access to the eurodac database to carry out fingerprint checks in order to enable the identification of those seeking asylum and those who have been detained for irregular border crossings. the controls would make it possible to verify whether asylum seekers have already applied in other eu countries and whether they have entered the territory irregularly, which would undoubtedly represent an important step forward for the protection of our countries.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i believe that the reform of the schengen agreements has achieved an important milestone, because for the first time the community method prevails over the governmental method: this means that the commission will have more power to put the common interest of europe before the interests of individual states. it is not just a technical reform, it is much more important, because it emphasizes that borders are becoming more and more european and less and less a monopoly of individual states, and at a time like this when there is a very strong tendency to let national egoisms prevail, this choice goes against the trend, reinforces the idea of a united europe, without barriers within itself, which favours freedom of movement. it is a matter of great political importance, which is why i voted in favour.

in writing. - as regards the evaluation mechanism approved today, we believe that the right to free movement within the schengen area will be better guaranteed by reforming its governance. in future, inspectors who ensure compliance with these rules will be empowered to make unannounced visits to prevent illegal border checks by national internal border authorities. in the case of external border inspection, however, the member state concerned must be informed at least 24 hours in advance. the teams will also be composed of experts from the member states, the commission and the european union agencies. the schengen borders code (sbc), as amended by our vote today, makes clear that any reintroduction of internal border controls is an exception and can only be undertaken as a measure of last resort, for a limited period of time, on the basis of specific objective criteria and an evaluation monitored at eu level. we have also agreed that in the event of a serious threat to public policy or internal security, controls may be re-established for 30 days, which may be extended for a maximum of six months.

in writing. - the financial market is often mentioned as a problem in the current crisis. while it is true that certain superficial behaviour did trigger an explosion in the real economy, i believe that it was wrong behaviour in a functioning context, and not the other way around. i therefore believe that it is very important to restore confidence in operators who do their job well. it is in this spirit that i voted in favour of this report, which seeks to raise the standards of transparency for securities listed on regulated markets. i congratulate the rapporteur.
in writing. − the transparency directive 2004/109/ec requires that issuers of securities in the eu market ensure adequate levels of transparency by disclosing information to be shared with the eu market. the report considers the abolition of the quarterly publication requirement for small and medium-sized companies and the publication of information on shareholdings conferring voting rights - in order to avoid unclear escalations to corporate governance. mining companies are required to inform the public about payments made to national governments - publish what you pay initiative. i therefore vote in favour of the proposal.
in writing. - we have today welcomed the directive on the new transparency rules for large oil, gas, mining and forestry companies. the new legislation aims to make firms using strategic resources and governments granting them more accountable. the main objective is to harmonise european accounting standards and to reduce red tape. we therefore believe that the large companies in question should be obliged to disclose the details of their payments to governments for each extraction project. in order to ensure full transparency, the information must be detailed for each lease or licence obtained to access the resources. in addition, we have approved an anti-avoidance clause to ensure that companies cannot artificially divide or aggregate payments to avoid disclosure. payments of production rights, dividends, bonuses and taxes will be made public; in addition, payments for infrastructure improvements will be disclosed. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environment from harmful substances.

in writing. − the legal basis of the proposal refers to article 11 of the financial framework (regulation 73/2009), on direct payments, as amended by regulation (eu) no 671/2012. it is stated that if the sub-ceiling is exceeded in a given year, a cut in direct payments must be made before 31 march, so that expenditure is brought under the ceiling. the commission proposes that the amounts to be paid to farmers above eur 5000 be reduced by 4.9%, except in bulgaria, romania and croatia, which are gradually introducing direct payments. the critical points of the proposal are related to the fact that the cut is based on the sub-maximum of the european council of 7 and 8 february 2013 and that a crisis reserve of 2.8 billion is to be introduced - but the procedure to reach the next mff is still ongoing, parliament has not yet given its consent. i do not think it is right to accept a proposal which has not been amended accordingly, so i shall abstain.

in writing. − we welcomed the draft allocation of seats among the 28 countries of the european union, in view of the next elections in 2014. we agree with the report by mr gualtieri and mr trzaskowski, who propose that, for the next european elections to be held at the end of may 2014, 12 member states lose one seat and that no member state be allocated more seats, in order to be able to receive croatian meps. we therefore welcome the proposal, aware that a review of the agreement will be necessary before the 2019 elections, to be submitted by the end of 2016. the rapporteur himself admits that this is the least imperfect of the possible solutions, although it is certainly not the best. we believe, however, that it is essential that the principle of degressive proportionality be respected, whereby members from larger member states represent more citizens than those from smaller states. finally, it is important to stress that the agreement reflects all kinds of changes in the number of member states and demographic trends, in order to continue to respect the overall balance of the institutional system, as required by the european treaties in force.
