in writing. − the rapporteur has identified some key problems in the administration of the cohesion financial instruments and i therefore announce a favourable vote. i would particularly like to support the points made in paragraphs 7 and 13 to 15. the indication that the exclusive clauses referred to in article 107 (3) (c) tfeu have been exceeded is of the utmost importance. the experience of these difficult years of crisis has led to a comprehensive and radical revision of the rules governing access to funds, which were drawn up in conditions very different from those of today, when the current economic scenario was beyond the scope of reasonable forecasts. the impact of aid on different business models and on economic systems in different regions will require a reassessment of the way in which it is granted and access to it. finally, i agree with the negative assessment that parliament cannot operate under codecision today: given the political centrality of cohesion financial instruments in times of reduced credit to enterprises, it is essential that any initiative be backed by full democratic legitimacy, as a result of the orderly composition of divergent interests. to exclude parliament from this responsibility exposes the commission to political censure and risks fuelling anti-european demagogy based on the stereotype of technocracy.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on state aid in the belief that the matter should be approached carefully, simplifying procedures to ensure an effective contribution to local development policies. the procedures for the notification and approval of support measures must be set up in such a way that public investment can play a real role in driving the economy forward, especially in a period of economic crisis such as the one we are experiencing.
in writing. - i supported, by my vote in favour, this important own-initiative report which expresses assessments and proposals on regional policy in the context of wider state aid schemes. i share the need for better coordination between cohesion policy and state aid policy, which, although they have different premises, have common objectives, such as aid to the less developed regions, promotion of their development, support for areas where there is a lower standard of living or where unemployment is high. while cohesion policy is subject to the ordinary codecision procedure, the parliament has only an advisory role in the process of modernising state aid. this creates a major democratic deficit which should be overcome. the new rules which are to be drawn up must strike the right balance between the objective of improving the competitiveness of enterprises in order to strengthen the internal market and support for enterprises which have already been too much tried by the severe economic crisis. failure to provide any special safety net support to regions not covered by the regional aid maps exposes them to serious risks and, above all, makes it difficult to achieve the eu 2020 targets. i believe that this last point deserves the utmost attention from all the institutions.
in writing. - the report we have adopted is central to the future of europe. we cannot afford a two- or three-speed union, and this applies not only to more or less developed countries but also to the most backward regions of countries considered to be advanced: i am thinking, for example, of france, germany, spain and italy. for this reason too, the decision to leave it to the national and local levels, in accordance with the principle of subsidiarity, to decide which farms may or may not participate in aid is to be welcomed. i stress this point because there is a strong movement today to challenge the project of european integration, based primarily on the fact that very often the national communities - rightly or wrongly - feel deprived of decision-making power. we shall not be able to revive the european spirit as long as parliament is the cinderella of our union. we are talking about the only institutional body - i want to remind you - voted directly by the peoples of europe. the emphasis on small and medium-sized enterprises is welcome, as is the move towards simplifying state aid so that it can be more accessible.
in writing. − in the context of the revision of state aid legislation, an important chapter is that devoted to so-called regional aid, i.e. aid covering a restricted area compared to the entire national territory. however, it is precisely this dimension that is closest to the citizens and local authorities, and thus manages to get the best of the situation: i believe that the whole architecture and approach of europe should be reviewed on a regional or macro-regional basis, because the present states are too large and heterogeneous to deal adequately with many situations. i would like to stress a key point in this report, namely that the granting of state aid should be determined not only by the size of the firm or the sector in which it operates, but also by the estimate of the number of jobs that could be created and maintained by the granting of the incentives, the quality and sustainability of the jobs and projects concerned and the long-term effects on the development of the region, including social aspects. the full impact of a company on the territory in which it operates is too often not considered, which is why i very much appreciated the attention in the text to the risks of industrial relocation.
in writing. − the cohesion policy legislative package and the commission communication on the modernisation of state aid have the advantage of creating situations which limit the need for states and regions to respond to the crisis with public instruments and initiatives that can ensure growth. the draft guidelines published by the commission introduce new subjects, almost all of them restrictive and reductive. the court's judgment in leipzig/halle makes an important point which must be taken into account, but beyond the cohesion policy aspects there is the problem of development and the need to create jobs. on the one hand, the crisis and on the other, the austerity policies have caused a very serious recession from a social point of view, with an unbearable increase in unemployment and a loss of competitiveness in the productive world. the new state aid guidelines should therefore take this situation much more into account and should provide the flexibility to facilitate and promote growth and the need for new investment, especially when it is in infrastructure and job creation. without this focused concern, all the more complex and reductive aid rules are reduced to bureaucratic formulas without a social construct.
in writing. - the european parliament, by approving the text on regional policy in the context of wider state aid schemes, is coming to the rescue of small and medium-sized enterprises and local authorities in need as a result of the economic crisis. our vote is our voice to make the european commission understand how much our entrepreneurs need immediate financial instruments to cope with the crisis. state aid granted more broadly to local and regional authorities, although it falls within the competitive field of the commission's exclusive competence, is sometimes, but especially in the present situation, made indispensable by the existence of small economic operators.
in writing. - having regard to the three main objectives of the process, namely to ensure growth while strengthening the internal market, keeping it dynamic and competitive, to address state aid cases that distort the internal market and to streamline and speed up decisions on state aid procedures, and agreeing with the rapporteur, i voted in favour of the proposal.
in writing. - today we voted on an important report on regional state aid. state aid which, together with antitrust and merger control policies, constitute the three instruments of the european union's competition policy. what i want to stress, and what i find very clear in the report, is the need for competition policy to be defined with the interests of the citizens and the rights of european consumers as its main target. this means that it must facilitate the entry of new players into the market, encourage the emergence of new ideas and techniques, and strengthen the single market as a motor of economic growth. but it is also necessary to introduce a system of collective redress and alternative dispute resolution at community level. in conclusion, of course, i join the call for greater involvement of the european parliament, with its co-legislative powers, and of the interested parties and civil society in the definition of competition policy.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the annual report on competition policy. the very balanced text emphasises the decisive role of competition in the development of a market for citizens and businesses. the report strongly stresses the duty of banks to improve access to credit for households and businesses and calls on the commission to strengthen controls on credit rating agencies by defining new rules to ensure that cases of conflict of interest in competition matters are resolved.
in writing. - lessons must be drawn from the events of recent years, both to avoid ideological rigidity on the competition principle and to prevent the spread of exceptions and cases of protectionism. the rapporteur was right to point out that if the financial industry has been supported in the face of the risks of systemic collapse, it is time for the sector to fulfil its strategic vocation, which is to support real economies. in times of crisis, the incomplete state of the single market and the low level of competition in many countries and sectors are a major factor in the slowdown of economies, an incentive to market distortions and ultimately a threat to household living standards, resulting in price volatility, unjustified increases in private charges (from insurance to transport to communications), erosion of savings and crises of private savings. it can therefore be said that increased competition would also help to ease the social pressure on governments, which, with very limited margins, are faced with the need to revitalise the productive base and domestic consumption, without being able to use the instruments of quantitative easing. i therefore vote in favour.
in writing. - the report voted today makes it clear that the road to the completion of the internal market is still a long one. i voted in favour of the report because i believe it identifies the areas where action to promote greater competition is needed. i hope that the commission will continue along the path laid down by the two single market acts promoted by commissioner barnier.
in writing. − competition policy is and must remain a fundamental pillar and an ever clear objective on the horizon of strengthening european integration. we cannot ignore the fact that in times of crisis, in the face of the difficulties which have arisen, there is a risk of succumbing to the temptation to put this important policy on the back burner. it is therefore necessary to reaffirm its valuable added value also in order to help overcome the economic stalemate in which we find ourselves. it is undeniable that competition policy is a valuable ally in economic reconstruction: antitrust, state aid and merger control all have a direct impact on the drivers of productivity and competitiveness. i voted in favour of this own-initiative report from parliament which makes interesting suggestions for continuing action in this area and strengthening the culture of competition at european and world level.
in writing. − this is an assessment of competition policy in various sectors of the european economy. banks that have received state aid should focus on the healthier economic activities, ensuring access to credit for both households and smes. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' in the definition of a public authority. the proposal also aims to preserve public finances while safeguarding the rights of european citizens. competition must be ensured in the food, energy, media, tourism, payments and transport sectors. the report as a whole seems to me to deserve a vote in favour.
in writing. - i thank the committee on economic and monetary affairs (econ) for the work it has done on the report presented today. competition is one of the cornerstones on which the european union is built. it is sufficient to recall that in 1957 the treaties of rome devoted the whole of title vi to this subject. it is not easy to talk about competition in the current historical period of economic and financial difficulties. the economic crisis always carries the risk of a loss of confidence in market mechanisms and, therefore, of protectionist tendencies. in this context, competition policy can and must become a key instrument in responding to market fragmentation, as it has always done in the past, by helping member states to achieve maximum efficiency in the allocation of resources and, therefore, public intervention. an efficient market is one that fosters innovation and the emergence of new economic actors, implementing the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy and maximising the benefits for all european citizens. in this context, an increasingly close dialogue between the commission and the european parliament, which must be more closely involved in the formulation of competition policy, is essential.
in writing. - today, in the plenary session in strasbourg, we welcomed the report by mr sánchez presedo on the annual report on european union competition policy. the european social market economy would be unthinkable without healthy competition, so proper pricing and efficient allocation and use of resources are essential. we are also convinced that competition itself can bring about adequate social progress. we are fully aware that we are in the fifth year of the financial, economic and social crisis, but we believe that competition policy should not be put aside, but should be used as a tool to respond to the crisis itself, to maintain fair conditions and an open and dynamic market. we encourage free markets because we believe they are necessary to achieve the europe 2020 goals for smart, sustainable and inclusive growth. but in the light of the facts, we are convinced that greater legitimacy and greater effectiveness are needed to achieve the objectives we have set ourselves. it is therefore necessary to encourage the involvement of stakeholders and civil society in order to strengthen the culture of competition at european and global level, ensuring that the commission has adequate resources to achieve a good result.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, in turkey, the environmental protest has been joined by political protests against the erdogan government, which is gradually becoming less secular and more fundamentalist, as its recent decisions show. violent repression is not only morally reprehensible, it is also in breach of the european charter of fundamental rights, which is an important pillar of the lisbon treaty and guides our foreign and security policy (cfsp). any negotiations with turkey must take this into account. it must also be said that the experience of the arab spring has shown that the ferments of freedom and democracy carried forward by the young people in the squares have never been rewarded and the regimes born of those revolutions prove to be more anti-democratic and fundamentalist than those that were overthrown. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the turkish authorities are not forced to accept the new regime. i believe that turkey is a key partner for the west and that destabilising turkey in a highly unstable area could lead to a serious threat to security in the middle east.

the rapporteur. - mr president, mr high representative, ladies and gentlemen, the report which parliament is about to vote on is intended to make a constructive contribution to the revision of the eeas. it does so on the basis of an assessment of these first years of activity which identifies limitations and problems, but which at the same time recognises the considerable progress achieved in a few years. when we helped launch the service in 2010, we knew that the goal of integrating structures from the commission and the council, union and member state officials was a difficult and ambitious challenge. the parliament then abandoned its request to place the service within the commission in order to pursue the objective of a broad service, capable of going from the common security and defence policy to development policy and at the same time close to the commission and subject to adequate control by parliament. this objective was then achieved and we have created a service - i think i can say this - with more powers than the commission would have wanted, but closer to the commission than the council would have wanted and subject to more scrutiny by parliament than either would have wanted. this gives the union an extraordinary tool for achieving a truly comprehensive approach to foreign policy, that is to say, for promoting synergy between the different instruments at europe's disposal in its external action, which are consistent with a foreign policy philosophy that gives a predominant role to so-called 'soft power', that is to say, to consensus, democracy, human rights, the development of peoples, without at the same time giving up the military instruments of crisis management and the objective of building a common defence. the proposals we are presenting today are not intended to overturn the basic framework defined in 2010 but rather to confirm implicitly its correctness. our report seeks to identify the problems that prevent the eeas from fully expressing its potential and identifies some possible solutions that seem to us to be consistent with the fundamental approach chosen in 2010 and pursued in recent years. i do not repeat the proposals already made by mr brok, the member or members for whom i want to reassure you that no one is thinking of european parliamentarians, the rationalization of the structure, the strengthening of the role of vice-president of the commission by the high representative, the integration of crisis management structures, the strengthening of the role of heads of delegation, full political control by parliament, the autonomy of recruitment procedures vis-à-vis the member states. we think these are reasonable proposals, some of which can be implemented on the basis of the existing decision, while others will require its revision, for which we ask that parliament be fully involved in the same way as in 2010. i am confident that a fruitful dialogue with you, the high representative, will develop around these proposals and that the review of the external action service will provide the european union with a better instrument for conducting a foreign policy commensurate with its responsibilities and ambitions.
the rapporteur. - madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i think this debate has shown that there is a broad consensus in parliament on the lines of our report. i was also pleased to hear, for example, from mr tannock the recognition of the importance and usefulness of the european external action service. the debate also showed a significant convergence between parliament and you, high representative. i must say, mrs ashton, that you made an excellent speech and that is a real source of satisfaction not only for the recognition you have given to parliament but above all because you have shown a vision of the nature, the tasks, the potentialities of the european external action service which we fully share. in particular, the challenge of the comprehensive approach, i.e. the ability to coordinate in a synergistic way the various instruments at europe's disposal to make its external action effective. that is why, although the cases of good cooperation with the commission which you have mentioned are undoubtedly real, we stress that much still needs to be done and can be done in this respect. i am confident that the review on this basis will be fruitful and i therefore thank you and all the staff of the european external action service, starting of course with pierre vimont, for their commitment, for the results and for their willingness to deal with this parliament.
madam president, i must say to baroness ashton, as a physician and a human being, that i have a specific concern, namely about so-called ‘cuban health diplomacy’. cuba is sending out doctors under government-to-government cooperation agreements. this practice has now become cuba’s biggest industry, bringing in usd 6 billion. in venezuela alone, there are more than 30 000 cuban doctors, traded for oil; in brazil there are 6 000 of them. the host countries pay for each doctor about usd 5 000 per month, while the doctors themselves receive only usd 25. these bilateral agreements clearly violate a number of international labour organisation conventions. one of the escaped cuban doctors recently stated, ‘we are the highest qualified slave labour force in the world.’ are we sure that we should continue to finance cuba, with eur 30 million each year?
mr president, i believe that any discussion at eu level on the freedom of the press and media in the world can only be credible if media freedom is safeguarded and respected within the union itself. we must remind ourselves that, in recent years, some european media have come under scrutiny for unethical and illegal behaviour. for this reason, the commission should closely monitor the independence of the press within the member states, while applying a global strategy of transparency and accountability. freedom of expression is the cornerstone of democracy. for this reason, the press must operate independently and free of political and financial pressure. too often in europe we see media empires, controlled or owned by politicians or industrial groups, carrying out misinformation campaigns, with disastrous results for democracy and freedom. at international level, i agree on the need to adopt a press and media strategy within eu foreign policy, involving in this effort multilateral bodies such as the council of europe, the oecd and the united nations.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, as a member of the ad hoc delegation of this parliament to observe the trials of journalists in turkey, i express my deep concern at the events of these days and the restrictions on freedom of expression and assembly in istanbul and other turkish cities. the eu cannot remain passive in the face of repeated violations of fundamental rights in an accession country such as turkey: there have been dozens of arrests of journalists accused of spreading false information about the anti-government street protests; hundreds of journalists are in prison in turkey for journalistic activities and are being charged instead of other punishments; there are hundreds of journalists in prison for reporting on the lack of freedom of the turkish kurdish minority in turkey. the union must play a more effective and decisive role in promoting freedom of expression, but without mrs ashton - let me say this - it will be impossible, because the representative who will be answering us shortly is certainly not in her head, she does not know what she is thinking. so i'm sorry to talk and not have the ashton here.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, today we are talking about freedom of the press and the media in the world, with particular reference to countries where there is no democracy or conflict zones. being a journalist also means being at the forefront of the struggle for human rights, which is why i join the call launched by the international federation for the freedom of all journalists, who are prevented or held hostage in the areas of the syrian conflict. i am also thinking of the italian journalist, domenico quirico, who gave his report last thursday after two months, but we hope above all that he will soon be free from his family and able to carry out his work; the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the media are not subject to unfair competition. i wonder whether the workers' rights have been respected and whether this decision, in terms of timing and method, does not constitute a breach of freedom of information.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, there is no doubt that freedom of the press, freedom of the media, freedom of expression are absolute values of our civilization. it is true that the activities carried out on the subject make it clear that in many areas, sometimes not far from the territories of the member states, in the member states themselves, the development of democratic life is not always supported by adequate and complete information, but the protection of the rights that are not available to life, self-determination, choice and religion requires information pluralism. that is why there is also an absolute need for investigative journalism, for journalists who are not afraid to say what they think, with respect for the truth and the moral integrity of these journalists, which must be protected, and for dialogue and cooperation to be strengthened with those parts of the world, some of which have already been identified and are still far from meeting acceptable minimum standards of information. information is a sacred right which serves to improve the civil environment in which we carry out our activities.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the provision of imprisonment for the crime of defamation prevents the full realisation of the principle of freedom of expression, with serious repercussions on the effectiveness and completeness of communications throughout europe. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to the full. in italy, for example, in recent months two newspaper editors, alessandro sallusti and giorgio mulé, have been sentenced to prison terms for the crime of defamation or failure to control. the commission and the council must take strong decisions to raise awareness among the member states and to decriminalise defamation immediately, guaranteeing full freedom of expression, the right of citizens to be adequately informed and the protection of the honour of those involved. so yes to harsh sanctions, including radiation when the defamation is certain and proven, no to prison sentences, punitive and not re-educational. i am therefore announcing that, having already collected more than 40 of the required signatures, i will be submitting a question to the european commission, requesting a debate in the house for the july plenary session.
member of the commission. − mr president, i would like to start by thanking the honourable members for their wide-ranging and very powerful interventions. i am grateful for the honourable members’ recognition of the initial steps that the eu has already taken to implement the eu’s strategic framework and action plan on human rights. however, i recognise that much still needs to be done. i believe there are three themes that will need to be addressed stemming from today’s debate. firstly, it is necessary to address human rights consistently in all eu policies. human rights and governance are also a core focus of eu development cooperation, and the european external action service and devco are working together to step up a rights-based approach to development assistance. at the same time, we also know that poverty alleviation is one of the issues that allow us to address human rights more sustainably. it is also clear that other areas – trade has been mentioned, as has migration policy – should step up a gear in order to respond to the human rights approach. but rest assured that my colleagues are really doing everything they can in their areas to support a human-rights-based approach, and we are very unselfish in our approaches. we make a case if it needs to be made, and our policy is definitely an example to the world. i would like to mention just one example: this house has adopted the commission’s proposal for transparency in the extractive industries. it is a world-leading proposal that provides for the necessary elements in the fight against corruption. the second issue is – as several members have pointed out – that it is essential that you raise human rights violations robustly with third countries. each case must be judged on its own merits. we are sometimes faced with a challenge, and we need to react more robustly and swiftly. honourable members can rest assured that the eu raises human rights consistently with all of our partner countries and at the highest political level, including with ethiopia. we have an even broader approach that is not just about responding to concrete cases. there is a political dialogue with asian countries and with acp countries, where it comes under article 8 of the cotonou agreement, where we address not only particular cases, but also systemic issues like media freedom, democracy, human rights and civil society. it is also clear that there are new challenges coming, and there are some trends that need to be addressed. one that was very worrying was media freedom. it is true that it is more concentrated. it is true that in many countries, governments believe that the media do not help in their reform policies. it is very clear that we need to be more strategic in this approach. in this respect, we are already working towards making our support for freedom of expression much stronger in our delegation guidelines. michael cashman mentioned issues with lgbti rights. this is really worrying. it is true that laws exist in many countries which stem from colonialist times, but it is definitely not in accordance with the spirit of the time. the fight for lbgti community rights is one of the focuses of today’s policy, and we are also preparing guidelines for our delegations on how to address this issue and how to make this case very strong and powerful. last but not least, i would like to welcome the european parliament’s contribution to human rights, democracy and freedom of press and media – the sakharov prize, ‘urgency debates’ and the work of the human rights subcommittee. all of these are invaluable in drawing attention to the violation of human rights and giving us additional arguments when working with our partner countries for human rights, democracy and media freedom. we look forward to carrying forward our work with parliament this year and in the years ahead. it is also great that you have allowed the special representative for human rights to be here to participate in the debate. seeing his interactions this year, i can assure you that he is available for all individual questions that you may have, and for other external activities that we carry out under his leadership. as regards human rights, democracy and media freedom, there are good days, and there are upsetting days. however, this does not sway our member of the commission. − madam president, honourable members, i would like to thank the rapporteur, mr martin, for his constructive work in bringing to the vote the interim economic partnership agreement with cameroon. the interim epa signed by the european union and cameroon is the first step in the establishment of a regional partnership for trade and development between the eu and central africa. thanks to this interim epa, cameroon has continued to enjoy full and free access to the european market for all its products without interruption since 2008. the conclusion of the interim epa in 2007 was key for cameroon as the eu is its largest trading partner. cameroon’s exports to the eu include products that are either not covered by the union’s generalised scheme of preferences, such as bananas and aluminium for instance, or which benefit from limited margins of preference. under the current commission mandate, there has been renewed activity in the context of negotiations with central african partners for a more comprehensive regional epa. we aim for significant progress in the coming months. upon its conclusion and ratification, the regional agreement will replace the interim agreement, which, as suggested in the title of this debate, will function as a stepping stone. the commission will keep the european parliament fully informed about the ongoing regional negotiations. the rapporteur mentions that there has not been sufficient encouragement to move forward. actually we have, under the 10th european development fund, doubled the support for regional integration, and in the context of the 11th edf we have had very constructive talks on how to strengthen regional integration. the main challenge, in my opinion, is that countries in this region see less need at this stage to forge trade between one another: they tend to look to their outward markets rather than the african market. this is a missed opportunity, but as the time goes on there is a chance, as commissioner de gucht has said, that we may conclude an agreement and thereby increase development support in order to implement mechanisms to support regional trade. it is the current pattern of trade that somehow prevents the regional countries from being more ambitious as to a regional epa. the issue of human rights and democratisation in cameroon, which was rightly raised, is a focus of special attention from the eu in terms not only of policy dialogue and advocacy but also of our targeted financial support for civil society organisations. areas of eu concern include justice, press freedom, democracy, the fight against corruption, and the promotion of human rights, particularly women’s rights and the rights of the lgbt community. there are also two other problematic issues: trafficking in human beings and the rights of minorities. these are matters to which we are paying very careful attention. we are also aware that we need to base our relationship with cameroon on a long-term vision, with the partnership continuing to develop and grow, offering a sustainable path to development based on full implementation of human rights needs. it is a process. we are well aware that we need to step up a gear in the negotiations about the human rights situation in cameroon but i would argue that this should not prevent us from supporting the interim epa with cameroon because i believe that it too strengthens our approach towards improving the human rights situation in the country.

the rapporteur. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, in the crisis there is a section of enterprises - the cooperatives - which has shown that they are able to withstand more and better than others, that they are able to hold on, to defend employment - and indeed to grow in the crisis - also because of the value they attach to work and thanks to their link with the social fabric and the local community. cooperatives are enterprises which do not primarily pursue profit but want to promote work, welfare and consumption through balanced economic management and contribute to local development, including through good business projects such as in the energy field. this is so true that the term "resilience" was coined to demonstrate this resilience that many studies now attest to. stronger resilience, the will and determination to stand up, the ability to defend one's business and to generate employment. our own-initiative report is intended to highlight a particular phenomenon in this world, namely the role of cooperatives in the face of production crises and company restructuring. when a company is failing and wants to close its doors, there are several ways to transform: there can be management leveraged buyout processes, but there can also be forms of worker buyout - workers getting together, becoming cooperatives, to continue the activity. we must leave all these possibilities open. europe must support them, including through appropriate instruments, because cooperatives play an active role in restructuring to save companies from the crisis. we have set ourselves a strategy of reindustrialisation and the growth of new enterprises. the first step is to defend the existing firms and to help them through the crisis. the cooperative model, with its dynamism, its ability to adapt to change, its flexibility and the support of local networks, is of great interest to the european economy. it is, of course, the vision of the social and market economy that europe claims as a model, but for which it does not do enough. it is a challenge of economic culture, because these enterprises are a powerful lever for development and can be very competitive. if europe did more in this field, it would strengthen its economic and productive heritage, because it is a grave mistake to relegate this sector - even if it is only a part of the continental economy - to the margins or to weakness. there is a study, as scalvini points out, which is a leader in the sector, from the us treasury department, which shows how, for fannie mae and freddie mac, a cooperative structure would have prevented the financial disasters that then triggered the global crisis. interesting, i think, as a lesson for our view of economics and finance. in short, the report, which refers back to the resolution we voted in this parliament at the end of the previous parliamentary term, on the social and market economy enterprises, points to the good practices already in place in many member states of the union - cases of cooperatives that have saved businesses from bankruptcy - and calls for europe to do more, for the commission to do more and in a more calibrated way. it is called for the commission's offices to be strengthened and dedicated to this, specifically it is called for the sector to be promoted, to be involved in the social dialogue and for budget lines to be devoted to supporting these restructuring practices in the future, moving from pilot projects. i think that europe must have more courage in pointing out new ways of doing business and economy, in order to make the most of its civil capital also at the economic level, because there are considerable economic advantages here and it is a bit out of the logic of welfare which often unfairly relegates the sector. more needs to be done to give substance to the implementation of concrete and appropriate instruments and measures.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to congratulate mr toia, not out of solidarity with italians, but because he has produced a very complete and very precise report. the cooperative model is a model which, in this difficult phase we are living through, puts the real economy back at the centre after years of finalising economic activities, stimulating the spread of a micro-economy which represents an important form of social economy. cooperatives are often also closely linked to local development and production and often manage essential services for citizens, playing an important role in sustainable and inclusive development, aimed at enhancing local production, cultures of belonging and human values in a time of sometimes unbridled globalisation. i can only give one advice, namely that we must identify a regulatory framework capable of countering and identifying those instrumental attempts to enter the cooperative world without representing it.
member of the commission. - mr president, the commission would like to thank ms toia for her excellent report which gives us the opportunity to explain briefly our policy on the promotion of cooperatives. the key goal of the commission’s policy is to create a stable legal and administrative environment at european level but also in every member state. i agree with the rapporteur and most of the speakers who underlined that cooperative and other social economy enterprises create jobs for millions of our people, including vulnerable citizens facing the crisis. i also agree with the fact that these cooperative businesses are more resilient to the crisis itself. the commission is therefore paying particular attention to ensuring that these particular principles, specific needs, goals, efforts and the working style of cooperatives are taken into account and respected. this is done in all areas of union policy, such as in state aid, accounting, company law, competition, social services of general interest and others. that is why we very much welcome the comments in the report and the calls for action. the policy in favour of cooperatives has always been high on the commission’s agenda. at present there are a number of ongoing initiatives and activities to which i believe it is worthwhile to draw your attention. vice-president tajani is currently organising a working group on cooperatives which will hold its first meeting in his presence on 10 july. this meeting will be followed by two more meetings during the year. at the end of this action the commission expects to have a number of innovative solutions to the most urgent problems faced by cooperatives, which can be supported by concrete european actions. the aim of the working group is to assess the specific needs of these organisations in relation to all the issues found in ms toia’s report. examples of these needs are a stable regulatory framework, financial and business support, promotion of the cooperative model among young people, internationalisation and business transfers, especially of enterprises in difficulty. all these issues are mentioned in the report we are discussing today and the commission is aware of them. regarding in particular business transfers and restructuring, which constitute a whole chapter in ms toia’s report, in february 2013 the commission convened the first session of the transfers of business expert group. the group met for the second time last week and its work will proceed at a meeting which will soon take place. the european confederation of worker cooperatives participates in this expert group. it is also invited to give input to a parallel study which will gather data about the various facets of a business transfer. a final conference is planned for early 2014; it will showcase the good practices identified by the expert group in the study. we hope that we will then have a concrete programme corresponding to the report’s conclusions.
the rapporteur. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, in february 2012 the european commission presented its communication on a bioeconomy for europe, where it proposed to move towards a greater and more sustainable use of renewable resources and called for a shift from a fossil-based society to a bio-based society, with the support of research and innovation. a little over a year after the adoption of this communication, parliament drew up its own-initiative report, welcoming many of these requests and then strengthening and deepening them. in this sense, the text we are about to vote on tomorrow at this part-session - reflecting the unanimous approval of the envi committee - sends a clear message to the commission in view of the presentation by the commission of a next legislative proposal on the bioeconomy. i am convinced that the bioeconomy has enormous potential. given the major challenges facing the european union, the bio-economy can be the answer to fossil fuel dependence and the way forward towards smart growth. the commission's proposal for a regulation on the establishment of a european agency for the evaluation of medicinal products for human use (emah) is based on the principle of mutual recognition of the quality of medicinal products for human use. in this context, the bioeconomy could also make an important contribution to countering the deindustrialisation process currently affecting europe, reversing its course and relaunching a new european model of industrialisation, by which to encourage the creation of new value chains and curb the phenomena of abandonment of industrial sites, as well as supporting economic and social development with an extremely high return in terms of employment. to enable this potential to be fully realised, it is necessary to develop an all-encompassing approach and to look at the bioeconomy model as the synthesis in which the synergistic encounter between european policies for agriculture, industry and the environment, research and innovation and between the different decision-making levels from the community to the regional and local is achieved in such a way as to create a harmonious and coordinated environment in which a continuous exchange of knowledge, skills, information and know-how is possible. at the same time, it will be important to ensure and develop coherent and interlinked research and innovation programmes, to provide instruments to support industrial investment and to ensure that the results achieved have the greatest impact on society and are fully understood by european citizens. in this context, new forms of partnership involving public and private entities can also make a strong contribution to economic recovery and sustainable development, especially in the current crisis context. leveraging private investment through the creation of a public-private partnership dedicated to bio-industries would in fact make it possible to support and encourage the development of new products and to achieve their fundamental and effective transfer to the market, limiting the risk that more favourable conditions would encourage the migration of excellence and innovative projects outside europe. the bioeconomy model developed within this strategy - i am sure - will not only solve the chronic contingencies, but in the longer term it will be able to bring about more sustainable and efficient production, consumption, development and lifestyles, reactivating the european growth process.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, apart from the numbers and figures that can be interpreted as one pleases, what should make us reflect is the difficulty with which this agreement was reached. a deal that's in the red, it's useless to deny it. the european commission should ask itself why the member states no longer seem to want to believe in europe, to the extent of drastically limiting its resources. the debate here is much broader and we must consider the costs and benefits of this union. in recent years it has become clear to everyone that this europe is no longer working and is a considerable cost, especially for italy, which has left brussels over 30 billion euros in revenue and expenditure in the last seven years. the benefits, i would say, have been rather modest if not nonexistent. the majority of european funds go to the south, which does not spend them or spends them badly, while the others are left with crumbs, which are difficult to obtain. europe has gone from being hope to being fear. we must think about this and draw the right conclusions.
vice-president of the commission. − mr president, i would like to take this occasion to personally thank you and parliament for your strong support in these very difficult negotiations. i know that without your personal involvement and very skilful negotiations on the overall mff package, this result would not be possible. i would also like to thank wholeheartedly the rapporteur, ms dagmar roth-behrendt, and her shadow rapporteurs mr baldassarre, ms lichtenberger, ms wikström, mr karim, mr maštálka and mr speroni. we have been working very hard on this file under an intense time pressure and in the end i think we managed to get a very honourable and good deal. i am very pleased about today’s vote because through these approved staff regulations and approved administrative reform we have clearly proven that the european civil service is in tune with the european citizens. it shares the efforts of many public administrations for more savings and further modernisation, but it is also a good decision for the institutions and staff. we will still be able to recruit the highly-qualified staff we need and, at the same time, today’s vote makes it clear that to work for the european institutions means not only showing strong european commitment and dedication, but also possessing the great ability and skill required to pass a most demanding selection procedure and to be prepared to work longer working hours and retire later than most colleagues in the national civil services. i would like to conclude by saying that i believe that through this modernisation the european civil service will be fully equipped to deal with the current crisis and with european and global challenges and to work on europe, which will, i believe, emerge stronger from the crisis than it was before.

in writing. - beyond the name, this function must be exercised with a great sense of responsibility and consistency. i would like to wish the new european ombudsman to work with serenity and with an awareness of the importance of his role. i hope very much that you will not have to intervene, but it is important to ensure that all complaints of maladministration in the institutions and bodies of the european union are investigated and analysed. careful analysis will help to identify problems and to solve them.
in writing. − after almost two years of difficult negotiations, we have finally reached an agreement that will save €2.7 billion by 2020 and modernise the european civil service. the savings are made possible by substantial changes and cuts such as the 5% reduction in hiring until 2017, the freezing of wages for two years, the raising of the retirement age and the reduction of various benefits. but the new statute will also make it possible to move towards a modern, competent and efficient public service. to this end, the career structure will be organised in such a way as to create a direct link between the responsibility assumed and the degree maintained. in addition, with the aim of rewarding those who deserve it and punishing those who do not achieve positive results, the jump within the same grade and disciplinary measures will depend on the annual performance evaluation report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the amendments to the staff regulations. the amendments concern mainly general measures on career advancement, working conditions, pensions and allowances. it is good to let european citizens know that we voted for the 5% reduction in hiring until 2017, the freezing of salaries in 2013 and 2014, the advancement to higher grades only by internal competition and for managerial functions, the automatic demotion following 3 insufficient evaluations and the launch of the dismissal procedure after 5 negative reports, the increase of working hours without compensation from 37.5 to 40, the retirement age from 63 to 66 (and in exceptional cases to 70), the abolition of early retirement without loss of rights and the reduction of days of leave and flat-rate reimbursement. these measures will save €2.7 billion by 2020, plus a further €1.5 billion linked to reduced days off and increased working hours. this reduces the costs of the european bureaucratic machine and improves the efficiency of the administration.
in writing. i voted in favour of my colleague dagmar roth-behrendt's report because it is a compromise report after difficult and long negotiations. it solves the double equation of the reduction in staff and the freezing of their salaries demanded by the european council while preserving a european civil service capable of functioning properly. this report, which has been the result of a year and a half of negotiations, also preserves the essential principles which must be safeguarded to ensure the proper functioning of our european institutions.
in writing. − i supported the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending the staff regulations of officials and other servants of the european union as it is necessary to ensure the recruitment and retention of highly qualified, multilingual staff equitably distributed by country of origin and by gender, in line with the high standards of professional ethics required by the european civil service.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending the staff regulations of officials and the conditions of employment of other servants of the european union, because i consider that a process of modernisation in this area is essential. the demographic and economic changes affecting europe require the institutions to work efficiently, ensuring a good performance and a good quality of service. the recent enlargement of the union to include croatia, the tasks arising from the treaty of lisbon and the economic crisis which has engulfed europe form a context which must be taken into account. so while it is true that costs must be reduced, it is also true that the obligations imposed on the institutions and bodies of the union by the treaties must in any case be fulfilled. for this reason, consideration should be given to the possibility of a decision to reduce staff by 5% automatically in each institution and agency: it is appropriate to adapt this choice to the needs of each branch of activity. the proposal to introduce a new category of assistance staff (ast) would be acceptable, aimed at ensuring that the staff is efficient and always renewed, prepared and competent.

in writing. − this convention includes a commitment to apply the basic safety principles for nuclear installations and to define detailed rules which are updated periodically in order to better protect human health and the environment in which we live. i think it is appropriate to give precedence to the european union's rules for those member states which ratified the 1997 protocol before joining the eu and for those states which are contracting parties to the paris convention: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's nuclear safety is not compromised. i am voting in favour of this resolution because i agree with these objectives.
in writing. - the amendments to the vienna convention have positive aspects for potential victims of a nuclear accident, namely an increase in the amount of liability and a broader definition of nuclear damage. therefore, after consulting stakeholders, it is recognised that any initiative in this area should not hinder member states' accession to international conventions that improve the situation of potential victims in the european union. in this respect, accession to the 1997 protocol can prove useful.
in writing. - liability in nuclear matters is regulated at international level by two instruments: the vienna convention and the 1960 paris convention. given the lack of uniformity still existing between member states as regards the rules concerning the procedure for the recognition and enforcement of decisions in nuclear damage, we believe that the primacy of community law should also be extended to the member states which ratified the 1997 protocol before joining the european union, namely latvia and romania. we also welcome the council's proposal to authorise the member states which are contracting parties to the vienna convention, namely bulgaria, the czech republic, estonia, hungary, lithuania, poland and slovakia, to ratify or conclude the 1997 protocol.
in writing. - ladies and gentlemen, the vienna convention was adopted with the aim of ensuring adequate and fair compensation for victims of damage caused by nuclear accidents by establishing a special civil liability regime in the nuclear energy sector. i agree with the rapporteur that parliament should give its consent to the draft council decision on the vienna convention, and i therefore voted in favour of the proposal.
in writing. the european commission proposes that the council authorise the member states, which are parties to the vienna convention on civil liability for nuclear damage, to conclude or ratify the 1997 protocol amending the convention. taking into account that there is still no specific and above all uniform legislation governing nuclear liability in europe (in fact, there is regulation (ec) no 864/2007 on the law applicable to non-contractual obligations which excludes nuclear liability from its scope and regulation (eu) no 1215/2012 on jurisdiction and the recognition and enforcement of judgments in civil and commercial matters), accession to the 1997 protocol would prove useful. amendments to the vienna convention would have a positive effect on potential victims of a nuclear accident, as they would increase the amount of liability and broaden the definition of nuclear damage. moreover, no action taken in this area would prevent member states from acceding to international conventions which improve the situation of potential victims in the european union. in view of the considerations which have been developed, i have given my favourable opinion on the proposal.
in writing. - liability in nuclear matters is regulated at international level by two instruments: the vienna convention and the 1960 paris convention on civil liability in the field of nuclear energy. both conventions are based on similar principles in substance. the vienna convention was adopted with the aim of ensuring adequate and fair compensation for victims of damage caused by nuclear accidents by establishing a special civil liability regime in the field of nuclear energy. in order to overcome the lack of uniformity still existing between member states as regards the rules on the procedure for the recognition and enforcement of decisions in nuclear damage, the commission undertook to consider the possibility of extending, in a future proposal, the solution of giving priority to eu rules also to those member states which ratified the 1997 protocol before joining the european union, namely latvia and romania, and to those member states which are contracting parties to the paris convention. it is therefore proposed to authorise the member states which are contracting parties to the vienna convention (bulgaria, the czech republic, estonia, hungary, lithuania, poland and slovakia) to ratify or conclude the 1997 protocol.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the pietikäinen report. i agree with the request in the text that the commission should be provided with more efficient and simpler mechanisms for assessing state aid, but above all with the need for the commission to refrain from intervening in the measures put in place by the member states, with the aim of implementing social measures which do not cause distortions on the market. i think it is essential to simplify the procedure for granting state aid.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this important parliamentary position. the amendments concern regulation (ec) no 659/99 on procedural rules in state aid matters. whereas the commission has until now been required to investigate every alleged infringement, irrespective of the source of the information, complainants are now required to submit a number of mandatory information and be interested parties. failing this, the commission will no longer be required to adopt a formal decision. this will allow us to concentrate on the most substantiated complaints, with a huge simplification of work. the text we have adopted will also enable the commission, as it already does in the field of antitrust, to carry out investigations more quickly and more precisely and also to impose sanctions. the changes adopted are, in my view, in the right direction, namely to improve the handling of complaints and to ensure effective and reliable market information collection. in this way, state aid can contribute more to the implementation of the 2020 strategy and to the consolidation of national budgets. in addition, these amendments will help states to grant state aid in accordance with agreed rules and the single market will function better because illegal and distorting aid is greatly reduced.
in writing. - today, in plenary, we welcomed the proposal to amend a regulation which is part of a more general reform of state aid in the european union. we are confident that the adoption of this proposal will help to improve the handling of complaints and ensure the efficient and reliable collection of market information. we believe that the priority is to remedy the problems identified in the complaints procedure, making it faster, more efficient and more transparent, so that the commission can deal with the cases which are most important for the proper functioning of the single market. it is therefore our duty to ensure that the commission has effective tools to verify that member states grant state aid in accordance with the agreed rules and do not impede competition within the european union by discouraging illegal state aid. we also believe that it is absolutely necessary to resolve the problem of divergent interpretations of state aid rules in some member states; we insist that these situations be clarified by assessing, through market surveys, what kind of demand exists for certain services.
in writing. the european union must, as part of its unification of development, have modern state aid control procedures. the possibility of recourse and complaints for measures distorting competition within the internal market should be simplified. the new rules that apply must, however, leave the member states free to decide in certain areas, as is the case in this report. that is why i voted in favour.

in writing. − state aid is an important contribution to the smooth functioning of the single market, as it contributes to a better allocation of public resources and to equal treatment of public and private enterprises, thus promoting free competition. since the european union has often found itself investigating state aid irregularly paid into the coffers of companies operating in the single market, an increase in the effectiveness of the control of such aid would be more than appropriate. i am in favour of the proposal to amend regulation (ec) no 659/1999 laying down detailed rules for the application of article 93 of the ec treaty in the field of state aid. i believe that the improvements proposed by the commission are the real starting point for action in this direction. improving the handling of complaints and ensuring the collection of effective and reliable market information would provide the commission with concrete tools for verifying the granting of aid, thereby allowing the community system to closely assist national courts in bringing the single market into line with the principles enshrined in the treaties.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the european aviation sector currently employs over 5 million people and contributes eur 365 billion to gdp each year, eur 1 billion a day, making a fundamental contribution to economic growth and to the territorial and social cohesion of the whole continent. this is therefore a key sector which must be able to meet the new challenges arising from other regions of the world which, benefiting from more permissive legislation in terms of building new airport capacity, are strengthening their position on the global aviation market to the detriment of european carriers. the competitiveness of airlines and businesses in the union must therefore be safeguarded and this objective can be achieved first by improving the capacity gap in many airports, either by allocating resources for the new construction of new works or by using existing infrastructure more efficiently, including and especially by improving the allocation of airport slots. i believe, and i conclude, mr president, that the fundamental role played by regional airports throughout europe should also be improved in this context.
in writing. − aviation plays a key role in the european economy: it contributes over eur 300 billion to european gdp and 5.1 million jobs depend on it. however, seven years after the commission's communication on the development of the community's external aviation policy agenda, the objectives have still not been achieved. new economic challenges are emerging in regions of the world where much more permissive legislation allows companies to build new airports that attract many travellers from european hubs. the commission is therefore proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'aircraft' in the definition of the term 'aircraft'. in my view, the european union should increase its airport capacity without delay to avoid losing competitiveness in relation to regions which are experiencing exponential growth in this sector, while at the same time making full use of the capacity of existing airports. i agree with the rapporteur that the growing number of low-cost airlines in the european internal market could be seen as a new model for strengthening the market rather than a competitive threat. the 'classic' and low-cost airlines could find a way to harmonise the european market and complement each other, so as to respond with greater stability to the challenges of external markets.
