in writing. − i voted in favour of the creation of a common statute for european foundations because, particularly at a time of tight national budgets, foundations are playing an increased role in european union economies. therefore, with this text, we are asking for a reduction in costs and legal uncertainties for foundations and for the establishment of a new european legal form to facilitate the establishment and operation of foundations in the single market. in addition, i believe that the creation of this statute will establish a clearer and consistent regulatory framework for cross-border organisations which will contribute to facilitating their institution and operation in the single market.
in writing. − there are 110 000 public benefit foundations in the european union, with an estimated €350 billion in assets and an annual employment of €83 billion, employing over 1 million european citizens, many of whom are unpaid volunteers. the commission is proposing a statute providing for the legal form of the european foundation for foundations and operators working in more than one member state, in order to ease and simplify the legal, tax and administrative obstacles which make it extremely difficult to operate in other countries. i think, however, that some of the terminology and legal definitions contained in the commission's proposal still need clarification, particularly as regards the issue of workers' representation, and for these reasons i have decided to abstain in this vote.
in writing. − the foundations pursue objectives of general public interest, carrying out activities focused on areas of importance to the citizens and the economy of europe and promoting research and culture. i think it is important to establish a single legal form, the 'european foundation', which would coexist with the national foundations with legal personality and capacity in all the member states. this statute would benefit a number of actors such as member states, donors, the foundations themselves and citizens and would make it easier to free up resources for education, social services and the environment. i agree with the encouragement to the member states to have a rapid and complete introduction of the statute with all the guarantees of transparency in order to remove the obstacles which prevent the cross-border activity of foundations and to promote the creation of new foundations. i am voting in favour of this resolution, agreeing with the points made in it and finding it useful and beneficial to europe.
in writing. − at this particular economic juncture it is important to remember the social role played by foundations. the institutions are not always able to meet the demands of the citizens, and that is why their contribution is crucial from a financial point of view. the foundations are increasingly operating across borders. most of the fields they deal with do not know borders: i think about health research or climate change. i think it is right to remove all the barriers which currently stand in the way of the transfer of funds. a citizen must be able to finance a good cause, no matter where the foundation operates.
in writing. - today in plenary we welcomed the explanatory statement by our colleague and rapporteur, mrs regner, on the importance and benefits of the statute of the european foundation (ef). we are aware that foundations play a major role in the european union, operating in such crucial areas as education, health, environmental protection, art, culture, sport and research. they are also a major employer in civil society and live off the unpaid work of many volunteers. we believe it is essential that foundations can carry out their work in more than one member state without having to face the current long and costly bureaucratic barriers to the recognition of their activities. whereas to meet the obstacles of civil and tax law, expensive consultancy is required, resources originally intended for public utility purposes are lost. finally, we are confident that the introduction of the statute will bring many benefits to all those concerned, citizens, donors, foundations and member states, especially by removing the costly obstacles to cross-border activity; we therefore urge all eu countries to implement the statute of the european foundation in a timely manner and to strengthen its credibility and trust through full sustainability and effective supervision.
in writing. - ladies and gentlemen, foundations play a major role in the european union, as they play a crucial role in education, research, social services, health, environmental protection, talent promotion, youth and sport, art and culture. i agree with the rapporteur on the importance of the duration and sustainability of the european foundation, and i therefore voted in favour of the proposal.
in writing. − foundations play an important role in the european union and the benefits of the adoption of a statute would be many and significant. in fact, as they increasingly operate across borders, foundations face a variety of barriers, mainly of an economic nature. the main problem is the differences between the various national legal systems, especially in civil and tax law. differences that pose obstacles that can be overcome by costly consultancy using funds instead of public interest activities. the foundations draw on their own profits and funds from donors: the commission has already taken a number of measures to improve the situation of the unemployed. in fact, a statute would not only confer personality and legal capacity on foundations but also reduce administrative costs and burdens, and give the fe greater certainty and credibility. donors would be encouraged to invest money and to provide useful resources to the foundation accordingly, encouraging projects in crucial areas: the commission has also been active in the fight against fraud, and has recently launched a new action programme to combat fraud. i therefore voted in favour of the proposal.
in writing. - foundations are increasingly operating across borders: in many cases, foundations wishing to operate in more than one member state or donors wishing to allocate funds to a good cause in a foreign country are hampered by bureaucratic problems. the commission proposal therefore aims to remove these barriers in order to facilitate the cross-border activities of foundations and to facilitate the transfer of funds. to be recognised as a european foundation, a foundation must operate in at least two member states and have a minimum capital of eur 25 000. the new statute of the european foundation, which is intended to coexist with national provisions, will be implemented and monitored by adapting existing structures.
in writing. - the report by mrs simpson 'on the proposal for a european parliament and council directive amending directive 2009/16/ec on port state control', while agreeable in its general objectives of increasing the protection of seafarers, leaves strong doubt that it was drafted to force member states that have not yet ratified the maritime labour convention to do so, which is why i abstained in this vote.
in writing. i shall vote in favour of this resolution. the safety of shipping and seafarers is very important, and its absence would have catastrophic consequences for workers, the environment and commerce. the shipowners, masters and states must ensure that ships comply with the relevant rules. it is therefore important for the eu to work together to provide mechanisms for states to verify that the rules are applied on board all ships calling at eu ports. i agree with the member states' recruitment of inspectors with the necessary skills to ensure the best protection in this field, while respecting the rules of the legal framework and ratifying the maritime labour convention.
in writing. - i do not believe that european legislation on the maritime labour convention (mlc) should be weakened, while recognising the validity and need for some changes aimed at reducing red tape and protecting workers. in this sense, i am in favour of the information being passed on to the international labour organisation to promote the dissemination of best practice. i also welcomed the introduction of some proposals to strengthen the clauses on the confidentiality of complaints, so that seafarers are not deterred from filing a complaint for fear of negative consequences in the future.
in writing. the european parliament has long been in favour of the establishment of minimum standards for living and working conditions on board ships. today in plenary we approved the amendment to the directive on port state control. we are insisting, first of all, that non-compliant ships are unacceptable as far as the rights of workers and the safety of ships, the protection and safety of the environment are concerned. in addition, despite the responsibility to ensure that ships comply with the rules on both owners and masters, we believe that the european union should provide mechanisms to verify that these rules are applied on board all ships calling at eu ports, regardless of the nationality of the seafarers or the flag of the ships. it is important, then, that while we welcome the establishment of minimum international standards, we should be careful that they do not constitute a possible justification for reducing the levels of protection afforded by european social legislation. finally, we believe that member states should employ a sufficient number of inspectors with the necessary skills, including the ability to assess the living and working conditions of seafarers on board ships.
in writing. i voted in favour of this proposal for a directive. the latter takes up the difficulties faced by the member states in responding to them in an intelligent and methodical manner. the proposal for a directive takes up proposals inspired by the maritime labour convention (mlc) adopted in 2006. the proposal also makes it possible to establish the necessary regulations to identify and remove from european coasts ships which do not comply with the basic rules of good maintenance and safety for seafarers but also do not take into account the possible damage to our environment and to our coasts.
in writing. - i supported the proposal for a european parliament and council directive on the conditions of employment of seafarers. the harmonisation of european legislation with the ilo maritime labour convention (mlc) through directive 2009/13/ec does not include some aspects that are crucial for the protection of the category but would fall under the responsibility of the flag state. it is therefore necessary to supplement the previous directive by clarifying international standards, including tools to promote the dissemination of best practices and the rights of such workers.
in writing. - safety at work is a key priority of community policy, especially in specific fields such as maritime employment. i voted in favour of the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council amending directive 2009/16/ec on port state control, because i believe that attention to the community regulatory framework on maritime labour liability is essential. it is necessary to adapt eu legislation to the union's external commitments arising essentially from the maritime labour convention in conjunction with the international labour organisation. in addition to appropriate legislation at community level, member states should undertake to monitor a system of control of the compliance of ships with safety standards, in order to ensure respect for the rights of workers on board and the protection of the natural environment. the invitation to do so would be addressed to the port states, irrespective of the nationality of the seafarers or the flag of the vessels, since flag states do not always fulfil their obligations in this respect.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, various statistical studies have shown that the main risk to road safety is the poor technical condition of the vehicle. the suspension of registration for a certain period is the most important instrument in this context to prevent accidents and thus unnecessary risks for citizens. moreover, the exchange of information between member states through national registers is of crucial importance in combating illegal phenomena and ultimately also in promoting road safety. the report by my colleague has addressed all the critical points of the proposal and as a result the aims of the report have been broadly shared by all the member states within the council. i therefore cannot but give my full support to the proposal and hope that it represents a substantial step forward and that the effects of these measures will bear fruit as soon as possible.
in writing. the aim of the 'technical inspection package' contained in the european commission's proposal is to support and enforce the technical inspection rules for motor vehicles with a view to improving road safety and environmental protection. the proposal aims to improve the application of the rules on roadworthiness tests and the roadworthiness inspection regime, in particular where the technical condition of a vehicle creates an immediate risk to road safety, through measures such as temporary withdrawal or permanent cancellation of the vehicle's registration. the commission has introduced more precise definitions of the place of registration of vehicles than the current act and has introduced the revocation and cancellation of registration certificates. i support the commission's proposal in general and i particularly welcome the establishment of electronic databases for the management of vehicle registration documents. at the same time, i hope that the national databases will be linked to those of other member states in order to facilitate vehicle identification. finally, i would draw the commission's attention to the importance of mutual recognition by all member states of the validity of technical checks.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by mr savisaar-toomast because i believe that this proposal will help to combat fraud and illegal car traffic, which in our country mainly concerns illegally registered vehicles from eastern europe.
in writing. - today, in plenary session in strasbourg, we approved the 'check-in package' proposed to support and enforce the rules on the check-in of motor vehicles, with a view to improving road safety and environmental protection. we believe that the system of road checks should be improved, especially in cases where the technical condition of a vehicle creates an immediate risk to road safety. we therefore welcome the proposal by mr savisaar-toomast, which provides for more precise definitions of the place of registration of vehicles and, most importantly, introduces the temporary revocation or permanent cancellation of the registration certificate. we are also convinced that it is essential to introduce new requirements for databases on the electronic registration of vehicles, and we hope that those in the various member states will be linked to each other in order to facilitate the identification of the vehicle. finally, we propose that the size of the registration certificate be reduced and that a link be marked to the technical inspection to reduce the actual burden that drivers have to carry with them at all times.
in writing. − in 2012, the commission presented a proposal on the 'technical inspection package' consisting of three legislative proposals aimed at strengthening road safety, environmental protection and fair competition by updating the current requirements for periodic technical inspections of commercial vehicles in the union. this proposal introduces a number of important new elements, including: a risk classification system for the selection of vehicles to be road-checked, the annual performance of a certain number of road checks by member states and the introduction of regular road-checking activities in consultation between member states. whatever technical measures are put in place, the effectiveness of a road safety policy depends, first and foremost, on the behaviour of users. i therefore believe that road safety education and enforcement are of vital importance. i welcome the proposal for the package, especially in view of the current enormous differences between the various member states in the way roadworthiness tests are carried out. in fact, according to recent data, the number of vehicles found not to comply with the technical requirements at the time of inspection varies from a minimum of 0.3% in one member state to 63% in another.
in writing. - we have today, in plenary, welcomed the proposal by mrs sehnalová on the harmonisation and strengthening of eu legislation on roadworthiness tests for motor vehicles, including the extension to two-wheelers. the proposal is based on the establishment of a european electronic platform which we believe is the right solution to achieve the objective of facilitating the exchange of information between member states on typeapproval, registration and results of technical inspections. we know that road safety is a crucial issue in our society, and we believe that the effectiveness of this policy depends first and foremost on the behaviour of users. we therefore believe that road safety education, training and enforcement are essential. we also support the introduction of a risk classification system. we believe that the selection of vehicles to be road-tested should be based on the risk profile of the operators so as to reduce the burden on those who maintain their vehicles properly. finally, we believe that road and technical inspections would be more effective if they had access to complete information on the vehicle's history and technical characteristics through a comprehensive data collection.

in writing. − the commission has recently presented new rules on periodic roadworthiness tests for motor vehicles, with the aim of further improving road safety and ensuring a high level of environmental protection. today we have approved the main elements of the proposal, considering it necessary to establish common minimum standards at european union level for vehicle inspection, while allowing member states to introduce stricter rules if appropriate. we consider it essential, first of all, that technical inspections be carried out by independent inspectors who have a good level of education and training. it is also essential to take strict measures against fraud in the field of mileage by recording mileage readings. we also think it would be a good idea to introduce compulsory checks on electronic security components. finally, it is important to remember that the directive on minimum standards for periodic vehicle inspections applies to cars, buses, heavy goods vehicles and their trailers, but not to mopeds or motorcycles.

madam president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, i would like to point out to you two problems which have emerged quite clearly from the recent events, namely those which have affected european countries, including my own, in the face of floods. when we talk about protection and prevention, we can no longer reason with the parameters of the past. the vast majority, i would say the totality of floods, are caused by sudden precipitation of a magnitude not comparable to historical floods. we are therefore facing a climate change which also requires a review of the criteria for prevention and protection. the second theme is the speed of action: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. if an economic activity does not resume in good time, it is damage on top of damage. so i think that is another reason why we will have to review our rules.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i too would like to address the council, but above all the eleven countries which have joined the enhanced cooperation because they must decide what to do and soon. in particular, i believe that they must draw a line of demarcation between where the boundaries of reasonable compromise lie and where the territory of yielding to the lobbying pressures of the powerful banking and financial powers begins. in this sense, the idea of moving the enhanced cooperation agreement halfway instead of at the beginning of 2014 would not seem to me to be good news. it is true that we must take things seriously, but that is no good reason to enter into the logic of postponement and delay. let's look at it from another angle. the transaction tax is an opportunity to demonstrate the autonomy of political choices and decisions in relation to the enormous power accumulated by the financial markets, a way to also loosen the perverse link between sovereign debts and the banking system. does that mean we are unreasonable? i'm not sure. the european parliament, as mr podimata has said, has shown itself to be reasonable, and no one wants to underestimate the undesirable side effects of a measure like this, but the lobbying campaign unleashed has appeared excessive, out of proportion and disproportionate. let's try to be balanced, there is no relationship between the amount of transactions made and the positive development of the financial markets. for these reasons, i do not believe that a reasonable compromise should lead to the total exclusion of government securities, secondary market sovereign bonds and derivatives. it is right to show flexibility in application and not to standardize rates and products, but it is not possible to exempt almost everything, and i think that this should be borne in mind by the countries which have accepted enhanced cooperation. we must show both courage and reasonableness in dealing with the taxpayers of europe.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, first of all i would like to thank the rapporteur, mrs podimata, and all the shadow rapporteurs for the excellent work they have done. this tax, which we are very keen to see introduced, is a clear sign of our intention to regulate the financial sector by preventing the speculative activities which are at the root of the economic crisis. the fact that eleven member states have committed to applying it is an important step forward, but the tax will only be optimal when it is applied by all member states and beyond. the commission has also proposed that the tax be applied uniformly, without any discretion on the part of the member states. it would involve a shift of capital in favour of certain countries, fragmenting the internal market and requiring the harmonization of quotas at european level. it is important that the revenue from the financial transaction tax should benefit the eu budget, which could be used more productively. this revenue should not replace national contributions but could simply be added to them in order to increase the spending capacity of the european union. i fully agree with what mr balcells said, commissioner, that it is necessary to provide for exemptions for non-speculative financial activities which have a social function and support the real economy. i am glad that these reflections have been included in the text we are going to vote on tomorrow. the financial transaction tax which we must apply at european level must have a precise purpose: significantly reduce speculative and dangerous activities, protecting european citizens and business, generating revenue that is used for productive purposes in support of european economic growth.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to thank mrs mccarthy and the shadow rapporteurs for their work on this dossier. after the financial crisis, it was clear that the european banking sector needed to be reformed. it is true that in some countries banking systems have held up well, but it is also true that in several countries we have seen the collapse of credit systems and the use of state aid which have made the european citizens pay the price for the undisciplined activities of the banks. in this situation, banking reform was inevitable and necessary. separating banking from risky and retail activities is a good way of simplifying the banking structure by making it more transparent, but we must avoid initiating such separations in a blatant way. there are financial activities which are marginal and which do not carry out speculative activities but, on the contrary, support entrepreneurial activity. care must therefore be taken not to eliminate these activities from the credit systems to the detriment of european enterprises. we must be ambitious and aim for a true banking union, only then can we have the most stable and secure credit system that can restore the transmission mechanism between banks and the real economy. this will put an end to the credit crunch and move towards a more transparent system. the banking union is therefore, commissioner barnier, the turning point for the resumption of growth and we must therefore move in this direction without delay and as soon as possible.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, it is a fact that the ets system is currently facing serious imbalances. the accumulation of surplus allowances is very significant and the trend is upwards. the price of carbon, going from 30 euros per tonne of co2 to about 7 euros per tonne of co2, is no longer sustainable for the trading system. we must unfortunately note that the whole system cannot function under such conditions and that it simply no longer provides sufficient incentives for sustainable scientific and technological innovation and new investment in low-carbon technologies. i am not sure that the commission is prepared to accept this amendment. we must accept this possibility for the sake of europe's future. however, i think there is one thing that needs to be taken more into account and that is concertation. since these are extraordinary measures, i believe it is essential to involve the sectors concerned.
in writing. − the european commission's proposal (backloading proposal) amending directive 2003/87/ec is aimed at clarifying the provisions on the timing of greenhouse gas emission allowance auctions. i would like to reiterate my opposition to the backloading measure for the temporary withdrawal of carbon dioxide emission allowances as proposed by the commission. the emissions trading scheme is working as a tool to reduce emissions in the most cost-effective way for industry: european industry will reduce its emissions by 21% by 2020, as set out by the european legislator. the low price of carbon dioxide is the consequence of a prolonged economic crisis, which has led to a collapse in industrial production in europe. therefore, backloading would have the effect of increasing the cost of energy in a period of contraction of the european economy and would not solve the structural deficiencies of the ets. in addition, it would create a precedent of regulator interference in a market instrument whose rules were set out in a 2008 agreement. i believe that the most appropriate way of restoring investor confidence is to define a regulatory framework by 2030 which, while respecting environmental commitments, ensures the competitiveness of european industries.
in writing. - i voted against the report by mr groote on the review of greenhouse gas auctions because i believe that the market should not be disturbed by such an invasive intervention. the ets is a real market, albeit an artificial one, and the commission should not tamper with the mechanisms and balances in place. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. reducing the total number of allowances now means that the recovery of industry, which is essential to its recovery, will be aggravated by new burdens and that operators in the sector who had made or planned investments will be put in difficulty by suddenly changing the rules of the game.
in writing. − to finance climate policy, the commission argues that the market is not functioning properly and that, to correct this malfunction, the exchange prices for emission allowances for the years 2013-2015 should be raised with a carry-over to the two-year period 2018-2020 ('backloading'). since backloading is a form of hidden taxation on industry, since the fall in demand is caused primarily by the recession and since the eu energy package is proving to be a failure, i am voting against.
in writing. - this is the second time that parliament has spoken on backloading. the resolution was adopted by 344 votes to 311 with 46 abstentions. the vote on the motions for resolutions will take place at the next voting time. the ppe group voted against the backloading mechanism, as it believes that a structural review of the entire ets system is necessary and a priority, rather than a temporary measure that would risk destabilising the market. we also believe that it is a mistake to intervene with this manoeuvre on a mechanism which was born as a market mechanism. there is no environmental motivation, because the targets for reducing emissions, precisely because of the crisis, will be reached. we hope that the future negotiations will produce a more balanced position, taking account of the difficulties of the crisis and of parliament's vote.
in writing. - today, at the strasbourg plenary session, we welcomed the proposal to amend the directive on the timing of greenhouse gas auctions. we agree with mr groote, the rapporteur, that the eu emissions trading system (eu ets) is a key instrument for reducing industrial emissions, with cost efficiency as the main objective. unfortunately, the current economic crisis, coupled with a significant inflow of external emission reduction credits under the clean development mechanism, has led to a significant accumulation of surplus allowances. we believe that in order to avoid jeopardising the stability and predictability of the eu ets, the auction calendar should be adjusted so that it is held only once in the third trading period of the eu ets. we believe that this is a good solution to ensure the stability of the eu ets system until final structural measures are adopted.
in writing. − considering that the european union emissions trading system (eu ets) is a key instrument of the new european policy, i thought it appropriate not to support the rapporteur's work.
in writing. - this directive had been referred back to committee by the house. unfortunately, despite the strong criticism of the text, the envi committee has not made any significant changes. the european commission will be able to decide arbitrarily on the value of the co2 allowances, regardless of the market value. one difference is that this arbitrary power has been limited to 900 million shares. today more than ever energy-intensive industries tend to relocate where costs and constraints are lower. if this directive were not rejected by this house, we would risk accelerating the relocation of a large part of european industry. i believe that europe, which is going through this endless crisis, cannot afford to do that, and i shall therefore vote against.
in writing. − the 10% reduction in greenhouse gas emissions over the 2008/2012 period is not entirely attributable to the eu emissions trading system (eu/ets) set up by the eu to reduce emissions because it is affected by the sharp decline in industrial production. the decline has led to a decline in the price of carbon allowances and has helped create a build-up of surplus allowances as well as imbalances that limit companies' investments in low-emission technologies. i voted in favour of the report because i believe that a short-term strategy is needed to strengthen the system, by adjusting the timetable for auctioning allowances under directive 2003/87/ec, pending the adoption of long-term structural measures. the eu has always been the strongest supporter of measures to reduce emissions. it would be desirable for the eu/ets system to adopt more harmonised rules on monitoring and verification of emissions in order to enhance its reliability and credibility, and i believe that it is necessary to exclude small installations with low emissions. to foster sustainable development, more action will be needed, including and especially by emerging economies.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, in the last few decades we have seen the spread of various epidemics at european level. at that time, coordination between the various european countries to deal with such emergencies was based on the voluntary principle and the inadequacy of this mechanism showed its limits. the creation of a legislative framework to strengthen the eu's capacity to respond to serious cross-border health threats has been a much-needed measure for years. i think that with this report the european parliament has done a fairly satisfactory job of filling this gap. however, on the other hand, i would like to point out that the amendment to article 23 has not been accepted. the question therefore remains whether the mechanism will be able to function quickly and effectively, since there will be no single strong coordinating body. i therefore support the commission and parliament in their willingness to make a public statement criticising the council for not accepting these measures.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a european parliament and council decision on serious crossborder threats to health, aimed at protecting the health of all eu citizens. i agree that risk assessment and coordination measures in the case of communicable diseases should be extended to all threats to health, whether they are of biological, chemical or environmental origin. the report also introduces the possibility of declaring a european public health emergency, with the aim of speeding up the supply of medicines. this is of great significance, especially in view of recent reports of the spread of diseases that seemed to have been eradicated and are now reappearing in very virulent forms.

in writing. − today, in plenary, we approved the commission's proposal to introduce measures to strengthen the eu's response capacity to prevent serious crossborder health threats. we believe it is essential to provide member states with the means, networks and structures to combat the threats posed by major disasters, especially given that in recent years they have been unprepared for emergencies. firstly, we believe that the scope of the rapid alert and response system should be extended to all serious crossborder threats to health; health crises caused by the misuse or marketing of defective medicines also fall into this category. we are also convinced that the importance of implementing a coherent and coordinated communication strategy in the event of a crisis must be stressed in order to facilitate the proper management of the situation and avoid serious economic consequences. finally, we would like to stress the need for cooperation between the members of the system and international organizations, in particular the world health organization (who), and also with third countries. finally, we would point out that the principles of confidentiality and retention of personal data must remain unchanged.
in writing. the recent health crises that have crossed the european union (pandemic of h1n1 influenza in 2009, volcanic ash in 2010, e. coli contamination in 2011) make us all aware of the need for european coordination in health security. this is the subject of this report, which outlines the lines of future european cooperation in the protection of the health of the citizens of the european union. risk assessment measures and coordination of national plans in different member states will be extended, as will cross-border emergency measures in the event of large-scale hospitalisation or when measures in one member state prove insufficient to control cross-border spread. the report envisages following up on these decisions by creating a 'european health emergency' to speed up the provision of medicines needed to combat health crises. all these new safety measures are beneficial to the citizens of the european union and to their health, and i therefore vote in favour of this report.
in writing. - i supported the european parliament's proposal for a decision on serious crossborder threats to health. the legislation provides for the strengthening of the union's capacity to deal with sudden threats such as pandemics, epidemics and viruses through instruments to facilitate cooperation between member states, such as collective purchases of vaccines and the possibility of declaring an emergency at community level.
in writing. - i shall vote in favour of the proposal for a european parliament decision on serious crossborder threats to health. following the events of the last health crises, the commission has presented a proposal for a decision providing for the establishment of a legislative framework, as well as means and structures, which can help coordinate the response and strengthen the eu's response capacity in the event of serious cross-border health threats. in order to ensure effective protection of citizens across europe, the preparedness of individual member states for health threats needs to include enhanced coordination of planning and response capacity, compared to the current voluntary approach. the text also proposes common temporary public health measures to create a safety net which would be of crucial importance in the event that the coordination of national responses proves insufficient in the face of an extreme emergency situation which could seriously jeopardise the protection of the union's population.
in writing. − health threats must be averted. today parliament voted a resolution establishing a european-wide rapid health alert system and a rule to facilitate cooperation between member states to buy vaccines. the measure adopted today will make it possible to declare a european emergency in the event of an epidemic or health crisis. this will increase the community's capacity to respond to cross-border health threats, such as the coronavirus or the 2009 and 2011 epidemics. this resolution will make access to vaccines more equitable, because they will be available at fairer prices. i can therefore only be satisfied that the legislation has been adopted. it represents a major step forward in the direction of greater protection of the health of european citizens.
in writing. the commission has presented a proposal for a decision providing the means and structures for effective protection of citizens across europe against a wide range of cross-border health threats. i am in favour of the proposal for a decision as it aims to increase the risk assessment and coordination measures currently applicable in the case of communicable diseases to all threats to health of biological, chemical or environmental origin and to strengthen the role of the health safety committee in view of better coordination of crisis management measures. i believe it is essential, in order to protect the patient, to recognise a european 'health emergency' with the aim of speeding up the supply of the necessary medicines. i believe that it is essential for the commission to adopt emergency crossborder measures in exceptional situations which cause deaths or hospitalisations on a large scale and in cases where member states' measures prove insufficient to control the spread of diseases from one country to another. the european centre for disease prevention and control should be supported as the official body for all information on the development of more or less contagious diseases.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a decision on serious crossborder threats to health, because i consider it essential to guarantee the right to health, especially in times of crisis. it is important that europe builds up its capacity to react, so that citizens are provided with the means and structures to deal with such situations. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council should be consulted on the draft directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to carcinogens at work. i believe, however, that in addition to promoting the work of the relevant internal bodies, such as the committee on health security, europe should be encouraged to cooperate with third countries and international organizations, first and foremost the world health organization. as regards health crises caused by the misuse of medicines or the marketing of defective medicines, it is desirable that everyone, both users and operators, appeal to the staff's common sense.
in writing. - the aim of mr pargneaux's report is to prevent crossborder threats to health by providing the european union with the means, networks and structures complementary to those already in place to protect its citizens in the face of such emergencies. in particular, i welcome the fact that today's vote will make it possible to coordinate the purchase of vaccines and medicines in europe in the event of a new pandemic, while keeping prices as low as possible: this is an important milestone especially for smaller countries that could not afford the exorbitant cost of vaccines during the last pandemics.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of mr podimata's report, which i congratulate on its excellent work. the financial transaction tax is expected to bring several tens of billions of euros into the eu's public coffers each year and help reduce speculative activities by making them more expensive and less profitable. i therefore fully support the revised proposal in the committee, which maintains the objective of combating evasion as well as capital transfers to other jurisdictions. i am therefore not concerned about the risks faced by banks and credit institutions who fear a flight of capital from the european union. the tax will not affect the financial sector itself, but its most dangerous parts such as automated high-frequency trading, that is, the financial sector which is at the origin of the serious economic crisis which is taking place and which must be decisively confronted.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i voted in favour of this report which calls for the introduction of a tax on financial transactions for several reasons. the crisis is very severe and affects the most vulnerable, citizens, businesses and households. this is no longer possible or acceptable. it is time to redistribute the cost of the crisis in a fairer and more equitable way. the new system must ensure that the banks also bear the burden of the crisis. the introduction of taxation has several advantages: the union's tax revenue could increase to up to eur 57 billion; the taxation will not affect the financial sector as a whole, but will limit the most speculative activities. italy is one of the 11 member states which have already adopted this tax, the so-called tobin tax. i hope that this directive will soon be introduced at global level too, so as to tackle evasion and increase benefits and ensure greater stability in the financial market.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, taxing high-risk financial speculation is essential to reducing distortions in the financial system. above all, it is right to say that the banks must also take up the crisis, just as citizens are demanding, especially as they are paying a very high price. the introduction of this tax will generate revenue of some eur 35 billion, which is a valuable additional resource to be allocated to measures for growth and employment. of course, its effectiveness is limited because not all the member states have joined. finally, some concern must be expressed about the application of this tax, albeit at a reduced rate, to government bonds.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the introduction of the tobin tax, the financial transaction tax, was a very courageous act designed to reverse the trend of taxation entirely concentrated on labour income and consumption. with this further act, which is now being voted on, after the previous votes in 2010 and 2011, the european union is demonstrating that it is able to overcome national egoisms, such as the british one, and is taking another act of courage that puts europe ahead of the rest of the world and constitutes a concrete act of anti-circumvention regulation of financial markets, which have enjoyed too much freedom and space for movement to the detriment of the economies of the states and their citizens. i voted in favour of this measure because it is a gesture of great ethical dignity towards a community of citizens who have been left at the mercy of the whims of the lords of financial transactions and i am convinced that acts of this kind will allow the real economy to reposition itself in relation to the speculative economy.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a council directive on the implementation of enhanced cooperation in the field of financial transaction taxation. indeed, as is well known, the 2008 financial crisis exposed serious shortcomings resulting from the long period of deregulation of financial services, with the result that the real economy was hit with serious consequences for growth, employment and public finances. the problems of the european union as a whole are still being faced. the european parliament has for the first time called for the introduction of a financial transaction tax, since the financial sector is not sufficiently taxed, since vat is not even envisaged, and because it would be appropriate to make a fairer contribution to the cost of the crisis. a progressive and socially fair tax and a fair instrument to shift the burden of the crisis from taxpayers to the financial sector.
in writing. - as members of the socialist and democratic group, we have repeatedly expressed our deep concern about the impact of the current economic crisis on the productive fabric of societies in the european countries. we have also denounced with equal force the error of believing that a simple austerity policy could be sufficient to prevent the financial crisis from causing a massive loss in productivity, jobs and, consequently, as reiterated by the istat, in the purchasing power of households. the outcome of the negotiations for the next multiannual budget of the european union 2014-2020 has shown that it is impossible to have a budget that fully meets the union's future challenges: the council has not in the least intended to call into question the level of appropriations. to reverse this trend, the community budget must change its composition. in view of the debate which will be opened on own resources, this is an opportunity to stress the extraordinary importance of the introduction of the financial transition tax, both as a means of generating a significant revenue for the community budget and as a concrete demonstration of the political will to involve the financial sector, which has contributed most to the recovery of the crisis by means of dangerous speculative operations, in the recovery of the crisis.
in writing. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competition' in the context of the directive. since this measure strengthens the single market, ensures that the financial sector contributes to the costs of the crisis, makes the market more efficient and introduces new sources of income, i am voting in favour.
in writing. - there are sound technical reasons for introducing a financial transaction tax. the 2008 crisis clearly showed that investors took too much risk, partly because financial products did not incorporate a correct assessment of their riskiness. securitisations and increasingly diversified portfolios had fed the illusion that risk had disappeared, generating growth in the production and trading of insurance derivatives. the cost of this glaring blunder, however, has not been borne only by investors but also by customers, employees, shareholders, ordinary citizens and even by all those financial institutions that had stayed away from subprime mortgages. the negative effects of financial activity and its repercussions on third parties are a fairly faithful reflection of the manual example of the factory which, with its waste, also ends up polluting the stream that flows nearby. a damage to the inhabitants of the neighboring village that has nothing to do with the factory. the podimata report is the result of rather complicated negotiations based on a series of compromises. finally, i would like to reiterate the importance of the question of financial taxation being placed as a priority on the agendas of the g8 and the g20.
in writing. this consultation of the european parliament on the taxation of financial transactions is really very important for all citizens of the european union and its implementation should be taken seriously. this tax is important in particular to make the financial sector, which is largely responsible for the crisis, bear the cost of the crisis, to discourage purely speculative operations, which do not benefit the real economy, and to avoid future crises. this tax does not affect small and medium-sized enterprises when they decide to raise funds on the financial markets, nor does it affect member states when they borrow on the financial markets. the text also reaffirms the need for eu representatives to promote a financial transaction tax at the global level, and more particularly at the g8 and g20. all these reasons make me vote in favour of this report.
in writing. - i supported the proposal for a council directive on a financial transaction tax (ftt) which covers a range of financial instruments from shares to bonds and derivatives and minimises the risk of circumvention and evasion.
in writing. − to reduce speculation and protect european citizens, this is the main objective of the report on the financial transaction tax. a clear sign of the european parliament's intention to regulate the financial sector by preventing the speculative activities that are at the origin of the economic crisis. the uniform application of the tax must be ensured by preventing any form of fragmentation of the internal market, and it is therefore necessary to harmonise the rates at european level and to provide for higher rates for financial transactions which are carried out outside unregulated markets. in addition, the revenue from the tax will have to be used to the benefit of the eu budget, where it could be used more productively. this revenue should not replace national contributions but could simply be added to them in order to increase the eu's spending capacity. however, it is necessary to provide for exemptions for non-speculative financial activities which fulfil a social function and support the real economy.
in writing. the commission has also proposed a new system of taxation for the financial services sector. the text confirms the tax rates proposed by the commission, namely 0.1% on transactions in shares and bonds and 0.01% on derivatives, and introduces clauses to make tax avoidance potentially much more onerous than the actual payment of tax. the payment of the financial transaction tax is linked to the acquisition of legal ownership rights, so that the purchaser of a security will not have actually owned it until he pays the financial transaction tax. i believe that this tax is the best way to help the sector emerge from the crisis and get back to the good work of serving the real economy. i therefore believe that what has been achieved in parliament today is a very good result and i hope that we will actually make a step forward in the direction of re-evaluating the european economy.
in writing. − the need for the financial sector to make a fair and essential contribution to covering the costs of the economic crisis is becoming more and more pressing. the financial system must be compact, serving the real economy and, above all, the common good. the financial transaction tax (ftt) is an effective instrument in this respect, because while it is a means of combating speculation, it also becomes a productive source of income that can be used to promote social and development policies, or for example environmental policies, which today require special support. i therefore voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a council directive implementing enhanced cooperation in the field of financial transaction tax. the fact that the itf is a product of enhanced cooperation between some of the member states should not be overlooked, in the sense that it would be desirable to ensure a harmonisation and efficiency of the collection mechanisms to avoid that the shortcomings of one state affect another, thus jeopardising the good outcome of the tax.
in writing. - it is not the first time that the european parliament has voted on this subject and mr podimata's report is the result of long and difficult negotiations and a series of compromises. it is clear that the financial transaction tax can generate significant new revenue at a time of great effort to consolidate public finances and can act as a buffer for purely speculative transactions, thus helping to stabilise financial markets and reorient the sector towards productive long-term investment.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the joint motion for a resolution on floods in europe because the natural disasters which now strike european countries with a certain frequency have increased considerably and continue to cause considerable damage and casualties. in order to deal with such situations in the best possible way, i believe that joint measures must be put in place to prevent such phenomena through broadly conceived strategies, which therefore involve a plurality of states and make it possible to assess risk management in a shared way. i think it is important to have territorial task forces studying the change in the soil and carrying out controls in order to safeguard the territory from continuous changes made by man. local authorities will have to demonstrate greater sensitivity through prevention policies for soil protection, also drawing on best practices used in other countries. i believe that more financial assistance is needed, promptly and adequately, to deal with emergencies in the best possible way and immediately, and that it would be useful to allocate more funds to disaster prevention and to the creation of projects that can mitigate the effects of disasters in areas considered at risk.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, it is essential to separate traditional banks from commercial banks in the interests of transparency and, above all, to avoid speculative drift. in the light of the monte dei paschi case in siena, i have repeatedly stressed that there should be zero tolerance for high-risk financial transactions without guarantees of transparency and accountability. above all, it is right to remember that it can no longer be the taxpayers, the citizens, who pay the cost of debts or the bankruptcies of banks. the legitimacy of all financial transactions must also be checked, also in accordance with the recommendations of the european banking authority, in order to protect the economy, citizens and businesses so that banks can rebuild confidence, so that the economy and development can return to a virtuous link with banks.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by my colleague mrs mccarthy on banking reform because i share parliament's commitment to act to ensure that europe builds as soon as possible the banking union that our economy needs. i share the call for the principles of reducing complexity, improving competition, improving corporate governance, creating a responsible remuneration system. i appreciate steps like this that can lead to a change in banking culture.
in writing. the european banking sector has a number of institutions that are considered 'too big to fail' and it is on these that the econ committee has focused its attention. at the end of 2012, the liikanen report highlighted that some causes of the crisis are also due to the connections that have been created between banks. the commission is proposing a reform to avoid spending public money to subsidize credit institutions and to increase the protection of retail customers, while also promoting access to credit for smes. since the aim is to reduce the size and complexity of banks, i am voting in favour.
in writing. − the objective of using the structure of the banking system to make it both more solid and secure, but also more flexible and able to respond to the needs of the economy and society as a whole, must be pursued with determination. we must wait until autumn to see what legislative proposals the commission will put forward. certainly some key words deserve to be repeated. it's simplification and competition. i would add to these the key issue of access to credit. we must build a near future in which a european entrepreneur can enter a bank with confidence and hope, and obtain trust and resources from the credit institution. today, unfortunately, that is not the case. it's not easy. the european institutions, and first and foremost, if i may say so, the european central bank, can work effectively in this direction by encouraging a policy of confidence and the opening up of credit lines.
in writing. the report by arlene mccarthy incorporates the recommendations of the liikanen group, which was convened to decide whether further structural measures should be taken to prevent further financial and economic crises. the group's conclusions are reproduced in this report and they are in favour of a separation of investment banks and deposit banks for savers. responsible banking practices must be promoted, leading to fewer economic shocks and fewer dangers for the real economy, which is the only one that is perceptible and useful to citizens and democracy. i therefore gave my vote in favour.
in writing. - i supported the proposal to reform the structure of the eu banking sector as a sector with a strong impact on the conditions of the european economy. the recent financial crises have shown how crucial it is to reform the structure of the banking system to make it more stable, efficient, secure and better integrated with the real economy and consumers.
in writing. - the separation of banking activities between risky and retail activities is undoubtedly a good way of simplifying the banking structure by making it more transparent. after the financial crisis it was clear that the european banking sector as a whole needed to be reformed, so banking reform was indispensable and necessary. we must be ambitious and aim for a true banking union. only then can we finally have a more stable and secure credit system which can restore the transmission mechanism between banks and the real economy. the banking union is therefore the turning point for the resumption of growth.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the reform of the structure of the banking sector in the european union because it is necessary to remedy the shortcomings in the current system, which in many countries do not allow the economy to unlock in favour of development policies, paralysing our businesses and our internal markets. solutions must be found to reduce the likelihood of national bank failures and the catastrophic impact on savers and businesses. structural reform of the banking system is necessary to safeguard citizens and protect the economic functions of enterprises. the banking system today appears to be too complex and involved in a multiplicity of fields which take it away from its primary function and i believe that a separation of the risk activities of banks from the collection of deposits and the granting of loans is necessary. the banking structures must be simplified, making them simpler and more transparent, and the supervisory systems must be strengthened to prevent crisis situations from burdening customers and governments. it is desirable to create a new, stable and secure circuit which meets the needs of savers and enables them to obtain credit to finance their activities.
in writing. − i voted for this report because it denounces the continuing problems with lack of standardised reporting of fraud by member states, despite their obligation under the treaty to share responsibility with the commission for fighting fraud in eu expenditure and revenue. in addition i think that is important to emphasise the need to intensify further the fight against customs-related fraud and that, given the fact that fraud is increasingly being committed across international borders, a stronger legal framework, with clear commitments from the partner countries, is needed. regarding olaf, i welcome the initiative to reform it, especially in order to strengthen its capacity to tackle fraud in the eu’s external policy dimension.
in writing. − the commission report com ((2012) 0408) specifies that the commission itself and the member states are obliged to fight against fraud and other illegal activities, protecting the eu's financial interests at the level of collection and expenditure. however, eu countries define the same offences differently and do not all use the same statistical criteria. it is therefore difficult to assess fraud uniformly. part of the report then presents the allegation that olaf initiated investigative actions which were atypical compared to those provided for under articles 3 and 4 of regulation (ec) no 1073/1999. given all these considerations, i am voting against the proposal.
in writing. - first of all, i would like to express my appreciation for the work done by mr vaughan. secondly, i would like to call on the commission to draw up an annual report in which the data on irregularities/fraud can be compared by means of a balanced analysis of the different anti-fraud systems in place in the member states (and therefore of the different capacity to detect fraud) and of the different methods/timing for sending data on the cases of irregularities/fraud detected. why do i think this annual report is appropriate? because i believe it will make it possible to reject any possible and eventual attempt to return to the 'baseline of old 'commonplaces', according to which, paradoxically, a greater number of cases of irregularity/fraud detected and reported honestly by an ms than others, can lead not only to a negative label specifically against that member state, but also to further and more burdensome and unfair consequences such as reduction of funding and penalties.
in writing. − the fight against fraud must be conducted jointly, both at national and european level; the commission has also been asked to provide information on the implementation of the new rules on the protection of the financial interests of the union. the defence of the financial interests of the union is in the interest of all of us, because it is our money, which is taken from the whole community in the event of fraudulent behaviour. the customs controls must therefore be improved, and it must be said that, for once at least, italy is at the forefront in this field, and it is rather the ports of northern europe that often carry out approximate and complacent controls. agriculture and cohesion policy, or the regional structural funds, are other areas where massive action is needed, because they are unfortunately subject to frequent cases of fraud. in addition to being an important economic battle, the fight against fraud is also a matter of civilization, since the 'cheating mentality' has no place in italy or europe.
in writing. the control of public expenditure and the fight against fraud are essential to obtain the confidence of citizens and sound and fair accounts for the proper implementation of the european union's aid programmes. the report notes the significant decrease in fraud in recent times. mr vaughan asks the supervisory bodies in each member state to put in place stricter measures to avoid lax examinations of files, especially in this time of crisis where every euro spent must be spent sparingly and rigorously. i therefore vote in favour of this report.
in writing. - i supported the european parliament's motion for a resolution on the protection of the european union's financial interests against fraud. fraudulent irregularities have a significant impact on the eu's finances and it is therefore essential to tackle this type of crime through measures to coordinate the collection of revenue between member states and customs, and to strengthen the efficiency of olaf.
in writing. - i gave a favourable opinion on the report on the annual report on the protection of the eu's financial interests because the financial impact of fraud and illegal activities is also a concern for the market and the community budget. the fight against fraud must be one of the union's priorities because it damages the whole system and in this time of economic crisis it is necessary to ensure that eu funds invested in the member states are well spent and entrusted to those who really need them. despite the progress made in recent years in the recovery of amounts wrongly received, work is needed to ensure that control systems are increasingly effective and that they are assessed on their results. to facilitate this task, each state will have to commit itself to providing detailed information on internal controls, so as to allow for more accurate geographical analyses and intervention manoeuvres. in the meantime, member states will have to try to recover unduly collected sums and it would be desirable to make a greater effort to streamline judicial processes by speeding up recovery. it is also necessary to define standard assessment criteria in all member states, coupled with appropriate penalties for offenders, and to provide greater support to the areas most affected by the phenomenon.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by my colleague on the integrated internal control framework because i believe that the internal audit model used in the eu needs to be optimised. the various partners in the process need to work together to ensure that procedures are carried out properly, involving in particular the member states which manage most of the funds in the context of day-to-day management. it will be necessary to work on common principles by providing the necessary guarantees on the regularity of transactions at each level of budget implementation and it may be necessary to use independent audit bodies to provide further guarantees on transactions. in collaboration with the member states, a model for national management declarations should be defined in order to better analyse the strengths and weaknesses of control systems, so as to assess the conformity of the results of the beneficiaries. i therefore believe that a broad collaboration of all stakeholders is needed to make further progress in this area and to maximise the benefits of union policies, and that it might also be useful to launch 'pilot projects' to evaluate the results of the various controls.

vice-president of the commission. − mr president, i would like to thank andrew duff not only for his presentation today but for over the years helping to build up a real european space. he is absolutely right: the voters’ participation in the european elections has steadily decreased from 62% in 1979 to 43% in 2009, but we see this happening not only in the european elections, it happens in the same way in national and regional polls. hence i believe that, if we start to think about how we can ameliorate participation in the european elections, it will help at the same time to ameliorate the participation in the national and regional polls. the commission has made a continued effort to encourage political participation and to improve citizens’ awareness of their rights in the eu. i remind you of the first eu citizenship report in 2010 and the 25 very concrete proposals which i put on the table then. the good news is that the 25 proposals have been implemented or are in the process of being implemented. the second citizenship report, in may 2013, has taken stock of the many proposals which we received from the citizens themselves, be it in the dialogues which we lead in the different member states, in the consultations which we have made on the internet, or be it by taking into account the essence of the more than one million requests the european union receives every year. so there we put on the table another 12 proposals to be completed before the end of this mandate and one of these proposals is to help citizens have a stronger awareness of their electoral right, particularly in the case of first-time voters. after the european year of citizens and having taken into account the experiences learnt during this year, the commission will produce a handbook presenting the most important eu rights of citizens in clear and simple language. furthermore, we will seek to strengthen and develop the european public space. what have we seen in our eurobarometers? for instance, eight out of ten citizens tell us they would be more motivated to vote if they knew more about the european union. there is very often a deficit of knowledge about what the rights and possibilities are and, by the way, what this house does for european citizens. i was very much astonished during the citizens’ dialogues to learn of citizens’ lack of knowledge about the effects and powers of the european parliament. other eurobarometers show that seven out of ten citizens believe that if they knew more about their national party and its affiliation to its umbrella european parties, that would greatly help, and six out of ten think that having party candidates for the commission president and a single voting day would also help the turnout. on the basis of this, on 12 march this year the commission issued its recommendation to national and european political parties and to the member states to further enhance the democratic, transparent and efficient conduct of the european elections, and we completely agree in our proposals with what andrew duff has just said in his presentation. i would like therefore to thank the parliament and its rapporteur for addressing all these issues and to take up also the proposals of our recommendation. we coincide in most of our proposals, but mostly we coincide in the will to reinforce the legitimacy of the eu decision-making process and bring this system closer to the citizens. the report also points to the need for an electoral campaign based on european party platforms and programmes. i believe that this is very important and will send a positive signal to citizens across the eu; citizens should know what they are voting for and it should be very transparent. they should also know where their elected candidates will sit in this parliament and for which programme they will stand. this is also the sense of the commission’s proposal to strengthen the effectiveness of all european political parties, because this proposal would give the european political parties greater visibility and enable them to operate across the eu by giving them a genuine european legal status. i believe that this will also be very important and i know we can count on the european parliament to work hand in hand with us in order to achieve our goals.
the european union has gradually become a union based on the dual legitimacy of citizens and states, with the introduction of direct elections to the european parliament and the subsequent conferral of increased powers and prerogatives on the latter. this development, enshrined in the treaty of lisbon, requires the creation of a genuine european political area in order to realize its full potential. the resolution we are voting on tomorrow proposes a number of practical measures of a non-legislative and non-constitutional nature which, if adopted, could make a significant contribution to strengthening the genuinely european character of the 2014 elections. in particular, many of the proposed measures revolve around the main innovation, the nomination by european political parties of their candidates for the post of president of the commission. this is a crucial innovation which is going to profoundly change the nature of the relationship of trust between parliament and the european commission and it is very positive that it is now supported by the commission itself. i would also like to remind those who have expressed scepticism, such as chancellor merkel, that the treaty clearly states that the president of the commission is elected by parliament and that the european council's proposal must take account of the result of the elections and be submitted after appropriate consultations, and these consultations obviously cannot concern the person whom the president is to elect, namely parliament, because it would be absurd to think that the phrase refers to the member states which are already members of the european council and which therefore do not need to consult each other. if, therefore, in the european elections in may next year, the citizens of europe are to vote not only for a national party but for a european party and thus also for the leadership of the commission, the electoral campaign and the voting process must give material shape to a european political space which makes the electorate's choice fully aware and informed. we are convinced that if this happens, and if the recommendations contained in this report are followed, the forthcoming elections will be a decisive step in the building of a political and democratic europe capable of meeting the challenges of the 21st century and of giving substance to its values and principles.

in writing. in the digital sector, europe is struggling to keep up with the innovation levels of other advanced economies. in my view, this gap cannot be filled without a true digital single market. in this context, i welcome the efforts of the community institutions to remove the remaining barriers to the completion of the european digital market, including the request by the eu council last march to the commission to draw up, by next october, an ad hoc plan to push digital harmonisation at continental level. i believe that the delay in the completion of the digital single market risks severely penalizing the investments of european companies compared to their american competitors who benefit from a strong internal market regulated in an open and digital-friendly manner. in times of economic and financial crisis, action to stimulate growth and create jobs is essential, emphasising that the completion of the digital single market would be a crucial step towards achieving this objective. in the light of these considerations, i would draw the attention of the european commission to the need to implement its plan for the launch and completion of the digital single market as soon as possible.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, the paradox of this debate is terrible. we are here to discuss the effects and consequences of our choices, our policies. the area of vulnerability, which affects the whole life cycle, namely children, women, young people, immigrants, the elderly, is growing because in recent years we have pursued a blind policy of austerity, which has cut our public budgets and thus called into question an entire model of welfare and social well-being to the point that in many european countries we are privatising what has been public for 10, 15, 20, 30 years and which made social investment the substance and identity of european policy. what then? first of all, we must reverse these policies - we cannot do it with policies to contain public finances - and resume a policy of public investment which reduces the risk area and puts in place preventive policies. at the same time - and this is the last point - we are trying to use cohesion policy, including integrated territorial investment, to bring together the social fund and the erdf, neighbourhoods, housing and also active assistance policies.
in writing. there is widespread fear that the crisis we have been experiencing in recent years has not yet unfolded its most severe effects. the policies put in place so far have proved ineffective in countering the most serious social effects and, in many cases, have had a counterproductive effect, leading to a marked worsening of situations of greatest vulnerability. the most vulnerable situations are those that have been worst affected by the crisis because, to an initial situation of weakness, the effects of linear cuts in essential services have been added. among these, health services and universal access to care should be considered non-negotiable elements, the maintenance and availability of which are essential for large sections of the european population. the austerity path is wrong and economically ineffective, but it also risks exacerbating injustice and suffering; europe, even and especially in a time of crisis, must defend and strengthen its social model, for this is the only way to fairly define the way out of the crisis.
