in writing. − the services sector is an important resource for the european union. i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on the opening of negotiations for a multilateral agreement on services, because i believe that europe must become increasingly integrated into a multilateral trading system in order to maintain and strengthen its competitiveness on a world scale. services are an essential element of the economy and trade and a source of social cohesion for citizens, from the local to the community level. i share the concern that the parties to the negotiations do not include the emerging markets and the brics countries, which would make a significant contribution as they have a steady and significant growth in trade and investment in services, but often face obstacles, especially in relation to foreign investment: the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the draft budget for the financial year. in the negotiations, european sensitivities concerning public services and services of general interest, such as public education, public health, water supply and waste disposal, must be taken into account.
in writing. the european union has been fighting for free trade since its foundation. this is not simply a declaration of principle, of course, but a battle in which a great many achievements have been made, including greater freedom of choice over the vast majority of goods and services, and lower costs through improved efficiency of firms in a more competitive market. clearly, like all political choices, there are pros and cons. however, when a country like norway defends its own agricultural production by artificially reducing the competitiveness of imported products, it does damage in two ways: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's energy policy is not undermined by the failure of the member states to implement the directive. and fortunately for other countries the norwegian market is rarely strategic, while for italy in particular i do not foresee major problems, relying on the willingness of the norwegians to pay higher prices in order to have italian quality at the table. i voted in favour of this resolution to underline the vulnus which norway has created in the international trading system.
in writing. the continuing increase in norwegian duties on agricultural products could not leave the european parliament indifferent. the house has today made its position clear by calling on the norwegian government to amend the recent measures taken, in clear violation of the letter and spirit of the bilateral agreement. the economic logic behind these measures is not seen, which have the effect not only of reducing trade but also of harming european and norwegian producers in the long run. i also think it is essential that the european commission expresses its opinion on the matter and clarifies what measures it intends to take in the event that norway does not wish to reverse its course.
in writing. - norway cannot be condemned at all, since it is only doing what the european union should do, namely defending its own interests. in this particular case, it is a kind of small trade war between sweden and norway, and oslo has every right to take whatever measures it deems appropriate to protect its products. the european union, instead of criticising this decision, should take it as an example and defend its own commercial interests vis-à-vis our non-eu partners. in brussels, on the other hand, they believe that protectionism is a kind of dangerous 'disease' that we must eradicate at all costs: nothing could be more wrong, because in doing so we expose ourselves too much to no defense. some timid initiatives, such as the eu's tariffs on photovoltaic panels and ceramics, have provoked strong reactions both outside and within the european union itself, demonstrating a clear contrast of views, which the name "union" alone cannot heal and hide. in the field of trade policy we have at least two european unions: the north, the big multinationals, who would like to have the doors open to relocate and do business elsewhere, and the rest of europe, the heart of small manufacturing, which is in danger of being crushed.
in writing. - i supported the european parliament's motion for a resolution on international trade concerning the increase in norwegian duties on agricultural products, condemning the recent protectionist measures imposed by the norwegian government which could have a negative impact on trade in the whole of the european union.

mr president, commissioner, the phenomenon of mobility among european citizens - a phenomenon of enormous positive significance - has brought the problem we are discussing to the fore, that is, it has brought the problem of the relationship between citizens who marry or are in registered partnerships despite having different nationalities to the fore more forcefully than before. the solution we can find is important and positive, but there is a problem, which the rapporteur has pointed out, not by chance, and which must be solved. the distinction between marriage and registered partnerships is justified only if the same rules and rights apply in both cases. for marriage to be neutral, it is necessary that those in a registered union also be free from discrimination. it is therefore necessary to take account of the indications given by the court and the european agency for fundamental rights and to allow registered partnerships to choose the law applicable to their property regime. only then will there be true unity.
mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i would first of all like to congratulate the rapporteur and the shadow rapporteurs on the excellent work they have done in the legislative process on this regulation on the property regime for marriages and registered couples. after two years of difficult negotiations and in the face of the extreme complexity of the matter, i am very satisfied with the result achieved. the compromise reached will help to achieve the three main objectives of the reform: the establishment of a clear and uniform legal system for determining the court with jurisdiction and the applicable law, the freedom of choice between the parties and the facilitation of the recognition and enforcement of judicial decisions. i am particularly pleased with the compromise reached on the freedom of choice of law for registered couples. the solution found respects the cultural and legal traditions of the member states and makes it possible to break the difficult political deadlock on this issue. finally, i agree with the rapporteur that it is still premature to abolish the exequatur. this regulation concerns a legal institution which is still very different from one member state to another and, since it introduces substantial new elements, it is necessary to wait for it to become more stable over time.
the commission has already submitted a proposal for a regulation on the common organization of the market in bananas. - mr president, as has already been stressed and according to research, the production of traditional biofuels has negative effects on food prices and climate change because of the so-called 'indirect land use change' which generates an increase in greenhouse gas emissions. for this very reason, the commission has tried to address this problem by recommending limits on so-called conventional biofuels that use food crops as their raw material. the committee on regional development also considered the territorial implications of the new directive, namely that renewable energy and biofuels for transport are often produced by small and medium-sized enterprises, so that the sector's regulation has an impact on the production fabric of many regions of the union. the proposal under discussion will lead to a reduction in the production of traditional biofuels and thus to a reduction in employment in many regions. it is logical that advanced biofuels can generate new growth and jobs, but it is precisely for this reason that it is urgent that the commission should assess more precisely the social and economic impact of the proposal by promoting the use of the structural funds and research.
mr president, the text approved by the committee on the environment, public health and food safety seeks to highlight and at least partially remedy the harmful consequences of the use of biofuels derived from agricultural raw materials, especially in developing countries. the transposition of the two directives on renewable energy and fuel quality has in the past encouraged the massive use of biofuels, but it has hidden the other side of the coin: the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council adopt a common position on the proposal for a directive on the protection of the environment and the working environment. among the most damaging consequences are the rising prices of agricultural raw materials used to produce biofuels and the growing phenomenon of land grabbing in developing countries. added to this is the production of additional co2 emissions as a result of changes in the use of cultivated land and the change in the use of large areas and land for new agroenergy crops. in the face of almost universal indifference, we have been undermining the biodiversity of many countries for years, with negative repercussions also from the social, agricultural and economic points of view. i therefore believe that the european union must now take a strong signal of change, by reconsidering the virtuousness of current biofuels, which has not been disputed so far, in relation to the targets set in the two directives mentioned, by taking account of their full effects and by taking a decisive step in the direction of the next generation of biofuels, often produced from waste and residues, on which many virtuous companies in europe are already starting to invest.
mr president, as has also been shown during the committee's work, this is a subject on which there are still very different and often very distant positions. there is no doubt that biofuels are a reality that has a market and is expanding more and more both geographically and technologically. when we add new elements to a policy already in place - as in this case - we cannot ignore what has already been done and the amount of investment mobilised to create the production chains that exist today. alongside our efforts to achieve the highest possible sustainability, we must always pay close attention to the competitiveness and soundness of the european energy system. i agree with the limitation of biofuels produced from raw materials that also produce food, but i am also strongly in favour of biofuels from advanced materials. the minimum threshold proposed by the two committees itre and envi is in line with what i believe is useful for this sector.
mr president, if it is true that a litre of biofuel requires 2,500 litres of water and that the land used to grow biofuels in 2008 would have fed 127 million people, i think some reflection is needed. we must ask ourselves whether, with the standards we set a few years ago, with the high expectations, if we continue along this path, we are not really going in the wrong direction and against our intentions. it is good that when an error is made, even from the point of view of forecasting, it is corrected promptly, clearly and decisively. i personally do not see any inconsistency in my being a member of the itre and deve committees, because i believe that we must try to be consistent in our policy choices and not that we must implement sectoral policies which cause negative effects which we must then correct with other sectoral policies. now, the proposals on the ground seem reasonable to me; i am in favour of a drastic reduction in the ceiling forecasts, i am in favour of 5 per cent (we shall see how the majority of this house will react), i am in favour of encouraging the second generation. the technologies are there, they are available, they have been produced with european union funds, so they are being put into practice! i also share the concern, which was very clearly expressed by the chairman of the committee on industry, research and energy, about the need to safeguard existing investments, which are also based on our forecasts. it seems to me that this protection of investments is contained in the text under discussion, but it must be emphasized. i think, however, that the investments made in the first generation have not yet reached the growth margin that we could set even with a halving of the target. so there is still room for growth and, most importantly, there is room for incentivizing new investments that do not make this very deleterious and damaging conflict between food and fuel. we need both of you for our future!

answer to a blue-card question. mr turmes, i agree with what you asked before i was interrupted the first time, namely that commissioner oettinger should work with commissioner almunia on a review of this state aid matter. i would also like to make this request so that examples such as those of the cooperatives can be made possible. this parliament has approved a report on energy-generating cooperatives and the possibility of providing for different production models, different industrial models, belonging to large industries or cooperative enterprises, which are still industries, albeit different. i believe that the european state aid rules must be adapted to these differences.

the rapporteur. mr president, i should like to begin by thanking the committee for the work it has done to approve this report by a very large majority, on which the house will be voting tomorrow, because it points to a path of certain interest to fishermen in the adriatic and ionian seas, but above all it represents a milestone in the reasoning that is to be introduced with regard to the whole of the mediterranean. first of all, the context in which this report is set is one in which the european commission is working on a maritime strategy for the adriatic sea, and that is that through a communication last november, based on a push from the adriatic countries, certain italian regions and croatia, which has just joined the european union determined the need to have an overall strategy on the maritime policies of this macro-region. this report fits into that framework, because it captures in substance some peculiarities of this sea, which i shall speak about in a moment. the other important context in which this report is being made - and it is therefore important that parliament approves it tomorrow - is that we are in the midst of the launching of the new fisheries policy: the european parliament will vote on the reform within the year, and the new seven-year period for the european fisheries and maritime fund will begin, which will determine the resources for the development of this sector in the coming years. the context is important because this report comes at a particular moment, when it has become clear that the existing legislation for that sea is too general to be able to regulate the issues of this defined maritime area as a whole. the adriatic, unlike the mediterranean, is a closed sea, where economic problems coexist which are totally different from those of the rest of the mediterranean. there is a different type of seabed, different fishing practices, a different history and tradition, a totally different system of international relations from the rest of the mediterranean. we are facing a sea of enclosure, with three countries that are part of europe - italy, slovenia and croatia - and three other countries with other rules and a different kind of mechanism, yet so close and so connected in terms of economic development. the same rules apply in all these countries as in the rest of the mediterranean. this is a serious limitation, because any action by the european union is likely to be in vain. the application of the control regulation on this sea is in vain, as is the effectiveness of the protection of existing fishery resources, which leads to a substantial impoverishment of fisheries and very often to a very strong economic and social burden. the commission's proposal is to be submitted to the council for adoption by the end of the year. the first: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. the second: the rules cannot be generic and apply to the whole of europe because there are objective differences. in conclusion, mr president, all this is being channelled into the process which is being set up in the whole sector, namely that of a pushed-forward regionalisation, if we really want the rules to be general and their application to be local. i think this report is an important milestone for the commission.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, parliament has repeatedly called for the strengthening of the procedural rights of the accused and the defendant, stressing the need to strike the right balance between freedom, justice and security. some of the measures in the roadmap agreed during the swedish presidency have already been implemented. the directive on the right to interpretation and translation in criminal proceedings and the directive on the right to information in criminal proceedings are among them. the proposal for a directive on the right of access to a lawyer in criminal proceedings and the right to be informed upon arrest is the third stage in the implementation of the roadmap. this report sets out the basic principle that all suspects and accused persons should have access to a lawyer as soon as possible, in order to enable them to exercise their rights of defence effectively. citizens must be able to count on full respect for their rights and be convinced that their security is guaranteed. i believe that this report is going in that direction and that is why i have decided to support it.

in writing. − the european parliament has always supported the need to ensure greater protection of the rights of victims of crime on the one hand and of suspects or accused persons on the other, strongly urging the introduction of an ambitious legal instrument on procedural guarantees in criminal proceedings. despite the existence of common principles and minimum standards deriving from both the echr and the eu charter, existing provisions in this area continue to vary significantly between member states. we regret that the provisions of the european convention on human rights and the case law of the european court of human rights are not uniformly applied and respected by the member states, with the result that there are divergent rules within the european union. in adopting this report, we are calling for the strengthening of the procedural rights of the accused and the defendant, stressing the need to strike the right balance between freedom, justice and security. european citizens must be able to count on full respect for their rights, be convinced that their safety is guaranteed when travelling and be aware that they enjoy the same guarantees in all member states.
in writing. - i supported this resolution which enshrines the basic principle that all suspects and accused persons should have access to a lawyer as soon as possible and in a manner which allows the effective exercise of their rights of defence. such rights must be ensured before the commencement of any interrogation, when procedural documents or evidence are taken and in the event of deprivation of liberty. the proposal also sets out the content of the right, stresses that meetings between the accused and his lawyer should be confidential, lists the exceptions to the general principles and provides for certain rules in the event of waiver of the right to a lawyer. finally, it recognizes the right to an interpreter, a right which has become indispensable since the freedom of movement of european citizens.
in writing. − the rights of suspects and accused persons in criminal proceedings in the european union are fundamental rights guaranteed by the eu charter and the european court of human rights. the text just voted defines definitively the minimum rights guaranteed for access to a lawyer in criminal proceedings; common minimum standards strengthening the procedural rights of suspects and accused persons. all eu countries will therefore have to guarantee access to a lawyer, the possibility for the accused to converse privately with the latter and the possibility of communicating with a third party at the time of arrest, thus strengthening the rights of the defence in criminal proceedings.
in writing. − the right of access to a lawyer is an essential part of the core rights enshrined by the european convention on human rights and the eu charter of fundamental rights. in the absence of further enhancements of regulations, however, it is hard to ensure that such rights are protected in practice, especially in criminal procedures. common minimum standards regarding the right of access to a lawyer and the right to communicate in the event of arrest not only promote mutual recognition of judicial decisions in criminal matters, but also prevent coercion on the part of the investigating authorities, ensure equality of arms between prosecution and defence, and reduce miscarriages of justice, which benefits our community. therefore, i voted in favour of this proposal.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council establishing the right of access to a lawyer in criminal proceedings and the right to be informed when arrested, because access to an effective defence in criminal proceedings is a key moment for eu legal policy. the proposal also seeks to adopt a horizontal and global instrument, proposing a gradual, less ambitious and more realistic approach.

mr president, we need quality legislation to strengthen consumer protection both at the contractual and pre-contractual stages. customers should receive all the information from intermediaries in order to conclude a contract in an informed and prudent manner. to further protect the client, the directive provides for the granting of authorization to intermediaries based on the possession of harmonised professional requirements. i agree with the rapporteur that mortgages are the most important long-term financial commitment of a family. often it is a matter of sacrificing a life. consider that mortgages are essential to access real estate in 70 percent of cases.
mr president, the proposal for a directive aims to harmonize the subject of consumer loans for the purchase of residential property and mortgage loans. the measures aimed at protecting consumers are to be regarded as positive. this is done by defining a minimum set of information which must be exchanged between the potential customer and the intermediaries in order to reach an informed and prudent conclusion of the contract through the introduction of the granting of an authorization based on the possession of requirements of professionalism and honesty. i have decided to vote in favour of the measures contained in the report, but i would like to express my doubts as to whether the report can at the same time be an effective instrument against the financial crisis. i do not think that an internal market for residential property loans is possible, since the markets have a strong local footprint and local advice is needed. the crossborder demand is rather low and there are considerable language barriers, not to mention the difficulties arising from the profound differences between the legal systems of the member states.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this directive on mortgage loans because it lays the foundations for a genuine european mortgage market. at the same time, it preserves systems that have so far proven to work very well. the final document, which was the result of lengthy negotiations with the council and the european commission, sets in motion a process of credit market integration which can be further developed in the future. the importance of regulation is clear to all, especially when one considers that the bursting of the housing bubble in the united states was the very cause of the economic crisis that continues to this day. it was the lack of controls on the credit system that triggered the crisis, and the european union's effort in recent years has been precisely to improve the efficiency, resilience and transparency of the system, while ensuring greater protection for consumers.
in writing. - i supported the sánchez-presedo report on the proposal for a european parliament and council directive on credit agreements relating to residential immovable property. i agree with the text which proposes greater control and transparency in the mortgage market to better protect european citizens by guaranteeing transparency and information to consumers and by imposing on credit institutions the obligation to monitor and ensure that contractors do not take on excessive financial risks.
in writing. - i voted to postpone the final decision on this very delicate proposal for a directive. we cannot afford to make hasty mistakes when the protection of mortgage claimants is at stake. in particular, at this time of tight credit, the competent institutions must protect the rights of those who want to take risks and who need loans to do so. i am in favour of the whole proposal. i am not saying that the commission should not be involved in this, but i am saying that it should be involved in the negotiations. however, the internal market aspect cannot be underestimated. i therefore asked for a little more time so that we could also reach agreement on the comparative tables.
in writing. - the purchase of a home of one's own is the dream of every citizen, and it is therefore right that there should be the best conditions for this to be realized. however, we must not forget the problems that have arisen in recent years with the granting of "rainy" loans, often without the slightest guarantees. but we have gone from one extreme to the other, and today for many young people, perhaps with precarious jobs, it is becoming impossible even to enter the real estate market. we cannot ignore the problems of the difficulties of paying the instalments of a mortgage due to the crisis: i would like to ask the commissioner whether he is aware that the commission has not yet taken a decision on the matter. some spanish regions have already moved in this direction: i hope that others, like italy, will follow this path because we cannot forget that we must first protect the people, and then the interests of the banks. what ?
in writing. − after lengthy negotiations with the council and the european commission, agreement was reached last may on the final text for the directive on credit agreements relating to residential immovable property. the main objective of the text, for which i was the shadow rapporteur for the epp, was to ensure greater consumer protection without burdening the credit system with greater burdens and costs. in the econ committee we avoided over-regulation which would only have blocked the credit market, and we also strongly insisted on quality regulation rather than quantity to avoid a situation similar to the 2008 housing bubble. this is a first decisive step towards a european mortgage market, which introduces a number of new features: the commission has also proposed a number of measures to improve the quality of the information provided by credit institutions, such as eu-wide harmonisation of pre-contractual information, a general right to early termination, a credit assessment not based solely on automatic mechanisms, a seven-day cooling-off period and stricter regulation for credit intermediaries. now, in order to approve the final legislative text, we are only waiting for the final arrangements with the council.
in writing. - under the new rules, the contractor who wants a loan in foreign currency will have to be informed prior to the signing of the contract that the amount of the instalments to be paid may increase. alternatively, the borrower may be allowed to change the currency, under certain conditions and at the exchange rate specified in the loan agreement. it is also considered that buyers should be able to benefit from a seven-day cooling-off period before taking out a loan or from the same period of time to exercise the right of withdrawal even after the contract has been concluded. housing is a primary value and i believe it is essential to help european citizens to prevent and support difficulties in buying.
in writing. the sanchez-presedo report, which lays the foundations for a european mortgage market, concerns the conditions applicable to creditors and credit intermediaries, the competent authorities and the supervisory requirements (which need to be strengthened in a manner consistent with the new european supervisory system). the main objective of parliament was to ensure greater consumer protection without burdening the credit system with greater burdens and costs, and avoiding over-regulation which would have the effect of blocking the credit market. the most important new features include harmonisation at community level of pre-contractual information, a general right to early termination, a credit assessment not based solely on automatic mechanisms, a seven-day cooling-off period and stricter regulation for credit intermediaries.
mr president, this proposal for a directive substantially revises the adm directive on internal market abuse, seeking to fill in the gaps and increase investor confidence and market integrity. the implantation generated by the proposal is certainly positive. however, it is in relation to the sanctions to be applied that we have seen the most heated debates between member states and between council and parliament. i would hope that the trilogues would seek to achieve greater harmonization of the penal system in line with, among other things, the position expressed by parliament. the time limit for exercising the option contained in the compromise, which is 24 months from the entry into force of the regulation, is considered satisfactory. however, i hope that the commission will assess the need for greater harmonisation of the member states' sanctioning regimes in the short term, otherwise i doubt that sanctions at eu level will be effective, dissuasive and proportionate in all member states.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mrs mccarthy's report on insider dealing and market manipulation. i agree with the rapporteur's hard line, which calls for stricter sanctions for those who distort the market to their own advantage.
in writing. - in the public imagination, the financial sector is one of the last in terms of perceived morality. there is a widespread misconception that finance does not create value, that the so-called "paper economy" is only for making money and getting rich without taking risks. these commonplaces, besides being patently false, are a brake on the bond of trust between savers and fund managers and risk jeopardising the integrity of the entire european financial system. i therefore believe that it is very important to monitor the financial markets as well as the markets for goods, services and labour, in order to detect abuses on the one hand and to detect and discourage abusive tendencies on the other. i voted in favour of this measure because it goes exactly in this direction: the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos at work is a very good one.
in writing. - it is undeniable that financial markets are a jungle in which it is very difficult to venture, especially if there are some players who play a dirty game, i.e. artificially manipulating data and abusing yield positions. this european regulation should serve precisely to prevent and, where appropriate, to punish such illegal behaviour, which is a real financial crime. market participants need to be fully aware of the nature of their investments, including the risks, in order to have a complete picture and to manage their choices in the best way. unfortunately, in the past, even in recent times, there have been too many instances of insider trading and market manipulation, to the point where, for example, the libor limit case, the benchmark rate governing interbank lending, has been found to have been artificially manipulated for several years. these fraudulent actions are causing significant economic damage and are also contributing to casting further shadows on a financial sector in which confidence has already been at a low ebb for some time: the solution to a healthy market is to ensure that the actors in it are completely fair, and that is my wish in supporting this report.
in writing. - i supported this resolution; the market abuse directive (mad) 2003/6/ec introduced a comprehensive regulatory framework to deal with 'market abuse' (insider dealing and market manipulation) practices. the proposal extends the scope of the market abuse framework to all financial instruments covered by the markets in financial instruments directive (mifid) in order to strengthen market integrity and investor protection, while ensuring a single regulatory text and a level playing field. while more than 80% of the emission allowance market is a derivative market, the new market abuse regulation aims to extend market protection to the primary market in order to avoid fraudulent practices that could undermine confidence in the ets. if ets allowances are reclassified as financial instruments in the context of the review of the mifid directive and fall within the scope of the market abuse framework, it is clear that some provisions need to be adapted in view of the specificity of those instruments.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this proposal so that legal certainty and clarity can be promoted to help combat market manipulation and insider dealing, which worsens the competitiveness and transparency of the market and harms the interests of european consumers and legal producers. it is parliamentʼs responsibility to provide a legal basis for the union and member states to properly regulate the market to ensure it functions well. thus, regulations should be made at european level to hold infringers accountable by discouraging behaviour that reduces market competitiveness and transparency, through punishment by judicial authorities and enhancing the competent authoritiesʼ access to relevant information channels.
in writing. - the legislation adopted today in strasbourg by a large majority introduced stricter sanctions for those who manipulate financial markets in order to ensure greater protection for european investors. the vote will mean that companies found guilty of market abuse will be liable to very high fines of up to 15% of their annual turnover. the same treatment will also be reserved for individuals guilty of the same offence, to which will be added a temporary ban on working with investment firms. i am therefore pleased with today's vote and hope that it will be part of the process of european economic development towards a stable and prosperous market economy.

mr president, so many small and weak national markets cannot end europe's energy dependence. thinking small means limiting the number of suppliers, making prices uncompetitive and providing services of poor quality. on the other hand, this is the picture of our energy market. i therefore welcome the report by mr buzek, which links the single market to the implementation of crossborder regional projects in accordance with an approach which looks at the real industrial, infrastructural and morphological make-up of the regions, and not at the barriers between national markets. in this respect too, mr president, national price support policies must be abolished, to give oxygen and competitiveness to this sector, which is a very important step: the single european energy market must remain a priority objective.
mr president, the buzek report stresses the importance of completing the single energy market. we know very well how much the cost of energy affects our competitiveness, but it is enough to point out that we are 50 per cent dependent on sources in other countries. in his report, mr buzek sets out a recipe which is entirely acceptable to all, starting with the full implementation, or rather the full transposition by all the member states, of the third energy package, and which, in short, provides for a policy which ensures that consumers are better informed about the costs and benefits of an internal energy market, greater clarity in national and european legislation, more modern infrastructure and therefore more investment. i hope that parliament's vote will enable the commission and the member states to take up this strong appeal.
mr president, mr buzek's report sets the course for completing an open, competitive, integrated and consumer-oriented internal energy market. in this context, the connecting europe facility plays a very important role, as it will give priority to infrastructure projects that can achieve internal market integration, in particular by encouraging the development of renewable sources, the creation of the necessary cross-border interconnections and security of supply. in order for europe to reduce its energy dependence, actions to support self-production from renewable sources will have to be implemented, with investment in the distribution network through the widespread development of networks and smart meters.
mr president, when mr buzek was president of our parliament, he organized meetings on this subject between us european parliamentarians and colleagues from the national parliaments, meetings in which i participated with great conviction. i therefore fully support this report, since its main objective is to create a fully integrated european single energy market, where prices are transparent, including the specification of excise duties and environmental costs. today in europe there are unacceptable differences in the price of energy, which vary too much from one country to another. for example, in italy, the cost of electricity for businesses is 130% higher than that paid by a french or polish industry and 80% higher than that paid by a german industry. it is clear that such disparities lead to unfair competition within the common market. just think of an energy-intensive industry whose costs are burdened by electricity for 30 percent of the total. think how much cheaper it would be for you to leave italy and move, perhaps to america, where the cost is even 400 percent lower!
mr president, the watchwords for households and businesses must be accessibility and sustainable prices. other colleagues said so: gas in europe costs four times as much as in the united states, and energy twice as much. households pay for energy costs from 7 to 20 percent. companies, especially energy-intensive ones, have prohibitive energy costs and are therefore at risk of closing down or moving outside the european union, where energy costs are much lower. the priority for the recovery of the european economy and enterprises is therefore to reduce their costs in order to make them competitive. the european union needs a competitive, integrated and fluid energy market that functions effectively and flexibly and is able to address climate and energy challenges.
mr president, we share mr buzek's report in supporting the completion of the internal energy market through the construction of new infrastructure and the full harmonisation of the rules for the functioning of the markets, a challenge which is necessary to adequately support the transition to a low-carbon economy. we regret, however, that the union is not yet ready for the full realisation of the internal energy market, given the slowness of the member states in adapting national legislation and in creating competitive markets. we believe that this parliament must work to ensure that our citizens and businesses have secure and low-cost energy systems in a globalised world where we are forced to depend on third countries and are often subjected to blackmail.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by mr guido milana in support of the need to develop a specific strategy for fisheries in the adriatic and ionian seas. the signs of a structural crisis in fisheries are clear in this area, and the limits of a policy that not only fails to improve the conditions of fishermen, but also fails to maintain biodiversity. it was a mistake to try to use the same strategy for areas with different characteristics. the application of generic measures without taking account of specificities has not, in the past, produced positive effects. it is therefore imperative to highlight the differences between the different areas and to adapt the application of the regulation to the particular contexts. the report presented by mr milana acknowledges the geomorphological peculiarities of the whole area and suggests a specific strategy for the adriatic and ionian seas. the document calls for closer relations with non-eu countries, in order to reconcile entrepreneurship with responsibility for protecting and preserving fish and natural resources, while making regionalization and dialogue with all stakeholders a top priority.
in writing. - the adriatic is a very important sea basin, bordering several european countries, including croatia, which has recently joined the union. the fact that different skills coexist in a virtually closed environment can create various problems and difficulties which should be resolved as soon as possible. the italian regulations are emblematic of this, forcing our vessels to remain in port to encourage the re-population of certain fishing areas, whereas these rules do not apply to croatian fishermen, for example: a common strategy should provide common rules for all, in such a way as to ensure equal opportunities. concerted action is needed both to protect fish stocks and to ensure a minimum requirement of respect and protection of the environment: the adriatic must once again be a source of employment and livelihood for the coastal communities, which have had a long tradition of centuries of fishing activity, which cannot and must not be abandoned, despite the difficulties of the period linked to very strong competition from foreign fisheries. what ?
in writing. − this report aims to promote the development of a new community strategy in the field of fisheries and aquaculture in the adriatic and ionian sea basin, with a view to making a substantial contribution to the development of sustainable activities with positive effects on coastal and inland communities. the adriatic sea and the adjacent ionian sea constitute an important marine area of interest to seven countries: the commission has also adopted a communication on the implementation of the european year of the environment (2007-2013) and a communication on the implementation of the european year of the environment (2008-2013). although there have always been intense economic and social interactions between these countries - now further strengthened by the eu accession process - the adriatic-ionian area has remained heterogeneous in economic, environmental and cultural terms.
in writing. − the adriatic-ionian macro-region is the meeting point of different economies, cultures and policies. the european union is on one side and the balkans are on the other, so it is essential to establish strategic coordination for fisheries, the ecological system and the economic and social interests of the inhabitants of these coastal areas. the main objective of the text is therefore to define an action plan with new rules for fisheries and aquaculture that will improve the socioeconomic conditions of the inhabitants of the whole region, on the part of the european union and in agreement with third countries.
in writing. − whereas the adriatic-ionian sea has been an important maritime and aquaculture area whose coastline takes in seven member states, candidate countries and potential candidate countries, a portion of this area is in international waters. this fact requires cooperation by these neighbouring countries to ensure sustainable fishing activities, especially considering the rise in the installation of fishing facilities that are incompatible with other activities in the area. with the assistance of the commission, a strategy promoting cooperation can be implemented to encourage responsible and sustainable fishing activities in the area. therefore, i voted in favour of this proposal.
in writing. - the report by mrs milana on a fisheries strategy for the adriatic and ionian seas was voted on today in plenary. the aim is to promote the development of a new community strategy in the field of fisheries and aquaculture in the adriatic and ionian seas. the countries bordering this sea area now share many resources, including fish stocks, and face a number of problems in this area where there is still no common regional plan. the european commission has recently adopted a communication proposing a maritime strategy for the adriatic and ionian seas, of which the promotion of sustainable fisheries is one of the four strategic pillars. i therefore agree with mr milana's report that we should act on this basis in order to launch a community macro-regional strategy for the adriatic and ionian sea basin which takes account of the specific characteristics of this sea basin in the fisheries and aquaculture sector.
in writing. - the aim of this document is to promote the development of a new common strategy for fisheries and aquaculture in the adriatic and ionian seas. for too many years, the limits of exploitation of these waters have been exceeded: the whole system now needs to be reorganised, developing sustainable activities that can have a positive impact on all the coastal communities concerned and their hinterland.
in writing. − in times of crisis, economic and labour force recovery is also a result of policies aimed at the exploitation of environmental resources. i therefore voted in favour of mr milana's report, which aims to promote the development of a new community strategy for fisheries and aquaculture in the adriatic and ionian seas, with the aim of making a substantial contribution to the development of sustainable activities with positive effects on coastal and inland communities.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the de lange report 'towards a more efficient and cost-effective interpreting service in the european parliament'. the text condemns the waste of at least eur 15.39 million in interpreting services over the past three years due to the inefficient use of resources and calls on the bureau to take the necessary measures to contain expenditure.
in writing. − multilingualism is one of the fundamental elements of the european parliament and of the union as a whole, and forms the basis of the political, co-legislative and communication activities of this institution. in recent years interpretation services have achieved significant improvements in terms of efficiency and cost reduction, while maintaining excellent quality of work. the fact remains that interpretation and translation expenditure continue to absorb a significant proportion of parliament's budget: i therefore agree with the rapporteur that the challenge of multilingualism at reasonable cost requires constant attention from parliament. it is essential that the resources to be allocated to multilingualism be contained by management based on the real needs of users, by empowering users and by better planning of requests for language services, without this compromising the right of members to use the official language of their choice in parliament.
in writing. - multilingualism and multiculturalism have always been a richness of the european system. the various enlargements, however, have had the effect of making multilingualism an increasingly complex challenge to tackle. to avoid it becoming an obstacle, it is essential to provide adequate financial support in the budget for the next financial period. i believe, however, that at the same time the interpretation service must be made more efficient, avoiding unnecessary waste and costs, such as those associated with late cancellations of interpretation requests. the ability to communicate in one's own official language is one of the eu's fundamental principles. but it is equally important to show our citizens that in these times of economic constraints, economic resources are being used in a really effective way.
in writing. - the european parliament is certainly one of the bodies in the world which makes the greatest use of interpretation services: this is for obvious reasons, because the european union recognises multilingualism as a key principle and because all services must be made available to members to enable them to fulfil their mandate in the best possible way. however, it is undeniable that this mechanism generates incredible costs, and the entry of new countries and new languages only makes the situation worse. a balance would therefore be needed between ensuring that everyone has a perfect capacity for expression and understanding and trying to limit unnecessary costs: i have often been in commission meetings and saw three people translating into a language without any member of that nationality present. this is unacceptable, and the cancellation mechanism for requests for interpretation should be revised, since the time limit is exceeded and there are heavy penalties and costs to cover the interpretation service. where it is not strictly necessary, and expressly requested, i would be in favour of limiting the interpreting service to a few selected languages, obviously trying not to penalize anyone.
in writing. - i supported this resolution because the european union is the only entity in the world to pursue an official policy of multilingualism based on 23 official languages, which will soon be 24. in 2011, 5 263 sessions were held with approximately 100 000 days/interpreters, for which external interpreters were used in 47,74% of cases and official interpreters in 52,26% of cases. the figures are alarming, but parliament's interpretation services are of the highest quality. these figures may seem impressive, but they guarantee that every european citizen can read parliament's acts in his own language!
in writing. − while the principle of multilingualism is a core concept of parliament and the european union as a whole, the cost of interpretation services in 23 official languages is considerably high. we have a responsibility to eu taxpayers to improve the efficiency of resources allocated to interpretation without sacrificing citizensʼ access to parliament and the cultural and linguistic diversity in europe. therefore, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. the de lange report stresses the need to improve the efficiency of multilingualism without compromising the quality of services and without calling into question the right of members to speak in their official language in parliament. the recent efficiency gains in the debate on parliament's budget and the good practices to be undertaken, such as the implementation of interpretation on request or the reduction of late cancellations, are undoubtedly a good starting point for achieving the objectives set.
in writing. - i thank the rapporteur for tackling such a delicate subject without any redundant moralisms, but with lucid and consequent determination. i am voting in favour of the report and i wholeheartedly support its recommendations. italy is one of the countries most affected by the growth of gambling addiction in connection with the weakening of households and falling incomes, especially in urban centres. health services estimate the number of patients at over one million, and the tax administration recorded a per capita expenditure of two thousand euros per year in 2011. i support the combined approach of offering a european-wide regulated gambling facility under a subsidiary system, with built-in limits on spending and time, and of taking a firm stance against illegal gambling, especially those aimed at manipulating sports competitions. the two obligations of public authorities must be distinguished: on the one hand, the moral duty, as well as the material interest, to protect vulnerable segments of the population; the commission has also been asked to present a report on the implementation of the directive on the protection of the financial interests of the community. i agree with the suggestion that the legal gaming industry should not be penalized, but should be regulated in a way that is appropriate to the delicate implications for social order and public safety.
in writing. - online gambling is not a market like any other. its negative health and social effects are well documented and its link to organised crime, money laundering and the manipulation of sporting events is a cause for concern. with this resolution we are not calling for the introduction of harmonised rules for a single market for online gambling but for greater coordination between member states and the commission for better organisation and regulation of online gambling services. but above all, what we are calling for is strong action against illegal online gambling, including the development of a notion of legal gambling operators. finally, particular attention should be paid to young people and the most vulnerable members of society who are very often victims of gambling addiction. we call for concrete measures to make it impossible for minors to access gambling; let us not forget that 75% of european young people between the ages of 6 and 17 use the internet. i believe that it is absolutely necessary to raise barriers to prevent young europeans from falling into this tragic addiction.
in writing. - i have followed this subject very closely since parliament drew up its own-initiative report. play therapy is now officially in the psychiatric textbooks, and gambling is a huge business. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the consumer is not left to his own devices, and that the consumer is not left to his own devices. i have greatly appreciated the attitude of the main players in the market, who have shown a sense of responsibility and a desire to be regulated more clearly, even at the cost of giving up some market shares. i think the rapporteur has done a very good job of balancing the interests and sensitivities of the different countries and political groups, to call for regulation on a national basis, which takes account of peculiarities and traditions, while putting a brake on all those behaviours and market segments in which it takes advantage of the state of submission of the customer. i therefore voted in favour of the report.
in writing. - the online gambling craze is a hope of 'settling down' people enter the online gambling industry hoping to solve their financial problems and chasing the illusion of winning, but instead risk falling into a very serious pathological state, developing addiction and engaging in obsessive-compulsive behaviour. the risk is therefore twofold, but unfortunately the impression is that while the risk of illegality is rightly called for and that strong action is called for, the risk of addiction to 'legal' sites does not seem to be perceived as such. i find it unacceptable that while people are calling for the closure of illegal websites, nothing is being done or said against the invasion of television poker tournaments with testimonials from the rich and famous! we can accept blacklists of illegal sites, but it is contradictory to have an entire tv dedicated to poker or to have football teams sponsored by betting agencies! i believe that there is still a long way to go and that europe must find the strength to promote, in concrete terms, a discipline which serves the interests of its weakest citizens, without having an eye on the need for the states to make money through what is a transfer from the pockets of the poorest groups.
in writing. - president, i voted in favour of the fox report because i believe it is essential that more careful control is exercised over online gambling in order to avoid possible negative effects on the health of citizens and on society, such as organised crime, money laundering and the manipulation of sporting events. the phenomenon is particularly widespread in italy; the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect. it should also be borne in mind that this activity may involve a high risk of addiction. in italy alone, there are about 708,225 pathological gamblers. the victims are above all the most vulnerable members of society, who are at risk of finding themselves in even more precarious living conditions. recognition of the specific nature of online gambling and consumer protection are therefore necessary. the adoption of additional measures to protect players by restricting and regulating such activity cannot be postponed. finally, given the cross-border nature of online gambling, there is a need to strengthen cooperation between member states in the fight against illegal activities related to online gambling.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal on online gambling because i believe that this would help to combat the phenomenon. the formulation of coordinated strategies between the commission, member states and the expert group on gambling services will also make it easier to remedy the problem by putting in place a policy of sharing best practice and information for the subsequent enforcement of enforcement measures against illegal operators. the aim is to strengthen consumer protection, including work on health-related aspects of pathological and problem gambling.
in writing. - this report aims to apply shared administrative practices for the member states on the subject of combating illegal betting and money laundering. online gambling is a growing market across the european union, but states are also faced with a number of related problems, including the notorious problem of gambling addiction. i support the report because it calls for specific action in this area.
in writing. the long negotiations which characterised the discussion on this subject ended with a satisfactory agreement. there are still some points on which i have some reservations, especially because they are difficult to reconcile with the regulations in italy. the amendments are appropriate to recognise the specific nature of the public gambling sector (with particular reference to the remote gaming sector). the meeting point was the necessary application of the principle of subsidiarity, according to which the national systems of concessions or licences issued by the member states constitute the best form of control of the supply of games on their territory. equally important was the recognition of the importance of combating illegal supply, thus ensuring consumer protection.
in writing. − we welcome the recent commission communication entitled 'towards a comprehensive european regulatory framework for online gambling', which we consider to be a step forward in ensuring that european consumers have access to safe and appropriately regulated online services. we believe that only effective regulation of the online gambling sector can prevent the risk of gambling addiction and ensure that gambling is fair, equitable, responsible and transparent. we therefore call on the commission and the member states to take action against the supply of illegal gambling from within the territory of the member states themselves, considering that a single european legislative act, aimed at uniformly regulating the entire gambling sector, is not appropriate because of subsidiarity concerns, but that in some areas a coordinated european approach alongside national regulations would undoubtedly provide added value, given the cross-border nature of online gambling services.
in writing. - online gambling has exploded in recent years across europe, with a growing turnover of billionaires and more and more individuals turning to this alternative to traditional gambling halls. like many activities on the web, this is difficult to detect and regulate and therefore maximum cooperation between the different national authorities is needed to ensure that no particular phenomena related to money laundering or to distort the proper conduct of sporting events, for example, occur. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council adopt a common position on the proposal for a directive on the protection of consumers in respect of online gambling. those who want to risk their lot and have fun should be allowed to do so, but always within certain limits, for it is not uncommon for individuals and entire families to be ruined by gambling: this is not only harmful to them, as it seems, but also to the whole community. finally, strict control should also be applied to suppliers operating on the european market but having their registered office outside the eu: the rules must apply to everyone. what ?
in writing. - i have cautiously supported this resolution on online gambling. my vote was hampered in some parts of the text by the importance of the message this parliament wants to send to consumers on the one hand and to the companies that operate online gambling sites on the other, which, without moral hypocrisy, are companies that make a profit, create jobs and contribute to the wealth of a country by paying corporate taxes. online gambling is a fast-growing service activity in the eu, with annual growth rates of almost 15%. annual revenues are forecast to be around eur 13 billion in 2015: compared to eur 9,3 billion in 2011, this would be a total growth rate of almost 40%. in order to safeguard the positive effects of this business on the european economy and the labour market, our institution must protect consumers, promote forms of education on the possible contraindications to gambling when it is carried out without the necessary balance and promote the utmost opposition to companies that illegally offer online gambling, without any guarantee for consumer users and perhaps based on their own tax centre and in those non-european countries with facilitated regimes.
in writing. - we support mr fox's report and reiterate that, in the face of the spread of gambling addiction, which is costing society so much in terms of treatment, and the many families ruined by gambling, it is more necessary than ever to take steps to make society more responsible. too many for the sake of play commit crimes and even kill themselves. we believe that it is essential to prohibit gambling advertising as is already the case with tobacco and to make gambling inaccessible to minors. the controls on the links between criminal organisations and gambling houses should be improved, as should the spread of gambling and gambling on the internet, where young people are difficult to control. the use of slot machines, which are rampant in many european establishments, should also be severely restricted, given the psychological illusion of greater ease of winning that brings so many people to the brink. the european union can no longer ignore the problem and must instead act to bring gambling back on the path of legality and respect for the health of citizens, limiting as much as possible the proliferation of harmful behaviour and fostering a sense of responsibility within the member states.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mr fox's text because i believe that limits should be placed on online gambling, especially in view of the risks of gambling addiction. setting limits and ensuring safe betting is in the interests of consumers and will reduce gambling addiction. it is also important to stress that the text voted on today reinforces the commitment to combat illegal gambling. ensuring transparency of information and responsible betting will facilitate the recognition and sanctioning of illegal betting.
in writing. − with online gambling providers present on the european union market, regulating the online gambling industry is necessary to ensure citizens are using online services safely and healthily and to minimise the disadvantages of online gambling activities, including potential compulsive gambling, money laundering and organised crime. the report suggests that efficient regulation should ensure consumers have access to high quality, fair and transparent online gambling services while reducing the negative health and social impact and combating illegal online gambling. it also specifies that vulnerable groups, in particular young gamblers, should be protected. i therefore voted in favour of this proposal.
in writing. - i am in favour of the text of the report because gambling is creating serious problems for many citizens of the union who, out of passion or desperation, risk ruining themselves and their families economically. even worse is the risk involved in online gambling where thousands of sites, many illegal, pose risks of fraud and money laundering. it is therefore important to implement the 'online gaming action plan' launched by the european commission in october 2012. the report proposes a set of common rules on restrictions on advertising, the fight against illegal betting and money laundering and stricter controls on operators.
in writing. − after work in the respective committees, a final text was drawn up which represents a step forward in consumer protection, the fight against illegal betting and the safety of the services offered. the regulation of the online gambling sector should aim to prevent the risk of gambling addiction and ensure that gambling is fair, responsible and transparent. it will also be necessary to combat illegal gambling through cooperation between the authorities of the member states, by strengthening the technical and legal tools to identify and sanction illegal operators and to ensure effective protection of players, especially the most vulnerable.

the agenda includes the debate on the report by mr giovanni la via, on behalf of the committee on budgets, on the council position on the draft amending budget no 2/2013 of the european union for the financial year 2013, section iii commission, [11693/2013 - c7-0245/2013 - 2013/2056 ((bud)) ] (a7-0287/2013).
on behalf of the efd group. mr president, i have never been soft in criticizing the european union's budgets, with expenditure that is sometimes frankly unjustifiable. however, one thing should be clear: the commitments must be respected and therefore payments for the actions already undertaken must be made. i would not want europe to pick up the bad habit of italy: a lot of commitments and then sobbing payments when they come. the commission's commitments and demands must therefore be honoured. i would like to see more realism in the future, that is, that commitments are only made if they can be respected. many european countries are suffering from serious budgetary problems and it is therefore not possible to expect the european union to live in another dimension. we therefore honour payments to carry out programmes which have some usefulness, such as support for small and mediumsized enterprises or for young people. on the other hand, other lines which are not at all priority are being cut, such as the billions given to turkey in recent years under the pre-accession funds.
member of the commission. − mr president, let me briefly respond to some voices in this house: what we need for 2013 to cover the real shortage – and accumulation of problems from previous years – is to cover legitimate claims, not an expenditure invented by the commission. this is about bills coming from the member states passing severe controls, as the taxpayers’ money coming to the european budget is better controlled than public expenditure at the member state level because there is not only a domestic control but also brussels control and the audit. what is suspended is suspended, and what is cancelled is cancelled but the amending budget is to cover legitimate claims coming from the member states. even in a time of austerity one needs to pay one’s electricity bill. this is a question of trust; this is a question of credibility. even in times of austerity you need to show your monetary gesture of solidarity with the victims of floods in germany and in austria. this is again a question of credibility and image of the eu institutions. anne jensen was asking a real question: whether eur 11.2 billion – a huge amount really, an accumulation of problems – is enough for 2013. first of all, that is to pay out what legally should be paid in 2013 and is for bills coming until the end of october, but we really need the full amount this year – so an additional 3.9 billion this year in order to reduce the legacy of this financial perspective for the next financial perspective to the size of normal overhang and not unusual overhang of claims as it was between 2012 and 2013. and for sound budgeting we need to exploit the full ceilings of the 2014 budget also. we are now starting an historical experiment of how to finance more europe with less money. more europe in terms of geography. we have a new member state; we have lot of new competences with less money. i do believe – and it has been demonstrated in various countries – that the european budget is an investment budget. this is a partial answer to how to solve the dilemma of financing growth, jobs and investment in times of fiscal consolidation. there is no perfect answer, but the eu budget is a partial answer to this problem.
the rapporteur. - mr president, it is clear from the debate in the chamber that most of the major political groups are moving towards adopting this amending budget. this is an important step because, as the commissioner rightly said, once commitments have been made, it is right to make subsequent payments. but it is also an important step because we want the new financial programming to start in the best possible way, without an extraordinary carry-over of payment debts from previous years. it is clear - and the message is sent to the council - that when commitments are made - and the council in this case has been extremely lavish in previous years in many cases - then it is time to pay the bill. today is that day! at a trilogue with the commission and the lithuanian presidency, the commissioner said that at this point in the year we have already used up two thirds of the payment appropriations for the 2013 budget. we are well aware that the part of the year when the greatest needs for payments are the last part of the year, because the commitments made in connection with cohesion policy and rural development policy are converted into invoices, transferred to the commission and the member states, which must be paid. it is therefore clear that this is the time when we have greater needs on many budget lines. this year the commission has been forced to make a very significant series of transfers, precisely in order to try to implement the policies. this is a clear sign that this is not a whim of the commission but rather a strong need for payment interventions for this latter part of the year, on which i hope that tomorrow this parliament will give a meaningful and favourable vote in favour of amending budget no 2. i take this opportunity to call on the commission once again to present the new amending budget as soon as possible.
