in writing. - the sardinian language is certainly one of the oldest european languages to which this report refers. and the protection of endangered languages and linguistic diversity must be a priority for the union. not only because of their obvious cultural value, as they contain centuries of history, or because they are the cornerstone of the sense of identity of the local communities on which the union is based. there are also pedagogical and economic reasons for this choice. it has been shown that bilingual children have a greater facility in learning additional languages than monolingual children. as there will be an increasing demand for multilingual workers in the european labour market, i believe that defending linguistic diversity is the right way to ensure more job opportunities for our young people. i welcome this report, but i regret that italy has not ratified the european charter for regional or minority languages, because a policy that is not sufficiently effective in this area can cause considerable damage to local ethnic communities and to the union as a whole, and i hope that the commission will also make its voice heard on this matter.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the alfonsi report which dealt with the issue of endangered languages and linguistic diversity. the text is very balanced and is based on a principle which i fully share: the european commission must create specific programmes and funds to support regional languages, which play a decisive role in the transmission and protection of traditions and cultures that are otherwise at risk of disappearing.
in writing. - i support the report by mr alfonsi, adopted by a large majority, on the protection of endangered languages in europe. languages can become extinct if they are no longer passed on between generations, if their use is banned from private or public spaces, or if there is a lack of learning materials. in my amendments i made it clear that we are asking the european commission and the member states to take concrete measures to this end in the new financial period 2014-2020. we also want to push ahead with the ratification of the charter for regional or minority languages. some member states - particularly italy and france - have not yet ratified the 1992 charter, which is regarded as a benchmark for the protection of minority languages. the example of the ladin language in my home region clearly shows that a language only has a chance if it is promoted in a targeted way. while in south tyrol it has been possible to keep the ladin language alive, in the ladin part of belluno, where nothing is being done, it is disappearing.
in writing. − this report calls on the commission and the council to provide for specific programmes and funds to support endangered languages and linguistic diversity in the union. other content that i think is of particular interest is the principles of non-discrimination of regional languages and the importance of their survival. i am voting in favour of this text because it shows how important it is to protect the culture of a language.
in writing. - this report is going in the right direction - culturally. the union's wealth lies in the variety of its cultural expressions, and it is up to us to preserve this wealth, which is part of a larger european identity. we know that many of the languages spoken in the eu are in danger, and that some of them may disappear within the century. it is therefore important that eu bodies act to promote and safeguard these cultural assets. this action must not be implemented solely through the union but, above all, through dedicated policies by the member states.
in writing. − europe is an extremely diverse linguistic community and linguistic diversity is respected by the european union as one of its fundamental rights, yet aside from the most-spoken languages, there are many endangered languages spoken by small groups of citizens. to preserve, protect and promote these endangered languages is consistent with our common values, and necessary funding should be provided to support certain protective actions, including early-age teaching and distance learning of endangered languages, but not wider political agendas. therefore, i voted in favour of this resolution to facilitate joint actions by parliament, the council and the commission to properly protect the rights of linguistic and cultural minorities.
in writing. - the european parliament, in plenary session this morning, voted on an alfonsi report on the european languages in danger of extinction. in a globalised world such as the one we live in today, it is crucial to promote and protect linguistic diversity, which is a fundamental value and cultural heritage of the union. supporting multilingualism, not just with useless proclamations but with ad hoc financial resources and concrete proactive policies, is a challenge which, if met, will undoubtedly bring benefits to social cohesion and the overall cultural enrichment of the union. finally, the report meets my expectations of safeguarding and defending neapolitan, which is already recognized as a language in all its aspects by unesco, but which is too often denigrated in the national and community context. i can therefore only express my agreement with a resolution which, in my view, not only meets the requirements of the identity of each european people but also takes on a relevant local dimension in the preservation of the neapolitan language.
in writing. − the european union and the member states must pay particular attention to endangered languages and protect linguistic diversity in europe. i therefore voted in favour, stressing that the amendment of many amendments which referred to 'minorities' and 'minority languages' to a more general reference to 'endangered languages' has made the text presented by mr alfonsi more balanced and therefore more acceptable to the various political groups.
in writing. - i support the report by mr groote on the appointment of the executive directors of the european environment agency (eea) and its need to bring it into line with the procedures for the appointment of the executive directors of other european agencies.
in writing. − the alignment of the criteria for appointing the executive directors of the european environment agency with those of the other authorities is a step forward in several respects. the need was felt to restore the fundamental monitoring function to the european parliament. it was not possible to continue to maintain an anomaly in the system of european agencies, due to the fact that the regulation of the environment agency precedes the founding regulations of the other agencies. the fact that the parliament, the institution representing the european citizens, has the right prerogatives to appoint the future executive directors of the eea shows the will of the union to ensure greater democracy in its system.
in writing. - this recommendation is technical and difficult to explain to our fellow citizens. i'm sorry about that. nevertheless, it has important political value. the first paragraph of article 9 of the regulation governs the appointment of the executive director of the european environment agency and does not currently include the requirement that the candidate selected by the agency's management board be heard by the competent organ of the european parliament before being appointed. however, this requirement is contained in the regulations establishing other agencies, in particular the european chemicals agency, the european medicines agency and the european food safety authority, which fall within the remit of parliament's committee on the environment, public health and food safety (envi). in fact, this lack of specific reference to the parliamentary hearing is mainly due to the fact that the regulation establishing the european environment agency predates the regulations establishing the other agencies, as its original version dates back to 1990.
in writing. − the european environment agency (eea) is an agency of the european union that serves as a major information source on environmental issues. regulations authorise the parliament to appoint the executive director of eea; however, whether candidates selected by the member board of eea should be heard by the competent body of the parliament is not specified, mostly due to the fact that the associated regulation is older than the regulations establishing other agencies, such as the european chemical agency and european medicines agency, which include this specific requirement. therefore, i voted in favour of this request to submit a proposal in order to amend the regulations.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this draft amending budget to support the work done by my colleagues during the negotiations with the council.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by mr la via on draft amending budget no 3/2013 which aims to enter in the budget the surplus resulting from the implementation of the 2012 financial year. in this way, the accounting for the surplus will result in a corresponding decrease in the member states' overall contribution to the financing of the eu budget, with a saving for each individual country.
in writing. - this draft amending budget helps the member states' economies by giving them some oxygen. as the full amount of the 2012 budget has not been spent, the contribution from the member states may be slightly reduced for 2013.
in writing. − i support the report by mr la via and mr vaughan on draft amending budget no 4/2013 on the recruitment of new staff for the european gnss agency (gsa) - staff of the education, audiovisual and culture executive agency (eacea) - staff of the court of justice of the european union. these new recruitments will not affect the budget but will allow these agencies to operate more efficiently.
in writing. - as for the report by mr fernandes, whose accounting face this measure is, i think it is appropriate to show solidarity with the eu countries affected by natural disasters.
in writing. − since the european gnss agency is in urgent need of new staff in order to prepare for its new task in january 2014, it is reasonable to amend the budget so that the agency can add 20 posts entrusted to the new task. however, the original request to add nine new law clerks to the court is unrealistic considering the associated costs, though recruitment is admittedly necessary for reinforcement. i therefore voted for the approval of the council position on draft amending budget no 4/2013 and to meet the demand for staff for the gnss agency, the eacea executive agency, and partially for the court.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the fernandes report on the mobilisation of the european union solidarity fund to help the slovenian and croatian regions of austria which were badly affected by the floods in late october and early november 2012.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this measure because i believe that, even in times of austerity, the eu should show solidarity with those countries in difficulty as a result of a natural disaster.
in writing. - the commission proposes to mobilise the european union solidarity fund for slovenia, croatia and austria, this agreement allows the mobilisation of the fund up to an annual ceiling of eur 1 billion. in parallel to this proposal to mobilise the solidarity fund for slovenia, croatia and austria, the commission presented a draft amending budget (oj no 5/2013 of 2 may 2013) to enter the corresponding commitment and payment appropriations in the 2013 budget, as provided for in point 26 of the iia. how can you be against it? but as a european parliament we must ask ourselves whether the union is really acting fairly towards all the member states, or whether the issue of natural disasters is a matter of double standards, as the case may be.
in writing. − in november 2012, intense rainfall caused major flooding in slovenia, causing eur 359 535 of damage. the neighbouring countries of austria and croatia were also affected. the flooding has met the ‘major disaster criterionʼ in accordance with relevant council regulations. in order to support disaster relief in the territory, i decided to vote for the mobilisation of the eu solidarity fund.
in writing. the european parliament adopted a resolution on the situation in the former yugoslavia. the commission has also received a number of letters from the member states, which have been sent to the council and the european parliament. the three beneficiaries will receive € 14,600,000 from the european union to help them repair the damage caused by the severe floods in 2012. the total will be divided differently between the three beneficiary states, the largest part (€14 million) going to slovenia, which was the most affected by the floods.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council establishing the mobilisation of the european union solidarity fund following the floods in slovenia, croatia and austria in autumn 2012. the proposal provides for eur 1 billion to be allocated to the countries concerned. this is a major natural disaster within the meaning of article 2 (2) of council regulation (ec) no 2012/2002. the fund will be used for reconstruction in the worst affected areas and for humanitarian aid. it is therefore a moral duty on the part of the eu to the member states affected by the disaster.
in writing. - i support this report, which lays down the draft amending budget to cover the mobilisation of the european union solidarity fund to support the regions of austria, slovenia and croatia severely affected by floods in late october and early november 2012.
in writing. - as for the report by mr fernandes, whose accounting face this measure is, i think it is appropriate to show solidarity with the eu countries affected by natural disasters.
in writing. - in today's vote, the european parliament has defined its position to put an end to the obvious side effects of european legislation, committing itself to preventing the production of biofuels and renewable energies from taking land away from agriculture and, therefore, food, especially in those countries which, more than the european union, need agricultural land and food. the result of the vote is not as straightforward as the socialist and democratic group would have liked, but it is important that there should now be a clear and rapid response from the member states to correct the course taken in the past years in the production of biofuels and at the same time to give a certain regulatory framework to the companies that have invested in this sector. we shall be working on second reading to correct the mistakes made in this house by the centre-right majority. in my region, with projects on so-called 'green chemistry', we have managed to strike a good balance by allocating to industrial production only crops grown on land which is now abandoned because it is no longer profitable, and i believe that this is the path that europe must also follow.
in writing. − the renewable energy directive sets the target of 20% renewable energy in total eu energy consumption and 10% renewable energy in transport by 2020. at the same time, the fuel quality directive introduced a binding target of a 6% reduction in the greenhouse gas emissions intensity of fuels for road transport and non-road mobile machinery. accelerating the switch to advanced biofuels, which has a broad consensus, is one of the objectives of the proposal. it is essential to give industry a clear signal of the european union's move towards advanced biofuels in order to encourage long-term investment. that is why i voted in favour of this directive.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by mrs lepage because i believe that it is essential that, as technology and scientific discoveries in the field of fuels progress, legislative modernisation should be achieved in parallel. i think that parliament should have set a more ambitious target for support for second generation biofuels, by adopting a lower percentage to define the limit of the contribution of first generation biofuels to the overall threshold. i also think we should pay more attention to the actual co2 reduction from the most advanced technologies.
in writing. the commission proposal amends the previous directives on fuel quality and the promotion of renewable energy to take account of iluc, i.e. emissions associated with land use change for biofuels, which reduce environmental benefits. the iluc proposal therefore aims to limit the role of biofuels derived from agricultural crops in accounting for the 10% renewable energy target for transport by 2020. i share the objectives of the commission's legislative proposal, which aims to reward the most virtuous biofuels, in terms of co2 emissions compared to the reference fossil fuel and non-competitiveness with the agricultural world for land use. on the other hand, it should be noted that the 5% rate for the use of biofuels and bioliquids produced from cereals and other starchy, sugary or oil crops actually penalizes the investments already made. in addition, the introduction of the four-counting system could have distortive effects on the market, as well as the risk of fraud. however, i believe that the data proposed for indirect land use change emission factors should be supported by international studies on the subject.
in writing. the directive addresses a problem of primary importance, which has a profound impact on the development prospects, particularly of the less developed areas of the globe. we cannot ignore the impact of biofuel production on food supplies. the incidence is even higher where populations are most affected by endemic shortages of primary goods. at the same time, however, it is unthinkable to ignore the scale of the investments already made or planned for the coming years by biofuel producers. a synthesis was needed that took this into account, but did not preclude the further development of second generation biofuels, which undoubtedly have a lower negative impact. the union must promote the transition to the second generation - gradually, without unfair penalties - since the consequences of the current system are no longer acceptable. the withdrawal of land from food production, with the consequent rise in food prices, the indiscriminate rush to grab land has had negative effects on the populations, who have paid a high price that europe can no longer afford. we know that we could have dared more and found the courage to take initiatives that would have brought more benefits to citizens and the global system.
in writing. - the vote in plenary today gave european citizens a double guarantee. on the one hand, the introduction of a 6% maximum threshold for the use of first generation biofuels is a positive element in protecting food security. over the past decade, the push for biofuels as a solution to energy over-reliance has led to excessive competition between food crops and biofuel crops, triggering a spiral of rising food prices. the commission also found that the exporting producers concerned had not provided any evidence that the measures in force were in breach of the undertaking. on the other hand, reaching a minimum threshold for the consumption of energy from advanced biofuels by 2020 will preserve investments already made in the sector and encourage the search for alternative solutions for energy production. unfortunately, the low figure of 2.5% foreseen for this threshold represents a missed opportunity to foster real innovation in the sector. i hope, however, that the council will reach a common position close to that voted today in plenary, in order to ensure that our citizens have a sustainable energy strategy in the long term as soon as possible.
in writing. - i supported this resolution. while existing investments should be protected, the aims of the commission's proposal are to limit the contribution of conventional biofuels to the objectives set by the renewable energy directive. the greenhouse gas performance of biofuel production processes should also be improved by increasing the greenhouse gas reduction threshold, protecting installations already in operation on 1 july 2014; finally, the market penetration of advanced biofuels should be encouraged, enabling them to contribute more to the objectives of the renewable energy directive than conventional biofuels.
in writing. − the report on the promotion of the use of energy from renewable sources and the quality of petrol and fuel, the so-called iluc (emissions associated with land use change for biofuels), sets as a main objective the use of 10% of renewable energy for transport by 2020. the impact of indirect land-use change on greenhouse gas emissions needs to be reviewed to be reduced in line with ongoing investments and production activities. the research into alternative materials must also be encouraged if we are to achieve this goal in the time allotted and protect the health of citizens through the increased use of renewable energies.
in writing. - i am voting in favour of the proposal for a european parliament and council directive amending directive 98/70/ec on the quality of petrol and diesel fuels and directive 2009/28/ec on the promotion of the use of energy from renewable sources. environmental protection is a key element of the europe 2020 strategy for smart, sustainable and inclusive growth. in order to achieve these objectives, transport is a strategic area for action. it is therefore of the utmost importance to take advantage of the progress made in research and innovation and thus to encourage the use of biofuels and bioliquids. however, in parallel, the indirect land use change factor (iluc) needs to be integrated into the methodology used to determine the effects of biomass fuels on the ecosystem. in addition, the possible impact on the market value of the raw materials involved in the production process of those biofuels and thus the possible social impact should be carefully assessed. for these reasons, i consider this proposal for a directive to be an appropriate response to the need to examine the problem of greenhouse gas emissions in greater depth in the light of new sustainability criteria and new possible alternatives.
in writing. - as the rapporteur has pointed out, the european eel stock is subject to a host of problems: over-exploitation, loss of critical habitats, pollution, pests, changes in ocean currents as a result of global climate change, and so on. there are also many unknowns regarding the size of the stock, the conditions leading to the determination of the sex of the eels and the possibility that the repopulated eels become full-fledged breeders. according to recent scientific advice from the international council for the exploration of the sea (ices, 2012), the condition of the stock remains critical and urgent action is needed. the stock has exceeded safe biological limits and fishing at current levels is not sustainable. it is essential that the commission, by aligning the regulation with articles 290 to 291 tfeu, adopt, by means of delegated and implementing acts, measures to address this critical situation.
in writing. - the question of the recovery of the european eel stock is at odds with the fact that the current regulation rightly places the recovery as a central element of the management plans for the eel, without however imposing any conditions and without any guidelines aimed at the result, that is to say that we have ensured that the recovery operation has as its outcome actual possibilities for recovery. it is therefore right to proceed with a new and more effective regulation.
in writing. - the european eel stock is subject to a myriad of problems: over-exploitation, loss of critical habitats, pollution, pests, changes in ocean currents as a result of climate change at the global level. added to this are other scientific uncertainties: to name just a few: the size of the stock is uncertain, the conditions leading to the determination of the sex of the eels are unclear and the possibility that the repopulated eels become full-fledged breeders remains a major question mark. the unknowns also concern the monitoring and control of the exploitation of eels, due to the mismatch between the catch and export data in the different databases, as well as the fate of a significant part of the catches and an international black market for eels that is known but not quantified. the exploitation of eel populations is a worldwide export activity with an estimated value of more than eur 10 billion between 1997 and 2007. the stock situation remains critical and urgent action is needed. the stock has exceeded safe biological limits and fishing at current levels is no longer sustainable. we have to move fast!
in writing. - today's vote has definitively exposed the deception and manipulation of the political debate which has been taking place in sardinia over the last few months on the adoption of the union customs code. the president of the region and the centre-right forces who support him have distorted the meaning of the political battle that for years sardinian citizens, associations and political forces have been waging for the full recognition of regional autonomy and for the definition of credible solutions to our insularity. the commission has already taken a number of initiatives, including the creation of a european centre for the development of vocational training, which will be set up in the near future. it is time to resume a serious debate and work on what can be done concretely in sardinia to support businesses and create jobs: the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a decision on the establishment of a european agency for the evaluation of medicinal products for human use.
in writing. the commission has proposed a revision of the community customs code to adapt certain provisions of the regulation establishing it to the evolution of customs legislation and to align it with the requirements of the lisbon treaty. the customs union is a fundamental element of the single market which can only function properly if the rules of modern customs systems are applied in a uniform manner across the member states. i agree with the rapporteur that the verification of further simplifications in the application of customs legislation by means of computerised procedures can be beneficial for the development of a dynamic environment in terms of competitiveness and growth, but on condition that the scope and time limit of such verification are made explicit in the regulation itself. i am concerned about the commission's proposal for a number of derogations for one or more member states on the compulsory use of electronic data interchange between customs administrations and economic operators. this strategy would involve a two-speed approach to customs procedures in the union with the risk of widening the gap between those states that choose to invest and those that do not. i therefore believe that it would be essential for the code to be applied uniformly in all 28 member states of the union.
in writing. - i am in favour of this revision of the union customs code, proposed by the commission, in order to bring it into line with the lisbon treaty and the regulatory developments. the uniform and consistent application of the code by member states is a key condition for deriving the maximum benefit from it for the whole single market. i very much share the need to simplify procedures by means of computerised procedures in order to develop a more dynamic environment in terms of competitiveness and growth. many other adjustments seem to me to be effective and aimed at improving the operation of the code, such as those relating to the enhancement of the status of economic operator, and the one on the need to provide for the entry summary declaration of a product to be regulated not already by delegated acts. i therefore believe that i can support them in the hope that they will be implemented as soon as possible to improve the operation of the whole system and to the benefit of the european market.
in writing. − the commission has proposed to adapt the union customs code to developments in customs legislation and other relevant areas and to the procedural requirements resulting from the lisbon treaty. the main elements of innovation are: the use of electronic systems by member states, the verification of further simplifications by computerised procedures, rules on the acquisition of the origin and preferential origin of goods. with a view to the proper functioning of the customs union, i have supported the updating of common customs systems and rules.
in writing. - european customs are the gateway for goods entering our continent: the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect. it is true that italy has quite strict customs controls, especially when compared to the complacent ports of northern europe: the european union is a political union, a political union of the peoples of europe. there are few countries for which the defence of domestic and quality products is a central point: for others there are different priorities and therefore different approaches. in my view, customs should be the starting point for a serious fight against counterfeiting, especially asian counterfeiting, which has brought entire sectors, starting with textiles, to their knees for centuries, especially tuscany and pratese. the european union should therefore have uniform rules, applied in the same way: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them.
in writing. − given that a common, consistent customs rule is a prerequisite for the functioning of a single market, the union customs code is a critical element in regulating the european economy. in order to adjust to the evolution of institutions and facilitate the eu integration process and, in the meantime, promote competitiveness and economic growth, it is necessary to simultaneously ensure free movement of goods, control international trade and protect consumers, which cannot be achieved without aligning the union customs code to a more modernised, harmonised and uniform customs environment. therefore, i voted in favour of this proposal to revise the union customs code.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council establishing the union customs code (recast) because i believe that the customs union is a fundamental element of the functioning of the single market. it can only function properly if customs rules and systems are based on state-of-the-art systems applied in a uniform and consistent manner. this regulation will ensure a dynamic environment in terms of competitiveness and growth, while providing an appropriately uniform level of control of goods.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the database provided for in it must continue to be updated and provide the european commission with the data needed to calibrate the common agricultural policy. i agree with the rapporteur's approach in principle.
in writing. the proposal approved today concerns the agricultural accountancy information network (arin) which was set up in 1965 to meet certain needs of the cap, in particular those relating to income and the analysis of the economic functioning of agricultural holdings. over time, fisr has evolved and the network has expanded to all the member states that have become part of the eu. it is an important tool for the development and evaluation of agricultural policies, as it collects data on income, costs and revenues from a representative sample of eu farms each year. the sample currently includes some 80 000 enterprises out of the approximately 6 million in the eu-27. the rica therefore enables the commission to analyse the economic-structural situation and to calculate a series of indicators concerning incomes, productivity and production costs. this information is important in the context of changes to the cap, as it also supports the various research institutes involved in agricultural policy and rural development analysis and simulation.
in writing. − the farm data accountancy network (fdan), established in 1965, is a database program that plays an important role in providing data to support the commission and various research institutes in conducting economic analysis and evaluation of agricultural policies. the proposed changes in regulations optimise the management and maintenance of fdan. i therefore voted in favour of this proposal.
in writing. the proposal aims to align the commission's current implementing powers, as defined in council directives on coffee extracts, cocoa and chocolate products, food sugars, fruit jams, jams and jellies, and concentrated and dehydrated milk, with the provisions of the lisbon treaty. i voted in favour of this proposal with my colleagues from the ppe group.
in writing. - this report makes technical amendments to existing directives as a result of the application of the treaty of lisbon. what is being discussed is therefore the procedural aspects and what the european commission, within its implementing powers, can and cannot do. i applaud the way in which the colleagues who dealt with it conducted the negotiations.
in writing. − what is worth highlighting is the flexible and open approach suggested by the rapporteur, who proposes to limit the delegation to a (renewable) period of five years and to monitor the delegation of power by asking the commission to report on this before the end of each five-year period. the rapporteur highlights in this respect the approach taken in the recent amendment of the fruit juice directive (directive 2012/12/eu) where the annex containing the names, definitions and characteristics of the products was excluded from the scope of the delegation. it is clear that those essential elements do not need to be amended by means of delegated acts. the rapporteur agrees with the proposal to abolish the powers conferred on the commission to adapt existing directives to the general eu provisions applicable to foodstuffs, as they are already covered by existing food law.
in writing. − under current regulations, texts are rather ambiguous and not specific or appropriate enough to ensure food safety directives confer promptly their power on the commission. the proposed new wording modifying these texts is a successful solution to this problem. therefore, i voted in favour of this proposal.
in writing. - i agree with the general objective of this amendment to the directive. i believe that environmental impact assessment should be of fundamental importance in the decision-making process on public projects which may reduce green space, and that this priority should be given in a feasible, practical and not excessively costly way. that is why i do not share the rapporteur's approach on certain points.
in writing. − directive 2011/92/eu provides for a legal obligation to carry out an environmental impact assessment (eia) of public and private projects that may have a significant impact on the environment, before they are authorised. there is a consensus that the main objective of the directive has been achieved; the principles of environmental assessment have been harmonised across the eu by introducing minimum requirements concerning the type of projects to be assessed, the main obligations of the contractor, the content of the assessment and the participation of the competent authorities and the public. at the same time, within the permitting process, the eia is a tool to assess the environmental costs and benefits of specific projects in order to ensure their sustainability. as a result, the directive has become a key instrument for mainstreaming environmental issues and has produced both socioeconomic and environmental benefits, as well as protection of the urban environment.
in writing. - i think it is always desirable to simplify the issuing of visas to certain categories of foreign nationals, provided that students and researchers are among them. in this way, the eu enriches itself with human capital and ideas, and creates the conditions for the development of these assets in the countries of origin. that's why i voted for this deal.
in writing. - i support the visa agreement between the eu and the republic of cape verde. the proposal, by introducing the important principle of reciprocity, aims at a positive continuation of the already good relations between the two partners. i support the report because i consider the republic of cape verde to be a reliable and stable country and because i see no criticism in the proposal.
in writing. − this initiative, which simplifies the procedures for issuing short-stay visas to specific categories of cape verdean and eu citizens, is to be welcomed. i would like to stress that italy welcomes this agreement in the wider context of visa facilitation. i would also like to point out that my country has also concluded a representation agreement with portugal, which has set up a 'common application centre' with eu funding, and this is proving to work very well.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this agreement because it simplifies the procedure for citizens when travelling between europe and cape verde. freedom of movement is one of the fundamental rights of the european union; facilitating the issue of visas promotes this right and reduces the cost associated with travelling, which particularly benefits frequent travellers such as students and researchers participating in seminars. as the republic of cape verde is a stable democratic country with good governance, rule of law, and strong historical relations with europe, facilitating the issue of short-stay visas will be unlikely to affect the security of the union. the implementation of this agreement will also encourage cape verde to strengthen its relations with europe.
in writing. − in the context of the eu/cfsp special partnership, the european union has pursued a policy that goes beyond the traditional donor-recipient relationship and aims to deepen relations with cape verde, promote good governance, security and stability, sustainable development and the fight against poverty, culture and the building of an information and knowledge society, regulatory and technical convergence. the republic of cape verde is a democratic and stable country. the high level of governance practices and standards that the country can boast of is a good reason to continue developing relations with the european union. two agreements are under consideration to further push the boundaries of the area of freedom, security and justice, extending it beyond the european union. i therefore voted in favour, together with my colleagues from the epp.
in writing. - in italy in particular, we often have problems with the expulsion of irregular immigrants. there was a chance of an agreement with cape verde, and i did not miss the opportunity to vote in favour. solidarity must not mean opening our doors to those who have no right to remain in europe.
in writing. - i support the report because it deals with the readmission of cape verdean citizens whose stay is irregular. these obligations are mutual and also apply to family members and minor unmarried children. given the shared nature of the text, i vote in favour.
in writing. - today's vote in the european parliament marks a new milestone in relations between the eu and the republic of cape verde. the principle of reciprocity will facilitate the issuing of short-stay visas, thus facilitating reciprocal travel for citizens of both countries. the political importance of this agreement goes far beyond eu-cape verde relations, as it is the first agreement between acp countries and the eu on short-stay visas. i hope that parliament, as the expression of citizenship, will be kept informed by the commission on the progress of these agreements.
in writing. - i welcome this recommendation in the context of the eu-cape verde special partnership, the european union has committed itself to a policy that goes beyond the traditional donor-recipient relationship and is aimed at deepening relations with cape verde, promoting good governance, security and stability, sustainable development and the fight against poverty, culture and the building of an information and knowledge society, regulatory and technical convergence. the republic of cape verde is a democratic and stable country. cape verde, like the european union, adheres to the values and principles of democracy, good governance, respect for human rights and the rule of law. in 2007, the commission adopted a communication on the future of relations between the european union and cape verde, in which it recognised the existence of strong and specific historical relations between the two parties, characterised by close human and cultural ties and shared socio-political values. the high level of governance practices and standards that the country can boast of is a good reason to continue developing relations with the european union.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this agreement because it simplifies procedures for citizens when travelling between europe and cape verde. freedom of movement is one of the fundamental rights of the european union; granting readmission of persons residing without authorisation promotes this right and reduces the cost associated with applications for readmission, which particularly benefits frequent travellers such as students and researchers participating in seminars, and reduces associated costs to the union. as the republic of cape verde is a stable democratic country with good governance, rule of law, and strong historical relations with europe, granting readmission of persons residing without authorisation will be unlikely to affect the security of the union. the implementation of this agreement will also encourage cape verde to strengthen its relations with europe.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because the rate of youth unemployment has reached unacceptable levels in many member states. i think that the resources allocated to the fight against unemployment are totally insufficient. for this reason i agree with the report about the importance of strategic investment of eu structural funds for regional development, competitiveness and sustainable jobs.
in writing. − it is extremely important that the eu continues to inspire young people in this time of crisis. by providing more opportunities in education and in all forms of training, by investing in young people and supporting an entrepreneurial and innovative spirit, by courageously funding programmes for young people and by believing that every euro invested in the new generation has exponential effects on europe's growth, as well as on its future social cohesion. the eu has the right policies and instruments to achieve these goals, but it is up to the member states to decide. with the eu youth strategy, we are sending clear messages, setting priorities and developing guidelines. it is up to the member states, especially those facing the most serious problems, to adhere to these guidelines in an effective and timely manner. we must speed up the pace, correct or subsidize ineffective initiatives and always remain true to a historic call for the eu. in the face of pessimistic estimates and gloomy forecasts, we must remain optimistic about the achievement of our objectives. i therefore voted in favour of the report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by mr papanikolaou because i fully share parliament's decision to express itself on such a crucial and often insufficiently considered subject. i join the call for greater attention to be paid to the problems of youth unemployment, which is growing alarmingly in many countries. i also appreciate the reference to new technologies, which can indeed prove to be a very useful tool in support of community and national policies.
in writing. - first of all, we must be clear and explicit: the resources allocated to the fight against youth unemployment under the future mff, namely eur 6 billion, are still insufficient and need to be significantly increased. however, it should also be noted that the eu - despite endemic funding shortages - has done and is doing its part. on the other hand, it is scandalous that some italian regions do not use the european funds made available. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament on the subject of the future of the community. priority should be given to youth employment, with particular attention to vulnerable groups at high risk of social exclusion, in particular neets and disadvantaged young people, who need training pathways aimed at integration into the workforce. more needs to be done, aware that europe can contribute actively, but that alone, without the contribution of the member states (and the regions benefiting from european funds) it will not be able to solve one of the most serious problems that the crisis has caused.
in writing. - the youth issue is now the big issue in the old europe. this challenge is about the opportunities we will be able to offer our young people. i would remind you that on 27 april 2009, the commission published for the first time a communication setting out a new eu youth strategy, aimed at establishing a framework for cooperation on youth-related issues for the next decade and providing young people with more and better opportunities. the eu youth strategy has focused mainly on youth employability, encouraging entrepreneurship and promoting youth participation. we can say that, however, all this is still not enough. youth unemployment rates - especially in the mediterranean member states - are increasingly worrying. the challenge of a european strategy for youth is, as the rapporteur has pointed out, to give the european parliament greater centrality as an institution of control and guarantee. the real answer, however, is to focus on the effectiveness of the measures, the spendability of the funds, the facilitation of access to eu contributions and measures to make the most of the available resources.
in writing. − i strongly supported this resolution, although it cannot be ignored that this text refers to the implementation of the strategy in the three-year period 2010-2012, while we already have to look ahead. the new cycle of the eu youth strategy (2013-2015), which the commission proposes to focus on youth employment, will target those not in employment, education or training and will make full use of eu funding. the impact of the crisis on young people should be addressed more effectively, given the unacceptable levels of youth unemployment, especially in the southern eu, such as greece (59,1% in january 2013), spain (55,9%), italy (38,4%) and portugal (38,3%). to meet this challenge, member states need to make full use of the eu funding available and make the most of the opportunities offered by the youth opportunities initiative for young people not in employment or in education or training.
in writing. − the union has adopted a youth strategy to ensure that sufficient opportunities in education, innovation and professional training for young people are provided. providing such opportunities is of even greater importance considering the current state of the labour market in the aftershocks of the crisis. for a promising future for us europeans, it is necessary to invest a portion of the eu budget to support the development of young people which will, i believe, be a rewarding investment. therefore, i voted in favour of this proposal to send the signal of continually and consistently implementing the eu youth strategy to the member states.
in writing. − on 27 april 2009, the commission published a communication setting out a new strategy for youth, aimed at creating a framework for cooperation in this area for the next decade with the aim of providing young people with better opportunities. i voted in favour of mr papanikolaou's report because it proposes concrete initiatives to address the challenges facing young europeans in the coming years, particularly in the fields of education and training, employment and youth entrepreneurship. the european union must send a clear and optimistic message to young people that europe has the capacity and the strength to overcome the current crisis.
in writing. - europe faces many challenges in the coming years. the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the eu's new financial instruments, including the european regional development fund, and will continue to monitor the implementation of the union's new financial instruments. i therefore voted in favour of mr papanikolau's report.
in writing. − i support this report because it emphasises that we need to tackle youth unemployment as a priority problem in the eu. in june 2013, 23.5 % of active young people were jobless, with the rates ranging from 10 % or less in austria and germany to 64.2 % in greece. this situation has alarming consequences for young individuals, lowering their self-esteem, leaving their ambitions unrealised, reducing their earnings and career prospects, and delaying their opportunity to take up an independent adult life. for this reason we call on the commission to develop a one-year relief plan to tackle youth unemployment by creating jobs for at least 10 % of the young people affected, and on national parliaments to hold their governments responsible for delivering on the youth guarantee scheme, and to ensure that serious steps are taken to ensure that each young person (unemployed or having left formal education) will within four months receive either a good-quality offer of employment, continued education, an apprenticeship or a traineeship.
in writing. - the current situation of young people in the labour market is complex. unemployment among people of working age reaches a level of 11%, while among young people this rate is twice as high at 23%. the lack of jobs and the prospects of rapid negative changes for young people are reflected in the worsening demographic situation in europe. young people put off the decision to start a family indefinitely because of the uncertain prospect of a career. for this reason, in my view, the fight against youth unemployment must include the harmonization of employment policy reforms with measures to stimulate a general economic recovery. one of the reasons for the high levels of youth unemployment, alongside the lack of work experience, is inadequate qualifications. i therefore agree with the rapporteur that it is appropriate to organise and support national and european campaigns to promote appropriate vocational training. at the same time, it is becoming essential that member states recognise informal training or skills acquired outside the formal education system. these can make a positive contribution to a young person's personal development, strengthening their social integration and improving their position on the labour market.
in writing. − all actions undertaken by the member states must be assessed for effectiveness, the mechanisms introduced must be monitored as they evolve and the funds allocated must be actually paid. the very difficult situation of young people requires decisive action and the investment of adequate financial resources, but in the current economic situation in europe, where the policy of financial consolidation is dominant, these means must be well targeted and bring about a clear correction of the situation. it is very important to ensure that young people have a high-quality training course for a qualification, to provide adequate financial support to those who will organise this training course, and to introduce a mandatory monitoring system to ensure that the appropriate level of training is maintained and that it is effective. further strong promotion of the practice for a qualification is needed among employers, who must treat this system as a possibility of preparing people for concrete work situations. it is also necessary to support further development of vocational education, to organise and support european and national campaigns promoting vocational education and to monitor european strategies for professional practice. that is why i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution.
in writing. - with today's vote, parliament has once again confirmed its commitment to combating youth unemployment. this is a scourge that affects every european country and which, if not tackled with serious reforms of employment policy and adequate financial resources, risks jeopardizing the future of the new generations. the crisis measures adopted by most eu countries have reduced public spending, leading to cuts in education, training and support services; it is time to reverse this trend and secure a future for our young people. we must ensure that the member states and the commission take action through action plans on youth employment which define measures that are valid not only in the short, but also in the medium and long term. the data available to us unfortunately confirm that the situation of young people is bound to worsen further, especially in the absence of concrete action. i voted for a living income because i believe that every young person has the right to a stable, quality and decent-paying job. failure to act, or to act through inadequate measures, means robbing entire generations of the prospect of a better future than that of our parents.
in writing. - the figures for youth unemployment are worrying: 5.5 million up to 25 years. a huge number that gives a glimpse of a bleak future. as a young member of parliament, i am very sensitive to this issue, which i consider to be a political priority for the eu as well as for the member states. i welcome the recent approval of the 'youth guarantee' instrument, although i believe that, in order to be really effective, it should be extended to young people up to the age of 30. i put a question to the council on 22 may, but i am still waiting for an answer. i agree with all the measures mentioned in this report. in this period of severe economic crisis and shortage of public resources, it is necessary to use the available funds in the most effective way. the support for entrepreneurship is urgent and indefinite, as are forms of tax exemptions or reductions for businesses to create new jobs. the need to identify ways of communicating between the world of work and business is to facilitate the meeting of demand and supply. it is inconceivable that we should speak of 'inadequate qualifications' and 'waste of brains' - highly qualified young people who could contribute to the building of our society's well-being but who are relegated to playing much lower roles.
in writing. − given that youth unemployment has reached intolerable levels in the eu countries (23%), all efforts must be focused on putting every possible tool in the hands of the european institutions and the member states to ensure that at least 10% of unemployed young people find a job. the report is going in the right direction. the three pillars envisaged (quality education and training; support for smes; promotion of traineeships and apprenticeships) can indeed make a contribution, provided that they are accompanied by other 'structural' interventions. modernising education policies, with more efficient use of the individual career guidance system and a system for monitoring future job offers, can make higher education choices more conscious. the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. on the other hand, young people must know how to start their own economic activity, and they must have a system of facilities and preferential conditions in the form of tax exemptions or reductions. in this respect, the second pillar is certainly a good contribution. that is why i am voting in favour of this resolution, but with the aim of ensuring that it does not remain an isolated instrument.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mrs skrzydlewska's report because europe's economic recovery depends on employment and there will be no future for the union if we cannot guarantee a decent future for our young people. according to the latest eurostat data on 30 august 2013, the youth unemployment rate in italy is 39.5%. in greece and spain, the figure was 62.9% and 56.1% respectively. these figures are worrying to say the least. europe has set itself the target of raising the employment rate for people aged 20 to 64 to 75% by 2020, and we cannot ignore this. in 2011, the economic loss associated with youth unemployment was estimated at eur 153 billion in the member states, or around 1,2% of the union's gdp. to create 2 million jobs, however, would require less than 10 billion euros. the european parliament therefore calls on the member states and the regional and local authorities to join forces in this direction.
in writing. the report condemns the growing youth unemployment for vaguely pre-setting the implementation of common actions to combat it. i shall abstain as i do not think it is sufficient to make 'rhetorical' statements; the commission is also proposing to introduce a new system of taxation for the benefit of the taxpayer.
in writing. - it is important that the rapporteur has emphasised, in the context of the ways out of the long and thorny issue of youth unemployment, the value of public support and improved cooperation between employment services, employment counselling services, institutions, training institutes and youth support services. it is important that the prevention of early school leaving was not forgotten, among other issues, and finally, it is particularly agreeable that the fight against youth unemployment should be carried out within the framework of a more general action to stimulate economic recovery and reform employment policies.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by ms joanna katarzyna skrzydlewska because it is a way for the european parliament to make its voice heard in support of one of the key pillars of recovery in the eu: a guarantee of stable, long-term and qualified employment for young people. the report commits the commission and the council to review the budget allocated to the employment chapter in the 2014-2020 budget, citing the inadequacy of the 6 billion provided for in the youth guarantee to address unemployment. in europe there are 5.5 million young people unemployed, while the neet threshold, those who are not in education or work, has reached 15%, with a negative impact on european gdp of -1.2%, and 2 million jobs to be filled. if the eu is serious about taking care of these numbers, more funds are needed to promote education, training, employment and the modernisation of employment systems, but above all we need to direct incentives towards regions and local authorities, the only ones who really know the local labour market and its needs.
in writing. - the situation of young people in europe is dramatic, especially in some countries, such as italy; the data are frightening, with youth unemployment peaking at around 50%: that means that one out of every two people in this age group is out of the job market. the social buffer is often the family, but it is clear that this situation cannot last for long: the young people are the future of society and should have the opportunity to play a direct role from the start, rather than being left to their parents for years. the other day in this house we were discussing mortgages: it is an example like many others, but one that illustrates the tragedy of the situation of young people today. the dream of owning a house is often destined to remain so, and the lack of employment also affects the chances of building and consolidating one's own family, with a child that has become a luxury that few can afford. we cannot delay any longer . the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat this problem, and i am sure that the commission will take them into account in its proposals for the future.
in writing. - i supported this resolution because the situation of young people in the labour market is very difficult. unemployment among people of working age reaches a level of 11%, while among young people this index is twice as high and stands at 23%. today, there are over 5.5 million unemployed people under 25 in the european union. there is a significant variation between member states - while in germany and austria the unemployment rate does not exceed 9%, in greece and spain, which are in the throes of the crisis, it is already above 55%. this situation creates a bleak outlook for the young person entering adulthood. the lack of jobs and the prospects of rapid negative changes for young people are reflected in the worsening demographic situation in europe. young people put off the decision to start a family and become parents indefinitely, as they face an uncertain career. for this reason, the fight against youth unemployment must be harmonized with actions based on incentives for general economic recovery and reforms of employment policy. that is why i supported the amendment by mr angelilli which calls for a tax relief for companies that employ young people.
in writing. - i shall vote in favour of the motion for a resolution by the european parliament on the fight against youth unemployment: possible solutions. the present employment situation is described by worrying data: the unemployment rate in the european union is 11%, but if you look at the category of young people under 25, the figure rises alarmingly to 23%. to combat this phenomenon, it is therefore urgent to adopt flexible measures which take account of regional specificities. firstly, young people must be given training adapted to the needs of the labour market and a counselling system to inform and guide them in their choice of educational path. as regards the current integration into the professional sphere, however, it is necessary to encourage private initiative, to simplify administrative procedures and to provide young people with tax exemptions and benefits. mobility must also be encouraged by means of a smooth and regulated community coordination system. i therefore consider this proposal useful in order to act on the two fronts of modernising education and integrating young people into a more open and inclusive world of work.
in writing. - the skrydlewska report was voted on today in plenary. in the european union, the number of unemployed people aged 25 and under is over 5.5 million. the lack of experience and skills unsuited to the needs of the labour market are increasing. the lack of employment is also reflected in the demographic situation in europe. young people put off the decision to start a family indefinitely because of the uncertain future they face in their careers. i therefore agree with the rapporteur that efforts to combat youth unemployment must be based on a comprehensive strategy, including measures to support smes, promote entrepreneurship among young people, reduce school failure and extend to holders of qualifications up to the age of 30 the system approved by the epsco council which currently guarantees young people under 25 a job, training or traineeship within four months of their registration on the unemployment register. in this context, particular attention should be paid to important elements such as the funds earmarked for this purpose from a separate budget line and from the european social fund which can be a real support to the member states in difficult times of crisis.
in writing. in europe, the unemployment rate among people of working age is 11%, while among young people it is twice as high, at 23%. i have chosen to support mr skrzydlewska's report because the fight against youth unemployment must be implemented through actions based on incentives for a general economic recovery and through employment policy reforms, through initiatives aimed at supporting entrepreneurship and creating new jobs. the effective improvement of the situation of young people depends to a large extent on the strengthening of cooperation between employment services, training institutions and youth support services, which also actively involve the social partners and representatives of young people or youth organisations.
in writing. the situation of young people in the labour market is unfortunately dramatic, with percentages exceeding 20% in almost all member states. the fight against youth unemployment must therefore be combined with measures based on the stimulus of a general economic recovery and on reforms of employment policy: the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos at work is a very good one.
in writing. - the report by mrs corazza bildt merely takes stock of the application of the services directive. but it is not the text that businessmen and service providers were expecting. it is however positive that some amendments have been incorporated which highlight the difficulties in implementing and interpreting the services directive for certain professional and business categories. more importantly, it has highlighted the increasing bureaucratic burdens on smes and the difficulties in accessing credit. thanks to an amendment tabled with many other colleagues, on authorizations/concessions, it was reiterated that a fair return must be guaranteed and not just a fair depreciation of investments. i did not, however, vote in favour of the report. i take this opportunity to call on the european commission to pay greater attention to the seaside tourism sector, which, with its more than 30 000 businesses, represents an italian excellence and specificity in europe. a sector which should have been excluded from the services directive, but which now needs specific legislation to safeguard jobs and business continuity.
in writing. - the rejection by the centre-right majority of all the amendments tabled to this report has convinced me to vote against its adoption. the rejection of references to social security and labour legislation in the service sector and the reactionary idea that economic development can only be achieved by regulating this and other sectors demonstrates, once again, the blindness of conservative and right-wing forces. they have not yet understood that the solution to the economic crisis and the lack of competitiveness of european companies cannot be found in the abolition of social and labour rights.
in writing. - the liberalisation of the services market is undoubtedly an important lever for overcoming the economic crisis. it has been estimated that its full implementation could bring it to around 2,6% of gdp. this requires every effort to fully implement the services directive. i believe that bureaucracy, which is sometimes an insurmountable obstacle, especially for smes, must be reduced, as must discriminatory practices affecting consumer confidence. i also share the need to create an interaction with the vocational qualifications directive, because it is appropriate for the states to abolish as soon as possible unjustified requirements that block access to certain professions. within the member states there are different entities, some of which are subject to the strict application of the services directive, but which will hardly bring added value to the european market. i am thinking of the italian maritime concessions, which the european commission considers to be authorizations, which would have to comply with strict competition rules, although it is a very limited sector, typical and representative of italy. in cases like this, i would like to see a real balance of interests in order to see what real potential benefits would be gained from the strict application of the directive in terms of jobs, welfare and economic growth.
in writing. - this is a completely inadequate resolution and that is why i have voted against it. the liberal approach which pervades it does not in any way call into question the negative effects which are also inherent in a simplistic application of the directive. in particular, it is not taken into account that - with the onset of the most serious economic and financial crisis europe has known since the end of the second world war - the implications for the companies concerned and, above all, the social implications for workers have changed completely. it cannot be ignored that the application of the directive at this stage must take account of the particularities of the territories, also in relation to the different impact of the crisis on the different regions of europe. in some circumstances parliament has lacked the courage. that is not the case: the commission has not yet taken a decision on the matter, but it is not yet clear whether the commission will take a decision on the matter. for these reasons i have voted against.
in writing. − the internal market committee has drawn up a further own-initiative report on the 'bolkestein' for its future stages. in view of the poor results achieved so far, our delegation does not share this text. it also contains false statements such as that 'bolkestein has delivered tangible results in terms of growth and employment'. the data coming from our territory says exactly the opposite. i therefore vote against.
in writing. - we all agree, or almost, in this house on the benefits that the internal market has brought. we certainly also agree that companies are subject to a long list of requirements which, taken individually, seem harmless, but which, taken together, constitute a serious burden for smes. articles 15 and 16 of the directive allow member states to decide whether certain national requirements may be maintained on the basis of checks of necessity and proportionality. unfortunately, too often some member states have interpreted the right to protect and promote national markets and professions too broadly. the member states must instead tackle responsibly, as a matter of priority, the so-called 'grey areas'. in particular, burdensome legal forms and shareholding requirements, territorial restrictions and economic necessity checks prevent establishment in another member state, hamper the provision of services and exclude certain players from the market. for example, architects may be forced to change their business model to open a branch in another member state. this is unacceptable in a single market with common rules.
in writing. - i am voting against the european parliament's motion for a resolution on the internal market in services, which takes account of the present situation and the next steps. the construction of a common european model that promotes a balanced and sustainable social market economy is clearly a priority. in particular, the services sector, which accounts for 65% of the eu's gdp, is the engine that can pull member states out of recession. although the single market in this area has been strengthened by the services directive adopted in 2006, the latter has not been implemented with the desired effectiveness and homogeneity. that is why i think this proposal is not up to the task, especially because it does not provide answers and does not address social issues.
in writing. - i voted against the report by mrs anna maria corazza because it is a political instrument which has little to do with reality. the committee on the internal market has in recent months drawn up its own-initiative report on 'bolkestein' looking towards the future; unfortunately, this document does not seem to open up a full and frank debate. this directive should be amended in particular in so far as it requires that, in the case of authorizations for the pursuit of an activity involving the exploitation of a limited public asset, tenders must in no way provide for any right of priority, guarantee or reimbursement of investments made and not yet amortised for outgoing suppliers. the text must also be rejected as it has not produced any concrete results in terms of growth and employment.
in writing. the text presented by mrs corazza bildt calls on the member states to assume their responsibilities by correctly applying the services directive. the economic crisis has made it even more urgent to act to unlock the full potential of the services sector for growth and jobs.

madam president, in view of the alleged pressure exerted by the russian federation on the states of eastern europe, i think we must ask ourselves: what is the state that does not defend its interests? we, as the european union, must ask ourselves the same question and set ourselves the same objective: we defend our interests! if we analyse the trade relations between the european union and russia in relation to those between the european union and the eastern partnership countries, it is clear from the comparison that relations with russia are by far the most important and that russia is the largest economic partner for the european union. in short, this simple comparison shows that russia's commercial role for our companies and our economic activities is very important. in this connection, i believe that the expansion and growth of these exchanges should be encouraged and promoted and that russia should be considered a resource and an important partner in the activation of privileged relations. i imagine that a programme of expansion of trade relations to the east which does not involve russia would be incomplete and might even create political friction between moscow and brussels. it is in our interest to understand and accept this fact as soon as possible because the european union has every interest in encouraging these relations.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to thank you for your report. the european union is the world leader in the production, sale and export of seeds and seedlings. it is not just the big companies that are always talking about. this is what many small and mediumsized enterprises throughout the european union are doing. i think these companies will be happy to have a clear regulation on how they access genetic resources. this creates legal certainty and also facilitates access to new genetic resources, which is absolutely necessary for breeding, without which breeding is not possible. but we must not introduce rules which will make european breeding inferior to other competitors in the world and perhaps cause them to leave europe. i think there are five points which we must take into account when ratifying this protocol and when we adopt the report tomorrow. we cannot demand rules that go beyond the nagoya protocol. secondly, we must not allow the protocol to be applied retroactively. thirdly, we do not need special funds where money is stored, where it is not known where it is going, but where it is known where it is coming from - that is, from the companies. fourthly, there must be no legislation which calls into question the breeder's privilege. fifthly, there must be no chain of responsibility beyond the first user, the grower. i am convinced that if we enforce these five principles, then the implementation of the nagoya protocol will be beneficial for those working in the breeding sector and thus for small and mediumsized enterprises in europe.

in writing. - i congratulate the rapporteur and the whole team who have followed this long and important negotiation on behalf of parliament. the details agreed in this measure are very important because, in this particular case, the 'how' is at least as important as the 'what' is done. to be clear, the shared objective of transferring some of the powers of prudential supervision from the national central banks to the european one is not enough. if this transfer is not done with respect to the principle of subsidiarity, efficiency is lost and only money is spent on translations. if the ecb is not given the powers of inspection and the legal instruments to act, it becomes a farce. if the transfer of competence is not gradual, a gap opens up in terms of organisation and staff adequacy. i voted in favour of this proposal because i found a great deal of coherence between the objectives and the instruments provided.

in writing. − the proposal for a council regulation conferring specific tasks on the ecb concerning policies relating to the prudential supervision of credit institutions is the linchpin of the future eu banking union. with this text, for which i thank mrs thyssen, the ecb will act as a supervisor and will have the task of preventing bank failures and preventing the instability of a single credit institution from spreading throughout the banking system, thus preventing the harmful effects on the real economy that we have seen since the 2008 crisis. this will ensure better monitoring of european banks and greater stability of the european financial and credit sector, to the benefit of businesses and households.
