mr president, i think that the resolution voted by this parliament on the syrian issue deserves some distinction. i want to distinguish them as an italian and i want to distinguish them as a catholic. as an italian, i would like to stress that italy is seriously affected by the current embargo on syria, since all trade relations with the mediterranean are affected by this embargo, which restricts the transit of goods both from syria and from other countries. the outbreak of war could be devastating for the italian economy and its commercial activities, but also for those of the european union. i would also like to point out that italy, because of its geographical location in the mediterranean, will have to endure any migratory phenomena and as a catholic i would like to make it clear that we are certain - indeed, we are quite certain - that the rebels currently fighting the assad regime will certainly not be kind to the many christians who live there.
in writing. − i support this resolution because it states that a lasting solution to the current crisis in syria can only be achieved through a syrian-led inclusive political process with the backing of the international community. for this reason it is fundamental to support the efforts of the european union and of un-arab league joint special representative lakhdar brahimi to achieve progress in the geneva ii process and at the un security council. with this text we also urge the eu and the member states to live up to their humanitarian responsibilities and to increase their assistance to syrian refugees. i personally strongly believe that any military intervention – with or without un authorisation – in syria is bound to have grave and highly unpredictable consequences and that a worsening of the situation on the ground cannot be excluded. only a strategic, global approach articulating humanitarian and political dimensions can put an end to the violence and mass human rights violations and promote a democratic transition in syria.
in writing. - i am very perplexed about what is happening in syria. diplomatic moves do not achieve the desired effect, military maneuvers seem to have begun but are hopefully not reaching the final stage, and meanwhile the civil war continues, reaping deaths on both sides and driving both (if there are really only two) parties away from some semblance of reason. i believe that the european union must exert all possible pressure to find a balanced, peaceful solution that minimizes the damage while respecting the principles on which the eu was founded and thrives.
in writing. - i think many of you will agree that the european union needs a common position on the situation in syria. a dramatic civil war with enormous international repercussions cannot go unnoticed, we must make our voices heard, not to take one side over the other, but because of the moral duty to react in order to protect the civilian population and to ensure that the international community is able to establish rules and take appropriate action against crimes against humanity. that is why i voted in favour of the european people's party resolution, in the hope that the diplomatic efforts to establish responsibility for the war crimes committed will bear good fruit for peace and the security of the citizens.
in writing. we all condemn the use of chemical gas against the syrian people, just as we condemn the massacres of christians in the countries so-called liberated by the arab spring. but how can we possibly think of countering the use of chemical weapons with depleted uranium missiles which will contaminate the air and water of a stricken country for decades to come? let us not forget that the assad regime is backed by the mullahs of iran and that just last weekend iranian militiamen, in concert with the iraqi army, stormed camp ashraf, carrying out cold-blooded executions of 52 helpless and defenseless refugees, even in the hospital. seven people, including six women, have been kidnapped and are being transported to iran, where they will face the death penalty. why has parliament not wanted to discuss this, rejecting the request made by my group, the epp? why is the baroness ashton silent? where was the un when camp ashraf was attacked?
mr president, the situation in egypt is still very dramatic and it seems very difficult to see any solution to a conflict which is literally tearing the country in two. the so-called "arab spring" has aroused too much enthusiasm and approval in the west, which fails to understand that the middle east is too sensitive an area to be able to express judgments, which risk being hurried and denied in a short time. egypt came from decades of one-man authoritarian rule, which it has held with the unconditional support of both the united states and europe. his fall, supported by the latter, saw new elections and the victory of the muslim brotherhood, which we saw how they governed: the remedy has been worse than the disease, demonstrating that a muslim-inspired government is not sustainable, especially in a country where there is a large christian minority and a strong feeling of institutional secularism. i just want to hope that these different souls can come to an agreement and resolve a situation that otherwise risks compromising the stability of the entire area.
in writing. − i support this text because after the military coup of july egypt is in a very unstable and worrying situation. the political tensions continue to provoke violent clashes, which have resulted in more than 1 000 deaths and many more injured. i am firmly convinced that any exclusion or prosecution against a democratic political force or actor in egypt can only lead to increased radicalism. we need to condemn in the stronger possible terms the disproportionate use of force against the protesters without penalising the egyptian population while suspending aid to the country. in addition, with this resolution we urge the eu to proceed without delay to establish an eu mechanism providing legal and technical assistance to arab spring countries in the process of asset recovery. this instrument, already supported by this parliament on several occasions, was delayed because of the turmoil in egypt. it is vital to bear in mind that asset recovery has a highly symbolic value and may contribute largely to restoring accountability, creating stability and building solid institutions in the spirit of democracy and the rule of law in the partner countries concerned.
in writing. - i have the utmost respect for the will of the people. i think it's one of the greatest achievements of the modern era. i cannot, however, understand how one can expect to convince the other side with weapons and violence. i am rather worried about the direction that political issues are taking in egypt, not so much for the outcome that they seem to have (as long as the people want it, i am fine) but for the methodologies that are described to us. i agree with this resolution because i would like a peaceful solution and would prefer to see the european union actively engaged in seeking mediation between the parties involved, in the interests of the population first and then of the stability of the whole airspace.
in writing. − i abstained in voting on this resolution because although it makes a good analysis of the importance of global maritime flows for the european union, it regrets cuts in national defence budgets. it also encourages increasing the military presence at seas in order to secure trade and energy routes. i addition, i disagree with the idea of an intensified eu-nato relationship and of any further civil-military cooperation.
in writing. - parliament has shown by its vote today that it is willing to give the maritime dimension, an aspect of the common security policy which has hitherto been dealt with in a fragmentary manner, the right importance. the csdp already has two maritime instruments, eunavfor and eucap, but these have not yet been properly implemented. the maritime dimension can play a key role in preventing and managing crisis situations and in defending freedom of navigation. i therefore believe that it is necessary that future action in the field of security and defence policy should also take account of this aspect in order to protect the strategic maritime areas to the greatest extent possible.
in writing. - it is time for europe to take responsibility for protecting our maritime borders: in recent years, the member states bordering the mediterranean, italy in particular, have been left to deal with a very difficult situation, with hundreds of disembarkations and thousands of refugees to be taken in. it is too easy to criticize the methods used when we have realities that have given so much, are always under pressure and are now close to collapse. the current situation in syria and egypt does not bode well for the future either, in the sense that there will very likely be further landings to escape the internal problems of these countries. i would like the european union to take direct and decisive action, particularly to combat the daily trafficking of human beings in the mediterranean, which is certainly enriching the organised crime that runs it. perhaps europe can do better than italy, and certainly its direct involvement would put it in a more responsible position to manage the entire migration emergency. we shall see if the european union is only capable and supportive in words, or if it finally decides that it is time to act in practice.
in writing. − maritime space is playing an increasingly important geostrategic role, as it involves different sectors such as international trade, security and the environment. the maritime dimension can also play an important role in the common foreign and defence policy. the european union has a strong interest in maintaining a safe maritime environment, guaranteeing the free movement and safety of goods and persons in this space, as well as ensuring the application of the principles of the united nations charter in this area. i therefore voted in favour of mrs gomes' report because a comprehensive approach, combining political, economic, social and diplomatic instruments, can be the most effective way for the european union to respond to a number of challenges in the maritime sector.
in writing. − i abstained in the vote on this report because i find the nobel prize to the european union incongruous with the desire to expand the eu military sector. in a time of economic crisis, i find reduction of the national defence budgets more than proper. we should support a drastic rationalisation of european military capacities in order to reduce existing overcapacities which are not sustainable.
in writing. - the military and defence sphere should, in my view, be a subject in which the european union would certainly need to be more involved. fortunately, we live in a time of peace on european soil and i do not think we should use force between the different member states to overcome our differences, which are important. i think it is very stupid and uneconomic to continue the arms race alone: it is absolutely useless in my view for the european states to have, for example, a considerable air force and perhaps to neglect the naval force. military intervention must always be the last resort, but in that case i would also welcome a real european army, which could possibly take action in missions where required: the new military technologies are very expensive and i believe that cooperation and sharing of costs at european level is necessary and appropriate. one of the key principles for me is subsidiarity, and that is why i have often criticized the european union when it intervenes inappropriately in the internal affairs of countries: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them.
in writing. − the report is one of a number of initiatives taken in the wake of the december 2012 european council to identify proposals to be brought to the attention of the december 2013 european council on security and defence, the first summit dedicated to defence since the entry into force of the lisbon treaty. i voted in favour of the report because it contains proposals on how to update the institutional framework of military structures, it encourages better planning of resources and better management of civilian and military missions, and it also calls for the creation of a european military union.
in writing. − i support this resolution because i believe that the eastern partnership summit in vilnius could become an important opportunity for the gradual improvement of eu-belarus relations. for this reason with this text we urge the belarusian authorities to respect human rights and work towards a democratic transition in order to end the country’s self-imposed isolation from the rest of europe. i also think that the eu should carry out an in-depth evaluation of the euʼs current restrictive measures against belarusian officials and entities, which have so far proved to be ineffective in bringing democratic change in belarus.
in writing. - i congratulate the rapporteur on the balance of the compromises. i voted in favour of this report because i think it is a good solution in an attempt to discourage recent behaviour which is unacceptable by our standards and which is aimed at drawing belarus into the european sphere of influence. i do not want to judge the policies of other states, and i do not do so in this case either, but the eu needs to have countries around it that can offer guarantees in terms of stability, respect for the law and economic growth. our policy towards belarus, while guided by these principles, must be pursued until it achieves the desired results.
in writing. − the european union has always shown particular attention to its eastern neighbours, as the enlargements of 2004 and 2007, and the recent enlargement to croatia, demonstrate. the union cannot therefore remain indifferent to the situation in belarus. the country's high democratic deficit, highlighted in the 2010 and 2012 elections, media censorship and political arrests in recent years are all elements that risk damaging the country's relations with the rest of europe. the eastern partnership summit in vilnius in november could be a unique opportunity to discuss these issues and to call for a loud signal from belarus that it is willing to make a democratic breakthrough.
mr president, i think that in the face of a state which is defending its commercial interests, the european union must respond by seeking common ground, by seeking elements which can lead to mutually beneficial results. it is clear that our relations of partnership with the east, which see russia as the state with which we have the greatest trade relations, must be implemented and improved, but when the result is russia's withdrawal from its historical partners, clearly nothing has been understood. i think it is in the interest of this european community to intensify relations with all the countries of eastern europe, especially those where there are greater opportunities for growth in our exports and those from which it is easier to import important resources in terms of raw materials.
in writing. − to stop the activities of international criminal networks and to contribute to their dismantling, to prevent terrorist attacks, to improve cybersecurity, to ensure border security, to increase resilience to natural disasters, to combat violence against children and women, and to combat child pornography: these are the objectives that the eu's internal security strategy should aim to achieve. greater eu coordination in these areas can provide added value. that is why i support this report.

in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because health and safety at work must be guaranteed and there should be clear legislation on that. that is why it is not acceptable that the strategy 2007-2012 on health and safety at work expired in 2012 but has not yet been replaced by the commission. for this reason with this text we urge the commission to present the new strategy for the years between now and 2020 as soon as possible.
in writing. − with this report we want to ask the european commission to commit itself to adopting a new european strategy for health and safety at work: i hope, of course, that it is not just a matter of fine words, as is often the case, but that it is focused on certain important points. one principle must be clear, and it is rightly reflected in the text: the economic crisis must not be used as a pretext for compromising policies to prevent occupational risks. in times of austerity, there is a risk of cutting expenditure items which are considered superfluous or non-essential, such as safety at the workplace: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. italy unfortunately has a sad record in this area, and we hear daily of the death of a person in the line of duty: this is intolerable, because work should allow us to live, not lead us to death. the number of accidents with injuries of varying severity is even higher: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to the full.
in writing. − protecting workers in both safety and health must be considered as one of the priorities for improving the quality of life of european citizens. the european strategy 2007-2012 on safety and health at work expired at the end of 2012 and parliament therefore called on the commission to act promptly, as it recognises the importance of promoting high quality and safe working environments. the commission has decided to launch a public consultation in 2013 on the direction of future eu policy initiatives in the field of safety and health at work, although in the commission staff working document entitled 'assessment of the european strategy for health and safety at work 2007-2012', accompanying the consultation, it is not clear whether or when the new strategy will be adopted by the commission. in view of the innumerable accidents at work, often fatal, i am expressing my support for the drafting of a document shared at european level, aimed at regulating workplaces for the protection of citizens, which does not, however, consist merely in an increase in burdens and costs for enterprises.
in writing. - the phenomenon of crossborder collective bargaining is still not widespread but, with globalisation, it is set to grow. despite the absence of legal provisions, the divergence of regulations and the plethora of problems that this entails, some 200 european transnational agreements have been concluded in recent years, involving some 10 million workers. this is, of course, a figure that is set to grow exponentially in the coming years. i think that is central and that we should insist on asking the commission to consider the possibility of an optional european legal framework for transnational corporate agreements, as it could prove useful and necessary for the purposes of greater legal certainty and transparency, as well as for the predictability and enforceability of legal effects for agreements which comply with the framework provisions. equally important is the demand for recognition of the contractual autonomy of the contracting parties, with the inclusion in the agreements of provisions on dispute settlement. it will be important in the near future to monitor and encourage the commission to take legislative initiatives as soon as possible to ensure legal certainty and the necessary safeguards.
in writing. the report calls for community legislative action to coordinate the trade unions of the various member states. the document presents one main problem: employers' associations do not seem interested in his promotion. there is also a risk of a lack of legitimacy, as the establishment of this body would lead to a separation (even physical) between trade union representatives and workers. i am voting against this report because, while it contains the shared objective of stopping the relocation to eastern europe, it contains other points which are not shared.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this resolution because the eu must pay particular attention to minors who arrive alone in our territory. we have a moral and a political obligation to protect the rights of children who need specific assistance and support due to their situation of vulnerability. moreover the conditions in which such minors are received in certain member states is completely unacceptable. for this reason we ask the commission to draw up strategic guidelines for member states which would be based on best practice at national level.
in writing. - on the subject of unaccompanied minors - coming from third countries and being in the territory of the member states without the assistance and representation of their parents or other adults legally responsible for them - i voted in favour of the resolution which aims to highlight the fragmentation of the current legislative provisions in this area and to suggest strategic guidelines to improve the situation of unaccompanied minors. i believe that all the issues relating to the interests of the child involved in every stage of the process which begins with his arrival on european territory must be analysed and addressed. in this regard, it is necessary for the commission to develop guidelines for member states and for member states to adopt national strategies to obtain a comprehensive picture of the number of unaccompanied minors, to examine specific needs in order to provide them with adequate protection and to address related issues with specific measures, sharing best practices. more specifically, adequate protection of the child will have to cover such fundamental aspects as housing, education and access to health care. the cooperation of the third countries of origin will be essential if we are to achieve the objectives we have set ourselves.
in writing. the report deals with the issue of unaccompanied minors arriving in the eu. one solution is to provide assistance through the legal guardian, whose task is to accompany, assist and represent the child, and to provide a range of services relating to his or her protection. this report, although it presents some shared elements concerning the protection of minors, cannot be fully supported by us because it contains elements of strong criticism such as family reunification, as the child himself could be used as a 'pass' to reach european territory. that is why i am voting for abstention.
in writing. the text presented by mr griesbeck contains general recommendations and strategic guidelines to improve the status and living conditions of unaccompanied minors in the territory of the union from the moment of their arrival and throughout the procedure of reception or return to the country of origin. in expressing my vote in favour, i would like to stress, as i have already done during the discussions in the committee on development on this sensitive subject, that children must always be regarded as particularly vulnerable and that the principle of the best interests of the child must prevail over all other considerations when dealing with unaccompanied children.
in writing. − according to the 2010 european competitiveness report, the cultural and recreational sectors account for 4.5% of gdp and provide 8.5 million jobs in the european union. several studies confirm the economic importance of these sectors, which, in a europe hit hard by the economic recession, are showing a higher than average growth rate. i believe that in a time of general economic crisis, which is putting our sense of belonging to europe at risk, it is essential to support the cultural and creative sectors which contribute to economic growth and employment in europe. these sectors play a major role as reference points for innovation, the positive effects of which are not limited to the spheres of culture and creation but extend to many sectors of the economy. as ambassadors of a dynamic and open europe, the cultural and creative sectors today face numerous challenges arising from the digital transition, globalisation, the strong cultural and linguistic fragmentation of markets and the difficulty of accessing funding. i therefore hope that the commission, also by developing cooperation between member states, will adopt an integrated policy approach so that these sectors are used as engines of economic and social development.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the strategy proposed by the european commission for the cultural and creative sectors, which account for 4.5% of gdp and provide 8.5 million jobs in the european union. i too believe that the potential for competitiveness and exploration must be unleashed to maximise the positive effects on the whole economy. skills development, access to finance, the dissemination of new business models, the widening of the audience, access to international markets and the strengthening of links with other sectors are all aspects that deserve to be strengthened. this will allow for better use of european funding, the creative europe programme with €1.8 billion for 2014-2020 and cohesion policy funds.
in writing. - a motion for a resolution was voted this morning in plenary in strasbourg on the need to promote the cultural and creative sectors in order to promote economic growth and employment. i agree with the rapporteur, marie-thérèse sanchez-schmid, that it is extremely important to support culture and creativity, as these are two activities which make a huge contribution to economic growth and employment in europe. for this reason, the cultural and creative sectors must be used as engines of economic and social development and be integrated into productive activities which, in addition to increasing employment and especially economic development, also offer benefits at the social level. i am, in the final analysis, satisfied with today's vote.
in writing. − according to the 2010 european competitiveness report, the cultural and creative sectors account for up to 4.5% of gdp and provide 8.5 million jobs in the eu. several studies confirm the economic importance of these sectors, which, in a europe hit hard by the recession, are showing a higher than average growth rate. in view of the fact that, in a time of general economic crisis, the cultural and creative sectors clearly contribute to stimulating economic growth and creating jobs, we believe that the political actors concerned will be able to work together in an organisational way in the broadest possible consensus to refocus europe on creativity and culture in order to better prepare us for the new challenges that are coming in a globalised world.

in writing. in the context of the regulation establishing a list of permitted health claims for foodstuffs, the european commission has approved a new health claim: "carbohydrates help maintain normal brain function". however, the use of this indication has been subject to certain conditions. it can only be labelled if the product is not 100% sugar and contains at least 20 g of carbohydrate. however, to make the use of the indication conditional on the presence of a certain amount of sugar is in fact equivalent to introducing a nutritional profile, bypassing the specific legal procedure for the definition of nutritional profiles. the commission is going beyond its mandate in doing so. furthermore, the introduction of the conditions of use by the commission is unscientific and arbitrary. the european food safety authority, explaining that a daily dose of 130 g of carbohydrates satisfies the brain's glucose needs, has not established any restriction on use with reference to the sugar content of the products. such an approach to the conditions of use for such indications risks discriminating between the individual product and creating confusion for the consumer. for these reasons, i support the report voted in the envi committee and i oppose the introduction of the health claim as proposed by the european commission.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, i wanted to emphasize the subject which has been, not by chance, at the heart of the debate in which we are participating. a treaty, a fisheries agreement, inevitably entails mediation and rapprochement which may benefit certain territories and certain countries and not be equally effective for others. it is, however, an extraordinary instrument of economic and social policy, on the condition - and it is no accident that this has been repeatedly mentioned - that it is fully respected and that if there is any deviation from its proper implementation, those who have promoted it, in this case the european union, have the means to take immediate corrective action. the time-testing is therefore very important because instruments of this kind must be widely accepted and not be a hindrance to the right course.

framework and to work inclusively with all countries and partners. during the 2013 european development days we will also dedicate a special panel to gender in the context of the post-2015 framework.

the next item is the report by erminia mazzoni, on behalf of the committee on regional development, on effects of budgetary constraints for regional and local authorities regarding the eu’s structural funds expenditure in the member states (2013/2042(ini)) (a7-0269/2013).
the rapporteur. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the report we are discussing analyses the effects on the spending of the structural funds of the budgetary constraints imposed on regional and local authorities by the stability pact: the economic and financial crisis has tightened the rules for balanced budgets by imposing blanket cuts in spending without any distinction between current expenditure and investment. the immediate effect has been to limit, almost to the point of totally inhibiting, policies aimed at boosting the economy and growth. the consequence of this situation has had repercussions in particular on cohesion policy, which is by its nature geared to investment expenditure in order to overcome social, economic and territorial imbalances between member states. unfortunately, amid cuts and restrictions, regional and local authorities, who are called upon to implement the european agendas, are now faced with the difficulty of meeting their programming commitments. the figures on the percentage of spending achieved, on the widening gap between strong and weak economies, confirm that cohesion is falling behind. the report therefore makes three proposals aimed at balancing the need for public investment with strict compliance with the fiscal rules of the union budget in relation to national co-financing of european structural funds programmes. the first is the exclusion of public expenditure related to the implementation of programmes co-financed by the structural and investment funds from the definition of structural deficit in the stability and growth pact: the justification is that this expenditure is intended to achieve the eu2020 objectives and to support competitiveness, growth and job creation. the current situation, on the other hand, creates a short-circuit between european policies, which means that on the one hand, spending is inhibited, and on the other hand, there are penalties for not spending. the second proposal in the report is that the investment burden should in any case be calculated net of taxation. these items are in fact current and capital items which are improperly used to determine the deficit. the third proposal is the possibility of budgeting the entire amount of european resources at the beginning of the programming period, leaving the national part of the cofinancing in subsequent budgets. the aim is to enable national, regional and local authorities to ensure that the revenue which they are expected to generate from investment in subsequent years is balanced. the report calls on the commission and the member states to take account of the proposals made in the ongoing negotiations on the cohesion package. the need for greater flexibility is also contained in the mandate which the regi committee has given to the rapporteurs who are involved in the trilogue on the cohesion legislative package, so we are working in perfect coherence. the report comes to the house with the almost unanimous vote of the committee on regional development: 40 votes in favour, with only 2 abstentions. in addition, the committee on budgets and the committee on employment and social affairs have given favourable opinions. this report is a fully coherent follow-up to the debate that has opened up in the european council, and is in line with the commitments on the introduction of the golden rule in european fiscal policies and with the objectives of building an inclusive, smart and sustainable europe by 2020. it is useless to continue to vote in this parliament calling on the european commission to promote employment, to promote the development of infrastructure, to stimulate the economy, if the critical points, the knots that the stability and growth pact highlights in the course of its implementation are not resolved. i hope, therefore, that in the light of these considerations parliament will be able to demonstrate, by voting in favour of the whole report, that it is an active and conscious co-legislator and will not be swayed by the attempts of a minority to weaken the community spirit in favour of a nationalist interest.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, mrs mazzoni's report is very good because it offers concrete proposals to ensure the necessary flexibility in respect of the stability pact. priorities include: it is worth remembering that 60% of the public productive investment is implemented at regional and local level; the commission will then exclude, if necessary even partially, the national part of the european funds from the pact. we are talking about strategic expenditure, which is vital to achieving the europe 2020 objectives. we are talking about supporting competitiveness, growth, jobs. the pact, it is worth remembering, is one of stability, but also of growth, we cannot die of austerity!
member of the commission. − mr president, the commission welcomes the parliament initiative and we also share the concerns expressed in the report by ms mazzoni. the economic crisis has really altered the convergence process among european regions and regional disparities are growing, in particular in terms of unemployment. regional and local authorities are key players to help european economies recover from the current crisis. in 2011, for example, more than 46 % of the growth-enhancing expenditure in the european union of 27 member states was carried out by sub-national authorities: 46 %. sub-national governments also contribute significantly to public investment. in 2012, around 60 % of total public investment in the european union of 27 was carried out by sub-national authorities. the economic crisis has reduced revenue for regional and local authorities, it is true, and the growth-enhancing type of expenditure and public investment has been dramatically squeezed. in 2011 sub-national public investment dropped to 2.1, returning to its 1997 level. in real terms sub-national public investment fell by 5.8 % in 2010, 6.5 % in 2011, and fell again in 2012. it is obvious that this situation has negative implications. several member states have signalled growing difficulties in co-financing eu programmes, which can only negatively affect delivery of the objectives. this trend is worrying as it shows that the economic crisis has seriously affected the capacity of regional and local authorities to provide public expenditure which is critical to maintaining favourable growth prospects in the future. the commission has proposed a number of measures to facilitate the budgetary management of these resources. firstly, we have proposed going for higher co-financing grades through top-ups in the current period and in the future. secondly, the current situation also requires that resources be used in the most effective manner: in particular, the strategic orientation of the programmes has been enhanced and focused on the europe 2020 strategy, procedures have been simplified and the use of alternative financing instruments has been greatly encouraged. third, cohesion policy should also be closely aligned with the macroeconomic reforms undertaken in the context of the european semester. this is why a set of mechanisms tying cohesion policy programmes to macroeconomic governance has been introduced in the form of the ‘macroeconomic conditionalities’. at the same time, the commission announced that it will allow, under certain conditions of course, temporary deviations from the requirements of the preventive arm of the stability and growth pact to accommodate the national cofinancing of the eu-funded investment projects. implementation modalities of this procedure were recently clarified by the commission.

member of the commission. − mr president, i wish to thank the rapporteur, mr elles, for the speech he has just given, for the work he has done on this report and for his chairmanship of the taskforce of the european strategy and policy analysis system. this is an interinstitutional project which is very important to us. i would like also to congratulate him for the initiative he has demonstrated in developing the concept of this policy system, both during the pilot project and now in the preparatory action. the world is indeed changing at a speed and intensity that leaves many policy makers struggling on occasions to make sense of what it happening and what the policy responses should be. this policy system is an attempt to define how the institutions of the union can work together in a collaborative manner to identify the key global trends impacting on us, what the implications of those may be, and to suggest how we might fashion policy responses. so this is a unique interinstitutional project involving parliament, the commission, the council of the european union and the external action service, and one that is currently engaged in the production of reports analysing the major global trends in the economy, society and in international governance and power. next year, this european strategy and policy analysis system is scheduled to deliver a report to the presidents of the institutions that will offer analysis for the next institutional cycle, as they seek to chart the way ahead for the european union. the interinstitutional taskforce is currently considering what shape and form a permanent system might take. work on this is ongoing, looking at light formulas for bringing about this foresight capacity without putting additional pressure on financial and human resources. the commission will continue to contribute positively to these discussions. i wish the rapporteur well in his role as chair of this european strategy and policy analysis systems taskforce.

member of the commission. − mr president, the commission thanks the rapporteur, mrs regner, and the parliament for raising the issue of jurisdiction rules in employment matters. we share the aim of ensuring strong protection for the rights of employees in general, and in particular when they are involved in employment disputes. let me recall that the rights of employees have already been specifically addressed and strengthened in the recent brussels i regulation (recast), adopted on 6 december 2012. for instance, the new brussels i regulation provides for the right for employees to sue several employers together and the right for employees to have access to courts in europe, even if the employer is domiciled outside europe. the commission will carefully monitor the application of the new rules over the coming years, in the process paying close attention to the employment matters raised by parliament. this can then be considered in the context of the review, provided for in article 79, of the recast regulation. in this perspective, the commission could in the future consider looking into the issue of employment contracts, which has already been mentioned. this could be done by looking more specifically into the suggested fallback clause in article 21 in cases brought by the employee against the employer, defining as relevant the place of business from which the employee receives, or received, day-to-day instructions, rather than the place where the business which engaged the employee is situated.

the rapporteur. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, tomorrow's vote on the revision of the directive on the environmental impact assessment of certain public or private projects is a crucial test for the future of the union's environmental policy, the impact of which will be reflected for several years in the lives of millions of european citizens. this directive is of fundamental importance because it establishes the principle of informed decision before authorising projects which may have a significant impact on the environment, from motorways to intensive poultry farms. after almost 30 years of application, it is therefore time to revise this text, not only in the light of the critical issues identified but also to align it with the new priorities that the union has set itself in the meantime, such as the soil protection strategy, the roadmap for an efficient and effective use of resources, the 2020 strategy and the protection of biodiversity. i would like to pay tribute to the commission's determination to propose this text, which is certainly necessary but which is unfortunately - and i say this with a heavy heart - perhaps too ambitious for the sensibilities of a large part of this house. as rapporteur, i have already declared my full and unwavering support for this proposal and shared its content. consequently, my proposals have been limited to strengthening the text, such as introducing a clear rule against conflict of interest, or proposing the adoption of corrective measures in the event that monitoring and the resulting compensatory measures are ineffective. unfortunately, many colleagues - particularly from the conservative groups - from countries where the current directive is applied effectively, have strongly opposed this text, which is considered burdensome for businesses and difficult to apply for public administration. the climate of cooperation between the shadow rapporteurs, which i am grateful for, has led to a major revision of the text, without, however, distorting the ultimate objective of improving the efficiency and effectiveness of the start-up procedure for all the actors involved: public administrations, contracting authorities and the public concerned. as a result of the compromises reached, for example, the one-stop shop has become an option for member states like scoping, the information that the contracting authority has to provide in the screening procedure has been simplified and a framework has been established regarding decision times that allows member states to shorten response times if they wish. the amendments which have caused the most noise, however, are those concerning shale gas, which the commission did not include in its proposal. in line with the precautionary principle and as requested by parliament in its sonik resolution of 21 november 2012, i proposed to submit the exploration of unconventional gases, i.e. shale gas and natural gas from coal fields, to an environmental impact assessment. i believe that our water is too precious a commodity to be put at risk by the use of high impact drilling techniques such as hydraulic billing and therefore it is vital for the european union that the exploitation of shale gas is subject to the strictest environmental standards. the commission has already made a number of proposals, and i am sure that the commission will be able to support them. it is a pity because the lithuanian presidency has been very determined to complete the analysis of the text and, despite a tight timetable, an agreement at first reading before the end of the legislature is still possible. i therefore appeal to the sense of responsibility of my colleagues to bear in mind that with tomorrow's vote we have the opportunity to equip the union with a crucial operational tool to respond to the global challenges of the 21st century and to contribute concretely to the realisation of a green economy capable of ensuring the sustainability of the projects we want to implement in our territories and a better quality of life for all citizens of the european union.
