in writing. − in italy, decreased ict demand and investment by both consumers and enterprises caused by the crisis contributed significantly to the slow-down in the italian ict and electronic components sector. the italian government is responsible for providing assistance in reintegrating 480 workers into employment, including interview techniques, skills profiling, tutoring and occupational guidance, exploring job opportunities with new employers, matching skills and jobs and mentoring during the first phase of a new employment, all of which are associated with significant costs. the european globalisation adjustment fund has been created in order to provide additional assistance to workers suffering from the consequences of major structural changes in world trade patterns. thus i voted in favour of this proposal to mobilise the fund to ensure those who experienced the recent shock to the economy will receive necessary support.
in writing. - today, parliament approved in plenary an appropriation of eur 1 164 930 from the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) for the italian authorities to facilitate the reintegration of lombardy workers during the current period of a sharp increase in unemployment. in the lombardy region, two italian ict companies - anovo italia s.p.a. and jabil cm s.r.l. - made 529 redundancies during the period from 20 march 2011 to 20 december 2011. the numbers are alarming. for this very reason, i am pleased with today's decision and i am sure that the funds allocated will alleviate the terrible economic recession in italy, which is rooted in the global crisis and the dynamics of globalisation.
in writing. the european parliament voted to approve aid worth €3.7 million from the european globalisation adjustment fund to help around 1,030 workers laid off by the car manufacturer de tomaso automobili in the provinces of turin and livorno and another 529 workers who lost their jobs when two computer companies in lombardy, anovo italia and jabil cm, went bankrupt. this was a practical aid not only to revive two italian excellences but above all to meet the needs of the many families who lived off them.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because in europe the european globalisation adjustment fund was set up to provide additional support for workers who are suffering from the consequences of major changes in the structure of world trade. in italy, the ict sector had achieved fairly satisfactory results in the period from 2005 to 2008, achieving a good level of production and economic growth. since 2009, unfortunately, due to the economic crisis that hit italy and the strong competition from low-cost countries, there has been a decline in demand and investment in the ict sector. this sharp decline in the ict sector in italy has also affected the two companies covered by this proposal, anovo italia s.p.a. (province of varese) and jabil cm s.r.l. (province of milan). the package covered by the report comprises measures for the reintegration into the labour market of 480 workers from the above-mentioned enterprises, which together form a coordinated plan of personalised services and represent active labour market measures aimed at the reintegration of workers.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the riquet report which proposes the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund and the allocation of € 2 594 672 to de tomaso automobili workers.
in writing. - i am particularly convinced that i shall vote in favour of the report: the de tomaso case is an example of the situations for which the fund was set up. i know the situation firsthand because about half the staff involved in the projects financed were employees of the former pininfarina plants in grugliasco, near turin. this is a story that has had unflattering pages, which have added further bitterness to the workers who have lost their jobs; in particular, there was an opportunistic attempt, soon unmasked by the determination of the local authorities and the investigating authorities, to take advantage of the widespread concern arising from the crisis in the company and the need to come to the aid of the employees and suppliers of the inductance in order to divert public funds, conditional on the maintenance of production and the retraining of the employees. in this sense, the measure - which i am sure will be quickly adopted by the council - acquires the value of moral compensation for the workers, who will finally see their right to an opportunity recognized, and of recognition of the good work on the dossier, the result of the collaboration of the authorities concerned, from the italian government to the regional administration.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this proposal for a parliament decision, as it is intended to promote the reintegration into employment of some of the many workers who have lost their jobs in the italian motor vehicle industry. the automotive industry is a major force for growth and prosperity in europe, employing a large number of skilled workers and providing a vital impetus for knowledge and innovation. the size of the automobile industry is also of concern to the whole of europe and, consequently, the difficulties it is currently facing require an effective response at european level. the european globalisation adjustment fund is part of this response. however, the european union's action must increasingly be geared to fostering the development of a strong automotive industry, capable of innovating and competing globally. to this end, i will continue to give all possible political support, in all the relevant institutions and bodies, to the revival of the automobile sector as a whole and the thousands of small and mediumsized enterprises which operate in it.
in writing. the european commission has proposed to mobilise the european globalisation adjustment fund and allocate €2.6 million to italy to help the 1010 redundant workers at de tomaso automobili s.p.a. on their way back to the labour market. it should be noted that, despite the fact that the budget for egf operations for 2012 was exhausted, it was possible to raise the necessary resources and that agreement was reached in the council on the reintroduction of the crisis-related mobilisation criterion in the egf regulation also for the period 2014-2020. they are important signs of attention to a world of work in serious distress.
in writing. - i hope that this money, just over two and a half million euros, will really help the more than a thousand former de tomaso workers who have been affected by the crisis at the historic and prestigious company. many of them have rightly felt that they were being mocked, including by the latest social developments: unfortunately, we should never play games and speculate on the workers' lives, who are the main victims. much of the european automobile industry is in crisis, suffering from the continued growth of asian manufacturers in particular. it is sad to have to accept that glorious brands are in difficulty, even forced to close down, as they are unable to remain on the market. more and more often we find ourselves voting for these european globalisation adjustment fund loans: it is a clear symptom that there is something upstream in european industrial policy that is not working as it should and that needs to be addressed immediately. i hope, however, that for the workers in livorno who have been affected by the closure of de tomaso, this money will be useful in helping them to find new employment and overcome the enormous difficulties they have had to face in recent months.
in writing. − compared with its major competitors, automobile manufacturing in the eu fell well behind in terms of growth. the eu is losing its market share in the sector; the eu-27’s market share in world production decreased from 28.4 % in 2006 to 26.3 % in 2010. in italy, many workers in the automobile manufacturing sector are expected to be reintegrated into employment in other sectors, and it is necessary to provide related services such as training, re-training and vocational training, accompanying measures towards business creation, etc. the european globalisation adjustment fund has been created in order to provide additional assistance to workers suffering from the consequences of major structural changes in world trade patterns. thus i voted in favour of this proposal to mobilise the fund to ensure those who experienced the recent shock to the economy will receive necessary support.
in writing. − in italy, as in europe, the market share of the automotive sector has been considerably reduced, with the eu market share of world motor vehicle production falling from 28.4% in 2004 to 26.3% in 2010. as the commission has also stated in its assessments of previous cases of egf intervention in the automotive sector following the globalisation of trade, the decline in the union market share is part of a long-term trend. the same considerations are also contained in the final report cars 21, published on 6 june 2012, which confirms that the european market is losing ground to the world market for passenger cars. considering that the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) was established to provide additional support to workers made redundant as a result of major structural changes in world trade flows due to globalisation and to assist them in their reintegration into the labour market, the measures initiated for the 1010 de tomaso automobili workers together form a coordinated package of personalised services and represent active labour market measures aimed at reintegrating workers into the labour market. i therefore express my favourable opinion.
in writing. the gomes report calls on the commission to set up an action plan to establish a mechanism for identifying and sanctioning private and public sector officials involved in cases of corruption and human rights violations in third countries, especially those to which eu economic aid is directed. i agree with the aims of the report, but i find the text unclear and unbalanced, and i therefore abstain.
in writing. - the report is concerned with contemporary and ancient problems: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. on the whole, however, it deserves a favorable vote. the tfeu also recognises legality as a necessary condition for economic and human development and corruption is therefore closely linked negatively to the exercise of civil and human rights. in the age of global communication, each episode contributes to an amplifying effect of the bad reputation of the country concerned, reinforcing the spiral of investment and consequent opportunities away; it is undeniable that corruption in third countries fuels corruption in governmental bodies and finances, also through money laundering, illegal trafficking, including the odious trafficking in human beings. the problem is so deep-rooted that even the world bank says it is unable to assess the actual levels of corruption in some countries. we have a duty to involve the european institutions in the fight against this, starting with the recommendations made by the committee chaired by mr iacolino last week.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution by parliament on the subject of corruption. the damage caused by corruption in the various public and private sectors and the serious consequences it brings to the public and individual welfare are highlighted in great detail. i agree that the european union can play an important role, especially by promoting cross-sectoral rules to reduce corruption. i am firmly convinced that this can be combated by information and education which will have an impact on the social behaviour which is fuelling it, and at the same time promote transparency and publicity of operations and actions. i am particularly in favour of the proposal to decriminalise, within the member states, the rules on defamation and slander when they concern complaints about cases involving allegations of organised crime, corruption and money laundering in the member states and abroad. this would make it possible to combat the lack of awareness which too often accompanies these criminal phenomena and which are dangerous for our civilised societies.
in writing. the report calls on the commission to develop an action plan to identify cases of corruption and help local populations. the aim is to establish a mechanism to identify and sanction officials from third countries involved in human rights violations and, in cases of corruption, to provide tax relief to the poorest people who may be victims of this phenomenon. i am voting for abstention because this report, while containing the shared objective of stopping corruption, has other less shared points.
in writing. − this report highlights the close links between corruption and human rights violations, which are typical of contexts where there is abuse of power, lack of transparency and the institutionalization of various forms of discrimination. the situation is aggravated by the fact that the very institutions which should guarantee respect for democracy and human rights are often permeated by corruption. the european union should ensure better monitoring and greater transparency in the use of funds for aid to third countries. states should strengthen the powers of anti-corruption institutions and extend their jurisdiction over individuals of any nationality who have committed crimes of corruption or misappropriation of public funds within their territory.
in writing. - the scourge of corruption in the public and private sectors must be combated by all possible means and, as the european union, we have repeatedly taken initiatives in this direction. the report, for which i voted in favour, also highlights the particular effects of corruption on human rights in third countries. in the context of bilateral agreements concluded by the eu with third countries, account must therefore be taken of the impact on human rights of corruption, which is often widespread because it is difficult to control in countries with a strong economic and social expansion. the eu must therefore step up its efforts and pay ever greater attention to the protection of fundamental human rights when it concludes trade or other agreements with these states.
in writing. − the european parliament has always stressed that corruption in the public and private sectors undermines democracy, governance and the rule of law, with significant repercussions on the respect and protection of human rights in third countries. the fight against corruption requires the elimination of tax havens, tax evasion and illicit capital flight from developing countries by introducing rules requiring transnational companies to automatically report profits and taxes paid in all developing countries. we therefore believe that the european union should adopt a common approach to both the external and internal dimensions in order to limit the non-transparent use of eu development aid. we therefore call for greater accountability and traceability in the use of eu aid funds and for a framework to be established for bringing legal proceedings against eu and foreign companies suspected of corruption in third countries.
in writing. - corruption is a harmful element which undermines the european parliament's ability to promote reform and development in third countries. it is clearly hindering progress in the fight against discrimination, gender equality and equal opportunities policies. corruption can affect disadvantaged groups, such as women, by preventing them from political participation, access to public services, justice and education. the cost of corruption stands at around 5% of global gdp, impeding economic growth and therefore poverty reduction. accessible data and open and transparent forms of government give citizens control by giving them access to information about government budgets and expenditure. these and other factors have led me to vote in favour of the report by mrs ana gomes.
in writing. - i would like to quote some figures from the world bank, according to which corruption represents 5% of global gdp and over 1 000 billion dollars are paid in bribes every year. corruption also accounts for 10% of the total cost of doing business globally. these figures are staggering and give a good idea of the damage that this widespread and illegal behavior is doing to the entire global economy. the situation is particularly serious in the least developed countries: according to some estimates, between 20 and 40% of the total aid received by these states is lost through multi-level corruption mechanisms. this is unacceptable, and the european union, the world's largest donor, should be at the forefront of ensuring that aid actually reaches those who need it and is not used to finance corrupt politicians and officials. we cannot afford to throw tens of billions a year into aid that does nothing but enrich a few notable people: i therefore hope that there will be strict and rigorous controls on the allocation of these funds, to ensure that we who pay them are protected and that those who should actually benefit from them are protected.
in writing. − in both public and private sectors, corruption undermines efficient governance and the rule of law. it also misallocates resources, which hinders the reduction of poverty. a key observation is that 25 % of all investigations initiated by the european anti-fraud office (olaf) concern european external aid to third countries, and eur 17.5 million have been recovered as a result of these investigations. practically, in order better to combat corruption in the eu which impacts on third countries, it is necessary to build a global system to track aid pledges and hold donor countries to their promises of aid, and to hold them accountable for the projects, institutions or groups that they support. i therefore voted for this motion.
in writing. - i am in favour of the report on corruption in the public and private sectors because europe will have to put in place increasingly effective measures to reduce and eliminate such phenomena. corruption is a threat to the eu because it pollutes our economies and puts honest citizens in difficulty. corruption is not only an abuse of delegated power to obtain an unfair profit, thus hindering harmonious economic development, but also creates unfair and discriminatory situations with regard to the equal enjoyment of human rights, whether civil, political and economic or social and cultural, creating negative impacts on the environment and disproportionately affecting the most disadvantaged and marginalised groups in society, depriving them in particular of equal access to political life, public services, justice, security, land, employment, education, health and housing. i would also like to stress that corruption often fuels crime and contributes to it by creating situations of social conflict, inevitably undermining the protection of human rights. i therefore believe that the fight against corruption should be given increasing weight in the framework of eu initiatives.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this owninitiative report of parliament because i consider the european system for policy and strategic analysis (espas), which brings together officials from the european commission, the european parliament, the council of the european union and (on invitation) the european external action service, to be a very useful tool. it is important to support cooperation between officials in the various european bodies and institutions involved in the formulation of future policies. in the current context, it is more urgent than ever to identify and analyse the key trends and challenges, and the resulting policy choices, that europe and the world are likely to face in the coming decades. reflect and discuss today to better plan for the future.
in writing. − we are in a period of profound change and must therefore prepare ourselves to face new and particularly challenging challenges. the union budget for 2010 therefore financed a pilot project that could provide analyses of likely developments on the most important issues for transmission to policy makers. the pilot project has been successfully completed. today we voted to move to the next stage, the establishment of the european system for policy and strategic analysis (espas). funding and developing this system on the basis of the principles outlined in this report will enable us to improve our ability to identify key issues, to improve the quality and content of our public debate and ultimately to decide better and faster on key issues in the interests of citizens.
in writing. − the elaboration of long-term socioeconomic strategies and their implementation are the responsibility of both the european institutions and the public institutions of the member states; the commission has therefore decided to extend the scope of the new regulation to include the following areas: with this report we want to underline the importance of the multiannual financial framework and its role as a fundamental instrument for the long-term planning of the european project, taking into account the european perspective and the union's added value. we therefore call for better coordination between the eu budget and the national budgets of the member states, in order to strengthen complementarity, coordination and synergies without duplicating resources, thus making an effective contribution to the achievement of the eu 2020 targets. we therefore recommend closer coordination of such reporting initiatives and the creation of an interinstitutional system for identifying long-term trends on the major policy issues facing the union, involving staff from all relevant eu institutions and bodies and creating a necessary reporting mechanism and a programmatic discussion involving the interest groups, business associations and non-governmental organisations concerned.
in writing. − rapid transitions have been taking place in recent decades in the area of dynamics of power, demographic change, climate change, urbanisation, technology, etc., and we can expect to witness more such transitions in the coming years. policy-making in the eu will depend more and more on the timely identification of long-term trends, which requires the establishment of a permanent system at eu level to provide analyses of these trends. according to the report, the proposed new system will provide policy-makers with common analyses of the probable outcomes of major policy issues, which will help to anticipate possible trends. i therefore voted in favour of this proposal.
in writing. − as we are living through a period of very rapid change, there is a need for policy makers to invest more effort in studying and monitoring the main long-term trends. the new global environment will increasingly evolve towards a higher level of uncertainty, which is why the identification of global trends will be a key aspect of europe's ability to prepare for and respond to future challenges. forecasting is more than just trying to find out what's going to happen tomorrow, it's a way to focus attention on the things that matter today. a better understanding of global change should help to provide the union with information and analysis to make more informed choices on issues of critical importance, and a better understanding of how long-term trends are likely to develop will enable the union institutions to gain a greater collective awareness of emerging priorities in the future policy agenda. i am in favour of a permanent interinstitutional system for analysing long-term trends which will help to improve decision-making within the union.
in writing. the reform of the regulation on jurisdiction and the recognition and enforcement of judgments in civil and commercial matters was signed last december. in my view, a number of important improvements have been made, including the promotion of a procedure which will make it easier to enforce a judgment in another member state. however, some decisions of the court of justice of the european union in the area of private international law and employment law have raised concerns about the possibility that european union rules may have consequences for the rules that protect workers' rights in the member states. i agree with the rapporteur that some further improvements to the regulation are needed to ensure that national legislation is not compromised in the european internal market. the aim of the amendments to the regulation is mainly to ensure legal consistency and to prevent prejudice to national legal traditions in the field of labour law, ensuring, as far as possible, that jurisdiction and applicable law do not overlap. in this context, i believe it is important to ensure that a member state can exercise jurisdiction over disputes to which its labour law applies.
in writing. - i support the regner owninitiative report on the improvement of private international law on jurisdiction rules applicable to labour. this proposal will make it possible to close the current gaps in labour law legislation, increasing legal certainty while preserving national legal traditions.
in writing. − given that labour law remains a subject largely left to the legislation of the member states, european union rules, which identify the applicable jus and the competent court for labour matters characterised by elements referring to different legal systems, are an essential instrument of harmonisation and judicial cooperation on such a sensitive subject. as is well known, the process of european integration has led to a sharp acceleration in the mobility of workers and businesses within the union and, as a consequence, to a sharp increase in crossborder employment relationships. in this sense, this proposal improves the rules of the brussels i regulation by extending to trade union activity and individual contracts of employment the principle that jurisdiction and the law applicable in labour disputes should, where possible, belong to the same member state. i therefore welcome the adoption of this proposal to amend the brussels i rules on jurisdiction in labour matters and therefore vote in favour.
in writing. the report aims to improve private international law to protect employees. the aim is not to interfere with national legislation and to leave it to a member state to exercise jurisdiction over labour law. i am voting in favour of the report because the proposal guarantees respect for national legal traditions on the right to work.
in writing. − with today's plenary vote, parliament has taken a further step in defining the jurisdiction applicable to labour law matters. the recast of the brussels i regulation, signed on 12 december, left a major gap in this area. i would remind you that labour law remains a particularly sensitive area in which the union has only a marginal influence. it is for the member states to define national labour legislation which respects the balance between workers' rights and freedom of activity. however, the application of the principle of free movement of workers does not allow us to ignore further crossborder labour disputes, for which there are serious difficulties in identifying the competent court. the amendments proposed by the report concerning the forum for disputes in trade union matters and the clause on the right of withdrawal in the absence of a habitual place of work do not cover all the shortcomings of the brussels regulation. they do, however, ensure greater legal coherence without uprooting national legal traditions, and they ensure greater protection for workers and our citizens.
in writing. − following the recasting of the brussels i regulation on jurisdiction and the recognition and enforcement of judgments in civil and commercial matters, a loophole has opened up concerning certain aspects of the rules on jurisdiction applicable to labour law which were excluded from the new legislation. we must remember that labour law is an area in which the european union exercises only a relatively marginal influence, and it is therefore not for the european union to try to interfere with national legislation in this area. however, in the light of the free movement of workers and capital, it is necessary to lay down certain rules governing, in cross-border situations, which courts of the member state are entitled to rule on disputes, including in matters of labour law. we therefore welcome this report, because the aim of the amendments contained in it is to protect employees collectively and individually, who are generally the weakest party in the employment relationship, and to ensure legal consistency and to prevent the prejudice of national legal traditions in the field of labour law, ensuring, as far as possible, that jurisdiction and applicable law do not overlap.
in writing. - i shall vote in favour of the motion for a resolution tabled by parliament on the improvement of private international law: the rules of jurisdiction applicable to employment. the debate on the exercise of powers within the eu is an issue inherent in the very nature of the community system. the general principles on which the allocation of those powers is based must be accompanied by a consistent implementation of the rules governing the applicable law in the case in question in the field of employment law. european private international law must provide clear guidance on the choice of court, and for this reason i welcome the points made in this motion for a resolution in the context of the revision of the brussels i regulation. in view of the possibility of applying the reorganisation procedure, the commission must clarify that article 7 (2) refers to the place where the trade union activity in question was undertaken. finally, if the overlap clause is applied, the place of work must not coincide with the location of the enterprise, but with the place where the worker 'receives or has received daily instructions'. in this way, the question of jurisdiction can be settled more efficiently.
in writing. − on 12 december 2012, the recast of the brussels i regulation was signed. the merger procedure does not affect certain aspects of labour law. the committee on legal affairs and citizens' rights has decided to publish a report on labour law, in view of the forthcoming amendment to the brussels i regulation. although labour law is an area in which the european union exercises marginal influence, it must be borne in mind that on the basis of the free movement of workers and capital within the european union, the union has established rules governing, in cross-border situations, the jurisdiction of the member states also in matters of labour law. the report considers it important to ensure that, as far as possible, a member state can exercise jurisdiction over disputes to which its labour law applies. jurisdiction and the applicable law should belong to the same member state, where possible. i therefore support the amendments proposed by the rapporteur.
in writing. − i voted in favour of this draft legislative resolution of parliament as i believe that it provides a detailed and effective framework to ensure full compliance by member states with the obligations arising from title v of the maritime labour convention 2006. as is known, the convention has now been ratified by a sufficient number of countries to ensure its entry into force and the european union has complied with the rules set out in titles i, ii, iii and iv of the convention by means of directive 2009/13/ec. european legislation therefore needs to be brought into line with the provisions of the clm, which stipulate, in particular, the establishment of an effective system of inspection and certification of maritime working conditions by member states on ships flying their flag. such a system is an indispensable condition for the substantial guarantee of the rights and important forms of protection provided for by the clm. in this sense, parliament's draft legislative resolution constitutes an important step towards the full transposition into eu law of the international standards established by the clm, providing a comprehensive and harmonised framework for the application of the specific rules contained therein.
in writing. − the report provides for member states to empower third bodies to inspect and certify vessels through monitoring; in addition, it is empowered to detain vessels found to be in breach of directive 2009/13/ec. i am voting against this because there is a fear that maritime trade will be paralysed by excessive surveillance measures.
in writing. − this report addresses the issue of flag state control over the application of the requirements of the 2006 maritime labour convention (mlc), in particular as regards ensuring that ships comply with the requirements of the convention accepted by the flag state. the flag state's responsibility to ensure such compliance should be enshrined in union law by including as much as possible the provisions of the clm, in order to avoid divergent interpretations by member states and related instances of unfair competition. i therefore agree with the amendments to the original proposal by the empl commission which go exactly in this direction.
in writing. − incorporating the maritime labour convention (mlc) into eu laws is consistent with the single european transport area strategy towards a competitive and resource-efficient transport system declaring a social agenda for maritime transport. enforcing seafarers’ labour law rights as agreed in the mlc will strengthen the maritime transport dimension and protect europe’s interests at global level. this proposal attempts to create a strong guidance framework for member states in their duties as flag states. to avoid different interpretations by member states, which could lead to unfair competition and social dumping, the report stresses the need for specific requirements. i therefore voted in favour of this proposal.
in writing. − today we voted to apply council directive 2009/13/ec on the convention relating to the employment of seafarers. it is considered that aspects of the maritime labour convention (mlc) 2006 should be enshrined in community law in a more detailed and specific manner and that some aspects of the legislation should therefore be amended. these amendments will concern in particular the general principles governing the responsibility of each state for ships flying its flag, the authorizations of recognised organisations, the introduction of a certification system and complaint procedures on board. i believe that, ultimately, today's decision will improve the current legislation on maritime labour.
in writing. − the eu has recently adopted council directive 2009/13/ec, which is an outstanding achievement of the social dialogue in this area and this proposal aims to ensure that it is adequately equipped for its implementation in the union. to this end, it is envisaged that member states will be required to apply directive 2009/13/ec in the exercise of their powers as flag states. however, the european social partners, who wish to implement their agreement by a council decision on the basis of article 155 tfeu, do not have the power to include in the agreement the implementing provisions of title v of the clm and have invited the commission to do so. this initiative aims precisely at this objective as regards the responsibilities of the flag state, and is part of the wider context of union policies aimed at enhancing the positive aspects of the maritime professions in the eyes of european citizens through actions involving the commission, member states and the maritime sector itself from time to time. for these reasons, i am in favour of the proposal.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i believe that none of us is questioning the harmfulness of smoking, that is out of the question, and yet i believe that it is essential to strike a balance between legitimate health concerns and the sustainability of our european tobacco industry. for this reason, while i appreciate the rapporteur's work, i felt i had to disagree on a number of points, as regards the use of flavourings and additives, consumer warnings and slim cigarettes. a legislative measure must not stifle entire market chains and the supply chain linked to them, and it cannot in fact be the solution to the just battle against smoking. tobacco-producing regions need policies for converting production, otherwise they will be the ones to pay the very high economic, social and employment costs of this new discipline. mr president, i believe that we must not hit the workers without substantially reducing the number of regular smokers.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, europe's task should not be to criminalize smoking, but to inform people about the dangers of smoking: the freedom of choice of the consumer is a priority. when too many limits are imposed in a field like this, there is a risk that smuggling of cigarettes will be encouraged. the various prohibitions, including the prohibition on the use of additives, even natural ones, will have a single effect: smuggled products will be brought to the european market at lower prices than legal products, but with the same characteristics as traditional cigarettes. it is a pity that the tobacco used for smuggled cigarettes will come mainly from third countries, causing huge losses for the italian and european tobacco chain, which offers a guaranteed product, and additional risks to the health of smokers. just think that in europe more than 80% of smuggled cigarettes come from china and that in 2010 alone 64 billion illegal cigarettes were consumed in the european union.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i think that the process of this directive, which is still in progress, has given the epp a role, particularly to the italian delegation, which has succeeded in introducing significant improvements. i am referring to the fact that the electronic cigarette cannot be sold only through the pharmacy network, as if it were a medical device, but it is right that it be sold in the traditional cigarette sales network which is the controlled and guaranteed one - at least on italian territory, but not only - through the tobacco shops. i would also like to stress that i have heard the theme of education among young people repeatedly, as if our regulations were supposed to educate young people. i would remind this house that young people must be educated by their families, so perhaps it is better to give more power to families where young people can perhaps learn that smoking is harmful, if there is any reason for it, because it seems to me that from this point of view national information campaigns are there and can only be made more effective.
in writing. - smoking is still a major cause of death within the union. it is a voluntary cause, since individuals freely choose to smoke, and the practice is not prohibited in our countries. nevertheless, it is right and proper for the institutions to identify all appropriate measures to achieve the objective of reducing smoking, especially since, according to the data available, young people are the most vulnerable to this practice. health is undoubtedly a primary good to be protected, but other related aspects cannot be ignored in identifying the most appropriate measures to combat smoking, given that the tobacco market has a considerable impact on national and european gdps. personally, i find the whole comparison on labelling excessive because, in my humble opinion, we will not have a reduction in european smokers if we leave 5 or 10% more on the warning label. without considering that the trademark is a guarantee of consumer protection because it ensures the quality of the product against counterfeit goods. we will be able to reduce tobacco use drastically through appropriate information campaigns, education programmes in schools, and by trying to guide the consumer's choice which is and remains free.
in writing. the vote by our assembly represents a decisive step towards further reducing tobacco consumption in the european union. the figures provided by the world health organization are both encouraging (think of the european death rate from smoking, which fell from 40% in 2002 to 28% in 2012) and puzzling. we are witnessing a worrying trend in the number of young smokers, despite the general decline in smoking. and yet, in the european union, there are still as many as 700,000 deaths caused by smoking every year! the answer which parliament gave in its vote is therefore an attempt to discourage the use of nicotine, for example by extending the health warnings to 65% of the surface of the cigarette pack or by banning vanilla, chocolate and menthol flavoured cigarettes, although not immediately. alongside the appropriate measures mentioned above, there should be widespread information campaigns on the harmful effects of tobacco on the health of smokers - often leading to a real addiction - and of 'passive' smokers.
in writing. the document voted in plenary clearly indicates the way forward: the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat tobacco. parliament has today taken a rational position by refusing to pass commercial measures such as the diameter of cigarettes and the rounded corners of packets, as if they were proposals made in the name of protecting people's health. such measures are likely to favour the illegal market. to create ever more smoke-free environments, the right way is the italian way: the ban on smoking in public places and the education of the very young, from the first years of school. i hope that important decisions will be taken in this respect in the future.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mrs mcavan's directive on the manufacture, presentation and sale of tobacco and related products because it is part of an organised, effective and long-term anti-smoking strategy, with well-defined scope and objectives. i am particularly in favour of those provisions which make smoking less attractive to young people. it should not be forgotten that smoking remains one of the main causes of death, and that among young people (15-25) it is a higher percentage than in the whole european population. voting in this way will bring enormous benefits for the future in terms of reducing tobacco consumption, not to mention the fact that the directive contains elements designed to discourage young people from taking up smoking.
in writing. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the following areas: it's called personal freedom. the commission has already taken the necessary steps to ensure that the tobacco industry is not affected by the introduction of new products. we therefore support measures to regulate the sale of electronic cigarettes in order to give consumers an effective alternative, but we do not think that some of the drastic measures presented by the commission and the rapporteur are appropriate, as they will not reduce the problem. rather than continuing with laws that kill people, there are other issues to be addressed which make smoking even more dangerous, i am referring to european legislation which requires the 'automatic' switching off of cigarettes, leading smokers to continuous lighting, and therefore combustion, with the increased chance of contracting cancers.
in writing. the directive on the processing, presentation and sale of tobacco and related products is a particularly important and sensitive text in which the best compromise between consumer protection and the protection of the production chain has been sought. over-regulation of tobacco production and trade would have damaged market balances, increased the risk of counterfeiting and led to job losses in the long run. on the other hand, efforts have been made to protect the health of consumers, especially young people, by increasing the number of contraindications and prohibiting the use of additives which might make tobacco more appealing to a younger audience. finally, it is hoped that this directive will reduce tobacco consumption in europe by avoiding too much damage to businesses and workers.
in writing. − smoking has become an increasing concern in europe; it remains the leading cause of preventable death in the eu and kills around 700 000 people per year, whereas from 2005 to 2010 smoking prevalence among young males increased in 14 countries and among girls in 9 countries, according to a recent who survey. concerning the harmfulness of smoking, it is important for policy-makers to ensure young people are well informed of the health hazards caused by smoking and are discouraged from smoking, especially in relation to the recently-emerged market in e-cigarettes, herbal products for smoking, and cigarettes with flavours and alternative additives.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, having voted overwhelmingly in favour of this report, i would like to emphasize the role of parliament in international fisheries agreements, which means that in the last few months parliament has had to take a very strong stand against the commission in order to give life to this type of report, trying to make the fisheries agreement appear as a mere trade agreement and to make it appear as part of the investment that europe is making in these poor countries, on which there is an objective need to maintain the environmental impact of our activities. i think that a good agreement has been reached, this agreement provides that europe, in return for a payment, can enjoy fishing opportunities for certain european fleets and it is the most important agreement, the most onerous of the whole package of agreements. it is a good agreement, we were right to vote for it.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the recommendation because i believe that the fisheries protocol negotiated between the eu and mauritania should be rejected. the fisheries protocol does not bring benefits to the eu, since the conditions of exploitation of the fisheries are such that they are not profitable, and at the same time it does not bring benefits to mauritania either, since the absence of the eu fleet will deprive it of a large part of the financial compensation, without taking into account the economic losses for the local coastal population. the general opinion expressed by national administrations and the fishing industry is that this protocol is expensive in relation to the fishing opportunities and technical conditions imposed and therefore not profitable. in conclusion, given the inefficiency of the fishing possibilities and the abusive nature of the technical conditions, i believe that the objective should be to review the fishing conditions and, consequently, to negotiate a new protocol.
in writing. − the revised eu-mauritania fisheries protocol, which was negotiated by the eu-mauritania joint committee for the 2012-2014 fisheries agreement, has room for improvement, especially as regards the cephalopod fisheries. however, some satisfactory results have been obtained. given the importance of the protocol, which involves 102 vessels, 12 member states and 8 fish species, and the need for it to enter into force as soon as possible in the interests of the european and mauritanian beneficiaries, i believe that the compromise reached sufficiently guarantees the union's position and must be implemented.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the draft council decision on the conclusion of the protocol setting out the fishing opportunities and financial contribution provided for in the fisheries partnership agreement between the european union and the islamic republic of mauritania for a period of two years. the agreement follows the guidelines set by parliament and proposes a new partnership model in the fisheries sector. the text promotes the responsible exploitation of fisheries resources, contributing to environmental and social sustainability, protecting the seabed and the local fisheries sector and improving food security. the protocol is not only a good investment for taxpayers and the european fishing industry, but also a key element of the eu's cooperation programme. the agreement can play a stabilizing role for mauritania and the sahel region, improving security and the fight against terrorism and radicalisation in the region. for these reasons, i believe that the protocol is an important signal of the eu's concrete commitment to a sustainable fisheries policy consistent with development policies.
in writing. - mauritania, which does not have its own national fleet, has opted to let foreign fleets, including the eu, exploit its resources. in its relations with mauritania, the eu must help the country in its social and economic development, and will provide sectoral support to ensure that mauritania manages its fishing activities sustainably and is able to combat illegal fishing by applying the principles of good governance and respecting international law of the sea. it is important to clarify that sectoral aid under the fisheries agreement is not the only cooperation aid that mauritania receives from the eu. the general opinion is that the current protocol is expensive in relation to the fishing opportunities and technical conditions imposed and therefore not profitable. the eu is not benefiting from this, since the conditions for exploiting the fishing opportunities it has obtained are preventing it from being profitable, nor is mauritania, since the absence of the eu fleet will deprive it of a large part of the financial compensation, without taking into account the wealth generated for the local coastal population by the activities of the vessels and the salaries of the seamen, for these reasons i am in favour of rejecting the current fisheries protocol.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i am pleased with the votes we have taken as the epp and, above all, with the role played by the italian delegation, because i think that it has done itself a favour and has particularly responded to the needs of our citizens, those who are represented in this parliament and who, from our point of view, are not only italians but also citizens of the whole of europe.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, it is estimated that in 1990 more than 100 million women were demographically missing from the world population as a result of genocide, and according to recent estimates this number may have risen to almost 200 million. genericide is usually committed whenever a pregnant woman, either of her own free will or under pressure, decides not to give birth to a female fetus because females are considered a burden to society. it must be emphasized that genocide remains a crime and a serious violation of human rights, which requires effective means to combat and eliminate all the root causes of this crime. i therefore join the call on governments to specifically criminalise femicide or genicide and therefore to develop and implement legislative measures to ensure that cases of femicide are investigated, perpetrators are brought to justice and women survivors are guaranteed easy access to health and long-term support services.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, genocide is an atrocity, an unacceptable violation of human rights and an extreme form of discrimination and violence against women. we are talking about millions of women around the world who have never seen the light of day because of the practice of infanticide and selective abortion and the women who have disappeared from the world population, their only fault being that they were conceived or born of the wrong sex, considered a burden to the family and to society. it is an intolerable extermination whose consequences generate more abuses, more injustices, forced marriages, human trafficking, sexual exploitation, precisely because of the strong gender imbalance that is caused. education, awareness and empowerment are needed to trigger a reversal of the trend, but we also need a strong political commitment against this cruel form of discrimination.
in writing. - gendercide is first and foremost combated by a strong cultural change and the case of south korea, which is moving towards normality, although it had a distorted numerical ratio between the sexes, is proof of this. there is no doubt that the stereotype of preference for the male child must be combated and this must certainly be helped by a policy and culture which encourages equality between the sexes. but not only is genicide a problem for the women who suffer it, but also for the lives that are not respected in them because of practices of pre-birth gender selection and forced abortions. the european union should, in my view, have a clear and strong position on this, in line with what the declaration of the rights of the child says, that 'every child has the right to adequate legal protection before and after birth, to survival and development and that girls enjoy equal status'. in addition to a policy in defence of life, europe should also spread the culture of conscientious objection as a means of refusing to give rise to abominable practices that disrespect life.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mrs papadopoulou's report because it represents a concrete commitment to combating social exclusion and discrimination and to promoting justice and gender equality. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environment from harmful substances. the commission is therefore proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environment from harmful substances. governments must address democratic shortcomings by legislating to defeat discrimination against girls and achieve the active participation of women in all sectors. we must aim at achieving economic, social and educational empowerment for women.
in writing. i am voting in favour of the motion for a resolution by the european parliament on genocide: the missing women. gender-based violence is a serious problem that significantly alters the gender balance and has a strong social and economic impact. this phenomenon arises from an ingrained preference for the male child in some societies, which leads to significant gender inequalities and does not allow full equality of women in access to education, health and employment. the resolution presents an integrated approach to combating genicide, calling for it, as well as sex selection, to be specifically qualified as crimes and reaffirming the importance of women's empowerment. in addition to raising awareness of women's rights, it is essential to address the socioeconomic causes underlying the phenomenon and ensure equality between women and men before the law. i welcome the call for the eu, in line with the european council on development, to introduce a strong gender component in partnerships with developing countries and humanitarian aid packages, identifying the issue of gendercide as a priority. for these reasons, i believe that the resolution represents an important step in the fight against the serious crime of genocide.
in writing. − equality between men and women and non-discrimination of gender is an essential part of human rights, enshrined in the treaty of european union. however, systematic, deliberate and gender-based mass killing of people belonging to a particular sex exists in many regions of the world. it is a global issue that pregnant women are under pressure not to give birth to female foetuses and sex ratios are considerably distorted, which significantly impacts the economy and social stability. the incentive of preferring to give birth to sons is not merely cultural, but also economic, as ageing parents are better supported, because inheritance goes to sons in their tradition, which is particularly important in developing countries, where no reliable social security system is in place. therefore, i voted in favour of this proposal to call on governments to promote gender equality, especially through combating the root causes of gendercide.
in writing. − the eu, through its treaty, promotes values common to all member states such as pluralism, non-discrimination, tolerance, justice, solidarity and equality between men and women, and enshrines the principle of gender mainstreaming by stating that the union's actions aim to eliminate inequalities and promote equality between men and women. i therefore support the eu's inclusion of genocide as a priority in its political dialogue with the third countries concerned and its inclusion as a key item in the post-2015 development policy agenda. in this fight against genocide, it is significant and encouraging that south korea is moving towards normality, achieved through a clear cultural change.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the financial cycle 2007-2013 is coming to an end and the balance we can draw from it, at least in the italian case, is not entirely positive. despite the serious economic and social crisis in europe, i must point out that hundreds of millions of euros have not been spent, not because of incompetence on the part of some people, but because of a budgetary pact that was too strict. most italian local authorities were faced with a surreal situation, as the lack of funds for local authorities was countered by a scenario in which vast resources were available but not usable, suspended for reasons that were completely incomprehensible. it is a matter of conviction that the budgetary pact has in this case proved inadequate to meet the challenges of the crisis. only a growth pact that allows for major investment at union level will be a suitable solution. today, it is agreed that without investment, fiscal austerity and budget cuts cannot revitalize the economy.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, without greater flexibility in the implementation of the stability pact, the conditions for economic recovery will be lacking: in recent years there has been a steady decline in investment with negative repercussions on education and sustainable employment. we cannot give economic growth a new impetus by fiscal austerity and budget cuts, and that is why i am opposed to macroeconomic conditionality, which would have a negative effect on regions and social groups already weakened by the crisis. europe needs growth, it needs development, it needs to strengthen the administrative capacity of local authorities, it needs to reduce bureaucracy, it needs to streamline, it needs to speed up, in order to facilitate access to the structural funds and to enable the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy to be achieved.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, investment in local authorities is being constrained by budgetary constraints and current expenditure and is a necessity if we are to reverse the negative trend caused by the economic crisis and prevent the burden of public debt from increasing for future generations. the correct and efficient use of the structural funds can therefore be a useful instrument for redistributing investment at regional and local level. unfortunately, this is not the case because the institutions often have difficulty in obtaining the necessary self-financing to cover the various projects that can be built. the european parliament has thus set out a clear path towards the elimination of the structural deficit in public expenditure on programmes cofinanced by the european structural and investment funds. i therefore voted in favour of mrs mazzoni's motion and i join in the congratulations which have been paid to her.

in writing. − the pna is a sub-regional agreement between the federated states of micronesia, kiribati, the marshall islands, nauru, palau, papua new guinea, the solomon islands and tuvalu. its main objective is the management of tuna resources in the eezs of those islands. distant water fleets are expected to contribute to reducing fishing pressure on tropical tuna stocks, including endangered species that are currently overfished. there is currently a multilateral agreement between the countries of the area and the usa; however, the existing system suffers from a lack of transparency and poor results in terms of meeting objectives, with reductions always being significantly exceeded. i therefore voted in favour of this proposal to establish a feasible framework to promote sustainable tuna fishing in the western and central pacific.
in writing. - the european parliament, in plenary session this morning, voted on a report by mr estévez on the union's overall strategy for fisheries in the pacific. consistent, coordinated and long-term modalities of action should inspire the eu in the development of an action plan on trade, development and fisheries policies with the countries of the western central pacific, which are members of the acp (asia, caribbean, pacific) group of countries with which important trade partnership agreements are already in force (cotonou 2010). on fisheries issues, it is crucial to strengthen the union's presence in the region in order to promote sustainable fisheries through transparent management, which will bring long-term benefits both to the union and to the pacific states, which already receive significant community aid. as a full member of the committee on fisheries, i can only express my support for a resolution which, in my view, increases the visibility of the eu in the region by promoting its socioeconomic development.
in writing. − i am in favour of this report because its objective is to recommend the establishment of a long-term fisheries strategy for the western central pacific that takes into account the need to coordinate european policies in order to strengthen potential synergies, to achieve a multiplier effect, maximising the benefits for both pacific states and the european union, and to increase the visibility of the eu in the region, so as to achieve consistency of union policies with the development objectives as provided for in article 208 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, thus contributing to greater stability and prosperity in europe, promoting cooperation at regional and subregional level and ensuring that the eu fisheries policy is compatible with the regional treaties and agreements in force, including the nauru agreement and the related implementing protocols.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, this report is an important report because it concerns the mediterranean and the interaction between eight european countries and 14 non-european countries. we have missed an important opportunity, but unfortunately an amendment has been passed which has slightly distorted the value of the report in its complexity. the amendment was of extraordinary importance because it encouraged europe to build bilateral relations and to build real agreements to ensure that the same fishing rules apply in the mediterranean as in europe. in fact, today we are witnessing a very strict relationship between europe and its seas, with rules and a complete absence of rules in the other mediterranean countries. this is a missed opportunity! the report does, however, have some positive features, which is why i voted for it.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by mr nikolaos salavrakos because i believe that better regulation of fisheries and territorial waters can help to avoid the emergence of any regional tensions and conflicts in the maritime areas of the mediterranean and the black sea. i believe that the introduction of economic zones and protection zones will effectively preserve the integrity of both basins, which are too often overexploited and congested by human activities such as fishing and maritime traffic.
in writing. − given that the mediterranean and black seas have specific characteristics from an oceanographic, fisheries, environmental and socio-economic point of view, and that increased competition for marine resources and more limited fish stocks leads to the emergence of regional tensions and possible disputes between coastal states concerning maritime areas, i believe that greater cooperation and political cohesion are needed between the coastal states concerned and i stress the important role of bilateral cooperation and international agreements, as the majority of the countries in the black sea and mediterranean region are not eu member states and are therefore not subject to union legislation. integrated maritime policy, and maritime spatial planning in particular, plays a central role in preventing conflicts between eu member states and with third countries. however, i believe that the eu cannot afford to provide financial and technical support to the third country to apply eu-level standards of sustainable management, given the limited funds allocated to the fisheries sector.
in writing. i voted in favour of mr harbour's report to harmonize the legislation in force on pleasure craft and watercraft designed for use at sea and in inland waters, with the exception of craft designed and used for the commercial transport of passengers. the amendments include reductions in noise and exhaust emissions, the introduction of more flexible conformity assessment procedures and alignment with horizontal standards on accreditation and ce marking.
in writing. − all the recent maritime disputes are mainly due to the exploitation of limited marine resources, mainly due to the over-exploitation and unsustainable use of some of them in the mediterranean and black seas. with this report, which has been adopted today, we wish to stress that the settlement of disputes relating to the delimitation of maritime boundaries and the establishment of fisheries protection zones must be carried out in full compliance with international law, on the basis of the principles of fair cooperation, transparency, equality and equity, ensuring the sustainability of marine resources and the protection of ecosystems, in particular by respecting the united nations convention on the law of the sea, and in particular article 62. the european union, for its part, considers it appropriate to continue to support developing countries in the coastal areas so that they can implement sustainable fisheries management plans in their territorial waters and effectively combat illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing. we therefore call for the adoption of a long-term strategic framework for scientific cooperation in the mediterranean and black sea basins, fostering cooperation in the field of marine research, including the exchange of scientific information and data.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mr salavrakos' report because the issues it highlights are of vital importance at this historic moment. the mediterranean sea is currently a significant resource on the world scene, accounting for 30% of the world's maritime traffic. the maritime management of this area is a requirement to be protected in accordance with the united nations convention on the law of the sea (unclos). an integrated maritime policy and appropriate maritime spatial planning are needed to prevent conflicts. sustainable fishing and increased control of iuu (illegal, unreported and unregulated) fishing must be promoted. a regional approach to the protection of fish species, sustainable fishing in the mediterranean and the black sea, is useful in respecting the waters, since these seas have limited rates of renewal and are therefore subject to heavy pollution.
in writing. − fishing remains an important sector in the mediterranean regions, creating significant wealth and jobs. the number of people concentrated in coastal areas is predicted to increase in the coming decade, which will cause the demand for fishing and water resources to increase as well. as a result, there will be greater competition for smaller stocks and marine resources, leading to the creation of regional tensions and possible disputes between coastal states about maritime areas. i therefore voted in favour of this proposal to call for increased efforts at regional, national and eu level towards enhancing the regulation of access to resources in order to ensure effective governance and international cooperation.
in writing. - i am in favour of this, because the union must make efforts to improve access to resources so that overfishing in the mediterranean and the black sea can be phased out, since the depletion of fish stocks will increase the risk of conflict in the area. this will only be possible if maritime management in the mediterranean and black sea is carried out with cooperation and political cohesion between the coastal states concerned, stressing the important role of bilateral cooperation and international agreements, as most countries in the black sea and mediterranean region are not eu member states and are therefore not subject to union legislation, which is why i call on the eu, in order to improve cooperation with neighbouring countries and the management of shared stocks, to aim at the conclusion of cooperation agreements for sustainable fisheries with these countries; calls for the cooperation agreements to be aimed not at acquiring fishing rights for eu vessels, but at creating a situation where the eu provides financial and technical support in order to have the third partner country apply standards comparable to those of the eu in terms of sustainable management;

first, a call for a change in cultural attitudes, to promote greater equality between women and men, because violence against women is rooted above all in the gender gap in society and is perpetuated by a culture that in fact tolerates, or at least justifies, gender-based violence. the convention also identifies a number of types of crime such as female genital mutilation, forced marriage, acts of persecution and thus stalking, forced abortion, forced sterilization and domestic violence. the convention will only enter into force when it has been ratified by at least 10 countries, 8 of which must be council of europe member states. what is the present status of signatures and ratifications? we have 26 signatures not followed by ratification, only 5 ratification: 2 member states of the european union italy and portugal together with albania, montenegro and turkey. some member states are completing the ratification process. our question is: what measures can be taken to speed up the process of signature and ratification of the convention by the member states and by the european union as a whole? in writing. - i voted in favour of the interinstitutional agreement between the european parliament and the ecb on cooperation on procedures relating to the single supervisory mechanism (ssm), because i believe that cooperation/surveillance between the european parliament and the ecb is of crucial importance for european monetary policy. the banking union for all euro area countries, based on the pillars of a single supervisory authority, a european resolution fund and a european deposit guarantee scheme, puts enormous decision-making power in the hands of the ecb over the entire eu monetary economy. i therefore believe that any major change in the supervisory role, including the transfer of powers to other institutions, must be accompanied by increased transparency and accountability to parliament, which must have full powers of inquiry and decision-making over the appointment and budgetary procedures. the creation of an interinstitutional agreement (iia) between parliament and the ecb will create parliamentary scrutiny of the ecb's supervisory tasks, through regular exchanges of views with the relevant parliamentary committee, and through closed-door oral discussions with the bureau of the committee. finally, the draft iia provides for parliamentary scrutiny of the procedure for selecting the chairman of the supervisory board.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the eia directive establishes the simple but fundamental principle of informed decision-making. before authorising the execution of a public or private project likely to have an impact on the environment, the competent authorities of the member states are legally obliged to obtain the information necessary to carry out an environmental impact assessment. i agree with the general approach of the report and welcome the introduction of the new measures on conflict of interest and corrective action. however, as regards public involvement, i have serious doubts that the guarantees available to citizens are being respected. i think it would have been more useful to introduce time limits on the notification of the intention to start certain projects requiring eia assessment, as well as the definition of a body responsible for verifying compliance with this directive directly on national territory.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the new environmental impact assessment directive requires that all projects likely to have an impact on the environment must be transparent and that the information needed to ensure maximum involvement of citizens in the decision-making process must be made available to everyone. among the priorities: soil protection, monitoring of cumulation with other projects or activities, mandatory eia for all projects with a significant impact on the environment, post-eia monitoring, but above all, certain timelines and clear procedures for public consultation and the population concerned. i understand the concerns expressed by many about possible negative repercussions and bureaucratic burdens, but it is still important to involve citizens as much as possible in the right to health and in environmental and landscape rights.
in writing. − directive 2011/92/eu concerns the assessment of the environmental impact of certain public/private projects and is a cornerstone of the european union's environmental policy. this directive has, over the years of its application, achieved some success in harmonising the principles of environmental assessment at european level, however, some weaknesses have been identified which have given rise to a significant number of legal disputes both at national level and before the court of justice of the eu. while i welcome the proposal in its broad outline, i do not think it is justified to involve the public in the preliminary stage of the environmental impact assessment procedure for projects covered by the directive. in my view, involving the public - as suggested by the rapporteur - creates a disproportionate burden on the contractor and slows down the decision-making process by the competent authorities. i also believe that the list of information required in the 'environmental report' has been arbitrarily extended: some forecasts, such as the requirement for the developer to present alternatives with a lower impact than the project, or the assessment of cumulative effects with other projects, are not relevant for the purpose of the impact assessment of the project and may result in an increase in the administrative burden for the developer of the project itself.
in writing. − i share the need to reformulate the framework for the environmental impact assessment procedure to adapt it to the new needs and political priorities of the union, but above all to give greater legal certainty to operators, given the numerous litigations that have been initiated before the court of justice. the amendments must, however, be designed to simplify the system further and certainly not to make the procedure more difficult. i believe that environmental impact assessment should be of fundamental importance in the decision-making process on public projects which may reduce green space, and that this priority should be given in a feasible, practical and not excessively costly way. that is why i do not share the rapporteur's approach on certain points.
in writing. - in the morning, the european parliament, in plenary, voted on a report by mr zanoni on the proposal for a european parliament and council directive amending directive 2011/92/eu on the assessment of the environmental impact of certain public and private projects. as a cornerstone of the union's environmental policy, the directive has played a crucial role in ensuring the environmental sustainability of the many projects within its scope over a period of some 30 years, by strongly affirming the principle of 'informed decision': the implementation of a public or private project likely to have an effect on the environment must be preceded by a careful analysis by the competent authorities to carry out an environmental impact assessment. i am very pleased with a resolution which improves the environmental audits to be carried out ex ante and ex post and strengthens the directive with due regard to the new challenges of biodiversity, resource efficiency and climate change.
in writing. − i have given a favourable opinion on the european parliament and council directive amending directive 2011/92/eu on the assessment of the environmental impact of certain public and private projects (eia directive). this legislation plays a crucial role in the union's environmental policy, as weaknesses have been identified and have given rise to a significant number of legal disputes both at national level and before the court of justice of the eu. the eia directive establishes the simple but fundamental principle of 'informed decision', i.e. before authorising the implementation of a public or private project likely to have an impact on the environment, the competent authorities of the member states have a legal obligation to obtain the information necessary to carry out an environmental impact assessment. it is essential to ensure that the environmental report is verified by fully independent experts with appropriate technical expertise in environmental matters. achieving a true 'green economy' also means ensuring the sustainability of projects on our territory, and designing and implementing them in relation to their impact on resource efficiency, climate change and biodiversity loss, particularly with regard to major infrastructure projects.

in writing. − under the directive approved by parliament, holders of professional qualifications - including doctors, pharmacists and architects - will be issued with a european electronic card to facilitate the exercise of the profession in any eu member state. the new rules will allow professionals wishing to speed up the recognition of their qualifications by another member state to opt for the european professional qualifications card which will be provided by the home member states, mainly for short periods of work abroad, and by the host member state in the event of a transfer of practice. this should speed up the time and process of recognition, as the holder of a vocational qualification could ask his home country to complete the preparatory stages instead of having to apply in the host country, as is currently the case. if a host member state fails to take a decision within the time limit set by the directive, the european professional card shall be deemed to have been issued and shall be sent automatically to the holder of a professional qualification. the directive aims to prevent health workers who have been convicted of a criminal offence or who have been subject to serious disciplinary action from being able to practise their profession in another member state.
