member of the commission. −commission’s position on amendments by parliamentreport carl schlyter schylter (a7-0132/2013) declaration by the commission on the procedure of adoption of implementing acts the commission underlines that it is contrary to the letter and to the spirit of regulation (eu) n. 182/2011 (oj l 55 of 28.2.2011, p. 13) to invoke article 5§4, subparagraph 2, point b) in a systematic manner. recource to this provision must respond to a specific need to depart from the rule of principle which is that the commission may adopt a draft implementing act when no opinion is delivered. given that it is an exception to the general rule established in article 5§4 recource to subparagraph 2, point b), cannot be simply seen as a ‘discretionary power’ of the legislator but must be interpreted in a restrictive manner and thus must be justified.
madam president, the vote is free and no one should be conditioned, because it is precisely on these sensitive subjects that each member must be free to vote in his own conscience.
madam president, i think that, on a request repeated by the house and widely shared, the presidency can reconsider its position and refer the matter back to committee. the decisions of the presidency are not dogmas of faith, and if there is a proposal which is supported by the majority of this house, i would ask you to take it into account.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this proposal for a regulation. i am in principle in favour of free trade, but in this case i am all the more in favour because i do not think that the two immediate effects are going to have an impact on italian production: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. i think that is a good compromise, although we must ensure that kosovar producers comply with the technical standards required in our market and that the share of these wines is not disproportionate to the rest of the world.
in writing. the report deals with the subject of wine imports: the commission proposes to amend the general tariff quota for all the balkan countries by allocating a specific quota of 20 000 hectolitres to kosovo and reducing the remaining quota for all the other countries to 30 000 hectolitres. i am voting against the text because the production costs and the different rules in terms of controls would lead to the entry of products which could unfairly compete with the wine of the member states.
in writing. − at present, the quantity of wine from albania, bosnia and herzegovina, croatia, kosovo, the former yugoslav republic of macedonia, montenegro and serbia that can be imported duty-free or at a lower rate of duty is subject to a series of quotas, i.e. a global tariff quota provided for by a council regulation, and a specific individual tariff quota granted by a series of stabilisation and association agreements concluded with the eu by all the states listed above, with the exception of kosovo. consequently, kosovo does not benefit from an individual tariff quota. the regulation voted today aims to correct this disadvantage by allocating a specific tariff quota to kosovo, which will be deducted, in a reasonable manner, from the overall quota provided for in the council regulation. this will keep intact the overall share of wine that this group of countries can export to the eu, enjoying preferential tariff treatment.
in writing. - we welcomed today in plenary the proposal for a regulation by mr winkler, which seeks to correct annex i to council regulation (ec) no 1215/2009 concerning the export of wine to kosovo. the latter, unlike other western balkan countries, having not concluded stabilisation and association agreements with the eu, can only benefit from the general tariff quota established by regulation (ec) no 1215/2009. however, once this global tariff quota is exhausted by the other countries, kosovo exporters lose preferential access to the eu market. we believe that it is essential to create a level playing field within the european union and since kosovar wine exporters are currently in a supposedly disadvantageous position compared to other western balkan exporters, we support this proposal to amend the regulation. it is also worth pointing out that such a change would merely change the allocations.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by mr iuliu winkler on the tariff quotas for wines because i believe in the commercial potential this could offer to the balkan regions not yet part of the union. the issue of the european union's stabilisation and association procedures refers to council regulation (ec) no 1215/2009 of 30 november 2009 establishing exceptional measures for countries involved in such procedures. the exceptional and unlimited duty-free access to the eu market for almost all products originating in albania, bosnia and herzegovina, croatia, kosovo, the former yugoslav republic of macedonia, montenegro and serbia allows for gradual but significant economic integration, with a view to future accession to the union of these countries.
in writing. − by council regulation (ec) no 1215/2009 of 30 november 2009, the european union granted exceptional and unlimited duty-free access to the eu market for almost all products originating in the countries benefiting from the stabilisation and association process, except for wine and baby beef, which remain subject to tariff quotas. the aim of these measures is to give a new impetus to the economies of the western balkan countries through privileged access to the eu market. it is believed that economic development will in turn promote political stability in the whole region. those trade preferences were granted for a period expiring on 31 december 2015 and currently apply to bosnia and herzegovina, serbia, albania, the republic of croatia, the former yugoslav republic of macedonia, montenegro and kosovo. kosovo has not concluded specific stabilisation and association agreements and can therefore only benefit from the general tariff quota. once this tariff quota has been exhausted by other countries, kosovo exporters have no preferential access to the eu market. i therefore consider the proposal to allocate an extra specific tariff quota of 20 000 hectolitres to that country to be legitimate if it can help stabilize the democratic conditions in that country.
in writing. − regulation (ec) no 1215/2009 governs tariff quotas and trade measures applicable to third countries linked to the eu by trade partnership agreements, customs clearance, access to the union market. the regulation covers a number of products which therefore enjoy special trade freedoms in terms of marketable quantities and exemptions from customs duties. the amendment therefore concerns the inclusion of wine in the list of these products by establishing a tariff quota favourable to the european wine sector.
in writing. − because the eu has no stabilisation and association agreement or interim agreement with kosovo, kosovo can benefit solely from the global tariff quota established in the current regulation on global tariff quotas for wine. but kosovan exporters then lose preferential access to the eu market when this global tariff quota is exhausted by other countries. as kosovo has demonstrated its potential to export wine to the eu, it makes sense to fix this asymmetry by allocating a specific tariff quota for wine specifically to kosovo. in order to promote level competition regarding imports of wine into the eu from all western balkan countries, i voted in favour of this proposal.
in writing. - the report by mr winkler on the tariff quotas for wine was voted on today in plenary. council regulation (ec) no 1215/2009 provides that imports of wine from all the western balkan countries are subject to a global tariff quota of 50 000 hl which sets the quantity of wine that can be imported duty-free or at lower duties and is only accessible subject to the exhaustion of the quotas provided for in the respective trade stabilisation agreements between the balkan countries and the eu. kosovo has not concluded any stabilisation agreement with the eu and can therefore benefit in respect of wine only from the general tariff quota established by the regulation. when this quota is exhausted by the other countries, kosovo exporters lose preferential access to the eu market. it is therefore appropriate, as proposed by the rapporteur, to adopt a proposal for a regulation correcting this asymmetry by amending annex i to regulation (ec) no 1215/2009 and allocating to kosovo a specific tariff quota of 20 000 hl, which will be deducted from the overall quota of 50 000 hl. this approach will create a level playing field for wine imports into the eu from all the western balkan countries by simply changing the allocation of the tariff quota.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation which is based on a reasonable approach to create a level playing field for wine imports into the eu from all the western balkan countries. i would point out that the allocation of a specific tariff quota for wine originating in kosovo does not entail any overall increase in the overall tariff quota for wine which can be imported from the western balkans, but merely changes the allocation of the quota, correcting the alleged unfavourable position of kosovar wine exporters. furthermore, it appears that the level of the wine quota allocated to kosovo is defined on the basis of previous trade in that product and, as this is the method normally used to determine the levels of the quotas, the wine quota allocated to kosovo does not appear to be disproportionate to the individual tariff quotas granted to the other western balkan countries for the same product under the association and stabilisation agreements or the interim agreements.
in writing. − council regulation (ec) no 1215/2009 of 30 november 2009 establishing a system of exceptional trade measures applicable to countries and territories participating in or linked to the european union's stabilisation and association process. in practice, it grants exceptional and unlimited duty-free access to the eu market for almost all products originating in albania, bosnia and herzegovina, croatia, kosovo, the former yugoslav republic of macedonia, montenegro and serbia. such asymmetrical liberalisation would normally constitute a breach of the wto provisions on non-discrimination; however, these trade preferences for the western balkan countries are explicitly authorised by wto derogation until 31 december 2015. with the exception of kosovo, all the above countries have concluded stabilisation and association agreements or interim agreements on trade and related matters with the eu. the winkler report concerns tariff measures for wines from kosovo, with which there is still no stabilisation and association agreement. the measure that will be applied is in line with the same type of products from serbia and i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. − today's vote marks an important step forward in the supporting work that the european union is carrying out with its neighbourhood policy. the financial assistance will enable the kyrgyz republic - which was badly hit by an outbreak of interethnic violence in 2010 - to continue the stabilisation process and constitutional reforms that will enable the country to continue on the path towards democratic and economic stability. as chairman of the parliamentary delegation for relations between the european parliament and central asia - and therefore also with kyrgyzstan - i have been following the development of this process closely. after almost two years of work, i therefore welcomed the result of the commitment shown by the institutions in reaching an agreement with a rapid second reading procedure. this outcome will allow, after a long period of bureaucratic deadlock, the release of financial support and will ensure that kyrgyzstan receives the support it needs to continue its commitment to development, stability, shared democratic values and economic growth. i am convinced that the restoration of the country's financial and social sustainability will also have a positive impact on the role kyrgyzstan plays in regional strategic stability.
in writing. - development cooperation is a budgetary chapter that is often tempted to be cut, especially in times of crisis. but it would be like a farmer saving on seeds because the harvest was not good: the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect. in this case, where the eu is providing assistance to kyrgyzstan, half in loans and half in grants, to improve its balance of payments, we have the opportunity to influence the development of a central asian country, in the hope that our investment will be fruitful and that the purchasing power that will be generated will also be directed towards our products.
in writing. − following a series of interinstitutional negotiations that began in june 2012, today's vote provides macro-financial assistance to the kyrgyz republic. the european union has therefore committed itself to providing 30 million euro, half in the form of grants and half in the form of loans, to help restore balance of payments stability in the country.
in writing. − in 2009, the kyrgyz republic was hit by the global crisis. soon after, economic problems were exacerbated by a popular uprising that in april 2010 brought an end to the regime of president bakiyev, accused of corruption and lack of democracy. in the resulting power vacuum, inter-ethnic violence erupted in the south of the country in june 2010, with a heavy toll of 470 victims and nearly 300,000 displaced. despite these tragic events, the new interim government won a vote in favour of democratic reforms in a constitutional referendum held on 27 june 2010. in june 2011, the imf entered into a follow-on agreement with the authorities of the kyrgyz republic (in the form of an extended credit facility) for usd 106 million to support a comprehensive economic adjustment and reform programme to be implemented in the period from mid-2011 to mid-2014. in the face of democratic efforts, it is reasonable and necessary for the community to open up further credit to this state by supporting this resolution.
in writing. - after difficult negotiations, during which the council and parliament had long been at odds over the procedure for the new comitology, parliament voted today to grant macrofinancial assistance of eur 30 million to the kyrgyz republic to rebalance the country's balance of payments.

in writing. − health is one of the most valuable assets for each individual and for the community as a whole, and is a determining factor for economic growth and development. in this context, the introduction of a regulatory framework to improve the safety of in vitro medical devices and the transparency of their use and marketing is an important step forward in raising the level of public health within the union. consumers and healthcare professionals will therefore benefit from this european regulation. that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report because i believe that the health of all citizens of the european union must be protected through better regulation of ivd medical devices. the above-mentioned devices, which are intended for diagnostic use in the field of hiv, dna or hepatitis c, need more control to ensure that low-quality tests are not placed on the european market. the report by mr liese therefore aims to regulate the safety, quality and efficiency parameters of medical devices, thus making a step towards a clearer and more reliable legislative proposal.
in writing. − in vitro diagnostic medical devices (ivds) include a wide range of tests, including self-testing tests such as hiv tests, dna tests and blood glucose tests. we agree with mr liese's proposal to improve the regulation of these medical devices, since they are the progenitors of all therapies. unfortunately, the current directive does not guarantee that even low-quality ivd devices cannot be placed on the market, and this represents a potential damage to the health protection of all european citizens. the proposal aims to ensure maximum safety on the european market by improving the supervision and surveillance by notified bodies and by introducing a network of reference laboratories specialised in this field. finally, we agree that the european union should not restrict access to dna testing for patients but should offer appropriate genetic counselling to inform about the consequences before the test is carried out, and should accept the possibility of taking other measures in addition to those required by the regulation.
in writing. − the current regulatory framework for in vitro diagnostic medical devices has certainly proved its merits, but in recent years it has also been the subject of harsh criticism. in an internal market with 32 countries and constant scientific and technological progress, considerable differences in the interpretation and application of the rules have emerged, which undermines the main objectives of the directive, namely the safety and performance of dmds and their free movement. this review aims to overcome these shortcomings and differences and to further strengthen patient safety. we can only welcome it.
in writing. the proposal for a regulation on in vitro diagnostic medical devices (ivds) is a text that will regulate the production and use of such devices to improve patient protection and increase patient confidence. a high level of health protection must be ensured by stimulating innovation and competition in the manufacturing sector. in line with the horizon 2020 programming framework, the report aims to simplify the three relevant directives into a single text.
in writing. − there is major concern over low quality ivd medical devices and hiv tests placed on the european market. research has shown that these tests gave many more false negative results than other hiv tests available, which means the tests said that there was no virus but in fact there was. there is a life-threatening risk for european citizens who take the test if there is a blood transfusion which involves a false negative hiv result. people infected with hiv who receive a false negative test may put their partners at risk as well. therefore, i voted in favour of this proposal to deal with this matter.
in writing. - i gave a favourable opinion because ivds are medical devices intended for diagnostic use outside the human body (in vitro) but very important for monitoring, screening and preliminary diagnosis tests such as blood glucose kits, hiv tests and dna tests. the placing on the market of low-quality idvs can have serious health consequences, not so much for the preliminary diagnosis of false positives, but for the diagnosis of false negatives, which would lead to a misdiagnosis with serious consequences, for example a defective hiv test which could cause dramatic consequences if the patient in question is a blood donor. a new classification system will be adopted to ensure the highest possible safety (a-d, a=low risk device - d=high risk device). many of the companies producing such devices are smes, the regulation will take account of the ability of smes to take on new tasks, so keeping this situation in principle for risk classes a, b and c but including compliance when it comes to class d tests.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, we voted today on the proposal for a regulation on medical devices. this is an important issue and, in parallel with the proposal on in vitro diagnostic medical devices, it is proposed to review the regulatory framework, which was stable in the 1990s, in order to strengthen it and overcome the differences in interpretation in the various member states. following some health scandals as already mentioned it was considered important to intervene for the safety of patients. we have therefore voted in favour of a text which sets itself the primary objective of protecting the health of european patients, but also of defining better and more clearly the safeguards for their protection, of monitoring more rigorously and of laying down more explicitly the obligations of manufacturers and healthcare professionals. in short, a great deal of attention has been paid at the same time to the medical device sector in order to ensure and safeguard competitiveness, given its extreme importance in terms of innovation and employment for the european reality, and to patient protection and safety. the hope is that this will continue in the next negotiating phases.
madam president, how can we forget the incident of the defective implants in thousands of people? it is very serious that an accident of this magnitude could have happened. health is a fundamental right and must be a top priority, and i therefore agree that there is a need to tighten controls on medical equipment, to improve its quality and safety, precisely to restore patient confidence. this can only happen in a clear, secure and strengthened legal framework, which is: the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the draft directive on the protection of consumers. all this in support of innovation and the competitiveness of a sector which employs over half a million people in europe and has an annual turnover of over eur 100 billion. but beware of the burden of procedures, especially at the expense of small and mediumsized enterprises.
in writing. − in recent years, the conformity assessment procedure for medical devices has shown significant gaps. a clear demonstration of this is the breast implant scandal that emerged in 2011, when it was revealed that over half a million women worldwide had received defective implants with serious risks to their health. such cases must not happen again. i therefore voted in favour of this report, which aims to improve market surveillance, strengthen and rationalise the system of conformity assessment bodies (especially for products presenting the greatest risks), and ensure greater transparency and traceability.
in writing. − it is essential to review the european legislative framework for medical devices, as we believe that improvements are essential to protect public health and european patients. we therefore support this proposal for a report which aims to further strengthen the existing regulatory framework. medical devices that pose a potential risk to patients, such as those implanted in the body containing a medicinal substance or using human or animal tissues, need to be subjected to increasingly stringent procedures. the evaluation committee for these devices, composed of the best specialists, will be supported by a representation of both patients and experts from the european medicines agency. we also agree that the staff of the national authorities should be strengthened so that they are increasingly competent, that manufacturers of medicinal products should be able to apply to a notified body in a member state other than that of registration and that clinical trials should only be started after a positive evaluation by an independent ethics committee. finally, it will be essential to always have a considerate eye on the financial allocations in order to avoid unnecessary waste.
in writing. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of in vitro diagnostic medical devices (ivds) such as blood tests, which are covered by directive 98/79/ec of the european parliament and of the council. the horizontal aspects common to both sectors have been harmonised, while the specific characteristics of each sector reasonably require separate legal acts. the current regulatory framework has proven its merits, but has also been the subject of strong criticism, in particular when the french health authorities found that a french manufacturer (poly implant prothèse, pip) had for several years apparently used industrial silicone instead of medical grade silicone for the production of breast implants, in violation of the authorisation issued by the notified body, harming the health of thousands of women worldwide. i am therefore glad that today a position has been taken against such practices in the future.
in writing. − the need to amend and modernise existing medical device regulation has been felt for years. i voted in favour of amending the directive because the scandals of recent years have threatened the safety and health of patients, who will now be guaranteed by this new regulation on product safety, production and safety of the various medical devices. in addition, with the advancement of technology, it was felt necessary to adapt the regulatory framework to new machinery, thus protecting and guaranteeing the patient and encouraging innovation and production of medical devices.
in writing. − the proposal for a regulation on medical devices and active implantable medical devices attempts to regulate the standards of safety, quality and efficiency of medical devices which affect citizens of the european union. different types of medical devices currently on the market in the european union, such as syringes and blood sampling devices, should be required by law to be safe not only for patients but also for the healthcare professionals who handle them. since these points are specified under this proposed regulation, i voted in favour of it.
in writing. − the medical device sector employs over half a million people and has a market value of eur 100 billion. european companies operating in the sector are mainly small and medium-sized enterprises that are innovators in the sector, with more than ten thousand patent applications in 2012. i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the legislation on medical devices needs to be modernised to ensure greater safety, transparency and traceability, but with some important amendments to the position contained in mrs roth-behrendt's report. in particular, i am against the introduction of a double level of certification for medical devices: a first check by the notified bodies and a second check by an evaluation committee. this would make the procedure too bureaucratic, extending it beyond the average life of the products themselves, with unsustainable costs for smes, which constitute the majority of companies in the sector. furthermore, as regards the reuse of single-use devices, i do not think that the costs of proper refurbishment are such as to justify the position that they would represent a significant saving for hospitals. i support the choice to introduce more controls on notified bodies and the possibility of clinical experts being involved in the evaluation.
in writing. - i welcome the commission's proposal to revise the existing regulatory framework for medical devices. this is a review of a legislative framework which has been in existence for 20 years and which was particularly necessary. in general, i agree with the commission's improvements in classifying medical devices into four classes according to the level of risk they pose to patients. in recent years, the conformity assessment procedure has shown significant shortcomings, such as lack of transparency, rapid approval and placing on the market of medical devices without adequate patient surveys and therefore sufficient clinical data, resulting in risks for patients. i believe that medical devices that are potentially more risky for patients should be subject to procedures that are more stringent than conformity assessment, and that a committee for the evaluation of medical devices (acmd) should be established to carry out case-by-case assessment where its members have found it necessary to request the examination of clinical data. the labelling of devices as single-use (or reusable) needs to be revised, as i believe that devices labelled as single-use should actually be single-use and that there should only be two options: single or reusable.
in writing. - i think it is right to refer to the regulation on shipments of hazardous waste from the eu to non-oecd countries in relation to ship recycling. there are many hazardous materials on board and it is right to consider that any ship from the eu that is to be demolished is itself a hazardous waste. in 2009, more than 90% of eu-flagged vessels were scrapped outside the oecd area, mainly in south asia (india, pakistan and bangladesh) using the so-called 'sanding' method which has significant environmental and health impacts.' although i think the aim is laudable, i still have doubts about the potential effectiveness of the proposed measures, and i therefore believe that we should further review the commission's proposal, as there is a danger that it could legalise the export from the eu to developing countries of end-of-life vessels containing hazardous waste. i agree with the call made by some ngos that all vessels flying the flag of an eu state or owned by an eu state should be scrapped within the oecd countries.
in writing. - we recall a book published by oxford university more than ten years ago, which clearly outlined the links between the market economy, economic development, technological innovation in industrial applications and respect for the environment. i agree with the opening statement of principle: i would add that tolerating sandblasting, in addition to being an unacceptable risk to health and the environment, is not good for the economy in the medium term and slows down industrial development. we need to demonstrate leadership in helping operators to look beyond the immediate horizon. it is easy to imagine, for example, that the clearing of land would be progressively confined, by virtue of consensus and therefore positive codification, to the most unstable areas of the globe and those most prone to corruption, widespread illegality and weakness of the governing cadre. a world in which the risks are such as to compromise any effective margin. i appreciate the report's consideration of the capacity and value of industry also in non-oecd economies, already in the perspective of that integration, also in terms of production, which will necessarily follow the entry into force of the hong kong convention. i therefore vote in favour.
in writing. the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a new regulation on the protection of the environment. the idea of imposing on european shipowners costs which have no counterpart elsewhere is self-defeating. i agree with the environmental objectives, and i think that the more economically advanced countries should set a good example, but self-harm is another story. i therefore welcome the direction taken by this dossier after the rapporteur's amendments, because the negotiations within parliament before and those with the council have allowed a good balance to be struck.
in writing. − it is necessary to ensure that the rules are respected and that companies that work seriously are protected. unfortunately, most eu-flagged vessels are scrapped outside the oecd area using the 'sandblasting' method. this practice poses serious risks to workers' health and the environment, but it helps to keep costs down. i think the commission's proposal to establish a european list of recycling plants worldwide that meet certain standards is correct. the creation of a fund to reward compliant installations, a mandatory recycling plan for all eu ships over 20 years old, more explicit requirements for recycling facilities, regular checks and inspections of installations and the provision of criminal penalties for certain infringements are also measures that will make european regulatory intervention more effective.
in writing. − attention to environmental problems and the resulting damage to the ecosystem and human health have always been topics on the european parliament's agenda. unfortunately, despite the 'amendment to the ban' provided for by the basel convention, several areas of south asia have become, over the years, a dumping ground for old ships. that is why we are supporting today mr schlyter's proposal, which makes essential changes to the commission's earlier proposal in order to deal with this environmental emergency. it is therefore very important to introduce a financing mechanism for environmentally sound ship recycling. ships registered in the european union will have to be dismantled in recycling facilities approved by the european union itself, which will have to meet specific requirements and be subject to regular inspections. this will limit the dispersion of hazardous materials and will be beneficial for both man and the environment. in addition, both community and non-community vessels will have to produce an inventory of dangerous materials when entering ports in the european union. finally, we fully agree on the inclusion of criminal sanctions for illegal waste shipment.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by mr carl schlyter on the very topical subject of ship recycling. the eu regulation on shipment of waste prohibits the transfer of hazardous waste from european countries to non-oecd countries. the european commission has found that 90% of vessels from the european union are scrapped in south asian areas. such activity has a negative impact on both the environment and human health. the rapporteur included among his acceptable proposals a tightening of criminal sanctions for breaches of the legislation in this area. he therefore proposed that the penalties provided for in directive 2008/99/ec should apply not only to cases of illegal waste shipment but also to cases of improper recycling.
in writing. the ship-breaking and salvage industry is a formidable and growing business: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. some countries such as india, bangladesh and pakistan have become the preferred destination for the demolition of european ships, because in these places there is no respect for environmental rules or for workers' rights, and this obviously represents a significant, if unfortunate, cost reduction. the ships to be scrapped are truly special and often very dangerous waste: it goes without saying that there are some minimum rules to be followed. i wonder, however, how it is possible that no italian port is suitable for handling the wreck of the concordia, which is likely to end up in some turkish port. for piombino, it could be vital to start from the recovery of this ship to relaunch perhaps even in this type of business, on which it would really be worth investing, to have other possibilities in the future, with considerable repercussions in economic and employment terms.
in writing. − some inappropriate and environmentally harmful practices in ship demolition are still a matter of serious concern. at the end of their useful life, most large merchant ships for maritime navigation are dismantled in plants using methods that have a significant impact on the environment and health. under the waste shipment regulation, ships flying the flag of an eu country and intended for scrapping are classified as hazardous waste because they contain hazardous substances. as such, they may only be demolished in oecd countries. however, this regulation is almost always circumvented by eu-flagged vessels, rendering international standards and union legislation ineffective. it is therefore high time that this parliament took a firm stand on the issue of sustainable ship disposal and recycling.
in writing. − the export of hazardous waste from the eu to non-oecd countries is prohibited by the eu waste shipment regulation, which implements the ‘ban amendmentʼ at european level. however, more than 90 % of eu-flagged ships were indeed dismantled outside the oecd, mostly in southern asia, with significant environmental and health impacts, as estimated by the commission in 2009. the negative impacts of the recycling of eu-flagged ships, especially in southern asia, need to be reduced therefore without creating unnecessary economic burdens. currently, shipowners dispose of their ships at sites with the lowest standards because they pay the highest price. to deal with this problem, the introduction of a finance mechanism is proposed to finance environmentally sound ship recycling; i therefore voted in favour of it.
in writing. - the european parliament, in plenary session this morning, approved the report by mr schlyter on the proposal for a european parliament and council regulation on ship recycling. ending the widespread practice of scrapping community-flagged vessels off the coasts of developing countries is a goal of crucial importance for workers' health, safety and the environment. in future, eu-registered ships will have to be dismantled in eu-approved permanent recycling facilities, which will have to respect the environment and meet certain safety requirements. in addition, community and non-community vessels will have to produce an inventory of hazardous materials on entry into union ports, for future treatment in authorised recycling facilities. i can only express my favourable opinion of a report which does not impose an unnecessary economic burden on italy and, more importantly, which prohibits the practice of demolishing ships which offends human dignity and destroys the surrounding environment.
in writing. - i voted in favour because any ship from the eu that is to be scrapped is a hazardous waste and therefore must be legally scrapped only in oecd countries at the moment. unlike in recent years, they are being brought as close as possible to a beach at high tide and are usually dumped on muddy expanses in the intercoastal zone of non-oecd countries, which dispose of the materials incorrectly and pollute the environment. the current legislation on ship specifications is very inadequate, it is difficult to determine when a ship becomes waste. the proposal for a regulation on ship recycling aims to significantly reduce the negative effects of recycling eu-flagged ships without imposing unnecessary economic burdens. the commission proposes to establish a european list of recycling facilities worldwide to check whether they meet certain standards. ships flying the flag of an eu country are no longer covered by the waste shipment regulation but must be allowed to be scrapped at the facilities on the list.
in writing. the sógor report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council deals with the subject of european demographic statistics and calls for the creation of a common framework for the systematic production of population data. as i believe that the 'common framework' drawn up by the european institutions will serve to justify new policies in favour of immigration and austerity, i have decided not to support this text with my vote.
in writing. − in a world where the weight and demographic structure of countries is increasingly a determining factor in global market competitiveness and the rise of the asian demographic giants - notably china and india - poses major challenges for the most advanced economies, europe needs a common framework for the production of harmonised and comparable demographic statistics. knowledge of and availability of statistical data is a key element of competitiveness in the current 'information age': the commission has also adopted a communication on the implementation of the european year of the environment, which is essential for the development of targeted economic and social policies and crucial for guiding business and investment choices. i therefore voted in favour of this resolution which aims at harmonizing and developing a better system for producing demographic statistics at european level.
in writing. the content of the report concerns the centralisation of the management of demographic data to be included in the eu's policy project. i am voting against this text, because the political manipulation of eu population statistics is often used to justify the opening of borders because of an alleged shortage of labour: i therefore find it inappropriate to justify these new pro-immigration policies.
in writing. - demographic change is a reality that the european union cannot afford to ignore, not least because it is an aspect that must be taken into account when formulating public policies. demographic statistics are therefore crucial for making proper comparisons and operational choices. the commission has proposed the creation of a common framework for the production of european demographic statistics, in order to regulate the collection, compilation and transmission of population statistics. the purpose of the proposal, as the rapporteur for the empl committee notes, is to guide the states in the production of statistics which are harmonised at european level and thus comparable. the amendments adopted in the empl committee and voted by parliament essentially concern the provision of a reference to the protection of personal data and the requirement to transmit regional demographic statistics to eurostat.
in writing. - at the strasbourg plenary session, we welcomed the report on the proposal for a regulation on european demographic statistics. we agree with the rapporteur, mr sógor, that demographic change has a significant impact on the regions and, as there are considerable differences between the member states, it would be useful to be able to compare future developments. the need is to define a common framework of demographic statistics to be transmitted to eurostat, with the aim of creating a harmonious and comprehensive system, which can highlight changes and differences within the countries of the european union. only with these statistics will it be possible in future to compare, draw conclusions and monitor growth within and between member states. it should also be stressed that the importance of the protection of personal data will not be overlooked.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mr sógor's report on european demographic statistics, because i understood the importance of creating, in a common framework, a tool for publicly displaying demographic statistics on the population. the aim is to ensure that accurate, reliable and comparable data are collected. this is important because it serves to address social, economic and territorial problems in a shared way, while supporting the union's decision-making process.
in writing. the subject of the present proposal voted on today is a regulation on demographic statistics, which aims to regulate the harmonization and transmission of data on population and civil status events in relation to population. the size of the population will be even more important when, under article 16 (4) of the treaty on european union, from 1 november 2014 a qualified majority will be defined as at least 55% of the members of the council, with a minimum of 15 member states representing at least 65% of the eu population ('double majority'). in a union which is becoming more and more important in the daily lives of its citizens, the updating of the framework of european demographic statistics is therefore of fundamental importance.
in writing. − the european continent is ageing rapidly, society is not providing enough for families and gives young people the feeling that having children is a problem. we need solutions to the demographic challenge we are already facing, solutions that we can take together as the european union, and the first step is to compare the demographic statistics of each country and harmonize them throughout europe. only if statistics are available can comparisons be made, conclusions drawn and choices made.

in writing. − to promote mobility and to help reduce unemployment, it is essential to improve the efficiency of teaching and learning through better recognition of skills and qualifications in europe, to promote the use of open educational resources and new technologies in order to increase access to teaching materials and to increase student participation. teachers must have access to adequate training to update their skills. in the current situation of economic instability, in europe and globally, one of the main challenges is unemployment and the ability of people to secure their livelihoods. the fight against unemployment must be our main objective and it is in this context that education and training play a key role. these actions must concern not only students and young people entering the labour market but also other people who want to improve their situation. the main idea of my explanation of vote is not only to identify the main challenges and skills needed by students and people entering the labour market, but also to find solutions on how to maintain the essential condition of their individual and economic independence.
in writing. - with great realism, without succumbing to a certain enthusiasm for hasty decisions in the past, the rapporteur starts from a careful recognition of the general picture (as set out in point 16), of the different situations in the candidate countries and of the not entirely satisfactory effectiveness of commitment and refinement of expenditure in relation to the institutional objectives of ipa programmes. we would do well not to underestimate the considerations on the applicability of such a narrow window for pre-accession projects, considering that we are faced with difficulties that often have far-reaching and robust cultural roots. it is right that the commission is demanding on the issues of judicial reform and the fight against corruption: as noted in the hearings leading up to the report on organised crime, there are open problems and difficult challenges which, if not addressed in time, could put the union's systems under stress and thus undermine the culture of european integration, including by fostering demagogic exploitation. the so-called new approach is likely to maintain the course and accelerate processes of institutional, legal and cultural convergence: the country-by-country review also provides an overall picture of progress towards the accession objectives. i therefore vote in favour.
in writing. − the fight against corruption and organised crime is one of the most important priorities for all 'candidate' or 'potential candidate' countries for accession to the european union. promoting the rule of law and democracy in these countries is not only the key to ensuring rapid convergence towards their accession, but also means creating a context of greater stability and security around the european union, to the direct benefit of all its citizens. that is why i voted in favour of this proposal which calls on the commission to allocate, under pre-accession financial assistance, a larger amount of funds than at present for the reform of the judiciary and the fight against corruption in those countries which are making the difficult journey towards accession to the european union. it also remains a priority to ensure that the commission constantly monitors the implementation of the funded projects and currencies, by collecting and regularly publishing data and analyses, their impact in terms of effectiveness in order to ensure maximum transparency to union citizens in this regard.
in writing. - a modern and efficient justice system is an essential requirement. the european commission has rightly promoted an approach which envisages addressing the problems of the judicial system and internal politics of the candidate countries for accession to the union from the initial stage of the accession process. however, the resources foreseen in the pre-accession programmes should be allocated in accordance with this indication, with greater investment in the reform of the judicial systems and the fight against corruption. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mrs macovei's report because it rightly highlights the lack of adjustment of the pre-accession fund. as we all know, the fight against corruption and the evaluation of judicial systems are fundamental prerequisites for countries aiming to join the eu and therefore providing adequate financial resources to civil society organisations carrying out these tasks is of paramount importance. as regards the evaluation of aid, as the report argues, it is useful, in the interests of the principle of transparency, to make public the database on all projects financed under the pre-accession aid programmes.
in writing. - we met today in plenary to approve new measures to manage the budget of european union funds in the areas of the judicial system and the fight against corruption in the candidate and potential candidate countries. the fight against corruption and organised crime is a top priority for all countries wishing to achieve their european perspective. the rule of law is the cornerstone of democratic government and the judiciary is tasked with protecting and promoting fundamental rights and fighting corruption in order to strengthen democracy itself. the need for a higher level of funding therefore arises because predictable and adequate funding is a key prerequisite for ensuring sustainable reforms of the justice system. it should also be borne in mind that cooperation on reform of these systems and the fight against corruption will have to take place both at political level through structured and country-specific dialogues and on the rule of law and the judicial system by formalising closer cooperation and the exchange of good practice with the candidate and potential candidate countries.
in writing. − since 2001, eu pre-accession assistance to turkey in the field of judicial reform has financed 30 projects for an amount of eur 128 938 935, of which eur 66 645 666 has been disbursed as at 31 december 2012; nine projects have been completed, 11 are in progress and 10 are to be launched. the commission initiated a recovery procedure in february 2012 in respect of two completed projects in turkey, namely the construction of three courts of appeal in ankara, erzurum and diyarbakır and support for the establishment of courts of appeal in turkey. in april 2012, eur 21 767 205,29 was recovered, corresponding to the payments made by the commission for both projects. however, the commission's decision to proceed with full recovery was contested by the external evaluators. we therefore invite the commission to provide detailed information on this issue by december 2013 and to explain the reasons for the choice of a full recovery, given that the projects have now been completed.
in writing. − corruption is a serious threat in terms of costs to the eu economy. not only does it affect the tax revenues of the member states and the eu as a whole, but it also imposes a cost to business estimated at more than eur 670 billion annually. fighting corruption is significant for the safety of european consumers, free and fair competition, an undistorted lawful business cycle, and the fundamental democratic principles on which the eu and its member states are based. since funding is necessary to reform the judicial system to fight corruption better, i voted in favour of this proposal.
in writing. − one of the eu's top priorities is the implementation of the rule of law, with particular attention to judicial reform, and the fight against corruption and organised crime. the funds that europe provides to the candidate countries or potential candidates are of vital importance, not only for the full establishment of democracy in the same countries, but also to avoid undermining the social and democratic fabric of europe as a whole. i am voting in favour of these measures because they are the means of achieving more sustainable results in improving the preparation of these countries for accession and, where possible, by promoting the sectoral approach in order to support the wide-ranging reform strategies of the beneficiary countries.
in writing. - the report by mr macovei stresses the need for better planning and financing of the fight against corruption, calling on the commission to develop a long-term strategy on union funding for civil society organisations. as regards the evaluation of aid, i share the rapporteur's view that it is useful to make public the data on all projects financed under pre-accession aid programmes.
in writing. − access to safe healthcare is a fundamental right of citizens. in a context of ageing populations and the development of antimicrobial resistance, patient safety must be at the forefront of the political agenda of the european union as well as at national and local level. the health sector is a high-risk sector because adverse events related to healthcare can result in serious injury or, in extreme cases, death of patients. it is estimated that between 30 and 40% of adverse events associated with healthcare could be prevented; these events include healthcare-associated infections, which affect as many as 3,2 million citizens each year in the european union. i agree with the rapporteur that the culture of patient safety must be strengthened, and in particular also through the promotion of education/training of healthcare professionals in patient safety and the development of research in this field. some of the actions recommended by the council to improve patient safety in the member states have so far been implemented by only a limited number of countries. i therefore call the commission's attention to the need to monitor the member states' implementation of these recommendations.
in writing. the rapporteur is tackling a very topical issue which is going to weigh increasingly heavily on our health and welfare systems. the situation is likely to improve as a result of the development of techniques, industrial applications and medical protocols, but new challenges are looming, such as the effects of demographic dynamics and a non-unique pattern of morbidity, with the return of diseases that were considered to have been eradicated for good. the ageing of the population is certainly a key factor which must be played out in a positive way: the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council should be consulted on the proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to carcinogens at work. this theme is accompanied by the challenges of globalisation and cultural integration, which are likely to affect the way in which care is delivered and managed. i'll close with a note: the issue of off-label medicines (to which we could add the spread of over-the-counter medicines, on which the ep has already spoken) is dramatically relevant again in the face of the crisis which pushes the most vulnerable patients to the margins, if not outside, the sphere of control of public authorities. the report deals with this subject with some shared guidance. i therefore confirm my vote in favour.
in writing. - i think the work done on this initiative has been excellent: the rapporteur was able to identify some very important aspects on which patients do not have contractual power vis-à-vis the healthcare system and to put in writing what measures should be taken to make the hospital stay safer, which is already a rarely happy event and chosen by the patient. the additional ability of mr tino rossi, to whom i congratulate, to bring all the political groups together and to achieve unanimity in the commission, is another reason for approving this proposal.
in writing. - the impressive numbers of patients affected by a healthcare-associated infection cannot leave parliament indifferent. we're talking about 3.2 million people a year. as highlighted in mr rossi's report, there is still much work to be done to implement the actions outlined in the 2009 council recommendation. the european centre for disease prevention and control is certainly an important instrument, and we must ensure that it receives adequate funding so that it can continue to carry out its coordination and surveillance tasks effectively. parliament has always shown itself to be sensitive and attentive to issues which affect people closely, and this is about protecting the health of our citizens, who must be guaranteed a safe and high-quality health system.
in writing. − healthcare is a fundamental right for all citizens of the european union, who therefore expect every effort to be made to ensure that hospital services and facilities function excellently for them. that is why we are supporting today mr rossi's report on patient safety through infection prevention and control (ipc), because it calls for action to develop health plans in all the member states of the european union, creating an increasingly harmonised and efficient system. particular attention will have to be paid to improving hospital and non-hospital care in all member states and not just in a limited number of them, as is unfortunately still the case. it will also be important to involve citizens, as potential patients, in improving their own safety through awareness campaigns against infectious or sexually transmitted diseases. it will be essential to provide specific funds for the education and training of health workers and those involved in the care of the sick. it will be essential to ensure that infection control and prevention play a leading role in european union policy, as well as at national, local and regional level.
in writing. - the issue of patient safety has become an increasing concern in healthcare systems around the world, which is why i voted in favour of mr rossi's report, which sets out the guidelines for a concrete eu commitment in this area. healthcare-related adverse events can result in serious injury, complications or suffering, if not death, in patients. i agree that as much as possible we should focus on measures to improve the public's knowledge of patient safety initiatives. given that the health sector is a high-risk sector, it is necessary to draw the attention of member states to the implementation of policies aimed at promoting greater patient confidence in healthcare.
in writing. − the right to health is rightly enshrined at all levels, both at national and european level, in the eu charter of fundamental rights. the member states, however, retain the prerogatives in this area within a european reference action. patients must be able to receive the best possible care and assistance, both in the actual treatment and in the field of information and communication: the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect. a separate reflection should be made on the possibility of obtaining cross-border care: in the border areas, where there are perhaps small isolated areas, cooperation in the field of health is necessary, as has been the case for some years now, for example, on the border between the french and spanish pyrenean mountain regions. in addition, the possibility of obtaining high-quality specific care, which may sometimes require specialised facilities in other countries, should be guaranteed and facilitated. a different argument is needed if we consider a phenomenon which has unfortunately become widespread in recent years, namely the indiscriminate 'exploitation' of the health services of other countries: this is absolutely unacceptable and some of the rules should be revised.
in writing. - we all know, or almost all of us in this chamber, that health is a matter for the member states and not for the eu, unless complementary action can bring real added value. eu action in the field of patient safety consists of helping member states to coordinate their efforts in this area and jointly supporting their actions. it is estimated that between 8 and 12% of patients admitted to hospitals in the european union suffer adverse events related to their care, whether they are errors during treatment or surgery, problems related to defective or insufficiently decontaminated medical devices, errors in diagnosis or failure to respond to medical examinations. we therefore welcome the commission's action to improve overall patient safety by promoting the exchange of good practice between member states and proposing common definitions and terminology for patient safety.
in writing. − access to healthcare is one of the fundamental rights of the european union and determines the quality of a healthcare system. patient safety must be the primary concern and therefore all member states must comply with european legislation and follow its recommendations. patient safety, prevention and health care must be ensured in all member states by further improvements in both hospital care and the education of health workers. in a context of an ageing population, patient safety must be one of the priorities on the union's political agenda.
in writing. − access to safe healthcare is a fundamental right for european citizens recognised by the eu and the european institutions. the safety of patients is thus prioritised in medical practices. however, there are substantial risks in the healthcare sector, some of which are related to the risks associated with vital operations or drugs, others caused by avoidable medical errors. harm caused to patients has placed a significant burden on european citizens, which is aggravated in times of economic crisis. investment in patient safety is therefore necessary because it will reduce the potential costs incurred in treating patients experiencing adverse events associated with healthcare. therefore, i voted in favour of this proposal.
in writing. − according to estimates from international studies, 5% of patients admitted to hospital suffer from infections linked to poor healthcare and 13%-16% of hospital costs - one euro in seven - are due to healthcare-related deficiencies. i believe that this report shows a significant commitment by the council and the commission to ensuring greater patient safety, through the identification of measures such as improving the training of healthcare professionals, the dissemination of information relevant to patients by healthcare facilities, research activities for the prevention and control of infections, closer control of medical devices and the dissemination of good hygiene practices. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. − access to healthcare is a fundamental aspect of the european union because it is a fundamental right recognised and guaranteed to all european citizens. patients therefore have the right to expect that every effort will be made to ensure their safety. the health sector is a high-risk sector as events can result in serious injury, complications or suffering, if not death, of patients. the harm caused to patients by adverse events associated with healthcare also imposes a heavy burden on society, the burden of which is even greater in a time of economic crisis. that is why the eu must invest as much resources as possible in this area if the right i have mentioned above is to be effectively implemented, without forgetting that, in addition to the obvious benefit to patients, any investment in the field of patient safety is therefore a potential source of savings. the priority given to patient safety also leads to a reduction in costs in terms of treating patients suffering from adverse events associated with healthcare and therefore a better use of financial and human resources. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. - the report is of particular importance because it contains a number of measures to combat deceptive marketing practices, in particular those unfairly practised by companies which compile yearbooks. the aim is to protect businesses from dishonest companies using deceptive marketing practices, such as sending businesses forms requesting an update of their yearbook data, ostensibly free of charge, but for which an annual fee is then charged. small and medium-sized enterprises are particularly vulnerable to this type of fraud. the economic damage caused to individual businesses by the scams perpetrated by these companies is estimated to be between eur 1 000 and eur 5 000 per year per company. while welcoming the commission's communication to strengthen existing legislation to explicitly prohibit deceptive marketing practices, i believe that there are gaps, potentially fillable, in the introduction of further measures in the field of prevention and information, enforcement and legal action in this area. finally, since deceptive marketing practices can take many forms and are not a european phenomenon, i stress the importance of strengthening international cooperation in combating this phenomenon.
