in writing. − in august 2012, the european commission presented the green paper 'oceanographic knowledge 2020: from seabed mapping to oceanographic forecasting' as part of the actions taken to promote, develop and expand the 'blue economy'. the blue economy is a global business model dedicated to the creation of a sustainable ecosystem, whose main objective is sustainable development, a form of development that does not hinder the growth possibilities of future generations, while taking care of the heritage and natural reserves that are exhaustible. it is not a question of blocking growth, but of economic growth which respects the environment and its limits. it will be an integral part of the 'europe 2020 strategy' as regards the sea, combining knowledge and technological innovation, sustainable use of resources, competitiveness and job creation for smart, sustainable and inclusive growth. to achieve this, a continuous multi-resolution digital seabed map of european waters should be in place by 2020. i am voting in favour of the creation of a digital map of the seabed, so as to create a coherent information system accessible to all.
in writing. − the european union currently lacks common legislation to enforce its rights under the wto and other international trade agreements. the need for the union to be able to exercise effectively the right to suspend or revoke concessions in response to violations of international trade rules by a third country is therefore becoming increasingly evident. i therefore wholeheartedly support the proposal for a regulation of the parliament and the council, which is necessary to ensure that swift action is taken to protect the union's rights - in the context of international trade agreements - and to guarantee the european union credibility and leverage in negotiations, both in the framework of the gpa and in bilateral trade agreements.
in writing. - it is a fact that in the current global scenario, retaliatory episodes are not uncommon and that the risks of a full-blown trade war, for example between the usa and china, in relation to the new asia-pacific trading platform and the chinese currency's strong arm are recurrent. the rapporteur takes this awareness to heart and recommends an instrument without which the union is unarmed even in the face of repeated trade violations, and in any case in a relatively weak position when it comes to confronting other interests in emerging markets. i agree that the availability of a horizontal instrument, which is easy to use in a timely manner, can have a positive impact on this plan, without prejudice to the union's commitment to the principles of free trade. i also support the applicability of the measures to the services sector, which according to the world bank now represents between 50% and 60% of the gdp of the countries of the union, an area in which trade with partners outside the eu is now a structural fact and is also essential in areas of strict public interest, such as security, networks, health systems. i therefore vote in favour.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mr rinaldi's proposal because i think it is useful to have a regulation which gives the eu an effective legislative instrument to defend its rights in international trade. in particular, a standard rapid decision-making procedure should be established in the event of an infringement and the ad hoc procedures used to date should be limited. this step strengthens the eu's role in defending its rights and discourages unfair competition measures from unfair countries. i believe that it is crucial to apply this also in the field of public procurement, as well as international agreements in the context of the world trade organisation and the customs union.
in writing. the content of this report concerns the protection of commercial interests to counter retaliatory measures or behaviour by third countries which breach the rules of the world trade organisation. the text is undoubtedly valid in that it will serve - by the very fact of its implementation - to dissuade certain third countries from not complying with wto rules. my vote is in favour because the country that is harmed will have greater protections.
in writing. − it is important to have a single legislative instrument to enable the union's interests to be defended more quickly and effectively. the european union has not yet had a single legislative framework to enforce its rights under the various international trade agreements. this means that retaliatory measures against third countries which do not comply with the agreements have been adopted individually by council regulations, following a case-by-case approach. i think the rapporteur has improved the proposal by introducing, for example, a systematic exchange of information between the commission and parliament.
in writing. − this proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council reflects the union's priority objective of effectively enforcing existing trade rights. this objective was set out in the commission communication on trade, growth and world affairs and endorsed in the council conclusions of 21 december 2010. the union currently does not have a common legislative framework to enforce its rights under international trade agreements. this proposal therefore seeks to remedy this situation and we welcome it.
in writing. - in the morning, parliament, in plenary session, voted on a report by mr rinaldi on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the exercise of the union's rights to the application and enforcement of international trade rules. the resolution pursues the legitimate aim of asserting the eu's trade rights, consolidating its credibility and convincing our trading partners to play by the rules of the game as laid down in international agreements, in a global context where trade retaliation is the order of the day. the rapporteur also suggests that the range of trade policy measures available to the eu should be extended to include the services sector. the proposal for a regulation also provides for practical cooperation between the commission and parliament without delaying the decision-making process. for these reasons, i cannot help but support a regulation which, by its very existence, constitutes a credible threat to our trading partners who are prone to disregard the rules of the game.
in writing. - world trade concerns us all, and although trade policy may seem like a technical subject, it actually affects the lives of all citizens. with globalisation, an increasing number of countries are participating in the world economy. the eu has a strong interest in creating the conditions for an expansion of trade and its position implies certain responsibilities towards the rest of the world. despite this, the eu currently lacks a horizontal legislative framework to enforce its rights under the wto and other international trade agreements. i am in favour of europe having an instrument designed for the legitimate purpose of asserting the eu's trade rights, consolidating its credibility and ultimately convincing our trading partners to play by the rules of the game as laid down in trade agreements.
in writing. − on 2 december 2011, the european commission approved the proposal for a regulation for the new european maritime and fisheries fund, which will replace the current eff. the transition to sustainability requires a radical change in the way we fish: the fund will provide operators with the necessary incentives to reduce the impact of their activities on marine ecosystems, to end the overexploitation of resources and to halt the decline of fish stocks, priorities which are not secondary to the economic importance of the fisheries sector in europe. i hope that the proposed budget will make it possible to achieve the objectives of the reform of the common fisheries policy (cfp) and also the objectives of the integrated maritime policy.
in writing. − the establishment of the european maritime and fisheries fund (emff), with a budget of around eur 6.3 billion, is an important instrument for the reform of the common fisheries policy. i therefore voted in favour of this motion for a resolution, which introduces a number of important new features. firstly, it guarantees greater support for small businesses and small-scale fishing, which create jobs and income for thousands of families in italy and europe. secondly, the proposal provides for the implementation of programmes for the vocational training of young people and the facilitation of their entry into the sector. finally, by strengthening scientific knowledge, using in-depth data and analysis and in constant dialogue with representatives of the sector, this resolution aims at a more effective common fisheries policy, protecting marine biodiversity and the workers in this sector.
in writing. − i supported the report on the european maritime and fisheries fund (emff), the new instrument to finance the common fisheries policy for the period 2014-2020. i believe that the compromises reached can contribute to a realistic european fisheries policy. on the one hand, account has been taken of the need to reduce fishing capacity gradually at union level. the reduction must not be achieved by reducing the number of vessels, but by more stringent controls on compliance with the ceilings on fishing quantities and by a policy of renewal and modernisation of the fleet and replacement of engines, which will ensure that vessels are more energy-efficient, more selective and less powerful. on the other hand, efforts have been made to ensure the sustainability and profitability of fishing activities by supporting diversification, vocational training and the entry of young people into the fisheries sector and the development of aquaculture. the role of the emff should be to encourage the creation of enterprises in the fisheries sector and to support, in particular, the competitiveness and sustainability of small-scale and coastal fisheries, which are so important for the vitality of coastal areas.
in writing. i voted in favour of the proposal by my colleague, mr alain cadec, on the european maritime and fisheries fund (emff), which is the financial component of the reform of the common fisheries policy. the aim is to provide effective support for the implementation of the new common fisheries policy: for an environmentally sustainable fisheries with the introduction of conservation measures such as biological rest periods or temporary stops and the freezing of subsidies for member states which do not comply with the rules of the common fisheries policy. for a competitive fishing sector through assistance for the establishment of young fishermen (under 35 years of age), support for the diversification of fishermen's income into activities complementary to fishing, investments in fishing port infrastructure, and support for innovation, including the design of more modern and environmentally friendly vessels. for an ambitious social component to improve health, hygiene and safety on board, vocational training for fishermen and conditions linked to compliance with the social legislation in force (no subsidy in case of non-compliance).
in writing. - as a citizen of the emilia romagna region, which faces the sea, i am generally satisfied with the text voted on today. the commission proposal for the multiannual financial framework (mff) for 2014-2020, adopted on 29 june, outlined the budgetary framework and the main guidelines for the financing of the common fisheries policy (cfp) and the integrated maritime policy. the current proposal for a regulation on the european maritime and fisheries fund aims to achieve the objectives of the reforms of the common fisheries and maritime policy on the basis of the following objectives, redefined in terms of funding: promote sustainable and competitive fisheries and aquaculture; to promote the development and implementation of the union's integrated maritime policy in a complementary manner to cohesion policy and the cfp; promote balanced and inclusive territorial development of areas where fishing activities are carried out (including aquaculture and inland fishing); contribute to the implementation of the common fisheries policy.
in writing. − the european maritime and fisheries fund (emff) will provide funds for structural aid to the maritime sector and fisheries under the new multiannual financial framework 2014-2020. the objective of the fund is obviously growth, employment, sustainability, modernisation of structures, and enhancement of the marine and coastal environment. the fund, which will have a total budget of eur 5.5 billion, is also intended to achieve the objectives of the integrated maritime policy and the reform of the common fisheries policy.
in writing. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'common carrier' in the definition of the term 'commercial vehicle'. the new cfp is based on the principle of subsidiarity, which is a fundamental principle of the cfp. i am particularly pleased with the promotion of small-scale artisanal coastal fishing. i also think it is important to provide for accompanying measures for young people who want to take up this activity and the possibility of scrapping boats to reduce fishing effort. these are fundamental measures to revive the sector, especially if we believe that this sector can still be a source of employment and attractive for young people.
in writing. − the additional allocation of €6.5 billion to the european maritime and fisheries fund will help fishermen to comply with the rules of the new common fisheries policy, such as the ban on discarding, through the purchase of more selective equipment. it will now be possible to improve the safety and working conditions of fishermen by adopting a new sustainable fishing model that will enable fishermen to live off the profits of their profession.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the repeal of council regulations (ec) no 1198/2006, (ec) no 861/2006 and (ec) no xxx/2011 on the integrated maritime policy. the desire to reduce the alleged overcapacity of the fleet would have no effect on the quantities caught, because the latter would continue to depend on the tacs and quotas fixed each year. the proposal to catch the same amount of fish with fewer vessels puts many fishing enterprises, including small-scale or coastal ones, and thus many jobs at risk. while strict control of fishing activities can lead to sustainable environmental and social management. to this end, it is recalled that member states are obliged to respect the capacity limits of their fleet as set out in the basic regulation.
in writing. - i express my general appreciation and a declaration of support for the resolution tabled by a number of colleagues in the committee on the environment. the objective to be achieved is certainly that of a single, comprehensive and binding international agreement on the fight against climate change for the post-kyoto period and to overcome the current difficulties; the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. in order to achieve ambitious objectives, the major emerging economies must also play their part, together with the traditional industrial players, on the basis of a fair distribution of effort and the principle of 'common but differentiated responsibilities'. i also think it is important that the eu confirms and reinforces its leadership on this issue by setting ambitious targets for reducing greenhouse gas emissions within ambitious time limits, by urging international partners to embrace a virtuous logic and by demonstrating how ambitious climate change mitigation targets can be combined with competitiveness, innovation and job protection.
in writing. - in view of the forthcoming un climate conference in warsaw, i voted in favour of this resolution which underlines some key points in the fight against climate change. the challenges related to climate change prevention, mitigation and adaptation remain multiple. however, these challenges can only be addressed through an integrated approach, which puts climate-related issues in the context of sustainable development, industrial policy and energy policy. in this respect, the eu needs to focus its efforts and establish an effective regulatory framework so that climate-related innovation in the industrial and energy sectors translates into a comparative advantage for the eu, putting it at the forefront of the global market for energy-related goods and services (a market with strong growth prospects). finally, it is important that the eu maintains a proactive role in the course of future international climate negotiations: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them.
in writing. − the united nations framework convention on climate change, which calls for the adoption of a legally binding global climate agreement by 2015 and its implementation by 2020, provides for the organisation of annual conferences between stakeholders, cop, to assess progress and gradually set new targets. the european parliament has voted today on the priorities for the warsaw cop, which will take place from 18 to 23 november. the report raises several critical points: the commission has also been working on a new strategy to reduce emissions from the transport sector, which is based on the principle of sustainable development. another key issue is the financing of emission reduction programmes: the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the green paper to include the environment, climate change, energy and transport. the european union must take a strong stance if it does not want its policies to tackle emissions to be an isolated effort.
in writing. − climate change is an urgent and potentially irreversible threat to human societies, biodiversity and the planet and is therefore a problem that must be addressed at international level by all parties; the doha climate gateway highlights with grave concern the significant gap between the aggregated effect of the parties' current commitments to reduce annual global greenhouse gas emissions by 2020 and the aggregated emission pathways that need to be followed to ensure that the increase in the planet's average annual surface temperature does not exceed 2 °c. the important work to be done by the ad hoc working group on the durban platform for enhanced action to establish the principles and framework for the new global climate agreement and the means to achieve it in time for cop 21 in paris in 2015 will need to be based on the ipcc fifth assessment report, due by 2014. the 2015 agreement should focus on the objective of reducing global emissions to below 1990 levels by 2030, with a view to phasing out global carbon emissions by 2050.
in writing. − climate change is an urgent and potentially irreversible threat to human societies, biodiversity and the planet and is therefore a problem that must be addressed internationally by all parties. i believe that the eu delegation plays an essential role in the climate change negotiations and therefore find it unacceptable that members of the european parliament have not been able to attend the eu coordination meetings during the previous conferences of the parties. that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. − the need for a european-wide mobilisation to combat organised crime is a priority today. it is a question that now transcends national borders: more than 3 600 criminal organisations operate internationally in the european union. these are organizations that have developed the ability to infiltrate the institutions of various countries in order to carry out their money laundering and corruption activities with impunity. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. another point of great importance is certainly the establishment of a european public prosecutor's office for the coordination of national authorities. finally, i believe it is essential to lay the foundations for a european legislative framework involving all the member states in the fight against mafia associations.
in writing. − the european parliament today approved the final report of the special committee on organised crime, corruption and money laundering (crim), set up in 2012 to analyse criminal activities and suggest guidelines for tackling the problem at european level. the report, which sums up the work of the special committee, proposes a european action plan to combat organised crime, corruption and money laundering, and sets out a series of priorities for the period 2014-2020 which this parliament could only endorse. these include the introduction of a common definition of criminal phenomena, the abolition of banking secrecy, the elimination of tax havens, the promotion of the confiscation of criminal assets, the establishment of the offence of illegal manipulation of sports, the introduction of appropriate sanctions for cybercrime, the strengthening of the fight against environmental crimes, drug trafficking and human trafficking, the ensuring of rapid mutual recognition of judicial measures and the establishment of a european public prosecutor's office.
in writing. the work of the crim commission marks an important moment in the life of the european institutions. finally, serious associative crime is analysed at european level and the gradual widening of the range of action of organisations is highlighted, as a result of the opening of frontiers. the recommendations contained in the resolution, which i supported with my vote, provide a platform for action for the member states to develop, within the limits of national sovereignty. coordination between national legislation and the response instruments of the systems is essential to tackle the problem effectively. the objectives to be pursued: the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the following areas: the protection of the financial interests of the union; the fight against the proceeds and assets of criminal activities; an efficient and corruption-free public administration; more responsible politics; a more credible judiciary; a healthier business environment; a more transparent banking system and professions. a list which expresses the objective of punishing crimes and above all of stopping the process of penetration into the vital nodes of public life. the commission's proposal for a regulation on the protection of the financial interests of the european communities and the european investment bank is a good one.
in writing. this report is a summary of the work carried out in recent months by the european parliament's special committee on organised crime, corruption and money laundering. the hearings were very interesting, with european experts in different fields sharing experiences and problems common to many countries. the result is a widely shared text, which lays the foundations for coordinated action at eu level: the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the draft directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos. in this case, police and judicial action is necessary to bring the authorities of the member states to cooperate in a thorough and continuous manner. the report also stresses the importance of targeting the proceeds and assets of organised crime in order to combat its illicit activities effectively. the economic and financial side has become the main business of the criminal world, and only if we can hit them in this area can we hope to stop them, before they irreparably infect the real economy, making it impossible for honest operators to survive. we hope that the italian experience in this field will be useful in europe too.
in writing. - we voted today in a strong message to criminal organisations, which are progressively extending their range of action on an international scale, as well as taking advantage of economic globalisation and new technologies, by forging alliances with criminal groups in other countries (as in the case of south american drug cartels and russian-speaking organised crime) to share markets and areas of influence. criminal groups are increasingly diversifying their activities and establishing links between drug trafficking, human trafficking, facilitating illegal immigration, arms trafficking and money laundering; corruption and organised crime are significant threats in terms of costs to the eu economy with significant impact on tax revenues of the member states and the union as a whole and an estimated annual cost to businesses of over eur 670 billion. we urge the commission to launch a european action plan against organised crime, corruption and money laundering, including legislative measures and positive action to combat these criminal phenomena effectively.
in writing. - the fight against organised crime must be fought with a concerted effort by all the countries of the union, which is why the report represents a positive and significant step forward in countering criminal organisations which are increasingly hostile and linked by interests which are often confused with business and economic initiatives. criminal organizations have infiltrated procurement, gambling, the exploitation of children and women, construction and often, sadly, political organizations. all the proposals put forward today are welcome and necessary, but we also recall that to combat the spread of crime in the trade sector, that is to say to combat counterfeiting and illegality, the customs system must be harmonized. whereas in order to combat the spread of drugs and the exploitation of women and children, different rules for the control of computer systems are needed; that to prevent the spread of the criminal power of gambling, it is necessary to prevent its publicity and to call for this sector to be harmonised by the european union and no longer be the sole responsibility of the member states; the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them.
in writing. - i have expressed my favourable opinion on the final report of the crim special committee chaired by mr iacolino, because the european union will finally be able to have a common strategy, set out in black and white, on the action to be taken against organised crime, corruption and money laundering. the guidelines that member states will have to follow in the fight against all mafia-like associations have been set out in a context of horizontal cooperation and full cooperation between the different police systems. in addition, all the cases to be considered as criminal situations and therefore liable to prosecution throughout europe have been listed.
in writing. − corruption, organised crime and money laundering are serious threats to the democratic principles and economy of the european union. recent observations proved the trend of extension of crime organisations’ operating range on an international scale. the number of international criminal organisations operating in the european union is estimated to be around 3 600, most of which consist of members from several countries who operate across borders exploiting the opportunities offered by economic globalisation. to better fight organised crime in europe and promote more credible criminal justice, more honest business practices, and more efficient public administration, i voted in favour of this proposal.
in writing. - the european parliament has given a very strong signal by its vote today, bringing the phenomenon of mafia-like criminal organisations, which unfortunately involve a large number of eu member states, to the attention of europe. the european commission's very recent legislative proposals, such as the establishment of the european public prosecutor, are promising first steps towards a common response to crime. the european public prosecutor's office, europol and eurojust will need to have the right human and financial resources to fully carry out the tasks assigned to them. finally, i hope that the european commission will include specific clauses on cooperation in the fight against the illicit trafficking of organised crime in the association agreements and trade agreements with third countries.
in writing. - the european parliament, in plenary session, delivered its opinion this morning on the report by mr iacolino on organised crime, corruption and money laundering. the union must respond with vigour to the challenge posed by the worldwide spread of such phenomena, which are often intertwined and interrelated and require targeted action and appropriate instruments. the time is long gone when organised crime was a functionally and territorially limited phenomenon: today, thousands of criminal organisations operate in the eu, diversifying their 'portfolio' of illicit activities and exploiting the new opportunities offered by economic globalisation and new technologies. it is therefore essential to establish a coherent legislative framework and to strengthen judicial and police cooperation at european and international level, in order to prevent crime from penalising the lawful economy, honest entrepreneurs and citizens. as a member of the european parliament from the southern constituency, i can only express my favourable opinion of a resolution which seeks to promote concrete initiatives to deal with phenomena which are unfortunately on the agenda in southern italy.
in writing. - it is now essential that the european union can have a common action plan to crack down on organised crime, corruption and money laundering. there are now about 3 600 international criminal organisations operating in the eu. better tools are needed now to target their activities and sources of income, while protecting the financial interests of the european union. the cost of the mafia, however difficult to estimate, is estimated to be between 4 and 5 points of gdp for the eu alone, a reality we can no longer afford to tolerate.
in writing. − according to the united nations office on drugs and crime, illicit proceeds globally amount to about 3.6% of global gdp, while the european commission estimates the cost of corruption in the eu to be around 1% of eu gdp. organised crime is increasingly resembling a global economic entity and, together with corruption, has a growing impact on the european economy, with significant repercussions for the member states and the union as a whole. i voted in favour of this report because i believe it provides the necessary instruments to respond strongly and decisively to these phenomena, which are draining significant resources from economic and social development, public finances and the well-being of citizens. the main measures required are: the mutual recognition of freezing and confiscation orders issued by the respective judicial authorities of the member states, enhanced administrative, police and judicial cooperation for the tracing of criminal assets throughout the european union, the reuse of confiscated criminal assets for social purposes and the strengthening of transparency mechanisms in public administration in order to prevent corruption.
in writing. − the presentation of this draft final report is the culmination of the work of the special committee on organised crime, corruption and money laundering. the aim is to produce, with the input and insights of the many personalities we met during these months, a text that responds to the need to combat in an appropriate way criminal phenomena that have taken on a global dimension. the european union is called upon to meet this challenge by equipping itself with the appropriate instruments to deal with it, on the model of the most advanced legislation in the member states. i am in favour of the eu adopting a homogeneous and coherent legislative framework to tackle the economic heart of organised crime, by strengthening judicial and police cooperation at european and international level, so as to create a genuine european judicial area throughout europe. to enable citizens to assert their rights throughout the union, it is necessary to facilitate their access to justice.
in writing. − the principal aim of the european neighbourhood policy is to strengthen the partnership between the eu and the countries and societies of the neighbourhood, in order to build and consolidate healthy democracies, respect for human rights and the rule of law. for this reason i believe that this is the right context to discuss about the on-going violation of human rights in western sahara. as neighbours and partner countries, we must urge morocco to continue negotiations for a peaceful and long-lasting solution of the western sahara conflict. the sahrawi people have the right to self-determination through a democratic referendum, in accordance with the relevant united nations resolutions. also, i believe that morocco should urgently release all the sahrawi political prisoners. we cannot ignore that the rights of sahrawis are those of us all. and we cannot ignore that one of our neighbour countries is perpetrating the last case of colonial oppression in africa.
in writing. − the european neighbourhood policy (enp) aims to avoid new fault lines between the eu and its neighbours by offering them gradual economic integration, financial assistance and political dialogue, and demanding structural reforms of their political and economic systems in return. the creation of an area of prosperity, democracy, development and security around the eu is an indispensable prerequisite for the union's integration process and the promotion and protection of the values and principles which underpin the european institutional architecture. unfortunately, political and social change in many partner countries remains slow and there are frequent abuses and violations of fundamental rights and freedoms. to this end, the union should strengthen the application of the principle of 'more progress, more aid', thus making its support and dialogue conditional on the effective implementation of the agreed economic and institutional reforms. i therefore voted in favour of this report on the enp, which sets out the essential guidelines along which the union's action in this field must be developed.
in writing. − this report, which was widely adopted in the assembly today, sets out a series of considerations on the implementation of the european neighbourhood policy, starting with the 2012 interim reports. the overall picture, as regards the eastern partnership countries and the partnership with countries in north africa and the middle east, is not showing particularly positive trends and suggests the need for a greater commitment by the eu. however, this commitment will not bear fruit unless the union imposes a number of conditions in terms of commitment by the partner countries. the report stresses that in the case of the eastern partnership countries, the process of integration and progress towards european values depends to a large extent on the choices and priorities of the partner countries themselves. in this context, the eu should maintain and strengthen the current differentiated and incentive-based approach to its neighbourhood policy, allocating more resources to the countries making the most progress.
in writing. − the resolution by mr panzeri and mr saryusz-wolski is a useful insight into the effectiveness of the neighbourhood policy and provides important insights into making the necessary adjustments to the european strategy in the 16 countries neighbouring the eu, with which we have been cooperating for almost a decade now on the basis of a mutual commitment to respect for common values such as democracy, the protection of human rights, the recognition of the rule of law, good governance, a market economy and sustainable development. the critical points identified in the country-by-country analysis are also starting points for updating the community's external effort. the data show little progress in the democratic process, some improvements in economic and trade relations and a weak recognition of the eu in the countries targeted by our programmes. the result is that the union is too cautious in its action and that we need to define a strategy for the two macro-areas of the mediterranean and the east, on which to refocus our interventions in order to make investment more efficient. an important work that i supported with my vote in favour.

in writing. - i voted in favour because i believe that this resolution, while welcoming some progress made, also highlights the need for important corrections. the 2013 european semester has delivered good results: the commission has also published a report on the economic situation in the eu, which shows a slight increase in employment, a slight recovery in the economy and a decreasing risk of a banking collapse in most member states. the specific recommendations, which address key areas such as public finances, competitiveness and growth, are showing beneficial effects. however, the employment performance is still poor, as a consequence of other policies. i therefore believe that there is a lot of room for improvement. i believe that the emphasis should be on the internal market and above all on the social dimension. supporting growth and jobs must remain a priority, as must strengthening the emu pillar and completing the banking union. the strengthening of the banking system will have a positive impact on both growth and employment. it will make it easier for citizens, and especially small and mediumsized enterprises, to access credit. in times of crisis such as the present one, in addition to macroeconomic objectives, care must be taken not to neglect priority objectives such as growth and development.
in writing. − the european semester, first introduced in 2011, aims to strengthen the economic governance of the european union through greater coordination of national economic policies, both fiscal and structural reform. this is a cycle of intensive economic cooperation between the european institutions and the member states, at the end of which the commission sends the latter specific recommendations, thus guiding their economic policy priorities and objectives. in this respect, european union coordination plays a very important role in bringing this long period of economic stagnation to an end and in reviving growth. however, much remains to be done. credit to enterprises (especially small and medium-sized enterprises) has not yet been fully restored, with negative repercussions on the real economy and employment. the revitalisation of competitiveness - based on innovation, human capital, scientific knowledge and the digitalisation of the economy - still requires a great deal of effort and must be a key driver in the european coordination of national economic policies. unemployment, especially among young people, has reached alarming levels. i therefore voted in favour of this report, which calls on the council and the commission to pay greater attention to this and to make greater efforts in this direction.
in writing. the report voted on today concerns the implementation of the priorities for 2013 under the european semester for economic policy coordination. parliament took note of the specific recommendations proposed by the european commission and adopted by the council for each member state: the common element in all the recommendations is the call on the member states to manage their public accounts properly, in pursuit of balanced budgets. the commission's view, shared by the rapporteur, is that the rules on fiscal discipline, accompanied by policies for employment, competitiveness and growth, are bearing fruit and that therefore the states must commit themselves to complying with the eu directives.
in writing. − significant differences in access to finance tend to accentuate internal divergences within the eu and the euro area in particular and create distortions of the internal market with unfair conditions of competition. while the consolidation of banks' portfolios is certainly an essential condition, the negative economic outlook only partially justifies these restrictive credit restrictions, especially for the most vulnerable recipients, such as young couples, small entrepreneurs, artisans, families who do not make it to the end of the month, the disabled. the application of the new prudential rules and banking sector practices in the financing of the real economy, in particular with regard to economically efficient smes, needs to be monitored more closely. in this regard, we recognise the important role that innovative new financial instruments can play in various european programmes and cohesion policy in terms of promoting public and private investment and we urge the commission to ensure legal clarity and transparency in the implementation of the new financial instruments in a timely manner and before the start of the 2014-2020 programming period.

in writing. - i welcome this report, much has been done in recent years to respond to the pressing challenges posed by the financial sector and sovereign debt crisis, with the aim of paving the way for a return to sustainable growth and employment, despite the many uncertainties in financial markets. however, the projected stagnation in economic activity in 2013 and unacceptably high unemployment levels show how crucial it is to accelerate efforts to support growth as a matter of priority, and in the meantime to achieve a growth-friendly fiscal consolidation. the european council, after a broad debate on the economic and social situation, set out the guidelines for the economic policies of the member states and of the european union in 2013, in particular: growth and employment. particular priority should be given to supporting youth employment and promoting growth and competitiveness.
in writing. − according to the international organisation for migration, since 1993, more then 20 000 persons died at sea. i believe that lampedusa should be a turning point for europe and that the only way to prevent another tragedy is to adopt a coordinated approach based on solidarity and responsibility, with the support of common instruments. the eu should do everything possible to save the lives of people in danger. for this reason with this resolution we welcome the intention of the european commission to establish a task force on the issue of migratory flows in the mediterranean. in addition the eu must continue to offer humanitarian, financial and political assistance in crisis areas in north africa and the middle east in order to tackle migration and humanitarian pressures at their root cause. but most of all, the member states must respect the principle of non-refoulement, in compliance with existing international and eu law. also, countries like italy, greece and spain must immediately put an end to any improper and extended detention practices in violation of international law.
in writing. - do not be fooled by those who are enthusiastic, unknowingly, about the adoption by the european parliament of a resolution on the need to "review or amend laws punishing those who help migrants" (which is not at all a denial of the bossi law). for two good reasons: 1) the bossi law does not punish those who help migrants at all, so much so that it has actually increased the penalties for those who organise the smuggling of illegal immigrants; the ep's resolutions have an effect comparable to water running on marble... 2) do not be deceived: we will defend the bossi law to the death, because we consider it the last bulwark against the invasion of illegal immigrants in italy and europe. once again rai news readily joins the immigration "vulgate", giving immediate air to the false news that the resolution would condemn the bossi immigration law: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to the full.

in writing. - the european parliament, in its collegiate nature, has expressed its solidarity with the victims of the tragedies suffered by migrants and has proposed political solutions to put an end to this barbarity. as an italian, but above all as a person of common sense, i could only vote in favour. two points, however, are worth noting: the first is that solutions cannot come from resolutions like this, which have no legislative value, but from the action that the competent institutions will take on these statements. the second is about a huge misunderstanding i read in the papers: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the fishermen in the fishing fleet are protected from the risk of being caught by the fishermen in the fishing fleet. in fact, since the law in question contains no such reference, no one has dreamed of interfering with italian sovereignty in the management of immigration.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution because it is the first time that there is talk of sharing responsibility between member states in the management of immigrants and this is very important for italy. unfortunately, today's vote in italy is being exploited by the left as the motion calls for "modifying or revising any regulations that impose sanctions on those who provide assistance at sea". the bossi-fini act was immediately attacked gratuitously and without justification. i would remind you that the bossi-fini act does not provide for any sanctions against persons who rescue migrants in distress at sea. the bossi-fini is a cause of shipwrecks because sailors fear being prosecuted for encouraging illegal immigration. this is political speculation on the lives of hundreds of desperate people and an attempt to weaken a law without which we would be at the mercy of unscrupulous pirates and smugglers.
in writing. - the need for a european-wide strategy to tackle the problem of migration flows in the mediterranean has been widely supported by myself and my italian colleagues. the recent tragedy in lampedusa, which saw 320 migrants die at sea, should be a turning point in our being genuinely european, not just in words but in action! only a coordinated approach based on common instruments and the principles of solidarity and responsibility-sharing can make a difference: there's a lot of work to be done on that. the creation of a task force on the problem of migration flows in the mediterranean, which considers both political and operational issues, can be a first step. the financial strengthening of existing common instruments, such as the frontex agency, which coordinates member states in the control of external borders, and the european asylum support office, is another priority. in addition, in the long term, the union and the member states should review visa policy and labour immigration legislation and conclude agreements with the countries of transit of migrants, in order to ensure respect for the fundamental rights of migrants themselves and to prevent them from falling into the hands of traffickers.
in writing. − i note with satisfaction that this joint resolution makes an explicit reference to article 80 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu), which reads as follows: 'the union's policies referred to in this chapter (i.e. policies relating to border controls, asylum and immigration) and their implementation shall be governed by the principle of solidarity and fair sharing of responsibility between member states, including in financial terms. where necessary, union acts adopted pursuant to this chapter shall contain appropriate measures to give effect to this principle. "any other comment would be superfluous, to indicate that all this has been completely ignored in all these years, which have seen thousands of people arrive on our shores, without the slightest intervention by the european union, and without the slightest solidarity from our supposed partners. i do not want to go into the political instrumentalisation of the bossi-fini act, whose objectives, in my view, are profoundly justified: i would rather see europe, which is always ready to appeal to the rules and the treaties, really committing itself to respecting what has been established in this area with the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon.

in writing. - it is good not to confuse the questions: the swift agreement is a great tool in the fight against international terrorism, and cooperation between the two largest economies in the world, the us and the eu, is necessary to achieve this fundamental objective. the other is the spying by the nsa, which has not yet been fully clarified, and i would therefore be much more cautious in assessing it. what i want, and what is voted for, is respect for the laws applicable in europe while remaining partners in this battle which is so important to us.
in writing. − in the summer of 2013, the libe committee was tasked with carrying out an inquiry into alleged mass spying activities carried out by the national security agency (nsa) against european citizens. the results of the investigation were rather poor: we have, however, been able to verify that these nsa activities have been carried out with legal cover under us and international law. the commission and europol have also clarified that there is no reason to believe that the united states has failed to comply with the provisions of the swift agreement, which governs the transfer of banking data to the united states in the context of the fight against terrorism. a suspension of this treaty by the european union would therefore have no real and proven justification at this time.
in writing. − the agreement between the european union and the united states of america on the processing and transfer of financial messaging data from the european union to the united states for the purposes of the terrorist financial transaction tracking program (hereinafter referred to as 'the agreement') entered into force on 1 august 2010. according to press releases in recent days, the us national security agency (nsa) has allegedly had direct access to the it systems of several private companies and to financial messaging concerning financial transfers and related data through an international financial messaging service provider currently subject to the agreement. as the eu's main objective is to promote individual freedoms, security measures, including anti-terrorism measures, must be pursued through the rule of law and must be subject to fundamental rights obligations, including those relating to privacy and data protection. we therefore believe that any transfer of personal data must comply with union and member state law and fundamental rights obligations, including those relating to privacy and data protection.

in writing. − in the current difficult economic environment, the promotion of environmental protection policies may seem to be a secondary objective, if not an obstacle to growth and competitiveness. environmental action, of course, sometimes involves very high costs, but it also creates benefits that neither public finance nor private investors can ignore. in this light, we need environmental policies that provide a clear and transparent legal framework that enables economic operators to reap these benefits, thereby becoming true catalysts of 'eco-innovation', generating efficiency, competitiveness, growth and jobs, with cross-cutting benefits across many industrial sectors. the seventh environment action programme (eap), by integrating the objectives of environmental policy with all the other sectoral policies of the european union, is geared in this direction and has therefore found my favourable vote. growth and competitiveness on the one hand and environmental protection on the other can no longer travel on separate tracks. we owe it to future generations, to our children, who, like us, claim the right to live in harmony with the natural environment while maintaining future levels of consumption and well-being no lower than today's.
in writing. - i don't think there are people in this room who don't care about the environment: we all live on the same planet, and i believe that we all want to protect it. but what sets me apart from the environmental fundamentalists is that i have a broader vision, open to multiple perspectives: the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of the environment is a very important one, and it is not enough to simply assess environmental measures without taking due account of the possible impacts they may have on everything around them, starting with the economic and social sphere. there is another question to consider: the european union is a very important player on the world stage, and i wonder why it is not able to impose minimum environmental standards on its external partners, starting with the new giants in the making, china for example. if we do not act globally, it is basically useless to insist on internal measures, sometimes just but sometimes perhaps too extreme. if we really care about the environment, we must make this principle of defence, protection and exploitation apply everywhere: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the environment is protected, and that the environment is protected in the community.
in writing. the european parliament, in plenary session, voted this morning on a report by mr franco on the proposal for a european parliament and council decision on a general union action programme on the environment up to 2020. in the current context of economic crisis and austerity, focusing on environmental policies can be perceived as an obstacle to economic growth and employment. overcoming this dualistic vision and moving towards an approach that effectively combines environmental and economic concerns is the union's key challenge, which is to promote the principles of sustainable development, 'smart' consumption and 'green' growth in the action programme. this requires a great deal of legislative and policy effort, from the development of adequate, coherent and scientifically sound environmental legislation to the creation of international environmental governance, in which the union is the guide and reference point not only for third countries and member states but also for community citizens, to whom educational and information initiatives are addressed to strengthen their commitment to the environment. for these reasons, i cannot deny my support for a resolution which seeks to reconcile the complex relationship between economic activities and environmental protection.

in writing. - the current legislative framework on basic safety standards against the dangers of exposure to ionising radiation - which has developed over a rather long period of time since the euratom treaty of 1957 - is now somewhat outdated or inconsistent. the proposal for a council directive to update and rationalise existing legislation will allow for more effective and timely application of health safety standards against the dangers arising from ionising radiation to workers, patients and other individuals exposed to this type of radiation. that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. - the report by mr ulmer on the dangers of exposure to ionizing radiation and the council proposal on this subject were voted on today in plenary. the council proposal, based on article 31 of the euratom treaty, merges the medical exposure directive, the directive on the control of high-activity sealed radioactive sources (hass directive), the directive on outdoor workers and the directive on information to the public with the directive on basic standards (96/29/euratom). the objectives of the recast are to eliminate contradictions between existing legislative provisions, to improve protection against exposure to ionising radiation and to integrate the latest scientific information and experience on radiation protection into existing legislation. the commission has also proposed that the directive on basic standards should include natural radiation for the first time in order to ensure better protection for the general public. however, the planned registration obligations may generate conflicts of objectives with regard to landfills in relation to the disposal of different radioactive substances. to prevent this from happening, it would be appropriate to amend the requirements for naturally occurring radioactive materials.
in writing. - i gave a favourable opinion on the proposal for a council directive laying down basic safety standards for protection against the dangers arising from exposure to ionising radiation because i believe that protection, especially for workers who are in close contact with ionising radiation, must be increased, subject to continuous checks and the introduction of ever more advanced safety standards. one of the aims of the recast is to eliminate contradictions between the existing legislative provisions. a further objective of the proposal is to incorporate the latest scientific information and experience in the field of radiation protection into existing legislation. in this respect, euratom legislation has always followed the scientific recommendations of the international commission on radiological protection (icrp). in addition, for the first time, natural radiation is to be included in the framework of the basic standards directive in order to ensure better protection for the general public. as regards medical exposure, minor changes are introduced to avoid duplication of work on medical devices emitting ionising radiation.
in writing. the proposal voted today for the recast of the council's basic standards directive is a further step towards improving protection against exposure to ionising radiation. one of the aims of the recast is to eliminate contradictions between the existing legislative provisions. the proposal has largely succeeded in its aim and consequently few changes are necessary in this respect. many of the aspects of radiation protection covered by the basic standards directive are working very well in practice; this is a finding which in turn indicates the need not to make excessive changes. a further objective of the proposal is to incorporate the latest scientific information and experience in the field of radiation protection into existing legislation. in this respect, euratom legislation has always followed the scientific recommendations of the international commission on radiological protection (icrp). the latter, in its 2007 publication 103, recommended that the changes to the existing radiation protection system now considered in the proposed directive be made.

the council, opens a new phase in european policies aimed at protecting and enhancing cultural and linguistic diversity and promoting the tangible and intangible cultural heritage, but also at making the european cultural and audiovisual industry more competitive. a balance between these two aspects is strongly desired by parliament, in the name of the dual nature of culture, which is an intrinsic value but also an economic sector, without which growth will be neither intelligent, nor inclusive, nor sustainable. in the wake of the most severe economic crisis since the second world war, culture, creativity, together with education and research, are finally becoming central to the 2014-20 programming as the only programmes to increase compared to the overall cut of 40 billion practiced by the council. in creative europe, cultural and creative enterprises, which were the subject of the 2011 green paper, are given full legitimacy as drivers of innovation and skilled employment, especially among young people. over 1 million businesses, 6 million employees, a share of between 5 and 7% of european gdp. the challenge of the digital shift, which has changed the entire chain of production, distribution and consumption of culture, from design to audiovisual, is fully recognised. the programme's focus is broadened from the creative to the value chain, from the development of the work to its promotion, to international circulation, but with an eye to the public, those european citizens who recent eurobarometer research indicates are increasingly distanced from the enjoyment and practice of cultural products and services, and not only for economic constraints. the sectors which have been effectively supported over the last twenty years by three separate european programmes - media, media mundus and culture - are brought together in a single programme but, thanks also to the work of parliament, retain their autonomy in terms of brand, budget and specific measures, while also taking in the cross-sectoral strand in which we have better defined the new financial guarantee instrument, entrusted to the eif, which will support grants and support loans from national financial institutions on the basis of portfolios specifically identified for these sectors, thus encouraging greater availability and expertise of the european credit system over the next seven years. the challenges faced by the cultural, creative and audiovisual sectors are common to the 14 sectors included in creative europe and are market fragmentation, undercapitalisation, lack of comparable data, digitalisation and audience development. creative europe helps to address these issues and initiates solutions in the light of a european added value that empowers businesses and broadens the opportunities for our artists and creatives and their works and circulation. at eur 1 462 million, the programme is up 9%. we would have liked a bigger increase, but it's a good sign. however, we must add to these funds the resources which, thanks to parliament, can be allocated to cultural heritage and creativity by the cohesion policies of horizon 2020, confirming that culture is not just a sector but a cross-cutting resource. i would particularly like to stress that the whole programme is open to participation by countries in the free trade area and the neighbourhood and by third countries through bilateral agreements. i would like to point out that support for cinema and audiovisual media and all forms of multimedia is also possible, as is the support for works produced by television in collaboration with independent producers, especially documentaries, children's programmes and animation. in culture, particular attention will also be paid to non-profit organisations and support will be given to platforms and networks to support the european circulation of works, as well as audiovisual education, including through film and video libraries, and the acquisition of skills for operators and the access of young people and underrepresented groups to the cultural heritage of europe. in conclusion, i thank my shadow colleagues, and i recall the dear departed colleague mr bisky, and the draftsmen of the opinions, mr göncz, mr matera and mr ţicău, who contributed to my work with their discussions and proposals, which was voted on almost unanimously by the committee on culture. i also thank the commissioner, the commission and also the directors-general of the dg for culture and the irish and lithuanian presidencies for the good work they have done together. i hope that in this way a new europe will be born more on the basis of a cultural and political project than on the basis of an economic and financial one.
mr president, many citizens and many associations often ask me whether there is a tool in europe to help protect and promote cultural diversity, the possibility of strengthening the competitiveness of the cultural and creative sectors in order also to promote the objectives set and set for ourselves in the europe 2020 strategy. or they ask me whether the european union can in any way support the capacity of the european cultural and creative sectors to operate also at transnational level, to promote the circulation of works and cultural and creative workers, to strengthen the financial capacity of the cultural sectors and of the small and mediumsized enterprises and organisations operating in this sector. i can assure these citizens and associations today that the answer is yes. the instrument exists and is called 'creative europe', the programme we will be adopting tomorrow which invests in this sector, including an increase in the budget. this is the right thing to do, considering that it is cultural enterprises that are the most dynamic, the least affected by the crisis and the ones that offer job opportunities.
mr president, commissioner, the excellent work of mrs costa allows the commission to look again at the development of this programme, which is very important for many reasons, as has been mentioned. culture has an economic value too and in a difficult time like this it is good not to forget that. but culture is above all the identity of peoples and must therefore be recognized as a means of enhancing differences and drawing all the benefits that can be derived from this. i think it is important for that reason to dwell for a moment on a point which the rapporteur has raised, namely the training of the public. we must not assume that access to cultural activities is automatic and that everyone has this tendency. so we have to think about a training path that starts from the levels of school training for the youngest up to the whole life of people in such a way ... member of the commission. − mr president, once again i would like to thank very warmly the rapporteur of this programme, silvia costa, the co-rapporteurs and all of you who have been involved. you have supported the ambition of the commission’s proposal from the very beginning and left your own imprint on the new programme. i am happy to see that parliament shares the commission’s vision of the importance of culture in the creative sectors for both the well-being of our societies and for the generation of growth and jobs. thanks to creative europe we will be able to fund artists and cultural professionals to work across borders and reach new audiences. i would of course be much happier if the original proposal for a 37% increase to the budget had been accepted by the european council, but i think in these times of austerity we have to be satisfied with a small increase rather than a decrease. without financial support it would be difficult for our artists to break into new markets. that is why creative europe brings a real european added value. cultural diversity lies at the very heart of the european idea. creative europe will support the people and the organisations who shape and renew that diversity. that is why the programme deserves your full support and i thank you in advance for that.

vice-president of the commission. − mr president, together we have achieved a fundamental reform in the way infrastructure is funded and managed in the union. i am very pleased with the result of this work, undertaken together with the council and member states. the new eu infrastructure policy will put in place a powerful european network across 28 member states to promote growth and competitiveness. it will connect east with west and replace today’s patchwork with a network that is genuinely european. with the new ten-t regulation we have a strong legal basis on which to implement our vision of a core network, connecting the main nodes of the eu, to be realised by 2030 and complying with technical standards allowing ships, trains and trucks to run freely throughout eu territory. the core network corridor structures, under the leadership of the european coordinators, will be powerful tools for realising this ambition. my particular thanks go to the rapporteurs, mr koumoutsakos and mr ertug, who have been strong defenders of the methodology for establishing the maps. this approach has allowed the emphasis to remain on eu added value, on the cross-border sections and on missing links. the infrastructure plan in the transport sector – like the energy plan, and the telecommunications plan still under discussion – will improve infrastructure planning and preparation. eu financial assistance will enable these plans to be implemented. the connecting europe facility (cef) constitutes a novel approach. the european parliament, and especially the three rapporteurs, ms ayala sender, ms vălean and mr riquet, have been instrumental in safeguarding and improving this essential feature of the cef. i would like to thank them for that. the ambition and the focus of the proposals have been retained. in the field of transport, this means an emphasis on the core network, on cleaner modes of transport and on higher co-funding rates for cross-border projects and interoperability. in the field of energy, financial assistance under the cef will continue to support studies and, for the first time, will make a concrete difference in enabling highly-beneficial electricity transmission lines, gas pipelines, liquid natural gas terminals and energy storage facilities that could not otherwise be built to go ahead. the financial support under the cef will complement the measures on accelerated permission procedures and regulatory solutions provided under the new ten-e guidelines to speed up energy infrastructure development, allowing the union to reap the full benefit of market integration and ensure high standards of supply security while making the energy system more sustainable. in telecommunications, given the decision by the european council, we modified our proposal for telecoms guidelines, in may. good progress has now been made in trialogues, along the lines of our modified proposal. this means making the most of a scarce budget, in both cross-border digital services and broadband infrastructure. despite difficult discussions on financial instruments, and especially on project bonds, we now have the tools necessary to build an environment conducive to private investment and to develop instruments that will be attractive for specialised infrastructure investors. financing for transport infrastructure will triple for the period 2014-2020 to eur 26 billion. this eu funding will be tightly focused on the core transport network, where there is most eu added value, and we will prioritise east-west connections. after the european energy programme for recovery, which dedicated eur 2.4 billion to energy infrastructure, the cef now clearly triples the budget for energy transmission projects. in addition, the possibility of developing and using innovative financial instruments in the field of energy infrastructure projects will make the spending even more efficient and the financial leverage even greater. the adoption of the cef is the start of a new policy based on truly european infrastructure funding.
the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial interests are protected. - mr commissioner, i would like to draw your attention to a specific point. i agree with what has already been said, namely that in the network we are discussing, the corridors are one of the most important, if not the most significant, points. the governance of the corridors and the role of the coordinators in this area are very sensitive and of the utmost importance. our decisions on the implementation of projects depend very much on the ability to connect the european union, the member states and local realities. the relationship with the latter is changing from a different and stronger role for coordinators, who are assigned the task of organising the discussion with civil society. all too often we face strong resistance from the territories and the citizens simply because we have not confronted them before. the early comparison is in itself an important democratic value which the coordinators can solve.

in writing. − i have chosen to support the proposal for a regulation on the multiannual financial framework 2014/2020, albeit a modest one. despite the fact that the eu budget has been reduced, i believe that the proposal is appropriate in the context of the economic crisis and the need for greater financial discipline. the regulation has a number of positive aspects: flexibility on commitment and payment appropriations; a clear definition of the principle of the unity of the eu budget; the safeguarding of outstanding payments for 2013; the establishment of a high-level group aimed at a more judicious use of eu resources; the commission has also taken a number of measures to promote employment, innovation and research. i welcome the increase in the appropriations allocated to achieving the objectives of horizon 2020 and the introduction of the cosme programme, which is designed to support smes. the agreement also provides for a high degree of flexibility in the commitment appropriations, both between one year and the next and between the different categories of expenditure, which is necessary to ensure a more efficient use of resources, especially in view of the reduction in budgets. the inclusion of the 'revision clause' will make it possible to modify the distribution of resources according to needs. the new mff is balanced, robust and sustainable.

in writing. − the european union has, since its inception, provided itself with the means to achieve its objectives and to carry out its policies. it therefore provides for a budget based on transparency and fairness, financed entirely from own resources. we welcome the recommendation on the draft rules on the multiannual financial plan, which was discussed today. in this time of financial instability, there is an increasing need for specific instruments to enable the european union to cope with unforeseen events or to finance aid, such as the emergency reserve or the fight against youth unemployment. it is also necessary to regulate any situations which may require the adjustment or revision of the multiannual financial framework, such as those relating to the implementation of the budget, the revision of the treaties, possible enlargements or the reunification of cyprus. specific provisions should therefore be adopted providing for the possibility of budgeting commitment appropriations beyond the limits of the previously fixed ceilings. as we are aware of the particularly difficult situation in which member states are currently paying, a review of the allocations for the years 2017-2020 will be necessary in 2016, which may see the application of the method of allocating resources on the basis of the statistics available at that time.
in writing. − after lengthy negotiations between the council, parliament and the commission, an agreement was finally reached on the adoption of the budget for the multiannual financial framework 2014-2020. the vote just taken underlines how the eu is working on the problems of employment, growth, sustainable development, cohesion and solidarity. funding has been increased for education and exchange programmes, solidarity funds for natural disasters, youth policies and the integration of young people into the labour market. the appropriations foreseen for the multiannual financial framework 2014-2020 are almost eur 4 billion for commitments and eur 900 million for payments.
in writing. − more measures have to be taken in order to improve the economic and social situation in europe, especially for the member states that have suffered most from the crisis. it is necessary to facilitate the budgetary process, optimise the allocation of investments and the use of special financial instruments and promote effective economic governance. i support the position of the rapporteurs in this regard, and i voted in favour of the multiannual financial framework.
in writing. − the european parliament has worked hard to reach agreement with the council and the commission on the multiannual financial framework 2014-2020. the agreement also provides for flexibility, allowing the appropriations not used to be used to cover expenditure for the following period, which will be directed mainly to combating youth unemployment. more funds will also be allocated to horizon 2020, which aims to stimulate research and innovation, erasmus and cosme, the programme for the competitiveness of european small and medium-sized enterprises. a review of the multiannual financial plan is also planned, to be held in 2016 at the latest, to allow the new parliament to adapt it to the changing economic environment. i voted in favour because i believe that any further delay in the adoption of the new multiannual financial framework would be politically irresponsible, since it would threaten the continuity of european programmes at an economic time when cohesion and consistency are essential for the growth of the union.
in writing. − after months of difficult negotiations, the eu budget for 2014-2020 was finally approved today. it is important to emphasize that in the agreement reached last june parliament had already ensured that its main priorities, such as flexibility in the transfer of unpaid funds and expenditure commitments, would be respected. this flexibility is intended to ensure that eu budget funds are used in situations where the need is greatest, especially in anticipation of the decrease in annual budgets. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover the whole of the eu.
in writing. − on 27 june 2013, a political agreement was reached on the multiannual financial framework 2014-2020 and the new interinstitutional agreement. the agreement was formalised by the council at its extraordinary coreper meeting on 28 june. despite the long and difficult negotiations in the council and at interinstitutional level, i believe it is necessary that the new instruments, in particular flexibility, should be used in the course of future budgetary procedures, not only to deal with emergencies such as youth unemployment or aid provided for under the eu solidarity fund and the european globalisation adjustment fund, but also for transfers between and within headings to encourage the full use of the funds available. in addition, the transparency and democratic nature of the whole budgetary negotiation process must be guaranteed, starting with respect for the legislative and budgetary powers conferred on parliament by the treaty of lisbon.
