in writing. − the recent economic crisis severely harmed employment in comunidad valenciana in spain. the unemployment rate in the region increased rapidly, rising from 9.61 % in the first quarter of 2008 to 29.19 % in the first quarter of 2013. the number of available jobs in nace revision 2 division 23 in comunidad valenciana decreased by almost 40 % from 2008 to 2011. the european globalisation adjustment fund has been created in order to provide additional assistance to workers suffering from the consequences of major structural changes in world trade patterns. tackling the issue of unemployment in comunidad valencia qualifies for the mobilisation of this fund. the proposed funding package includes such measures for the reintegration of 300 workers into employment as training and job-search assistance, as well as outplacement incentives and support for setting up a business. therefore, i voted in favour of it.

in writing. − the agreement on government procurement (apa) is an international, legally binding agreement on access to government procurement markets dating back to 1994 and is therefore, in most cases, limited to developed economies. we therefore agree with the recommendation put forward by mr scholz, because it makes significant improvements to the main text by extending the current membership of the wto to other countries. for the citizens of these countries, public procurement is a key instrument for stimulating employment, economic activity and promoting high standards of environmental protection and decent working conditions. it is therefore essential that the revision of the public procurement agreement is fair and redefines the award rules, promoting greater clarity and transparency. in addition, it will be important not only to establish modern award procedures such as electronic procurement, but above all to demonstrate that the benefits of such procedures outweigh the administrative costs. this will be a positive sign and will help to increase legal certainty and the fight against corruption in third countries.
in writing. - i voted in favour of approving this agreement on public procurement, which should cover, in addition to the eu, 15 contracting countries, including the united states, canada, israel, korea and japan, and 10 others currently listed as 'observers' involved in accession negotiations, such as china. the european union is certainly one of the most open markets in this area, which unfortunately cannot be said for most of its trade and economic partners. these new rules should ensure greater transparency and openness, towards what i have been calling for for some time, namely measures to ensure full reciprocity. if we give others the opportunity to participate in public tenders on our markets, the same opportunity should be given to our companies that decide to participate in those markets. unfortunately, the reality today is far from that, but i hope that we will be able to incorporate these principles of fairness more and more in all the agreements that the european union is committed to concluding.
in writing. − the agreement on government procurement (gpa) is a legally-binding international agreement which requires parties to guarantee transparency of procedures and equal treatment of bidders and not discriminate between domestic and bidders of other gpa parties. in many countries outside the gpa region, the government and state-controlled agencies are the biggest purchasers of goods of all kinds. hence, i voted for the proposal to expand membership of gpa to these countries, which will allow competitive european investors to enter certain foreign markets with less discrimination and trade barriers.

in writing. − in june 1987, the first network between european universities was launched, allowing students to spend a period of study abroad, recognised in their curriculum. in that year, 3,244 students were involved in the exchange: today, three million people are expected to move. there is no doubt that this program has been a great success. it has enabled university students to study in other countries, to learn their languages, to confront other systems of life, to mingle with their peers. the erasmus experience takes on the meaning of an open worksite, in which a common culture is built from below: the european commission has recently published a report on the implementation of the european year of the environment. and it's mostly built by young people. it will take time to achieve cultural union. but it is only in the field of education, of shared education, that the consciousness of a common european citizenship can be born. and so, perhaps in the not too distant future, the power of ideas developed through the exchanges of erasmus will give a soul to europe and make it less fragile. i am voting in favour of the following report, and i welcome the commission's intention to reduce the fragmentation and overlapping of the current programmes.
in writing. − the european parliament adopted today the erasmus+ programme, which represents a major milestone for european cooperation in the fields of education, youth, culture and sport. the most interesting news is that of sports: the commission will also be able to use the financial resources of the european union to support the implementation of the union's policy on the environment and sustainable development. this will enable millions of amateur sportsmen and women to travel, train, play and meet athletes within the eu countries.

in writing. - the report deals with a number of central issues in the common market and competitiveness policies, and my vote in favour is reinforced by the awareness that our individual countries risk losing ground if they fail to take advantage of the added value inherent in integration processes. the comparison with the white paper on growth signed by jacques delors 20 years ago is illuminating. the infrastructure backlog compared with the 1990s was estimated at some 70 billion for hard infrastructure alone in italy. on the other hand, the digital divide is becoming more and more topical. italy has 22 broadband connections per 100 inhabitants, below the eu average; the electronic transactions with public administrations are literally off the charts, with an additional cost per capita of more than eur 4000; the latest report of the un commission places italy in 57th place in the ranking for the use of the internet for information, entertainment and e-commerce activities. according to some estimates, doubling the average speed of connections would be enough to gain half a point of gdp. the provisions of this regulation, which allow for action to be taken through rationalization, integration and simplification, are therefore appropriate.
in writing. - i voted in favour because the cef will be the key eu financial instrument for the trans-european transport network. the cef will finance three types of european infrastructure: transport, energy and telecommunications, which are the basic sectors of the european single market. the cef provides for significant investments in modern, durable and effective mechanisms and infrastructure, which are essential for achieving the europe 2020 objectives and sustainable economic growth. the cef is therefore a crucial and strategic instrument in the multiannual financial framework 2014-2020, especially with regard to investments in growth and jobs, aimed at a definitive exit from the current economic crisis. by focusing on digital networks, intelligent, sustainable and interconnected transport networks, it will make a major contribution to the completion of the european single market. the cef provides for a greater concentration of financial support towards projects with eu added value, the exploitation of cross-sectoral synergies, a greater emphasis on the use of innovative financial instruments and greater flexibility in the allocation of funds. the report will insist on funding in particular energy isolation projects, the elimination of bottlenecks towards the completion of the internal energy market and the deployment of the world's fastest broadband by 2020.
in writing. - this proposal for a regulation is one of the best answers to the anti-europeanists: the articulation of this mechanism is in fact a good compromise between the need to create infrastructure to restart the economy in europe, the need to identify priority areas in which to invest in times of crisis in order to be better prepared for a world which, in these years, continues to change, and the obligation to ensure the economic and environmental sustainability of our economic model. the mechanism also makes it possible to exploit the synergies that can and must be created between states which pool their resources to think over a longer horizon. i congratulate the rapporteurs and the whole team who worked on this dossier, for which i voted in favour.
in writing. - we have today adopted in plenary the report on the proposal for a regulation on transeuropean links. the connecting europe facility (cef) programme will aim to accelerate financing for the completion of transport, energy and telecommunications infrastructure, thereby improving the mobility of citizens, goods and services across the european union. it is important to emphasise that this project will aim to create increasingly reliable, robust and efficient transport systems, making them globally competitive and eliminating the mosaics of national approaches that currently exist. for this reason, the european union and its institutions should cooperate synergistically, reinforcing their ambitions in relation to major infrastructure projects such as the ten-t (trans-european transport by road, water, air and rail) multimodal core network, as they will not only contribute to improving economic, social and territorial cohesion but above all because they will promote the increase in employment levels in all eu member states.

madam president, transport is a crucial element for the european economy and it will not be able to grow and prosper without efficient and quality transport networks. i have therefore strongly supported from the outset the project to create the new ten-t network, a transport network with high european added value capable of upgrading existing infrastructure and facilitating the mobility of citizens and goods throughout the union. i believe that the main challenge of the new network is the need to ensure adequate connectivity to all regions of europe, including island regions such as sardinia, which were initially excluded from the core network. for this reason, the contribution to the dossier was directed from the outset to filling this regulatory gap in the commission's original proposal, so that island regions can also enjoy the benefits of the inclusion of their urban nodes. finally, i am pleased that my amendments to include sardinia in the central network have been accepted by the rapporteurs mr koumoutsakos and mr ertug, whom i thank for the excellent work they have done and for their excellent representation of the european parliament's position in the negotiations with the council.

in writing. - i voted in favour because the new agreement on eu infrastructure policy aims to create a genuine transeuropean transport network. today, the ten-t remains a patchwork of national networks: the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the draft directive on the protection of the environment in the event of a natural disaster. the proposal aims to make the network more accessible, efficient, intermodal and interoperable by linking the nodes which allow the exchange of different modes of transport, making better use of existing infrastructures and creating a more precise and binding framework for its practical and rapid implementation. the agreement provides for a core transport network to be established as a priority by 2030. this network will constitute a selection of the most important sections of the global network and will become the backbone for transport within the single market, directly contributing to its completion. the global network, which is to be completed by 2050, will cover the whole of the eu and be accessible to all, citizens and businesses.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this motion for a regulation. i am convinced that even in a crisis situation such as this, the european union must not give up thinking big and must continue to focus on the small measures needed in the short term and on the more far-reaching measures, without which there is no future. i particularly welcome the choice of the legal instrument, the regulation, which leaves no room for differences in transposition but obliges all member states, at the same time and in the same way, to adapt to ensure the achievement of the objectives set, among which i particularly appreciated interoperability, the use of renewable fuels and intermodality. i hope that the commission will monitor implementation and that all those concerned will be able to raise the necessary funds without further pressuring the citizens, who should only benefit from these measures.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the report by mr koumoutsakos and mr ertug because i think it addresses the current challenges of a significant delay in some eu territories in implementing ten-t projects, as well as their difficulty in financing projects in times of economic crisis. in this context, the port of augusta, the palermo-catania high-speed railway, the port and the airport of cagliari could be among the major sicilian and sardinian infrastructures which could be financed from community resources for the development of the transeuropean transport network ten-t. sicily, which is part of corridor 3 with italy, the scandinavian-mediterranean corridor, because it runs from helsinki to malta, must take advantage of the possibilities offered by european funds to improve internal mobility, and i hope that the italian, sicilian and sardinian governments will soon propose projects consistent with the measures envisaged by european programming, focusing on public-private partnership investments. of the €15 billion allocated for the eu as a whole, italy could be allocated a share of around €2.5 to €3 billion if it has a rapid design response capacity. this demonstrates the eu's attention to italy and in particular to sicily and sardinia, which are the eu's real strategic platforms in the mediterranean.
in writing. − the development and operation of transeuropean transport networks contribute to the achievement of important objectives such as the proper functioning of the internal market and the strengthening of economic and social cohesion. they also have the specific objective of enabling sustainable and unhindered mobility of people and goods, improving accessibility to all regions of the european union. that is why we are supporting today the report by mr koumoutsakos and mr ertug on the proposal for a regulation on the development of a transeuropean transport network, because good mobility is the backbone of a successful economy and an essential element for social cohesion and integration. a weak network would have a significant impact on the free movement of goods and people, so it will be essential to create a central and a global network that complement each other, so as to bring significant improvements to the functioning of the single market and ensure economic growth and mobility, which are fundamental to the quality of life, to the benefit of third countries as well. finally, once all costs and benefits, including social and environmental ones, have been considered, it will be essential to ensure a positive contribution to the well-being of all citizens of the european union.
in writing. − the trans-european transport network (ten-t) is one of the major projects that are indispensable to the functioning of single market, social cohesion and mobility of european citizens. however, many ten-t projects are forced to delay, facing difficulties in financing, a lack of coordination between different financing instruments, and insufficient information and statistics. in order to meet the challenges, the commission proposed to introduce a new methodology with common criteria for the whole network to integrate all regions equally and strengthen the reporting obligations for the member states through the interactive geological and technical information system and data from the european investment bank. as these approaches contribute to the promotion of ten-t, i therefore voted in favour of this proposal.
in writing. the transeuropean transport network is one of the focal points of the development of the common market: it ensures the mobility of citizens and contributes to the economic and social cohesion of the union. i voted in favour of this report because i believe it identifies the priorities for completing the transeuropean road, rail, water and air transport network: overcome the current fragmentation along national lines of the transport network, solve the problem of coordination of financing instruments at central and decentralised level and ensure the transparency of financing, in particular from the european funds and the european investment bank.
in writing. − the development of a trans-european transport network will facilitate the movement of goods and people and will reduce the peripheral location of some of the union's most deprived areas. the eu treaties aim to create a european internal market and to develop economic and social cohesion, and this single market, with the free movement of goods, people and services, requires efficient and modern infrastructure. the development of the trans-european transport network responds to this objective, as well as to ensure the interconnection and interoperability of national networks. in addition, the construction of trans-european networks is also seen as an important element of economic growth and employment. i therefore vote in favour.
in writing. − the trans-european transport network is one of the union's key projects and is of paramount importance for the mobility of european citizens, for social and territorial cohesion and for the economic and employment development of the member states. today's vote is particularly important because it proposes major changes to the current ten-t network layout to address problems such as a significant delay in the implementation of some projects, the lack of coordination between the different funding instruments, and the lack of information and statistics on the funding of some projects.
in writing. the commission proposal aims to rationalise the european statistical system. in particular, regulation (ec) no 223/2009 of the european parliament and of the council of 11 march 2009 on european statistics defines the european statistical system (ess) as a partnership between the european statistical authority, namely the commission (eurostat), and the national statistical institutes (nis) and other national authorities in each member state responsible for the development, production and dissemination of european statistics. as the rapporteur's proposals give more detail on the expiry of the commission's powers and bind the commission to an obligation to report to parliament, i voted in favour of the reports.
in writing. − this proposal represents a technical adjustment following a regulation adopted in 2011. it is therefore normal to follow up the full approval of the committee responsible by voting in favour.
in writing. - this proposal, for which i voted in favour, aims to amend the nine legislative acts in the field of agricultural and fisheries statistics in order to bring them into line with the new institutional framework. in this sense, the objective behind the proposal was to replace the regulatory procedure with the control procedure (rps) by means of delegated acts and to start a rationalisation of the european statistical system. as with the new common agricultural policy, further simplification and alignment of statistical collection tools with the new regulations will be beneficial for the analysis of data in the sector.
in writing. − the european commission has the power to adopt delegated acts for a period of five years or more (as from their entry into force) unless the european parliament or the council objects to such extension. we are opposed to the indefinite duration of the mandate, and we therefore support this proposal, which requires agreement between the various institutions. the nine legislative acts in the field of agricultural and fisheries statistics will need to be amended in order to adapt them to the new institutional context. the main objective will be to replace all provisions containing references to the regulatory procedure with scrutiny, concerning statistical surveys to be carried out in the dairy sector, the economic accounts of agriculture and the transmission of statistical data on fishery products landings in member states, by delegated acts in the nine existing legislative texts. in addition, the role and tasks of the european statistical system committee should be streamlined, since it should no longer be excluded from the study of statistical data relating to agriculture and fisheries in the exercise of its powers in support of the commission.
in writing. − statistics are critical to policy making and are among the major building-blocks upon which european policy-makers make decisions. the commission proposed to modify nine legislative acts related to agricultural and fishery statistics so that they fit better in the new institutional context. agricultural and fishery statistics specifically serve to help the commission exercise its power, assisted by the standing committee for agricultural statistics (scas). therefore, i voted in favour of this proposal to support the commission and improve the efficiency of european institutions.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mr groote's report, which i consider to be balanced and acceptable.
in writing. − the 1992 helsinki convention is an important instrument of cooperation between states aimed at preventing and controlling pollution of transboundary waterways and international lakes. the opening of the convention to all un member states is a great opportunity to extend cooperation on water and river basins around the world. i therefore voted in favour of this motion for a resolution calling for parliament to adopt the amendments to the helsinki convention necessary to transform it into a regulatory framework for global cooperation.
in writing. - we voted in favour of this report in order to ensure that the eu can proceed with the acceptance of the amendment providing for a comprehensive opening to the un convention. at the same time, the formal adoption by this house of this report allows non-eu countries to join the union. this is in the context of increasing cooperation on the protection and use of transboundary waterways and international lakes.
in writing. - we fully support the recommendation by mr groote on the proposal on the protection and use of transfrontier waterways and international lakes. we are convinced that the establishment of a framework for bilateral and multilateral cooperation initiatives aimed at preventing and controlling pollution of transboundary watercourses and the rational use of water by the countries of the united nations economic commission for europe (unece) is more necessary than ever. the aim must be to enable countries outside the unece region to become an integral part of it, in order to promote cooperation in the field of river basins throughout the world, particularly in those countries which are neighbouring, such as afghanistan, china, iran, and those which are located in central asia. it is therefore essential to be able to guarantee a global opening and access to the commission for all those countries which are interested in joining this multilateral cooperation project.
in writing. − the use and protection of international waterways and lakes and in border areas are also issues for the european union. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council and parliament on the subject of the environment. the text approved concerns in particular the acceptance of certain amendments to articles 25 and 26 of the helsinki convention on the protection and use of transboundary watercourses and international lakes. the amendments seek to extend the convention to countries outside the united nations economic commission for europe, so that they can jointly control and manage the same rivers and lakes that bathe countries that are sometimes far apart.
in writing. − the unece convention introduces a framework for bilateral or multilateral cooperation to prevent and control the pollution of transboundary watercourses and the rational use of water. amendments to this convention shall enter into force for the parties to the convention which have accepted it on the ninetieth day after the date on which two thirds of those parties have deposited with the depositary their instruments of acceptance of the amendment. in a resolution on the 6th world water forum adopted on 15 march 2012, the european parliament urged the commission to promote the entry into force of the amendments to the helsinki convention. according to the report, this proposal aims at extending the scope beyond the current unece countries. it is consistent to the interest of the union to improve cooperation by opening the convention globally to enable accession of non unece countries willing to do so, especially for the countries bordering the current unece region. considering the potential benefits, i voted in favour of this proposal.
in writing. - the report by mr groote on the helsinki convention on the protection and use of transboundary watercourses and international lakes, which aims to establish cooperation initiatives to prevent and control pollution of transboundary watercourses and to rationalise the use of water by the countries of the united nations economic commission for europe (unece), was discussed in the house today. the eu has been a party to the convention since 1995. in 2003, the intention was expressed to extend the scope of the convention to countries outside the unece region, through an amendment to articles 25 and 26; the eu has not yet accepted the amendment. in agreement with the rapporteur, it should be recalled that parliament had already expressed its position in a resolution on the sixth world water forum in march 2012, calling on the commission to promote the entry into force of amendments to the convention in order to broaden the scope of this instrument. in this way, the convention could ensure particular relevance for important neighbouring countries in the unece region, such as china, afghanistan and iran.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the remek report which proposes the adoption of an additional research programme for the iter (international thermonuclear experimental reactor) project 2014-2018, in order to demonstrate that fusion is a possible, safe, sustainable and economically viable future energy source for the eu.
in writing. − innovation in the development of innovative energy sources is essential to reduce dependence on fossil fuels, increase energy security and thus build a strong, competitive europe that is able to meet the important challenges of the future. by signing the convention establishing the international fusion energy organisation iter (which includes the eu, japan, russia, the usa, china, the republic of korea and india), europe has committed itself to hosting and leading the construction of the iter (international thermonuclear experimental reactor) project. it is estimated that by 2050 this project will have met a large part of the continent's electricity needs. in this context, the european union must carry forward its commitments with one voice and maintain its credibility with its international partners. this requires the resources to be made available to continue long-standing research and innovation projects and to reap the benefits in the future. for these reasons i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution which provides for the reintegration of the iter programme into the union's multiannual financial framework.
in writing. - in today's vote i voted in favour of the adoption of a supplementary research programme for the iter project. this programme is intended to demonstrate the importance of nuclear energy as a possible source of safe, environmentally friendly and sustainable energy, and in this sense i believe that a global restructuring of the union's activities should be considered.
in writing. − we support the report on the adoption of an additional research programme to support the iter project, as it is a unique design on a global scale, as it emphasises the development of fusion energy as a credible alternative for commercial production of energy with zero greenhouse gas emissions. nuclear fusion has the potential to make a significant contribution to the creation of a sustainable and secure energy supply in the coming decades. developing the necessary technology would make it possible to produce energy in a cost-effective and environmentally friendly way; the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's scientific and technological potential is not undermined by the fact that the community is not able to provide scientific and technological assistance to the developing countries. implementing this strategy will require a radical restructuring of the european union's merger activity, including governance and financing. this will require constant financial support for both mainstream projects and research and development in key areas. only in this way can significant cost reductions be achieved without compromising the overall scope of the projects themselves.
in writing. − the international thermonuclear experimental reactor (iter) is the largest tokamak ever constructed and an indispensable part of the next step on the road to fusion as a worldwide energy source. nuclear fusion can be a much safer source of energy than fission, because there is no chain reaction involved. given the strategic importance of the project, the eu should continue its involvement in the next programming period of the iter project. this proposal aims at providing sufficient funding for the project without endangering other critical research projects of the union; therefore, i voted in favour of it.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the skinner report on the research and training programme of the european atomic energy community. the text is very balanced and i believe that irrespective of whether a member state chooses to use nuclear energy or not, all member states can and should benefit from nuclear research and the european added value of the euratom framework.
in writing. the rapporteur rightly points out that whatever the energy policy decisions of individual member states, the union cannot afford to ignore the sector or to let the systems for advanced nuclear research and development be impoverished. this specific regulation, in its relationship with the horizon 2020 framework programme, crosses two fundamental areas, namely applied research and energy planning. the interdependence of these factors with the economic recovery is beyond question: if we look at the current recovery scenario in the united states, we will soon discover a direct link between the further increase in technology patents and the energy revolution brought about by the even politically counter-cultural assertion of shale gas and green coal production. our programmes do not set out the ambition of becoming, like the united states today, a net exporter of energy, but there are certainly clear commitments on the composition of the energy mix and the prospect of energy security. in this respect, it is vital to have an appropriate research sector, first of all in terms of human capital and technological leadership. in this sense, the suggestion of using erdf funds in districts with established 'champions' in the field of nuclear engineering is also interesting. i therefore vote in favour.
in writing. the euratom programme - one of the main building blocks of the community project in the 1950s - is still the most important research and development programme in the european union. over the years, atomic research has made important scientific advances with positive effects in many fields. for this reason, i believe that the integration of euratom into horizon 2020 will make it possible to exploit the existing synergies between the two programmes, avoid duplication of costs and promote the creation of a scientific and technological base necessary for europe's competitiveness and future. i therefore voted in favour of this motion for a resolution, which stresses, among other things, the need to rationalise the costs of the programme, improve the working conditions of researchers and, last but not least, increase the involvement of small and mediumsized enterprises.
in writing. − the research and training programme of the european atomic energy community is part of the horizon 2020 package. given that it is up to each individual member state to decide whether or not to use nuclear energy, i believe that in order to make an informed and conscious choice, everyone should benefit from the results of nuclear research and the european added value of the euratom framework. this is also to allow for an efficient use of resources for the promotion of excellence in the nuclear field.
in writing. − the horizon 2020 programme provides the european union with a range of research and innovation opportunities, including nuclear. this programme is based on three fundamental pillars, namely excellence in science, industrial leadership and the major societal challenges facing the union and its citizens. we therefore support the proposal for more research funding, which will bring considerable benefits to the whole of the european union in the future. it is necessary to maintain leadership in this area and to ensure that it is not compromised by excluding it from the multiannual financial framework. in addition, it is important to emphasise the importance of international cooperation in adopting and promoting appropriate security measures and to promote access for eu researchers. further emphasis should be placed on improving the situation of smes by ensuring their equal access to all innovative financing instruments for nuclear research and by relieving them of the high administrative burden. the european union is currently perceived as a leading region in fusion and fission competence; it is important that this status is not lost and can be used to attract new researchers and new investments.
in writing. − establishing the framework programme for research and innovation for the 2014-2020 period is of great importance for the union’s competitiveness. individual member states will benefit as a part of the european union from nuclear research and the added european value of the euratom framework, even if they choose not to use nuclear as a source of energy. while development of frontier science and technology is consistent with the union’s long term strategy, international co-operation should also be encouraged to ensure nuclear safety and security of research and training. as these important aspects are specified in the proposal, i voted in favour of it.
in writing. − the horizon 2020 programme provides the union with a number of opportunities in the field of research and innovation. this applies to nuclear research as well as to other aspects of research in the union. the contribution of nuclear researchers to all aspects of research in the union remains vital and therefore it is appropriate that nuclear research is also covered by horizon 2020. the three pillars of horizon 2020 are excellence in science, industrial leadership and the big societal challenges, objectives entrusted to the union and its citizens, all of which are reinforced by the inclusion of nuclear research and researchers. the exclusion of nuclear research from horizon 2020 would therefore undermine the achievement of these objectives by the union. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. - i support the krahmer report on the creation of an instrument for cooperation in the field of nuclear safety. i believe that it is essential to create coordinated action at international level in the field of nuclear safety, and this instrument is aimed at ensuring sufficient means for the union to promote strategic and human security by responding to the challenges in the field of nuclear safety, radiation protection and nuclear safeguards.
in writing. the tragic consequences of the explosion at the chernobyl nuclear power station in 1986 are still vivid in the collective memory. the world suddenly became aware of the serious health risks associated with nuclear power, and numerous research programs were launched to make the use of this energy source safer. the fukushima accident in 2011 reaffirmed the need for coordinated international action in the field of nuclear safety: it is clear that our security is tied in two ways to the security standards adopted by third countries. to that end, the european instrument for nuclear safety cooperation (insc) aims to ensure that the union, in its external action, is able to initiate concrete forms of cooperation and assistance with other countries. in particular, the union's international engagement will be directed towards ensuring a progressive approximation of existing regulation and a fruitful sharing of know-how in this field. for all these reasons, i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution.
in writing. − the challenges in the nuclear sector are changing very fast and some of the previous eu projects are now obsolete. that is why i voted in favour of this report, so that it can become a new european instrument for cooperation in the field of nuclear safety. an instrument to ensure strategic and human security by responding to the challenges in the field of nuclear safety, radiation protection and nuclear safeguards in third countries.
in writing. − the 1986 chernobyl accident highlighted the importance of nuclear safety worldwide, as did the 2011 fukushima daiichi accident, which confirmed that every reactor carries nuclear risks. it is therefore necessary to continue efforts to improve nuclear safety in order to achieve the highest standards reflecting the most advanced practices. that is why we are supporting the report on the proposal on nuclear safety today, because it is vital that the european atomic energy community is able to support it in third countries, eliminating the risks to the lives and health of the population. the consistency, coordination and complementarity of the european union's assistance in the field of nuclear safety will have to be ensured through the individual efforts of the member states and other international, regional and local organisations, in order to avoid overlaps and duplication of funding. specific objectives will need to be pursued, such as the promotion of a genuine nuclear safety culture and effective governance; the implementation of higher standards of nuclear safety and radiation protection; the responsible and safe management of spent fuel and radioactive waste and, finally, the long-term impact on the environment.
in writing. − nuclear energy remains an important source of energy, whereas nuclear safety has been one of the major concerns across europe, involving nuclear safeguards not only in europe but also third countries. better coordination is desired at international and national level as well as international, local and regional organisations. on the other hand, it is necessary to improve financial management to ensure optimal use of the eu’s financial resources in times of economic hardship. as the proposal stressed the need to promote economic development and respect fully the highest safety standards in the production of nuclear energy in the meantime, i voted in favour of it.
in writing. - i consider the chichester report on the nuclear decommissioning assistance programmes in bulgaria, lithuania and slovakia to be a balanced text, which is why i voted in favour of it.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that the decommissioning programmes for the nuclear installations in lithuania, slovakia and bulgaria, while of fundamental importance for the health and safety of all european citizens, must be carried out in an efficient and thrifty use of the funds made available. for this reason, i am in favour of the commission monitoring these programmes, ensuring that the union's financial resources are allocated and used in accordance with criteria of efficiency and economy.
in writing. - lithuania, slovakia and bulgaria are three countries with old nuclear reactors which the international community considered to be too outdated and for which it was not possible to adapt to the minimum safety standards required. in the course of the negotiations for accession to the european union, the three countries undertook to close and deactivate the nuclear reactors within certain time limits, with the financial assistance of the european union itself. although all the units concerned have been closed within the deadlines, some decommissioning programmes continue to suffer economically harmful and politically unacceptable delays. we therefore agree with the report by mr chichester, because it is essential to ensure the safety of all citizens of the member states through a more stringent monitoring system. it will be necessary to assess the progress made, to verify the decommissioning of the eight reactors and also to mitigate the negative economic effects which will inevitably be caused by their final closure. in order to assess the adequacy of the appropriations allocated to the programme through the european union funds and taking into account the financial co-responsibility of the union and the member states concerned, it will be necessary to monitor systematically the amounts disbursed, so that they are used efficiently and sparingly.
in writing. − in lithuania, slovakia and bulgaria, dated nuclear reactors associated with huge risk of safety issues were operated. unfortunately, it has been concluded that these nuclear reactors could not be cost effectively upgraded to meet the minimum required safety standards. currently available funding falls at eur 2500 million less than the estimated cost. the process of decommissioning is put at risk due to the lack of funding; it is necessary for the union to provide financial assistance and monitor the usage to avoid the potential social, environmental and economic problems. therefore, i voted in favour of this proposal.
in writing. - in the morning, parliament voted in plenary on a report by mr chichester on the proposal for a council regulation on union support for nuclear decommissioning assistance programmes in bulgaria, lithuania and slovakia. eu financial assistance to complete the closure of obsolete nuclear power plants with inadequate safety standards responds to growing public concern about environmental issues, which all too often have the potential to negatively impact the health of citizens. in the light of recent events in japan and given the geographical proximity of the slovak republic and bulgaria to our country (in this connection, it is worth recalling the chernobyl disaster, which is much further away from italy than the two countries mentioned), ensuring the safety of the nuclear installations of the three countries in question represents a financial burden which the union must assume, given the real environmental risks associated with the lack of support for nuclear decommissioning programmes. for these reasons, i cannot help but support a resolution allocating some eur 900 million to prevent a potential environmental disaster which could also harm italian citizens.
in writing. - lithuania, slovakia and bulgaria are three countries where old nuclear reactors were in operation which were too outdated and for which it was not possible to adjust to the minimum safety standards required in a cost-effective way. in the agreement reached by the european union, the three countries have committed themselves to shutting down and subsequently decommissioning the nuclear reactors within certain strict deadlines. i acknowledge that the early shutdown represented a social, environmental, economic and financial burden of exceptional scope, and i agree that the european union has committed itself to providing financial assistance until the end of 2013, both for the decommissioning of the reactors and as a contribution to dealing with the consequences of an early shutdown, preventing any environmental damage in advance. that is why i gave a favourable opinion.

member of the commission. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the financial crisis which originated in the united states and which has deeply shocked the whole of europe has not only highlighted the importance that certain financial institutions can have for the stability of our economies and the real economy. it also showed that individual investors, i.e. citizens, were also vulnerable, fragile and directly affected by the difficulties of these large financial institutions. any person seeking to invest his savings is necessarily in an unequal situation vis-à-vis the financial operator who is going to sell him investment products. there's a kind of asymmetry in information, and a very high level of understanding between the two sides. this situation naturally leads to much abuse. we are not counting the cases of investors all over europe who bought products sold as safe and ended up with losses far beyond what they could have imagined. it is not surprising that consumers, citizens, have developed a certain distrust of financial service providers. one consequence is that savers no longer invest their savings with confidence or efficiency. this results in a concentration of savings in bank deposits. in many countries of our european union, the proportion of financial assets deposited by consumers in bank accounts reaches 40%, or even 50%. this means that at the present level of interest rates european savers are barely shielded from inflation. it's not good for the economy either. the financial crisis has highlighted the dubious market practices that the different rules in force have not been able to prevent. the distribution of financial products to retail investors is subject to many different texts. similar products are regulated differently. this is particularly the case with regard to investor information requirements. that is why i proposed measures last year to better protect investors. the rules relating to the marketing of products are the in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation on the establishment and operation of european satellite navigation systems, as it constitutes the new financing and governance framework for the two european satellite navigation programmes, galileo and egnos, for 2014-2020. galileo is the eu's programme for the development of a global satellite navigation system under european civilian control. it will be compatible and interoperable with the american gps and the russian glonass, but independent of them. the european geostationary system egnos, on the other hand, aims to improve the american gps system by means of important applications for aviation and maritime safety. the regulation provides for the development of applications and the maximisation of socioeconomic benefits, the strengthening of the role of the gsa, the european gnss agency, in promoting and marketing the services offered by both programmes, the development of applications and the coordination of a european network of centres of excellence, and a clear governance structure for the relationship between the gsa and the esa. the regulation also aims to clarify the commission's role in assessing the activities promoting the systems and ensuring their use in the various sectors of the economy.

in writing. − satellite navigation makes a major contribution to a wide variety of sectors, such as transport and industry. it is of strategic importance to establish a satellite navigation system for european citizens which is independent of the american gps and russian glonass for positioning, navigation and time. the galileo and egnos programmes have already started and we should avoid losing the benefits. therefore, i voted in favour of this proposal.
in writing. - the european parliament, in plenary session, voted this morning a resolution by mr marinescu on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the establishment and operation of european satellite radio navigation systems. in a market such as satellite navigation, where the us gps system is undisputedly dominant, developing the community's galileo and egnos technologies means offering citizens an independent european alternative that is also interoperable with the other global navigation systems. to this end, parliament has played a key role in ensuring that the navigation system can be used in the daily lives of citizens. both systems will enable the creation of new satellite navigation applications aimed at improving safety, efficiency and reliability in sectors with many implications for the well-being of citizens, such as aviation, maritime, road and agriculture. for these reasons, i am in full support of a resolution which i believe will make life easier for citizens and represents a great potential for european industry and new jobs.
in writing. - i decided to vote in favour because the european satellite navigation policy will make available to the union two very important satellite navigation systems, the system created by the galileo programme and the egnos system. gnss (global navigation satellite system) technologies are crucial for improving efficiency in many sectors of the economy and in many areas of citizens' daily lives. the aim of the galileo programme is to create the first global navigation satellite system (gnss) built under civilian control, completely independent of other existing systems, interoperable with the different navigation systems and designed to provide uninterrupted gnss services. satellite radio navigation is already crucial for european transport and industry and it is important to overcome the dependence on the us gps and the russian glonass for positioning, navigation and timing. european gnss services must be provided by a european infrastructure, which is not dependent for its reliable operation on the military priorities of the usa, russia or china.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the proust report on the eu-russia agreement on drug precursors. i think it is essential to regulate and control the circulation of chemicals which can also be used for the synthesis of drugs.
in writing. − the regular verification by the international narcotic control board (incb) of the database of countries party to the 1988 un convention on trade data exchange provides startling evidence of the adaptability and operational flexibility demonstrated by criminal organisations in the diversion of precursors and chemicals essential for the manufacture of drugs. it is truly remarkable that there is still no framework for effective international cooperation to respond to these findings and that we must proceed along the more politically manageable but more complicated path of bilateral agreements. i am well aware of the difficulty of balancing the practical aspects of the fight against traffickers with the complex problems of trade and international relations, which in this case is demonstrated by the absence of a sanctioning apparatus and a specific declaration on violations. however, agreements such as the one the report is concerned with must be seen as a precondition, a first barrier to drug trafficking, a barrier which must then be strengthened in the various areas, from best business practices to security, defence and stabilisation policies. i therefore vote in favour of the report.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution to approve the agreement concluded by the eu with russia on cooperation in the control of the trade in 'drug precursors'. 'drug precursors' are substances which are lawful in themselves but which can nevertheless be used in the manufacture of narcotic drugs. within the european internal market, these substances are already subject to special import, export and transit arrangements. however, international cooperation remains an essential tool to break up the drug trafficking network and prevent the criminal organisations operating within it from exploiting the opening of the european single market for illicit purposes. the agreement with russia is the latest in a series of similar agreements with the united states, china and a number of latin american countries. i hope that the eu will continue to pursue this path with determination and conclude many similar agreements in the coming years.
in writing. - i supported mr proust's report, voting in favour of it, because i share the need to strengthen cooperation between russia and the eu in the fight against drug trafficking. in advocating the need for greater control over legal substances used in the production of synthetic drugs, such as acetic acid used to produce heroin, the report makes a number of points which i felt it was necessary to support.
in writing. − the eu and russia have long been partners in international trade; at the current stage, it is necessary to improve cooperation between eu and russia to combat drug trafficking. russia has become a destination for drug traffickers; the flow of synthetic drugs between the eu and russia has significantly increased, including highly addictive and dangerous drugs such as amphetamines and methadone. regarding the urgency of improving cooperation to monitor the trade of easily-obtained legal substances which can be used for the manufacture of synthetic drugs, i support the rapporteur’s position and voted for this proposal.
in writing. - i have decided to vote in favour of the agreement between the european union and russia on drug precursors as it is part of the improvement of cooperation on the surveillance of these products. the drug precursors are substances which are legal in themselves but which can be used in the chemical process of manufacturing synthetic drugs. the agreement establishes cooperation between the two parties in the surveillance of trade in certain chemicals, a mechanism for mutual administrative assistance and introduces a system of pre-export notification by the exporting country, followed by a three-week period during which the importing country may object to such importation on the basis of written reasons.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the agreement between the european union and the russian federation aimed at improving cooperation between these two major trading partners in the field of drug precursor trade surveillance. these precursors are legal substances that can be used in the chemical process of manufacturing synthetic drugs. for example, acetic acid is used in the manufacture of heroin. this agreement is part of a clear european strategy based on a common approach to the major trading powers, in particular producers and consumers of drugs, to curb the trafficking of narcotic substances within them by strengthening joint and ambitious surveillance of trade in the international trade in these precursors, which make it possible to produce a large number of synthetic drugs. the eu has already concluded and signed similar agreements with the united states, china and a number of latin american countries. the aim is to strengthen the barriers to traffickers by enhancing surveillance of the origin and destination of the chemicals and medicinal products concerned without jeopardising the legitimate trade in such products. russia has now become a destination rather than a transit or production area.
in writing. the european commission has concluded an agreement with russia to prevent the misuse of precursors and chemicals frequently used in the illicit preparation of narcotics. i voted in favour of this agreement, which provides for prior notification by the exporting country, which may be followed by objection by the importing country in the form of written comments.

in writing. - i join the rapporteur's position with a favourable vote: it is quite reasonable to wait for the final text of the new europol regulation, which will also affect agreements with third countries. however, i would like to stress, in line with the rapporteur's own reasoning, the need to seriously address the unresolved issues - from the permeability of police forces to the security of sensitive information - which complicate the conclusion of agreements with certain countries. in 2013, the activities of the police authorities of the member states continue to reveal a worrying pervasiveness of criminal organisations from some of the countries concerned in the european territory: in june, an italian police operation was carried out against the georgian criminal organisation of 'thieves in law', active in drug trafficking, human trafficking, money laundering and contract murder. in july, interpol's lionfish operation led to a record seizure of 30 tonnes of drugs from a trafficking organisation operating in the gulf of mexico that had infiltrated europe via french dom-tom. two of many. it is therefore clear that there is an opportunity and an urgency to perfect an arrangement with these countries.
in writing. - as is well known, the lisbon treaty has considerably extended the powers of the european parliament, making it de facto co-legislator, together with the council, in a number of areas of union law, including police cooperation. parliament's participation in the legislative procedure for adopting the union's legislative acts guarantees a level of democratic legitimacy which no legal system, which is based on the principles of democracy and the rule of law, such as that of the european union, can renounce. for this reason i am not in favour of the council unilaterally deciding, on the basis of rules which came into force before the treaty of lisbon, to extend the list of countries with which europol (the european police office) can conclude agreements. parliament could be involved in this area in the context of the commission's recent proposal for new regulations for europol.
in writing. − the text refers to the draft council decision amending decision 2009/935/jha concerning the list of third countries with which europol may conclude agreements. the new states are brazil, georgia, mexico and the united arab emirates. the director and the management board of europol are requested to refrain from initiating negotiations on operational agreements with the countries listed in the draft until the new europol regulation has entered into force. in addition, some of these countries have low data protection and therefore cannot guarantee the protection of personal data. i therefore vote in favour.
in writing. − the commission has proposed for a regulation on europol to modify the procedure for concluding agreements with third states and organisations; amendments to the measures for implementing the repealed decision should not be considered at this point. furthermore, privacy and fundamental rights cannot be guaranteed in many of the associated countries, as personal data is under insufficient protection. therefore, i support the position of the civil liberties committee and voted to reject the draft council decision.
in writing. - i have decided to vote in favour of this report because it calls for the rejection of the draft council decision which has included brazil, georgia, mexico and the united arab emirates among the third countries with which europol may conclude agreements. the director and the management board of europol should refrain from negotiating operational agreements with the listed states until the new europol regulation enters into force. it is also recalled that some of these countries do not have a sufficient level of data protection and cannot guarantee the fundamental right to the protection of personal data.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the sartori report on the legal framework applicable to a consortium for a european research infrastructure. the text, which is very timely and balanced, deals in a proactive way with a sensitive and strategic issue for citizens and businesses alike.
in writing. − the european union's real chances of safeguarding its competitive position in the world economy and thus of guaranteeing a future of growth and prosperity for its citizens are linked in two ways to its ability to provide adequate incentives for innovation and scientific advances. that is why i voted in favour of this resolution approving the commission's proposal to promote the establishment and operation of european research infrastructures.
in writing. − the eric regulation was adopted by council in 2009 to facilitate the establishment and operation of european research infrastructures on a non-economic basis. norway and other third countries have indicated that they intend to contribute as host or member to a significant number of erics. i therefore voted for the proposal in support of expanding the membership and scope of eric.
mr president, i have worked a lot on the dossier on the european communities' funds, which certainly has some positive features, such as the simplification features: the commission has also proposed that the member states should adopt a general regulation covering all five structural funds, which will make it possible to streamline procedures and make uniform the rules for the regulation and access to the funds. the introduction of the new category of regions - intermediate regions - which will also allow the economic situations of regions situated between the more developed and the less developed regions to be taken into account, which was a handicap of the previous regulations, is also a positive element; the commission has also proposed the introduction of a partnership agreement with the commission and ex ante conditionality, which will provide sufficient guarantees as to the effective use of the funds. i must, however, complain about the negative entry concerning macro-conditionality. i have already expressed a negative opinion on this matter, which i confirm, and which casts a serious shadow over the whole of the dossier.
in writing. - in a situation where it is necessary to boost investment and the economy of our regions and territories, the management of the structural funds cannot be conditioned by the principle of austerity and rigor. this puts at serious risk the use of the resources available to combat the dramatic effects of the economic crisis. the regions and local authorities must be helped to grow and invest for recovery, not held back by budgetary problems or the rigid constraints of the stability pact. this is the spirit of the instruments and funds of cohesion policy. it would have been useful, as the committee on regional policy initially decided, to separate national cofinancing from the structural deficit calculation, based on a clear distinction between current and investment expenditure. for these reasons i voted against the inclusion of 'macro-conditionality clauses' in the agreement. cohesion policy is by its very nature an investment. introducing strict austerity rules for the structural funds too can only lead to an emptying of the raison d'être of the first pillar of the eu.
in writing. - i believe that the choice of the committee on regional development to base the reform of the new cohesion policy on a clear and balanced strategic framework based on a limited number of objectives and priorities was the wisest choice given the economic context and budgetary constraints. the increased thematic focus of investment will allow for a more concentrated use of resources and they are therefore convinced that the measures envisaged for post-2013 cohesion policy will be adequate to ensure a sustainable economic recovery. we must certainly focus more on competitiveness and, since the report reflects my conviction, i have decided to vote in favour of it. finally, i would add that to ensure that investment has an effective impact, we must promote a new generation of indicators to measure the quality and results of the projects financed.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this regulation. cohesion policy, which over the years has made a significant contribution to growth and job creation and to reducing disparities between member states and regions, is now even more important. the economic crisis which has struck the whole of europe, which imposes austerity rules to consolidate public budgets, makes the structural funds even more important and requires us to choose the most appropriate rules for the best possible use in terms of effectiveness, efficiency and economy. it is undeniable that, if the european states and regions make good use of it, this funding will undoubtedly be an important lever for the redistribution of national markets and the consolidation of the single european market.
in writing. - today we have seen once again how this europe wants to enslave us, finding all possible means to limit the freedom of action of the member states. the most important issue to be addressed was that of macroeconomic conditionality, i.e. the need to link the disbursement of community funds to compliance with budgetary constraints: the commission has not yet taken a decision on the matter, but it is not yet clear whether the commission will take a decision on the matter. at this point we have states, forced to comply with absurd constraints imposed by brussels, which can even see funds blocked if they do not comply to the letter with what is imposed by some bureaucrats lacking any popular legitimacy. i would like to remind everyone, just so that it is clear to everyone, that the money for the european funds does not come from brussels by divine grace, but is allocated by the member states, by contributing to the european budget. in the last financial framework 2007-2013 italy left an average of 5 billion per year between what it paid as contributions and what it received in return from these european funds. from now on, we may never see this money back. it's time to ask yourself a lot of questions.
in writing. - i voted in favour because public budgets require us to be more innovative and to make the available funding have a greater impact. the use of its instruments, in particular the structural funds (the regional development fund and the european social fund) and the cohesion fund, has demonstrated its added value as an indispensable investment instrument to effectively support growth and job creation, while responding accurately to the needs of all regions. it has not only contributed to reducing disparities between member states and regions, but also to the economic recovery and development of the union as a whole. the same applies to the agricultural development fund and the fisheries fund. the following elements are strongly supported: ensure better regulation, further simplification of implementation rules, transparency and flexibility and the development of a new generation of indicators to measure the quality and results of funded projects. in the post-2013 outlook, the european structural and investment funds remain the most effective and efficient investment instruments for delivering growth and jobs and easing pressure on national budgets.

in writing. - i voted in favour because the report will allow for a more efficient use of eu resources and a considerable improvement in the effects of policies to boost growth and employment within the union. the proposal provides for the allocation of funds according to the priorities of the europe 2020 strategy, a greater thematic concentration, the allocation of 20% of the fund's appropriations to the promotion of social inclusion and the fight against poverty, and a streamlining and simplification of the procedures for accessing the fund. the four main objectives of the proposal are to promote employment and professional mobility, with particular regard to youth employment and professional mobility, to invest in education, skills and lifelong training, to promote social inclusion and the fight against poverty, to strengthen institutional capacity and to create an effective public administration. the new esf will work towards social inclusion, by raising skills and employment levels and speeding up vocational integration. support for young people remains a priority, with 21% of them currently unemployed. through simplification of the rules and procedures for accessing the fund, a more pragmatic approach and more targeted objectives, there will be a better absorption and use of available eu resources.

in writing. − the current population of unemployed people in europe is estimated to be approximately 23 million. to help these people adapt to changes in the labour market and promote social cohesion, it is of great importance to effectively use the european union’s principal instrument, the european social fund (esf), established in 1957 under the treaty of rome. in the coming period of 2014-2020, the esf will be allocated in promoting employment and labour mobility, investing in education, skills and life-long learning, promoting social inclusion and combating poverty, and enhancing institutional capacity and efficient public administration, as proposed by the commission. regarding its consistency to the mission of ecf, i voted for this proposal.
in writing. − the european social fund (esf) for the period 2014-2020 is making good progress, which deserves my vote, in helping europe's population to adapt effectively to changes in the labour market by co-financing training projects and employment support programmes: the european social fund is designed to support the geographical and occupational mobility of workers. the four main objectives of the esf will be implemented for the period 2014-2020: 'promotion of employment and professional mobility', 'investment in education, skills and lifelong learning', 'promotion of social inclusion and the fight against poverty' and 'strengthening institutional capacity and the creation of an effective public administration'. support for young people is essential, given that 21% of young people in the european union are currently unemployed. the esf therefore remains an important instrument for social inclusion through employment, with an integrated approach supporting personalised or global pathways towards the goal of maximum and quality employment. the esf must also be used as a tool for anticipating future skills needs in order to significantly increase the number of highly qualified workers that europe will need in the near future.
mr president, i voted in favour of mr olbrycht's report, which i congratulate on its excellent work. improving the distribution of european regional development fund support is essential to finally add to the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy, while responding to the different needs of regions across the european union. i therefore support the setting of a limited number of objectives by means of the new element of thematic concentration, with a view to improving coordination with other specific actions. i am also very pleased that eco-innovation has been included among the investment priorities to strengthen research and technological development. i also believe that the integrated actions for sustainable urban development are strategic and far-sighted.
mr president, we have approved with satisfaction the dossier on the european regional development fund. the 11 specific thematic objectives to be pursued, which are those indicated for the achievement of the europe 2020 strategy to pursue those objectives, are positive aspects and will therefore allow us to approach the targets indicated in those policies for the next seven years, exploiting the cohesion funds. the introduction of thematic concentration, focusing in particular on four of the eleven thematic objectives, which will enable the regions to implement integrated policies, avoiding the dispersion of funds as in the past, should be welcomed. i would like to express my regret, however, that the handicaps of the island regions, which are condemned - i emphasize this - simply to the gdp parameter, have not been taken into account, without any consideration of the need for a direct link. we will have to fight this, but this was not possible because of the voting procedure adopted by parliament, which did not even allow us to discuss some of the amendments we had tabled on this subject.
mr president, today's vote and the procedure followed not only prevented the change in the criterion of macro-conditionality, in order to mitigate its negative impact, especially on certain member states and their regions, but also prevented this house from giving its opinion on another amendment to this regulation, which would have sought to correct a non-political meaning which had arisen from the trilogue at the insistence of the commission and the council. article 4 of the regulation on the european regional development fund introduces a derogation in the concentration of resources, which is intended to respond to the specific natural handicaps of island regions. strangely, however, this derogation applies only to some of these island regions and not to all of them. i would like to ask the commissioner whether he has not already taken the initiative in this area, and whether he has not already taken the initiative in the other areas. the island status and its difficulties are the same everywhere and cohesion policy should have taken this into account, thus rebalancing and re-establishing the derogation for all island regions.

in writing. - i supported the proposal because the european regional development fund (erdf) is designed to reduce the gap between the levels of development of the various european regions and the backwardness of the less-favoured regions. the proposal provides for the erdf to support local and regional development over the period 2014-2020 by co-financing investments in the following areas: r&d and innovation, climate change and environment, support for smes, services of general economic interest, telecommunications, energy and transport infrastructure, health, education and social infrastructure, and sustainable urban development. to ensure that erdf support is more focused on the priorities of the european union, the proposal provides for more targeted objectives, while taking account of the different levels of regional development. the report also aims to avoid unnecessary duplication of effort and the effects of dispersion and insufficient prioritization, which in the past have limited the added value of european investment. i believe that in a time of scarcity of resources, thematic concentration and the definition of investment priorities in line with the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy are essential. the regulation also provides that special attention should be paid to sustainable urban development, in particular by allocating at least 5% of erdf resources to this purpose.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the regulation on the european regional development fund (erdf). the result achieved is also a result of the work of parliament, which fought to see its own proposals for amendments incorporated, which have made the programme much more effective and operational. in particular, the scope of support has been extended by introducing the eligibility of small-scale infrastructure for culture and sustainable tourism and allowing support for productive investments to be granted also in the case of large-scale enterprises. another important aspect is that of the urban dimension and its sustainable development, which i consider to be of paramount importance because it is the best way of making the european project a reality at local level, that is, within reach of the citizen.
in writing. − the tfeu provides that the european regional development fund (erdf) is intended to contribute to the correction of the main regional imbalances in the union by reducing the gap between the levels of development of the different regions and the backwardness of the least favoured regions. the objective is to contribute to the implementation of the eu 2020 strategy for smart, sustainable and inclusive growth. with the new regulation, which i supported with my vote in the house, the erdf will focus on research and innovation, information and communication technologies, smes and the promotion of a low-carbon economy, taking into account the level of development of the region. i am very pleased with the success of the battle waged with the support of my group for the introduction of objectives such as sustainable tourism and the enhancement of the cultural and natural heritage, as part of a strategy for specific areas, which includes the conversion of declining industrial regions.
in writing. the erdf aims to contribute to strengthening economic and social cohesion by reducing regional disparities. amendments were introduced to improve the distribution of erdf support in the next programming period, succeeding in extending it by introducing the eligibility of small-scale infrastructure for culture and sustainable tourism and allowing support for productive investments. the investment framework is clearer and simpler, as it ensures better coordination with the other fund-specific regulations and the common provisions regulation (cpr), through links with the thematic objectives and/or investment priorities. this is an important event in terms of improving coordination and strengthening synergies with the funds and their implementation, with a view to ensuring smart, sustainable and inclusive growth in line with the europe 2020 strategy. the new element of thematic concentration provides for a high concentration of resources on a limited number of objectives, which should ensure a higher added value of interventions. the new erdf also introduces a mandatory urban dimension for the first time and ensures that greater attention is paid to urban development at a strategic level.
