in writing. - i voted in favour of the zeller report on the proposal for a european parliament and council regulation on european territorial cooperation groups. the text is well suited to the objective of simplifying the existing regulation in order to facilitate and promote territorial cooperation, including crossborder, transnational and interregional initiatives.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the proposal because it aims to reduce the bureaucratic burden on european groupings for territorial cooperation (egtcs) and to make the rules governing them simpler and more flexible. the changes introduced include an improvement in the approval procedure for an egtc, ensuring greater transparency and legal certainty for applicants; the authorisation procedure for new egtcs is also expected to be more efficient. the regulation makes a clear distinction between the statute and the convention. only the latter will be subject to formal approval, which will reduce administrative burdens and speed up the authorisation procedure. the staffing arrangements will be made clearer and more transparent. the egtcs will be open to all public enterprises providing public services. territorial cooperation in areas such as public transport, energy and water supply, health, education and vocational training will be facilitated and encouraged. a clearer, more precise and more complete definition was accepted as regards the participation of third countries. third countries neighbouring the union will be able to become members of an egtc. these clear and simple rules will encourage territorial cooperation within the eu and between regions in the member states and in third countries.

in writing. − european groupings of territorial cooperation (egtc) were created to overcome the obstacles hindering territorial cooperation. however, some aspects have been shown to cause confusion and clarification is needed to ensure more visibility and communication on egtcs. the proposed amendments simplify and clarify this regulation to improve legal certainty and encourage better cooperation within the eu as well as between regions of member states and third countries. therefore, i voted for the proposal.
in writing. − in 2013, only 17.6% of non-executive members of the largest eu companies were women. full support therefore for effective and binding measures to ensure equal access and to ensure that - by 2020 - at least 40% of non-executive board seats are filled by women. this is an effective way of tackling the considerable disparity in representation in key decision-making roles that still exists at both european and national level. countries that have introduced mandatory quotas have achieved important results in terms of gender balance on company boards (france +14.4 percentage points; netherlands +8.7 pp and italy +8.4 pp) but the most recent data (april 2013) show that, despite some progress, women represent only 16.6% of the top management of listed companies. but it's not just a matter of numbers. it is about empowering qualified and capable women and breaking down prejudices and stereotypes.
in writing. - i welcome the conclusion of the work on this important directive, which has just been adopted, after a rather arduous process of discussion. the gender imbalance remains very strong in politics as well as in managerial positions in the public and private economy. in italy the problem is particularly acute: although the proportion of women on boards of publicly listed companies increased by 4.9% in 2013, it is still dramatically flat at 11%. it is therefore of the utmost importance that, when transposing this directive, member states should adopt clear and effective sanctions against those undertakings which fail to comply with its requirements. a real improvement on the directive introduced by the european parliament. we would have liked to have done more, to have broadened the scope and the target groups of the directive, but it must be admitted that the compromise reached is generally satisfactory.

in writing. - the accession of a substantial proportion of women without executive positions to the boards of directors of listed companies represents a necessary cultural evolution, if we consider that, even today, the european economic system is entrusted to a peculiarly male management. that is why i voted in favour of the report drawn up by mrs kratsa and mrs regner, which lays the foundations for overcoming such a market dysfunction. my support for this report is therefore based on the awareness that gender equality is not only an essential cornerstone of the european value system but also, and above all, an objective to be pursued in practice.
in writing. − promoting the presence of women in top executive positions in companies is a sign of civilization, which unfortunately must be introduced into our systems through the legislative instrument, to recover the gap in presence accumulated over decades. the proposal for a directive, which i supported with my vote, takes account of the operational needs of company management and makes the appropriate distinctions according to the size of the company, taking into account the concerns expressed by the business world itself. it sets a minimum target of 40% for non-executive directors in listed companies, but leaves some flexibility for executives, and introduces a derogation for smes and sectors where women represent less than 10% of the workforce. the levels set must be reached by 2020. i am convinced that the compromise reached is extremely positive, because it opens the way to an important process of democratic growth and at the same time does not undermine the organization of work in enterprises.
in writing. - i have rarely seen proposals as full of useless ideological content as this one: you start with a fair assumption, gender equality, but you end up with ridiculous rules that are hard to enforce. firstly, it is a question of determining the proportion of women in non-executive bodies, as if to say that a representative seat is guaranteed, but at a relatively low level. in addition, they would like to impose criteria for the selection of candidates based not on merit but on sex, leaving the way open to different choices, without understanding on what basis, a real triumph of the contradiction. some passages, i think, are almost ridiculous, such as the one asking companies to evaluate the "creation of a nursery of women ready to take up managerial positions". so you want to create a caste of the chosen and the predestined? i'd like to know what the women who have worked their asses off and earned their leadership positions think. some research and surveys, such as that of the centre for policy studies in london, have also shown that women themselves often do not aspire to these posts, having other aspirations and goals in life.
in writing. − gender equality is among the fundamental rights enshrined by the european union. however, the progress in offering women greater possibilities to take on a leading decisional position in europe is rather slow. this proposal set up an objective to at least 40% of female in non-executive board-member positions in all companies in all sectors; it also offers a framework for member states and companies to take efficient procedures in order to promote gender balance on boards of all listed companies. it is proposed that companies failing to comply in meeting the objective should be subject to sanctions, which will considerably facilitate the process of improving gender balance. therefore, i voted in favour of this proposal.
in writing. − today, with 459 votes in favour, the european parliament in plenary approved the proposal for a parliament and council directive on improving the gender balance among non-executive directors of listed companies. as mrs kratsa and mrs tsagaropoulou's report show, the directive aims to ensure that women without executive positions are represented on the boards of listed companies up to a threshold of at least 40%. by encouraging greater transparency and meritocracy, it offers women greater opportunities to access key positions in business management. this is therefore of fundamental importance given that member states and the european institutions have always worked together to promote gender equality in the economic sphere.
in writing. − the decision to introduce pink shares in european listed companies to ensure that by 2020 at least 40% of non-executive positions in the cdas are held by women is the decision we have been waiting for. sanctioning companies that fail to introduce this procedure will send a strong and clear signal to reverse the trend that in 2013 only 17.6% of women were in the largest european companies. giving deserving, highly qualified women an extra chance to fill a deserving role will allow the entire economic system to reap the benefits.
in writing. − the positive effects of binding targets demonstrate the ability of companies to comply with measures to ensure gender balance at recruitment. in addition, it should be noted that member states where no binding measures have been adopted are still far from achieving an acceptable gender balance. to effectively overcome the challenges facing the eu in a vulnerable economic crisis, the full human capital needs to be mobilised to achieve growth, competitiveness and better financial performance at company level. measures to ensure a better gender balance on boards contribute to that objective. the proposal is based on the principles of equality, transparency, meritocracy and common procedures and objectives. the directive will strengthen social justice in the labour market and contribute to economic growth by making full use of all available resources, skills and strengths, so as to realise the benefits of the eu's human potential. that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. − european listed companies, under the text adopted today, will have to adopt transparent recruitment procedures to ensure that at least 40% of non-executive board seats are filled by women by 2020. the adoption of this resolution thus sends a strong signal to companies and stakeholders: the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council adopt a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to carcinogens at work.

in writing. - financial education is a very important topic that i hear from time to time. although the current crisis was generated by so-called "information asymmetries", which allowed the sale of financial products capable of propagating the disastrous effects of rash choices, without the buyer being aware of it, it still seems that basic courses in the principles of finance are a chimera. it is therefore right that the european parliament should demand greater transparency from financial intermediaries, so that small savers have more information, which can be more easily compared, about the investment products they buy. more information means less fraud, or at least less misunderstanding, with greater satisfaction for both the buyer and the seller.
in writing. − any measure that improves and makes financial markets more transparent is certainly to be strongly supported: the report we have adopted today deals with investment products. retail investors are faced with a range of very complex choices and products, sometimes very difficult to understand in depth. the regulation is intended to clarify certain key information which could allow a more informed choice for those who decide to invest their money in this way. unfortunately, there have been many cases in the past of people being totally ignorant of the product they were signing up for, and many times there have been unfortunate consequences. these new rules will certainly be useful, but my advice is that we should always be very careful and not suddenly become experts in matters where we are probably not.
in writing. − though there are a wide variety of different types of investment products available on the market, european retail investors often have difficulties in understanding the complex features of each specific investment product, and have often made investments with unpredicted risk and costs. to improve the transparency of the investment product market and better provide accessible and comprehensible information to consumers to make decisions, the commission proposed to establish a common standard for key information documents and ensure uniform disclosures. in view of the benefit of this programme to european consumers in the investment product market, i voted in favour of it.

in writing. − the nauru agreement, to which kiribati is a signatory, was established to ensure coordinated management of fisheries resources in its members' eezs and to increase the benefits. its members have negotiated several implementing agreements setting out the minimum conditions for the licence, such as provisions on vessel monitoring, transhipment, closed fishing areas, gear restrictions, landing obligations and observation cover and appeal. shipowners can buy and trade days at sea to gain access to the waters of the countries that have signed the agreement. the un fish stocks agreement, ratified by the eu and kiribati, calls on states to cooperate "to enhance the capacity of developing states, in particular least developed countries and small island developing states, to conserve and manage transboundary and highly migratory fish stocks". overcapacity and excessive fishing effort are key issues that need to be addressed in all regions. in this context, the eu should actively support the current regional actions to address overcapacity and limit fishing effort.
in writing. the debate on the various seats of the european institutions, and more specifically on the three seats of the european parliament, and their operating costs, is a constant subject of debate in this chamber, but also of high attention in the external media and in community public opinion. if we were to give parliament the full right to decide on its seat, its organisation and its functioning, we would be able to respond, i believe, effectively to the many doubts and criticisms that are constantly being raised about the present situation and its costs. this situation deserves a thorough discussion, bearing in mind the historical and political reasons which led to the choice of the three seats of the european institutions, but which must be answered and solved efficiently: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them.
in writing. i voted in favour of the following text: the fact that the european parliament has two seats is an unacceptable waste against which i am fighting and will always continue to fight.
in writing. - i voted in favour because the report envisages reducing the financial, environmental, organisational and logistical impact of the current relocation of the eu institutions. the report, given the present context of budgetary austerity for many member states, envisages saving resources and eliminating unnecessary expenditure by fixing the sole seat of the european parliament in brussels. the arguments in favour of a single seat for the ep include isolation from the other institutions, the cost of parliament's geographical dispersion, the environmental impact, the constitutional argument (the ep should have the right to determine its own organisation) and the support of citizens, as 1.27 million people have signed a petition calling for a single seat for the ep. the report therefore proposes that parliament should undertake to initiate a regular review of the treaties in order to be able to decide on the location of its seat and its internal organisation. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover all the activities of the european parliament. the bureau of the european parliament is invited to request eurobaromater to conduct a survey of eu citizens' opinions on this matter.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution because i have long been a strong supporter of the european parliament's action to abolish its three seats and to define a single seat. this is a situation which cannot be tolerated any longer and which must be changed as soon as possible. the maintenance of three sites has no plausible justification, especially after the great information campaign which has brought to light the environmental problems and the disproportionate costs involved in maintaining the current situation. the important petition signed by european citizens also reminds us of our responsibilities and obliges us to continue fighting to achieve this important result.
in writing. − the organisation of the european parliament's work based on the rule of dual seating produces unjustifiable costs and reduces efficiency. i have been following for some time the various initiatives to amend the treaty in order to restore the unity of the seat. the reasons which led to the decision to split parliamentary activities between strasbourg and brussels have now disappeared. politics must have the strength and courage to go beyond the interests of the individual. i believe that this moment of crisis and the resulting further alienation of citizens from the european project make the need for such a decision very timely. i am satisfied with the answer which parliament has given, also with the contribution of my vote, by supporting the resolution.
in writing. − the european parliament currently has two permanent meeting sites, one in brussels and one in strasbourg, and a third location in luxembourg. meps and staff members have multiple offices and have to travel between the two cities on a monthly basis, which costs significant loss of time in travelling, a large amount of emissions and a waste of european taxpayers’ money. locating the european legislators in a single place will surely reduce expenditure and improve efficiency. therefore, i voted in favour of this proposal.
in writing. - i have repeatedly spoken in this chamber against the maintenance of two chambers which essentially serve the same function. the monthly migration between brussels and strasbourg has a negative symbol for most european union citizens, including myself, as well as a considerable economic cost, especially at a time when the financial crisis is affecting the citizens of the union. we have asked the appropriate bodies to revise the treaties to propose the changes needed to enable parliament to decide on the location of its seat and its internal organisation. the costs, which are converted into potential savings, arising from the geographical dispersion of the parliament (between brussels, luxembourg and strasbourg) are estimated at between €156 million and €204 million - this includes the additional costs of the strasbourg seat, estimated at €103 million. the total cost of the three workplaces represents about 10% of its annual budget. with co2 emissions associated with transfers to and from the three work sites estimated at between 11,000 and 19,000 tonnes. i wonder if, in the face of the general crisis we are undergoing, all this makes sense.

vice-president of the commission. - madam president, i would like to thank parliament and mr creutzmann and mr rübig for their contribution, because the compromise reached on the cosme programme shows that, at this particular moment of economic crisis, the community institutions are paying close attention to the real economy and to the 23 million small and mediumsized enterprises which are at the heart of the european union's economy. cosme does not have big figures but it is still important to have given a very clear political message: we want to support this sector and ensure the competitiveness of small and medium-sized enterprises through internationalisation and easier access to credit: cosme contains a dedicated venture capital package, which is too little used in europe, but is doing very well in other parts of the world, particularly in the united states of america. the cosme report is a strong signal, adding to the agreement reached between parliament, the council and the commission on the application of rules different from those of basel iii for small and medium-sized enterprises up to eur 1.5 million, for whose loans basel ii still applies. in addition, a significant part of horizon 2020 funding is reserved for small and medium-sized enterprises. so, it's a strong strategy also for the use of the regional funds 2014-2020: the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. i therefore share the view expressed by my colleague, commissioner hahn, who has repeatedly said that the funds should not be used for the organization of concerts or village parties. it is necessary to increase employment, to help businesses that employ young people and to build infrastructure. it is in this philosophy, i believe, that the cosme package fits, which will also contribute to the implementation of the entrepreneurship 2020 action plan. i very much appreciate the interest shown by parliament in this matter. the success of smes obviously depends on the entrepreneurs. we need a new generation of entrepreneurs, young entrepreneurs, women entrepreneurs and also immigrant entrepreneurs, as envisaged in our action plan. the training aspect is also important. i hope that all the countries of the european union will use the dual system adopted in germany and austria, which allows young people, once they have finished school, to have a thorough knowledge of the world of work, not only theoretical but also practical. in reply to the first of the questions in mr rübig's question, i would point out that the action plan will be incorporated into the implementation of the small business act and that the commission has already planned the way in which the two initiatives will be coordinated, avoiding as much as possible duplication of action by the member states. so, from next year, the implementation of the action plan will be fully integrated into that of the small business act. as regards education and training as a competence of the member states, we have presented a communication, entitled 'rethinking education', accompanied by an action plan, and we are working with national authorities at all levels and with all stakeholders. there are already excellent programmes in europe promoting the development of entrepreneurial skills in schools and universities (i also mentioned the dual system) and what we need to do is to take these good practices and transfer them into our educational systems. the action plan calls on the member states to include key entrepreneurship skills in school curricula and to provide young people in training with the opportunity to gain practical entrepreneurial experience during compulsory schooling, i.e. as a preparatory step towards the establishment of a genuine dual system: we're going to start with extended internships during the school term and then really have a full dual system. since training and education policies are predominantly a matter for national or regional competence, the effective implementation of the action plan is left to the member states: i am far from wanting to violate the principle of subsidiarity with which i identify. but if we want a genuine european policy to support the real economy, we must also encourage the member states to initiate some reforms. we have taken some concrete steps to encourage entrepreneurial culture and education, particularly among new aspiring entrepreneurs, through the launch of the programme, erasmus for young entrepreneurs, mentioned earlier. the programme supports the development of new skills, the exchange of good practice and the networking of new aspiring entrepreneurs, who are also offered the opportunity to work closely with established entrepreneurs from other member states. finally, to generate growth, innovation and competitiveness in europe, member states will need to encourage young people to acquire more and more computer and technology skills. as regards question 3 the integrated approach to facilitating entrepreneurship those who decide to take risks on their own,should be facilitated in every way. therefore, on a proposal from the commission, the competitiveness council of may 2011 set the targets of three days and eur 100 to start a business. the commission has already taken a number of measures to improve the quality of the information it receives. through the refit programme, the commission services have mapped all union legislation to identify burdens, gaps and inefficient or ineffective measures. the programme, which follows our consultation on the ten laws which weigh most heavily on businesses, is a decisive initiative to reduce the impact of legislation on the competitiveness of businesses. citizens and businesses will thus be able to benefit directly from this programme. question no 4 was answered during the opening of the debate. question no 5 concerns the vat. i am pleased to inform you that we expect the next commission proposal on the standard vat return to be adopted by the end of 2013 and i am confident that this proposal will bring considerable benefits to small and medium-sized enterprises and especially to micro enterprises. the aim is to enable businesses to file a single tax return in each member state where such a return is obviously required, so as to reduce administrative burdens and obstacles to cross-border trade. thanks to this initiative, annual cost savings of eur 15 billion should be achieved fairly quickly. i can assure you that, after the approval by parliament and the council, the commission is ready to proceed with the rapid implementation of the cosme programme which - i repeat - we consider to be of the utmost importance and which we are already putting to good use with the growth missions i am organising around the world. i am a member of the mission in vietnam, myanmar and thailand, where we promote the entrepreneurial capacity of small, medium and large enterprises in our union to make industrial policy. these are missions which are being very successful, because helpdesks for the internationalisation of small and mediumsized enterprises already exist through the external service of the european union and at the external service embassies. i 'll just quote one fact: during the mission in china, the helpdesk of the european union external service embassy organised about 2000 b2bs between european and chinese companies and there are already european companies working in china thanks to these b2bs. the same thing happened in thailand the other day, the same thing happened in myanmar with vice president ashton, and the same thing happened in vietnam. so we're working very hard because cosme is part of a strategy: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial instruments are not used as a financial package in themselves states that one in three of europe's small and medium-sized enterprises has direct difficulties in accessing credit. the second difficulty is to find new markets and new customers for its products. on behalf of the efd group. mr president, i commend you on your resilience. in italy, of the approximately four and a half million enterprises, 95% are micro, 4.5% small and 0.5% medium-sized. they produce 57.7 per cent of gdp and create 64 per cent of jobs. in the first nine months of 2013, almost 9,000 companies went bankrupt, closing about 1,000 vat returns a day. the paradox is that companies die because they have credit, and the main insolvent debtor is the state, which owes 130 billion to companies. on the one hand, there is the tax axe of 70 percent, on the other the guillotine of credit crunch. how can we talk about a single currency when in germany the entrepreneur has money at 1 per cent, while in italy the rate applied by the banks ranges from 5 to 20 per cent? the euro has devastated the small entrepreneurs who made italy great. the way out is the redemption of monetary sovereignty.

on behalf of the efd group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, when we talk about tax fraud and tax evaders, we all agree that the watchword should be 'anti-avoidance', but that there should also be different rules and laws. but in this europe of banks and hidden powers, there is something worse than tax evasion: the hypocrisy. in my country there are entrepreneurs who had to choose between paying taxes or paying their workers: they decided to pay their own workers. there are also multinationals that have paid their taxes regularly, that have used european funds to invest and then suddenly decided to close down in my country to move to another country in the european union where taxes and labour costs were lower. and they used european funds there too. i'm with the first entrepreneurs, the ones who decided to keep jobs in my country. until we have uniform rules for all, we will hardly make any headway in the fight against evasion, which unfortunately remains today a wrong way to survive in this single market of hypocrisy.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i congratulate the rapporteur on his work. this is certainly a difficult subject for the council to reach agreement on, but i very much hope that it will be possible. the fact that we are discussing this in this house is important, as well as being a success of parliament. it is very important to strengthen cooperation in the fight against tax evasion and fraud. but we need to achieve a fiscal union precisely because we need to harmonize income taxation for both natural and legal persons. we have in fact achieved economic union but not fiscal union and we must try to harmonize the system to be even more competitive. i am speaking as an italian, where the tax burden is very high; so let us try to be european in all respects. i would like to address my colleagues and the commissioner on this, because there is one aspect i would like to put to you briefly: does it seem normal to you that an italian citizen living near the french border should pay taxes in italy and, by producing income in france, should also be required to pay an advance on the alpine taxes? true, this deposit will be returned to him, but in the meantime how will he support the expenses of feeding his family? the same applies to all crossborder workers in other areas throughout italy. i call on all of you to urge your respective states to coordinate their tax policies with regard to this particular category of citizens who are forced to move to other member states because perhaps there is no work in their own countries.

in writing. − i am aware of the importance of horizon 2020 for european development. but my abstention from voting shows that real progress is also driven by the value of human dignity, which is always the same from conception. so while i appreciate the commission's assurance that european money will not directly contribute to the destruction of human embryos and that it will not take steps to promote projects which encourage the destruction of human embryos, i must denounce the contradiction in the commitment to fund research using previously destroyed human embryos: the commission has not yet taken a decision on the matter. however, the commission's commitment to not grant any funding in this field until after a scientific evaluation and, after that, an ethical evaluation is to be commended. i see in this a promotion of the european initiative 'one of us', whose very large numbers of subscriptions are being checked in all the member states. the initiative calls for a major ethical and scientific debate on the use of embryonic stem cells. i therefore hope that the commission will suspend the response to any request for funding for procedures involving the destruction of human embryos until the one of us initiative has completed its course through the european institutions.
in writing. - i voted in favour of horizon 2020. i am pleased that we have chosen to bring together, for the first time, research and innovation funding under a single 'common policy framework'. promoting scientific excellence will strengthen our industrial leadership and support smes with a financial allocation of €70.2 billion. i agree with the objectives set and particularly support grants to individual high-level researchers and new investments in technology and training. this will certainly help to put a stop to the notorious phenomenon of 'brain drain' by those who have been trained in the member states of the union and then go to non-european countries to have good opportunities to put their acquired skills to use. i also think it is important to provide for new investment in strategic areas such as health, energy, climate action research and biotechnology. finally, i think it is right to allocate at least 11% of the programme to smes, which represent a valuable asset for the whole of europe and deserve our full support.

in writing. − i voted in favour as the proposal provides for a substantial increase in funding for the european institute of innovation and technology (eit) for the period 2014-2020. the eit, set up in 2008 by the european commission as an autonomous european body to support innovation and research worldwide, brings together universities and research centres to achieve its goal through an innovative concept of cross-border public-private partnerships called kics, knowledge and innovation communities. to date, three kics have been created, focusing on renewable energy, climate change and the information and communication society. the capital increase for the eit under horizon 2020 will allow the first four kics to establish and grow and will pave the way for the creation of six new kics by 2018. the latter will focus on the following themes: healthy living (2014), raw materials (2014), food for the future (2016), urban mobility (2018), manufacturing industry (2016) and smart and secure societies (2018).

in writing. according to european commission data, smes represent more than 98% of all enterprises in the eu (about 20.7 million enterprises) with over 87 million employees. these figures tell us a great deal about their weight in the european economy. smes have already proven to be the main instrument for securing more and better jobs in europe, but they need support, both in political and financial terms, to help us get out of the current economic and employment crisis. i therefore believe that it is important to implement programmes such as cosme, which unlock the growth potential of smes by promoting their access to finance, reducing regulatory burdens and encouraging an entrepreneurial culture.
in writing. − the international competitiveness of european smes is undermined by market and institutional policy failures, such as limited access to finance and markets and regulatory burdens. as a result, european smes have lower productivity and grow more slowly than their counterparts in other parts of the world and have greater difficulties adapting to change than larger firms in europe. recent data show that the difficulties of smes have further worsened following the economic and financial crisis of 2008. in the context of the current multiannual financial framework, the european union is funding measures to support entrepreneurship, innovation and promote the development and growth of smes through the entrepreneurship and innovation programme. the next multiannual financial framework (2014-2020) will include the programme for the competitiveness of enterprises and small and medium-sized enterprises (cosme) which will focus on competitiveness, growth and entrepreneurship. i welcome the proposal for the cosme spending programme specifically aimed at our smes; however, given its limited budget, in my view it should focus on actions with greater impact and leverage such as reducing administrative burdens, access to finance and markets.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the creutzmann report on the programme for the competitiveness of enterprises and small and medium-sized enterprises 2014-2020 (cosme). the text calls for the commission to provide concrete support for enterprises by requesting €2.3 billion in funding.
in writing. − i strongly supported the proposal for the cosme 2014 programme as it aims to strengthen the competitiveness and sustainability of european enterprises, in particular small and medium-sized enterprises, to promote access to finance, to provide business support services, to encourage an entrepreneurial culture and to promote the creation and growth of smes. in particular, the cosme programme is aimed at entrepreneurs, especially smes, who will benefit from easier access to finance for their businesses, citizens who wish to start their own business and face difficulties in setting up or developing their own business, and member state authorities who will receive better assistance in their work to design and implement effective policy reforms. cosme will also contribute to the implementation of the european strategy for the internationalisation of smes, which will help businesses to understand, seize and make the most of all the opportunities available within the community.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the cosme programme because i consider it to be a very important instrument for our enterprises, especially smes. the latter, in particular, are one of the fundamental pillars of the european economy and must therefore be helped to establish themselves and, above all, to grow. in particular, the cosme programme is providing eur 2.03 million for the latter aspect to boost their competitiveness through improved access to markets. i agree with the choice to provide for at least 60% of the total financial envelope to be allocated to financing through risk capital or loan guarantees for smes, given the many difficulties in obtaining liquidity from banks. i also think it is particularly important to identify ways of reducing bureaucracy, which is a real obstacle for entrepreneurs who are too often discouraged by the formalities involved in setting up a new company.
in writing. − limited access to finance, market failures, the crisis and regulatory burdens have always undermined and slowed down the competitiveness of small and medium-sized enterprises (smes). in my vote in favour of the proposal for the cosme programme (competitiveness of enterprises and small and medium-sized enterprises), i welcome the eu's spending programme to support small and medium-sized enterprises, aimed at reducing administrative burdens, market access and bank financing. i remain confident that cosme will also focus on smes at local, regional and national level and not just on smes with cross-border activities.
in writing. − small and medium enterprises (smes) are the major factor in driving economic growth and create job opportunities. between 2002 and 2010, 85% of new jobs in the eu were created by smes. the proposed regulation aims to establish a programme focusing on improving the competitiveness of smes, mainly through reducing administrative burden, providing better access to finance and markets, support for business transfers and incentives of sustainable competitiveness. regarding the important role of smes in implementing the europe 2020 strategy and achieving the goals of smart, sustainable and inclusive growth, i voted in favour of this proposal.

in writing. − the european competitiveness of european small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) is undermined by the current economic crisis; as a consequence, european smes have lower productivity, and access to finance has become the main concern for european smes as a result of the economic and financial crisis, as banks are more reluctant to lend and investors are more risk-averse. i am therefore in favour of the objectives of cosme which is the only eu spending programme specifically targeted at smes, with one particular feature: cosme will not only focus on smes with cross-border activities, but also on smes active at local, regional and national level where there is proven eu added value. the eu's added value can also be in addressing market failures that cannot be addressed by the member states alone.

in writing. the title of this report may certainly give some initial shock: the last thing i would like is a european tax. the reality is fortunately very different, and it is a question of developing a programme, called fiscalis, which should interact and complement another programme which we voted on today, namely customs 2020. the european commission originally even envisaged merging the two programmes into one, but then it was decided, for a number of reasons, primarily legal, to keep the two initiatives separate, although closely related. this programme on european taxation is essentially intended to improve cooperation between the various authorities in order to prevent crossborder fraud, double taxation and, last but not least, to establish common measures and objectives which may restrict access to so-called tax havens. i believe it is in the interest of all european citizens and taxpayers that all possible measures be taken to deal with the phenomena of tax evasion and avoidance, which increasingly cross the borders of the member states and constitute an objective and serious harm to those who behave honestly and comply with the rules.

in writing. − the report refers to the regulation establishing an action programme for the customs of the european union (2014-2020). the objective of the programme is to encourage the european union to strengthen customs cooperation and the customs union between the member states (based on article 33 tfeu). i am voting in favour of this programme because it is of considerable importance and because some 75 to 80% of the funds will be used to adapt the computer systems of the european customs authorities for the purpose of controlling counterfeit and contraband goods.
in writing. - i have already stressed on several occasions the importance, perhaps unknown to most, of customs for the whole european economy: the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's agricultural policy is not disrupted by the crisis. this is particularly true of the large ports of northern europe, which are often portrayed as models of absolute efficiency: in fact, this is not always the case, because sometimes this supposed efficiency is due to the fact that very soft checks are carried out, i.e. goods are allowed to enter without too much care. this is obviously very dangerous and harmful, because we are being invaded by counterfeit goods of poor quality, often from emerging countries in asia: the consequences of these phenomena are not abstract, but unfortunately very concrete. unfair competition on our market leads companies in our territories to reduce production, relocate or even close down entire businesses, with serious consequences for the economic and employment systems of entire territories. the new european customs programme should allow for greater harmonisation and computerisation of systems within the different member states, with the hope that the threshold and effectiveness of controls will be raised and uniformised everywhere.
in writing. − the commission proposed a regulation on customs in the european union for the period of 2014-2020, succeeding the current regulation. increased cooperation in the sector of customs is consistent with the europe 2020 strategy for smart, sustainable and inclusive growth by strengthening the single market and customs union. therefore, i voted in favour of the proposal.

in writing. − as government spending on defence has significantly increased in many third countries, europe should improve its competitiveness in the defence sector as the budget has been cut back. also, further steps need to be taken to harmonise defence at european level, abolish protectionist measures and promote a more liberal, competitive single defence market of europe, as well as to improve mutual market access between the us and europe and the resulting imbalance in defence trade. therefore, i voted for this proposal which addresses the above issues.

the agenda includes a brief presentation of the report by kay swinburne on the recovery and resolution framework for non-banking financial institutions [2013/2047(ini] (a7-0343/2013).
vice-president of the commission. − madam president, i would like to thank ms swinburne for an excellent report. it is true that the regulatory framework in this area is in line with the international commitments undertaken at g20 level to improve the functioning of financial markets and to avoid taxpayers having to bear the cost of the failure of a financial institution. we welcome the contribution this report makes to this important debate. so, based on our own consultations and the international work underway under the aegis of the financial stability board, we agree that the priority in this area should be to develop appropriate tools for the recovery and resolution of central counterparties. these institutions, already systemic by their nature, are set to grow further in importance as the g20 commitment to bring over-the-counter derivatives into ccp clearing houses is implemented. regarding the other institutions mentioned in the report, we agree likewise on the need to focus efforts on implementing the stronger prudential requirements currently being finalised at eu level – the solvency ii regulation on central security depositories – and to roll out appropriate proposals in due course for their recovery and resolution, taking account of the findings of the ongoing international work. we appreciate the consideration the report gives to some of the key questions which a regulatory framework for ccp recovery and resolution will need to address: for example, mechanisms to allocate potential losses which exceed existing requirements or contractual arrangements should be transparent and effective. in view of their central role, the continuity of the services provided by ccps should be safeguarded but this should not be done in a way which distorts incentives for the users of ccps or gives rise to moral hazards. the commission takes note of these and other issues raised in the report and will carefully consider them when preparing its policy response in this area.
the debate is closed. the vote will take place on tuesday 10 december 2013.

in writing. with its indispensable contribution in terms of employment and innovation, the automotive industry is a central element for the european economy and a driver for its growth process. this text recognises this role and, while acknowledging the growing difficulties facing the automotive sector - due to the current crisis and the consequent contraction of the european market - it defines an action strategy consisting of coherent policies and interventions targeted at the crucial aspects of this sector. among these, it proposes to fund innovation and human capital through a series of regulatory initiatives to support research and innovation; improving market conditions through the reduction of red tape and the application of more streamlined and effective regulation; strengthening competitiveness on non-european markets through an internationally harmonised trade policy; enhanced and improved cooperation between the various levels of government and the various actors involved in the sector, inspired by the principles of fairness and transparency. the adoption of this action plan will therefore be a key step in the setting of long-term objectives to maintain the competitiveness of an industrial sector of major importance for the european economy and employment.

the rapporteur. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i think that today is a very important and exciting day for all of us who have worked on this document. the negotiations were long and we are finally voting on the new civil protection mechanism, which i believe is a small but important step towards a safer europe, towards a safer world. i'd like to start by thanking you. i would like to thank all the members of parliament who have worked constructively together from the very beginning. i believe that parliament has once again shown that it is the institution most sensitive to the feelings of the european citizens. we know that the european citizens are not experiencing europe in an extraordinarily positive way at the moment, at least for a large part of our fellow citizens and especially in certain sectors. there are, however, wide areas in which europe can work and show its citizens that europe is close to them, that europe is a friend, that it is the common home of the european citizens. i think we are finally writing a positive chapter in this regard today. we are expressing our solidarity with this document, with this new mechanism which is revolutionary, which completely changes the philosophy of the current civil protection, which is already an extremely important and useful instrument, and we are telling our fellow citizens today that europe is standing by them and i hope that from here a path of dialogue with all the peoples and citizens of europe can also be started. as rapporteur during the trilogues i was able to work - precisely because i had the backing of a strong and firm parliamentary position - to ensure that parliament's position was maintained, that it was strengthened, that i was able to defend and promote it. i also thank commissioner kristalina georgieva for her passion. anyone who is on the ground and lives through those dramatic hours of disaster response and is among the people and sees what the suffering is, the heartbreak and the wounds that are inflicted on communities and families, on people affected by these immense disasters, which are happening more frequently and with more violence today, i believe cannot but convey that emotion and that deep humanity, that charge of humanity that is breathed in those places. that's why, i think, we've written new chapters on prevention and preparedness. a new chapter on prevention because what we want is to protect citizens by preventing as much as possible, we want disasters to be prevented and if they cannot be prevented we want their effects to be reduced significantly. we also want to promote a culture of prevention. it is enough to think of risk management plans, a fundamental tool for planning a coherent and efficient risk management policy, as well as the creation of the voluntary pool of funds that states on a voluntary basis identify and make available for operations under the mechanism. it is a lot of pages, but i did not want to dwell on the technical aspects that we all know, i wanted to emphasize that we have tried to overcome even those which were some of the perplexities of the states, having as its pole star subsidiarity and solidarity. solidarity and subsidiarity are to be found throughout the document. i am grateful for this and i shall be listening to the speeches of other members besides the commissioner.
member of the commission. − madam president, i wish to thank members very much for all the comments made. let me make four points: firstly, for this legislation we are harnessing the will of our citizens. it is very important to stress that nine out of ten europeans have told us that they want us to stand together in the face of growing threats that affect their lives, their livelihoods and their property. secondly, we are setting up solidarity where it makes sense, and where we can do more for our people. 90% of disasters are local, and there the solidarity mechanism has no direct role to play, but for the 10% of disasters that overwhelm either our countries or a third country, this solidarity makes a huge difference: fewer people die and there is less damage. we are also harnessing solidarity between civil protection forces themselves, because when our teams train together, work together and deploy together they are much more effective. indeed, let me stress that we are harnessing the solidarity of the solidarity fund, as we have worked together to make sure that the solidarity fund and the civil protection mechanism can effectively be deployed with simplified decision-making for solidarity fund deployment. thirdly, this is about respect for solidarity. we have built this proposal to be a bottom-up system, not a top-down one, and i am very grateful to those who have recognised that we have done a good job together with parliament and the member states on that point. last but not least, my fourth point is that this is about cost effectiveness. it is about creating a culture of preparedness and prevention which we so much need for a future where inevitably, because of climate change, this is going to be one of more frequent and devastating disasters.
the rapporteur. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, thanks to all the speakers and to the commissioner, i think we are talking about something very important here today, because we are talking about solidarity, we are talking about the european spirit, we are talking about citizens who are already demanding more europe and, i repeat, this is something that does not happen very often these days, but we are already talking about a european civil protection system that works. in these days in my country, in venice in particular, a european exercise is in full swing, which began yesterday and will last for four days, involving teams from several countries, the united kingdom, austria, estonia, hungary and, of course, italy. we are talking about a european mechanism which is already working, which we want to make even more efficient, based on the experience gained, and it is not so important how much money has been invested - which is still very, very little, because if we open the prevention chapter, we have to put billions there - but we know that prevention costs much less than intervening after a disaster has occurred. i'd like to close with something: this weekend i was at the 16th day of the civil protection volunteering in friuli venezia giulia, the italian region where the italian civil protection mechanism that is known in the world was born. the then commissioner, mr giuseppe zamberletti, was also present. i guarantee you that if you were there you would understand what we are talking about, because we are talking about a community that after 40 years of that terrible earthquake still has gathered with emotion on this day where, in a region of only 1 200 000 inhabitants, volunteers have given and we have quantified in the last ten years a value in volunteer work that can be quantified in 200 million euros. i think that's where the sense of civil protection lies, the sense of belonging to a community, the sense of solidarity, the sense that we can look to the future and give back a more resilient society and community and territory to our children and to the generations that come after us. i believe that this is the best and most positive aspect of the european union. i thank you again for this and believe me, today's vote may seem a small vote, but it is a very important step. i think today is a day to remember and i thank commissioner kristalina georgieva once again for all she has done and the passion, the great passion she has put into it, the heart.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, this report is of fundamental importance in the work of this parliament, it contributes to the construction of the common european area of justice, freedom and security and it introduces a single instrument, simplifying the existing ones, to achieve the objective of building the single european area. so a single programme that combines criminal justice, civil justice and the instruments for prevention and information on drugs. the commission will allocate eur 472 million to achieve this objective. i think this is an important programme, and i think that supporting targeted spending in this direction also helps to promote growth, because the level of justice in a territory measures its degree of civilization and its degree of attractiveness. i believe that we are taking a step forward in the direction of building the single european area, but also in the direction of the growth of the european union.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the justice programme 2014-2020 aims to develop a european area of justice based on mutual recognition and mutual trust, in particular by promoting judicial cooperation and cooperation in civil and criminal matters. in all its activities, it aims to promote equality between men and women, the rights of children and to combat all forms of discrimination. i therefore voted in favour of this programme, which i regard as an important means of achieving a european legal and judicial culture.
in writing. − the principle of mutual recognition of judicial and extrajudicial decisions in civil and criminal matters, a common european legal culture among professionals in the field, the judiciary and prosecutors, and a thorough knowledge of eu legal instruments are essential elements for the effective establishment of a european judicial area. mutual trust between legal practitioners should be promoted through knowledge of national judicial systems in order to ensure the smooth functioning of judicial cooperation. i would like to stress that judges, prosecutors and professionals dealing with judicial matters concerning children (particularly vulnerable subjects such as victims or witnesses) should receive appropriate and specific training on their rights and needs.
in writing. − the main objective of this programme is to promote the effective, comprehensive and practical application of community legislation in the field of judicial cooperation and civil and criminal matters. this is complemented by a commitment to make eu justice more accessible and a programme approach to drug prevention and control. the text also calls for funding to be concentrated on raising awareness among citizens, combating illicit trafficking and other illicit activities linked to drug trafficking. in line with the council's position and after closely following the negotiations and identifying its priorities, i and my colleagues from the epp decided to vote in favour of this text because we consider it to be in line with our expectations in this area.
in writing. − i found the positions expressed in the report by mr berlinguer and mr claeys, analysing the new 'justice' programme 2014-2020, to be agreeable. the programme envisages the merger of the three existing ones, rationalising and simplifying the subject with the consequent saving of resources and a possible maximisation of results.
in writing. − i supported the justice programme 2014-2020 with my vote in favour. i think it was a good choice to combine the three previous programmes into one programme: this will improve accessibility and awareness for those, natural or legal persons, who wish to benefit from these funds. it is important that the union provides financial support to help member states in the prevention of drugs, crime and the suppression of illicit activities in general, which remains a top priority for the improvement of our civil societies.
in writing. − the report concerns the justice programme 2014-2020, the european commission's programme which will bring together the three funding programmes for the period 2007-2013 (civil justice, criminal justice, drug prevention and information). the programme has a budget of eur 472 million and will be targeted at public and private actors in the field of justice. the objectives of this programme are: to create a common area of justice for judicial cooperation in criminal and civil matters, to facilitate access to justice, and to prevent and reduce drug trafficking. i find the objectives described above to be shared. i am voting in favour of this programme because it is useful.
in writing. − the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu) provides for the creation of an area of freedom, security and justice in which people are free to move. to this end, the union may adopt measures to develop judicial cooperation in civil and criminal matters and to promote and support the action of the member states in the field of crime prevention. in further developing a european area of justice, respect for fundamental rights and common principles such as non-discrimination, gender equality, effective access to justice for all, the rule of law and a well-functioning and independent judiciary - and i emphasise the latter adjective, having voted in favour of the report - must be ensured.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i am extremely pleased with the work that has been done and i voted with conviction for this report which introduces a new programme for rights and citizenship for the period 2014-2020, making available substantial european union resources for the purpose of promoting awareness of the heritage of citizenship and protecting the rights associated with it. the single programme also aims to simplify the instruments, since it will incorporate the three previous programmes relating to the promotion of citizenship. i am pleased with the result achieved by my group, the european people's party, in terms of the emphasis it has placed on the protection of minors among the citizens. the commission has already taken the initiative in the matter of the legal protection of minors, and i would like to ask the council to take the initiative in the matter of the legal protection of minors.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the european union is founded on respect for human dignity, freedom, democracy and fundamental freedoms. that is why, without hesitation, i voted in favour of the rights, equality and citizenship programme 2014-2020, which aims to contribute to the development of a europe in which the equal rights of persons as enshrined in the treaty and international conventions are promoted, protected and effectively implemented. only by increasing our knowledge of the union's law and policies, and of the values and principles on which they are based, will we be able to look to the future with a brighter outlook.

in writing. - although the göncz report is a text whose approach could initially be shared and positive, its continuing call for funding for many projects that seek to facilitate the integration of immigrants and those belonging to ethnic minorities such as the roma cannot find my support. that is why i did not vote for this text.
in writing. − i voted in favour of the rights, equality and citizenship programme 2014-2020, which is an important source of funding for european actors interested in pursuing actions in a social sector of some importance. human rights, equality between citizens and a sense of belonging to europe through a conscious citizenship are fundamental pillars to ensure the sound and effective continuation of the european integration process. it is not enough to say that rights exist, but they must be recognized in practice. the financial allocation for this programme is therefore: i hope that many individuals and companies will participate in the calls.
in writing. − non-discrimination is a fundamental principle of the union. article 19 tfeu provides that measures are to be taken to combat discrimination based on sex, racial or ethnic origin, religion or belief, disability, age or sexual orientation. non-discrimination is also enshrined in article 21 of the charter to be applied within the limits and in accordance with article 51 of the charter. the specific characteristics of the various forms of discrimination should be taken into account and, in order to prevent and combat discrimination on one or more grounds, appropriate measures should be developed in parallel. we therefore welcome this 'rights and citizenship' programme proposed by the commission.

in writing. - we have approved the text of this fisheries protocol with morocco for two fundamental reasons. firstly, the fishing categories are the same as in the previous protocol and, although the number of vessels is reduced from 137 to 126, the fishing opportunities increase by about 33%, mainly due to the increase in the category of industrial pelagic fisheries (from 60 000 to 80 000 tonnes). secondly, the fishing zones have been modified to better adapt to the needs of the fleets and to allow certain requirements imposed by morocco to be met. thus, the extension of the zones for categories 1 and 2 reflects the industry's request to include the port of mohammedia which, in addition to being an important port of refuge, has landing facilities.
in writing. - i did not intend to support the estevez report on the eu-morocco fisheries agreement with my vote, as the text does not provide for the exclusion of western sahara from the territorial application.
in writing. the committee on fisheries' report, which led to the negative vote, was particularly critical on three points: the economic aspect, which highlighted the low cost-benefit ratios due to the low use of fishing opportunities; the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the moroccan fisheries sector is protected from the effects of the environmental aspect and, in the rapporteur's view, the financial contribution has had little impact on the moroccan fisheries sector. the fishing categories are the same as in the previous protocol and, although the number of vessels is reduced from 137 to 126, the fishing opportunities increase by about 33%, mainly due to the increase in the category of industrial pelagic fisheries (from 60 000 to 80 000 tonnes). the largest reduction is in category 3 (20 to 10 vessels) and 4, the most underused category, where the previous 22 vessels are reduced to 16. the fishing zones have been modified to better adapt to the needs of the fleets and to allow certain requirements imposed by morocco to be met. thus, the extension of the zones for categories 1 and 2 reflects the industry's request to include the port of mohamedia which, in addition to being an important port of refuge, has landing facilities.
in writing. - the fisheries sector is central to the moroccan economy because of its importance (more than 65 000 jobs and some 500 000 indirect jobs have been created) and because of the potential for strengthening and increasing cooperation between the northern and southern shores of the mediterranean, with the resulting economic development and social progress for neighbouring countries. in 2009, morocco launched the halieutis plan to ensure the sustainability of resources, the visibility of economic actors to foreign investors and to ensure that fishermen benefit from the benefits. the plan also aims at developing the region through dedicated projects (such as the expansion of the port of dakhla and the construction of the new port of boujdour), with a turnover of 366 million to be shared locally through national programmes to improve the work and living conditions of fishermen, support the work of women involved in the commercial and processing sectors and ensure the accessibility of fish products to all moroccan consumers. we must increase our support for morocco, which has managed to reorganise itself through appropriate reforms, which have put an end to the uprisings, and which is europe's gateway to the mediterranean countries. the union must speak for the interests of the mediterranean.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the draft council decision on the conclusion, on behalf of the european union, of the protocol between the european union and the kingdom of morocco setting out the fishing opportunities and financial contribution provided for in the fisheries partnership agreement between the european union and the kingdom of morocco. the protocol takes into account the european parliament resolution of 14 december 2011, improving environmental and economic sustainability. the text introduces legal obligations to ensure the sustainable exploitation - and limited to surpluses - of fishery resources. the cost to eu taxpayers is reduced by an increase in fishing opportunities, making the protocol more economically beneficial. the protocol includes clear commitments on respect for human rights and democratic principles and obliges morocco to report on the use of funds for sectoral support, economic and social benefits and their geographical distribution. for these reasons, i believe that the protocol is an important signal of the eu's concrete commitment to a sustainable fisheries policy and represents an additional tool for monitoring compliance with international law.
in writing. − the fisheries partnership agreement between the eu and morocco will greatly benefit europe, as european fishing vessels will be allowed to obtain a maximum of 126 licenses in the categories of small-scale fishing, demersal fishing and tuna fishing, and for a maximum of 80 000 tonnes of catches for industrial pelagic fishing. sustainability is also highlighted in the protocol; therefore, i voted in favour of it.

in writing. - i generally support measures which promote free trade in goods. whether this means increasing competition and allowing the consumer to have better quality at the same price, or a lower price at the same quality, or both, is easy to agree. if, on the other hand, the principle of free trade is to be used as an excuse to justify damage to the local economy (such as redundancies due to uncontrolled relocations), or to circumvent rules which, even before they are written, derive from common sense, then i believe it is my duty as a member of parliament and as a citizen to stand up for them. this general principle is the basis of my campaigns for product traceability, and it led me to vote in favour of this proposal: the more traceable firearms are, the greater the chances of tackling illicit manufacturing and trafficking. there is already too much violence in our cities, and whatever the cost of increased controls is certainly justified by the goal of saving lives and giving less leeway to those who misuse those weapons.
in writing. - i supported this report which stresses in particular the crucial importance of the exchange of information provided for in article 12 of the protocol: the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat this problem, and i am sure that the commission will be able to take action in the future. it is essential to exchange information on criminal groups, their methods, means and routes used, illicit firearms, manufacturers, dealers, authorised importers and exporters and good practices in combating illicit production and trafficking. there are many control systems such as marking and the system of export or import authorization and licensing, but they are not really effective unless information is shared. we therefore strongly urge the member states to step up the exchange of information through the europol eis information system, which will allow the identification, sharing and cross-checking of some 20 data items, including those relating to illicit firearms.
in writing. − the united nations convention against transnational organized crime (untoc) was adopted in 2000 to fight better against transnational organised crime and trafficking in firearms. supplementing protocols to the convention established specific measures against trafficking in persons, smuggling of migrants and illicit manufacturing of and trafficking in firearms. therefore, i voted in favour of the recommendations on the protocols in order to prevent trafficking in firearms and improve security for eu citizens.
in writing. - i voted in favour because the protocol aims to prevent, combat and eradicate the illicit manufacture and trafficking of firearms, their parts, components and ammunition by making it a criminal offence to commit illicit trafficking in firearms and ammunition and to falsify or abrasion the marking of weapons, as well as to attempt or facilitate such an offence, without prejudice to the various legal traditions of the contracting states. firearms must be marked by the contracting states at the time of manufacture, import or transfer to a given country in order to enable the manufacturer, the country and the year of import to be identified. the exchange of information between contracting states through a single point of contact will be important in order to strengthen the capacity of states to prevent, detect and investigate illicit trafficking in firearms. illicit firearms trafficking also benefits criminal groups and terrorists, providing them with another source of income and multiplying their destructive potential. the protocol will therefore make it possible to strengthen the security of european citizens without, however, harming the legal users of firearms.
in writing. − the united nations international convention against transnational organized crime, adopted in 2000, is the first global instrument to combat transnational organized crime and the trafficking of firearms. three protocols specify the convention by providing for specific measures to combat specific crimes. the protocols cover trafficking in human beings, smuggling of migrants and the illicit manufacture and trafficking of firearms respectively. the european community signed the convention and protocols against the smuggling of migrants and trafficking in persons on 12 december 2000 and the protocol against the illicit manufacturing of and trafficking in firearms on 16 january 2002. the ratification of the latter protocol makes it possible to prevent and combat illicit trafficking in firearms more effectively, by better controlling weapons through their marking and import and export authorizations, and by strengthening cooperation and the exchange of information between the contracting states. this has paved the way for enhancing the safety of european citizens without harming the legal users of firearms.

in writing. the european union and the united states of america are locked in a long-running dispute over the eu's ban on hormone-treated beef. however, on 13 may 2009, the eu and the us signed a memorandum of understanding, paving the way for a final settlement of the so-called 'hormone beef dispute'. this amendment to the protocol is to be supported for three main reasons. first, if it is not amended by 1 february 2014, the current mou would be voided and the us would be able to re-impose sanctions on eu agricultural products worth usd 116.8 million annually. secondly, the protocol allows the union to maintain its ban on hormone-treated meat and meat products, despite having been found to be in breach of its wto obligations. thirdly, by supporting this agreement, the european parliament is sending an authoritative political signal to the united states at an important time for the negotiations on the transatlantic trade and investment partnership (ttip).
in writing. − the eu and the us signed a memorandum of understanding in 2009 to negotiate a resolution on the dispute over hormone-treated beef. as the mutual obligations will expire on 1 february 2014 but a permanent settlement terminating the dispute has still not been reached, i voted in favour of the extension and revision of the memorandum and i urge that a final solution be negotiated.
in writing. the european union and the united states of america are locked in a long-running dispute over the eu's ban on hormone-treated beef. however, on 13 may 2009, the eu and the us signed a memorandum of understanding, paving the way for a final settlement of this dispute. a mutually acceptable solution allowed for a gradual suspension of retaliatory sanctions applied by the united states to certain european agricultural products in exchange for the opening of an autonomous tariff quota free of duties for high-quality non-hormone-treated beef. this was followed by the suspension of sanctions and the extension to 45 000 tonnes of the tariff quota for high-quality beef on the basis of the most-favoured-nation principle. that memorandum of understanding expired on 1 august 2013, but the reciprocal obligations remain valid until 1 february 2014. since the eu-us protocol is an international agreement, its amendment is subject to the approval of parliament, which, supporting the commission's proposal, decided to extend until 2015 the agreement on imports of certain hormone-free beef from the united states.
