mr president, ladies and gentlemen, europe is regularly hit by major natural disasters: floods, floods and forest fires. community cooperation in the field of civil protection is therefore essential. the union mechanism is indeed a major step forward in civil protection cooperation and will support, coordinate and complement member states' actions for more effective and timely prevention and immediate response in the event of disasters. i believe, however, that it is essential to complete the measures against hydrogeological risks by revising the stability pact, in order to remove from the parameters and constraints of the pact all measures aimed at soil protection and the safety of schools and public buildings.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, unfortunately we are seeing more and more emergencies and today's vote on the union's civil protection mechanism is an important vote, which in some way redeems the eyes of the european citizens of the union's institutions in relation to so many decisions taken that do not appear to be in the interests of the citizens. this is because it meets the need for solidarity which was one of the main pillars and driving forces behind the birth of the european union. i voted in favour of this report because i believe it is a high-quality document, which takes account of the need for prevention in particular and of the european union's response in this area. the amendments it proposes introduce simplified rules and procedures for the activation of the mechanism and enhance the effectiveness, efficiency and coherence of the eu's response to disasters. the increased involvement of regions, cities and local communities in their key role in prevention and emergency response, as well as the evidence provided by the specific needs of the outermost regions, sea basins, islands, mountainous, isolated and inaccessible regions, should not be underestimated.
in writing. - following the recent tragedies that also affected italy, the new european union civil protection mechanism is a tool that finally addresses the prevention of risks and the reduction of the effects produced by natural disasters with an integrated and system approach. it has been estimated that, in the last 20 years alone, natural disasters have killed around 90,000 people in europe and caused damage worth €211 billion. these are impressive figures and they require strong and concrete responses. risk analysis, risk assessment, prevention and immediate response capability are the priorities of the new civil protection mechanism in order to reduce the impact of natural disasters both in terms of loss of life and public resources to be allocated to the recovery of affected areas. this is an important step forward, but it should be accompanied by another measure, which is even more urgent at the moment, namely the revision of the stability pact in order to remove from the parameters and constraints of the pact all interventions, carried out mainly by local authorities, aimed at soil protection and the safety of schools and public buildings.
in writing. − i supported this text because i believe that the preparation of the new multiannual financial framework is a good moment to revise the existing legal framework of union civil protection. the number and gravity of natural and man-made disasters increased significantly in the past years, and climate change is expected to trigger even more extreme disasters in the future. for this reason cooperation needs to be strengthened between the eu and member states in order to increase their effectiveness, in terms of prevention, preparedness and response in the event of disasters – both inside and outside the eu.
in writing. − in recent years there has been a significant increase in both the number and severity of natural and/or man-made disasters. even more extreme disasters are expected in the future, mainly due to climate change. while welcoming the commission's proposal to establish a union civil protection mechanism, i agree with the rapporteur that it is appropriate to introduce some amendments to strengthen the legislative proposal and to create the conditions for the establishment of a union civil protection mechanism which is more reliable than in the recent past. member states in the same region are exposed to the risk of disasters of a similar nature. despite existing bilateral and regional agreements, the union civil protection mechanism should further promote regional cooperation in terms of sharing of knowledge, best practices and training programmes. finally, i believe that the resources financed by the union and the european emergency response mechanism in the form of a voluntary pool are fundamental steps towards a better and more reliable european disaster response system. however, for the better functioning of the pool, the european commission should define not only quality criteria but also interoperability criteria.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this proposal by mrs gardini because it is necessary to revise the community system of civil protection, given the importance it plays in dealing with the effects of natural disasters, which have been increasing in recent years, also and especially because of climate change. the lisbon treaty introduced a new legal basis for civil protection, but the concept of civil protection activity itself was not defined either in the treaty itself or in the legislative proposal. the resolution welcomes the commission's proposal for a uniform civil protection mechanism, but adds some useful elements to it in order to create a more reliable mechanism that meets the needs of the present day.
in writing. - i believe it is essential to safeguard the prerogatives and competences of the member states, in particular as regards risk management, modules and the european emergency response system, and for these reasons i supported the text with my vote.
in writing. − in may this year, oxford university press published an interesting comparative study on the economic impact of natural disasters, which looks at the case of six countries, identifying the characteristics of responses in different societies and economic systems. although the scientific literature on this subject is now substantial, we still have few certainties: however, we know that natural disasters cause significant declines in per capita output in the immediate term, but that in the medium term they can lead to significant improvements in response and even trigger economic recovery (see the interesting 2011 paper by the universities of tokyo and rieti). it is not surprising that both member states in a bilateral logic and individual private companies managing services of public importance (from energy to transport) have long since adopted transnational operational protocols for disaster management. the report identifies a central union mechanism which should generate an efficiency multiplier, while ensuring flexibility for states to fulfil their duties to protect the security of citizens. it will be important to build on the experience already gained at regional level and above all to work towards empowering the populations concerned, which can make the difference in terms of timeliness and lives saved. i therefore vote in favour.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. i congratulate the rapporteur on her excellent work. the improvement of the civil protection mechanism is an important objective because it gives concrete expression to solidarity in times of greatest need and thus in disasters and emergencies in the member states and other third countries. it is also an open instrument for other non-eu countries and therefore allows other national realities to be involved. strengthening the union's coordination in this field and allocating substantial financial resources seems to be a choice that deserves our support. analysis, risk assessment, prevention and immediate response capability are the priorities in order to reduce the impact of natural disasters both in terms of loss of life and public resources to be allocated to the recovery of the affected territories.
in writing. − i find the idea of establishing a common european mechanism that can support, coordinate and integrate member states' actions in the field of civil protection, improving the effectiveness of systems for preventing, preparing for and responding to natural disasters, interesting and useful. in recent years, unfortunately, we have seen a continuous escalation of phenomena which have required the rapid intervention of the civil protection forces; there have often been cases where organisations from different countries have collaborated, both because of the cross-border nature of these events and because in some cases, such as devastating earthquakes, the impact has been so substantial that external collaboration is also required. but of course we must also, and above all, focus on prevention, because this is essential if we want to limit the tragic effects of a natural disaster: it is perhaps in this field that close and coordinated european cooperation can prove useful, allowing comparison and mutual exchange between the different specialisations in the field.
in writing. − civil protection in the union is currently governed by the community civil protection mechanism and financial instrument covering the period 2013–2020. following the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon, the legal framework needs to be revised to tackle better humanitarian crises and strengthen the link between emergency measures, rehabilitation and development with humanitarian and development operators. i therefore voted for this proposal and the corresponding amendments.
in writing. - i voted in favour of mr gardini's text, which sets out the new rules for the union's civil protection mechanism to coordinate responses to natural and man-made disasters such as earthquakes, fires or leaks of harmful substances. member states will be able to respond to disasters jointly and share all preventive information on risk assessment. the proposal provides for more funding and simplifies the procedure for pooling resources such as rescue teams and aircraft, thus making it easier to respond to disasters outside the eu.
in writing. - i voted against this legislative proposal together with my colleagues from the forza italia delegation and fortunately we were able to get the majority of members to vote against this text, which would be reductive to call bad. not only did it contain proposals that are aberrant to those like me who seek to defend and protect christian values, but it also had a clear message against the family and against life. values which i consider to be unquestionable and untouchable.
in writing. - i agree with the sánchez report the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the consumer is informed of the risks involved in the purchase of a home. that is why i wanted to support it with my vote.
in writing. - i voted to postpone the final decision on this very delicate proposal for a directive. we cannot afford to make hasty mistakes when the protection of mortgage claimants is at stake. in particular, at this time of tight credit, the competent institutions must protect the rights of those who want to take risks and to do so need loans. i am in favour of the whole proposal. i am not saying that the commission should not be involved in this, but i am saying that it should be involved in the negotiations. however, the internal market aspect cannot be underestimated. i therefore asked for a little more time so that we could also reach agreement on the comparative tables.
in writing. − the 2008 financial crisis was triggered by the bursting of a housing bubble in the us, where mortgages were granted without much control and consumers were encouraged to take excessive risks. this directive has improved the regulation of the european credit market. this is the first step towards a european mortgage market. after two years of lengthy negotiations, the european parliament has reached an agreement that protects consumers without overburdening the banking system. the rules of conduct and transparency have been increased without entailing an increase in costs. a general ban on tied sales practices has been introduced. finally, rules have been introduced on variable rate lending and foreign currency lending, and the basis has been laid for more flexible and reliable credit markets.
in writing. - the report by mr sánchez presedo deals with the conditions applicable to creditors and credit intermediaries, the competent authorities and the supervisory requirements. these need to be strengthened in a consistent manner through the new european supervisory architecture. the proposal also contains provisions on information and practices prior to the conclusion of the credit agreement, the annual percentage rate of charge, the assessment of creditworthiness, access to databases, advice and early repayment.
in writing. i voted against the murphy report on the import of rice from bangladesh into europe at reduced rates of duty. it is clear that such action would distort the internal market and hit our producers hard.
in writing. - i voted against this resolution because of its approach which, while it was motivated by environmental considerations which were partly to be shared, was also likely to cause further problems for the manufacturing sector in terms of energy supply. the commission has already taken a number of measures to improve the quality of the products it produces.
in writing. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover all the activities of the european union. that is why i did not support the text with my vote.
in writing. - the european union is clearly ahead of other global players of comparable size in environmental policy. the degree of development of the emissions market is only an indicator. however, proposing to withdraw securities in order to artificially increase the price is a controversial operation for two reasons: the first is that it is built on a shaky foundation, because it cannot reasonably be assumed that there is a surplus of supply right now that, because of the crisis, polluting companies have less work and therefore produce less energy and therefore pollute less. the second is that, precisely because we are in a time of crisis, it does not make much sense to add to the costs of european industries in general and italian industries in particular, which are already heavily burdened by an enormous taxation of labour compared to competitors and by a far higher cost of energy. i therefore voted against this proposal.
in writing. - it is inconceivable, given the economic crisis still affecting the european economy, to think of an increase in energy prices. businesses and consumers cannot afford to be salted any further and this type of reasoning must therefore be stopped. this operation is bringing to its knees one of the sectors that is suffering most from the current economic situation. the paradox is that europe, as commissioner tajani has pointed out, is relying on manufacturing to revive the community economy. we must not, therefore, put ourselves in the way of european industrial ambitions. in this context, the short-term measure so passed with a split vote in parliament should not be seen as a solution to the current imbalances but rather as a way of ensuring the stability of the eu ets system until the necessary long-term structural measures are adopted.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution for purely procedural reasons. i think it is appropriate to remind the council that the amendments to the waste directive which we could discuss cannot be made through the so-called comitology but must follow the procedure laid down for all other legislative acts. the european union is already doing a lot to recycle paper. this does not mean that we cannot do better, but we have an advantage (over 70% of paper is recycled). changing the criteria for defining recovered paper as 'waste' is a useful way to improve statistics, but should be discussed in the relevant bodies if changes are appropriate. the council recalls that the treaty of lisbon is now in force.

in writing. the european automotive industry is a strategic sector for the european union's economy and employment. the automobile industry in europe is experiencing an unprecedented crisis. in 2012, the union recorded only 12 million units sold compared to 17 million in 2007, i.e. before the economic and financial crisis, which was the lowest level of sales since 1995; at the beginning of 2013, the figures indicated a further decline. one of the reasons for this decline is certainly the sudden and lasting loss of purchasing power of european households. while welcoming the work done by the commission with its cars 2020 action plan and its intention to improve the position of the european automotive industry in terms of gdp by 2020, i believe that the scope of the action plan shows some weaknesses. in general, it merely takes stock of the overall situation in the sector and does not contain any proposals for the reforms needed to consolidate its industrial policy in the automobile sector at european level. in my view, the car industry is a pillar of our industrial economy and therefore deserves priority and rapid political action. the commission's commitment must be made as soon as possible at the operational level.

in writing. - i am particularly interested in this subject. i was born and raised in veneto, a region where one in five citizens volunteers, giving their free time to those who need it most, to the most disadvantaged people. it is a sign of civilization and one of the most beautiful features of living together. when you are in trouble, it is reassuring to know that you can always count on someone. european civil society is responding to the crisis thanks in part to this world, made up of people with big hearts and strong wills. the world of volunteering is therefore a strength of our society which must be implemented and coordinated from a european perspective. the data collected so far are showing how important it is to continue working in this direction so that volunteering is not just a celebration of a year in a strategic sector of the union. we must try to make it one of the main instruments of social and cultural cohesion in the european union.
in writing. - i am not the one who should be emphasising what is obvious to everyone, namely the extreme importance of volunteering in our societies. as this report rightly points out, volunteering, which is increasingly popular among young and old alike, actively promotes cultural identity and solidarity between generations, also contributing to active ageing and civic participation at all stages of life, improving the quality of life. normally, volunteering is closely linked to the realities in which it takes place on a daily basis, but this does not prevent there being a european dimension, which can be achieved through an exchange of good practices, but also by referring to specific shared programmes and tools. this is a huge social, but also economic, added value which is often not recognised as it deserves, and that is why institutionalisation measures should perhaps be envisaged, even if, by its very nature, volunteering is characterised by its spontaneous nature and could hardly be incorporated into predefined schemes and concepts.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution: volunteering is an important pillar of our democratic and pluralistic societies. it is an expression of commitment, support and active participation in social life. volunteering includes all forms of non-profit-making activities: the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the programme and will continue to monitor the implementation of the programme. the impact on society is immediate as it promotes solidarity between generations, contributes to active ageing and civic participation at all stages of life leading to effective social inclusion. i know something about volunteering, having lived through the tragedy of the earthquake in emilia romagna last year. the mobilization of teams of professionals and volunteers, whom we will never cease to thank, was effective and impressive, as was the solidarity that came from italy and from much of europe. i myself organized a benefit concert for earthquake victims, which raised the sum of 25,000 euros directly for the most needy families. in 2011, the initiative to establish a european year of volunteering was welcomed as a way to pay tribute to and promote the commitment of volunteers and the organisations that work with them.

light at the end of the tunnel is missing. europe remains fully engaged and is committed to facilitating finding solutions to ukraine’s acute political crisis, based on the firm conviction that moving rapidly towards the signature of the association agreement would constitute a key step for restoring confidence. we are talking about confidence not only towards ukrainian citizens but also towards choosing and we have drawn the necessary conclusions. keeping in mind the lessons learned in vilnius, and preparing for the summit in riga we need to swiftly proceed with the implementation of the eastern partnership agenda. we are strongly determined to sign the association agreement including the dcftas with georgia and the republic of moldova by autumn 2014 before the end of the term of this college. we will continue negotiations with azerbaijan. at the same time we will need to reflect on how to proceed with armenia given the current situation. further advancement in the area of mobility deliver, need to be rewarded without any delays. moldova has become the first success story and an example for the others; and we should enhance our efforts in helping others to achieve the same. visa facilitation and liberalisation with the eastern partners is probably one of the best and most promising investments in the region and i call on ukraine to deliver on outstanding reforms so that it can follow in moldova’s path. we need to be more strategic and resolute. history will judge us not by the promises we made in vilnius, but by the promises we keep. i am not a plan b politician and i will always resist the temptation to play someone else’s game. we have the right policy and we have the right instrument and i am committed to working with catherine ashton, together with my colleagues, even more in order to make the best sense of it to the benefit of the transformation of that part of europe and for the benefit of the people of eastern europe.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the problem of counterfeiting the euro should be given great attention, especially as regards its links with organised crime. large-scale counterfeiting can damage the european economy and the stability of the currency itself. the euro is not, however, a currency subject to frequent counterfeiting. this is largely due to its design and the structures at national and union level for monitoring and combating counterfeiting. the pericles programme has played an important role in this process. this well-established programme has played an important role in disseminating best practices in the fight against counterfeiting and has thus contributed to the safeguarding of the financial interests of the union. however, the commission proposal still lacks a clear definition of certain areas and this report therefore seeks to develop this proposal by allowing the programme to optimise the use of the resources allocated to it.

in writing. - counterfeiting of the euro is undoubtedly a serious criminal offence and its link with organised crime must be taken into account when assessing the economic and social implications of counterfeiting on the lives of citizens. the euro is not, however, a currency subject to frequent counterfeiting, largely due to the structures in place at national and union level to monitor and combat counterfeiting. the pericles programme has played an important role in this process, disseminating best practice in the fight against counterfeiting. the proposal for a directive put forward by mr mcintyre aims to strengthen the pericles programme by introducing, for example, a minimum penalty of six months' imprisonment for the production and distribution of counterfeit coins and, in parallel, a maximum penalty of eight years' imprisonment for individuals for the distribution of at least eur 5 000.

in writing. - convention no 189 of the international labour organisation (ilo) provides for the obligation to protect domestic workers, most of whom are women, often in a highly vulnerable situation and victims of discrimination. domestic work is one of the least protected and visible jobs. in view of this situation, i voted in favour to emphasize the need, as mr zuber has said, to adopt measures to ensure decent working conditions, social rights and the prevention of abuse and domestic violence.
in writing. - i supported this report. the 2011 convention no 189 provides for the obligation of states that ratify it to take measures to ensure decent working conditions and social rights, preventing abuse, violence and child labour in domestic work. the european commission submitted on 21 march 2013 a proposal for a council decision authorising member states to ratify the convention. such authorisation is necessary as the convention concerns matters falling within the competence of the eu. we are asking the european parliament to allow the process to move forward with this report. it should be noted that several countries, in particular those from which migration flows originate, have already ratified the convention: the commission has also received comments from the exporting producers concerned. some eu countries have also already taken the necessary steps to ratify the convention, including italy and two other countries which intend to do so shortly: germany and belgium. in latin america, countries such as the dominican republic, colombia, argentina and costa rica have already expressed their willingness to sign the text. it is therefore a positive sign and by supporting it we have today given a sign of civilization to those workers who are often subject to non-existent occupational protections.
in writing. − in many member states of the european union, domestic workers often work without a contract, are required to work extra hours and on public holidays without due payment of their wages and with social security contributions unpaid. according to eurostat data, there are 2.6 million domestic workers in the eu, of whom 89 % are women and half are migrants. domestic workers are among the most unprotected workers, often uninformed of their rights and under-represented in labour associations or unions which can enable them to defend their labour and social rights. taking actions to guarantee decent conditions for domestic workers in europe is of great importance, therefore i voted for the proposal.
in writing. the main objective in the field of domestic work is to develop domestic workers as they play an important role in the economy. there is a need to define and regulate domestic work as one of the least protected and visible jobs, given the 'isolation' of those who do it. it is necessary to define a domestic worker as any person who performs domestic work within the framework of an employment relationship, having recognized the fundamental principles and rights in work, with equal treatment with other classes. the convention refers to the protection of migrant workers and introduces the need for a contract or a proposal from the employer before the worker arrives in the country of destination. it is necessary to ensure that such workers do not have a lower level of social and labour protection than other workers and in particular that employers make the payments due for social security contributions. it is also important to ensure that minimum wages correspond to the minimum wages laid down by national legislation. that is why i voted in favour.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, after yesterday's vote on the civil protection mechanism, parliament is today approving another instrument of solidarity with workers and another instrument of a social nature: the globalisation adjustment fund, which is intended to cover the following expenditure: the fund was set up in 2007 to provide support in the european union to workers made redundant as a result of major structural changes caused by globalisation or unexpected crises, such as natural disasters, leading to the closure of a factory. today, however, we have adopted an innovative regulation which i supported, introducing new features which simplify access to the fund, the admission applications, the evaluation and approval procedures and, above all, extend the scope of application to temporary workers, the selfemployed and farmers, and thus the fund has a greater extension. the only regret, mr president, and i conclude, is that the fund will be reduced in size in the coming years, but otherwise it is certainly a positive instrument which is a credit to this house.
in writing. - the european parliament has today delivered a concrete message to help workers made redundant as a result of the effects of globalisation and the economic crisis. it was essential to maintain the european globalisation adjustment fund for the coming years and there was a strong commitment from the european parliament to extend this instrument to other categories of workers. from january 2014, the egf will also be available to self-employed workers, temporary workers and young people who are not in employment or training, the so-called neets. in recent years, the egf has proved to be an effective instrument for reintegrating workers into the labour market, improving their employability (the rate of reintegration is close to 50%) and offering new opportunities also to the most vulnerable categories of workers. i would remind you, however, that this is not a fund to finance new social insurance schemes, but to co-finance active measures for reintegration into the labour market, i.e. training, guidance and vocational retraining.

in writing. − milk quotas will expire in 2015 which will greatly affect the dairy sector in the europe union, causing some market disruption, especially in the disadvantaged areas and the outermost regions. for these areas, milk production is often the only source of income and the local community depends heavily on the dairy sector. therefore, i voted in favour of this proposal to provide sufficient economic certainties to ensure the most vulnerable areas do not suffer from depopulation in the market transition of the dairy sector.
in writing. the report by mr dorfmann on milk production in lessfavoured areas after the expiry of the milk quota system was approved today in plenary. in 2015, the european milk sector will no longer be governed by milk quotas. this substantial change is likely to cause market distortions in this sector, especially in disadvantaged areas and in the outermost regions where milk production is often the only source of income for the local community. i agree with the rapporteur that in order to ensure a stable future for the sector and to avoid depopulation of rural areas, measures must be taken at european level and the impact of the abolition of quotas, particularly in the areas most at risk, must be further analysed in order to ensure adequate living conditions for farmers and a future for rural areas.
in writing. − the european dairy sector will undergo a major change after the abolition of milk quotas in 2015. for the first time in 31 years, the sector will not be regulated by milk quotas. this substantial change is likely to cause market distortions in the dairy sector, especially in the less-favoured areas and the outermost regions. in these areas, milk production is often the only source of income and the local community is heavily dependent on the dairy sector. to ensure a stable future for the sector and to avoid the depopulation of rural areas, as well as negative economic and environmental consequences, action will need to be taken at european level. the so-called 'milk package', which aims to strengthen the bargaining power of producers, is only a first step in this direction, but it will not ensure the future of milk production in these most vulnerable areas. it is also vital to further analyse the impact of the abolition of quotas, in particular in disadvantaged areas and the outermost regions. the main objective of this report is therefore to focus on the areas most at risk, to ensure adequate living conditions for farmers and a future for rural areas. that is why i voted in favour.

in writing. - invest first so as not to have to pay much more later. worldwide, disasters have caused enormous loss of life, as well as severe economic losses. according to data from the united nations office for disaster risk reduction (unisdr), between 1992 and 2012, 64% of the world's population was affected by disasters, with 1.3 million deaths and $2 trillion in damage. the poorest countries suffer the most. and more and more often the affected populations suffer, precisely as a result of disasters, severe food crises. since 2000, the number of food emergencies occurring each year has been between 50 and 65, compared to 25-45 in the 1990s. it is usually said that "prevention is better than cure". it 's true . investing in resilience and disaster risk reduction initiatives is more cost-effective. one euro spent on prevention is worth 4/7 euros spent on disaster response. but despite this, 95 percent of the funding is still going to disaster response, while only 5 percent goes to prevention. it's important to change course.

in writing. − disaster risk reduction is certainly an essential component of resilience, as it requires risk analysis and management to reduce vulnerability to disasters and build resilience. investing in resilience and disaster risk reduction initiatives is also more cost-effective. according to asian development bank estimates, one dollar invested in disaster risk reduction in a crisis-prone area saves at least four dollars in relief and reconstruction costs. in the light of the constraints imposed on national and eu budgets by economic difficulties and the growing political need to demonstrate greater effectiveness of development spending, a strong commitment to the promotion of resilience and disaster risk reduction strategies is therefore necessary in view of their cost-benefit ratio. in order to make significant progress on the resilience approach, mr mitchell calls for resilience measures to be closely integrated into humanitarian and development aid programming, while also recognising the challenges posed by climate change and emphasising the need to take account of climate change adaptation needs in resilience and disaster risk reduction initiatives.

in writing. - in the european economy, the retail trade has particular features which make it worthy of special attention: firstly, it is not transferable, in the sense that having a shop in the centre of milan is not like having one in a remote suburb of paris or in a small town in lithuania; however, it is replicable, so that the same trader can have business activities in the three locations mentioned, which has important implications in terms of the internal market. finally, for reasons of survival of the population that is supplied there, going below a certain concentration would have counterproductive effects (in the sense that if there were only one grocery store in the whole of milan it would make a lot of money, but if there were only one in the whole of lombardy the people who live in the mountains would have serious problems with supplies during the winter). these considerations lead me to support the proposal put forward by mr de jong, although i think that more attention to small shops in towns would be appreciated.

the rapporteur. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, mr vice-president of the commission, with this report parliament wants to contribute to the debate on the future of the european institutions. the angle of observation is that of multi-level governance, that is to say, of the mechanisms of differentiation which historically have made it possible to reconcile the development of integration and unity and to ensure, one might say, in an aristotelian way, the substantial respect of the principle of equality, which means equal treatment of equal situations, but differentiated treatment of different situations. this is a crucial issue after the introduction of the single currency and especially after the crisis made clear the need to strengthen the governance of economic and monetary union. the report's main argument is that not only is it possible to build an economic governance of the euro within the institutional framework of the union, but that this is the only way to make this enhanced governance effective and democratically legitimate. the theory and practice of differentiation which the report proposes is therefore that of differentiation as an instrument of the unity of the union and not as an element of division and fracture. a differentiation based on the union institutions and not on the tendency to rely on intergovernmental procedures and instruments that prevailed after 2010. the report analyses and proposes a set of procedures consistent with this philosophy, among which i would like to highlight, among other things, the combination of article 352 and enhanced cooperation which, in some cases, with effects equivalent to those of a reform of the treaties, could make it possible to avoid the veto of countries outside the euro area. one of the main points of the report concerns democracy and the role of parliament. here the thesis is clear and argued: the european parliament is also the parliament of the euro, and the symmetry between the european parliament of the union and the council, which instead votes in the euro-zone format, provided for in article 136, for example, when combined with article 121 (6), is a fully legitimate procedure which allows the interests of the euro-zone member states to be balanced against the general interests of the union, which are in any case affected by the choices made within the euro-zone. there is no need for a euro-zone parliament and there is no need to go back on the principle introduced by the lisbon treaty, which states that members of parliament represent the citizens of the union. it is possible and necessary, of course, through the rules of procedure and through the political action of the groups, to organise specific forms of differentiation within parliament, linked to economic and monetary union, but without revising the treaty on this point and without providing for a formal differentiation of the role of members on the basis of nationality. the last two parts of the report analyse and propose reforms to existing treaties and, finally, hypotheses for treaty change. in the first case, the contribution of the econ and empl committees was decisive, taking up and developing many of the points already contained in the thyssen report. i would just like to emphasize a specific contribution on the technical possibility of placing the solidarity mechanism and then a fiscal capacity within the union budget. on the other hand, the report proposes a number of hypotheses, some of them ambitious, on the reform of the treaties: introducing codecision in economic policy, making the commission the centre and the backbone of a genuine european economic government, providing a sort of gateway through article 136 to achieve a competitive economic competence for the eurozone countries, which would lead to overcoming unanimity on the mff and own resources, and finally addressing the same procedure for revising the treaties. so a broad report, an ambitious report, for which i would like to thank the excellent cooperation i had with mr trzaskowski, who is now a minister in poland, and with him all the shadow rapporteurs and the other groups, a report on which i hope there will be broad agreement in the vote tomorrow.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, while we are talking about the air we breathe and wasting time in useless chatter, in italy, at this hour, tens of thousands of people are protesting in the streets and squares against the italian government, against this europe, against the euro. nineteen million are unemployed in the euro area, of whom 40 percent are young people. thirty percent of italian citizens are at risk of poverty. these are the real problems facing our people every day, and they cannot be solved by more europe, by the fiscal compact, by austerity policies or by balanced budgets. clear rules must be established which apply equally to all, otherwise our businesses will be destroyed by unfair competition, social dumping, taxes and bureaucracy. the citizens have only one certainty today: the european union is a great example of the kind of europe that is not only a great example of the kind of europe that is not only a great example of a great europe, but also a great europe. either we change course quickly or history will decree the end of the euro and the death of europe.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i too have the duty and the pleasure of thanking the rapporteurs and of praising their excellent work, which has resulted in a near-unanimity of agreement within the committee - only three members of the committee voted against - and it is hoped that in tomorrow's vote a near-unanimity will be repeated. i must say that what i appreciate about this report is that it is really a real treaty - a small treaty - which explains in detail and precisely what the various levels of governance have been so far, but above all it gives a clear indication of the direction in which we are moving. we must never forget that the treaty of lisbon defines itself as a milestone and that milestone implies an end. so, the assessment of what has happened and what is happening must be measured in terms of the goal. it is clear that if the goal is merely the well-being of a single country which can be derived from membership of an economic community, there can be criticism, but if the goal is the greatness of the greatest political project of all time, that of a united europe, no longer bloodied by the death of its children, but becoming a continent at peace and a peacemaker in the world, then the discourse changes. multi-level governance has a different meaning, it is no longer a sign of incipient decomposition, but a sign of ongoing construction, according to an initial design in which different levels are reached one by one. that is why the rapporteurs are right when they describe the current situation of governance at various levels in a positive way - and they all describe it very accurately - but they are also right when they say that we must avoid new decisions and structures which can slow down the construction, can decompose it, can take away its harmony. in this respect, i think that the report they have presented is entirely to be supported, and i thank them again.
vice-president of the commission. − mr president, mr leinen described the crisis as dynamite to many well-established policies in the european union and it is true that the crisis was and still is very difficult for our citizens and the eu as a whole. we had to overhaul economic governance systems completely, we had to use crisis management tools very often and on many occasions we really had to act very quickly. i think that you would all agree that very often we also observed quite strong temptations from the member states to use preferably intergovernmental methods, an intergovernmental approach. to be completely honest, sometimes that was the only way decisions could be adopted, especially when the decision was very pressing and had to be done at very short notice. i am afraid that it looks as though this would again be the preferred approach when it comes to the single resolution fund, because after yesterdayʼs discussion it seems that the compromise, if agreed next week, would imply establishing national compartments in the resolution fund for the transition phase, with these accumulated contributions from the national banking sectors being progressively mutualised. at the end of the ten-year build-up phase, the national compartments would disappear and all would contribute equally to any resolution operation. and i think that, despite this, we also have to emphasise the fact that in the last crisis years we have learned that the community method is clearly preferable to the intergovernmental one, because it reflects the union diversity better, it takes more account of differences between big and small member states, north and south member states, there is much better incorporated expression of the will of the citizens through the directly elected representatives in this parliament and it gives the truly communitarian european institutions, both parliament and the commission, the appropriate role. therefore this is always always a starting point for the commission and it is always a reference point for presenting proposals or indeed the ultimate goal, where we would like to see cooperation, even if set up on an intergovernmental basis, ultimately transformed and changed. it is, i think, our common task as it was on many previous occasions; as i am sure it would be with the overall construction of the banking union. with our president, dear miguel ángel, we have already seen in cosac, in the article 13 conference, in our interparliamentary dialogues, renewed interest by the national parliaments in european efforts, in european cooperation. this is good because it enhances ownership of eu decisions and it brings better information to the national parliaments, but what is very important and what has very often to be stressed is that at the same time we have to respect our prerogatives. what should be dealt with at european level, what should be deal with at national level? we have to do this in full respect of institutional laws which are different, and in full respect of the appropriate balance. if something was started as intergovernmental, then i think that later on we have to explore all possibilities as to how to get it on to a strong european communitarian platform. if you will allow me, i will conclude on the specific question posed by mr hughes, who was calling for a green paper on the eu-level automatic stabilisers. i think this is a very important question and as such it was already discussed in the blueprint on emu and also in the communication on the social dimension of emu. from our analyses, our bottom line is that such measures could only be envisaged in the much longer term as this would require significant treaty changes to the current eu competencies in this area, which are quite limited. but it is an idea that is worth exploring further. however for now i think that we need to focus on what we can achieve in the intermediate term, meaning the convergence and competitive instruments especially, and explore all the possibilities we have with our current competencies and in the framework of the current treaties.
the rapporteur. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, this debate has brought to light many points, many important contributions, and some important critical remarks, and it is impossible for me to answer all of them in this short time. however, i wanted to follow a line of reasoning starting from mr rangel's correct remark, which underlines what the real aim of the report is. i do not want to speak of differentiated integration as an end, but to emphasize that it is a means, a means made necessary by the current state of asymmetry between the euro zone and the union, which is temporary, except for the moment for some knocked-out states, but that the objective and philosophy of differentiated integration as a means and not as an end that we propose is precisely that of an instrument to safeguard the unity of the union and to allow this integration, this construction of a governance of the euro zone to rest on the institutions of the union and therefore be democratically legitimated. that is why, in the various procedures which we have mentioned and identified, the one referred to by mr scholz, namely enhanced cooperation, is only the last in the order of priority. we believe that we should always try to start with legal acts of a general nature, perhaps including derogations which are historically and legally provided for by the union's structure, and then move on to article 136 and only as a last resort to strengthened cooperation, precisely in line with this philosophy of differentiation based on unity. of course, there are different sensitivities, especially on a fundamental political point, that of parliament on the question of its possible differentiation, and in particular that of mr goulard, the spokesman, so to speak, of a line which seeks to consider, as you have said, the institutionalisation of the eurozone as legitimate. i continue to believe that only by building on the existing institutions and not backing down on the role of parliament as the representative of all citizens can we give an adequate response in terms of democratic legitimacy and that the road of differentiation within parliament, beyond this parliament, a possible new parliament, does not lead very far and leads in a direction that is different from the one we are currently taking. if we consider that the principle of the vote we have had today, a vote of consent by parliament at the top of an institution whose function does not concern all the countries of the union, but this binding vote was obtained by all members of parliament, is accepted in the ssm, it is clear that progress has already been made in this direction and so i believe that this report, together with many other indications, makes an important contribution to maintaining this line, which is the only one that i believe can lead us consistently to follow a common thread between the necessary differentiation of today and the possible unity of tomorrow.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, mr lamassoure's report touches on a very important and sensitive subject. i would like to stress two points in particular which i consider to be absolutely decisive and central. the first is the european council's actual interference with the ordinary legislative procedure, which we have had a very clear experience of in the context of the adoption of the regulations relating to the mff and which is now likely to be repeated in the course which could lead to a regulation on so-called contractual agreements. it is contrary to the letter and spirit of the treaties for the european council to bind the council by a unanimous procedure and thus to empty the ordinary legislative procedure, which is based on qualified majority voting and the equal role of two co-decision-makers. i therefore welcome the proposal to include a standard wording in the european council conclusions. the other aspect of great importance for the forthcoming elections is the election of the president of the commission. the elections, which it is good to remember first of all that they are elections and not a vote of consent - that is what the treaty unequivocally says, and that this is therefore necessary, not only because of what the treaty itself says about the way in which the european council's proposal must take account of the result of the elections - this election can only be triggered by a procedure which the european council must undertake to respect and to establish, which moreover the eleventh declaration annexed to the treaties calls for defining and clarifying - and therefore also in this sense the proposal by mr lamassoure to ask the european council for a formal commitment which is not only about how it intends to respect, but also a commitment to define by common agreement a procedure precisely for implementing the eleventh declaration and thus making article 17, paragraph 7, substantial, is a proposal of great importance which i share.
i am not going to go into the details of the commission's proposals, but i would like to say that the commission has already made a number of proposals. of course, the esm is an intergovernmental body, we know that. but if you want to go down the road of saying that the european union has nothing to do with the esm, i do not understand why the council and the commission have gone into detail, explained to us why this article, that article, because it would be a burden on the budget of the european union, you could do it with an agreement, but it would take 18 months. if it had nothing to do with you, the only logical response would have been to not answer. since it is a matter for the european union, and we know this well, because it is based on the commission, the decisions it takes are taken by the eurogroup, and it is even included in an article of the treaty which we have just amended, it is quite obvious that it is ridiculous to say: we have nothing to do with the esm. so you can't escape the first fundamental question: how is it that the administrative tribunal covers 50,000 people with seven judges and to perform the same function it takes five judges for 100 people? is this a wise use of taxpayer resources? and who exercises the supervisory and scrutiny function in the esm? parliament is not, because it is not part of the european union. are the national parliaments capable of doing this? what is this esm? it is in danger of becoming a body which is really out of control, and this small example, this small incident - which is not so small after all - is actually a worrying symptom of a trend which we, when we gave our opinion, precisely on the 136 amendment, the esm, clearly said was not the way to go, and there was also a clear indication in the conclusions of the european council. the way forward is to gradually integrate the esm into the legal and constitutional framework of the european union and not to remove it from it. and so, in view of the possibility that vice-president šefčovič has confirmed that the administrative tribunal will be used, it is really incomprehensible that the member states have chosen to allow this body to go in the opposite direction. and i must say with regret that the council representative's justification that five judges for every 100 people would represent a saving is laughable, whereas using the seven judges to cover 50 000 would have cost the european union's budget, which is then fed with the same resources because clearly not all the members of the european union are members of the esm, but all the members of the esm are members of the european union. so, really, i want to be clear: we're not here. the european parliament will continue to exercise its role of control and scrutiny over the esm and will call on the member states, including through cooperation with the national parliaments, to account for a policy choice which is in fact a worrying indication of a direction which is the exact opposite of the one that the governance of the euro area should take.

member of the commission. − mr president, honourable members, the gsp+ is the centrepiece of the eu’s trade and development policy and has been a success so far, one that we wish to build on. let me reiterate that applicant countries have committed to taking bold steps to implement core human, social and labour rights, sometimes even before applying for preferences. they have met the entry requirements and this can be economically costly and politically difficult. the eu is proud that these countries are taking such steps, but we are not lenient: we have been tough in assisting them and assessing them. in terms of the analysis of the gsp+ entry criteria, the commission considers that a single delegated act better ensures that similarly situated gsp beneficiaries get identical treatment instead of individual delegated acts per country. the gsp schemes reflect the world trade organization’s principle that identical treatment should be available to all similarly situated gsp beneficiaries. as for the monitoring mechanism, the application will be ensured on a country-by-country basis in order to take into account the individual degree of progress that beneficiary countries will ensure. we are now completing the first technical phase for the first ten applicants. now a second phase will begin, focusing on compliance with the obligations taken on by the applicants under international conventions. the scrutiny and follow-up mechanisms provided in our legislation and which foresee an important role for the european parliament will require gsp+ beneficiary countries to prove that they are making genuine, verifiable progress. in this phase, the committee on international trade experts are invited to attend all gsp expert group meetings. the committee on international trade secretariat will receive all relevant documents shared with member states. draft updated scorecards will be discussed with the international trade committee which may also request dedicated commission briefing on monitoring throughout the duration of the gsp+ scheme. in applying this scheme, the eu institutions share the same objective: promoting development and eu values concurrently. through gsp and, in particular, gsp+, the commission considers it has lived up to parliament’s call in a resolution passed in april this year on advancing development through trade. i thank you very much for your contribution, for your positions, for your concerns and the points you have made, and i will pass your messages to commissioner de gucht.
author of the book. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, the climate crisis is before our eyes and is getting worse every year, and is reaching a point of no return. every decade has been warmer than the last for the past 30 years, and greenhouse gas emissions continue to rise. a stronger global initiative is needed to reach an agreement that seriously involves the major polluting extreme weather events such as storms, hurricanes and floods has also increased in europe, most recently flooding in sardinia, italy, and northern europe. heatwaves have also become more severe. increasing temperatures, changes in the intensity and frequency of rainfall and droughts also have an impact on soil, fertility, erosion, aridity and desertification. in this context, the resolution on green infrastructure and its implementation, which is based on a question from the committee on the environment, is very important. green infrastructure is a tool for achieving ecological, economic and social benefits based on natural solutions. according to some studies, these infrastructures are economically advantageous, more durable than traditional ones and, in many cases, create new job opportunities at local level, can sometimes be an alternative, sometimes a component of traditional solutions, can be introduced into a network of natural and semi-natural areas, if strategically planned with other environmental elements can provide a wide range of ecosystem services. the role of green infrastructure becomes essential and must be placed in a european and national system; the strategy therefore needs to be implemented at national and local level in order to be effective. the european strategy needs to be transposed into member states' measures in order to give impetus to interventions based on the use of natural solutions based on the sustainable use of natural resources. i would like to mention briefly some of the possibilities for using green infrastructure: for example, in cities, with the design and construction of new green areas, green belts, parks, gardens, green groves, roofs and green walls; adaptation, integration and management and development of existing green infrastructure, aiming at mitigating the effects of heatwaves and improving the local microclimate. green infrastructure can make important contributions to restoring the eco-hydrogeological functionality of the land in areas of controlled flood expansion, to maintaining river basins and embankments, to stabilising slopes in mountain areas, but also in coastal areas where natural structures can be built. in addition, we believe that in order to develop the strategy even more effectively, we need to increase the involvement of the private sector in projects concerning green infrastructure. the resolution therefore urges the commission and the eib to set up a financing facility as soon as possible, including subsidy mechanisms for investment in green development fund and the european agricultural fund for rural development. i conclude: to achieve this, coordination is needed and a detailed mapping of the actions to be taken is needed. we know that there is still a lot to be done, but a recent study shows that green infrastructure initiatives could theoretically cover, for example, in italy and france, a record 95% of the territory, with a total area of almost 290 000 square kilometres. a more realistic estimate limits the pool of actual applicability to a gigantic area of 50 percent. green infrastructure can also be a great opportunity for small and medium-sized enterprises, which can play a key role in this field, especially because of their propensity to innovate and to be sustainable. in this connection, i think it is a good idea to establish common european certifications and labels to support investment in green infrastructure and also to facilitate the exchange of good practice between companies. we thank the european commission for the effort it has made to give impetus to these issues and we call on it to implement as soon as possible a financial measure to accompany these policies and to make every effort to integrate all relevant instruments of the european union in order to contribute to the development of green infrastructure.

the rapporteur. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, mr draghi, commissioner, as you and we know, the economic situation on our continent remains dramatic, despite the very tentative signs of recovery. the specter of deflation is looming in the euro area, a clear sign of anemic demand. the picture in southern europe is, unfortunately, even worse. you, mr draghi, are an italian like me and i believe you are watching with the same unease as i am the riots that are sweeping our country at this hour. either the record is changed or the very project of european integration is at risk, because it is being challenged by the disillusionment and anger of millions of citizens. we must change our pace before it's too late. the ecb, president draghi, has done a great deal under your leadership and has broken important taboos, as we acknowledge in our report. i am thinking in particular of the orlt operations which have allowed the banking system to breathe in the short term, and i am also thinking of the announcement of the omt programme which has played a decisive role in stabilising expectations. but now more must be done. the transmission chain of monetary policy is still stuck, as evidenced by interest rate differentials and the decline in lending to small and medium-sized enterprises. the president is also aware of the seriousness of the situation and, as you said at your press conference last thursday, the ecb is ready and prepared to intervene. in our resolution we acknowledge that unconventional monetary policy instruments have revealed all their limits in supporting the real economy and we call on the ecb to consider the adoption of new measures. these new measures must be directed towards supporting small and mediumsized enterprises, and a very large majority has been created in parliament on this. the report identifies a number of measures: the adoption of a programme modelled on the example of the 'funding for lending' programme in england; in writing. − to ensure social cohesion in times of economic crisis, characterised by high unemployment, high energy prices, scarce raw materials and dependence on imports, the creation of sustainable employment and economic growth is a priority. innovation is a key factor in achieving this and must therefore be encouraged. one way to do this is to promote eco-innovation, a concept that combines environmental protection with growth, competitiveness and job creation. environmentally friendly innovations are very important to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, to use resources such as water and raw materials more efficiently, to increase the use of recycled materials and to produce quality products with a lower environmental impact. for these reasons i have expressed my support for mr kadenbach's text, which calls for a series of initiatives to develop eco-innovation, with the support of the public sector, the private sector and the european commission.
in writing. - i support the quisthoudt-rowohl report analysing the agreement at second reading on adaptation to the new rules on delegated and implementing acts for the trade policy package called 'trade omnibus i'.
in writing. − the lisbon treaty allows the commission to adopt a new type of act: the delegated acts. this is an important innovation, making it possible to make the union's decision-making processes more efficient and streamlined, the length of which is the main obstacle to the ability of the european institutions to respond in a timely manner to the needs of citizens. for this reason, i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution to adapt the commission's rules for taking decisions in trade matters to the new system of delegated and implementing acts.
in writing. − in the light of the changes introduced by the lisbon treaty and the subsequent adoption of regulation (eu) no 182/2011 (on implementing acts), the commission had to adapt the rules for taking decisions on trade policy to the new regime of delegated and implementing acts. as a result, the commission has put forward two alignment proposals known as omnibus i and omnibus ii. each of these brings together in a single instrument the basic commercial regulations that need to be updated; the first mainly concerns implementing acts, while the second mainly deals with delegated acts. the proposal under consideration (omnibus i) therefore makes the necessary amendments to the basic texts and specifies the procedures to be applied, in particular as regards the choice between the advisory procedure and the examination procedure for implementing acts. the opportunity presented by today's debate allows me, however, to remind you that the market is not helped by regulatory instruments alone.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution because it aims to make the decision-making process and the implementation of decisions taken in the field of trade policy more efficient. we can no longer afford for europe to respond to the needs of its citizens with legislative procedures that are often too long and inefficient. any improvement in this direction will always find my favour and political support. the institutions are lean, efficient and able to give concrete answers: this is the recipe for a europe that can meet the challenges of the future.
in writing. − in the light of the changes introduced by the lisbon treaty and the subsequent adoption of regulation (eu) no 182/2011 (on delegated acts), the commission had to adapt the rules for taking decisions on trade policy to the new regime of delegated and implementing acts. the commission has therefore put forward two alignment proposals known as 'omnibus i' and 'omnibus ii', each of which brings together in a single instrument the existing trade regulations that need to be updated; the first covers mainly implementing acts, while the second covers mainly delegated acts. the present proposal ('omnibus ii') therefore introduces the necessary adjustments to be made to the existing texts which previously referred to the old comitology decision 1999/468/ec. we must thank the rapporteur, jörg leichtfried, for the sensitivity with which he has followed this dossier. we must all bear in mind that there is widespread discontent with this europe. that is why we must correct the mistakes of the past and, as we speak today, work towards ever greater integration between the countries of europe.

in writing. − our will was already expressed in the resolution of 4 july 2012 with recommendations to the commission on access to basic banking services: more needs to be done to improve and develop the single market for retail banking. these developments must go hand in hand with efforts to ensure that the financial sector serves both business and consumers. at present, the lack of transparency and comparability of charges, as well as the difficulties in transferring the payment account, still create obstacles to full integration of the market. the discrepancies in product quality and the low level of competition in retail banking services need to be addressed and high quality standards ensured.
in writing. - the european parliament, in plenary session, voted this morning on a resolution by mr klute on the proposal for a european parliament and council directive on the transfer, comparability and access to basic bank current accounts. the text establishes the right for anyone legally resident in the eu to open a basic bank payment account, a right which should not be denied on the grounds of nationality or place of residence. insisting that most payment service providers, such as banks, offer a basic bank account can make life easier for consumers, increase business efficiency and help to modernise our economies. the resolution also implements a number of provisions on transparency and comparability of charges relating to the account, as well as greater simplicity in switching from one basic account to another, to ensure a high quality of customer service. for these reasons, i am in full support of a report which meets the general expectation of citizens that basic banking transactions should be simplified.
in writing. - the proposal for a directive tabled by mr klute, which was approved today, aims to improve the transparency and comparability of information on expenditure relating to bank accounts, to eliminate discrimination on the basis of residence in relation to access to accounts and to ensure common features for opening accounts throughout the union. therefore, anyone legally resident in the eu must have the right to open a basic bank account and this right cannot be denied on the basis of nationality or place of residence.

in writing. - i thank mr scurria for the excellent work he has done on this text which was adopted today. the text is a new commission proposal, which proposes to continue the european capitals of culture initiative after the current action expires in 2019. the new proposal establishes the order in which countries nominate cities for the title until 2033. in addition to the two member states sharing the title each year, the proposal also provides that candidate or potential candidate countries may nominate a european capital of culture every three years. i share the rapporteur's view that the commission's proposal to continue the european capitals of culture action beyond 2019 should be welcomed, with a renewed legal basis, seeking to resolve the problems raised by the current decision and attaching to the decision a new chronological list of member states (2020 to 2033).
in writing. − today, in plenary, the european parliament voted on the report by ms scurria on the eu action on the european capitals of culture for the years 2020 to 2033, with the aim of providing a new legal basis for further action to protect those cultural heritage sites which embody the european cultural consciousness. since its inception, the initiative has gained wide appreciation and interest throughout europe, becoming a highly coveted prize for those cities that aim to present themselves as european centres of culture and creativity. the approved text, while maintaining the main features and structure of the action currently under way, introduces a number of new features aimed at improving, inter alia, the visibility, the selection process of the action and the involvement of local civil society, in an overall perspective of long-term growth and urban development of the selected capitals. for the reasons stated above, i can only express my agreement with a resolution which, in the present context of a general economic crisis which threatens our sense of belonging to europe, provides concrete and tangible incentives for long-term cultural initiatives.
